Dwarf remains are a quest item used only in Dwarf Cannon. The remains are those of Gilob, and are given to Captain Lawgof after recovering them during the quest. It is found on the 1st floor of the watchtower south of the Coal Trucks.

Duplicates cannot be obtained, as it does not respawn after the player has picked it up for the first time.
1:
The toolkit is a quest item used only in Dwarf Cannon. It is obtained from Captain Lawgof after rescuing Lollk in the Goblin Cave.

It is used to fix the broken multicannon he has set up nearby in the dwarven outpost, south of the Coal Trucks near Baxtorian Falls.

Duplicates can be banked by talking to Captain Lawgof to obtain another. After speaking to Captain Lawgof after fixing the multicannon, all copies of the toolkit in the inventory are deleted.
2:
Steel cannonballs are ammunition used for a dwarf multicannon, as well as for a boat cannon during boat combat. They can be fired from steel cannons or stronger.

Four can be made from a single steel bar with level 35 Smithing, granting 25.6 experience per bar. Smithing cannonballs require the use of an ammo mould, which requires partial completion of Dwarf Cannon to obtain. Alternatively, a double ammo mould (requiring Foundry Reputation to purchase via the Giants' Foundry minigame) allows players to process two bars into eight cannonballs at the same speed as a regular ammo mould processes one bar into four.

Players with level 87 Sailing can further speed up smithing cannonballs by using the ancient furnace in the Grimstone Dungeon, which halves the time it takes to create cannonballs from 8 ticks to 4 ticks. Combining this with a double ammo mould, players can smith cannonballs at four times the normal speed.

Lastly, players with level 50 Smithing can use granite dust on steel cannonballs to create granite cannonballs, which gives superior stats on boat cannons, and increases the max hit of dwarf multicannons by 5. This yields no experience.
3:
Nulodion's notes are a quest item used only in Dwarf Cannon. It is obtained from Nulodion after speaking to Captain Lawgof after repairing his broken dwarf multicannon.

It is given to Captain Lawgof alongside Ammo mould to complete the quest.

Duplicates can be banked by talking to Nulodion to obtain another.
5:
The Instruction manual, or Dwarf Multicannon Manual, is a book that details how to set up and fire the dwarf multicannon, how to create cannonballs, and includes warranty information for the dwarf multicannon.

After completion Dwarf Cannon, it is found on a bookshelf in a player-owned house or is purchasable from Multicannon parts for sale for 10 coins or Rasolo the Wandering Merchant for 20 coins.
10: Cannon barrels are the third part of the dwarf multicannon set up on top of the cannon base after placing the cannon stand and before the cannon furnace. They shoot the enemy with a barrage of steel cannonballs or granite cannonballs. It is purchased from Multicannon parts for sale for 200,625 coins.
14:
A railing is a quest item used only in Dwarf Cannon. In the quest, six railings are obtained from Captain Lawgof and used to replace six bent railings in the fence surrounding the Coal Trucks. A hammer is also needed to repair the fence.

There is a chance to fail when repairing sections of the fence, and the player may receive small amounts of damage which will deal 1-2 Hitpoints. The player will also receive a message saying either You cut your hand on the rusty old railing., You strain your back trying to handle the railings., or You accidentally crush your hand in the railing.
15:
The holy table napkin is a quest item obtained from Galahad in the Holy Grail quest. It is used to see the magic whistle spawn in Draynor Manor's top floor.

If the player wants to return to the Fisher Realm, it can be safely dropped if the player has access to fairy rings or keeps the magic whistle from the quest.
16:
The magic whistle is a quest item in the Holy Grail quest which is originally obtained in the southern room on the top floor of Draynor Manor. This spawn can only be seen and picked up while the player has a holy table napkin in their inventory. In this spawn location, there are two whistles, one for the player and one which must be given to Sir Percival.

Blowing the magic whistle while standing in the location where all of the mysterious statues point, under the tower north-west of Brimhaven, allows players to access the Fisher Realm. Blowing the magic whistle in the Fisher Realm returns the player to Karamja. Attempting to blow the whistle anywhere else will display the following message: The whistle makes no noise. It will not work in this location.

If lost after the quest, another may be obtained in the same manner as during the quest, or if the player has access to the fairy rings, there are several spawns in the Fisher Realm: one on a table inside the house in the north-west, one just outside that house, and one on a table just inside the castle.
18:
The magic gold feather is a quest item used in the Holy Grail quest given to the player by King Arthur to help find Sir Percival.

Blowing on the feather will cause the feather to point either north, east, south, or west until the player reaches Goblin Village. Once the quest is completed, the feather has no use and can be safely dropped.
20:
The white cog is a quest item used only in Clock Tower. It is found behind a gate that can be opened by adding rat poison to the food trough in the Clock Tower's basement.

It is used to repair the western white clock spindle on the 2nd floor.

Duplicates can be acquired by picking up another one after putting the first cog on the clock spindle and before completing the quest. Once the quest is completed, the cog can not be picked up from the spawn or if the duplicate is dropped.
21:
The black cog is a quest item used only in Clock Tower. It is found in a burning room in the Clock Tower's basement, requiring a bucket of water in the inventory, or ice gloves or smiths gloves (i) equipped to pick up.

It is used to repair the eastern black clock spindle in the basement.

Duplicates can be acquired by picking up another one after putting the first cog on the clock spindle and before completing the quest. Once the quest is completed, the cog can not be picked up from the spawn or if the duplicate is dropped.
23:
The red cog is a quest item used only in Clock Tower. It is found in a room with three ogres in the Clock Tower's basement.

It is used to repair the northern red clock spindle on the ground floor.

Duplicates can be acquired by picking up another one after putting the first cog on the clock spindle and before completing the quest. Once the quest is completed, the cog can not be picked up from the spawn or if the duplicate is dropped.
25:
The red vine worm is used in the Fishing Contest quest to catch the giant carp that wins the contest. They also may be needed to make a pair of magic secateurs in the quest A Fairy Tale I - Growing Pains, and can be possible a clue for finding Solus Dellagar in the quest Wanted!.

They are obtained by digging with spade near the red vines that can be found in McGrubor's Wood. The fairy ring code ALS can be used to quickly reach the vines.
26:
The fishing trophy is a quest item used only in Fishing Contest. It is obtained from Bonzo after catching a raw giant carp.

It is given to either Austri or Vestri to complete the quest.

Multiple fishing trophies can be obtained by using the drop trick; drop the original trophy given by Bonzo, ask for another, then pick up the other trophy from the floor. Using additional trophies on either Austri or Vestri after the quest will cause them to be taken off you.
27:
The fishing pass is a quest item used only in Fishing Contest. It is obtained from Austri or Vestri upon starting the quest.

It is shown to Morris to enter the competition area each time.

If lost, the dwarves can replace it with another. More fishing passes cannot be acquired after completing the quest. It is not needed to enter the competition area after talking to Aggie about white dyes during the Land of the Goblins quest.
28:
Insect repellent is a container of bug spray that can be used on beehives, large mosquitoes, and mosquito swarms.

Using insect repellent on beehives, located in the apiary west of Catherby and in southern Seers' Village, causes the bees to leave. Using a bucket on the beehive then gives a bucket of wax, which is used in Merlin's Crystal and Troll Romance. Insect repellent must be used on the beehive every time, otherwise the bees will have returned and no wax will be collected.

It is also used on large mosquitoes and mosquito swarms encountered in the Tai Bwo Wannai Cleanup minigame to halve their combat stats and prevent them from attacking for six seconds. This can be done multiple times until their stats are reduced to 1. Giant mosquitoes found on Mos Le'Harmless are unaffected.
30:
A bucket of wax is obtained by interacting with a beehive in the apiary south of Seers' Village, west of Catherby. The player must have an empty bucket in their inventory, and either wear full beekeeper's outfit or use insect repellent on the beehive first. This process must be repeated per bucket of wax. It is used in the Merlin's Crystal and Troll Romance quests.

There is a bucket spawn right beside the gate of the apiary.

In the Merlin's Crystal quest, Morgan Le Faye tells the player how to release Merlin in exchange for sparing Sir Mordred's life, requiring a black candle among other things. The Candle maker in Catherby offers to make one for the player if they bring him a bucket of wax.

In the Troll Romance quest, swamp tar is used on a bucket of wax with a cake tin in the inventory to make wax. The wax is then used on the sled, so that players can slide down Trollweiss Mountain to get to the trollweiss they need to pick.
32:
A black candle is a light source used in the Merlin's Crystal quest.

During Merlin's Crystal, in exchange for sparing Sir Mordred's life, Morgan Le Faye details how to free Merlin, requiring a black candle among other things. The Candle maker in Catherby offers to make one if the player brings him a bucket of wax. Once all the other items are obtained, it is lit with a tinderbox when inside the magical symbol, inside the fence on the north-east side of Camelot Castle. After the remaining items are used, and with the correct incantation, Thrantax the Mighty is summoned for the player to command to free Merlin.

Black candles can not be purchased from the Candle maker after Merlin's Crystal, but multiple can be obtained during the quest. Although they aren't tradeable, they can be put in empty candle lanterns to make candle lanterns, which are tradeable.
34:
A lit candle is an unobtainable version of the Lit candle. Candles were previously tradeable and could be turned into banknotes. However, they were made untradeable due to an unfixable bug where trading a lit candle in a dark area would not update the lighting for either player. Any player who had a noted Lit candle was given this now discontinued item. Originally, the item was identical to the real lit candle, except being stackable.

As this change occurred prior to August 2007, the item has never been obtainable in Old School RuneScape.
35:
Excalibur is a one-handed sword and a quest item obtained from the Merlin's Crystal quest and used in the Holy Grail quest. It requires 20 Attack to wield and has similar stats to the adamant longsword, except for 6 less strength bonus and 1 more magic defence.

In the Merlin's Crystal quest, the player must use Excalibur on the crystal to smash and free Merlin. It is obtained from Lady of the Lake after she tests the purity of the player's spirit when giving a beggar bread at Grum's Gold Exchange in Port Sarim.

In the Holy Grail quest, Excalibur must be equipped as the Black Knight Titan dies in order to enter the Fisher Realm and be able to continue the quest. If another weapon is equipped when he dies, the fight will restart.

Low level players may find Excalibur useful for combat because of its stats, low requirements to obtain and wield, and is free the first time.

If lost, it can be retrieved from the Lady of the Lake in Taverley for 500 coins.
36:
A candle is the lowest tier of Firemaking light sources. It can be lit with a tinderbox. Lit candles can be extinguished by clicking extinguish on them or falling into swamp water in the Lumbridge Caves. Candles may be acquired through various means such as finding them within certain houses, purchasing them from a candle seller or candle maker, or by trading with other players.

A candle is a required item for Enlightened Journey and Enakhra's Lament.
38:
A black candle is a light source used in the Merlin's Crystal quest.

During Merlin's Crystal, in exchange for sparing Sir Mordred's life, Morgan Le Faye details how to free Merlin, requiring a black candle among other things. The Candle maker in Catherby offers to make one if the player brings him a bucket of wax. Once all the other items are obtained, it is lit with a tinderbox when inside the magical symbol, inside the fence on the north-east side of Camelot Castle. After the remaining items are used, and with the correct incantation, Thrantax the Mighty is summoned for the player to command to free Merlin.

Black candles can not be purchased from the Candle maker after Merlin's Crystal, but multiple can be obtained during the quest. Although they aren't tradeable, they can be put in empty candle lanterns to make candle lanterns, which are tradeable.
39:
Bronze arrowtips are made with a bronze bar requiring 5 Smithing, yielding 12.5 Smithing experience and 15 bronze arrowtips. They are made into bronze arrows when used with headless arrows, requiring 1 Fletching, yielding 19.5 Fletching experience per 15 arrows.

They are purchased for 1 coin at the ranging shops: Hickton's Archery Emporium in Catherby, Armoury in the Combat Training Camp, Dargaud's Bow and Arrows in the Ranging Guild, Gulluck and Sons on the 2nd floor of the Grand Tree, and Void Knight Archery Store at the Void Knights' Outpost.
40:
Iron arrowtips are made with an iron bar requiring 20 Smithing, yielding Smithing 25 experience and 15 iron arrowtips. They are made into iron arrows when used with headless arrows, requiring 15 Fletching, yielding 37.5 experience per 15 arrows.

They are purchased for 2 coins at the ranging shops: Hickton's Archery Emporium in Catherby, Dargaud's Bow and Arrows in the Ranging Guild, Gulluck and Sons on the 2nd floor of the Grand Tree, Void Knight Archery Store at the Void Knights' Outpost, and Ava's Odds and Ends in Draynor Manor. They are purchased for 3 coins at the Armoury in the Combat Training Camp.
41:
Steel arrowtips are made with a steel bar requiring 35 Smithing, yielding 37.5 Smithing experience and 15 steel arrowtips. They are made into steel arrows when used with headless arrows, requiring 30 Fletching, yielding 75 experience per 15 arrows.

At 47 Thieving, they can be stolen from chests in Hemenster, Rellekka, and West Ardougne.

There is an item spawn in the northern section of the Edgeville Dungeon at level 10 Wilderness by the earth warriors.

They are purchased for 6 coins at the ranging shops: Hickton's Archery Emporium in Catherby, Dargaud's Bow and Arrows in the Ranging Guild, Gulluck and Sons on the 2nd floor of the Grand Tree, and Void Knight Archery Store at the Void Knights' Outpost. They are purchased for 7 coins at Ava's Odds and Ends in Draynor Manor, and they are also purchased for 9 coins at the Armoury in the Combat Training Camp.
42:
Mithril arrowtips are made with a mithril bar requiring 55 Smithing, yielding 50 Smithing experience and 15 mithril arrowtips. They are made into mithril arrows when used with headless arrows, requiring 45 Fletching, yielding 112.5 experience per 15 arrows.

They are purchased for 16 coins at the ranging shops: Hickton's Archery Emporium in Catherby, Dargaud's Bow and Arrows in the Ranging Guild, Gulluck and Sons on the 2nd floor of the Grand Tree, and Void Knight Archery Store at the Void Knights' Outpost. They are purchased for 24 coins at the Armoury in the Combat Training Camp.
43:
Adamant arrowtips are made with an adamant bar requiring 75 Smithing, yielding 62.5 Smithing experience and 15 adamant arrowtips. They are made into adamant arrows when used with headless arrows, requiring 60 Fletching, yielding 150 experience per 15 arrows.

They are purchased for 40 coins at the ranging shops: Hickton's Archery Emporium in Catherby, Dargaud's Bow and Arrows in the Ranging Guild, and Void Knight Archery Store at the Void Knights' Outpost.
44:
Rune arrowtips are made with a runite bar requiring 90 Smithing, yielding 75 Smithing experience and 15 rune arrowtips. They are made into rune arrows when used with headless arrows, requiring 75 Fletching, yielding 187.5 experience per 15 arrows.

They are purchased for 200 coins at the ranging shops: Hickton's Archery Emporium in Catherby, Dargaud's Bow and Arrows in the Ranging Guild, and Void Knight Archery Store at the Void Knights' Outpost.
45:
Opal bolt tips are created by using a chisel on a cut opal with 11 Fletching, yielding 1.5 Fletching experience and 12 opal bolt tips.

They are made into opal bolts when used with bronze bolts, requiring 11 Fletching, yielding 16 Fletching experience per 10 bolts. They can also be made into opal dragon bolts, requiring 84 Fletching, yielding 16 Fletching experience per 10 bolts. Both of these can then be enchanted into opal bolts (e) and opal dragon bolts (e) respectively.
46:
Pearl bolt tips are created by using a chisel on an oyster pearl or oyster pearls with 41 Fletching, yielding 3.2 Fletching experience both, but 6 and 24 pearl bolt tips respectively.

They are made into pearl bolts when used with iron bolts, requiring 41 Fletching, yielding 32 Fletching experience per 10 bolts. They can also be made into pearl dragon bolts, requiring 84 Fletching, yielding 32 Fletching experience per 10 bolts. Both of these can then be enchanted into pearl bolts (e) and pearl dragon bolts (e) respectively.
48: A longbow (u) is made using a knife with logs, requiring 10 Fletching and yielding 10 Fletching experience. Stringing a longbow (u) with a bowstring makes a longbow, also requiring 10 Fletching and yielding an additional 10 Fletching experience.
50: A shortbow (u) is made using a knife with logs, requiring 5 Fletching and yielding 5 Fletching experience. Stringing a shortbow (u) with a bowstring makes a shortbow, also requiring 5 Fletching and yielding an additional 5 Fletching experience.
53:
A headless arrow is used in Fletching to make arrows. Attaching 15 feathers to 15 arrow shafts, requiring 1 Fletching, yields 15 Fletching experience and 15 headless arrows. 15 arrowtips can be attached to headless arrows to make arrows.

There are several item spawns of headless arrows in the Scorpion Pit, deep in the Wilderness.
54: An oak shortbow (u) is made using a knife with oak logs, requiring 20 Fletching and yielding 16.5 Fletching experience. Stringing an oak shortbow (u) with a bowstring makes an oak shortbow, also requiring 20 Fletching and yielding an additional 16.5 Fletching experience.
56: An Oak longbow (u) is made using a knife with oak logs, requiring level 25 Fletching and yielding 25 Fletching experience. Stringing an oak longbow (u) with a bowstring makes an oak longbow, also requiring 25 Fletching and yielding an additional 25 experience.
58: A willow longbow (u) is made using a knife with willow logs, requiring 40 Fletching and yielding 41.5 Fletching experience. Stringing a willow longbow (u) with a bowstring makes a willow longbow, also requiring 40 Fletching and yielding an additional 41.5 experience.
60: A willow shortbow (u) is made using a knife with willow logs, requiring 35 Fletching and yielding 33.3 Fletching experience. Stringing a willow shortbow (u) with a bowstring makes a willow shortbow, also requiring 35 Fletching and yielding an additional 33.3 Fletching experience.
62: A maple longbow (u) is made using a knife with maple logs, requiring 55 Fletching and yielding 58.3 Fletching experience. Stringing a maple longbow (u) with a bowstring makes a maple longbow, also requiring 55 Fletching and yielding an additional 58.2 Fletching experience.
64: A maple shortbow (u) is made using a knife with maple logs, requiring 50 Fletching and yielding 50 Fletching experience. Stringing a maple shortbow (u) with a bowstring makes a maple shortbow, also requiring 50 Fletching and yielding an additional 50 Fletching experience.
66: A yew longbow (u) is made using a knife with yew logs, requiring 70 Fletching and yielding 75 Fletching experience. Stringing a yew longbow (u) with a bowstring makes a yew longbow, also requiring 70 Fletching and yielding an additional 75 Fletching experience.
68: A yew shortbow (u) is made using a knife with yew logs, requiring 65 Fletching and yielding 67.5 Fletching experience. Stringing a yew shortbow (u) with a bowstring makes a yew shortbow, also requiring 65 Fletching and yielding an additional 67.5 Fletching experience.
70: A magic longbow (u) is made using a knife with magic logs, requiring 85 Fletching and yielding 91.5 Fletching experience. Stringing a magic longbow (u) with a bowstring makes a magic longbow, also requiring 85 Fletching and yielding an additional 91.5 Fletching experience.
72: A magic shortbow (u) is made using a knife with magic logs, requiring level 80 Fletching and yielding 83.3 Fletching experience. Stringing a magic shortbow (u) with a bowstring makes a magic shortbow, also requiring 80 Fletching and yielding an additional 83.3 Fletching experience.
74:
A Khazard helmet is a quest item in the Fight Arena quest. It is a dark coloured medium helmet that is part of the Khazard armour set. It has stats similar to an iron med helm, except unlike most medium helmets, it does not have a penalty to Magic, making it a viable choice for mages and rangers.

In the Fight Arena quest, a Khazard helmet and Khazard armour can only be found by searching the chest in a building north of the Fight Arena. They both must be worn to enter the Khazard prisons. Unequipping either the helmet or armour inside the jail causes the guards to kick the player out.

If lost, it can be reobtained in the same chest. Multiple armour pieces can be obtained through the drop trick.
75:
A Khazard armour is a quest item in the Fight Arena quest. It is a dark coloured platebody that is part of the Khazard armour set. It has stats worse than a bronze platebody, but unlike most melee armours, it does not have a penalty to Magic or Ranged accuracy, nor does it interfere with Ava's devices, making it a viable choice for mages and rangers. It also weighs far less than a typical platebody. Another nearby quest item, Carnillean armour, has over double the stab defence and +3 slash defence bonuses, at the cost of -2 crush defence and nearly 20x the weight.

In the Fight Arena quest, a Khazard helmet and Khazard armour can only be found by searching the chest in a building north of the Fight Arena. They both must be worn to enter the Khazard prisons. Unequipping either the helmet or armour inside the jail causes the guards to kick the player out.

If lost, it can be reobtained in the same chest. Multiple armour pieces can be obtained through the drop trick.
76: Khazard cell keys are a quest item in the Fight Arena quest. They are obtained by giving a Khali brew to the Head Guard in the south-eastern room of the jail at the Fight Arena, north of Yanille. The keys are used to unlock the door to the cell that holds Sammy Servil prisoner.
77: Khali brew is a quest item in the Fight Arena quest. Once the player has spoken to the Head Guard in the south-eastern room of the jail, it is possible to buy the beer for 5 coins from the Khazard barman in the bar in the south-west corner of the Fight Arena. The Khazard barman suggests lying down before drinking it so there is less distance to collapse; however, there is no option for the player to drink it. Giving it to the Head Guard will get him drunk and allow you to steal the Khazard cell keys.
78:
Ice arrows are a quest item in the Temple of Ikov quest. They have the same Ranged Strength as steel arrows, but must be fired from a yew bow or better.

In the Temple of Ikov quest, they are collected randomly when searching chests in the eastern Temple of Ikov dungeon and required to defeat the Fire Warrior of Lesarkus. While not required, ice arrows can also be used to defeat Fareed from the Desert Treasure I quest, as all other ammunition will drop to the floor as ashes, bypassing the ammo-saving effect of Ava's devices.

Upon completion of the quest, players can still go back and obtain more should they desire it.
83:
The lever is a quest item in the Temple of Ikov quest. It is found in the eastern room in the Temple of Ikov after crossing the bridge which requires the player's weight to be below 0 kg (using boots of lightness or other weight-reducing clothing) to successfully cross. It is used to operate a broken lever which opens a door leading further into the temple.

After the quest, the item is still obtainable, but has no further use beyond the quest.
84:
The Staff of Armadyl is a quest item in the Temple of Ikov quest. If allied with Lucien, the staff of Armadyl is stolen from a table within the Temple of Ikov dungeon after killing a Guardian of Armadyl and brought to Lucien to complete the quest. If allied with the guardians, the player will receive an Armadyl pendant to equip and prove they are no longer allies of Lucien, then go and kill him.

Multiple copies of the staff cannot be obtained. The staff also cannot be telekinetically grabbed. If the staff is dropped and then the quest is completed, attempting to pick up the staff will yield the message: "You have completed the quest of the Temple of Ikov."

However, by dying while carrying the staff, it can be sent to Death’s Domain. This allows the player to take another staff, and any extra staves stored there will remain when the quest is completed.

A replica of the staff is on display at the Varrock Museum after explaining what it looks like to the museum curator on the 1st floor with the quest complete.
85: The shiny key is obtainable after partial completion of the Temple of Ikov quest, found at the end of the Temple of Ikov dungeon. It is used to take the shortcut from the house in McGrubor's Wood to the lesser demon area of the Temple of Ikov dungeon. It can be placed on the steel key ring.
87:
The Armadyl pendant is a quest item in the Temple of Ikov quest. A Guardian of Armadyl in the Temple of Ikov dungeon gives the player the pendant if the player sides with them. Equipping it allows players to attack Lucien, once he is defeated, the quest is complete.

This pendant is the easiest obtainable protection against Armadyl and followers of Armadyl in the God Wars Dungeon.

If lost, it can be reobtained by:

Talk to a Guardian of Armadyl if sided with Guardians of Armadyl during the quest.

Killing a Guardian of Armadyl if sided with Lucien during the quest.

A shiny key is needed for the fastest method. Down the ladder of the house in McGrubor's Wood, fairy ring ALS, walk west until there is a wall with the "Push" option. Depending on alignment, kill or talk to a Guardian for a replacement pendant.

Multiple Armadyl pendants can be obtained through the drop trick.
88: Boots of lightness reduce weight by 4.535 kg when worn, and offer slight defensive bonuses. As they are easy to obtain in bulk, they may be safely used in the wilderness. While they grant a higher weight-reduction than the graceful boots, they do not give an increase to run energy restoration rate.
89: Boots of lightness reduce weight by 4.535 kg when worn, and offer slight defensive bonuses. As they are easy to obtain in bulk, they may be safely used in the wilderness. While they grant a higher weight-reduction than the graceful boots, they do not give an increase to run energy restoration rate.
91: A guam potion (unf) is an unfinished potion made by using a guam leaf on a vial of water, requiring 3 Herblore. Using an eye of newt on a guam potion (unf) with 3 Herblore yields an attack potion (3) and 25 Herblore experience. In the Watchtower quest, using Jangerberries on a guam potion (unf) with 14 Herblore yields a vial (jangerberries and guam leaf) and 10 Herblore experience.
93: A marrentill potion (unf) is an unfinished potion made by using a marrentill on a vial of water, requiring 5 Herblore. Using a unicorn horn dust on a marrentill potion (unf) with 5 Herblore yields an antipoison(3) and 37.5 Herblore experience. In the Bone Voyage quest, a marrentill potion (unf) and 2 vodka are given to the Apothecary for a potion of sealegs.
95: A tarromin potion (unf) is an unfinished potion made by using a tarromin on a vial of water, requiring 12 Herblore. Using a limpwurt root on a tarromin potion (unf) with 12 Herblore yields a Strength potion(3) and 50 Herblore experience. In the Shades of Mort'ton quest, after reading the diary of Herbi Flax, using ashes on a tarromin potion (unf) with 15 Herblore yields a Serum 207 (3) and 50 Herblore experience. In the Grim Tales quest, using shrunk ogleroot on a tarromin potion (unf) with 52 Herblore yields a Shrink-me-quick and 6 Herblore experience.
97: A harralander potion (unf) is an unfinished potion made by using a harralander on a vial of water, requiring 22 Herblore. Using a volcanic ash on a harralander potion (unf) with 22 Herblore yields a compost potion(3) and 60 Herblore experience. Using a red spiders' eggs on a harralander potion (unf) with 22 Herblore yields a restore potion(3) and 62.5 Herblore experience. Using blamish snail slime on a harralander potion (unf) with 25 Herblore yields blamish oil and 80 Herblore experience. Using a chocolate dust on a harralander potion (unf) with 26 Herblore yields an energy potion(3) and 67.5 Herblore experience. Using a goat horn dust on a harralander potion (unf) with 36 Herblore yields a combat potion(3) and 84 Herblore experience.
105: A kwuarm potion (unf) is an unfinished potion made by using a kwuarm on a vial of water, requiring 55 Herblore. Using a limpwurt root on a kwuarm potion (unf) with 55 Herblore yields a super strength(3) and 125 Herblore experience. Using a dragon scale dust on a kwuarm potion (unf) with 60 Herblore yields weapon poison and 137.5 Herblore experience.
109: A dwarf weed potion (unf) is an unfinished potion made by using a dwarf weed on a vial of water, requiring 72 Herblore. Using a wine of Zamorak on a dwarf weed potion (unf) with 72 Herblore yields a ranging potion(3) and 162.5 Herblore experience. Using nihil dust on a dwarf weed potion (unf) with 85 Herblore yields an ancient brew(3) and 190 Herblore experience. Using a lily of the sands on a dwarf weed potion (unf) with 88 Herblore yields a Menaphite remedy(3) and 200 Herblore experience.
111: A torstol potion (unf) is an unfinished potion made by using a torstol on a vial of water, requiring 78 Herblore. Using jangerberries on a torstol potion (unf) with 78 Herblore yields a Zamorak brew(3) and 175 Herblore experience. Using a super attack, super strength, and super defence on a torstol potion (unf) with 90 Herblore yields a super combat potion(4) and 150 Herblore experience. Using an anti-venom(4) on a torstol potion (unf) with 94 Herblore yields an anti-venom+(4) and 125 Herblore experience. Using a demonic tallow on a torstol potion (unf) with 81 Herblore yields a surge potion(3) and 185 Herblore experience.
113:
A Strength potion is a potion that can be made by free-to-play players in addition to members. Both non-members and members can make a strength potion (4) by providing the Apothecary in Varrock with 5 coins, a limpwurt root, and red spiders' eggs. Members who have attained at least level 12 Herblore additionally have the ability to use a limpwurt root on a tarromin potion (unf), yielding a Strength potion(3) and 50 Herblore experience. A dose of Strength potion provides a temporary skill boost to Strength equal to 3 + 10% of the player's current Strength level, rounded down. This is less than the super Strength's and super combat potion's boost of 5 + 15% of the player's current Strength level, rounded down.

After Barbarian Herblore Training, roe or caviar can be added to a Strength potion(2), requiring 14 Herblore, yielding a Strength mix and 17 Herblore experience. A Strength mix has 2 doses, boosts Strength equal to 3 + 10% of the player's current Strength level, rounded down, and heals 3 Hitpoints.

A Strength potion(2) can occasionally be obtained from a chest inside the maze random event.

A Strength potion(3) can be purchased from the Warriors' Guild potion shop for 15 coins.

A Strength potion(4) is a reward from Jekyll and Hyde random events if a guam leaf is given to Dr Jekyll. If the player talks to Dr Jekyll and does not give a herb, then Dr Jekyll gives a Strength potion(2).

Having the Apothecary make a Strength potion is a requirement for completing the medium Varrock Diary and creating a Strength potion in the The Deeper Lode pub in Lovakengj is a requirement for completing the easy Kourend & Kebos Diary.

121:
An attack potion is a potion made by using an eye of newt on a guam potion (unf), requiring 3 Herblore, yielding an attack potion(3) and 25 Herblore experience. It is the first available potion to make with the Herblore skill. A dose of attack potion provides a temporary skill boost to Attack equal to 3 + 10% of the player's current Attack level, rounded down. This is less than the super attack's boost of 5 + 15% of the player's current Attack level, rounded down.

After Barbarian Herblore Training, roe or caviar can be added to an attack potion(2), requiring 4 Herblore, yielding an attack mix and 8 Herblore experience. An attack mix has 2 doses, boosts Attack equal to 3 + 10% of the player's current Attack level, rounded down, and heals 3 Hitpoints per dose.

A Defence potion(4) is a reward from Jekyll and Hyde random events if a toadflax is given to Dr Jekyll.

A Defence potion (3) or (4) is used in the A Kingdom Divided quest.

157:
A super strength is a potion made by using a limpwurt root on a kwuarm potion (unf), requiring 55 Herblore, yielding a super strength(3) and 125 Herblore experience. A dose of super strength provides a temporary skill boost to Strength equal to 5 + 15% of the player's current Strength level, rounded down.

Super strength along with super attacks are popular for player killing, bossing, Slayer, or melee training. The dragon battleaxe special may be preferable for melee training because it provides a similar boost while being much cheaper in the long run.

Crystal dust may be added to super strength, 1 dust per dose of potion, to make a divine super strength potion, requiring 70 Herblore.

A super strength(4), super attack(4), super defence(4), and a torstol can be combined to make a super combat potion, requiring 90 Herblore.

After Barbarian Herblore Training, caviar can be added to a super strength(2), requiring 59 Herblore, yielding a super str. mix and 42 Herblore experience. A super str. mix has 2 doses, boosts Strength equal to 5 + 15% of the player's current Strength level, rounded down, and heals 6 Hitpoints.

A super strength(4) is a reward from Jekyll and Hyde random events if a snapdragon is given to Dr Jekyll.

175:
An antipoison is a potion made by using unicorn horn dust on a marrentill potion (unf), requiring 5 Herblore, yielding an antipoison(3) and 37.5 Herblore experience. A dose of antipoison cures poison and provides immunity to poison for 90 seconds. Drinking two doses of antipoison will cure venom. The first dose will reduce the venom to poison and the second will remove the poison.

The next cheapest alternative, superantipoison, cures poison and provides immunity for 6 minutes.

After Barbarian Herblore Training, roe or caviar can be added to an antipoison(2), requiring 6 Herblore, yielding an antipoison mix and 12 Herblore experience. An antipoison mix has 2 doses, cures poison and provides immunity to poison for 90 seconds, and heals 3 Hitpoints.

181:
A superantipoison is a potion made by using unicorn horn dust on an irit potion (unf), requiring 48 Herblore, yielding a superantipoison(3) and 106.3 Herblore experience. A dose of superantipoison cures poison and provides poison immunity for 6 minutes. Drinking two doses of superantipoison will cure venom. The first dose will reduce the venom to poison and the second will remove the poison.

A superantipoison(1) can be found in the southern most collapsed building north-east of the Observatory, near the entrance to the Observatory Dungeon with a respawn time of 55 seconds.

Creating a superantipoison from scratch in the Seers' Village/Catherby area is a requirement for the medium Kandarin Diary.

After Barbarian Herblore Training is completed, caviar can be added to a superantipoison(2) to produce an anti-poison supermix. This requires 51 Herblore and provides 35 Herblore experience. An anti-poison supermix has 2 doses, each of which heals 6 Hitpoints in addition to the normal superantipoison immunity.
