See the finding the water source section of the Legends' Quest guide.
746:
The dark dagger is a quest item obtained during Legends' Quest. It is given to the player by the entity Echned Zekin. The dagger can then either be given to Ugandulu for a one-use Holy force spell, or used to kill Viyeldi which converts the dagger into a glowing dagger. It is then given to Echned, who turns out to be the demon.

If players have misplaced their glowing dagger after the quest, it can be reclaimed from Radimus Erkle, and can be investigated via-right click afterwards to switch its appearance between a dark or glowing dagger.

It has the same stats as an iron dagger albeit without a strength bonus.
747:
The glowing dagger is a quest item obtained and used during the Legends' Quest. It has the same combat stats as an iron dagger, only lacking the +4 strength bonus.

It is created when players are given the dark dagger by Echned Zekin, requesting them to kill Viyeldi because he was the one that murdered him and wants revenge. Once the dagger is used to kill Viyeldi, it will convert into a glowing dagger. It can then be taken back to Echned Zekin, who will reveal his true form - the demon Nezikchened. Alternatively, it can be taken to Ungadulu.

Players can obtain another glowing dagger after the quest by speaking to Radimus Erkle in the Legends' Guild, and can be investigated via-right click afterwards to switch its appearance between a dark or glowing dagger.
748:
Holy force is an item that players receive during the Legends' Quest by showing Ungadulu the dark dagger. Players must use it to reveal the true form of Echned Zekin (which is that of the demon Nezikchened) and to prevent him from draining their prayer.

This item does not have any use following the Legends' Quest, and can be re-obtained by using another dark dagger or glowing dagger on Ungadulu. This no longer works after quest completion.
749:
The yommi totem is a quest item used during the Legends' Quest to replace the evil totem in the centre of the Kharazi Jungle. It may be cut from a yommi tree, grown from yommi tree seeds in the fertile soil just north-west of the pool of pure water.

Players must be quick in producing the yommi totem in order to prevent the tree from rotting. If the tree does rot, players may ask Ungadulu for more seeds to restart the production process.

While yommi tree seeds are not obtainable after completing the quest, any seeds left over from the quest will still work and another yommi tree can be grown, allowing the player to obtain another totem. However, it is useless at this point, and it cannot be used to replace the evil totem pole again (because the totem pole is no longer cursed after it is replaced in the quest).
751:
Gnomeballs are received by winning 5 points in a game of Gnome Ball, from the gnome restaurant minigame, or as a drop from dolphins. With the item in your inventory, you can click "Use" with it, and click another player. If that player has their right hand empty, they will catch the ball, and it will end up in their weapon slot. It is not advised that you throw it to a player you do not know, as they can very easily walk away with it.

Gnomeballs cannot be used on or by Ironman Mode players.
757:
Books are items obtained in quests and elsewhere in Old School RuneScape. Most books can be read by players, which provides information ranging from lore to information on game mechanics.

When a player reads a book, an interface will appear to display the book's contents, and their character will be seen reading a green (sometimes yellow) book.
758:
The Phoenix hq key was an item used in the first months of RuneScape during the Shield of Arrav quest to access the Phoenix Gang's headquarters. Previously, after delivering the Intel report to Straven, two keys would be received. The quest was silently reworked in a hidden update several months after release; the key was removed in favour of Straven not letting players enter the hideout if they had not joined the gang. At the time of its release, it was tradeable, since non-tradeable items did not exist during 2001.

This item was previously named just "Key" until the Varrock update, when it was renamed to "Phoenix hq key", possibly to avoid confusion with other keys.

As it was discontinued long before 2007, it has never been obtainable in Old School RuneScape. Despite this, the item's examine was updated in 2015.
763:
The broken shield is one of the two halves of the restored Shield of Arrav.

In the Shield of Arrav quest, the player must combine both parts of the broken shield to get the complete shield. One player must join the Black Arm Gang and retrieve the right half from a cupboard upstairs in the base. The other player must be in the Phoenix Gang and must get the left half from the chest in the underground base.
765:
The broken shield is one of the two halves of the restored Shield of Arrav.

In the Shield of Arrav quest, the player must combine both parts of the broken shield to get the complete shield. One player must join the Black Arm Gang and retrieve the right half from a cupboard upstairs in the base. The other player must be in the Phoenix Gang and must get the left half from the chest in the underground base.
767:
The Phoenix crossbow is a quest item, although it can be traded. It has the same stats as a regular crossbow except for attack range, but weighs significantly less. It can be obtained and is used in the quest Shield of Arrav. The Phoenix crossbow has no requirements to wield, and can only fire bronze bolts. It can also be used with a mith grapple for Agility shortcuts.

The Phoenix crossbow is not often used, as the bronze crossbow requires the same Ranged level to equip, but gives a Ranged accuracy of +18, whilst the Phoenix crossbow only gives +6. However, the Phoenix crossbow is essentially free, and since bronze crossbows and above are members-only items, the Phoenix crossbow is the second-best crossbow available to free-to-play players. While the Phoenix crossbow is lighter than and has the same +6 range bonus as the standard crossbow, the Phoenix crossbow has a maximum range of 7 tiles, whereas the standard crossbow has a range of 10 tiles.
773:
A 'perfect' ring is a quest item in the Family Crest quest. It is made with a 'perfect' gold bar, ruby, and ring mould at a furnace, requiring 40 Crafting and yielding 70 Crafting experience. A 'perfect' ring and 'perfect' necklace are given to Avan in exchange for his crest part.

It is possible to mine 'perfect' gold and craft 'perfect' jewellery without speaking to Boot, but he must be spoken to in order to give the jewellery to Avan.

More of them can be crafted after or during the quest, but they have no use, offering no stat bonuses and are unable to be Lvl-3 Enchanted into a ring of forging.
774:
A 'perfect' necklace is a quest item in the Family Crest quest. It is made with a 'perfect' gold bar, ruby, and necklace mould at a furnace, requiring 40 Crafting and yielding 75 Crafting experience. A 'perfect' necklace and 'perfect' ring are given to Avan in exchange for his crest part.

It is possible to mine 'perfect' gold and craft 'perfect' jewellery without speaking to Boot, but he must be spoken to in order to give the jewellery to Avan.

More of them can be crafted after or during the quest, but they have no use, offering no stat bonuses and are unable to be Lvl-3 Enchanted into a Digsite pendant.
775:
Cooking gauntlets are a pair of gloves available after completing the Family Crest quest, along with the goldsmith and chaos gauntlets. The gauntlets, when worn, significantly decrease the likelihood of burning lobsters, swordfish, cooked kyatt, monkfish, sharks, and anglerfish when cooking them. They do not work on other types of food.

Players can obtain the cooking gauntlets by bringing the steel gauntlets that were rewarded from the quest to Caleb in or around the house north of the archery shop in Catherby. (Note: if your gauntlets have a different enchantment on them already, Caleb will charge you 25,000 coins).

The text that appears when you give your gauntlets to Caleb is: "Caleb takes the gauntlets from you, pours some herbs and seasonings on them, bakes them on his range for a short period of time, and then hands them back to you."

Prior to completing the Family Pest miniquest, if lost, they are re-obtained free of charge from Dimintheis. After completion of the Family Pest, they can be claimed from Caleb for free at any time and without the need for steel gauntlets; and all forms of the Family Crest gauntlets can be owned simultaneously. They can also be claimed in free-to-play worlds but cannot be equipped in free-to-play.

The gauntlets cannot be taken to Entrana.

Fishing and cooking 5 sharks with the cooking gauntlets in Catherby is a requirement for the Kandarin elite diary.

The Cooking cape is strictly superior to and supersedes the cooking gauntlets, meaning the latter no longer need to be used once a player reaches level 99 Cooking. Nonetheless, they should not be discarded, as they are a requirement for a master clue step from Falo the Bard.
777:
Chaos gauntlets are a pair of gloves available after completing the Family Crest quest, along with the goldsmith and cooking gauntlets. The gauntlets, when worn, increase the maximum damage done by all bolt spells by 3 (before the boosted damage is multiplied by Magic Damage stats), thus making the max hit of bolt spells only 1 below that of blast spells and Inferior Demonbane. There are no requirements to wear these gloves.

Players can obtain the chaos gauntlets by bringing the steel gauntlets that were rewarded from the quest to Johnathon, located upstairs in the Jolly Boar Inn, which is north-east of Varrock. (Note: if your gauntlets have a different enchantment on them already, Johnathon will charge you 25,000 coins).

The text that appears when you give your gauntlets to Johnathon is: "Johnathon takes your gauntlets from you, and begins a low chant over them. You see them glow and sparkle, before he returns them to you."

Prior to completing the Family Pest miniquest, if lost, they are re-obtained free of charge from Dimintheis. After completion of the Family Pest, they can be claimed from Johnathon for free at any time and without the need for steel gauntlets; and all forms of the Family Crest gauntlets can be owned simultaneously. They can also be claimed in free-to-play worlds but cannot be equipped in free-to-play.

Upon death, they will be lost unless they are a protected item.
779:
The crest parts are items obtained during the Family Crest quest. Each part is owned by one of three Fitzharmon brothers, who have all left their family home. Each brother took a separate piece of the crest with him to prevent the other two brothers from inheriting the family fortune.

The player must complete a set of tasks for each of the brothers as follows:

Caleb (Catherby): Collect five different cooked fish: swordfish, bass, tuna, salmon, and shrimp

Avan (Al Kharid); Make a 'perfect' ring and 'perfect' necklace.

Johnathon (Varrock): Defeat the demon Chronozon in Edgeville Dungeon.

Once the player has all three crest pieces, they can be combined to make the whole family crest, which can then be given back to Dimintheis Fitzharmon, the boys' father, in Varrock.
780:

Once the player has all three crest pieces, they can be combined to make the whole family crest, which can then be given back to Dimintheis Fitzharmon, the boys' father, in Varrock.
781:

782:
The Family crest is a quest item obtained during the Family Crest quest. It is made by combining the three crest parts given to the player by the Fitzharmon brothers, Avan, Caleb, and Johnathon, in return for performing a set of tasks for each brother.

If a player tries to put the crest back together with only two pieces, they will receive a message saying You still need one more piece of the crest.

The completed family crest must be returned to Dimintheis Fitzharmon, the brothers' father, in Varrock to complete the quest. You can obtain multiple crests, the 1st crest part from Caleb can be obtained through drop tick, the 2nd crest from Avan is not until you get the 3rd crest part by defeating Chronozon, the 3rd crest part can be obtained multiple times by killing Chronozon only during the quest. Dimintheis Fitzharmon takes all crests from your bank and inventory.
784:
The Translation book, or Gnome-English Translation Dictionary, is a book written by Anita. It is obtained during The Grand Tree quest to help players translate what Hazelmere, who only speaks in the Gnomic tongue, is telling them. It is also used to help solve a puzzle later in the quest. During The Eyes of Glouphrie however, players don't need the book to talk to Hazelmere, as he will use magic to communicate with the player instead.

After completing the quest, players can reclaim the book from their bookcase in their player-owned house under the name 'Gnome Translation Dictionary'.

The book is also required for the Monkey Madness II quest and can be obtained from King Narnode Shareen after showing him the scrawled note.
785:
Glough's journal is found during The Grand Tree quest by searching a cupboard within Glough's house. The journal looks a little deeper into the mind and motives of Glough the gnome. It's used as a key piece of evidence as to what he's planning.

After finishing the quest, the book can be found on the shelves in your house.

Item can be safely discarded after quest completion.
786:
Hazelmere's scroll is an item used during The Grand Tree. Players obtain it by using the bark sample on Hazelmere. Hazelmere writes on the scroll in gnome language, and gives it to the player.

Players must then deliver this message back to King Narnode Shareen.

Item can be safely discarded after quest completion.
787:
The lumber order is a quest item that is part of The Grand Tree quest.

It is an order from Glough, who intends to build up a gnome army to wipe out humans. Players obtain it from a foreman in the Karamja ship yard, either by talking to him or killing him.

Players will also need to obtain Glough's invasion plans, and take both pieces of evidence to King Narnode Shareen.

Item can be safely discarded after quest completion.
788:
Glough's key is an item used during The Grand Tree quest. It opens a chest in Glough's home just south of the Grand Tree. The player finds invasion plans in the chest which can then be shown to King Narnode Shareen as evidence.

Players obtain this item by talking to Anita in the Tree Gnome Stronghold. Her home is in the north-west of the stronghold, just west of the swamp. The key has no use after the quest.
789:
Twigs are quest items used only in The Grand Tree quest. King Narnode Shareen gives all of the twigs to you. When placed on the pillars in Glough's house to spell out "TUZO" ("OPEN" in Ancient Gnomish), the trapdoor in Glough's house with open, and gives access to a secret passage into the roots of the Grand Tree.

There are four separate items, each bound in the shape of a different letter. The player must arrange them in the correct order on the barrels by the trapdoor in order to unlock it. After the quest, the trapdoor remains open, rendering the twigs useless.
790:
Twigs are quest items used only in The Grand Tree quest. King Narnode Shareen gives all of the twigs to you. When placed on the pillars in Glough's house to spell out "TUZO" ("OPEN" in Ancient Gnomish), the trapdoor in Glough's house with open, and gives access to a secret passage into the roots of the Grand Tree.

There are four separate items, each bound in the shape of a different letter. The player must arrange them in the correct order on the barrels by the trapdoor in order to unlock it. After the quest, the trapdoor remains open, rendering the twigs useless.

793:
A daconia rock is a magical rock that has been hidden in the roots of the Grand Tree in order to poison it.

The Daconia rocks were created by Hazelmere - allegedly as a precaution in case the Grand Tree should grow out of control, and are the only thing that can kill it. Players discover this precaution has been subverted in The Grand Tree quest.

Players find and remove one of these stones from the roots of the Grand Tree as the ultimate goal of The Grand Tree quest. Removing the last Daconia rock heals the Grand Tree and you get your reward. It is possible to drop trick this item to obtain a duplicate to keep after the quest.

You find out about the rocks by talking to Hazelmere. You will not understand him, but eventually you will communicate. He will take your bark sample, and after examining it he will give you a message. When translated using the translation book it reads:
796: The Exploding vial is an animation item used during the Watchtower. It is temporarily wielded during an animation if the player makes a mistake while creating the Magic ogre potion. Aside from this, it cannot be obtained.
798: The Grinder is an animation item used during Herblore. It is temporarily wielded during animations where the player uses a pestle and mortar. Aside from this, it cannot be obtained.
799:
A bank note or note is a stackable certificate that represents an item. It is equivalent in value to the item it represents, but cannot be used physically until exchanged for the real thing. Almost all tradeable items can be 'noted' and 'unnoted' in the bank interface, with very few exceptions (such as mysterious emblems).

Notes are useful for players who wish to trade large amounts of items at a time. They can also be used for training magic or for converting into coins via the Low or High Level Alchemy spells.
800: The bronze thrownaxe is a Ranged throwing weapon. There are no requirements to wield a bronze throwing axe. They can be obtained either by buying from the Tribal Weapons store at the Ranging Guild or trading with another player. The bronze throwing axe can be wielded with a shield or prayer book for protection.
802: The steel thrownaxe is a Ranged throwing weapon. To wield a steel throwing axe the player must have at least level 5 Ranged. They can be obtained either by buying from the Tribal Weapons store at the Ranging Guild or trading with another player. The steel throwing axe can be wielded with a shield or prayer book for protection.
803: The mithril thrownaxe is a Ranged throwing weapon. To wield a mithril throwing axe the player must have at least 20 Ranged. They can be obtained either by buying from the Tribal Weapons store at the Ranging Guild or trading with another player. The mithril throwing axe can be wielded with a shield or prayer book for protection.
804: The adamant thrownaxe is the third strongest type of thrownaxe, requiring level 30 Ranged to wield. They can be obtained by buying them from the Tribal Weapon Salesman in the Ranging Guild.
805:
The rune thrownaxe, like all thrownaxes, is a members-only Ranged throwing weapon and is the second most powerful type of throwing axe, behind the dragon thrownaxe. To wield a rune throwing axe the player must have at least 40 Ranged.

The door-supports that block access to lower floors of the Waterbirth Island Dungeon can be destroyed using a rune thrownaxe special attack on the middle support. As the doors usually require another player to open, players without level 85 Agility for the rocks shortcut to skip the doors often use one to reach the Dagannoth Kings conveniently.

The combat achievement From One King to Another requires the player to kill Dagannoth Prime using a rune thrownaxe special attack bounced off Dagannoth Rex.
807:
Iron darts are Ranged throwing weapons made from iron. Iron darts can be wielded at level 1 Ranged. They can be obtained by using the Smithing and Fletching skills or trading with another player. Iron darts can be poisoned and can be wielded with a shield or god book for protection.

To create iron darts the player must have completed the Tourist Trap quest and have at least level 19 Smithing and level 22 Fletching. Players can smith iron bars into iron dart tips. Each iron bar creates 10 iron dart tips and gives the player 25 Smithing experience. Feathers then must be added to create the iron darts. 3.8 Fletching experience is rewarded per iron dart fletched.
808:
Steel darts are Ranged throwing weapons. To wield steel darts, players must have at least level 5 Ranged. They can be obtained by either using the Smithing and Fletching skills or trading with another player. Steel darts can be poisoned and can be wielded with a shield or god book for protection.

To create steel darts, the player must have completed the Tourist Trap quest and have at least level 34 Smithing and level 37 Fletching. Each steel bar will create 10 steel dart tips and the player will receive 37.5 Smithing experience. When feathers are added the player will receive 10 steel darts and 7.5 Fletching experience per steel dart.

Steel darts have almost the same stats and speed as iron knives, which are often used for Ranged training at lower levels - however, they are far cheaper in price than iron knives due to people training Fletching.

A steel dart is one of the possible items requested by the rowdy dwarf during the Forgettable Tale quest.
809:
Mithril darts are Ranged throwing weapons made from mithril that are only available to members. Mithril darts require level 20 Ranged to wield. They can be obtained by either using the Smithing and Fletching skills or trading with another player. Mithril darts can be poisoned and can be wielded with a shield or god book for protection.

Mithril darts are one of the most cost effective Ranged training weapons for lower level players, as they have an extremely quick rate of fire and cost very little compared to similar training methods like throwing knives or arrows. They can be bought in large numbers from the Grand Exchange, costing less than half of what similar tier ranged ammunition costs.

To create mithril darts the player must have completed The Tourist Trap quest and have at least level 54 Smithing and level 52 Fletching. Players can smith mithril bars into mithril dart tips. Each mithril bar creates 10 mithril dart tips and gives the player 50 Smithing experience. Feathers or Stripy Feathers then must be added to create the mithril darts. 11.2 Fletching experience is rewarded per mithril dart.
810:
Adamant darts are Ranged throwing weapons. To wield the player must have at least 30 Ranged. They can be obtained by either using the Smithing and Fletching skills or trading with another player. Adamant darts can be poisoned and can be wielded with a shield or god book for protection.

To make adamant darts, the player must have completed the Tourist Trap quest and have at least 74 Smithing and 67 Fletching. Each adamant bar will create 10 adamant dart tips and the player will receive 62.5 Smithing experience. When feathers are added the player will receive 10 adamant darts and 15 Fletching experience per adamant dart.
811:
Rune darts are throwing weapons requiring level 40 Ranged to wield. They are created by combining rune dart tips with feathers. Rune darts can be poisoned and can be wielded with a shield or god book for protection.

To create rune darts the player must have completed the Tourist Trap quest and have at least level 89 Smithing and level 81 Fletching. Players can smith rune bars into rune dart tips. Each rune bar creates 10 rune dart tips and gives the player 75 Smithing experience. Feathers then must be added to create the rune darts. 18.8 Fletching experience is rewarded per rune dart.

Smithing and fletching 10 rune darts while in Varrock is required to complete the Elite Varrock Diary. Fletching a rune dart is required to complete a master clue scroll skill challenge assigned by Sherlock.

818:
The Poisoned dart(p) is an unobtainable item that was added during the RuneScape 2 beta. Its purpose is unknown; however, it may have been created in order to test poisoned darts in RuneScape 2, or as part of an interface.

The item briefly appeared in the search interface of the trading post. Aside from this, it has never been obtainable in Old School RuneScape.
819:
The bronze dart tip is a dart tip made with the Smithing skill. Players with at least 4 Smithing can smith 10 dart tips by using a bronze bar on an anvil with a hammer in their inventory. They can be fletched into bronze darts at level 10 Fletching when used with feathers, granting 18 Fletching experience per 10 darts made.

To smith darts, one must complete the Tourist Trap quest.
820:
The iron dart tip is a dart tip made with the Smithing skill. Players can craft this item using an iron bar on an anvil with a hammer in their inventory and a Smithing level of 19. Each iron bar creates 10 iron dart tips and gives the player 25 Smithing experience. They can be fletched into iron darts at level 22 Fletching when used with feathers, granting 38 Fletching experience per 10 darts made.

To smith darts, one must complete the Tourist Trap quest.
821:
The steel dart tip is a dart tip made with the Smithing skill. Players can craft this item when using a steel bar on an anvil with a hammer in their inventory and a Smithing level of 34. Smithing one set of 10 dart tips will provide the player with 37.5 Smithing experience. They can be fletched into steel darts at level 37 Fletching when used with feathers, granting 75 Fletching experience per 10 darts made.

To smith darts, one must complete the Tourist Trap quest.
822:
A mithril dart tip is a dart tip made with the Smithing skill. Players can smith this item when using a mithril bar on an anvil with a hammer in the inventory and 54 Smithing. Each bar makes 10 mithril dart tips and yields 50 experience. They can be fletched into mithril darts at level 52 Fletching when used with feathers, granting 112 Fletching experience per 10 darts made.

To smith darts, the Tourist Trap must be started and progressed to the point where the player returns to the Bedabin Camp with the weapon plans.
823:
Adamant dart tip is an item that can be created at level 74 Smithing. It grants 62.5 Smithing experience upon making and requires one adamantite bar to make 10 adamant dart tips. They can be fletched into adamant darts at level 67 Fletching when used with feathers, granting 150 Fletching experience per 10 darts made.

To smith darts, one must complete the Tourist Trap quest.
824:
The rune dart tip is a dart tip made with the Smithing skill. Players can craft this item by using a rune bar on an anvil with a hammer in the inventory and a Smithing level of 89. Each bar creates 10 dart tips, yielding 75 experience. They can be fletched into rune darts at level 81 Fletching when used with feathers, granting 188 Fletching experience per 10 darts made.

To smith darts, one must have completed the Tourist Trap quest.

Fletching a rune dart is required to complete a master clue scroll skill challenge assigned by Sherlock.
825:
The bronze javelin is a type of member's only Ranged ammunition used by the light and heavy ballistas. They are the weakest type of javelin. As with most javelins, they can be poisoned.

They can be fletched by attaching bronze javelin tips to javelin shafts at level 3 Fletching, granting 15 experience per 15 javelins made. They can also be obtained by buying them from the Ranging Guild, the Void Knight Archery Store or from Oobapohk's Javelin Store after Monkey Madness II.
826:
The iron javelin is a type of member's only Ranged ammunition used by the light and heavy ballistas. They are the second weakest type of javelin. As with most javelins, they can be poisoned.

They can be fletched by attaching iron javelin tips to javelin shafts at level 17 Fletching, granting 30 experience per 15 javelins made. They can also be obtained by buying them from the Ranging Guild, the Void Knight Archery Store or from Oobapohk's Javelin Store after Monkey Madness II.
827:
The steel javelin is a type of member's only Ranged ammunition used by the light and heavy ballistas. As with most javelins, they can be poisoned.

They can be fletched by attaching steel javelin tips to javelin shafts at level 32 Fletching, granting 75 experience per 15 javelins made. They can also be obtained by buying them from the Ranging Guild, the Void Knight Archery Store or from Oobapohk's Javelin Store after Monkey Madness II.
831:

833:

They can be fletched by attaching steel javelin tips to javelin shafts at level 32 Fletching, granting 75 experience per 15 javelins made. They can also be obtained by buying them from the Ranging Guild, the Void Knight Archery Store or from Oobapohk's Javelin Store after Monkey Madness II.
837:
The crossbow is the weakest type of crossbow, along with the Phoenix crossbow, and requires a Ranged level of 1 to wield. It can only fire bronze bolts and mith grapples. The crossbow and the bolts can be bought from Lowe's Archery Emporium in Varrock. There is a crossbow spawn in the Graveyard of Shadows, Bone Yard, and Hugor's house at Land's End (south-west of the Kourend Woodland).

It possesses the longest rapid-style attack range of any crossbow in the game, with 10 tiles.
839:
The basic longbow is a bow made from regular logs. It can be equipped at any Ranged level and can fire arrows up to iron. It has a longer range than its shortbow counterpart, but fires at a slower speed.

A longbow can be made at level 10 Fletching by using a knife on some logs to create a longbow (u), granting 10 experience, and then using a bowstring on the unstrung bow, granting another 10 experience.

Fletching a longbow from logs and bow string will profit −164 while fletching a longbow from a longbow (u) and bow string will profit −143.
841:
The shortbow is the weakest bow in Old School RuneScape and can use arrows up to iron. Players can purchase this bow from Lowe's Archery Emporium in Varrock.

Players are supplied with this bow along with several bronze arrows as their first ranged weapon on Tutorial Island.

Members can make a shortbow through the Fletching skill at level 5. First, a player must cut an unstrung shortbow from logs, granting 5 Fletching experience. Then, the player must string the unstrung shortbow with a bow string, granting 5 experience.
843:
The oak shortbow is a shortbow stronger than the standard shortbow that can use arrows up to steel. It requires a Ranged level of 5 or higher to wield.

Oak shortbows can be made at level 20 Fletching by using a knife on oak logs to cut them into an oak shortbow (u), granting 16.5 Fletching experience. Then, the player must string the unstrung oak shortbow with a bow string, granting another 16.5 experience.

Fletching an oak shortbow in the Tree Gnome Stronghold is a requirement for the Easy Western Provinces Diary.
845:
An oak longbow is a longbow made from oak. It can be made at level 25 Fletching by using a knife on oak logs to cut them into an oak longbow (u), granting 25 experience, and then using a bowstring on the unstrung bow, granting another 25 experience. It requires level 5 Ranged to wield and can fire arrows up to and including steel.

It has identical stats to the oak shortbow, but fires at a slower speed.

During the quest Ghosts Ahoy a player might acquire a signed oak bow which is exactly the same as the oak longbow, aside from its name.

Fletching an oak longbow from oak logs and a bow string will profit −154 while fletching an oak longbow from an oak longbow (u) and a bow string will profit −122.
849:
The willow shortbow is a two-handed ranged weapon stronger than the oak shortbow, but weaker than the maple shortbow. It can use arrows up to mithril. The willow shortbow requires a Ranged level of 20 or higher to wield. Players can purchase this bow from Lowe's Archery Emporium in Varrock.

Members can also make a willow shortbow through the Fletching skill at level 35. First, a player must cut an unstrung willow shortbow from willow logs, granting 33.3 Fletching experience. Then, the player must string the unstrung willow shortbow with a bow string, granting an additional 33.2 experience.
851:
A maple longbow is created by attaching a bow string to a maple longbow (u) with at least level 55 Fletching. Fletching from a maple log yields a total of 116.5 experience (58.3 for fletching and 58.2 for stringing). The bow can use arrows up to adamant and requires level 30 Ranged to wield.

The maple longbow differs from the shortbow only in terms of speed and attack range. However, the shortbow is preferred over the longbow due to its faster attack speed. It can also be a reward for the Observatory Quest.

Fletching a maple longbow from maple logs and a bow string will profit 99 while fletching a maple longbow from a maple longbow (u) and a bow string will profit 38.
853:
A maple shortbow is a two-handed Ranged weapon that can be created with the Fletching skill at level 50 by using a bow string on a maple shortbow (u), granting 50 experience. A Ranged level of 30 is required to wield it. The bow can use arrows up to adamant. However, this bow isn't powerful enough for the use of broad arrows.

It is notable for being the best bow that free-to-play players can use.
855:
The yew longbow is a longbow stronger than the maple longbow that can use arrows up to rune. The yew longbow requires a Ranged level of 40 or higher to wield.

Players can make a yew longbow through the Fletching skill at level 70. First, a player must cut a yew longbow (u) from yew logs, giving 75 Fletching experience. The unstrung bow is then strung with a bow string, for an additional 75 experience for a total of 150 experience a log. It can also be obtained as a very rare drop from a young impling.

Fletching a yew longbow from yew logs and a bow string will profit 290 while fletching a yew longbow from a yew longbow (u) and a bow string will profit 206.

Creating a yew longbow from scratch in Seers' Village is a task for the Kandarin hard diary.
857:
A yew shortbow is a two-handed ranged weapon stronger than the maple shortbow but weaker than the magic shortbow. It can be made with a Fletching level of 65 by using a yew shortbow (u) on some bow string, granting 67.5 experience when made, or 135 total experience when making one from scratch.

Fletching a yew shortbow from yew logs and a bow string will profit 67 coins while fletching a yew shortbow from a yew shortbow (u) and a bow string will profit 32 coins.

The bow requires level 40 Ranged to equip and can fire ammunition up to rune.

The yew shortbow can be combined with Scurrius' spine using a knife to create the bone shortbow, requiring 35 Fletching. Alternatively, Historian Aldo can do so for a fee of 50,000 coins.
859:
The magic longbow is a longbow fletched from magic logs. It requires a Ranged level of 50 to wield and can fire arrows up to amethyst.

Players can make a magic longbow with a Fletching level of 85 by cutting an unstrung magic longbow from magic logs, granting 91.5 Fletching experience, and then stringing unstrung magic longbow with a bow string, granting a further 91.5 experience.

Fletching a magic longbow from magic logs and a bow string will profit 202 while fletching a magic longbow from a magic longbow (u) and a bow string will profit 185.
861:
The Magic shortbow is a bow that requires level 50 Ranged in order to use and can fire arrows up to amethyst. It is one of the few shortbows in the game with a Special attack. The bow has an attack range of 7, with longrange increasing attack range by 2.

To make this bow, players must use a magic shortbow (u) on a bow string. This requires 80 Fletching, and grants 83 experience. They can also be received from hard clue scrolls, or as a rare drop from spiritual rangers.

The Magic shortbow can be imbued by using a magic shortbow scroll on it to make a magic shortbow (i). The imbue increases its ranged attack bonus to +75 and lowers the special attack cost to 50%.

The magic shortbow is often the most powerful ranged weapon available to mid-level players. Because of its fast attack speed and ability to fire rune and amethyst arrows, it is usually an effective ranged weapon for completing Slayer tasks. The rune crossbow is a viable alternative for players who desire a shield, the special effects of enchanted bolts, or the easy availability of broad bolts. The Dorgeshuun crossbow can also achieve very similar damage-per-second to a magic bow with lower-level arrows (such as steel arrows), due to its higher firing speed than normal crossbows, while using very cheap and easily-obtainable ammunition in the form of bone bolts.

Despite its low max hit, the magic shortbow is popular for player killing due to the ease of stacking its damage with a more powerful melee attack for a knockout blow.
863:
The iron knife is a throwing knife that does not require a Ranged level to wield. It is stronger than a bronze knife but weaker than a steel knife. To create iron knives, the player must have at least 22 Smithing. Each iron bar will create 5 iron knives and give the player 25 Smithing experience. They can be poisoned and can be wielded with a shield or god book for protection.

Throwing knives are among the fastest weapons in the game (along with darts), and are commonly used for PKing or training Ranged. Iron knives can be purchased from Martin Thwait's Lost and Found shop in the Rogues' Den with 50 Thieving and 50 Agility.
864:
Bronze knives are the lowest level throwing knives available, and do not require a Ranged level to wield. They can be poisoned, and due to being one-handed, can be wielded alongside a shield.

Bronze knives can be created from a bronze bar at level 7 Smithing. Each bar makes 5 knives, and grants the player 12.5 Smithing experience. The knives can also be purchased from Martin Thwait's Lost and Found shop in the Rogues' Den, requiring 50 Thieving and 50 Agility.

Throwing knives are among the fastest weapons in the game (along with darts), and are commonly used for player-killing, training Ranged, or tagging enemies for barraging.

877:
Bronze bolts are the weakest bolts, and may be shot from any crossbow.

Bronze bolts are crossbow bolts made out of bronze. To make them, a player must smith unfinished bronze bolts. This requires a Smithing level of 3, and for each bronze bar that player smiths they will get 10 unfinished bronze bolts and 12 Smithing experience. Then a player must attach flights to the bolts. Attaching flights to each bolt requires a Fletching level of 9 and 1 feather, granting 0.5 Fletching experience per bolt. They may also be stolen from the crossbow stall in Keldagrim. As with most bolts, they can be poisoned, however this will prevent the addition of bolt tips.

Bronze bolts may be tipped with opal or barbs. To tip the bolts with opal, a player must have a Fletching level of 11 and use opal bolt tips with the bronze bolts, granting 1.6 Fletching experience for each opal bolt tip attached and making the bronze bolts into opal bolts. To barb the tips of the bolts, a player must have a Fletching level of 51 and use barbed bolt tips with the bronze bolts, granting 9.5 Fletching experience for each barbed bolt tip attached and making the bronze bolts into barbed bolts.
878:
Bronze bolts are the weakest bolts, and may be shot from any crossbow.

Bronze bolts are crossbow bolts made out of bronze. To make them, a player must smith unfinished bronze bolts. This requires a Smithing level of 3, and for each bronze bar that player smiths they will get 10 unfinished bronze bolts and 12 Smithing experience. Then a player must attach flights to the bolts. Attaching flights to each bolt requires a Fletching level of 9 and 1 feather, granting 0.5 Fletching experience per bolt. They may also be stolen from the crossbow stall in Keldagrim. As with most bolts, they can be poisoned, however this will prevent the addition of bolt tips.

Bronze bolts may be tipped with opal or barbs. To tip the bolts with opal, a player must have a Fletching level of 11 and use opal bolt tips with the bronze bolts, granting 1.6 Fletching experience for each opal bolt tip attached and making the bronze bolts into opal bolts. To barb the tips of the bolts, a player must have a Fletching level of 51 and use barbed bolt tips with the bronze bolts, granting 9.5 Fletching experience for each barbed bolt tip attached and making the bronze bolts into barbed bolts.
879:
Opal bolts are bronze bolts tipped with opal bolt tips. Opal bolts can be created through the Fletching skill for players of level 11 or above. Use a chisel on a cut opal to make 12 opal bolt tips. Attaching opal bolt tips also requires a Fletching level of 11, and for each opal bolt tip attached to a bronze bolt, a player is granted 1.6 Fletching experience. Once the opal bolt tips have been attached, the bronze bolts become opal bolts.

Opal bolts can be enchanted through the spell Enchant Crossbow Bolt (Opal) by a player with level 4 Magic. The spell enchants 10 opal bolts at a time, and once they are enchanted they become enchanted opal bolts and gain a special ability.
880:
Pearl bolts are iron bolts tipped with pearl bolt tips. Pearl bolts can be created through the Fletching skill by attaching pearl bolt tips to iron bolts. Attaching pearl bolt tips requires 41 Fletching. Once the pearl bolt tips have been attached, the iron bolts become pearl bolts.

Pearl bolts can be enchanted through the spell Enchant Crossbow Bolt (Pearl) with level 24 Magic. The spell enchants 10 bolts at a time. Once they are enchanted they become enchanted pearl bolts and gain a special ability.
882:
The bronze arrow is an arrow made of bronze. These arrows are the weakest type of arrows in Old School RuneScape and are compatible with most bows. As with most arrows, they can be poisoned.

In order to create this item players must first smelt bronze bars. Then using a hammer and anvil, the player must turn the bar into bronze arrowtips. Creating the bronze bar has no Smithing requirement, while a player must have level 5 Smithing to create the arrowheads. Then players should cut logs, and using a knife, turn them into arrow shafts. After attaching feathers to the arrow shafts (creating headless arrows) players can then use the arrowheads on the headless arrows to create bronze arrows. This entire process requires level 1 Fletching.

In addition, arrows can be purchased from a variety of general and archery stores.
883:
The bronze arrow is an arrow made of bronze. These arrows are the weakest type of arrows in Old School RuneScape and are compatible with most bows. As with most arrows, they can be poisoned.

In order to create this item players must first smelt bronze bars. Then using a hammer and anvil, the player must turn the bar into bronze arrowtips. Creating the bronze bar has no Smithing requirement, while a player must have level 5 Smithing to create the arrowheads. Then players should cut logs, and using a knife, turn them into arrow shafts. After attaching feathers to the arrow shafts (creating headless arrows) players can then use the arrowheads on the headless arrows to create bronze arrows. This entire process requires level 1 Fletching.

In addition, arrows can be purchased from a variety of general and archery stores.
884:
Iron arrows are stronger than bronze arrows, and are compatible with most bows. Iron arrows can be made at level 15 Fletching by using 15 iron arrowtips on 15 headless arrows, granting 37.5 Fletching experience. As with most arrows, they can be poisoned.

Iron arrows can be purchased from Lowe's Archery Emporium in Varrock.
885:
Iron arrows are stronger than bronze arrows, and are compatible with most bows. Iron arrows can be made at level 15 Fletching by using 15 iron arrowtips on 15 headless arrows, granting 37.5 Fletching experience. As with most arrows, they can be poisoned.

Iron arrows can be purchased from Lowe's Archery Emporium in Varrock.
886:
Steel arrows are stronger than iron arrows, and can be used with any standard bow of oak or stronger. Steel arrows can be made at level 30 Fletching by using 15 steel arrowtips on 15 headless arrows, granting 75 Fletching experience. As with most arrows, they can be poisoned.

Ava's accumulator (from the Animal Magnetism quest) generates steel arrows in the ammo slot, and also randomly attracts items into your inventory.

Steel arrows can be purchased from Lowe's Archery Emporium in Varrock, or Brian's Archery Supplies in Rimmington.
887:
Steel arrows are stronger than iron arrows, and can be used with any standard bow of oak or stronger. Steel arrows can be made at level 30 Fletching by using 15 steel arrowtips on 15 headless arrows, granting 75 Fletching experience. As with most arrows, they can be poisoned.

Ava's accumulator (from the Animal Magnetism quest) generates steel arrows in the ammo slot, and also randomly attracts items into your inventory.

Steel arrows can be purchased from Lowe's Archery Emporium in Varrock, or Brian's Archery Supplies in Rimmington.
888:
Mithril arrows are arrows made of mithril, are stackable, and can be used with any standard bow of willow or stronger. Stronger than steel arrows, mithril arrows can be made at level 45 Fletching by using mithril arrowtips on headless arrows. Doing so grants 112.5 experience for every batch of 15 arrows made. As with most arrows, they can be poisoned.

Mithril arrows can be purchased from Lowe's Archery Emporium in Varrock, or Brian's Archery Supplies in Rimmington.
889:
Mithril arrows are arrows made of mithril, are stackable, and can be used with any standard bow of willow or stronger. Stronger than steel arrows, mithril arrows can be made at level 45 Fletching by using mithril arrowtips on headless arrows. Doing so grants 112.5 experience for every batch of 15 arrows made. As with most arrows, they can be poisoned.

Mithril arrows can be purchased from Lowe's Archery Emporium in Varrock, or Brian's Archery Supplies in Rimmington.
890:
Adamant arrows are stronger than mithril arrows, and can be used by any standard bow of maple or stronger. They can be made at level 60 Fletching by using 15 adamant arrowtips on 15 headless arrows, granting 150 Fletching experience. As with most arrows, they can be poisoned.

They are the best arrows available to free-to-play players.

Adamant arrows can be purchased from Lowe's Archery Emporium in Varrock, or Brian's Archery Supplies in Rimmington.
891:
Adamant arrows are stronger than mithril arrows, and can be used by any standard bow of maple or stronger. They can be made at level 60 Fletching by using 15 adamant arrowtips on 15 headless arrows, granting 150 Fletching experience. As with most arrows, they can be poisoned.

They are the best arrows available to free-to-play players.

Adamant arrows can be purchased from Lowe's Archery Emporium in Varrock, or Brian's Archery Supplies in Rimmington.
942:
Bronze fire arrows are bronze arrows wrapped in an oily cloth, which are then lit by using them on a tinderbox. They, along with any other fire arrow, are primarily used to pierce the guide rope in the Underground Pass to lower the bridge so that a player may walk across.

They have the same ranged strength as regular bronze arrows.
943: A Worm is an unobtainable item seen when conversing with a Gnome child. When talking to a gnome child, they have a chance of offering you a snack, which displays a picture of this item in the chatbox. Although the "Worm" item is shown, King worms are obtained instead.
948:
Bear fur is an item obtained by killing a bear. It can be sold to Baraek for 12 coins, or 20 with the Ring of Charos(a). Bears are located in, among other places, north-east of East Ardougne, the Wilderness, near Goblin Village, in Isafdar, east of Varrock and north of Falador. Bear fur can also be purchased from the fur merchant in the marketplace in East Ardougne.

Although the examine text says, "This would make warm clothing," currently no clothing can actually be made by players from the fur. Wooden cats, used in the The Great Brain Robbery quest, can be made with bear fur.

One piece of bear fur is needed during the quest Mourning's End Part I and the quest Getting Ahead.
950:
Silk can be bought from various silk traders around Gielinor.

Silk can be stolen from silk stalls with a Thieving level of 20, yielding 24 experience. The Silk merchant who runs the silk stall in Ardougne will buy silk from the player for as much as 60 coins through his dialogue, if the player first offers to sell them for 120 coins each.
952:
A spade is a multi-functional tool used for a variety of activities. One of its major uses is in the Farming skill, though it also comes in handy for many quests and Treasure Trails. A spade is also needed to enter the Barrows crypts and the Mole Hole.

Spades are sold in farming shops and many general stores, and an infinite supply can be added to the player-owned house by making a tool store 2. They can also be obtained from a rogue kit, or taken from scenery objects found in various places. Finally, players can ask Konoo at the saltpetre mine in Hosidius for a spare spade.
954:
Rope is an item used for many things, such as quests and the creation of certain items. It can be obtained by purchasing at a shop, trading with Ned in exchange for 4 balls of wool, or by a player spinning yak hair on a spinning wheel.

The best store to buy rope, without requirements, is at Ned's shop in Draynor Village. However, you can get a full inventory of rope for free from the Tempoross minigame in the ropes container. A convenient place to get rope is in the Ardougne general store (helpful for those doing the Waterfall Quest and Plague City) where there is a stock of 20, but Martin Thwait's Lost and Found at Rogues' Den is a far better option since it stocks 50 and is next to a bank (although it requires 50 Thieving and 50 Agility to access his shop). Khazard General Store is also within close proximity of a bank.
958:
Grey wolf fur is an item dropped by werewolves. Grey wolf fur can also be bought, or stolen from the East Ardougne fur trader, the Port Roberts fur stall and the Rellekka fur trader (after The Fremennik Trials quest).

Grey wolf fur can also be obtained from salvaging at merchant shipwrecks and sorting the Opulent salvage recovered. Level 87 sailing is required.

Baraek the fur trader will buy grey wolf furs for 120 coins, or 150 coins with the Ring of Charos(a). He will not buy any noted fur.
966:
A tile is a formerly useless item that can be found in certain places in the Wilderness. Some tiles spawn in the Graveyard of Shadows and the western ruins.

Prior to the release of the Construction skill in 2006, many players speculated that tiles would be used in player-owned houses; however, they were never given a purpose when the skill was released. The tile remained a useless item until the robe bottom of ruin was discovered during the Crack the Clue III event, as a tile is required to obtain this reward.

This item cannot be traded on the Grand Exchange.
968: Rock or rocks may refer to any of the following:
970:
Papyrus is an item used in building various furniture in a player-owned house. Additionally, after completing Enlightened Journey, using a ball of wool and unlit candle on a papyrus results in an origami balloon.

Papyrus is notably required for the following quests:

Darkness of Hallowvale (given during quest)

Three for Enlightened Journey

At least three for Legends' Quest to map the Kharazi Jungle

One for The Golem quest to write him a new program

Zogre Flesh Eaters (given during quest)

Shilo Village

While Guthix Sleeps
972:
Papyrus is an item used in building various furniture in a player-owned house. Additionally, after completing Enlightened Journey, using a ball of wool and unlit candle on a papyrus results in an origami balloon.

Papyrus is notably required for the following quests:

Darkness of Hallowvale (given during quest)

Three for Enlightened Journey

At least three for Legends' Quest to map the Kharazi Jungle

One for The Golem quest to write him a new program

Zogre Flesh Eaters (given during quest)

Shilo Village

While Guthix Sleeps
973: Charcoal is used as a writing and sketching tool in quests. It is often used with papyrus.
975:
The machete is an item used in the Woodcutting skill. It can be obtained from the mainland Karamja general store and Shilo Village general store or by trading with another player. It can also be found by looking in Radimus Erkle's cupboard in the Legends' Guild; however, after the quest is complete you may no longer search the cupboard for a machete and are given the message "You don't think Radimus Erkle would be very pleased if he caught you rifling through his possessions".

The machete can be used as a weapon but is primarily used to cut Jungle during the Tai Bwo Wannai Cleanup minigame. It has no requirements to wield though cutting Light, Medium, and Dense jungle requires 10, 20, and 35 Woodcutting to harvest respectively. A machete is also required to gain access to Kharazi Jungle if the player doesn't have access to the level 79 agility shortcut to the south-east of Shilo Village.

You can also obtain opal, jade, and red topaz machetes, which have a progressively higher speed at chopping down the jungles. To obtain these machetes, you can buy them from Gabooty in Tai Bwo Wannai, or speak to Safta Doc and make an exchange with him. Alternatively you can buy them from players or on the Grand Exchange.
977: The cooking pot is an interface item visible in the Cooking skill guide summary and it previously appeared in the Cooking level-up interface. However, the leveling up interface was updated on 26 June 2007 with an image of a different pot, before the release of Old School RuneScape. As a result, it served no purpose and could not be seen or obtained by players during normal gameplay until the skill guide summaries update in 26 March 2025.
979:
The Highwayman mask is an unobtainable item that was added to the RuneScape 2 beta. It has an identical name and appearance to the Highwayman mask obtainable from Treasure Trails.

Its purpose is unknown, though it may have been accidentally added to the game early when the Highwayman mask's model was added to the level up screen for Thieving.
981:
The disk of returning is an item purchased from Diango's Toy Store for 21,000 coins. Players can activate the disk, which requires them to be inside the Dwarven Mine; when activated, the player is teleported into the Blackhole, where Thordur resides. To leave, simply activate the disk again. This will cause players to reappear in the Dwarven Mine, next to Boot and the sign in the north-western corner of the mine. This means it could conceivably be used to quickly travel from the south-eastern part of the mine to the north-western part. This can be useful for Free-to-play Ultimate Ironmen to train their Smithing with Superheat Item in the mines, by accessing the anvils next to the respawn location after leaving the black hole, or for players running from Falador to the Ruins of Camdozaal.

The 'blackout' option on the disk may also be used in the easternmost part of the White Knights' Castle Crypt, although the 'activate' option does not work. This may be used to quickly reach certain clue step locations by teleporting to Falador, entering the crypt, and then entering and leaving the blackhole.

If not inside the Dwarven Mines, activating the disk of returning simply returns the message You can only enter Thordur's Blackholes from the Dwarven Mines, beneath Falador.

Attempting to drop it while inside the blackhole will result in a confirmation message asking, "Really drop your Disk of Returning?" Choosing "Yes, something cool might happen" will give the message "That was disappointing". Occasionally, though, the chatbox message will state "Something cool happens" as the player performs the dance and clap emotes. This interaction is a reference to a scam that frequently occurred in RuneScape Classic, where visitors of the blackhole were told "something interesting would happen" if they dropped their disk of returning, resulting in a significant number of unoffending players getting stuck inside.

Note: You can still get out of both holes after dropping the disk of returning, either by talking to Thordur and asking how to get out, or by exiting through the light in the blacker blackhole. Any items dropped on the ground in either hole will be deleted upon leaving.
983:
The brass key is a key which allows the player to enter the locked shed found west of the Cooking Guild. The shed provides an alternate entrance to the Edgeville Dungeon, entering north of the Hill Giant room.

To get the key, you must enter the Edgeville Dungeon through the entrance south of the Edgeville bank and make your way through the dungeon. Just north of the hill giant room, there is a small circular room with the key on the ground. It re-spawns every minute.

This key is tradeable and can also be placed on the steel key ring.
987:
The loop half of key is an item dropped by any monster that has access to the gem drop table or the rare drop table. It is also a reward from various random events, the gnome restaurant, from Managing Miscellania, caskets, looting magpie implings, and unlocking the crystal chest in Taverley. It can also be found in the Barrows chest as a separate item if the player has 100% rewards potential.

The loop half of a key is used with a tooth half of key to make a crystal key, which is used to unlock the crystal chest, which contains a dragonstone and an assortment of other items.
989:
The crystal key is created by combining a tooth half of key with a loop half of key, displaying the message, "You join the two halves of the key together." Key halves can be obtained as rewards from Barrows, the Gnome Restaurant minigame, Managing Miscellania, Treasure Trails, looting magpie implings, random events, the rare drop table, etc.

It is used to open the crystal chest located inside a house in Taverley. The chest always contains an uncut dragonstone in addition to a variety of other items. Some items of note are 3 runite bars, rune platelegs/plateskirt (depending on the player's gender), or another half of the crystal key. After the key is used, it disappears and the player must use another one if they want to open the chest again.

The crystal key may not be placed on the steel key ring, as it is non-reusable.

The crystal key can be upgraded to an enhanced crystal key at a singing bowl in Prifddinas, for the cost of 10 crystal shards.

One is required for a medium Falador Diary task of opening a Crystal chest.
991:
The muddy key is a key that can be used to open the muddy chest in the centre of the Lava Maze in the Wilderness. You will need a knife or sword to access it. It can be obtained as a drop from chaos dwarves (in both the Wilderness and Taverley Dungeon), and the crazy archaeologist.

Using a muddy key to open the muddy chest is a medium Wilderness Diary task.
993:
The sinister key is used to open the sinister chest in the Yanille Agility dungeon. The sinister chest contains nine noted grimy herbs: 2 harralanders, 3 ranarr weeds, 1 irit leaf, 1 avantoe, 1 kwuarm, and 1 torstol. The sinister key is dropped by Salarin the twisted and the Chaos Fanatic, and can also be looted from a Magpie impling.

The value of the sinister key is linked to the value of the herbs contained in the sinister chest. Buying a key, opening the chest, and selling the grimy herbs from it currently produces a profit of 4,538.

A lockpick is required if you're entering the dungeon via the house in Yanille.
995:
Coins (also referred to as gold pieces, gp, gold, or simply money) are the most common form of currency in Gielinor. They are used among players and non-player characters alike to exchange for items and services.

Players often refer to one thousand (1,000) coins as 1k and one million (1,000,000) coins as 1m or 1mil. Both can be applied to larger numbers, for example, 10m refers to ten million coins (10,000,000). 1b or 1bil refers to one billion coins (1,000,000,000).

Alchemy spells, which create coins, cannot be cast on coins. If a player attempts it, a message will inform the player that Coins are already made of gold. Curiously, other items made of gold, such as gold ore and gold bars, can be turned into coins with Alchemy spells.

Wearing a ring of wealth will automatically pick up coins dropped by NPCs upon killing them as long as the player has inventory space available.
1005: A white apron is a piece of clothing that gives no stat bonuses and is largely worn for fashion. It is used in the Pirate's Treasure and Mourning's End Part II quest. A white apron respawns in Gerrant's Fishy Business every 10 ticks, and another spawns in Wydin's Food Store in Port Sarim, though players must be wearing a white apron to grab the one in Wydin's Grocery.
1007: A red cape can be made by using red dye on another coloured cape, or purchased from Thessalia's Fine Clothes in Varrock or Barkers' Haberdashery in Canifis.
1009:
A brass necklace is a cosmetic piece of jewellery. It provides no stat bonuses and does not have any uses.

The necklace cannot be made using the Crafting skill; it can only be obtained as a drop from goblins and cave goblins, or as an item spawn in Edgeville Dungeon near the hobgoblins and in the Varrock west bank basement (requires the Telekinetic Grab spell or completion of Crack the Clue III to obtain).
1015:
Black skirts are one of several skirts available. They are sold by various clothes shops, including Thessalia's shop, Thessalia's Fine Clothes, located in Varrock. They can also be dropped by Forgotten Souls.

Black robe skirts are often worn with black robe tops, in the same way blue skirts are worn with wizard tops. However, they provide no bonuses.
1017:
A black wizard hat is an item of clothing that can be worn in the head slot. It has the same bonuses as the blue wizard hat. It can be purchased from Betty's Magic Emporium in Port Sarim, and can be found as a drop from the dark wizards south of Varrock.

It can be created by using black dye on a blue wizard hat; similarly, blue dye can be used on it to create a blue wizard hat.
1019: A black cape is a low-level cape that is commonly obtained by killing a highwayman. It can also be made by using black dye on any coloured cape, and can be purchased from Barkers' Haberdashery in Canifis and Shayzien Styles in Shayzien.
1021:
A Blue cape can be made by using blue dye on another coloured cape and can be purchased from Barkers' Haberdashery in Canifis, Valaine's Shop of Champions in the Champions' Guild, or Shayzien Styles in Shayzien.

A blue cape may also be among the items you can obtain from chasing Solus Dellagar during the Wanted! quest, the player calls this cape the "Cape of Champions" during the quest because it is sold in the Champions' Guild.
1023: A yellow cape can be made by using yellow dye on another coloured cape and can be purchased from Barkers' Haberdashery in Canifis, Fancy Clothes Store in the Varrock, or Shayzien Styles in Shayzien.
1025:
A right eye patch is an item commonly worn by pirates, and can be obtained as a drop from them. An eye patch can be bought from the Fancy Dress Shop or Trader Stan's Trading Post. When equipped, the eye patch takes place in the head slot, which means players may not wear a helmet or any other headgear at the same time.

Players who have completed Cabin Fever can pay Patchy 500 coins to sew together an eye patch and pirate bandana to create a bandana eyepatch. Players can also bring Patchy an eye patch and pirate's hat, to create a hat eyepatch, or a big pirate hat and eye patch to create a pirate hat & patch. It is also possible to ask Patchy to combine this item with a left eye patch to create a double eye patch. A book o' Piracy is not required.

It is one of the possible items that the rowdy dwarf may ask players to bring him during the Forgettable Tale of a Drunken Dwarf quest. It is also a possible request from Gunslik or the rowdy dwarf when doing Keldagrim tasks.

This item can be stored in the mahogany treasure chest of a costume room under master tier.
1027: A green cape can be made by using green dye on another coloured cape and can be purchased from Barkers' Haberdashery in Canifis.
1033:
The Zamorak monk bottom is part of the Zamorak monk robes set. They are bright red, and like the related Zamorak monk top they are dropped by disciples of Iban and monks of Zamorak.

Zamorak monk robes are commonly used by mages in the Wilderness due to providing decent Prayer and Magic bonuses and being easy to replace if lost. They can also be used to telegrab Wine of Zamorak at the Chaos Temple (Asgarnia) without being attacked.

The Zamorak monk bottom counts as a Zamorak item in the God Wars Dungeon.

The Zamorak monk bottom is notable for being the only free-to-play leg slot item with a Magic attack bonus.
1035:
The Zamorak monk top is part of the Zamorak monk robes set. They are bright red, and like the related Zamorak monk bottom they are dropped by disciples of Iban, necromancers and monks of Zamorak.

Zamorak monk robes are commonly used by mages in the Wilderness due to providing decent Prayer and Magic bonuses and being easy to replace if lost. They can also be used to telegrab Wine of Zamorak at the Chaos Temple (Asgarnia) without being attacked.

One of only three free-to-play bodies with a magic attack bonus, the Zamorak monk top has 1 less Magic attack and 3 more Prayer bonus when compared to the Black robe, Blue wizard robe, and their ornamental variants.

The Zamorak monk top counts as a Zamorak item in the God Wars Dungeon.
1037:
Bunny ears are an untradeable cosmetic holiday item worn on the head. A pair of bunny ears can be obtained by completing one of the Easter holiday events that occur once per year. This also rewards the player with all other holiday items associated with Easter.

Previously, they were obtainable during the 2013 Rare Drops event (from 14 July to 21 July) as part of a rare item drop.

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room. Thessalia in Varrock will also return this item to the player if destroyed.
1038:
Red partyhats are tradeable cosmetic items obtained by completing one of the Christmas holiday events that occur once per year.

Previously, they were obtainable during the 2013 Rare Drops event (from 4 July to 14 July) as part of a rare item drop.
1042:
Blue partyhats are tradeable cosmetic items obtained by completing one of the Christmas holiday events that occur once per year.

It can be sewn with sagacious spectacles to make Partyhat & specs by talking to Patchy, along with 500 coins. Doing so requires the completion of Cabin Fever and a book o' Piracy.

Previously, they were obtainable during the 2013 Rare Drops event (from 4 July to 14 July) as part of a rare item drop.
1046:
Purple partyhats are tradeable cosmetic items obtained by completing one of the Christmas holiday events that occur once per year.

Previously, they were obtainable during the 2013 Rare Drops event (from 4 July to 14 July) as part of a rare item drop.
1050: Santa hats are tradeable cosmetic items obtained by completing one of the Christmas holiday events that occur once per year.
1052:
The cape of legends is a cape that can be bought for 675 coins from Siegfried Erkle at the Legends Guild Shop of Useful Items on the western portion of the 2nd floor of the Legends' Guild. They can also purchase it from Perdu for 1,900 coins should they lose it after purchasing it at least once. Like the obsidian cape, it has balanced defence bonuses, but has 2 less in each stat while also being much cheaper.

As the Guild's interior can only be accessed upon completion of the Legends' Quest, this cape can only be owned by those that have completed said quest and became a member of the Guild. There are various NPCs who appear to be wearing the cape or some variation thereof. (See Trivia)

The cape may be mounted in the Quest Hall of a player-owned house in the Guild trophy space. This requires 3 teak planks and grants 300 Construction experience. This has little purpose other than showing guests that the host has completed the Legends' Quest.

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room.
1053:
The Green halloween mask is a tradeable cosmetic item. Green halloween masks can be obtained by completing one of the Halloween holiday events that occur once per year. This also rewards the player with all other holiday items associated with Halloween.

After player decided polls, it was decided that all tradeable rares will be distributed during their corresponding holiday events thus making them seasonal rares and not completely rare, this to prevent them from being worth hundreds of millions of coins again, like in RuneScape 3.

Previously, they were obtainable during the 2013 Rare Drops event (from 17 June to 24 June) as part of a rare item drop.
1055:
The Blue halloween mask is a tradeable cosmetic item. Blue halloween masks can be obtained by completing one of the Halloween holiday events that occur once per year. This also rewards the player with all other holiday items associated with Halloween.

After player decided polls, it was decided that all tradeable rares will be distributed during their corresponding holiday events thus making them seasonal rares and not completely rare, to prevent them from being worth hundreds of millions of coins again, like in RuneScape 3.

Previously, they were obtainable during the 2013 Rare Drops event (from 17 June to 24 June) as part of a rare item drop.
1059: Leather gloves are basic gloves worn in the hands slot, offering slight defensive bonuses. Making them requires 1 Crafting, 1 leather, 1 thread, and a needle, yielding 13.8 Crafting experience.
1061: Leather boots is a part of leather armour worn on the foot slot that offer slight bonuses to defence. They can also be found while big net fishing.
1063:
Leather vambraces are leather armour worn on the hands. With no requirements to equip, they are most commonly used by low-level rangers, and often mages (as there is no magic penalty). Overall they are generally a superior alternative to leather gloves with a notable exception of the crush defence, and could be considered the best "gloves" for free-to-play users who lack 40 Ranged to equip green dragonhide vambraces, as well as the best-in-slot mage gloves due to their lack of negative penalties.

Kebbit claws can be used on these vambraces to make spiky vambraces, requiring a Crafting level of 32.
1067:
Iron platelegs are melee leg armour made of iron. There is no Defence requirement to wear them, as is the same with bronze armour. As such, it is recommended to skip bronze tier items and start out with iron tier items. They have the same defensive stats as an iron plateskirt but weigh more.

They can be made at level 31 Smithing with 3 iron bars, granting 75 experience.
1069:
Steel platelegs are the third weakest platelegs in the game. They have the same bonuses and penalties as a steel plateskirt but weigh more. A player with 46 Smithing can make them by using three steel bars on an anvil while carrying a hammer, granting 112.5 Smithing experience. They can also be bought from Louie's Armoured Legs Bazaar. They require 5 Defence to wear.

As they spawn in the Wilderness at the Ruins north of the Graveyard of Shadows, they are one of the most easily accessible and most popular money making methods for new Ironman accounts when being sold to Louie's Armoured Legs Bazaar starting at 650 each at base stock of 2, reducing by 10 per extra set.

Their respawn rate in the Wilderness is between 10 and 20 minutes, depending on the number of players in a world.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Ardougne knight armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
1071: Mithril platelegs are the third best free-to-play platelegs. They require level 20 Defence to equip. A player with 66 Smithing can make it by using three mithril bars on an anvil while carrying a hammer, granting 150 Smithing experience. Mithril platelegs offer similar stats to a mithril plateskirt but weigh more.
1073:
Adamant platelegs are platelegs made of Adamant and, as such, require a Defence level of 30 to wear. These platelegs have the same stats as the Adamant plateskirt, but are 1kg heavier.

Adamant platelegs can be smithed using 3 adamant bars at level 86 Smithing, granting 187.5 experience.
1075:
Bronze platelegs are leg armour made of bronze, requiring level 1 Defence to wear (as is the same with other bronze and iron items). They share the same defensive stats as a bronze plateskirt but weigh more. They can be made at level 16 Smithing by using a hammer and 3 bronze bars at an anvil.

These can be bought from Louie's Armoured Legs Bazaar in Al Kharid.
1077:
Black platelegs have the same bonuses as the black plateskirt but weigh more. They require level 10 Defence to wear. They can be bought from Louie's Armoured Legs Bazaar in Al Kharid or Valaine's Shop of Champions in the Champions' Guild. Like all other black armour, it cannot be made with the Smithing skill.

Black platelegs are used in King's Ransom and Heroes' Quest if you're part of the Black Arm Gang.

Black platelegs (t) and (g) can both be obtained as a reward from easy Treasure Trails. They provide no extra bonuses than regular black platelegs other than being aesthetically improved.
1079:
Rune platelegs are platelegs made of runite. They require level 40 Defence to wear. Rune platelegs are identical in function to the rune plateskirt, but is 1kg heavier. Players may receive these from the crystal chest if they are a body type A character.

They can be created with the Smithing skill by using 3 runite bars and a hammer on an anvil; this requires level 99 Smithing and yields 225 Smithing experience.

Along with the rune plateskirt and two-handed sword, this is the best bar-per-alch item in the game. If smithing for money, rune platelegs, plateskirt and two-handed sword will give the best value for each bar.

They can also be put into the nest found on top of the Aldarin windmill in Varlamore in order to get a runite bar.
1081:
The iron plateskirt is a plateskirt made from iron. It has the same stats as iron platelegs but weighs less.

They can be made at level 31 Smithing with 3 iron bars, granting 75 experience.
1083: The Steel plateskirt is a plateskirt made from steel, requiring level 5 Defence to wear. It can be made at level 46 Smithing by using 3 Steel bars on an anvil with a hammer in the inventory. It has identical stats to the steel platelegs, with the notable exception that it weighs less.
1085: Mithril plateskirts give the fifth best stat bonuses of all plateskirts. This piece of armour can be made with Level 66 Smithing by using 3 mithril bars on an anvil, therefore granting the player with 150 smithing experience. At least 20 Defence is required to wear it. Mithril plateskirts have similar stats to mithril platelegs but weigh less.
1087: A bronze plateskirt is the weakest plateskirt in Old School RuneScape. It has identical stat bonuses to the bronze platelegs but weighs less. A player with 16 Smithing can make it by using three bronze bars on an anvil while carrying a hammer, granting 37.5 smithing experience. They can be bought from Ranael's Super Skirt Store in Al Kharid.
1091:
The Adamant plateskirt is a plateskirt made out of adamant. At least 30 Defence is required to wear it. The plateskirt has the same stats as the Adamant platelegs, but are 1kg lighter.

They can be made at level 86 Smithing using 3 adamantite bars, which grants 187.5 experience.
1093:
The rune plateskirt is a plateskirt made out of runite. It requires level 40 Defence to wear. The rune plateskirt is identical in function to rune platelegs, but is 1 kg lighter.

It can be created with the Smithing skill by using 3 runite bars and a hammer on an anvil; this requires level 99 Smithing and yields 225 Smithing experience.

Characters may receive these from the crystal chest.

Along with the rune 2h sword and platelegs, this is the best bar-per-alch item in the game. If smithing for money, rune 2h sword, platelegs, and plateskirt will give the best value for each bar.
1095: Leather chaps is a part of leather armour that is worn in the legs slot, most commonly by low-level rangers. Low-levelled player mages also often wear these chaps, since they give a slight defence bonuses without a magic attack penalty.
1097: Studded chaps are part of studded leather armour set and they require 20 Ranged to equip.
1101:
The iron chainbody is the second weakest chainbody, and can be worn by a player with 1 Defence. A player with 26 Smithing can make the chainbody by using three iron bars on an anvil while carrying a hammer, granting 75 Smithing experience.

An iron chainbody is required for the Black Knights' Fortress, King's Ransom, and While Guthix Sleeps quests.
1105:
The Steel chainbody is the third weakest chainbody, and it can be worn by a player with level 5 Defence.

A player with level 41 Smithing can forge the steel chainbody by using three steel bars on an anvil with a hammer in their inventory, granting 112.5 Smithing experience. It can also be bought from Wayne's Chains in Falador, or Horvik's Armour Shop in Varrock.
1107:
The black chainbody is stronger than the steel chainbody, and can be worn by players with 10 Defence. Players can purchase this item at the Keldagrim and Falador Chainmail shops. This item cannot be made using the Smithing skill, and has the same bonuses as a white chainbody, except it lacks a prayer bonus.

Sold at Wayne's Chains shop in southern Falador for 1,440 coins, and at Saro's armour shop in Keldagrim for 1,872 coins.

As with all black and white equipment, the black chainbody cannot be made from raw materials using the Smithing skill.
1109:
The Mithril chainbody is a chainbody made out of mithril. As with all mithril armour, it requires 20 Defence to wear.

Like all chainbodies, it provides better Crush defence than a platebody made of the same material, at the cost of lower Stab and Slash defence.

The Mithril chainbody can be made with level 61 Smithing using 3 mithril bars, and grants 150 Smithing experience.
1111: Adamant chainbody is piece of armour made from adamantite. A player can create an adamant chainbody by using an adamantite bar on an anvil while a hammer and 3 adamantite bars are in the player's inventory. A Smithing level of 81 is required to make an adamant chainbody and doing so will grant the player 187.5 Smithing experience. Level 30 Defence is required to wear an adamant chainbody. It can also be bought from Wayne's Chains in south Falador. One adamant chainbody is required for Song of the Elves.
1113:
A rune chainbody is a chainbody made of runite. To wear this chainbody, a player needs at least level 40 Defence. This piece of body armour is less resistant than the rune platebody in all stats except crush and magic and wearing it does not require completion of Dragon Slayer I. For this reason it is commonly worn by players who have not finished said quest or who are fighting against monsters that use crush attacks. It is also useful for rangers since it has higher defence bonuses than the green d'hide body and it does not penalise ranged attack.

A player with 96 Smithing can make the chainbody by using three runite bars on an anvil, granting 225 Smithing experience. It can also be bought at Scavvo's Rune Store in the Champions' Guild, or for members, at Seddu's Adventurer's Store in Nardah.
1115:
