1486:
A piece of railing is a quest item in the Underground Pass quest. It is obtained by searching a cage that contains a unicorn. The railing is used to lever a rock off of a ledge so that it crashes down and breaks the cage open, killing the unicorn in the process. The player can then search the broken cage to obtain a unicorn horn.

It can be safely dropped after obtaining the horn, as it serves no other purpose during the quest.
1491:
The witch's cat is encountered in the Underground Pass quest. The cat must be recovered from the maze of walkways deep inside the dungeon west of West Ardougne and then used as a distraction to allow the player to enter Kardia the witch's house and search a chest to find the Doll of Iban.

In the past, it was possible to take the cat out of the area by grabbing another one and keeping it with you via banking. Dropping it though, it will always run away, essentially disappearing. Should the player manage to get another cat after returning the cat to Kardia and use it on the door, the game will say, "The witch is busy playing with her other cat...".

The cat can be spoken to if a catspeak amulet is equipped.
1492:
The Doll of Iban is a quest item used in the later stages of the Underground Pass quest. It is initially obtained by searching the chest belonging to Kardia the witch in her house deep in the underground pass, west of West Ardougne.

The doll is turned into an effigy of Iban by using Iban's shadow, Iban's ashes, Iban's blood and Iban's dove on it, all of which have to be obtained by completing various tasks in the dungeon. Progress on the doll is saved if it is lost. At the end of the quest, the doll is thrown down the Well of Voyage to banish Iban from Gielinor.

If lost, it can be reobtained by searching the chest in the witch's house or by speaking to Niloof. Niloof will also give the player a History of Iban. It also should be noted that if the player were to try to drop the doll into the well before adding all the needed ingredients, the game will give the message The doll is still incomplete. and the player will be unable to kill Iban.
1494:
The History of Iban, or The Tale of Iban, is found in the chest found within the witch's house during the Underground Pass quest. It gives some history on Iban, how he was killed, as well as a few hints on how to defeat him.

After completion of the Underground Pass quest, the book can be found on the shelves in the player's house and it can also be found in the Grand Library in Prifddinas after completion of Song of the Elves.
1497:
The Amulet of Othanian is an item used in the later stages of the Underground Pass. It is obtained by killing the level 91 demon Othainian. Once Othainian and his comrades Holthion and Doomion have been killed, the player can use their amulets to open a chest that contains Iban's shadow.

After the quest, the amulets cannot be obtained and have no other use.
1501:
Dwarf brew is a potent spirit made by Kamen. It is used in the later stages of the Underground Pass quest. It is obtained by using an empty bucket on the brew barrel inside Klank's house, found deep inside the Underground Pass.

The brew is used to light a pyre over the tomb of Iban, cremating his remains and turning them into Iban's ashes which must then be used on the Doll of Iban to create his effigy. The brew only needs to be used once on the tomb, after which it can be lit as many times the player likes as long as they don't possess the ashes in their inventory or have used such ashes on the doll.

This is the same beverage that Kamen offers to the player which causes the player to lose 4 Agility levels should they accept.
1503:
The warrant is a quest item used only in Plague City. It is obtained from Bravek after giving him a hangover cure and telling him about the kidnapping.

The warrant is used to distract the mourner guard by the entrance to the plague house in the south-east corner of West Ardougne, granting the player access to search for Elena.

After rescuing Elena, this house can be accessed without needing the warrant, so it serves no further use.
1505:
The Ardougne teleport scroll is a quest item reward in Plague City. It is obtained from Edmond after completion of the quest.

When read, players will be able to cast Ardougne Teleport spell (requiring level 51 Magic), although reading the scroll itself does not have a magic level requirement. Players do not need to read the scroll to use the Ardougne teleport tablet.

Duplicates can be drop tricked by talking to Edmond to acquire another. After reading the scroll for the first time, players will not be able to duplicate any more scrolls. After reading the scroll for the first time, reading any additional scrolls will explode on use, converting into ashes.
1506:
The gas mask is a quest item used in Plague City and Biohazard. It is made by giving dwellberries to Alrena in East Ardougne. The mask is required to be worn to enter West Ardougne before completion of Biohazard. Gas masks are also dropped by the mourners who are present in Mourning's End Part I.

Gas masks serve as a way to protect player from damage in the Smokey Dungeon and Smoke Devil Dungeon. The mask also reduces damage from the clouds whilst sulphur mining in Lovakengj, and prevents infection from Nex's virus attack, which makes them useful even after their intended quest use.

Duplicates can be drop tricked by searching the cupboard on the ground floor of Edmond's house to obtain another. This is only possible when the original mask was created by Alrena for the first time. Additional sets of Dwellberries are not required. Wearing a gas mask is no longer required while in West Ardougne after completing Biohazard.

If you've completed Song of the Elves, you can find this mask in a closed chest in the basement of the Mourner headquarters.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Mourner gear set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
1509:
Books are items obtained in quests and elsewhere in Old School RuneScape. Most books can be read by players, which provides information ranging from lore to information on game mechanics.

When a player reads a book, an interface will appear to display the book's contents, and their character will be seen reading a green (sometimes yellow) book.
1510:
The picture is a quest item used only in Plague City. It is found in Edmond and Arlena's house in the north-west of East Ardougne.

It is shown to Jethick, who will direct the player to the Rehnison house in West Ardougne.

After completing the quest, Edmond will take it from the player's inventory. Duplicates can be obtained after the quest, but it serves no further use. Using the picture on Jethick after the quest will result in nothing interesting happening (but does not yield in nothing interesting happens message).
1511:
Logs, also called normal logs, are obtained from cutting regular, evergreen, jungle, dying and dead trees, and uncommonly from infected roots. Players can burn these logs using the Firemaking skill. Cutting the logs gives 25 Woodcutting experience, and burning them gives 40 Firemaking experience. These logs have no requirement to be cut or burnt.

Members training Construction can bring logs to a sawmill to make planks at a cost of 100 coins each. Alternatively, the Lunar spell Plank Make can allow players to convert them to planks at a lower cost, but at the expense of runes.

While wearing Kandarin headgear 1 or higher, normal trees anywhere give double logs when chopped down but no additional experience is provided.

It is currently the only log which can be coloured with gnomish firelighters, which are obtained as rewards from Treasure Trails. These firelighters produce fire in one of five predetermined colours: red, blue, green, purple, or white. Coloured logs also give 50 Firemaking experience, slightly more than lighting the logs normally.

Members can also fletch these logs into bows and arrow shafts, and are the only type of log that can be made into javelin shafts.

Normal logs are also used to travel to Entrana or Taverley using the Balloon Transport System after completing the Enlightened Journey quest (they are also required during the quest).

Four normal logs respawn on Lumbridge Castle's roof, in a house in Draynor Village, in the Wizards' Tower, and in a house in Rimmington. They also spawn south of Varlamore.
1513:
Magic logs are logs that can be acquired using the Woodcutting skill from magic trees. Cutting magic trees requires a Woodcutting level of 75 or higher and yields 250 Woodcutting experience per log cut. Due to the slow speed at which magic trees are cut at this level, it is advised that players wait until they have a Woodcutting level of at least 85 before chopping magic trees. Players can expect to gain up to 130 magic logs per hour using a dragon axe.

Magic logs can be fletched into unstrung magic shortbows with a Fletching level of 80, granting 83.3 Fletching experience, or into unstrung magic longbows with a Fletching level of 85, granting 91.5 Fletching experience.

Magic logs can also be burnt with a Firemaking level of 75, granting 303.8 Firemaking experience.

Magic logs are needed for three quests: twelve for Desert Treasure I, one for Mourning's End Part I, and three for unlocking the Gnome Stronghold balloon route (requirement for Monkey Madness II), requiring sixteen magic logs in total.

Ultimate Ironmen can permanently store magic logs with the Friendly Forester log storage or balloon transport log storage.

6 magic logs can be used to light an Abyssal lantern, requiring 75 Firemaking.
1515:
Yew logs are logs obtained from cutting yew trees, which require at least level 60 Woodcutting for players to cut. They give 175 experience when cut with an axe. Players can burn these logs with the Firemaking skill at level 60, granting 202.5 Firemaking experience.

Yew logs can also be made into bows, stock, and arrow shafts using the Fletching skill. When the log is cut into a yew longbow (u) at level 70, it yields 75 experience. Cutting a yew shortbow (u) at level 65 will give 67.5 experience. Stringing the unstrung bows will give the same experience as for cutting them.

One full inventory of yew logs gives 4,900 Woodcutting experience. Players would need to cut 72,919 yew logs to go from 60 to 99 Woodcutting.

Yew logs can also be used to travel to Castle Wars on the Balloon transport system, costing 10 logs on the initial trip, and 1 log for every trip following that.

6 yew logs can be used to light an Abyssal lantern, requiring 60 Firemaking.
1517:
Maple logs are received from cutting maple trees requiring a Woodcutting level of 45 and yield 100 Woodcutting experience (110 with Kandarin Medium Diary) per log. Maple logs can be burned with a Firemaking level of 45, giving 135 experience per log. Maple logs can also be fletched into different items: arrow shafts, maple shortbow (u), maple longbow (u), maple stock and maple shield.

Because of their low price and the moderate experience they provide, maple logs are commonly used for training Firemaking.

6 maple logs can be used to light an Abyssal lantern, requiring 45 Firemaking.
1521:
Oak logs are logs obtained from cutting oak trees at level 15 Woodcutting and give 37.5 experience points each. Players can burn these logs using the Firemaking skill at level 15 for 60 experience each. Members can also fletch these logs.

Members training Construction can bring oak logs to a sawmill to make oak planks at a cost of 250 coins each. Alternatively, the Lunar spell Plank Make can allow players to convert them to planks at a lower cost, but at the expense of runes. The use of oak planks in Construction increased the price of oak logs.

Oak logs are used to travel to the Crafting Guild on the Balloon Transport System.

Training Woodcutting via oak trees is a fairly quick method of obtaining nests.

6 oak logs can be used to light an Abyssal lantern, requiring 15 Firemaking.
1523:
A lockpick is an item used with the Thieving skill that can be used on certain locked objects. While some objects require a lockpick to be unlocked, certain objects are instead only made easier to open.

Lockpicks can be obtained by pickpocketing bandits (with 53 Thieving) and rogues (32 Thieving), or as drops from young implings and scavenger beasts. They can also be purchased from Martin Thwait, though this requires level 50 Thieving and Agility, or level 99 Thieving.

Lockpicks have a chance to break when performing certain actions, including: Ogre Coffins, the secure chest during Desert Treasure I, the small rune caskets during Ali Morrisane, and the first Ancient Gate during Legends' Quest. Outside of these activities, lockpicks will never break.
1527:
Grimy ardrigal is the grimy form of ardrigal, a herb obtained by searching the palm trees with large leaves on the north-eastern peninsula of Karamja, on the south side of the tree grapple shortcut. It is the second herb Trufitus asks the player to bring him during Jungle Potion, and is also used during Legends' Quest in combination with snake weed to make a bravery potion.

Trufitus will buy clean ardrigals for a random amount of coins between 1 and 4. This can only be done by using the herb on him, as there is no dialogue option for selling them to him. He will not buy grimy ardrigals, his reasoning being that he cannot identify what the herb is.

Ardrigal grows back 60 seconds after being picked.

It cannot be stored in the herb sack.
1528:
Ardrigal is the clean form of grimy ardrigal, a herb obtained by searching the palm trees with large leaves on the north-eastern peninsula of Karamja, on the south side of the tree grapple shortcut. It is the second herb Trufitus asks the player to bring him during Jungle Potion, and is also used during Legends' Quest in combination with snake weed to make a bravery potion.

Trufitus will buy clean ardrigals for a random amount of coins between 1 and 4. This can only be done by using the herb on him, as there is no dialogue option for selling them to him. He will not buy grimy ardrigals, his reasoning being that he cannot identify what the herb is.

Ardrigal grows back 60 seconds after being picked.
1530:
Sito foil is a quest item used in Jungle Potion. It is made by cleaning grimy sito foil.

It is given to Trufitus so he can create a potion.

Duplicates can be made during and after the quest, but it serves no further purpose besides selling it to Trufitus for a few coins. It can not be used as payment for the ogre boat ride to Feldip Hills.
1531:
A grimy volencia moss is a herb that can be cleaned to make a volencia moss. Cleaning a grimy volencia moss requires a Herblore level of 3 and gives 2.5 Herblore experience. It is involved in the quest Jungle Potion and Fairytale I - Growing Pains, where a clean volencia moss may be one of the random items needed to obtain the magic secateurs. Players can find it in the black rocks at the Karamja Jungle mine north of Shilo Village on Karamja. In order to be able to collect the herb, the player must have started the Jungle Potion quest.

It cannot be stored in the herb sack.
1532:
Volencia moss is a herb which requires level 3 Herblore to clean, yielding 2.5 experience. It is used in the Jungle Potion quest as the fourth herb that the player brings Trufitus. Players can make volencia moss by cleaning the grimy volencia moss obtained by searching the grey rocks at the Karamja Jungle mine, north of Shilo Village. In order to be able to collect the herb, the player must first have started the Jungle Potion quest.

Volencia moss is one of the items that Malignius Mortifer may ask the player to give to the Nature Spirit during the quest Fairytale I - Growing Pains.
1538:
The Crandor map is a quest item used only in Dragon Slayer I. It is made by using any two pieces on each other when all three map parts are in the inventory.

It is given to Ned so he can sail the player to Crandor.
1539:
Steel nails are nails made with a steel bar on an anvil with a hammer in the player's inventory, requiring 34 Smithing, yielding 15 steel nails and granting 37.5 Smithing experience per bar.

These nails are the only nails that can be made in free-to-play because they are required in the Dragon Slayer I quest. Steel nails are tradeable and the sawmill operator will sell them to members for 3 coins each.

Members can use steel nails to construct certain types of wooden furniture. With 56 Construction, five steel nails can be used along with two planks to repair broken bridges in the Hallowed Sepulchre, granting 150 Construction experience; without a hallowed hammer in the player's inventory, there is a chance of failing to repair the bridge and breaking nails in the process. With 33 Fletching, they can be used on flighted ogre arrows to create steel brutal arrows, granting 5.1 Fletching experience per arrow. With 62 Crafting, fifteen steel nails can be used with a maple shield and two pieces of green dragon leather to craft a green d'hide shield, granting 124 Crafting experience per shield.
1540:
The anti-dragon shield is an item given by Duke Horacio in Lumbridge Castle during the Dragon Slayer I quest. After the quest, the shield can be purchased from Oziach, or obtained from Duke Horacio for free. It is tradeable, but can only be equipped if the player has started Dragon Slayer I.

The anti-dragon shield mitigates the effects of dragonfire, reducing the maximum hit of most dragon-breath attacks by roughly ~80%. It also prevents Elvarg from severely draining the player's combat stats. The effects of antifire potion stack with the anti-dragon shield; using both provides full protection from standard dragonfire attacks.

The shield's melee and ranged defensive bonuses are similar to those of an iron sq shield, but this shield also provides Magic defence and has no offensive penalties. This gives it some usefulness as an all-purpose shield and best-in-slot for free-to-play mages.
1542:
The maze key is a key used to open the front door of Melzar's Maze. It is obtained from the Guildmaster in the Champions' Guild when the player has returned to him after speaking to Oziach during Dragon Slayer I.

It can be added to a steel key ring. Should players lose it before completing the quest, they may return to the Guildmaster to claim another. Afterwards, it can also be bought from the Legends Guild Shop of Useful Items. in the Legends' Guild or received from the Guildmaster in the Champions' Guild.
1543:
The red key is a quest item used only in Dragon Slayer I. It is dropped by the small zombie rat with the long tail on the ground floor floor of Melzar's Maze.

Is it used to unlock the red doors, where it will disintegrate upon being used.
1544:
The orange key is a quest item used only in Dragon Slayer I. It is dropped by the ghost wearing a hood and no cape on the 1st floor floor of Melzar's Maze.

Is it used to unlock the orange doors, where it will disintegrate upon being used.
1545:
The yellow key is a quest item used only in Dragon Slayer I. It is dropped by the skeleton wielding a round shield on the 2nd floor floor of Melzar's Maze.

Is it used to unlock the yellow doors, where it will disintegrate upon being used.
1546:
The blue key is a quest item used only in Dragon Slayer I. It is dropped by one of the two zombies in the basement of Melzar's Maze.

Is it used to unlock the blue door, where it will disintegrate upon being used.
1547:
The magenta key is a quest item used only in Dragon Slayer I. It is dropped by Melzar the Mad in the basement of Melzar's Maze.

Is it used to unlock the magenta door, where it will disintegrate upon being used.
1548:
The green key is a quest item used only in Dragon Slayer I. It is dropped by the lesser demon in the basement of Melzar's Maze.

Is it used to unlock the green door, where it will disintegrate upon being used.
1550: Garlic is an item used in several quests. Although it cannot be eaten on its own, it is used in Cooking in making Spicy sauce and in Herblore in making Guthix balance potions.
1554:
Fluffs' kitten is a quest item used only in Gertrude's Cat. It is found in one of the mewing crates in the Lumber Yard.

The kitten must be used on Fluffs to progress. If the player drop the kitten, it will become an NPC and run off into crates again, forcing the player to search for it again.
1561:
Cats are common pets that can follow the player. In order to obtain a pet cat, a player must complete the Gertrude's Cat quest, after which Gertrude will give them a kitten as part of the reward. After three hours, the kitten will grow into a pet cat. Unlike kittens, cats do not need food nor attention, and will not run away if neglected.

After another five to six hours of having the adult cat following the player, it will become an overgrown cat. Overgrown cats can be trained into wily cats after the completion of the Ratcatchers quest. These cats will eventually become lazy cats, but can repeatedly be trained back into wily cats.

Only one kitten may be owned at a time, including the hellkitten variant. Players may purchase a new kitten from Gertrude for 100 coins whenever their current kitten turns into an overgrown cat, or their cat is stored in a player-owned house menagerie. The colour of the kitten will be randomised, unless the player wears the Ring of Charos(a) while purchasing the kitten, which allows them to choose the colour.

Any type of cat can be turned into a Hellcat variant by chasing the hell-rats in Evil Dave's basement. Hellcats can be morphed back into their original colour by feeding them a bucket of milk.

Cats can be interacted with in a number of ways, such as by stroking them, showing them a ball of wool or wielding a mouse toy while the cat follows the player. Cats may be spoken to with a catspeak amulet, or without it after partial completion of Dragon Slayer II. They can also chase rats, with a successful catch rate depending on the type of cat. Regular adult cats have a success rate of 50% (or 70% during Ratcatchers).

Players may name their wily and lazy cats by speaking to Felkrash after the completion of Ratcatchers.

Similar to every pet, cats can be stored in the menagerie of a player-owned house. They however cannot be insured by Probita and will run off if the player dies, if they were either in the player's inventory or following the player.

Players can use their adult cats, including hellcats, on civilians in West Ardougne in the south-western area of the city to sell it to them for 100 death runes (19,000). This increases to 200 death runes (38,000) with the easy Ardougne achievement diary reward. Cats can also be shooed-away if the player no longer wishes to keep them.

If a cat dies in combat, it is permanently lost and the message Your cat has passed away. will appear in the chatbox. Cats cannot die in a Menagerie arena. Cats can also be lost if they are following the player when their membership expires. If a cat is lost and replaced, quest dialogue will not reflect this; the replacement will recall events as though they were the same cat.

1567:
Overgrown cats are pet cats that the player has continued to grow after becoming an adult cat. After 5-6 hours of following the player, a regular adult cat will become an overgrown cat, and will lose its ability to catch vermin (though it can still fight Hell-Rat Behemoths). Overgrown cats may be spoken to with a catspeak amulet, or without it after partial completion of Dragon Slayer II.

Players can sell their regular, overgrown, wily and lazy cats to civilians in West Ardougne in the south-western area of the city for 100 death runes (19,000). This increases to 200 death runes (38,000) with the easy Ardougne achievement diary reward. Use the pet cat on the civilian in order to make the trade. Hellcats do not need to be transformed back to normal cats before being traded in.

There is no limit to how many overgrown cats can be owned. After the completion of the Ratcatchers quest, players can speak to Felkrash to have her train their overgrown cat into a wily cat.

1573:
Doogle leaves are herbs that players can use on a raw sardine to make a seasoned sardine. They then feed the seasoned sardine to Fluffs, a cat in the Gertrude's Cat quest. After the quest, players may still season sardines with the leaves, but the doogle sardines can not be used to feed player-owned kittens.

It may also be needed for the Big Chompy Bird Hunting quest as a possible seasoning for Fycie, Bugs or Rantz.

They are found on the ground south of Gertrude's house (west of Varrock), in Feldip Hills (directly west of the swamp where you can fill your ogre-bellows and catch the toads during the Big Chompy Bird Hunting quest), and east of Rellekka, near the swaying tree.
1575:
A cat training medal is an item worn in the neck slot that members can obtain by having their cat or kitten catch 100 rats, and then talking to Gertrude in Varrock. Hell-rats are included in this count, as well as hell-rat behemoths. This item has no effect when worn, and is purely cosmetic. If players lose or drop their training medal, they may talk to Gertrude to get another one. It is not tradeable on the Grand Exchange, but it can be traded in person with other players.

Kittens have a low chance of catching rats, so it is recommended to wait until your kitten has grown into a cat before you try to catch rats. The cat must catch the rats before it turns into an overgrown cat, which cannot hunt vermin. Players who only have overgrown cats must buy another kitten from Gertrude (or wait for it to become lazy). Note that wily cats are not eligible for a medal, and training an overgrown cat into a wily cat also resets the rat kill counter to zero even after it becomes lazy. Receiving a new kitten from Gertrude will also reset the counter, as will letting a cat mature into an overgrown one.

One of the best places to catch rats is in Evil Dave's basement, where Hell-Rats may be caught to obtain spices for making spicy stew. These stews can be useful when attempting to get a +5 stat boost in specific skills, which allows players to complete quests and achievement diaries at lower levels than with most other methods. Aside from that, the basement contains a very high density of rats, making it easy to catch rats continuously. The Varrock sewers also have a high density of normal rats, useful for quick training.

While training, your character will occasionally engage in dialogue to track your cat's progress. A message such as "Well done puss! 10 horrible rodents caught!" will appear after 10, 50, and 100 rats. If you do not see this message after 10 kills, go back and make sure your cat is eligible for the medal as described above.
1577: Pete's candlestick is a quest item used in Heroes' Quest. The player must work collaboratively with another player to kill Grip in order to obtain his keyring and can then use this to access a treasure room that contains the candlesticks. However, players cannot complete the quest if they trade someone else's candlestick, they must obtain their own.
1579:
A thieves' armband is one of the three items required by Achietties during Heroes' Quest. To obtain it for the quest, you must speak to your gang leader (Black Arm Gang, Katrine; Phoenix Gang, Straven). You will also need a partner from the other gang.

Firstly, both of you must go to the Black Arm Gang's hideout Brimhaven. The Black Arm gang member should be wearing full Black armour (Black full helmet, Black platebody, Black platelegs). Then, the Black Arm gang member is to retrieve an ID to enter the building, but you must get two candlesticks from Scarface Pete first. (Note: You need to give one to your Phoenix gang partner.) Then, you must retrieve a Miscellaneous key, in order for your partner to range the level 22 Grip, who drops the key required for the armband. Both of you must bring your candlestick back to your gang leaders for reward, that is: Straven for the Phoenix gang member, and Katrine for the Black Arm gang member.

If you speak to your gang leader after the quest, they'll provide you with another armband. It cannot be worn.
1580:
Ice gloves are a piece of armour dropped by the Ice Queen under White Wolf Mountain. The gloves are required for multiple quests, as well as several skilling activities. They can be combined with Smiths gloves to combine the effects of both in Smiths gloves (i). This process is reversible.

Although the Ice Queen is a high level, she is very easy to kill, especially when using Protect from Melee. You do not need to start Heroes' Quest to obtain the ice gloves, and the gloves can be obtained as many times as desired. The gloves are obtainable at level 3; however, a boostable level of 50 Mining is required to mine an obstacle on the path to her lair.
1581:
Blamish snail slime is a quest item in Heroes' Quest. When added to a vial of water with Harralander it makes blamish oil, which can be used on a fishing rod to make an oily fishing rod. The oily fishing rod can then be used to catch lava eels in the Taverley Dungeon or the Lava Maze, or infernal eels in Mor Ul Rek.

Blamish snail slime can be made by going to Mort Myre Swamp, killing a Myre blamish snail, and grinding the raw snail (thin, lean, and fat all work equally) with a pestle and mortar with an empty sample bottle in the player's inventory. Sample bottles can be obtained from the general store in Canifis or from Rasolo the Wandering Merchant.

Gerrant provides players with blamish snail slime for free during Heroes' Quest.
1582:
Blamish oil is a quest item used in Heroes' Quest. It is made through the Herblore skill, and it turns a normal fishing rod into an oily fishing rod. Oily fishing rods can only be used at lava fishing spots to catch lava eels or infernal eels.

To make blamish oil, combine blamish snail slime with a harralander potion (unf). It requires level 25 Herblore to be made and gives 80 Herblore experience. Completion of Heroes' Quest is not required to create the blamish oil in this way.

After completion of Heroes' Quest, blamish oil is a rare drop from the citizens of Rellekka and the citizens of Canifis, only if they are in human form, which requires a wolfbane dagger to stop them from transforming into werewolves.

Blamish oil has a "Drink" option, but if a player attempts to do so, their character says, "You know... I'd really rather not."
1584: The id papers is needed to get into ScarFace Pete's mansion during the Heroes' Quest. Using it while the player is dressed in full Black armour will allow the player to pass themself off as a Black Knight called Hartigen. The ID paper can be obtained by talking to Trobert.
1586: Miscellaneous key is a quest item obtained during the Heroes' Quest from Grip. It is used to access the windowed room in Scarface Pete's mansion in Brimhaven. From here a second player can kill Grip using a Ranged attack, and the first player, the one doing the quest, is then able to retrieve Grips' key from the body. This is one of the keys that cannot be held on a steel key ring.
1588:
Grip's keyring is a quest item that players obtain whilst doing the Heroes' Quest if they are in the Black Arm Gang. They can only obtain this item after their partner kills Grip with ranged or magic attacks.

The keyring is used to unlock the door to a treasure room in the Black Arm Gang's second hideout in Brimhaven in order to obtain the candlesticks required to continue the quest.

It cannot be stored on a steel key ring.
1590:
The dusty key is a key that unlocks a gate to the Taverley Dungeon, allowing passage into the deeper parts of dungeon from the Lesser demon area to the Blue dragon area.

The player can get the key from Velrak the explorer, who is imprisoned in the Black Knight headquarters in the southern part of the Taverley Dungeon. Kill the jailer to get a key to enter Velrak's cell and talk to him, but do not ask for a reward!

The dusty key can also be purchased for one coin on the 2nd floor of the Legends' Guild, by players who have completed the Legends' Quest.

One dusty key spawns deep in Taverley Dungeon, near the Lava eel fishing spot south of the blue dragon area. Note that this key spawns in the deeper area of the dungeon, so players who need a key to access the deeper dungeon cannot obtain it here. Players with level 70 Agility can obtain this key by using the agility shortcut near the entrance to the dungeon. The shortcut goes to the blue dragon area. If expense is not an issue, players can also access the spawn by buying a Key master teleport on the Grand Exchange, which goes to Cerberus' Lair. This method is risky for players without Protect from Melee, as they will need to run past hellhounds and black demons.

The dusty key is not tradeable, but multiple copies can be obtained. It can be placed on the Steel key ring.

During the Heroes' Quest, players without level 70 Agility need the dusty key to reach the lava eel fishing area (unless they obtained the lava eel through the Lava Maze in the Wilderness or from Charred Dungeon with 60 Sailing).
1591:
The jail key is dropped by the Jailer, found in the Black Knights' Base, deep within Taverley Dungeon. The key gives access to the jail cell containing Velrak the explorer, who will in turn give players the Dusty key which may be used to travel deeper into the dungeon. It can also be used to unlock the door that holds two dwarves, opposite to Velrak the explorer's cell.

The jail key is also one of the fifty required items to hand the dwarf in the Mourning's End Part II quest if you need a death talisman.

The jail key is not required for exiting the cells.

This key cannot be placed upon the key ring.
1592: A ring mould allows a player to make rings through the Crafting skill out of gold bars and possibly gems by using them on a furnace. It can be bought at various crafting shops, and an unlimited amount can also be taken from a tool store 4 in a player-owned house.
1594:
An unholy mould is a mould which is used to make silver bars into unpowered symbols using the Crafting skill. To do this, the player can use it on any furnace using the Crafting skill. Unholy moulds can be found by speaking to the Spirit of Scorpius at his grave after completion of the Observatory Quest.

It is also a rare drop from chaos druids and elder chaos druids after completion of the quest. Zombies in Tarn's Lair can also drop them, even if the quest hasn't been completed.
1599:
A holy mould is a Crafting tool used in a furnace to make unstrung symbols from silver bars.

They can be purchased from Rasolo, north-west of East Ardougne, Jamila's Craft Stall in Sophanem, Dommik's Crafting Store in north-eastern Al Kharid, or from Rommik's Crafty Supplies in Rimmington. An unlimited amount can be taken from a player-owned house tool store 4.
1601:
Diamonds are precious gems used mainly in Crafting. They can be cut from uncut diamonds with a chisel at level 43 Crafting, yielding 107.5 experience.

A diamond is required to enter the Zanaris marketplace.
1603:
Rubies are precious gems used mainly in Crafting. They can be cut from uncut rubies with a chisel at level 34 Crafting, yielding 85 experience.

A one-time reward of 2 cut rubies can be obtained by using a chisel and hammer on Thammaron's throne during The Golem quest. Completing Olaf's Quest rewards 4 cut rubies.

In exchange for 250 cut rubies, 500 fire runes (combination runes will not work), 100 cosmic runes, and 1 Digsite pendant of any charge Curator Haig Halen will award the player with a Curator's medallion. The medallion is needed to build a Mounted digsite pendant in the portal nexus of a player-owned house.
1605: Emeralds are precious gems used mainly in Crafting. They can be cut from uncut emeralds with a chisel at level 27 Crafting, yielding 67.5 experience.
1609:
Opals are semi-precious gems used mainly in Crafting. They can be cut from uncut opals with a chisel, yielding 15 experience. There is a chance to unsuccessfully cut the opal, resulting in a crushed gem and 3.8 experience.

Opals are the lowest level gemstone.

One opal is required for The Dig Site, either cut or uncut, and one for Legends' Quest.
1611:
Jade is a semi-precious gem used mainly in Crafting. It can be cut from an uncut jade with a chisel at level 13 Crafting, yielding 20 experience. There is a chance to unsuccessfully cut the jade, resulting in a crushed gem and 5 experience.

One jade is used in the Legends' Quest.
1613:
Red topaz is a semi-precious gem used mainly in Crafting. It can be cut from uncut red topaz with a chisel at level 16 Crafting, yielding 25 experience. There is a chance to unsuccessfully cut the red topaz, resulting in a crushed gem and 6.3 experience.

3 red topaz can be given to Safta Doc alongside a gout tuber and 1,200 trading sticks in exchange for a red topaz machete.
1615:
Dragonstones are rare gems which can be cut from uncut dragonstones, requiring 55 Crafting and yielding 137.5 experience. It can then be made into dragonstone jewellery by using a furnace along with a gold bar and a mould.

Monsters with access to the rare drop table have a chance to drop cut dragonstones.

Dragonstones from the Mage Training Arena minigame are different, providing pizazz points when enchantment spells are used on them and they cannot be taken outside the enchanting chamber.

5 dragonstones can be given to Olbertus in the Forthos Dungeon to receive a temple coin and unlock the Sacred Bone Burner.
1617:
An uncut diamond is a precious gem used in Crafting. It can be cut with a chisel to make a diamond, requiring 43 Crafting and yielding 107.5 experience.

Uncut diamonds can be obtained in several ways: randomly while mining ores, as drops from monsters (mainly those which have access to the rare drop table), gem shops, or as a reward from certain minigames and random events. They are also a common reward from Managing Miscellania.

With level 40 Mining and the quest Shilo Village completed, players can mine the gem rocks in Shilo Village. Gem rocks may also appear while playing the Tai Bwo Wannai Cleanup activity, where players can mine them 3 times. Another method to get uncut diamonds is by cracking wall safes in the Rogues' Den, but this requires level 50 Thieving.

An uncut diamond is a reward from the Troll Romance quest and is dropped by the Slagilith during One Small Favour.
1619:
An uncut ruby is a precious gem used in Crafting. It can be cut with a chisel to make a ruby, requiring 34 Crafting and yielding 85 experience.

Uncut rubies can be obtained in several ways: randomly while mining ores, as drops from monsters (mainly those which have access to the rare drop table), gem shops, or as a reward from certain minigames and random events. They are also a common reward from Managing Miscellania.

With level 40 Mining and the quest Shilo Village completed, players can mine the gem rocks in Shilo Village. Gem rocks may also appear while playing the Tai Bwo Wannai Cleanup activity, where players can mine them 3 times. Another method to get uncut rubies is by cracking wall safes in the Rogues' Den, but this requires level 50 Thieving.

Uncut rubies are a reward from the Misthalin Mystery and Troll Romance quest.
1621:
An uncut emerald is a precious gem used in Crafting. It can be cut with a chisel to make an emerald, requiring 27 Crafting and yielding 67.5 experience.

Uncut emeralds can be obtained in several ways: randomly while mining ores, as drops from monsters (mainly those which have access to the rare drop table), gem shops, or as a reward from certain minigames and random events. They are also a common reward from Managing Miscellania.

With level 40 Mining and the quest Shilo Village completed, players can mine the gem rocks in Shilo Village. Gem rocks may also appear while playing the Tai Bwo Wannai Cleanup activity, where players can mine them 3 times. Another method to get uncut emeralds is by cracking wall safes in the Rogues' Den, but this requires level 50 Thieving.
1623:
An uncut sapphire is a precious gem used in Crafting. It can be cut with a chisel to make a sapphire, requiring 20 Crafting and yielding 50 experience.

Uncut sapphires can be obtained in several ways: randomly while mining ores, as drops from monsters (mainly those which have access to the rare drop table), gem shops, or as a reward from certain minigames and random events. They are also a common reward from Managing Miscellania.

With level 40 Mining and the quest Shilo Village completed, players can mine the gem rocks in Shilo Village. Gem rocks may also appear while playing the Tai Bwo Wannai Cleanup activity, where players can mine them 3 times. Another method to get uncut sapphires is by cracking wall safes in the Rogues' Den, but this requires level 50 Thieving.
1625:
An uncut opal is a semi-precious gem used in Crafting. It can be cut with a chisel to make an opal, granting 15 Crafting experience. There is a chance to unsuccessfully cut the opal, resulting in a crushed gem and 3.8 experience. Opals are the lowest level gemstone and are worth very little.

Uncut opals are found mostly with the Mining skill, only by mining gem rocks which are located in Shilo Village after a player has completed the Shilo Village quest, in the Lunar Isle mine after Lunar Diplomacy, or on The Onyx Crest after 47 Sailing; or by mining the shell of the Gemstone Crab. Opals can also be found while panning at the Digsite near the River Salve, or they may be stolen from H.A.M members via the Thieving skill.
1627:
An uncut jade is a semi-precious gem used in Crafting. It can be cut with a chisel at level 13 Crafting to make a jade, granting 20 experience. There is a chance to unsuccessfully cut the jade, resulting in a crushed gem and 5 experience.

Uncut jades are found mostly with the Mining skill, only by mining gem rocks which are located in Shilo Village after a player has completed the Shilo Village quest, in the Lunar Isle mine after Lunar Diplomacy, or on The Onyx Crest after 47 Sailing; or by mining the shell of the Gemstone Crab. Jades can also be found while panning at the Digsite near the River Salve, or they may be stolen from H.A.M members via the Thieving skill.
1629:
An uncut red topaz is a semi-precious gem used in Crafting. It can be cut with a chisel at level 16 Crafting to make a red topaz, granting 25 experience. There is a chance to unsuccessfully cut the red topaz, resulting in a crushed gem and 6.3 experience.

Uncut red topaz is found mostly with the Mining skill, only by mining gem rocks which are located in Shilo Village after a player has completed the Shilo Village quest, in the Lunar Isle mine after Lunar Diplomacy, or on The Onyx Crest after 47 Sailing, or by mining the shell of the Gemstone Crab. They can also be obtained by completing hard Gnome Restaurant deliveries, by stealing from Dorgesh-Kaan Rich Chests, by completing the Wise Old Man's tasks, or by salvaging merchant shipwrecks. In addition, there is a very rare chance to find one while searching certain scenery objects across Gielinor.

Three uncut red topaz can be given to Safta Doc alongside a gout tuber and 1,200 trading sticks in exchange for a red topaz machete.
1631:
Uncut dragonstones are rare gems which can be cut into dragonstones, requiring 55 Crafting and granting 137.5 experience. They can be obtained from the crystal chest in Taverley, unlocked with a crystal key, along with other various items.

While uncut dragonstones are available from the gem shop within Mor Ul Rek for 1,500 Tokkul, they are not in stock unless sold by another player. Their cut counterparts are dropped very rarely by a wide variety of monsters.
1635:
A gold ring can be worn in the ring slot, but does not give bonuses and does not provide any functions to the player, teleports or otherwise. Like all rings, they are not visible on player characters. They can be sold for up to 245.00 coins to Grum's Gold Exchange in Port Sarim.

Gold rings can be obtained as a reward from the Casket from the Pirate's Treasure quest, as a possible reward from the Capt' Arnav's Chest random event, from bird nests, from salvaging, or from crafting.

The ring itself has little use outside a few Treasure Trails clues.
1637:
The sapphire ring is made by using a gold bar on a furnace while having a sapphire and a ring mould in one's inventory. Making it requires a Crafting level of 20, and gives 40 experience.

Grum's Gold Exchange in Port Sarim buys at better price than High Alchemy, depending on his current stock. If he has no sapphire rings for sale, he buys the first for 630 coins.

They are dropped by Crawling Hands, and can also be obtained from bird nests. The sapphire ring can be enchanted into a ring of recoil by members with the Lvl-1 Enchant spell.
1639:
The Emerald ring is made by using a gold bar on a furnace whilst having an emerald and ring mould in the inventory. Making it requires a Crafting level of 27, and gives 55 experience.

The ring has no stats but can be enchanted using Lvl-2 Enchant ( 27 ) to make a ring of dueling.

Emerald rings can be sold to Grum's Gold Exchange in Port Sarim, starting at 892 coins each when none are in stock.
1643:
The diamond ring is made by using a gold bar, a cut diamond and a ring mould on a furnace. Making it requires a Crafting level of 43, and gives 85 experience.

The diamond ring can be enchanted into a ring of life by members through the use of the Lvl-4 Enchant spell.
1647: The Black ring is an interface item. It can be seen in the interface for crafting jewellery. If the player does not have the correct gem to craft a ring, the black ring appears in its place as a greyed out version.
1654:
The gold necklace is a piece of gold jewellery.

It has no stats and cannot be enchanted, making it purely cosmetic. However, it can be sold for 45-315 coins to Grum's Gold Exchange in Port Sarim, depending on how many he already has.

One can also be obtained in Varrock west bank basement, though 33 Magic for Telekinetic Grab or completion of Crack the Clue 3 is required.
1656:
The sapphire necklace is made by using a gold bar, a sapphire and a necklace mould on a furnace. This requires a Crafting level of 22 and gives 55 experience when made.

Grum's Gold Exchange in Port Sarim buys at a higher price than High Alchemy, if he has no sapphire necklaces for sale. He will buy the first for 735 coins, compared with the High Alchemy value of 630 coins. However, his price decreases in relation to the amount he has in stock, going below High Alchemy value when his stock goes above five.

Members may cast Lvl-1 Enchant on a sapphire necklace to turn it into a games necklace. This requires 7 Magic, one cosmic rune and one water rune, and grants 17.5 Magic experience.
1658:
The emerald necklace is made by using a gold bar on a furnace with an emerald and a necklace mould in your inventory. It requires a Crafting level of 29 and provides 60 experience when made.

The emerald necklace can be enchanted into a binding necklace by casting Lvl-2 Enchant. This requires a Magic level of 27, a cosmic rune and three air runes.

Emerald necklaces can be sold to Grum's Gold Exchange in Port Sarim, starting at 997 coins each if there are none in stock.
1662:
A Diamond necklace is made by using a gold bar, a diamond, and a necklace mould on a furnace. This requires level 56 Crafting and gives 90 Crafting experience.

A diamond necklace can be enchanted into a phoenix necklace by using the Lvl-4 Enchant spell. This requires level 57 Magic, one cosmic rune, and ten earth runes.
1664:
A dragon necklace, also known as a dragonstone necklace, is a necklace made by using a gold bar, a dragonstone and a necklace mould on a furnace, requiring a Crafting level of 72 and providing 105 experience when made. It can also be obtained as a reward from elite clue scrolls.

The dragon necklace can be enchanted into a skills necklace with the Lvl-5 Enchant spell. This requires level 68 Magic, one cosmic rune, fifteen earth runes and fifteen water runes.
1677:
An emerald amulet (u) can be made at level 31 Crafting by using a gold bar on a furnace while carrying a cut emerald and an amulet mould. This grants the player 70 Crafting experience. The amulet can then be strung with a ball of wool to create a strung emerald amulet, granting an additional 4 experience. The strung amulet can be enchanted into an amulet of defence using the Lvl-2 Enchant spell, requiring level 27 Magic.

This amulet can also be strung with a magic string instead, turning it into a pre-nature amulet. This amulet can then be enchanted into an amulet of nature.
1679:
A ruby amulet (u) is made by using a gold bar on a furnace, while having a cut ruby and an amulet mould in the inventory.

Level 50 Crafting is required to make one, giving 85 experience. When used with a Ball of wool, it becomes a ruby amulet, giving 4 experience. The ruby amulet can also be strung using the lunar spell String Jewellery, giving 83 Magic and 4 Crafting experience.

The ruby amulet can then be enchanted into an Amulet of strength through the use of the Lvl-3 Enchant spell, requiring 5 Fire runes, 1 Cosmic rune and level 49 Magic. This gives 59 experience.
1681:
A diamond amulet (u) is the unstrung version of the regular diamond amulet. It is made by using a gold bar on a furnace, while having a cut diamond and an amulet mould in the inventory.

Level 70 Crafting is required to make one, yielding 100 experience. When used with a ball of wool, it becomes a diamond amulet, giving 4 experience. After it is strung, it can be enchanted into an amulet of power, requiring level 57 Magic and yielding 67 experience.
1683:
A dragonstone amulet (u) is the unstrung version of the regular dragonstone amulet. It is made by using a gold bar on a furnace, while having a cut dragonstone and an amulet mould in the inventory.

Level 80 Crafting is required to make one, and crafting this item grants 150 experience. Stringing this item using a ball of wool gives 4 experience.

After it is strung, it can be enchanted into an Amulet of glory, which requires level 68 Magic and yields 78 experience. This is the highest level item that can be made with a dragonstone.
1696:
The emerald amulet is created by using a gold bar on a furnace while also carrying a cut emerald and an amulet mould. This requires 31 Crafting and grants 70 Crafting experience. The resulting unstrung amulet is then used with a ball of wool, granting an additional 4 experience.

It has no stat bonuses, but can be enchanted with the Lvl-2 Enchant spell to become an Amulet of defence which gives some defensive bonuses.

Emerald amulets can be sold to Grum's Gold Exchange in Port Sarim, starting at 892 coins each if there are none in stock.
1698:
A ruby amulet is made by using a gold bar on a furnace with a ruby and an amulet mould in the inventory. It requires a Crafting level of 50 or higher and provides 85 Crafting experience when made. The amulet must be strung before wearing or enchantment by using a ball of wool or the String Jewellery spell. Stringing provides 4 Crafting experience. A total of 174 Crafting experience is granted when cutting the ruby, making the amulet at a furnace and stringing the amulet.

The ruby amulet can be enchanted into an amulet of strength by players through the use of the Lvl-3 Enchant spell, which requires 5 fire runes, 1 cosmic rune, and a Magic level of 49 or higher. Ruby amulets can be sold to Grum's Gold Exchange in Port Sarim starting at 1,417 coins if there are none in stock.
1700:
A diamond amulet is an amulet created by using a ball of wool on a diamond amulet (u). Doing so, grants 4 Crafting experience.

The unstrung diamond amulet is created by using a gold bar and a diamond on a furnace with an amulet mould in the inventory. It is the fourth highest level amulet that can be created. This requires a Crafting level of 70 and provides 100 Crafting experience when made.

It can be turned into an amulet of power with Lvl-4 Enchant granting 67 magic experience.

An easier way for P2P ironmen to obtain one without level 70 Crafting is to loot the H.A.M. Store rooms.

The diamond amulet is the highest level craftable object that F2P can make.
1702:
The dragonstone amulet is an amulet worn in the neck slot. It is made by stringing an unstrung dragonstone amulet with a ball of wool or the String Jewellery spell. The unstrung amulet requires 80 Crafting and is made by using a gold bar on a furnace with a cut dragonstone and an amulet mould in the inventory.

Crafting one in the Neitiznot furnace is a task in the Elite Fremennik Diary.

The amulet can be enchanted with the Lvl-5 Enchant spell into an amulet of glory, where it gains the ability to teleport to Edgeville, Musa Point, Al Kharid, and Draynor Village when charged at the Fountain of Heroes, Fountain of Uhld and the Fountain of Rune.
1704:
The amulet of glory is a dragonstone amulet that has been enchanted by the Lvl-5 Enchant spell. After completion of Heroes' Quest, it can be charged at the Fountain of Heroes and the Fountain of Rune. When charged at the Fountain of Rune they will have 6 charges instead of the normal 4. With the completion of Dragon Slayer II, it can be charged at the Fountain of Uhld below the Myths' Guild. The amulet of glory is tradeable on the Grand Exchange only when it has zero, four, or six charges.

It is a very popular amulet in members-only worlds amongst players of all levels, as it provides good damage bonuses, has no requirements to wear, is much less expensive than the amulet of fury, and offers useful teleports.

Like other dragonstone jewellery, it is one of the few items with a teleportation ability that will work up to level 30 Wilderness, while most other means of teleportation will not work above level 20 Wilderness.

A trimmed version, the amulet of glory (t), may be obtained from hard Treasure Trails, but is no different than a normal amulet of glory aside from appearance and the inability to use it for certain Treasure Trail steps.

Certain Treasure Trail clue steps in the Hard, Elite and Master tiers require having an amulet of glory equipped, which can be difficult for ironmen, given the very high Crafting level of 80 required. However, this can be somewhat alleviated by using a mushroom pie to temporarily boost Crafting by 4 levels, meaning an actual Crafting level of 76 is required for these clue steps.
1706:
The amulet of glory is a dragonstone amulet that has been enchanted by the Lvl-5 Enchant spell. After completion of Heroes' Quest, it can be charged at the Fountain of Heroes and the Fountain of Rune. When charged at the Fountain of Rune they will have 6 charges instead of the normal 4. With the completion of Dragon Slayer II, it can be charged at the Fountain of Uhld below the Myths' Guild. The amulet of glory is tradeable on the Grand Exchange only when it has zero, four, or six charges.

However, this can be somewhat alleviated by using a mushroom pie to temporarily boost Crafting by 4 levels, meaning an actual Crafting level of 76 is required for these clue steps.
1710:
The amulet of glory is a dragonstone amulet that has been enchanted by the Lvl-5 Enchant spell. After completion of Heroes' Quest, it can be charged at the Fountain of Heroes and the Fountain of Rune. When charged at the Fountain of Rune they will have 6 charges instead of the normal 4. With the completion of Dragon Slayer II, it can be charged at the Fountain of Uhld below the Myths' Guild. The amulet of glory is tradeable on the Grand Exchange only when it has zero, four, or six charges.

It is a very popular amulet in members-only worlds amongst players of all levels, as it provides good damage bonuses, has no requirements to wear, is much less expensive than the amulet of fury, and offers useful teleports.

Like other dragonstone jewellery, it is one of the few items with a teleportation ability that will work up to level 30 Wilderness, while most other means of teleportation will not work above level 20 Wilderness.
