Note that it is possible to decant water into other containers, for example using a vial of water on an empty bucket. Doing this before refilling the waterskin will quadruple the amount of water refilled in the skin.

After completing Beneath Cursed Sands, a charged circlet of water can be used as an alternative to carrying waterskins, though it must be equipped to take effect.
1831:
A waterskin carries up to four servings of water, and provides protection against the desert heat effect in the Kharidian Desert. The amount of water will be noted by the waterskins name in parenthesis e.g. "Waterskin (4)" is a waterskin that is holding the maximum amount of water.

These can be bought from Shantay, in the Shantay Pass, south of Al Kharid. There are several ways to refill waterskins. In the table below, different methods of refilling are given, along with the amount of water doses are refilled by that method. Note that it is possible to decant water into other containers, for example using a vial of water on an empty bucket. Doing this before refilling the waterskin will quadruple the amount of water refilled in the skin.

After completing Beneath Cursed Sands, a charged circlet of water can be used as an alternative to carrying waterskins, though it must be equipped to take effect.
1833:
Desert shirts are suitable for desert environments, like the Kharidian Desert south of Shantay Pass. When worn, this clothing item delays the desert heat effect by 12 additional seconds. It has no other bonuses.

A full set of desert clothing is needed for the The Tourist Trap quest. They are given to a slave miner in exchange for a set of slave robes to allow the player access to a deeper area of the mining camp.

During the Shadow of the Storm quest, the desert shirt can be changed into a black desert shirt when it is dyed using black dye. Note that the black desert shirt will no longer offer protection from the desert heat.
1835:
Desert robes are suitable for desert environments, like the Kharidian Desert south of Shantay Pass. When worn, this clothing item delays the desert heat effect by 12 additional seconds. It has no other bonuses.

A full set of desert clothing is needed for the The Tourist Trap quest. They are given to a slave miner in exchange for a set of slave robes to allow the player access to a deeper area of the mining camp.

During the Shadow of the Storm quest, a desert robe can be changed into a black desert robe when it is dyed using black dye. Note that the black desert robe will no longer offer protection from the desert heat.
1837:
Desert boots are boots suitable for desert environments such as the Kharidian Desert south of Shantay Pass. Wearing the boots delays the desert heat effect by 6 additional seconds. The boots have no other bonuses.

A full set of desert clothing is needed for the The Tourist Trap quest. They are given to a slave miner in exchange for a set of slave robes which permit the player to access a deeper area of the mining camp.
1842: Ana in a barrel is the result of using a barrel on Ana, which is used to smuggle her out of the mining camp she has been imprisoned in, and is a quest item used by the player during The Tourist Trap quest. If a player drops the barrel, Ana will climb out of it, and she will appear in the mines again. Players who attempt to teleport out while carrying her will drop the barrel first.
1843:
The Wrought iron key is a reward from the Tourist Trap quest. It opens a door deep inside the Desert mining camp and allows passage to a special mining area inside. If you lose it, it can be replaced by searching one of the tables in the building located inside the Desert Mining Camp.

This key allows access to the north-western most tunnel (after riding the cart underground) that has several higher rocks for mining including adamantite ore and mithril ore bearing rocks.

This key can be placed on the steel key ring.
1844:
The slave shirt is an item of clothing that is required to enter the mine undetected in The Tourist Trap quest. Players obtain this item by trading a desert shirt with a slave during the quest. Rowdy slaves can also be killed in the mine to drop it.

Wearing the slave shirt will delay the onset of desert heat by 6 seconds.
1845:
The slave robe is an item of clothing that is required to enter the mine undetected in The Tourist Trap quest. Players obtain this item by trading a desert robe with a slave during the quest. Rowdy slaves can also be killed in the mine to drop it.

Wearing the slave robe will delay the onset of desert heat by 6 seconds.
1846:
The slave boots are an item of clothing that is required to enter the mine undetected in The Tourist Trap quest. Players obtain this item by trading desert boots with a slave during the quest. Rowdy slaves can also be killed in the mine to drop it.

Wearing the slave boots will delay the onset of desert heat by 3 seconds.
1847:
A scrumpled paper is a recipe for Ugthanki kebabs that is dropped by Shantay (found in the Shantay Pass) when a player talks to him. To get one quickly, players can spam the "Talk-to" option until one is dropped.

When one is dropped on the ground, the message Something drops out of Shantay's pocket onto the floor. It looks like a piece of paper. is given.
1848: The Shantay disclaimer was an item that was given to players passing through the Shantay Pass, saying that no responsibility is taken if the player dies in the desert. By retaining one, players were able to skip a long-winded dialogue explaining the dangers of entering the desert. This system was replaced with the Doomsayer in July 2007, and the shantay disclaimers were removed. As a result, they have never been obtainable in Old School RuneScape.
1849:
The prototype dart is a quest item made during the Tourist Trap quest. It is made by smithing a prototype dart tip on an experimental anvil that is not visible on the Minimap. 10 Fletching experience is given after attaching the feather.

Should the player have a spare (via the drop trick) and speak to Al Shabim (after the quest section is complete or after completing the quest), he will confiscate the item and exclaim: Where did you get this from Effendi! I'll have to confiscate this for your own safety!
1850:
The technical plans are a quest item from The Tourist Trap quest. You bring these plans for a weapon to the Bedabin nomads and use their experimental anvil to make it. After you've shown the prototype to Al Shabim, he takes the plans from you.

The first option on this item is "Read", if you read it, this comes up: The plans look very technical! But you can see that this item will require a bronze bar and at least 10 feathers. Upon completing the quest, it will instead read: Some technical looking plans.

Should the player have duplicated the item (via the drop trick) Al Shabim will retake the plans from the player upon continuing his dialogue.
1852: The Bedabin key is a key used during the Tourist Trap quest to open a chest in Captain Siad's room. It can be obtained from the Bedabin Camp north-west of Pollnivneach.
1853: A prototype dart tip is a quest item used in Tourist Trap. It can be made by using a bronze bar on an experimental anvil in the Bedabin Camp. If used on a feather, it will create a prototype dart.
1855: Rock or rocks may refer to any of the following:
1857:
The totem is a holy relic of the Rantuki Tribe. It is a quest item used only in Tribal Totem. Lord Handelmort of Ardougne had stolen it from the Rantuki Tribe and the player is asked by Kangai Mau, a member of the tribe, to retrieve it.

The player can acquire multiple totems in the quest by using the drop trick.
1858:
The address label is an item used during Tribal Totem. Players can obtain it by searching the double-stacked crates south-east of the southernmost bank in East Ardougne in the GPDT Depot.

The player must then use the label on the teleport block created by Wizard Cromperty so that it is delivered to Lord Handelmort's Mansion, after which the player can teleport into his house to continue the quest.
1861:
Ugthanki meat is a type of food that restores 3 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking raw ugthanki meat, granting 40 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt meat. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Ugthanki meat is unusual as despite lacking a cooking requirement, it never stops burning altogether even at level 99. At levels up to 82, the chance to burn this meat is higher on a range than on a fire.

Ugthanki meat is used to make ugthanki kebab which restores 19 hitpoints.
1863:
Pitta dough is created by mixing a pot of flour with either a bucket of water, bowl of water, or jug of water. It can be cooked on a range (not a fire) to make pitta bread.

Unlike many cooking recipes, this item cannot be burned, even though the burnt version exists. This is because players can no longer burn it by the time they have the level required to cook it.

While this item is tradeable, it cannot be sold on the Grand Exchange.
1865:
Pitta bread are a type of food used to make Ugthanki kebabs, and can be obtained by baking pitta dough on a cooking range, requiring level 58 Cooking and granting 40 experience when successful. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 37 on ranges. However, since the Cooking requirement is level 58, it can never be burned.

Players can make pitta dough with level 58 Cooking by combining a pot of flour with a jug or bucket of water. They can then use the cooked pitta bread with kebab mix to complete an ugthanki kebab.
1867:
Burnt pitta bread is the result of accidentally burning pitta dough while attempting to make pitta bread. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 37.

However, since pitta bread cannot be made until level 58 Cooking, burnt pitta bread cannot be obtained via normal means. The method used to obtain a burnt oomlie wrap cannot be used, since using chill to drain from 58 to 36 Cooking would take longer than it takes to cook a full inventory of pitta bread. Furthermore, pitta dough can only be cooked at a range, which are not found in proximity to areas with the chill effect.

If it were possible, attempting to use a burnt pitta bread with kebab mix would give the message "This pitta is too burnt to make an edible kebab."
1875: Onion & tomato is a type of food that restores 3 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by using chopped onion with a tomato or using chopped tomato with an onion. Creating Onion & tomato is one of multiple steps needed to create the ugthanki kebab which requires level 58 Cooking and restores 19 Hitpoints.
1887:
A cake tin is an item used to bake cakes. Players need to add an egg, a pot of flour and a bucket of milk on to the cake tin and used in an oven.

They can be found in the Cooks' Guild, bought from any general store (except for the ones in Port Phasmatys, Ardougne, Port Khazard, Canifis, Keldagrim, Auburnvale, and Burthorpe), bought from the Culinaromancer's Chest in Lumbridge, or taken from the wooden shelves from a player-owned house. The cake tin also respawns at the house with an anvil in the level 21 Wilderness.

Once baked, the cake tin will separate from the cooked cake, unlike the pie dish, where it comes with the pie.

One cake tin is needed for the quest Troll Romance to make wax.
1889: Uncooked cake can be made with the Cooking skill by using an egg, a bucket of milk, and a pot of flour with a cake tin. To bake a cake, players must use it on a range with level 40+ Cooking. This will either turn the uncooked cake into a Cake or it will burn the cake (burnt cakes have no use). After cooking the cake, successfully or burnt, the player will receive back their cake tin. Optionally, at Cooking level 50+, players may then use a chocolate bar (which can be found in the Cooks' Guild) or chocolate dust on the cake to make a chocolate cake.
1897:
Chocolate cake is a type of food that restores 15 Hitpoints in total, 3 bites each healing for 5. It can be obtained by using a chocolate bar or chocolate dust on a cake, requiring level 50 Cooking and granting 30 experience. Both ingredients can be bought from the Ardougne Baker's Stall.

Chocolate cake is a reward from the quest Gertrude's Cat, and optionally from The Dig Site when not choosing the fruit blast as a reward. It will also be served by the butler when asked to prepare food in your player-owned house.

One chocolate cake is needed for the quest A Tail of Two Cats.
1899:
Chocolate cake is a type of food that restores 15 Hitpoints in total, 3 bites each healing for 5. It can be obtained by using a chocolate bar or chocolate dust on a cake, requiring level 50 Cooking and granting 30 experience. Both ingredients can be bought from the Ardougne Baker's Stall.

Chocolate cake is a reward from the quest Gertrude's Cat, and optionally from The Dig Site when not choosing the fruit blast as a reward. It will also be served by the butler when asked to prepare food in your player-owned house.

One chocolate cake is needed for the quest A Tail of Two Cats.
1901:
Chocolate cake is a type of food that restores 15 Hitpoints in total, 3 bites each healing for 5. It can be obtained by using a chocolate bar or chocolate dust on a cake, requiring level 50 Cooking and granting 30 experience. Both ingredients can be bought from the Ardougne Baker's Stall.

Chocolate cake is a reward from the quest Gertrude's Cat, and optionally from The Dig Site when not choosing the fruit blast as a reward. It will also be served by the butler when asked to prepare food in your player-owned house.

One chocolate cake is needed for the quest A Tail of Two Cats.
1903:
Burnt cake is the result of accidentally burning an uncooked cake while attempting to bake a cake. The burn rate will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 74.

A burnt cake has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.
1905:
Asgarnian ale is a type of ale that restores 1 Hitpoint and temporarily boosts Strength by 2 while draining Attack by ⌊Level×5100⌋+2 (see table below). It can be obtained through brewing at level 24 Cooking granting 248 experience. It is brewed using 2 buckets of water, 2 barley malt, 4 asgarnian hops, and a pot of ale yeast. The stronger, mature version of the ale is the Asgarnian ale(m).

4 Asgarnian ales are required during the Recipe for Disaster Dwarf subquest, where they are turned into Asgoldian ale by using a coin on them. One is also required for the Death Plateau quest.
1907:
The wizard's mind bomb is a type of ale that restores 1 Hitpoint and temporarily boosts Magic by +2 (+3 if level 50+ Magic) while draining Attack, Strength and Defence by ⌊Level×0.05⌋+1 (see table below). It can be obtained through brewing at level 34 Cooking, granting 314 experience per batch. It is brewed using 2 buckets of water, 2 barley malt, 4 yanillian hops, and a pot of ale yeast. It can also be bought from several shops.

The stronger, mature version of the ale is the mature wmb.

It is required for the quest Dragon Slayer I, and may also be used in Below Ice Mountain in place of a regular beer.
1909:
Greenman's ale is a type of ale that restores 1 Hitpoint and temporarily boosts Herblore by 1 while also draining Attack, Strength, and Defence by 3 when consumed. It can be obtained through brewing at level 29 Cooking, granting 281 experience per batch. It is brewed using 2 buckets of water, 2 barley malt, 4 harralander, and a pot of ale yeast. The stronger, mature version of the ale is the Greenman's ale (m).

One is required for the quest Recipe for Disaster/Another Cook's Quest.
1911: Dragon bitter is a type of ale that restores 1 Hitpoint and temporarily boosts Strength by 2 while draining Attack by 5% + 2. It can be obtained through brewing at level 39 Cooking granting 347 experience. It is brewed using 4 krandorian hops, 2 buckets of water, 2 lots of barley, and a pot of ale yeast. The stronger, mature version of the ale is the dragon bitter(m).
1915: Grog is a type of ale that restores 3 Hitpoints and temporarily boosts Strength by 4% + 1 and drains Attack by 5% + 3. Unlike other ales, it cannot be brewed.
1921:
A bowl of water is made by using a normal bowl on a water source that is not a well. The Humidify spell will also turn any empty bowls the player is carrying into bowls of water. Players can use a bowl of water on a stove or a fire to create a bowl of hot water.

Adding some nettles will make it into nettle-water, and if this is heated it will turn into nettle tea. You also can make an incomplete stew by using a potato on the bowl of water, and people do this to make easy profit. Bowls of water, just like buckets and jugs of water, can be combined with pots of flour to make any kind of dough, though this is less commonly done.

A bowl of water cannot be used to counter the desert heat effect as the water evaporates under the heat. The water can, however, be transferred into a waterskin from the bowl.

One bowl of water respawns in the house inside the Desert Mining Camp.
1923:
A bowl is a vessel used primarily in Cooking to hold water, stew, curry, kebab mix, etc.

Bowls can be created by using a piece of soft clay on a potter's wheel and then firing the unfired bowl in a pottery oven. Players may also choose to take bowls from the Mess Hall utensil cupboard and bank them at the bank chest to the south-east.

A player is required to make a bowl in Barbarian Village as part of the easy Varrock Achievement Diary.
1927:
A bucket of milk is a Cooking ingredient used to make a variety of drinks and foods such as choc saturdays and cakes, as well as several feeders. Players can use a bucket on a dairy cow or dairy buffalo to create a bucket of milk, or simply click on the cow or buffalo with at least one empty bucket in the inventory.

Players can turn a bucket of milk into chocolatey milk by adding chocolate dust, or add milk to nettle tea (though this does not add any effects). Depending on their Cooking level, Members can use a dairy churn to turn a bucket of milk into a pot of cream, a pat of butter, or a piece of cheese.

A bucket of milk is required to complete the quests Cook's Assistant, Gertrude's Cat, Plague City (to make a Hangover cure), and the Skippy and the Mogres miniquest (to make a hangover cure).

This, alongside the chocolatey milk, milky mixture, and hangover cure, can be stored in a bottomless milk bucket. Each bottomless milk bucket can only store one type of dairy product at a time.
1929:
A bucket of water is made by using a bucket on a water source such as a fountain, a sink or a well. A bucket is the only vessel that can be filled from a well.

Like other vessels filled with water, a bucket of water has everyday uses such as transforming clay into soft clay. A bucket of water can also be used to fill a watering can.

A bucket of water is also used in quests such as Plague City (to soften the soil outside Edmond's house) and Clock Tower (to cool the black cog).

For ironmen, one of the fastest methods to fill buckets with water is in the Lumbridge cellar. Use the Culinaromancer's Chest in the cellar to bank and the nearby sink to fill the buckets. If you have access to the Hosidius kitchen, there is a pump directly next to a bank chest. The Lunar Spellbook spell Humidify can also be used to quickly fill all empty buckets in your inventory all at once.
1935:
A Jug is an item that can be filled with water to create a jug of water. Wine can also be made by adding grapes to a jug of water.

Jugs can be bought at general stores for one coin each. Jugs are not sold at the Catherby, East Ardougne, or West Ardougne general store. However, jugs are sold by the charter crew members in Catherby. Wine Shop in Draynor Village sells them for the same price as the general stores, and they can be thieved from the stall. Hassan at the Al Kharid palace may also give free jugs of water if the player has not completed Prince Ali Rescue.

Jugs can also be found at their spawn points in the basement of Lumbridge Castle, the Crafting Guild, the Cooks' Guild (top floor), and some other kitchens.

Jugs can only be filled with water from sinks, fountains and with the Lunar spell Humidify. They cannot be filled with water from wells; upon attempting to do so, a player receives the message "If I drop my jug down there, I don't think I'm likely to get it back." Also, jugs can be filled by filling another vessel with water and then using it on the jug (e.g. filling a bucket from a well, then using the bucket of water on the jug).
1937:
A jug of water is a jug filled up on a water source such as a fountain or sink; it cannot be filled using a well. The humidify spell will also turn any empty jugs in the player's inventory into jugs of water. Jugs of water cannot be consumed; they are only used in the making of other things, such as: doughs, jugs of wine, soft clay, mud pie, and filling waterskins.

A free jug of water can be obtained by speaking with Hassan in the Al Kharid Palace.

One jug of water is required during the Monk's Friend quest to sober up Brother Cedric.

The closest water source to a bank for filling many jugs is the Hosidius Kitchen, but banks in the Farming Guild or Aldarin also have nearby water sources, along with the Lumbridge Castle basement if the Recipe for Disaster quest has been started.

In free-to-play, the closest water source to a bank would be the Waterpump next to the Hairdresser going to Falador west bank; another close water source to a bank would be the water fountain in the centre of Varrock square going to Varrock west bank.
1939:
Swamp tar is a thick substance found in the Lumbridge Swamp, Mort Myre Swamp, and in tar barrels.

Swamp tar can be turned into swamp paste, which is used for various repairing purposes. It can also be distilled into lamp oil, which is used as fuel for various light sources, or be used to make guam, marrentill, tarromin, harralander, and irit tar, which are used as bait and ammunition for salamanders.
1941:
Swamp paste is made by mixing flour with swamp tar to make raw swamp paste, and then cooking the mixture on a fire, yielding 2 Cooking experience. It cannot be cooked on a range. It is possible to burn the tar, though it is automatically discarded. Swamp tar spawns in Lumbridge Swamp and Mort Myre Swamp.

To make a large amount of swamp paste from swamp tar, use a barrel of flour at either the Sinclair Mansion or Gordon and Mary's farm. Bring as much swamp tar as needed and 26 pots, Gordon's farm also has a pot spawn. Click the barrel to fill the pots, then combine with the swamp tar to create raw swamp paste. Repeat this until the desired amount is obtained, then cook it. A permanent fire is recommended for large amounts. There is a permanent fire at the base of Mount Karuulm, very near the fairy ring and in front of the shack with a rope spawn.

Swamp paste can also be bought from the Trader crewmembers at any of the ports in the Charter ship network, the Khazard General Store (south of Ardougne), and Rasolo (west of the Fishing Guild) are very useful for some of the quests listed below. It is also sold at the Mort'ton Builder's Store.

Swamp paste also tends to be rewarded in abundance when unlocking chests within the Shades of Mort'ton minigame.

Unlike swamp tar, swamp paste cannot be combined with herbs to form ammunition for a Salamander using the Herblore skill.
1942:
Raw potatoes are a food item that can be picked from fields around Gielinor or grown through the Farming skill at level 1 with potato seeds. They heal 1 hitpoint when eaten raw. When picking potatoes from fields, members may randomly receive 1 potato seed.

They are used in the following recipes:

Baked potato (must be cooked on a range, not a fire)

Veg ball (Gnome cooking)

Stew

Curry

Fish pie (admiral and regular, which temporarily boost Fishing level by 5 and 3, respectively)

Raw potatoes are purchasable from various stores for 1 coin each. Hudo at the Grand Tree has a stock of 10; Cobado's Groceries a stock of 10; Frenita in Yanille a stock of 5; and Wydin in Port Sarim a stock of 1, to name a few.

Members can store up to 10 potatoes in an empty sack, creating a sack of potatoes. 1 sack of potatoes is needed to protect growing onions. Adding potatoes to a compost bin makes regular compost.
1946:
Flour was an item that could be obtained by killing black knights in RuneScape Classic. It could not normally be picked up, and players were intended to use a pot on it in order to obtain a pot of flour. However, it was possible to obtain the heap of flour by casting Telekinetic Grab. Upon the release of RuneScape 2, knights were changed to drop a regular pot of flour instead, initially making it one of the rarest discontinued items in the game.

Flour was inadvertently made obtainable again with the release of Player-owned Houses, as the Teak larder gave this item instead due to an oversight. Since it was useless in cooking, players could only bake by dropping the flour and picking it up with a pot.

As a result of this fiasco, all existing flour were transformed into pots of flour, including those obtained during RuneScape Classic. Therefore, it has never been obtainable in Old School RuneScape.
1949:
A chef's hat is a white hat that grants players access to the Cooks' Guild with a Cooking level of 32. Aside from this, it has little practical use and is purely cosmetic.

It can be obtained as a drop from multiple monsters, most notably goblins, and can be purchased from the Shayzien Styles store in Shayzien.

Members can obtain an infinite supply from Teak shelves 2 in a player-owned house using the Construction skill.
1951:
Redberries can be harvested from a bush patch after planting redberry seeds or picked from wild redberry bushes. They are used in Cooking to make redberry pies, or to create red dye.

Adding redberries to a compost bin makes regular compost, and using them on the Rocky pet will change his appearance to Red, a red panda.

Redberries are unpalatably tart in their uncooked form, and cannot be eaten. They are native to Misthalin but have been cultivated across Gielinor.
1953:
Pastry dough is used to make pies. It is made from a pot of flour and either a bucket of water, bowl of water, or jug of water. It can then be used on a pie dish to make a pie shell. The pie shell is then used with the filling, which varies according to which pie is to be made.

Pastry dough can also be made as a source of money. By buying or making one pot of flour, and one bucket of water or jug of water, then mixing the ingredients together, selling the dough will give profit.
1957:
Onions are a food item that can be picked from fields around Gielinor or grown through the Farming skill at level 5 with onion seeds. They heal 1 hitpoint when eaten. When eaten, the message You eat the onion. is displayed. If eaten at full health, a message will appear saying, It's always sad to see a grown [man/woman/person] cry.. If eaten below full health, the message It makes your eyes water, but it does heal some health. is displayed instead. When picking onions from fields, members may randomly receive 1 onion seed.

They are used in the following recipes:

Mushroom potato

Ugthanki kebab

Vegetable batta, veg ball, worm hole (Gnome cooking)

Garden pie (temporarily boosts Farming level by 3)

Onions are purchasable from various stores for 3 coins each. Hudo at the Grand Tree has a stock of 10; Cobado's Groceries a stock of 10; and the Greengrocers of Miscellania a stock of 10, to name a few.

Unlimited onions can be taken from teak larders inside a player-owned house. They can also be gathered from the Theatre of Blood chest if the player died during certain fights. An onion spawns on the 1st floor of the Lumbridge General Store. There is an onion farming field located just north of Rimmington where 15 onions can be collected.

Members can store up to 10 onions in an empty sack, creating a sack of onions. 1 sack of onions is needed to protect growing cabbages and Asgarnian hops. Adding onions to a compost bin makes regular compost.

Two onions are used in creating yellow dye by taking them to either Aggie or Ali the dyer.
1959:
Pumpkins are the first holiday food rare and second holiday rare to be dropped, the first being the scythe. Pumpkins can be obtained by completing one of the Halloween holiday events that occur once per year. This also rewards the player with all other holiday items associated with Halloween.

If you plan to sell your pumpkin, it is recommended that you put it in note form to avoid accidentally eating it.

When eaten, the pumpkin heals 14 hitpoints. However, due to their price, it is not recommended to consume pumpkins, as they heal just as much as a swordfish, which is much cheaper.

Previously, they were obtainable during the 2013 Rare Drops event (from 10 June to 17 June) as part of a rare item drop.

Since the 2014 Halloween Event, Jagex decided to host a number of events in-game, most of which were live-streamed. They gave community leaders and other familiar faces an item that could be used to scatter pumpkins. Doing this allows for more consistent and varied events throughout the holiday period.
1969:
Spinach roll is a food item that restores 2 hitpoints when eaten. It is received as a reward from random events such as the Mysterious Old Man and Rick Turpentine, or looted from opening a Crystal chest, Christmas cracker or Barrel.

During Demon Slayer, Traiborn will give players a spinach roll if they choose chat options ( 3•2•1)…When eaten, the messages You eat the spinach roll. and It tastes a bit weird, but it fills you up. are displayed.
1973:
A chocolate bar is a food item that heals 3 Hitpoints when eaten. It is used as an ingredient in Cooking but can also be ground to chocolate dust using a pestle and mortar or a knife, which is required for the Plague City quest.

When eaten, the message You eat the chocolate bar. is displayed.

The chocolate bar can be added to a cake with 50 Cooking to create a chocolate cake.

Chocolate bars spawn in the Cooks' Guild, Zanaris, or in The Culinaromancer's Chest during and after the Recipe for Disaster quest. After full completion of Recipe for Disaster the Culinaromancer's Chest stocks 50 chocolate bars which can easily be bought and banked before hopping worlds. Chocolate bars can also be bought from each of the bakers' stalls in Ardougne market place for 10 coins; their stocks are 7 and 9.
1975:
Chocolate dust is made by using a knife or a pestle and mortar with a chocolate bar. It can also be obtained by bringing Wesley in Nardah noted chocolate bars, who will crush them for you for a fee of 50 coins per item. Chocolate dust can be bought from Hudo and Heckel Funch at the Grand Tree.

It is used for making energy potions in Herblore, chocolate cake for food or chef's delight by brewing. It is also used to make chocolatey milk.
1977:
Chocolatey milk is a type of untradeable drink that restores 4 Hitpoints when drunk. It can be obtained by using chocolate dust on a bucket of milk. Chocolate dust can be obtained by using a knife or pestle and mortar on a chocolate bar. Unlike other dairy products, it cannot be made using a dairy churn.

Chocolatey milk can be used with snape grass to create a Hangover cure which is required for the Plague City quest and the Skippy and the Mogres miniquest.

This, alongside the bucket of milk, milky mixture, and hangover cure, can be stored in a bottomless milk bucket. Each bottomless milk bucket can only store one type of dairy product at a time.
1978:
A cup of tea is a drink which restores 3 Hitpoints and temporarily boosts Attack by 2 + 2% (rounded down); it will also instantly cancel the effect of the goading potion. Upon drinking a cup of tea, the player will exclaim Aaah, nothing like a nice cuppa tea! and an empty cup will remain in the player's inventory.

Tea may be purchased at Ye olde Tea Shoppe in Varrock or stolen at the nearby Tea stall with 5 Thieving.

A tea flask may be used to store up to five cups of tea, which will have the standard effect when consumed.
1982:
Tomatoes are a food item mainly used in Cooking. They can be grown through the Farming skill at level 12 with tomato seeds. Eating one heals 2 hitpoints.

They are used in the following recipes:

Ugthanki kebab

Egg potato

Cheese+tom batta, vegetable batta (Gnome cooking)

Pizza base ingredient

Garden pie (temporarily boosts Farming level by 3)

Tomatoes are purchasable from various stores for 4 coins each. Hudo at the Grand Tree has a stock of 10; Cobado's Groceries a stock of 10; Pollnivneach general store a stock of 5; and Wydin in Port Sarim a stock of 3, to name a few. The culinaromancer's chest in the Lumbridge Castle cellar also sells them in high quantities.

Members can store up to 5 tomatoes in a basket, creating a basket of tomatoes. Baskets of tomatoes are needed to protect growing Yanillian hops (x1), cadavaberry bushes (x3), and oak trees (x1). Adding tomatoes to a compost bin makes regular compost; however, a full bin of tomatoes produces a bin of rotten tomatoes instead.
1984:
The rotten apple is a quest item used only in Biohazard and Mourning's End Part I. Although they have an "Eat" option, rotten apples may not be eaten, attempting to do so will result in the message Nothing interesting happens..

In Biohazard, it is used to poison the stew to enter the Mourner's Headquarters while wearing a medical gown.

They are aesthetically similar to rotten tomatoes, although appear duller in colour and differ slightly in shape. Duplicates can be obtained after completing the quests, but it serves no further use.
1985:
Cheese is a food item which heals 2 hitpoints when eaten. Its primary use is an ingredient in other dishes, including pizza and a baked potato with cheese.

Cheese can be bought from Port Sarim, in the Grand Tree, or from the Culinaromancer's chest in Lumbridge. Members can make some by using a bucket of milk on a dairy churn at level 48 Cooking, giving 64 Cooking experience. A pot of cream can also be churned into cheese, giving 46 Cooking experience, as well as a pat of butter or not garlic butter, which both give 23.5 Cooking experience.

Cheese also spawns in Aggie's house in Draynor Village, and the cooking shop in the Bandit Camp (Wilderness). Cheese may also be found in teak larders inside of player-owned houses.

It is used in the Witch's House quest, the Ratcatchers quest, and optionally in the Mourning's End Part II quest.
1987:
Grapes can be produced through planting grape seeds at the Hosidius Vinery, requiring level 36 in Farming. They are also dropped in noted form by several bosses. They can also be obtained from the Vineyard foreman in Aldarin by harvesting his Grapevines for him.

They are an ingredient for making a jug of wine at level 35 Cooking by using them on a jug of water, which grants 200 Cooking experience when fermented after a short period. If fermentation fails, a jug of bad wine will be created instead. Players stop creating jugs of bad wine when they reach 68 Cooking.

A bunch of grapes is also required for Monkey Madness II.
1989:
Half full wine jugs are rewards given out during various holiday events. Drinking a half full wine jug will restore 7 Hitpoints, and like normal wine, will temporarily decrease Attack by 2.

A regular jug of wine cannot be drunk to make a half full wine jug, nor can two half full jugs be decanted to make a full jug. Interestingly, the half full wine jug heals more than half of a regular jug of wine.

It is not advised to drink half full wine jugs as they are more expensive than most other food items that heal just as much or more. They are more valuable as a collector's item.
1991:
A jug of bad wine is obtained when a player attempts to ferment grapes or Zamorak's grapes and fails, similar to burning food. To ferment grapes, a Cooking level of at least 35 is needed. Fermenting grapes is no longer failed at a Cooking level of 68, while Zamorak's grapes cease to fail at level 98.

A player does not receive any Cooking experience when the player's unfermented wine or Zamorak's unfermented wine goes bad. Players can drink the bad wine, but this will temporarily reduce the player's Attack level by 3. This is more than the 2 level reduction from wine, and it also does not heal. Drinking more jugs of bad wine will stack this effect.

Should players wish to get rid of all their jugs of bad wine from their bank, the incinerator can destroy stacks of items from within the bank interface.
1992:
A Jug of bad wine is an unobtainable version of the Jug of bad wine. Bad wines could previously be traded and turned into bank notes; however, they were made untradeable in 2007 due to frequent use in scams where players conflated them with Half full wine jugs. Any player who had a noted bad wine was given this now discontinued item. It is identical to the real wine, except it is stackable.

As this change occurred prior to August 2007, the item has never been obtainable in Old School RuneScape.
1993:
A jug of wine is a type of drink that restores 11 Hitpoints and temporarily lowers Attack by 2, leaving behind an empty jug after consumption. It can be obtained by using grapes with a jug of water, requiring level 35 Cooking. The process of fermenting takes 12 seconds, but if another jug of wine is created within this time period, the 12 seconds restart. When the process is finished, all unfermented wine in the player's inventory or bank will ferment. Each jug of wine grants 200 Cooking experience, but every jug that fails to ferment becomes a jug of bad wine instead. The fail rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will stop failing entirely at Cooking level 68.

Jugs of wine can be blessed at the exposed altar in Ralos' Rise to create a jug of blessed wine.

The Culinaromancer's Chest sells both jugs and grapes and has a nearby sink for filling the jug, making it an ideal location for creating jugs of wine. They may also be purchased, with the closest shop to a bank being Sunlight's Sanctum in Aldarin which offers an unlimited supply. Furthermore, there is a bank deposit box outside this bank, closer to Sunlight's Sanctum than the bankers.

Wine is notable for its affordability and accessibility which makes it a popular low cost food, especially for activities that do not excessively utilise run energy as it is notably heavy. Making wines is also a cheap and effective method of training Cooking; for more details, see here.
1995:
An Unfermented wine is created when a player with a Cooking level of 35 or more uses grapes with a jug of water. After 12 seconds, this item will automatically turn to either a jug of wine, granting 200 Cooking experience, or a jug of bad wine, granting none. With 14 wines possible per inventory, each inventory grants you 2800 experience once fermented. The player will also stop making bad wine at level 68 Cooking.

Wine ferments on a single 12 second timer that resets each time the player makes a new jug of unfermented wine, whether banked or in their inventory. This means that any stack of wine in their bank will ferment all at once. Due to that, players can obtain massive amounts of experience in one tick.
2001:
Uncooked stew is an inedible food made using the Cooking skill. It is created by adding a raw potato and either cooked meat or cooked chicken into a bowl of water; the product is the same regardless of which type of meat is used. The ingredients can be added in any order.

Adding a first ingredient creates an incomplete stew and adding the second ingredient creates the uncooked stew. It can then be cooked at level 25 Cooking to make stew, granting 117 experience. Alternatively, adding three curry leaves or one spice before cooking the stew produces an uncooked curry, which can be cooked at level 60 Cooking to make curry, granting 280 experience.
2003:
Stew is a type of food that restores 11 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking uncooked stew on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 25 Cooking and granting 117 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt stew. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Stew is one of a number of foods with a reduced burn rate while using the Lumbridge Castle range with Cook's Assistant completed. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 58, or 54 when using the Lumbridge range.

Stew is the starting ingredient for spicy stew.

A maid in a player-owned house can make a stew for the player.

Many stews are needed for the Freeing Evil Dave Recipe for Disaster sub-quest, as well as one stew for the The Queen of Thieves quest.
2005:
Burnt stew is the result of accidentally burning an uncooked stew while attempting to make stew. Cooking stew requires 25 Cooking. Players will stop burning stews at level 58 Cooking.

The burnt stew has no use whatsoever, although it can be emptied to reclaim a bowl. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.
2007:
Spice is an item used in Cooking. It can be bought from the Culinaromancer's Chest after completing the beginning portion of Recipe for Disaster or from spice stalls in Ardougne, Civitas illa Fortis, and Prifddinas. It can also be stolen from those stalls with level 65 Thieving or looted from a Gourmet impling or Baby impling.

You need spice in the goblin sub-quest of Recipe for Disaster, as well as for the Desert Treasure I quest.

Spice can be used to make Curry in place of 3 Curry leaves.
2009:
Uncooked curry is made by adding a potato and either cooked meat or cooked chicken to a bowl of water (in any order) to create uncooked stew, then adding either three curry leaves or one spice. The final product is the same regardless of which of the two types of meat is used.

At level 60 Cooking, it can be cooked to make curry, granting 280 experience. Burning it will produce burnt curry. The player stops burning curry at level 74 Cooking.

When making this item from the bank via the ingredients bowl of water, cooked meat or cooked chicken, a potato, and spice, a player should be able to yield 14 (uncooked curry) in 60 seconds.
2011:
Curry is a type of food that restores 19 Hitpoints when eaten. An empty bowl will remain after consumption. It can be obtained by cooking uncooked curry on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 60 Cooking and granting 280 experience when successful. When cooking, there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt curry. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 74.

At 50 Construction, a demon butler can be hired, who can serve curry in player-owned houses. The number of curries served is equal to the number of people in the house, up to 10.

Curry is popular for fighting the Chaos Elemental and Chaos Fanatic, as the left-over empty bowls prevent these enemies' special attacks from un-equipping worn equipment into what would otherwise be empty inventory slots.
2013:
Burnt curry is the result of accidentally burning uncooked curry while attempting to make curry. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 74.

The burnt curry has no use whatsoever, although it can be emptied to reclaim the bowl. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.
2017:
Whisky is an alcoholic beverage that heals 5 hitpoints and temporarily increases Strength by 5% + 1 and decreases Attack by 2% + 3. It is also used as an ingredient to make the gnome drink choc saturday. It, along with the other gnome drinks, is often used at player parties or other events.

There are several ways to obtain whisky: it can be bought from Heckel Funch at the 1st floor of the Grand Tree, from The Asp & Snake Bar in Pollnivneach, from Jossik at the 1st floor of the Lighthouse, from Atlazora's Rest in Outer Fortis, or from The Flaming Arrow in Civitas illa Fortis. It can also obtained for free by searching Grip's cupboard (while Grip and the guards are dead) in Scarface's mansion from the Heroes' Quest.
2021: Brandy is an alcoholic drink which can be purchased at Jossik's store in the Lighthouse, at the Tree Gnome Stronghold in Heckel Funch's store or at the Asp & Snake Bar at Pollnivneach. It is an ingredient in the gnome cocktail Blurberry special. It heals 5 hitpoints, increases a player's Strength by 5% + 1 and decreases Attack by 2% - 3 when drunk. Unlike the other types of alcoholic drinks bought from stores, brandy has a cone-shaped bottle.
2028:
A premade blurb' sp. is a drink that can be bought at Blurberry Bar in the south-east corner of the 1st floor of the Grand Tree. Premade drinks cannot be used in the Gnome Restaurant minigame. It can also be found on the table next to the gnome glider on Karamja (Take the gnome glider to Karamja, Gandius/Palm Tree location).

It functions exactly the same as the blurberry special drink that can be made with the Cooking skill, healing 7 Hitpoints, increasing Strength by 5% + 2 levels, and reducing Attack by 2% - 3 levels.

A blurberry special (fresh or premade) may be given to Harold during the Death Plateau quest to make the gambling section of the quest far easier, as it will cause him to become so drunk he assumes you win every dice game you play with him.

Drinking it will leave behind a cocktail glass and give the messages:
2030:
A premade choc s'dy is a drink that can be bought at Blurberry Bar in the south-east corner of the 1st floor of the Grand Tree. Premade drinks cannot be used in the Gnome Restaurant minigame.

Drinking it heals 5 Hitpoints, lowers Attack by 2% - 3 levels and increases Strength by 5% + 2 levels, just like the chocolate saturday drink that can be made with the Cooking skill.

Drinking it will leave behind a cocktail glass and give the messages:
2032:
A premade dr' dragon is a drink that can be bought at Blurberry Bar in the south-east corner of the 1st floor of the Grand Tree. Premade drinks cannot be used in the Gnome Restaurant activity. When drunk, It heals 5 Hitpoints, lowers your Attack by 2% - 3 levels, and raises your Strength by 5% + 2 levels, just like the drunk dragon drink that can be made with the Cooking skill.

Drinking it will leave behind a cocktail glass and give the messages:
2034:
A premade fr' blast is a drink that can be bought at Blurberry Bar in the south-east corner of the 1st floor of the Grand Tree. Premade drinks cannot be used in the Gnome Restaurant minigame.

Pineapple punches, fruit blasts, and their premade versions are the only gnome cocktails that do not affect stats, and heal 9 hitpoints.

Unlike the regular fruit blast, ashes cannot be added to it to make a dirty blast.

Drinking it will leave behind a cocktail glass and give the messages: You drink the cocktail. It tastes great.
2036:
A premade p' punch is a drink that can be bought at Blurberry Bar in the south-east corner of the 1st floor of the Grand Tree. Premade drinks cannot be used in the Gnome Restaurant minigame.

Pineapple punches and fruit blasts, along with their premade versions, are the only gnome cocktails that do not affect stats, and heal 9 hitpoints.

Drinking it will leave behind a cocktail glass and give the messages: You drink the cocktail. It tastes great.
2038:
A premade sgg is a drink that can be bought at Blurberry Bar in the south-east corner of the 1st floor of the Grand Tree. Premade drinks cannot be used in the Gnome Restaurant minigame.

Like the short green guy, a premade sgg heals 5 hitpoints, boosts Strength by 5% + 1 levels, and reduces Attack by 2% - 3 levels when drunk.

Drinking it will leave behind a cocktail glass and give the messages:
2040:
A premade wiz blz'd is a drink that can be bought at Blurberry Bar in the south-east corner of the 1st floor of the Grand Tree. Pre-made drinks cannot be used in the Gnome Restaurant minigame. Like the wizard blizzard, the premade wiz blz'd heals 5 hitpoints and boosts Strength by 6% + 1 levels, but reduces Attack by 2% - 3 levels.

Drinking it will leave behind a cocktail glass and give the messages:
2048:
Pineapple punch is a drink that can be made at level 8 Cooking, granting 70 experience points. It heals 9 hitpoints. To mix a pineapple punch, a player needs a lemon, 2 oranges, 3 pineapples, a lime, a cocktail shaker, a knife, and a cocktail glass.

To make it:

Use the "mix-cocktail" option on the shaker, and select pineapple punch.

Use the knife on the remaining pineapple and select "dice".

Use the knife on the lime and select "dice".

Use the knife on the orange and select "slice."

Use the cocktail shaker on the glass or select "pour mixed punch" on the cocktail shaker.

Drinking it will leave behind a cocktail glass and give the messages: You drink the cocktail. It tastes great.
2054:
Wizard blizzard is a drink that can be made at level 18 Cooking, granting 110 Cooking experience. When consumed, the wizard blizzard heals 5 hitpoints and boosts Strength by 6% + 1 levels, but reduces Attack by 2% - 3 levels.

The ingredients for wizard blizzard are: two bottles of vodka, one bottle of gin, one orange, one lime, and one lemon. To make the wizard blizzard, put all of the ingredients into a cocktail shaker, next pour the contents of the cocktail shaker into a cocktail glass. Finally, add pineapple chunks and lime slices.

Drinking it will leave behind a cocktail glass and give the messages:
2064:
The Blurberry special can be mixed with 1 vodka, 1 brandy, 1 gin, 1 orange, and 2 lemons. It can be finished by adding 1 equa leaf, 1 sliced lime, 1 diced lemon, and 1 diced orange as a garnish. This requires 37 Cooking to make.

All of these ingredients can be purchased at Funch's Fine Groceries and cost a total of 30 coins per Blurberry special made (not including cocktail shaker, cocktail glass, or knife). A Premade blurb' sp. (premade Blurberry special) can be purchased at the Blurberry Bar for 30 coins.

It heals 7 Hitpoints, increases Strength by 5% + 2 levels, and reduces Attack by 2% - 3 levels.

A Blurberry special (fresh or premade) may be given to Harold during the Death Plateau quest to make the gambling section of the quest far easier, as it will cause him to become so drunk he assumes you win every dice game you play with him.

Drinking it will leave behind a cocktail glass and give the messages:
2074:
A chocolate saturday is an gnomish alcoholic drink that can be made at level 33 Cooking, granting 170 Cooking experience. It is used in the Gnome Restaurant minigame. It heals 5 Hitpoints, lowers Attack by 2% - 3 levels and increases Strength by 5% + 2 levels.

The ingredients are whisky, equa leaves, a bucket of milk, some chocolate dust, a pot of cream and a chocolate bar. Access to a range is also required to complete the beverage. To mix it, players need a cocktail shaker, and a cocktail glass.

There is a premade choc s'dy spawn in Brimstail's cave.

Drinking it will leave behind a cocktail glass and give the messages:
2080:
Short green guys (commonly abbreviated to SGG) are drinks that can be made at level 20 Cooking, granting 120 Cooking experience. They heal 5 hitpoints, boost Strength by 5% + 1 levels, and reduce Attack by 2% - 3 levels. Short green guys are a good way to cheaply train without leaving the Gnome Stronghold, since they require only one type of fruit, have cheap ingredients, and only require one chopped/sliced item.

Creating a short green guy requires one vodka, three limes, one sliced lime, and one equa leaf.

Drinking it will leave behind a cocktail glass and give the messages:
2084:
A fruit blast is a type of drink that restores 9 Hitpoints when consumed. It can be obtained by mixing 1 pineapple, 1 orange, and 1 lemon. You must then finish the cocktail by adding lemon slices as a garnish, requiring level 6 Cooking to complete. To create the cocktail, click "Mix-cocktail" on a cocktail shaker. All ingredients and tools can be bought from Funch's Fine Groceries just east of the Blurberry Bar.

Ashes can be added to a fruit blast to create a dirty blast, which is a requirement for the first part of Recipe for Disaster. A premade fr' blast will NOT work for the quest; ashes can only be added with a regular fruit blast.

A fruit blast may also be obtained from the Ocean Man, or by using the Level 3 certificate from The Dig Site quest on Curator Haig Halen and choosing a drink.

Drinking it will leave behind a cocktail glass and give the messages: You drink the cocktail. It tastes great.
2092:
Drunk dragon is a drink that can be made at level 32 Cooking, granting 160 Cooking experience. When consumed, it heals 5 Hitpoints, lowers your Attack by 2% - 3 levels, and raises your Strength by 5% + 2 levels.

To make the drink, mix vodka, gin, and dwellberries in a a cocktail shaker. Click on the shaker when you have all of these ingredients in your inventory. Click on the shaker again to pour it into a cocktail glass, which gives 30 Cooking experience. Click on the "mixed dragon" to add the pineapple chunks and cream. Lastly, heat it on a range to complete the drink, giving 130 Cooking experience.

Drinking it will leave behind a cocktail glass and give the messages:
2112:
Orange slices are a food item that players can obtain by using a knife on an orange. Eating orange slices will heal 2 hitpoints. Orange slices are needed in the Goblin part of Recipe for Disaster.

Orange slices are used in gnome cooking as an ingredient in a pineapple punch cocktail. They are used in the final step of creating the drink, and must be in the inventory along with 1 lime chunks and 1 pineapple chunks to pour a mixed punch into a cocktail glass.

Oranges can be obtained from Farming in a tree patch, or from shops and NPCs at the Grand Tree.
2114:
A pineapple is a fruit that can be found growing just south of Brimhaven or on a player grown Pineapple plant. Additionally, they may be purchased from Trader Crewmembers operating Trader Stan's Trading Post, Funch's Shop from Heckel Funch, or from Hudo in the Grand Tree Groceries store.

Pineapples provide an easy way to make supercompost by putting it into a compost bin, as they are relatively cheap and easy to obtain. It can be sliced or diced with a knife. Slicing the pineapple will yield 4 pineapple rings, each healing 2 Hitpoints. Dicing the pineapple yields one pineapple chunks, an ingredient used in gnome cooking, which also heals 2 Hitpoints when consumed. When slicing the pineapple into pineapple rings if you don't have enough space in your inventory, the rings will drop to the ground instead.

10 pineapples are also used as a payment for papaya trees.

Even though there is an eat option, you cannot eat a pineapple, attempting to do so will result in this message You can't eat it whole; maybe you should cut it up. as you can eat it after cutting it with a knife.

For Ironman accounts, pineapples are the most accessible ingredient for making supercompost, as they are sold at Trader Stan's Trading Post.
2116:
Pineapple chunks are a food item that heals 2 hitpoints when consumed. Players can make pineapple chunks by using a knife on a pineapple or a tenti pineapple by choosing "Dice".

The main use for pineapple chunks is as an ingredient in other foods; for example, members can use them to make a pineapple pizza with level 65 Cooking.

Pineapple chunks are mostly used in Gnome cooking, where they are an ingredient in a fruit batta. They are also used in making drinks such as pineapple punch, wizard blizzard, and drunk dragon.
2118:
Pineapple rings are a members-only Cooking ingredient that are used on plain pizzas to create pineapple pizzas.

Pineapple rings are obtained by using a knife on a pineapple or a tenti pineapple and choosing the "slice" option. 4 pineapple rings are obtained for each pineapple that is sliced. If the "dice" option is chosen, the player will receive Pineapple chunks instead.

If eaten, it heals 2 hit points.
2120:
A lime is a members-only green fruit used in Gnome Cuisine, most often used in Gnome cooking. It can be diced with a knife into lime chunks, or sliced with a knife into lime slices. These both heal 2 Hitpoints each.

Unlike most other fruits, it cannot be grown using the Farming skill. Instead, they must be bought from Hudo's groceries and Heckel Funch in the Grand Tree. It is also available from the market seller in Pollnivneach, gotten as drop from gnomes throughout Tree Gnome Stronghold or it can be stolen at the fruit stall in Hosidius or in the Kourend Castle courtyard.

Limes are compostable – they will make regular compost.

A lime may also be one of the three items required during the quest Fairytale I - Growing Pains in order to obtain the magic secateurs.
2122: Lime chunks are a food item that are obtained by using a knife on a lime and selecting "Dice". When eaten, they heal 2 hitpoints. After being diced, lime chunks may be used in gnome cooking to make either a fruit batta or pineapple punch.
2124: Lime slices are food obtained by using a knife on a lime. They are an ingredient in gnome cocktails.
2128:
Equa leaves are ingredients utilised in gnome cooking that heal 1 hitpoint each. They are used in almost all gnome food, and have little other use, besides possibly in the Big Chompy Bird Hunting quest.

They can be purchased at the two food stores on the 1st floor of the Grand Tree in the Tree Gnome Stronghold. Several respawn points are located in the south-east of Feldip Hills.
2134:
Raw rat meat is usually obtained by killing a giant rat. It can be cooked on a range or on a fire. It requires level 1 Cooking to be turned into Cooked meat, granting 30 Cooking experience if successful. It is one of the four raw meats needed in the Druidic Ritual quest. It can be used as bait when trapping sabre-toothed kebbits. Raw rat meat can be bought from Rufus in Canifis. Unlike raw beef, raw boar meat, and raw bear meat, raw rat meat cannot be turned into sinew.

If looking for a giant rat to kill, level 3 giant rats are common in Lumbridge Swamp and always drop raw rat meat. The level 6 giant rat in Lumbridge Swamp, the giant rat near the mine south-east of Varrock and the giant rats in the Stronghold of Security rarely drop rat meat.

Raw rat meat is always dropped by brine rats, and brine rats sometimes drop 18 noted raw rat meat.

Raw rat meat spawns cannot be picked up by ironmen.
2138:
A Raw chicken is an uncooked food item dropped by chickens or roosters. They are also sold at Rufus' Meat Emporium in Canifis and Wydin's Food Store in Port Sarim.

There is also a crate in Wydin's shop in Port Sarim that provides unlimited raw chicken. A white apron is required to enter the room which contains the crate.

Raw chicken can be cooked into cooked chicken by using it on a fire, a range, or an ogre spit-roast. Doing so requires only level 1 Cooking for the fire and the range, and grants 30 experience points. The ogre spit-roast requires level 30 Cooking. At level 34 Cooking, raw chicken can no longer be accidentally burnt.

Raw chicken is used with together with a raw swordfish to make a swordchick in Creature Creation after completion of Tower of Life.
2140:
Cooked chicken is a type of food that restores 3 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking raw chicken on a fire or cooking range, granting 30 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt chicken. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Cooked chicken is one of a number of foods with a reduced burn rate while using the Lumbridge Castle range with Cook's Assistant completed. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 34, or 31 when using the Lumbridge range.

Cooked chicken does not require a cooking level to cook, and can be used as an ingredient to make a stew or curry. It is an easily obtainable early food source, as killing chickens at the Lumbridge East Farm is a common activity for a low level player.
2142:
Cooked meat is a type of food that restores 3 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking various raw meats on a fire or cooking range, granting 30 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt meat. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Cooked meat is one of a number of foods with a reduced burn rate while using the Lumbridge Castle range with Cook's Assistant completed. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 34, or 31 when using the Lumbridge range.

Cooked meat is used in the making of stews, pies, and steak sandwiches, or as a topping on pizzas.

Unlike most food, players can deliberately burn cooked meat by using it on a fire or cooking range. One burnt meat is required for Witch's Potion.
2144:
Burnt chicken is the result of accidentally burning a raw chicken while attempting to make cooked chicken. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 34. Players can also deliberately make burnt chicken by cooking a piece of cooked chicken, displaying the chatbox message, You deliberately burn the nicely cooked chicken.

Burnt chicken may be used for the Forgettable Tale... quest, in which it may be one of the random items requested by the rowdy dwarf before he will give the player his Kelda seed. It is also one of the items that Gunslik and the rowdy dwarf can request when doing Keldagrim tasks.

Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.
2146:
Burnt meat is the result of accidentally burning various raw meat while attempting to make cooked meat. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 34. Players can also deliberately make burnt meat by cooking a piece of cooked meat, displaying the chatbox message "You deliberately burn the nicely cooked meat."

Burnt meat is used for the Witch's Potion quest. It is often dropped by Imps, and is also a reward from Burntmeat after Eadgar's Ruse and My Arm's Big Adventure.

Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.
2148:
Raw lava eels require level 53 Fishing to catch, and a Cooking level of 53 to cook. Raw lava eels may be caught using an oily fishing rod and bait in the lava rivers found in Taverley Dungeon, the Wilderness Lava Maze, the Charred Dungeon (level 60 Sailing), and the Wyrmscraig Cavern (after completion of Fallen From Grace).

During the Heroes' Quest, guild-master Achietties will ask players to obtain a cooked lava eel to prove that they are worthy of membership to the Heroes' Guild. Players will then need to visit Gerrant in Port Sarim to learn how to make an oily fishing rod to catch them.

Catching a raw lava eel in the Lava Maze is a hard Wilderness Diary task.

Lava eels do not offer the player a chance to roll a pet drop while fishing.
2149: Lava eel is a type of untradeable fish that restores 11 Hitpoints when eaten. During Heroes' Quest, guild master Achietties will ask players to obtain a cooked lava eel to prove that they are worthy of membership to the Heroes' Guild. It can be obtained by cooking raw lava eel on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 53 Cooking and granting 30 experience when successful. There is no chance of burning a lava eel.
2152:
Toad's legs are a food used in Cooking and Herblore. They are made by pulling the legs off of swamp toads found in the swamp of Tree Gnome Stronghold or lake south of Taverley, and from pickpocketing gnomes, requiring 75 Thieving. They heal for 3 Hitpoints. Adding them to a toadflax potion (unf) makes an Agility potion (3), requiring 34 Herblore, and yielding 80 Herblore experience. Toad's legs are main ingredients of the gnome cooking foods: Tangled toad's legs, toad batta and toad crunchies.

Toad's legs can be used as a fast food, a subtype of food that incurs non-standard attack or eating delays when consumed. Toad's legs may be consumed after other foods with almost no delay; this does not work if the toad's legs are eaten first, and does not work when eating two toad's legs in a row. This technique (commonly referred to as combo eating) can be further enhanced by drinking a dose of Saradomin brew after your alternative food item, and before your toad's legs (food>brew>toad's legs).
2154:
Equa toad's legs was previously obtained during Gnome cooking when making a Toad batta. It could be made by adding Equa leaves to Toad's legs. Gnome spice was then added to these in order to create Seasoned legs, an ingredient in the Toad batta.

As this process was unnecessarily intricate, it was altered with the Gnome Restaurant rework in 2006. Now, the toad's legs, equa leaves and gnome spice are all automatically added at once to create a Half made crunchy. If the player attempts to add equa leaves to toad's legs, nothing happens.

Because the item was removed before 2007, it has never been present in Old School RuneScape. However, it remains in the game files.
2162:
King worms are used in gnome cooking to make worm crunchies, worm holes, and worm battas. They can be eaten to heal 2 Hitpoints. When eaten, the message You eat the king worm. It's a bit chewy. is displayed. It is a possible item chosen randomly from a list in the Fairytale I - Growing Pains and Forgettable Tale... quests, to enchant the Secateurs, and trade for the Rowdy dwarf's kelda seed.

When talking to a gnome woman, they occasionally give king worms.

King worms are also used to feed the Cormorant while Aerial fishing on the island on Lake Molch.
2164:
A batta tin is used for making battas in the Gnome Restaurant minigame. It can be obtained in the Grand Tree by buying from the Gnome Restaurant food shop owned by Hudo, by searching the nearby cupboard to find one, or by looting it from the gnomes in the stronghold.

If one gianne dough is added into the tin a raw batta is created, and if this is cooked over the gnome cooker or any other range, half baked batta will be made. From here, any of the battas in the gnome cuisine can be made. Examples of battas include worm batta, toad batta, cheese and tomato batta, fruit batta, and vegetable batta.

Please see gnome cooking for more information on gnome cuisine.
2166:
A gnomebowl mould is an item used in gnome cooking. It can be bought in the Grand Tree by talking to Hudo in the north-west corner on the 1st floor, or it can be acquired for free by searching the tree gnome kitchen cabinet at the northernmost part of the Grand Tree for a "gnome bowl".

Adding gianne dough to the mould will create a raw gnomebowl, the basis for gnomebowl cooking.
2167:
Gianne's cook book is a cook book written by Aluft Gianne. It is full of Gnome recipes, and useful for the Gnome Restaurant minigame, or if players want to make gnome foods for themselves.

The cook book can be obtained from Aluft Gianne himself, Hudo the nearby grocer, or from the bookcase in a player-owned house. The book will not be available in your bookcase until completing the cooking tutorial with Aluft Gianne snr.. It mentions Pukkamay, a great Gnome cook.

Note that this book does not contain Gnome cocktail recipes, as these recipes are written in the The Blurberry Cocktail Guide.
2169:
Gnome Spice is an ingredient used to make spicy sauce and certain gnome foods. It can be bought from Grand Tree Groceries, run by Hudo in the Grand Tree. It will never run out while making Gnome foods.

To create spicy sauce, gnome spice is used with chopped garlic. This uses up the gnome spice.

When placing it into nest atop the Aldarin mill and then logging out of the game, it will transform into an iron pickaxe.
2171: Gianne dough is an ingredient in gnome cooking used to make gnomebowls, gnome crunchies, and gnome battas. It can be bought from Hudo in the Grand Tree. Gianne dough cannot be cooked by itself; instead, players must use the dough on a crunchy tray, batta tin, or gnomebowl mould and then precook it on a range. It was probably named after Aluft Gianne snr., the gnome cook. 100 Gianne dough is also given as a reward for completing the Gnome Restaurant training.
2177: The half baked bowl is an item used in gnome cooking and is obtained by using gianne dough with a gnomebowl mould, then using the resulting raw gnomebowl on a range. The raw ingredients can be added by selecting prepare and choosing a gnomebowl type. This creates a half made bowl.
2178:
Raw gnomebowls are the base of gnomebowl cooking and are obtained by using gianne dough on a gnomebowl mould. They can be used on a range to make half baked bowls.

Unlike other items requiring a range, raw gnomebowls cannot be cooked using Mor Ul Rek sulphur vents.
2185:
A chocolate bomb is a food that players consume in one bite, healing 15 hitpoints. Players may need to make one as part of Training part I for the Gnome Restaurant minigame. Premade chocolate bombs are sold by gnome waiters in the north-west corner of the 1st floor of the Grand Tree for 160 coins, with 3 in stock.

Members can make a chocolate bomb via gnome cooking with 42 Cooking, yielding 190 experience. Like all gnome foods, they stop burning at Cooking level 38.

Making a chocolate bomb is a requirement for the Medium Western Provinces Diary.

This food is an order in the Gnome Restaurant minigame and may also be obtained by completing an order through a Gnome restaurant Reward token. Like all gnome cooking, premade versions cannot be used in the minigame.

Gianne dough, gnomebowl moulds, chocolate (decadently added), chocolate dust, pots of cream, and equa leaves can be bought from Hudo who is located in the north-west corner the 1st floor of the Grand Tree.

2283: A pizza base is an ingredient used to make pizza. It can be made by using either a bucket of water, bowl of water, or jug of water with a pot of flour. With a Cooking level of 35 it can be used with a tomato and cheese to make an uncooked pizza, which can then be cooked. Tomato must be added first, then cheese to make an uncooked pizza. Pizza bases can also be purchased from Tony's Pizza Bases in the Bandit Camp.
2287: Uncooked pizza requires 35 Cooking to make and is obtained by using a pizza base with tomato and cheese. It can be cooked on a range (but not a fire) into a plain pizza, which gives 143 Cooking experience. Some toppings can then be added, see the pizza page for more details. It is possible to fail the cooking, which will result in a burnt pizza.
2293:

When the first bite is eaten, the message You eat half of the meat pizza.is displayed. The second bite gives the message You eat the remaining meat pizza..

2301:
Pineapple pizza is a type of pizza that restores 22 Hitpoints in total, 2 bites each healing for 11. It can be obtained by using pineapple chunks or pineapple rings on a cooked plain pizza, requiring 65 Cooking and granting 45 experience. It is recommended to cut the pineapple into rings, as this yields four rings for use on multiple pizzas, compared to the single chunk if dicing it. Pineapple pizza is one of the highest healing foods in the game and are also a type of fast food.

100 noted pineapple pizzas can be given to Yama to initiate a fight that is identical to the aether catalyst, oathplate shard, and diabolic worm acquisition contract fights, as a way to practice these fights in exchange for standard loot rolls.

A Cook in a player-owned house can make a pineapple pizza for the player.

2307: Bread dough is made by mixing either a bucket of water, bowl of water, or jug of water with a pot of flour. It can be used on a range to make a loaf of bread at level 1 Cooking, granting 40 experience and healing 5 hitpoints when consumed. It is one of the most basic items used for the Cooking skill. Players will also get a pot of flour and a bucket of water to make bread dough on Tutorial Island, as a tutorial for cooking.
2309: Bread is a type of food that restores 5 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by baking bread dough on a cooking range, granting 40 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt bread. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Bread is one of a number of foods with a reduced burn rate while using the Lumbridge Castle range with Cook's Assistant completed. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 38, or 34 when using the Lumbridge range. Bread may also be bought or stolen from the Ardougne Baker's Stall in the Ardougne marketplace.
2313:
A pie dish is used in Cooking to bake pies. Players must add a pastry dough (a pot of flour and either a jug of water, a bucket of water, or a bowl of water combined) to the pie dish to form a pie shell. It then can be filled by the filling of choice. Afterwards, the pie can then be baked in an oven. Players can create this in a pottery oven.

Despite unfired pie dishes requiring 7 Crafting to make, turning an unfired pie dish into a pie dish has no Crafting requirement and can be done at level 1.
2315:
A pie shell is used to make various kinds of pie. It is made by using a pastry dough on a pie dish. Players can fill a pie shell with any of several fillings to make a raw pie which must be cooked on a range.

Possible fillings include: redberries for redberry pie, cooked meat or cooked chicken for meat pie, or cooking apple for an apple pie and many more. Members have access to a wider variety of fillings from mud pies to summer pies.
2317:
An uncooked apple pie is an uncooked food item made by using a cooking apple on a pie shell that has already had pastry dough added to it. Players need at least level 30 Cooking to make it. If successfully cooked, an apple pie provides 130 Cooking experience.

The uncooked pie can be cooked on a range (but not a fire) to make an apple pie. However, there is a risk that the pie will burn and become a burnt pie. Like other pies, apple pies can also be cooked with the Lunar spell Bake Pie without the chance of burning.

A convenient place to make uncooked apple pies and cook them is the Cooks' Guild, which requires level 32 Cooking and a Chef's hat to enter. All of the ingredients needed to make apple pie are found around the guild, as it has 3 cooking apple spawns, a pie dish respawn, a jug respawn, a sink, a mill, wheat, and cooking ranges.
2319: An uncooked meat pie is made by adding cooked meat or cooked chicken to a pie shell. It can be cooked to make meat pie, or if unsuccessful, a Burnt pie.
2321: An Uncooked berry pie is made by adding Redberries to a Pie shell. Its cooked variant is a redberry pie.
2323:
Apple pie is a type of pie that restores 14 Hitpoints in total, 2 bites each healing for 7. A pie dish will remain after both bites are consumed.

It can be created by baking an uncooked apple pie on a cooking range, requiring level 30 Cooking and granting 130 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt pie. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 63. Alternatively, casting the Bake Pie spell from the lunar spellbook will always create a pie without burning it.

Apple pie is a possible task from Romily Weaklax in the Cooks' Guild. Three apple pies and three meat pies are given to the player when starting Nature Spirit.
