It can be created by baking an uncooked apple pie on a cooking range, requiring level 30 Cooking and granting 130 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt pie. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 63. Alternatively, casting the Bake Pie spell from the lunar spellbook will always create a pie without burning it.

Apple pie is a possible task from Romily Weaklax in the Cooks' Guild. Three apple pies and three meat pies are given to the player when starting Nature Spirit.
2337:
Raw oomlie may be obtained by killing the oomlie birds found in the depths of the Kharazi Jungle, south of Shilo Village. To get into the Kharazi Jungle, the player must have started Legends' Quest. At 50 Cooking, it can be wrapped in a palm leaf to get a wrapped oomlie, which can then be cooked to get a cooked oomlie wrap.

Wrapping it in a palm leaf is required to cook it; the raw oomlie cannot be cooked on its own. Attempting to do so will always fail (even with a cooking cape), resulting in a burnt oomlie, with the message You cook the Oomlie Meat on the fire..., and after the player burns it, "The meat is far too delicate to cook like this. Perhaps you should wrap it up to protect it from the heat."

Eating a cooked oomlie wrap is a hard task in the Karamja Diary.

Raw oomlie is sometimes given as a tip from the Gnome Restaurant minigame.
2345: Burnt oomlie wrap is the result of burning a wrapped oomlie while attempting to make a cooked oomlie wrap. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 40 when cooking on a range and level 44 when cooking on a fire.
2347:
A hammer is a tool used for smithing items on an Anvil, and it is vital to level the Smithing skill. Hammers can be bought from most general stores and will never break. Alternatively, players can obtain a hammer by talking to the Master smithing tutor at the West Varrock anvil. A hammer is also used in the Construction skill when making furniture, and it is required for some minigames. At 15 Construction, members can make a Tool store 1 for the workshop room of their house; this tool store provides an unlimited supply of hammers.

A hammer is required to access Bandos' stronghold in the God Wars Dungeon; warhammers are an acceptable substitute.

The Imcando hammer can be used instead of a hammer when performing tasks like Construction or Smithing.
2349:
A bronze bar is a bar of refined bronze. It can be created through the Smithing skill at level 1 by using a copper ore and a tin ore on a furnace, granting 6.2 Smithing experience. A bronze bar can be smithed on an anvil through the Smithing skill to create bronze weapons and armour. A list of bronze items that can be smithed from bronze bars and the Smithing levels required can be found here. When smithed, each bar gives 12.5 experience, with a maximum of 62.5 experience given for the bronze platebody.

Members can purchase bronze bars from the Shantay Pass Shop in the Shantay Pass south of Al Kharid for 8 coins each, or from Jiminua's Jungle Store north of Tai Bwo Wannai village for 12 coins each.

4-6 bronze bars are required for quests. Observatory Quest requires 1, The Tourist Trap requires 1-3 (dependent on the luck), Prince Ali Rescue requires 1 and One Small Favour requires 1. Furthermore, Creature of Fenkenstrain and Recipe for Disaster/Freeing Pirate Pete require 3 bronze wires each, for a total of 10-12 bronze bars.
2351:
An iron bar is a bar of refined iron. It can be created through the Smithing skill at level 15 by using iron ore on a furnace, granting 12.5 Smithing experience. When smelting iron ore, there is a 50% chance that it will be too impure; it disappears, yielding no Smithing experience nor an iron bar. However, wearing a ring of forging, casting Superheat Item, or using the Blast Furnace would give a 100% success rate.

An iron bar can be smithed on an anvil through the Smithing skill to create iron weapons and armour. When smithed, each bar grants 25 experience, with a maximum of 125 being given for the iron platebody.
2355:
A silver bar is a bar of metal, refined through the Smithing skill by smelting a silver ore in a furnace, requiring 20 Smithing and granting 13.7 Smithing experience. It may also be bought (or stolen) from a silver merchant, such as the one in Ardougne market, or from other players.

The primary use of a silver bar is to create jewellery with the Crafting skill. To craft silver bars into jewellery players must use a silver bar on a furnace with a proper mould in their inventory. If players wish to craft jewellery with gems inset, the cut gems must be present in the player's inventory before crafting the jewellery. One silver bar is used during the Creature of Fenkenstrain quest, and another during Shadow of the Storm.

Unlike gold bars, which cannot be made into weapons, silver bars can be made into silver sickles. They can also be ground to silver dust in the Ectofuntus grinder for use as an ingredient in the guthix balance potion.

Currently, smelting a silver bar yields a profit of 41.

One effective method of gathering silver bars is exchanging reward tokens gained for completing Temple Trekking minigame. This method is commonly used by ironman players, as it can net upwards of 1000 silver bars per hour.
2359:
A Mithril bar is a bar of refined mithril ore. It can be created through the Smithing skill by using a mithril ore and 4 pieces of coal on a furnace, granting 30 experience. The Superheat Item spell can also be used to make mithril bars. Both ways of creating mithril bars require level 50 Smithing. It can also be created in the Blast Furnace, which can be considerably cheaper as it halves the amount of coal needed.

A mithril bar can be smithed on an anvil by using the Smithing skill to create mithril weapons and armour, granting 50 Smithing experience per bar used. A list of mithril items that can be smithed from mithril bars and the Smithing levels required can be found at Smithing tables.

Currently, smelting a mithril bar yields a profit of 242 in a standard furnace and 538 in the blast furnace.
2361: Adamantite bars can be smelted with 6 coal and 1 adamantite ore at level 70 Smithing. Smelting the bar grants 37.5 Smithing experience, and any item that is smithed from adamantite bars grants 62.5 Smithing experience per bar, yielding a net of 100 experience.
2365:
A 'perfect' gold bar is an untradeable gold bar smelted from 'perfect' gold ore. It is used in the Family Crest quest with a ruby and a necklace mould or ring mould to craft a 'perfect' necklace and 'perfect' ring respectively. It can be used as a normal gold bar when crafting any other item of jewellery, creating a normal piece of jewellery, which will not receive the prefix of 'perfect'.

Just like normal gold ore, two 'perfect' gold bars can be smelted at once at the Edgeville furnace if the appropriate tier of Varrock armour is worn.

It cannot be used to make a gold helmet or gold bowl.
2366:
The shield left half is an item that can be joined with the right half to create the dragon square shield with level 60 Smithing. Joining the right half with the left half nets 75 Smithing experience. The other half of the shield is sold by Siegfried Erkle in the Legends Guild Shop of Useful Items for 750,000 coins.

This item is a rare drop from the rare drop table. Wearing a ring of wealth will increase the chances of receiving one from the rare drop table. Goraks fought in the Gorak Plane are likely droppers of the shield left half, with a drop rate of 1/243.75 (with a ring of wealth equipped) if Fairytale II - Cure a Queen and Legends' Quest have been completed.

Skotizo is the monster most likely to drop the shield left half, with a drop rate of 1/100, and is the only monster to have it on its standard drop table.

The intricate pouch from Guardians of the Rift has a chance to contain the shield left half, as well as other dragon items.

Creating a dragon square shield from the two halves in West Ardougne is a hard task in the Ardougne Diary.
2368:
The shield right half is an item which can be bought in the Legends' Guild or the Myths' Guild for 750,000 coins. It can be combined with the shield left half (provided that you have 60 Smithing) to form the dragon square shield. A hammer and anvil is needed to combine the shield.

Creating a Dragon square shield from the two halves in West Ardougne is a hard task in the Ardougne Diary.
2370: Steel studs can be smithed from a steel bar at an anvil with level 36 Smithing, granting 37.5 experience. They can then be used on leather bodies with level 41 Crafting or leather chaps with level 44 Crafting, to make studded bodies and studded chaps respectively.
2372:
An ogre relic is a quest item that appears in the Watchtower quest. During the quest, it is given as a gift to the ogre guards, who stand at the gates of Gu'Tanoth. In return, they grant the player permanent access to the city. It should also be noted from a lore point of view that upon gifting the relic to the guards, they recognise it as a statue of the ogre warrior, Dalgroth.

The player can make the ogre relic by giving the three individual pieces to the Watchtower Wizard and having him combine them, each of which is obtained by performing tasks for ogres who live in and around Gu'Tanoth. Attempting to use the pieces on each other in order to combine the pieces will only result with the game message, "The pieces look like they would fit together, but you can't work out how to do it. Maybe someone with more experience of ogres could help."

Relic part 1 is obtained by retrieving a stolen bar of gold for Og.

Relic part 2 is obtained by defeating Gorad and giving his ogre tooth to Grew.

Relic part 3 is obtained by giving Toban a dragon bone.

Should the item be lost or destroyed before being given to the ogre guards near the gates of the ogre city, it can be reobtained by speaking to the Watchtower Wizard.
2373:
The relic part 1 is a quest item that appears in the Watchtower quest. When combined with Relic part 2 and Relic part 3 it forms an Ogre relic which can be used to access the ogre town of Gu'Tanoth.

To obtain Relic part 1 the player must retrieve a bar of gold that Toban stole from Og.
2374:
The relic part 2 is a quest item in the Watchtower quest. Combining it with the relic part 1 and relic part 3 makes the ogre relic required to access the ogre town of Gu'Tanoth.

To obtain it, the player must defeat Gorad and return his Ogre tooth to Grew.
2375: The relic part 3 is a quest item that appears in the Watchtower quest. When combined with Relic part 1 and Relic part 2 it forms an Ogre relic which can be used to access the ogre town of Gu'Tanoth. To obtain Relic part 3 the player must give the ogre Toban a dragon bone.
2376:
The skavid map is required to successfully navigate the Skavid caves around Gu'Tanoth. Without possession of this map, players entering into one of the Skavid caves will immediately exit the next cave entrance in a clockwise direction, the last one being next to Toban's island, before starting at the north-west cave again. Players do not need to read the map to enter the Skavid caves, only have it in their inventory.

During the Watchtower quest, you obtain the map by visiting the ogre city guards all the way at the end of the path leading into Gu'Tanoth. To obtain the map the first time, you will need a rock cake, a death rune and 20 coins to reach the city guard and buy the map. If you lose the map, you'll only need 20 coins to get back to the city guard to replace it.

After the quest, the map can be freely reobtained if lost by talking to one of the two city guards. The city guards are located next to the ogre named Keef, on top of the eastern hill next to the agility shortcut. You can access here by climbing the agility shortcut (71 Agility required), or by following the four bridges around to it, starting at the south-west of the city. Please note that if you're following the four bridges, you will once again have to pay 20 coins to cross the last bridge even with the quest finished. However, a rock cake and a death rune are no longer necessary.

A skavid map is required in order to pick cave nightshade from a skavid cave for a medium achievement in the Ardougne Diary. One can be found in the northernmost cave entrance, west of Yanille, and south of the lake with the island in it.
2377:
The ogre tooth is obtained from the corpse of Gorad when he is killed by the player during the Watchtower quest.

The player must then bring the tooth to Grew, as proof that his request for Gorad's death was fulfilled.
2378:
Toban's key is given by Og in the Watchtower quest to open the chest near Gorad. After opening the chest you will find Toban's gold and the key will be consumed.

If you should happen to destroy Toban's gold bar or lose it by any means, return to Og to be given another key and return to the chest to obtain another gold bar.
2379:
A rock cake is a strange ogre delicacy. It is a cake made of stone. Players cannot buy rock cakes from the ogres. Instead, they are stolen from the market stall in the ogre town of Gu'Tanoth. Stealing a rock cake requires a Thieving level of 15 and yields 6.5 Thieving experience.

Rock cakes cannot be gained until the relevant part of the Watchtower quest. A rock cake is required as a bribe in order to access the central parts of the Gu'Tanoth, which is necessary during the Watchtower quest. The player must give a rock cake to an ogre guard in order to be allowed to climb over a rampart that blocks the way to a rope bridge.

Rock cakes are inedible by a human. When "eaten", the player character will say, "Ow! I nearly broke a tooth!". After this dialogue is dismissed, the player loses a fraction of their current HP, and the cake is destroyed. Using the "guzzle" option will deal twice as much damage as using the "eat" option.

Even though Ogre rock cakes can be obtained after the Watchtower quest, they aren't an optimal method of depleting one's own hitpoints; many have to be "eaten" in order to fall under 10% Hitpoints. The dwarven rock cake has similar effects when "eaten", although it won't be destroyed in the process and can be eaten again with no delay.
2380: Crystal is a material used by the elves, which was gifted to them by their goddess Seren. It is infused with some of her divine power, and is an important part of elven culture. It can be shaped, formed, and magically charged into weapons, tools, or other items with magical powers by the use of crystal seeds and crystal shards. Crystal seeds and shards can be transformed via crystal singing, either by using a singing bowl with sufficient Crafting and Smithing levels, or by the service of a crystal singer. Crystal shards can also be ground into crystal dust for use in Herblore, to transform certain combat stat-boosting potions into divine potions.
2381: Crystal is a material used by the elves, which was gifted to them by their goddess Seren. It is infused with some of her divine power, and is an important part of elven culture. It can be shaped, formed, and magically charged into weapons, tools, or other items with magical powers by the use of crystal seeds and crystal shards. 2383: Crystal is a material used by the elves, which was gifted to them by their goddess Seren. It is infused with some of her divine power, and is an important part of elven culture. 2384:
Fingernails is a quest item that appears in the Watchtower quest. During the quest, the player can find it by searching the bushes surrounding the Watchtower outside the north wall of Yanille.

The fingernails must be given to the wizard in the Watchtower in order for him to be able to identify who stole the power crystals that make the tower operate.

The fingernails are from a skavid, as they are also found in two of the Skavid caves. After the quest, the item can be reobtained, but it serves no purpose.
2385:
Old robe is a quest item that appears in the Watchtower quest and it can be found after the quest's completion. The player can find it by searching the bushes surrounding the Watchtower outside the north wall of Yanille.

This item serves no purpose and is most likely there as a red herring. It cannot be worn.
2386: Unusual armour is a quest item found during the Watchtower quest. Players can find it by searching the bushes surrounding the Watchtower outside the north wall of Yanille, even after the quest is complete. It serves no purpose during the quest and is merely a red herring. It cannot be worn.
2388: The tattered eye patch is a quest item that appears in the Watchtower quest and it can be found after the quest's completion. Players can find it by searching the bushes surrounding the Watchtower outside the north wall of Yanille. It serves no purpose during the quest, and it cannot be worn.
2389: Vials are typically filled up with water and are most commonly used in the Herblore skill to make potions or mixes. Upon finishing a potion, the empty vial is left in the player's inventory; however with completion of Alfred Grimhand's Barcrawl, players may speak to the barbarian guard outside of the Barbarian Outpost to learn how to automatically smash vials upon finishing a potion. This feature also works in free-to-play. The player may also toggle this feature from the settings menu.
2390: Vials are typically filled up with water and are most commonly used in the Herblore skill to make potions or mixes. Upon finishing a potion, the empty vial is left in the player's inventory; however with completion of Alfred Grimhand's Barcrawl, players may speak to the barbarian guard outside of the Barbarian Outpost to learn how to automatically smash vials upon finishing a potion. This feature also works in free-to-play. The player may also toggle this feature from the settings menu.
2391: Ground bat bones is an item used in the Watchtower quest and in the Herblore skill. They are made by using a pestle and mortar on bat bones. Provided that the player has level 14 Herblore, when combined with a Guam potion (unf) it will explode (dealing 5 damage), and will leave the empty vial only. Should the player have their hitpoints less than 8, it will not kill them and will deal less than 5 damage. Additionally, when the item is combined with a vial of water, the water will evaporate followed by a dialogue box with the player saying, "Oh dear, the mixture has evaporated." This also leaves an empty vial. The item can be created before, during, and after the quest; however, it serves no purpose outside of the quest.
2393: Toban's gold is a bar of gold stolen from Og by his nemesis, Toban. The player must recover this item from Toban as part of the Watchtower quest. This is a unique gold bar, and Og will not accept a gold bar created by normal use of the Smithing skill.
2394:
The potion is a quest item that is created during the Watchtower quest. It is used to kill the ogre shaman that lives in the caves below Gu'Tanoth.

To make the potion the player must mix guam leaf, jangerberries, and ground bat bones into a vial of water. This specific order must be followed or the potion will explode, damaging the player. Then, it needs to be enchanted by the Watchtower Wizard, to turn it into a Magic ogre potion. This item will disappear when dropped. Before dropping the item, it will ask for confirmation, stating: "This item will likely break if you put it down here, and you will have to go looking for another."

The mixture can be created after completing the quest; however, it has no further use. Additionally, using the potion on the Watchtower Wizard will result in the wizard taking the item, stating that it is too dangerous and may cause an injury.

Mixing the ground bat bones into the vial (jangerberries and guam leaf) to create the potion prints the message You mix the ground bones into the liquid., followed by You produce a strong potion..
2395:
The magic ogre potion is a quest item in the Watchtower quest. It is used to kill ogre shamans in the Ogre Enclave below Gu'Tanoth.

It is made by adding to a vial of water a guam leaf, jangerberries, and ground bat bones, in that order, and then bringing the resulting potion to the Watchtower Wizard to enchant. Making the potion requires 14 Herblore. This item will disappear when dropped. Before dropping the item, it will ask for confirmation, stating: "This item will likely break if you put it down here, and you will have to go looking for another."

Using the potion to kill the ogre shamans during the quest requires 14 Magic. After using it to kill the last Ogre shaman it will become an empty vial. The magic ogre potion cannot be made after the quest, and if one is brought to the Watchtower Wizard, he will confiscate the potion, claiming it is too dangerous.
2396: Spell scroll is a scroll that you receive as a reward from the quest, Watchtower. When read, the player learns the Watchtower Teleport (requires level 58 Magic). If a player loses the scroll before use, they can speak to the Watchtower Wizard. The player may learn the spell even without the requirement of level 58 Magic to use it. The drop trick may be performed to obtain multiple scrolls, allowing the player to 'learn' this spell multiple times.
2397: The shaman robe is an item that can be found during or after the Watchtower Quest on the ground inside the Ogre Enclave. The robe cannot be worn. It only serves for the purpose of retrieving the cyan crystal if during the quest the player has lost it. The crystal can be found by searching the robe. After doing so, it has no other use and it can be safely dropped.
2398:
Cave nightshade, also known as cave belladonna, is used in Herblore to make weapon poison(++) or as an addition to dynamite for poison dynamite.

Players can eat nightshade, but this is not recommended in most situations. When eaten, the player will say, "Ahhhh! What have I done!" and take up to 15 damage (damage taken scales with the player's current Hitpoints). Like most self-damaging items, it is impossible for the player to kill themselves with it. (Note: It is possible for players to eat this without losing health; if the player were to accidentally eat the nightshade, they can teleport away to avoid losing any hitpoints, provided they don't click "Continue" on the dialogue text.)

Damage taken is given by the following formula:

Damage(Hitpoints)={15,if Hitpoints≥20⌊Hitpoints2⌋if Hitpoints<20

There are two spawns in the Skavid caves by the ogre city Gu'Tanoth south of Yanille: the northern-most cave entrance, just south of the western entrance to Yanille, and the southern-most cave entrance within the city of Gu'Tanoth across a bridge. The skavid map (obtained during the Watchtower quest) and a light source are needed to enter these caves. These spawns can be picked up without wearing gloves or gauntlets and respawn about every 54 seconds. Collecting a cave nightshade from one of these spawns is a task in the medium Ardougne Diary. The Reagent pouch does NOT hold Cave nightshade, saying "You can't possibly put that in there. It would spoil your pouch."

Cave nightshade may also be grown using the Farming skill, though this yields a stackable variant of nightshade instead.

Although cave nightshade is untradeable, it is an ingredient to make a tradeable potion; therefore, it has a theoretical value of 1,880 coins when buying coconut milk and poison ivy berries and selling the resulting weapon poison(++).
2399:
There are 3 Silverlight keys used in the Demon Slayer quest:

Silverlight key (Captain Rovin)

Silverlight key (Sir Prysin)

Silverlight key (Wizard Traiborn)

They are needed for Sir Prysin to unlock the box that contains the Silverlight sword.
2400:
There are 3 Silverlight keys used in the Demon Slayer quest:

Silverlight key (Captain Rovin)

Silverlight key (Sir Prysin)

Silverlight key (Wizard Traiborn)

They are needed for Sir Prysin to unlock the box that contains the Silverlight sword.
2401:
There are 3 Silverlight keys used in the Demon Slayer quest:

Silverlight key (Captain Rovin)

Silverlight key (Sir Prysin)

Silverlight key (Wizard Traiborn)

They are needed for Sir Prysin to unlock the box that contains the Silverlight sword.
2402:
Silverlight is a magical sword used in Demon Slayer and Shadow of the Storm. It is a demonbane sword that is very effective against demonic creatures. As it is a silver weapon, it is also effective against most vampyres. It is obtained by bringing the three Silverlight keys to Sir Prysin during Demon Slayer.

In Demon Slayer, it is used to defeat Delrith. In Shadow of the Storm, it is dyed black using black dye, and later transforms into Darklight when it gets stained with the blood of Agrith-Naar.

It can be mounted on the wall in the quest hall of a player-owned house.
2403: The Hazeel scroll is a scroll containing the incantation used to free Hazeel in the evil side of the Hazeel Cult quest. The scroll is located up in a secret room on the 2nd floor of the Carnillean Mansion in a locked chest which can only be opened with a chest key. It is used by Alomone to reconstruct Hazeel's body.
2404:
Chest key may refer to:

Chest key (Digsite)

Chest key (Fancy chest)

Chest key (Ghosts Ahoy)

Chest key (Hazeel Cult)

Chest key (The Path of Glouphrie)

Chest key (Pirate's Treasure)
2405: Carnillean armour is obtainable only during Ceril's side of the Hazeel Cult quest by killing Alomone and looting the nearby chest. It is possible to get multiple armour pieces by looting the chest multiple times. Carnillean requires a Defence level of 1 to wear but has lower defensive bonuses than the iron platebody. Some mages or archers may wish to use Carnillean armour due to it not lowering magic or ranged attacks. This piece of armour will not interfere with Ava's devices.
2406:
Hazeel's mark is a quest item from the quest Hazeel Cult. The item is only obtained when you choose Hazeel's side. It does not give any stat bonuses and is not used in any other quests.

If lost, Hazeel's mark can be reclaimed from Clivet. Multiple marks can be obtain using the drop trick.
2407:
The ball is a quest item used only in Witch's House. It is found in the shed of Nora T. Hagg's garden and can be picked up after killing the witch's experiment.

It is returned to the boy to complete the quest.

Duplicates cannot be obtained. If players try to use Telekinetic Grab on the ball, the message I can't reach that! will appear in the chatbox; therefore they must fight the experiment to retrieve it. Players may re-enter the shed to fight the experiment again, but they cannot take a duplicate ball. If they try to, they will receive the message: You already have the boys ball...

After completing the quest, the ball can still be seen in the shed once it has respawned, but cannot be retrieved. This is because Nora's garden becomes inaccessible after the quest; attempting to open the door to her house will result in the chatbox message: It would be rude to break into this house.

If the player somehow manages to have a second ball on the ground outside the witch's house and tries to pick it up after the quest, the game will give the message, "Another ball! The witch must have found another one. You decide to leave this one here."
2408:
The witch's diary is a quest item used only in Witch's House. It is found on the desk on the ground floor of Nora T. Hagg's house.

It reveals information on some of the witch's experiments, giving the player clues on how to get into the back yard and what to expect during the fight.

Before starting Grim Tales, it only includes entries up to the 9th of Pentember, afterwards additional days are revealed upon progressing through Grim Tales.

Duplicates can be obtained during the quest, but it serves no further use. It can be found in the bookcases of the player's house.
2409:
Door key can refer to the following:

Door key (Darkness of Hallowvale) - A key acquired during the Darkness of Hallowvale quest.

Door key (Witch's House) - A key acquired during the Witch's House quest to open said house. May also be required for Mourning's End Part II.
2411:
The key is a quest item used during the Witch's House quest to open the shed door and retrieve the ball. It is found by searching the fountain in Nora T. Hagg's garden.

Duplicates can be drop tricked by searching the fountain to obtain another. This key cannot be added to a steel key ring.
2412:
The Saradomin cape is a reward from Mage Arena I miniquest. To receive the cape, the player must defeat Kolodion in his four guises, then speak to him, step through the nearby sparkling pool, and finally pray at the Statue of Saradomin. Upon praying at the statue, the Saradomin cape will appear next to the player and can be picked up.

The Saradomin cape and the Saradomin staff are required to benefit from the Charge spell, which enables the player to hit up to 50% more damage with the Saradomin Strike spell.

Once lost, a player can get a new cape by once again praying at the statue of Saradomin. Kolodion does not have to be fought again. Alternatively, players can purchase one from Perdu for 23,000 coins (although this requires the player obtain the cape at least once from the Mage Arena).

The Saradomin cape can be imbued with the items dropped by Justiciar Zachariah, Porazdir, and Derwen, during the Mage Arena II miniquest to make an imbued Saradomin cape. Subsequent imbues will require only the Justiciar's hand.

The Saradomin cape can be combined with the max cape to change its appearance by turning it into the Saradomin max cape.

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room.
2414:
The Zamorak cape is a reward from Mage Arena I miniquest. To receive the cape, the player must defeat Kolodion in his four guises, then speak to him, step through the nearby sparkling pool, and finally pray at the Statue of Zamorak. Upon praying at the statue, the Zamorak cape will appear next to the player and can be picked up.

The Zamorak cape and the Zamorak staff are required to benefit from the Charge spell, which enables the player to hit up to 50% more damage with the Flames of Zamorak spell.

Once lost, a player can get a new cape by once again praying at the statue of Zamorak. Kolodion does not have to be fought again. Alternatively, players can purchase one from Perdu for 23,000 coins (although this requires the player obtain the cape at least once from the Mage Arena).

The Zamorak cape can be imbued with the items dropped by Justiciar Zachariah, Porazdir, and Derwen, during the Mage Arena II miniquest to make an imbued Zamorak cape. Subsequent imbues will require only the Demon's heart.

The Zamorak cape can be combined with the max cape to change its appearance by turning it into the Zamorak max cape.

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room.
2416:
The Guthix staff is a god staff that can only be obtained by finishing Mage Arena I miniquest. Like the other God staves, this staff requires level 60 Magic to acquire and therefore wield. To get it, the player must defeat Kolodion the mage in all of his forms. Afterwards, they will have to pick a god to worship to receive a cape and the staff corresponding to that god. If the player has already chosen another god, the staff can be purchased from the Chamber Guardian for 80,000 coins.

The staff allows wielders to cast the Claws of Guthix spell, which must be cast 100 times inside the Mage Arena minigame to gain the ability to use it outside of the arena. The spell has a chance to lower the opponent's defence by 5% on a successful hit, which does not stack with subsequent hits and will not re-occur until the opponents defence has returned to their original level. The spell can also be temporarily powered up by casting the Charge spell first.
2419:
The wig is an item used in the Prince Ali Rescue quest. Ned creates it if three balls of wool are given to him. A yellow dye can be used on a grey wig to turn it blonde. The player may ask Ned to create as many as they want.

The wig is one of the necessary items to disguise Prince Ali as Lady Keli, as part of the rescue operation.

The wig is removed from the inventory after talking to Prince Ali.
2421:
The wig is an item used in the Prince Ali Rescue quest. Ned creates it if three balls of wool are given to him. A yellow dye can be used on a grey wig to turn it blonde. The player may ask Ned to create as many as they want.

The wig is one of the necessary items to disguise Prince Ali as Lady Keli, as part of the rescue operation.

The wig is removed from the inventory after talking to Prince Ali.
2422:
Blue partyhats are tradeable cosmetic items obtained by completing one of the Christmas holiday events that occur once per year.

It can be sewn with sagacious spectacles to make Partyhat & specs by talking to Patchy, along with 500 coins. Doing so requires the completion of Cabin Fever and a book o' Piracy.

Previously, they were obtainable during the 2013 Rare Drops event (from 4 July to 14 July) as part of a rare item drop.
2423:
A key print is a quest item in the Prince Ali Rescue quest. It is obtained by pressing Lady Keli's cell key into soft clay. The key print is used to make a bronze key that unlocks the cell door.

If lost, you must speak to Lady Keli again with soft clay, pink skirt, paste, and a dyed yellow wig in your inventory to obtain a new key print.
2424:
Paste is a quest item used in Prince Ali Rescue to disguise Prince Ali so he can escape from Lady Keli's prison.

Aggie can make it from ashes, redberries, flour, and water for free.
2425:
Vorkath's head is an item dropped by Vorkath. The head has various uses, such as being used to upgrade Ava's accumulator, as a cosmetic upgrade to the Slayer helmet, or sacrificed for Prayer experience. For any given kill, the drop rate of the head is 1/50, with the exception of the 50th kill, when the drop is guaranteed.

Players can take the head along with 75 mithril arrows, and either Ava's accumulator or 4,999 coins (for a new device), to Ava in Draynor Manor to obtain Ava's assembler, which gives increased stats and improved ammo return. Players can also use the head on a ranging or max cape to give the enhanced ammo-returning effect to those capes. Additionally, players can bring the assembler and Dizana's quiver to Ava to grant the quiver the ammo-returning effect.
2426:
Burnt oomlie is the result of burning a raw oomlie. This requires 50 Cooking, but unless it is wrapped in a palm leaf first, it will always be burnt.

The burnt oomlie has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.
2428:
An attack potion is a potion made by using an eye of newt on a guam potion (unf), requiring 3 Herblore, yielding an attack potion(3) and 25 Herblore experience. It is the first available potion to make with the Herblore skill. A dose of attack potion provides a temporary skill boost to Attack equal to 3 + 10% of the player's current Attack level, rounded down. This is less than the super attack's boost of 5 + 15% of the player's current Attack level, rounded down.

After Barbarian Herblore Training, roe or caviar can be added to an attack potion(2), requiring 4 Herblore, yielding an attack mix and 8 Herblore experience. An attack mix has 2 doses, boosts Attack equal to 3 + 10% of the player's current Attack level, rounded down, and heals 3 Hitpoints per dose.
2432:
A Defence potion is a potion made by using white berries on a ranarr potion (unf), requiring 30 Herblore, yielding a Defence potion(3) and 75 Herblore experience. A dose of Defence potion provides a temporary skill boost to Defence equal to 3 + 10% of the player's current Defence level, rounded down. This is less than the super Defence's boost of 5 + 15% of the player's current Defence level, rounded down.

After Barbarian Herblore Training, caviar can be added to a Defence potion(2), requiring 33 Herblore, yielding a Defence mix and 25 Herblore experience. A Defence mix has 2 doses, boosts Defence equal to 3 + 10% of the player's current Defence level, rounded down, and heals 6 Hitpoints.

A Defence potion(3) can be purchased from the Warrior Guild Potion Shop for 144 coins.

A Defence potion(4) is a reward from Jekyll and Hyde random events if a toadflax is given to Dr Jekyll.

A Defence potion (3) or (4) is used in the A Kingdom Divided quest.
2440:
A super strength is a potion made by using a limpwurt root on a kwuarm potion (unf), requiring 55 Herblore, yielding a super strength(3) and 125 Herblore experience. A dose of super strength provides a temporary skill boost to Strength equal to 5 + 15% of the player's current Strength level, rounded down.

Super strength along with super attacks are popular for player killing, bossing, Slayer, or melee training. The dragon battleaxe special may be preferable for melee training because it provides a similar boost while being much cheaper in the long run.

Crystal dust may be added to super strength, 1 dust per dose of potion, to make a divine super strength potion, requiring 70 Herblore.

A super strength(4), super attack(4), super defence(4), and a torstol can be combined to make a super combat potion, requiring 90 Herblore.

After Barbarian Herblore Training, caviar can be added to a super strength(2), requiring 59 Herblore, yielding a super str. mix and 42 Herblore experience. A super str. mix has 2 doses, boosts Strength equal to 5 + 15% of the player's current Strength level, rounded down, and heals 6 Hitpoints.

A super strength(4) is a reward from Jekyll and Hyde random events if a snapdragon is given to Dr Jekyll.
2444:
A ranging potion is a potion made by using a wine of Zamorak on a dwarf weed potion (unf), requiring 72 Herblore, yielding a ranging potion(3) and 162.5 Herblore experience. A dose of ranging potion provides a temporary skill boost to Ranged equal to 4 + 10% of the player's current Ranged level, rounded down, and will wear off at a rate of 1 level every 60 seconds (90 with preserve).

Crystal dust may be added to ranging potion, 1 dust per dose of potion, to make a divine ranging potion, requiring 74 Herblore.

After Barbarian Herblore Training, caviar can be added to a ranging potion(2), requiring 80 Herblore, yielding a ranging mix and 54 Herblore experience. A ranging mix has 2 doses, boosts Ranged equal to 4 + 10% of the player's current Ranged level, rounded down, and heals 6 Hitpoints.
2446:
An antipoison is a potion made by using unicorn horn dust on a marrentill potion (unf), requiring 5 Herblore, yielding an antipoison(3) and 37.5 Herblore experience. A dose of antipoison cures poison and provides immunity to poison for 90 seconds. Drinking two doses of antipoison will cure venom. The first dose will reduce the venom to poison and the second will remove the poison.

The next cheapest alternative, superantipoison, cures poison and provides immunity for 6 minutes.

After Barbarian Herblore Training, roe or caviar can be added to an antipoison(2), requiring 6 Herblore, yielding an antipoison mix and 12 Herblore experience. An antipoison mix has 2 doses, cures poison and provides immunity to poison for 90 seconds, and heals 3 Hitpoints.
2448:
A superantipoison is a potion made by using unicorn horn dust on an irit potion (unf), requiring 48 Herblore, yielding a superantipoison(3) and 106.3 Herblore experience. A dose of superantipoison cures poison and provides poison immunity for 6 minutes. Drinking two doses of superantipoison will cure venom. The first dose will reduce the venom to poison and the second will remove the poison.

A superantipoison(1) can be found in the southern most collapsed building north-east of the Observatory, near the entrance to the Observatory Dungeon with a respawn time of 55 seconds.

Creating a superantipoison from scratch in the Seers' Village/Catherby area is a requirement for the medium Kandarin Diary.

After Barbarian Herblore Training is completed, caviar can be added to a superantipoison(2) to produce an anti-poison supermix. This requires 51 Herblore and provides 35 Herblore experience. An anti-poison supermix has 2 doses, each of which heals 6 Hitpoints in addition to the normal superantipoison immunity.
2452:
An antifire potion provides slight immunity to a dragon's breath. When used in conjunction with an anti-dragon shield or dragonfire shield, a single dose will provide complete immunity against dragonfire for 6 minutes. It can be made by a player with 69 Herblore by mixing clean lantadyme and then dragon scale dust in a vial of water, which grants 157.5 Herblore experience. It may only be used after starting Dragon Slayer I. Additionally, it can be upgraded to either an extended or super antifire by adding lava scale shards with 84 Herblore or crushed superior dragon bones with 92 Herblore, respectively.

Players will get a warning in their chatbox when the potion is about to wear off after approximately 5 minutes, 45 seconds: "Your antifire potion is about to expire." Then they will get another message when it has worn off, approximately 6 minutes in total: "Your antifire potion has expired." This allows you to keep track of how long you have until you have to drink again.

Protect from Magic, in conjunction with an antifire or extended antifire, may be used in place of an anti-dragon shield or dragonfire shield to grant complete immunity to close-range dragonfire attacks, such as those from chromatic dragons. Using Protect from Magic does not provide any dragonfire protection from the long-range dragonfire attacks of metal dragons, such as mithril or rune dragons, and an anti-dragon shield or dragonfire shield must be used for complete immunity.

It can reduce the damage from Cerberus' lava pool attack if combined with other sources of dragonfire resist.

Warning: Players should remember that an antifire potion alone will not fully protect them from dragonfire (players will get a message in their text box stating that they have been horribly burnt by the fire). The potion's protection is so slight that, when used alone, even a single dragon can cause extensive damage to the player from its breath. Only when the potion is combined with the anti-dragon shield or dragonfire shield will players be completely immune to dragonfire.

After Barbarian Herblore Training is completed, caviar can be added to an antifire potion(2) to produce an antifire mix. This requires 75 Herblore and provides 53 Herblore experience. An antifire mix has 2 doses, each of which heals 6 Hitpoints in addition to the usual antifire immunity.

2460:
Assorted flowers are a type of flower that can be harvested after planting mithril or adamant seeds.

When planting the seeds, players have an option to either pick the flowers (and obtaining a random coloured flower) or leave them planted on the ground. A player only has one chance to pick their flowers; if they refuse to do so, they will not get the option again unless they plant another seed. Flowers that are left on the ground will stay there temporarily for around 5 minutes.

Flowers can be wielded in the weapon slot, and are classified as a fun weapon in legacy duels within the Emir's Arena because it gives the wielding player negative bonuses.

Flowers that are left on the ground will stay there temporarily for around 5 minutes.

2481:
Lantadyme is a high level herb requiring a Herblore level of 67 to clean. It is obtained by cleaning grimy lantadyme which can be grown from a lantadyme seed with a Farming level of 73.

Lantadymes are used to make anti-fire potions (with ground blue dragon scales) and magic potions (with potato cactus). To create a potion, you need to add the cleaned herb to a vial of water to create a lantadyme potion (unf), and then add the secondary ingredient.
2483: A lantadyme potion (unf) is an unfinished potion made by using a lantadyme on a vial of water, requiring 69 Herblore. Using dragon scale dust on a lantadyme potion (unf) with 69 Herblore yields an antifire potion (3) and 157.5 Herblore experience. Using a potato cactus on a lantadyme potion (unf) with 76 herblore yields a magic potion (3) and 172.5 Herblore experience.
2489:
Red d'hide vambraces are a piece of red dragonhide armour worn in the hand slot that requires a Ranged level of 60 to equip and a Crafting level of 73 to create.

Kebbit claws can be used on these vambraces to make red spiky vambraces, requiring a Crafting level of 32.
2495:
Red d'hide chaps are a piece of the red dragonhide armour set, and require level 60 Ranged to wear. Similarly to other dragonhide chaps, they have no Defence level requirement.

A player with 75 Crafting can make them using 2 red dragon leather and 1 thread with a needle, granting 156 experience.
2501:
A red d'hide body is red dragonhide armour equipped in the body slot, requiring 60 Ranged and 40 Defence.

Although the Dragon Slayer I quest must be completed to equip the green d'hide body, it is not required to equip the blue d'hide body, red d'hide body, or black d'hide body.
2503:
Black d'hide body is a part of the black dragonhide armour set. It requires at least level 70 Ranged and 40 Defence to be worn.

It is the strongest standard dragonhide body and is among the most resilient armours against Magic damage. However, Blessed dragonhide armour provides higher defensive stats while maintaining the same offensive stats.

Due to its effectiveness relative to its low cost, it is a very commonly used piece of armour in the Wilderness, however not as ubiquitous as it used to be since the stats were reduced.

Although players must complete Dragon Slayer I in order to wear the green d'hide body, completion of this quest is not required to equip the blue, red, or black dragonhide bodies.
2507: Red dragon leather is used in the Crafting skill to make red dragonhide armour. It can be created by giving a red dragonhide and 20 coins to a tanner. Tanners can be found in Al Kharid, the Ranging Guild, Canifis, Forthos Dungeon, Crafting Guild, Kebos Lowlands, and Auburnvale. The last two tanners require the completion of Getting Ahead and children of the Sun, respectively. Alternatively, red dragon leather can be made using the Tan Leather spell. Crafting any piece of red dragonhide armour will grant the player 78 experience per hide.
2509: Black dragon leather is used in the Crafting skill to make black d'hide armour. It can be created by giving a black dragonhide and 20 coins to a tanner (45 coins at Sbott in Canifis). Tanners can be found in Al Kharid, the Ranging Guild, Forthos Dungeon, Canifis, Auburnvale, and the Crafting Guild. Alternatively, black dragon leather can be made using the Tan Leather spell. Crafting any piece of black dragonhide armour will grant the player 86 experience per hide.
2511:
Logs, also called normal logs, are obtained from cutting regular, evergreen, jungle, dying and dead trees, and uncommonly from infected roots. Players can burn these logs using the Firemaking skill. Cutting the logs gives 25 Woodcutting experience, and burning them gives 40 Firemaking experience. These logs have no requirement to be cut or burnt.

Members training Construction can bring logs to a sawmill to make planks at a cost of 100 coins each. Alternatively, the Lunar spell Plank Make can allow players to convert them to planks at a lower cost, but at the expense of runes.

While wearing Kandarin headgear 1 or higher, normal trees anywhere give double logs when chopped down but no additional experience is provided.

It is currently the only log which can be coloured with gnomish firelighters, which are obtained as rewards from Treasure Trails. These firelighters produce fire in one of five predetermined colours: red, blue, green, purple, or white. Coloured logs also give 50 Firemaking experience, slightly more than lighting the logs normally.

Members can also fletch these logs into bows and arrow shafts, and are the only type of log that can be made into javelin shafts.

Normal logs are also used to travel to Entrana or Taverley using the Balloon Transport System after completing the Enlightened Journey quest (they are also required during the quest).

Four normal logs respawn on Lumbridge Castle's roof, in a house in Draynor Village, in the Wizards' Tower, and in a house in Rimmington. They also spawn south of Varlamore.
2522:
White toy horseys are items made as a joke by Jagex, poking fun at the requests made by players to have horses. Toy horseys are obtainable from Diango for 150 coins, and come in 4 different colours: white, black, grey, and brown. They can also be made from a plank on any crafting table in a player-owned house, which requires level 10 or higher Crafting.

When you play with the horsey, an animation showing your character playing with it appears, and your character says Just say neigh to gambling!
2526:
Grey toy horseys are items made as a joke by Jagex, poking fun at the requests made by players to have horses. Toy horseys are obtainable from Diango for 150 coins, and come in 4 different colours: white, black, grey, and brown. They can also be made from a plank on any crafting table in a player-owned house, which requires level 10 or higher Crafting.

When you play with the horsey, an animation showing your character playing with it appears, and your character says Just say neigh to gambling!
2528:
The lamp is a reward obtained from several random events or by opening an Intricate Pouch that differs from those awarded by quests. While these lamps cannot be traded or banked, rubbing one gives the option of adding experience to any skill a player chooses. The amount given is ten times their skill level of choice (e.g. a skill at level 21 would give 210 experience).

Lamps always go to your gravestone on death unless protected.
2530:
Bones are the remains of most creatures with an animalistic or humanoid appearance.

Bones give 4.5 Prayer experience when buried. This can be increased by offering the bones in different ways:

13.5 XP when casting Sinister Offering.

13.5 XP when using the sacred bone burner after the appropriate faith level has been achieved.

15.7 XP when offered at a gilded altar with two burners lit or at the Chaos Temple. The Temple additionally has a 50% chance to not deplete the bones; effectively doubling the XP to 31.4 per bone.

18 XP when offered at the Ectofuntus in the form of bonemeal.

20 XP when blessed, broken down into blessed bone shards and offered at the libation bowl with jug of blessed wine, or 24 XP when offered with a jug of blessed sunfire wine. Virilis outside the altar will exchange noted bones for 10 coins each.

Players may also use the Bones to Bananas or Bones to Peaches spells to turn normal bones to edible bananas or peaches.

25 regular bones are used in the Demon Slayer quest.
2532:
Iron fire arrows are iron arrows wrapped in an oily cloth, which are then lit by using them on a tinderbox. They, along with any other fire arrow, are primarily used to pierce the guide rope in the Underground Pass to lower the bridge so that a player may walk across.

They have the same ranged strength as regular iron arrows.

2541:

2550: A ring of recoil is created by using Lvl-1 Enchant on a sapphire ring. When worn, a small percentage of damage received is dealt to the attacker; it has limited uses before it shatters. They can be used to charge a ring of suffering for the same recoil effect.
2568:
A ring of forging gives smelting iron ore a 100% success rate of creating an iron bar while it is worn. It can be made by casting Lvl-3 Enchant on a ruby ring, or by paying 250 coins with a ruby ring to Murky Matt in the south-east quadrant of the Grand Exchange.

A newly-enchanted ring has 140 charges. Each time the player smelts an iron ore while wearing the ring, one charge is consumed; after all charges are consumed, the ring crumbles to dust. If the player auto-smelts more iron ores than the number of remaining charges, the smelting will stop once the ring crumbles. The number of charges is specific to the player, not the ring, so swapping, dropping, or alching rings before 140 charges are used will not reset the number of smelts the player has left before a ring breaks. Players can right-click a ring of forging to either "check" how many charges remain in it or "break" it and reset the next one they use to its maximum charges.

When smelting multiples of an ore at the Edgeville furnace while wearing Varrock armour, there is a chance to smelt 2 bars at once. If this activates while smelting iron with a ring of forging, 2 charges from the ring will be used.
2570:
The ring of life is a diamond ring that has been enchanted with Lvl-4 Enchant. While worn, if the wearer is attacked and has 10% or less of their Hitpoints remaining, the ring automatically teleports the wearer to their respawn point. The ring crumbles to dust after one use. A Defence cape can be worn for the same effect, which does not destroy itself on activation. An Escape crystal can be configured to provide the same effect and more.

The ring does not guarantee total safety, as a player wearing one will still die if they are hit from above 10% of their maximum Hitpoints to zero (for example, being hit 15 while at 15 hitpoints), and it will not cure poison. Self-inflicted damage, such as guzzling a dwarven rock cake or using a locator orb, can also activate the effect. If it is worn along with a phoenix necklace, the necklace effect will trigger first. In PvP, the Tele Block spell will prevent a player's ring of life from activating.

It is one the few items whose teleports will work up to level 30 Wilderness, while most other means of teleportation will not work above level 20 Wilderness.

In Wintertodt, the ring will activate if warmth drops below 10%.

Upon the completion of medium Ardougne Diary, the teleport destination can be toggled to East Ardougne.

A ring of life is a reward from the The Lost Tribe quest.

When the ring of life effect procs, a player wearing the ring of life will be teleported and the following chat message will appear: Your Ring of Life saves you and is destroyed in the process.
2574:
A sextant is an item used for solving coordinate clues whilst on a Treasure Trail. It does not need to be brought with the player if the exact coordinate is known beforehand.

A chart can be obtained by first talking to the Observatory professor (who may be at the Observatory or the nearby Observatory reception building to the north-east, depending upon whether the player has completed the Observatory Quest), then, speaking to Murphy in Port Khazard, who will give you a sextant. Murphy is found on the dock near the trawler for the Fishing Trawler. Brother Kojo in the Clock Tower can then give the player a watch.

After first obtaining a sextant from Murphy, the player may thereafter make sextants with level 23 Crafting or higher. A sextant can be made by having one steel bar in the inventory and clicking on a crafting table 4 in the Workshop of a player's house. Making a sextant will give 15 Crafting experience.

Operating the sextant is a fairly simple task. The idea is to put the horizon and the sun in the middle of the screen.

First use the vertical 'arrow buttons' on the right to put the horizon in the centre of the viewer on the right hand side. Then use the horizontal arrow buttons to move the sun onto the horizon in the middle of the screen. Clicking 'get location' will give the coordinates of the player's position. This consists of two numbers; the first indicates how far the player is north or south of the Observatory, in degrees and minutes, and the second how far east or west. Note that one degree is 60 minutes, and each game square is approximately 1.875 minutes.

Sextants will often need to be used quickly in wilderness locations, as monster attacks can interrupt plotting.

A watch is an item for solving coordinate clues whilst on Treasure Trails. A chart can be obtained by first talking to the Observatory professor (who may be at the Observatory or the nearby Observatory reception building to the north-west, depending upon whether the player has completed the Observatory Quest). After talking to him, you have to receive the sextant from Murphy at Port Khazard in order for Brother Kojo to give you a watch at the Clock Tower.

Although not required for coordinate clues, a watch can be used with a sextant and a chart in the inventory to find the coordinates.

After first obtaining a watch from Brother Kojo, the player may thereafter make watches with level 28 Crafting or higher. A watch can be made by having one steel bar and one clockwork in the inventory and clicking on a crafting table 4 at the Workshop of a player's house. Making a watch will give 15 Crafting experience.

The drop trick can be used to obtain multiple charts if desired.

2795:
Puzzle boxes can be obtained by doing hard, elite, and master Treasure Trails. Before you are able to continue with your clue scroll, you will have to complete the puzzle.

A puzzle box is always scrambled 101 times before being handed to the player, by randomly sliding a piece into the empty position starting from the solved state.

If you have a duplicate puzzle box, (obtained by a method such as the Drop trick) in your inventory or bank after completing the clue, you cannot obtain another clue.

2832:
A key is an item needed to unlock a chest or drawer during a Treasure Trail.

There will be a clue telling you where to get it. The key is a drop only when carrying the clue scroll. It disappears when used to open the chest or drawer. Keys are non-tradeable objects, specific to the player who finds them. They are used on all levels of treasure trails.

It is possible to obtain more than one key using the drop trick. However, after taking a clue from the chest/drawer, the key won't open it again, and the player gets a message: "The chest (or drawer) is locked." Keys obtained this way from the same clue will still remain in the bank; however, keys obtained from different clues will not stack.

2862:
Achey tree logs are logs that can be obtained at level 1 Woodcutting from Achey trees for 25 experience each. Players can burn these logs at level 1 Firemaking for 40 experience each.

These logs are needed for the Big Chompy Bird Hunting quest to make ogre arrows, as well as composite ogre bows for Zogre Flesh Eaters.

With a knife, they can be made into 2-6 ogre arrow shafts for 1.5 Fletching experience per shaft made. With a knife and wolf bones, players can make an unstrung comp bow.

After giving Uglug Nar a relicym's balm during Zogre Flesh Eaters, he will open his store which stocks 100 achey tree logs at a base price of 4 coins. Uglug's store is the quickest way to obtain achey tree logs.
2864: Ogre arrow shafts are components used in making ogre arrows and brutal arrows. They require level 5 Fletching and starting the quest Big Chompy Bird Hunting to make. They are made by cutting an Achey tree and using a knife on the Achey tree logs. The amount of shafts given is random; between two and six will be made. 1.6 Fletching experience is gained per shaft made. Adding 4 feathers to each shaft makes flighted ogre arrows.
2865:
Flighted ogre arrows are made by using a knife on achey logs to make ogre arrow shafts, and then using 4 feathers per arrow shaft made. Doing so requires level 5 Fletching, granting 0.9 Fletching experience per flighted arrow.

Adding wolfbone arrowtips makes ogre arrows, while adding nails with a hammer will make brutal arrows instead.
2866:
Ogre arrows are used for hunting large game birds such as Chompy birds and Jubbly birds. These arrows can only be fired from ogre bows or composite ogre bows. Ogre arrows are required in Big Chompy Bird Hunting and the Freeing Skrach Uglogwee sub-quest of Recipe for Disaster.

They can be created through the Fletching skill at level 5, by using wolfbone arrowtips on flighted ogre arrows. 6 arrows can be made at a time with 1.0 Fletching experience granted per arrow made.

The player can claim ogre arrows once daily for free from Rantz after completion of the Western Provinces diary. He will give players 25, 50, 100, or 150 free ogre arrows each day, depending on completion of the easy, medium, hard, and elite diaries, respectively.
2871:
Ogre bellows are obtained by "unlocking" the Locked Ogre chest (i.e. pushing a boulder off from on top of it) in the north-west part of the cave near Rantz (not on worldmap) in eastern Feldip Hills where the ogre Rantz and his son and daughter live, directly north from the quest start icon where Big Chompy Bird Hunting is started (fairy ring code AKS is nearby). Multiple ogre bellows can be taken from Rantz's chest.

This item is also needed for obtaining various chompy bird hats, a section of the quest Recipe for Disaster, Mourning's End Part I, and the Western Provinces Diary.

The bellows are first filled with three loads of swamp gas from the swamp to the west. They are then used on the swamp toads found nearby to produce bloated toads. Only three toads may be carried at any one time in your inventory, though more than three may be laid on the ground. The now incapacitated bloated toad may be placed anywhere in the ogre area to attempt to attract a chompy bird. When filling the bellows, your character will attempt to fill all the bellows in your inventory automatically. Alternatively, the player can use the bellows on the swamp bubbles to fill them without delay.

Swamp toads that can be picked up cannot be used to fill ogre bellows. Attempting to do so results in the chatbox message stating "The chompy bird doesn't like this species of toad."

2875:
Bloated toads are used to catch chompy birds during and after the Big Chompy Bird Hunting quest. Their dyed variant, coloured toads, are used during Mourning's End Part I. Bloated toads can be obtained by using ogre bellows which have been filled with swamp gas on a swamp toad. Only three toads may be obtained at one time, and they cannot be banked.

Bloated toads may only be dropped in the ogre areas east and south of Gu'Tanoth. Once dropped, they have a chance of causing a chompy bird to land, lasting 1 minute before exploding and dealing 1-2 damage to all players within one tile (including diagonally). This damage cannot kill players.

Inflating a toad a second time by using filled ogre bellows on a bloated toad will lead to the toad floating away in a comical manner if the player is not in the possession of a ball of wool and a suitable rock; if these materials are available, however, a balloon toad will be created instead.
2876:
A raw chompy is obtained by killing a chompy bird. It can be cooked on an iron spit or at the ogre spit-roast near Rantz's cave, to make cooked chompy. Failure to cook it properly will result in a ruined chompy. Raw chompy is one of the three main ingredients in a wild pie.

The ability to hunt chompies is unlocked during the Big Chompy Bird Hunting quest. They are also used in the quest Recipe for Disaster during the portion where Skrach Uglogwee needs to be freed.
2878:
Cooked chompy is an ogre delicacy obtained by skewering a raw chompy with an iron spit, then cooking the skewered chompy on a fire, requiring level 30 Cooking and granting 100 experience when successful. Players may burn the chompy while cooking one, resulting in a ruined chompy; the burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 99.

Cooked chompy heals 10 Hitpoints. If hunting chompy birds, due to the meat's weight of 10 kg, it is recommended to do so south-west of Castle Wars. Big Chompy Bird Hunting is required to hunt them.
2883:
The ogre bow is a weapon requiring 30 Ranged to wield. Along with the comp ogre bow, it is used to kill chompies. The bow cannot be fletched, and it can fire ogre arrows as well as brutal arrows up to mithril brutals.

The ogre bow is obtained from Rantz during the Big Chompy Bird Hunting quest. If the bow is lost, another can be purchased from him for an amount which changes each time, but is in the range of 500-550 coins. The bow is also required for Freeing Skrach Uglogwee in the Recipe for Disaster quest.

The bow has the same ranged attack bonus but a much slower attack speed than the comp version; additionally, the comp bow is tradeable. For this reason, the regular ogre bow is rarely used after the quest is complete.

The player can check the number of chompy birds they have killed by selecting the "Check kills" option on the bow. Kills are only tracked after completing Big Chompy Bird Hunting.
2885:
"Whoopsie" is the name given to several unobtainable items in the cache. Many items were changed to have their noted forms removed: since items could not be fully removed once created, Whoopsies were added in a hidden update to fill these slots. The actual item was just a copy of a pink skirt.

In RuneScape 2, the item later became viewable via Quick Chat, causing much confusion.

All of the Whoopsies were gradually removed from Old School RuneScape and replaced; however, one remains, which was originally the noted form of the "Chompy bird object" item that appears in the chatbox when checking the Chompy bird kill count.
2886:
The battered book, titled Book of the Elemental Shield, is a quest item used in Elemental Workshop I. It is found by searching the east bookcase in the building with a cooking range, south of the building with anvils in it in Seers' Village.

It is read to start the quest. When a knife or any slash weapon is used on it, the player will receive a battered key to get into the Workshop and the book will become a slashed book. The battered or slashed book also acts as a tool in the player's inventory to make elemental shields. After the Elemental Workshop II quest, mind shields can also be smithed.

The battered book (or the slashed book) may be one of the items on the item list, given by Thorgel, that is needed to receive a death talisman during or after Mourning's End II; however, it is not needed to finish the quest as long as you already have a death talisman or catalytic talisman.

Duplicates can be drop tricked by searching the bookcase to obtain another. If the player searches the bookcase after creating the slashed book, all copies in the player's inventory and bank are deleted. Duplicates cannot be obtained after creating the slashed book. It can also be found in the bookcase in your house after getting it from Seers' Village.
2887:
The battered key is a quest item used in Elemental Workshop I. It is made by using a knife on a battered book. Additionally, it can be found by searching the bookcase where the battered book was originally found, only after creating a slashed book for the first time.

It is used to open the Odd looking wall in the building with the anvils in Seers' Village in order to access the workshop.

Duplicates can be drop tricked by searching the bookcase to obtain another only after the player has created a slashed book. Duplicates can be obtained after completing the quest. This key can be added to a steel key ring.
2890:
The elemental shield may be made during and after the Elemental Workshop I quest in the Elemental Workshop dungeon.

To make the shield, players must have a Smithing level of 20, an elemental metal, a hammer, and either a battered book or slashed book in their inventory. Use the elemental metal on a workbench in the elemental workshop to make the shield. Smithing the shield grants the player 20 Smithing experience. To equip the shield, players must have completed the Elemental Workshop I quest.

An elemental shield can be used for partial protection against the breath of skeletal wyverns and wyverns. When worn, it reduces the maximum damage of wyvern icy breath attacks to 10.

Upon completion of Elemental Workshop II, players can equip the mind shield for an additional +3 magic defence over the elemental shield.
2892:
Elemental ore is an ore that may only be obtained by killing a level 35 earth elemental after trying to mine the elemental rock. This ore can only be obtained during and after the Elemental Workshop I quest, and turned into elemental metals. Elemental ore is only found in the Elemental Workshop dungeon beneath the Seers' Village, in the house with the anvil, next to the bank. Earth elementals are found in the western area on the first level of the workshop.

The second level is to make bars, and repairs are needed here too. One elemental ore and four coal may be smelted into a bar of elemental metal using the blast furnace in the southern area of the Elemental Workshop (level 20 Smithing is required). This bar is used to smith the elemental shield and helmet.

At level 30 Smithing, the elemental metal may be primed and turned into a primed elemental bar. This may be used to create the mind shield and mind helmet in the Elemental Workshop II quest.
2893:
Elemental metal is a metal bar that is used in the quests Elemental Workshop I and Elemental Workshop II. It is made by using one elemental ore and four coal on the furnace on the south side of the first floor of the Elemental Workshop. Each bar must be made individually.

The elemental metal can be used to make an elemental shield or an elemental helmet. During Elemental Workshop II, it is also used to make an elemental claw and is processed into a primed bar in the second level of the Elemental Workshop.
2894:
Grey boots can be purchased in Canifis from Barker in his store, Barkers' Haberdashery. The boots come in five different colours: grey, red, yellow, teal, and purple. They give the same stats as leather boots.

Unlike leather boots, these cannot be crafted. Because of their stats, they are mostly worn for cosmetic purposes.
2896: Grey robe tops can be purchased in Canifis from Barker in his store, Barkers' Haberdashery. The robe tops come in five different colours: grey, red, yellow, teal, and purple.
2898: Grey robe bottoms can be purchased in Canifis from Barker in his store, Barkers' Haberdashery. The robe bottoms come in five different colours: grey, red, yellow, teal, and purple.
2900: Grey hats can be purchased in Canifis from Barker in his store, Barkers' Haberdashery. The hats come in five different colours: grey, red, yellow, teal, and purple.
2902:
Grey gloves can be purchased in Canifis from Barker at his store, Barker's Haberdashery. The gloves come in five different colours: grey, red, yellow, teal, and purple. These gloves are often worn to match certain armour sets, such as gold-trimmed and god armour sets.

Their defence bonus is equal to that of leather gloves.
2904:
Red boots can be purchased in Canifis from Barker in his store, Barkers' Haberdashery. The boots come in five different colours: grey, red, yellow, teal, and purple. They give the same stats as leather boots.

Unlike leather boots, these cannot be crafted. Because of their stats, they are mostly worn for cosmetic purposes.

2908: Red robe bottoms can be purchased in Canifis from Barker in his store, Barkers' Haberdashery. The robe bottoms come in five different colours: grey, red, yellow, teal, and purple.

2918: Yellow robe bottoms can be purchased in Canifis from Barker in his store, Barkers' Haberdashery. The robe bottoms come in five different colours: grey, red, yellow, teal, and purple.
2924:

2928: Teal robe bottoms can be purchased in Canifis from Barker in his store, Barkers' Haberdashery. The robe bottoms come in five different colours: grey, red, yellow, teal, and purple.
2930: Teal hats can be purchased in Canifis from Barker in his store, Barkers' Haberdashery. The hats come in five different colours: grey, red, yellow, teal, and purple.
2932:
Teal gloves can be purchased in Canifis from Barker at his store, Barker's Haberdashery, and are also dropped by Crawling Hands. The gloves come in five different colours: grey, red, yellow, teal, and purple. These gloves are often worn to match certain armour sets, such as gold-trimmed and god armour sets.

Their defence bonus is equal to that of leather gloves.
2936: Purple robe tops can be purchased in Canifis from Barker in his store, Barkers' Haberdashery. The robe tops come in five different colours: grey, red, yellow, teal, and purple.
2938: Purple robe bottoms can be purchased in Canifis from Barker in his store, Barkers' Haberdashery. The robe bottoms come in five different colours: grey, red, yellow, teal, and purple.
2940: Purple hats can be purchased in Canifis from Barker in his store, Barkers' Haberdashery. The hats come in five different colours: grey, red, yellow, teal, and purple.
2944:
The golden key is a quest item used only in Priest in Peril. It is dropped by the hooded level 30 Monk of Zamorak in the Paterdomus Temple.

It is used to open the first gate under Paterdomus after killing the Temple Guardian and then it is exchanged for the iron key by using it on the southern monument (the one referencing to "Saradomin being the key"). After unlocking the first gate for the first time, it is not required to be in the inventory to open the gate again.

Duplicates can be drop tricked by killing another monk to obtain another before unlocking Drezel's cell. Additionally, should the player lose the iron key they can get another by swapping (using) a golden key at the southern monument. The golden key also cannot be added to a steel key ring.
2945:
The iron key is a quest item used only in Priest in Peril. It is obtained by using a golden key on the southern Monument in the Paterdomus mausoleum.

It is used to unlock the cell Drezel is detained in. Once used, the key disappears.

Duplicates can be obtained by using another golden key on the monument even if there is already a golden key on it. This can only be done before using the blessed water on the coffin. The iron key also cannot be added to a steel key ring.
2947:
A golden candle is a quest item used only in Priest in Peril. It is obtained by using a candle (extinguished) on the north-west Monument in the Paterdomus mausoleum.

It serves no purpose in the quest, and has no uses outside the quest, as it cannot be used as a light source in a dark area. However, players can cast Low Alchemy or High alchemy on it.

It cannot be obtained once Drezel has moved to the dungeon after the player has exhausted all dialogue with him after using the blessed water on the coffin.
2948:
A golden pot is a quest item used only in Priest in Peril. It is obtained by using a pot on the west Monument in the Paterdomus mausoleum.

It serves no purpose in the quest, and has no uses outside the quest, as it cannot be used for storing any materials. However, players can cast Low Alchemy or High alchemy on it.

It cannot be obtained once Drezel has moved to the dungeon after the player has exhausted all dialogue with him after using the blessed water on the coffin.
2949:
A golden hammer is a quest item used only in Priest in Peril. It is obtained by using a hammer on the north Monument in the Paterdomus mausoleum.

It serves no purpose in the quest, and has no uses outside the quest, as it cannot be used in Smithing, Construction, or for opening the Bandos door in the God Wars Dungeon. However, players can cast Low Alchemy or High alchemy on it.

It cannot be obtained once Drezel has moved to the dungeon after the player has exhausted all dialogue with him after using the blessed water on the coffin.
2950:
Golden feather or gold feather may refer to:

Golden feather (Eagles' Peak), a quest item from Eagles' Peak

Golden feather (Priest in Peril), a quest item from Priest in Peril

Magic gold feather, a quest item from Holy Grail
2951:
A golden needle is a quest item used only in Priest in Peril. It is obtained by using a needle on the south Monument in the Paterdomus mausoleum.

It serves no purpose in the quest, and has no uses outside the quest, as it cannot be used in Crafting. However, players can cast Low Alchemy or High Alchemy on it.

It cannot be obtained once Drezel has moved to the dungeon after the player has exhausted all dialogue with him after using the blessed water on the coffin.
2953:
The murky water is a quest item used only in Priest in Peril. It can only be made during the quest by using a bucket on the well in the Paterdomus mausoleum to obtain water from the River Salve.

It is used to make blessed water by speaking to Drezel.

Duplicates can only be made during the quest. After talking to Drezel to bless it, all copies in the inventory are converted into blessed water. Duplicates cannot be obtained after completing the quest, as using a bucket on the well will only make a bucket of water.
2955:
Moonlight mead is a type of ale that restores 4 Hitpoints. It can be obtained through brewing at level 44 Cooking, granting 380 experience. It is brewed using 2 buckets of water, 2 barley malt, 4 mushrooms, and a pot of ale yeast. The stronger, mature version of the ale is the moonlight mead(m).

It can be bought for 5 coins from Roavar in the Hair of the Dog tavern, located in Canifis.

Upon drinking, the chatbox will state "You drink the foul smelling brew. It tastes like something just died in your mouth."
2957:
The druid pouch is an item first obtained during the Nature Spirit quest. Its main use is to protect the player against the ghasts that haunt the Mort Myre Swamp.

If lost, an empty druid pouch can be reclaimed from the inside of the Nature Spirit's grotto - one respawns near the grotto pool.

Building the Fire of Dehumidification after completing Making Friends with My Arm is a strictly better, non-consumable alternative to druid pouches, though the fire does not have any effect within the Temple Trekking minigame.
2958:
