If lost, an empty druid pouch can be reclaimed from the inside of the Nature Spirit's grotto - one respawns near the grotto pool.

Building the Fire of Dehumidification after completing Making Friends with My Arm is a strictly better, non-consumable alternative to druid pouches, though the fire does not have any effect within the Temple Trekking minigame.
2959:
Rotten food is food that has been attacked by ghasts in Mort Myre Swamp. It is inedible and almost useless, where the only use is to have it converted to stew by Abidor Crank encountered rarely during the Temple Trekking minigame.

Players can prevent ghasts rotting their food by:

Travelling direct to the desired location mitigating the need to travel through Mort Myre Swamp.

Filling the druid pouch, obtained during the quest Nature Spirit, to turn all ghasts who attempt to attack the player into attackable foes who can simply be walked past without risk of rotting the player's food.

Lighting the fire of dehumidification in the Mort Myre Swamp following the completion of Making Friends with My Arm will give the player permanent protection against ghasts rotting food (outside Temple Trekking/Burgh de Rott Ramble).

Equipping Morytania legs 4 completely blocks the attack that ghasts use.

Eating the piece of food that would have been turned into rotten food on the same tick as its being rotted. Doing so will allow you to eat the food and recover health, while the resulting rotten food will be placed in the first available inventory slot instead of replacing the rotted food.

Rotten food is obtained during the Zogre Flesh Eaters quest, when the player searches the backpack found deep within the Jiggig crypts.

It cannot be used to make Compost.
2964: A washing bowl can be found on a bench in Filliman Tarlock's Nature Grotto, south of the Mort Myre Swamp. Hidden underneath it is a mirror required for the Nature Spirit quest. The bowl respawns almost instantly and serves no purpose in the quest after revealing the mirror.
2966: A mirror is used in the Nature Spirit quest to prove to Filliman Tarlock that he is dead. It can be found under the washing bowl on a bench near the entrance to the Nature Grotto south of the Mort Myre Swamp. It is also obtainable after the quest, but it serves no purpose.
2967:
Filliman Tarlock's journal is one of a number of items that are simply called 'Journal' in the inventory. This particular journal is obtained by searching the tree in the middle of Filliman's grotto south of Mort Myre Swamp during the Nature Spirit quest. The player must read the journal to find vague instructions on how Filliman can transcend his current ghostly form to become a nature spirit.

The journal is not available from the tree after the quest. It is not found in the bookcase in a player-owned house.
2968:
The druidic spell is a spell scroll that can cast Bloom on rotten logs in Mort Myre Swamp to grow Mort myre fungi.

The spell is given to the player by Filliman Tarlock during the Nature Spirit quest and can be used only once, after which it turns into a used spell. The spell can only be used once the player has been blessed by Drezel during the quest. Attempting to use the spell before receiving Drezel's blessing will yield the message, "You need to be blessed before you can cast this spell." However, after completing the quest, the player can cast Bloom using a Silver sickle(b), or any of: Emerald sickle (b), Enchanted emerald sickle (b), Ruby sickle (b), Enchanted ruby sickle (b), Blisterwood sickle, Ivandis flail, or Blisterwood flail. For collectors, be cautious about dropping this item inside the grotto right before the quest's end. If left on the ground, it will disappear when the grotto shifts.
2976:
A sickle mould is a type of mould that can be used together with a silver bar to create a silver sickle. One can make a silver sickle at a Crafting level of 18.

The sickle mould can be purchased from the following shops:

Dommik's Crafting Store in Al Kharid

Jamila's Craft Stall in Sophanem

Rasolo the Wandering Merchant west of the Fishing Guild

Rommik's Crafty Supplies in Rimmington
2979:
The bowman hat (in-game: Chompy bird hat) is a members only decorative hat. To wear this hat, the player needs at least 5 Fletching and 30 Ranged. To obtain this hat the player must first kill at least 40 Chompy birds, then talk to Rantz. As this hat is purely for decoration, it gives the player no bonuses.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Chompy bird hat set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
2996:
Agility arena tickets were earned from tagging ticket dispensers within the Brimhaven Agility Arena minigame. Each ticket was rewarded after tagging more than one dispenser in a row. Tickets could then be redeemed for Agility experience and rewards from the Brimhaven Agility Arena Ticket Exchange run by Pirate Jackie the Fruit.

Exchanging larger amounts of tickets for Agility experience offered experience bonuses, up to 33% more per ticket. Wearing Karamja Gloves 2 or higher from completing the medium Karamja Diary when exchanging tickets rewarded 10% more total experience. Completing the elite Karamja Diary rewarded a 10% chance of receiving double tickets when tagging a pillar. The experience rewards increased by 5 per ticket for each Agility level above 40.

The item was discontinued and a new version was introduced following the 9 May 2024 Project Rebalance update, which can only be redeemed for Agility experience at a flat rate, as well as introduced Brimhaven vouchers, which can be exchanged for items. The discontinued tickets, as well as the former shop, are still available in-game for players who have the discontinued tickets to redeem. Players can also exchange the discontinued tickets for Brimhaven vouchers by using the ticket on Pirate Jackie the Fruit.
2997:
The pirate's hook is a reward from the Brimhaven Agility Arena that occupies the glove slot. It can be purchased from Pirate Jackie the Fruit for 800 Brimhaven vouchers.

Without the completion of the elite Karamja diary, it takes a minimum of 800 minutes (or 13 hours 20 minutes) to earn enough tickets for this item, assuming no dispensers are missed. Players with the diary completed have a 10% chance to gain double tickets, which lowers the time to 728 minutes (12 hours 8 minutes).

Players who have completed Cabin Fever can pay Patchy 500 coins to combine the hook with a crab claw to make a crabclaw hook. The hook cannot be stored in the player-owned house.
2998:
Toadflax is a low level herb, requiring level 30 Herblore to clean. It can be acquired from Random events or grown with a Farming level of 38, by planting toadflax seeds in herb patches. It can also be acquired by trading in 3 vouchers from the Brimhaven Agility Arena or as a reward from Temple Trekking. It is used to make agility potions and most commonly, Saradomin brews. To create a potion, you need to add the cleaned herb to a vial of water to create a toadflax potion (unf), and then add the secondary ingredient.

Using Toadflax in the coconut milk based Antidote+ potion is often considered a waste, as Antidote++ is vastly preferred by PvM'ers, whereas the Antidote+ is not usually in demand. However, Antidote+ can be a viable and cheaper option in certain situations, such as fending off poison while training Ranged or Magic at the Skeletal Monkeys on Ape Atoll. Ironmen may also prefer to create Antidote+ until they reach a high enough level to create its more potent counterpart.

According to the book Gielinor's flora - herbs, the flowers of a toadflax plant are often believed to resemble a toad's mouth, which is likely where it got the name. In addition, it is often mistaken for snapdragon and is widespread in rural spots.
3000:
Snapdragon is a herb which can be cleaned at level 59 Herblore. It may be grown from a snapdragon seed with a Farming level of 62, granting 98.5 Farming experience for every snapdragon grown. Once planted, the herb takes 80 minutes to fully grow.

Snapdragons are used to make super restore potions and sanfew serums with a Herblore level of 63 and a Herblore level of 65 respectively. To create a potion, you need to add the cleaned herb to a vial of water to create a snapdragon potion (unf), and then add the secondary ingredient.

According to the book Gielinor's flora - herbs, snapdragon is native to the rocky areas of Tirannwn, and is supposedly named due to its resemblance of the face of a dragon.
3002:
A toadflax potion (unf) is an unfinished potion made by using a toadflax on a vial of water, requiring 34 Herblore. Using toad's legs on a toadflax potion (unf) with 34 Herblore yields an agility potion (3) and 80 Herblore experience. Using a crushed nest on a toadflax potion (unf) with 81 Herblore yields a saradomin brew (3) and 180 Herblore experience.

One is used in the Land of the Goblins quest.
3004: A snapdragon potion (unf) is an unfinished potion made by using a snapdragon on a vial of water, requiring 63 Herblore. Using red spiders' eggs on a snapdragon potion (unf) with 63 Herblore yields a super restore(3) and 142.5 Herblore experience.
3006: A firework is an unobtainable potion released alongside snapdragon and the Brimhaven Agility Arena. It was presumably intended to be a cosmetic potion created from snapdragons, but was scrapped for unknown reasons.
3016:
A super energy is a potion made by mixing avantoe with mort myre fungi in a vial of water, giving 117.5 Herblore experience. It requires level 52 Herblore.

Super energy potions recover 20% of run energy per dose.

At 77 Herblore they can be used to make stamina potions using amylase crystals.

After Barbarian Herblore Training is completed, caviar can be added to a super energy(2) to produce a super energy mix. This requires 56 Herblore and provides 39 Herblore experience. A super energy mix has 2 doses, each of which heals 6 Hitpoints in addition to the normal super energy recovery.

Super energy potions can be a budget friendly option for players wishing to save costs on supplies. Super energy potions give the same 20% run energy restore as Stamina potions just without the 70% reduction in run energy depletion for 2 minutes. Stamina potions can run as much as 3x the cost of super energy potions so players may wish to use super energies when reduction in run energy depletion isn't needed, and only additional run energy is needed for their current task. Additionally, players can make unused Super energy potions into stamina potions as they progress their accounts as mentioned above.

3024:
A super restore is a potion that restores all player stats that have been lowered, including Prayer, but not Hitpoints. Players with level 63 Herblore can make a super restore potion by using a red spiders' eggs on a snapdragon potion (unf), giving 142.5 experience. Super restores can further be made into Sanfew serums by adding (in order) unicorn horn dust, snake weed, and nail beast nails into a super restore potion.

The restore value obtained per dose is 8 + 25% of the player's base level (rounded down) in each of the affected skills. For example, a player with 84 Thieving and 63 Smithing would restore both 29 points of Thieving and 23 points of Smithing for each dose consumed. The maximum amount of points that can be restored with this potion is 32 at level 96. This means that a super restore potion will restore 1 more Prayer point per dose than a prayer potion.

If a Prayer cape or ring of the gods (i) is equipped, or a holy wrench is in the player's inventory, the prayer restore increases to 8 + 27% of the player's current Prayer level, rounded down. This does not affect the rate of restoration of stats other than Prayer.

Two 3-dose super restores can be obtained by starting the Zogre Flesh Eaters quest.

After Barbarian Herblore Training is completed, caviar can be added to a super restore(2) to produce a super restore mix. This requires 67 Herblore and provides 48 Herblore experience. A super restore mix has 2 doses, each of which heals 6 Hitpoints in addition to the super restore recovery.

3049:
A grimy toadflax is a herb that has not yet been cleaned to make a toadflax. Grimy toadflaxes are grown from a toadflax seed with a Farming level of 38. Each herb grants 38.5 Farming experience when harvested. This is a great way to make a profit through farming, as toadflax seeds are inexpensive. Cleaning a grimy toadflax requires a Herblore level of 30 and gives 8 Herblore experience. Clean toadflaxes are used to make agility potions, antidote+, and saradomin brews with Herblore levels of 34, 68, and 81, respectively.

Grimy toadflax is one of the five herbs that cannot be obtained from the Sorceress's Garden minigame. They can, however, be purchased with 3 Brimhaven vouchers at the Brimhaven Agility Arena or with points at the Pest Control minigame. They can also be earned from Temple Trekking.

One of the few monsters that drops toadflax is the Tree spirit.
3053:
A lava battlestaff is a lava elemental staff which provides unlimited amounts of earth and fire runes as well as the autocast option when equipped. It requires 30 Attack and 30 Magic to wield.

The mystic lava staff is an even stronger alternative, providing better melee and magic stat bonuses. It is obtained by taking the lava battlestaff and 40,000 to Thormac. (Reduced to 30,000 or 20,000 with completion of the hard and elite Kandarin diaries respectively.)

This type of elemental staff is the best (once you've reached level 87 Magic) for getting enchantment points when training Magic at the Mage Training Arena. It is also useful for Enfeeble-alching.

The staff is obtainable as a potential drop from various monsters, Cerberus, or a potential reward from Barbarian Assault.

Players can use a lava staff upgrade kit, obtained from Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing, to cosmetically enhance their lava battlestaff, creating a lava battlestaff (or). This only alters its appearance, and becomes untradeable. It can be reverted, but the kit will not be retained.

This staff allows the casting of Lvl-6 Enchant, Shadow Veil, Battlefront Teleport, and Civitas illa Fortis Teleport without using elemental runes.
3054:
The mystic lava staff is an elemental staff requiring 40 Attack and 40 Magic to wield. In addition to increased Melee and Magic Attack bonuses, the staff provides unlimited amounts of earth and fire runes as well as the autocast option when equipped.

This type of elemental staff is the best (once you've reached or surpassed level 87 Magic) for getting enchantment points when training Magic at the Mage Training Arena. It is also useful for Enfeeble-alching.

This staff can be created after the completion of the quest Scorpion Catcher by taking a lava battlestaff and 40,000 to Thormac. After completion of the Hard Kandarin Diary and Elite Kandarin Diary, Thormac will only require 30,000 or 20,000 respectively.

It can also be obtained as a potential drop from Abyssal Sires, a potential reward from Barbarian Assault, traded by other players, and bought on the Grand Exchange.

Players can use a lava staff upgrade kit obtained from Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing to cosmetically enhance their mystic lava staff, creating a mystic lava staff (or). This only alters its appearance, and becomes untradeable. It can be reverted, but the kit will not be retained.
3058:
Mime top is a reward from the Mime random event and is part of the mime outfit. It gives no bonuses apart from its cosmetic appeal.

This item can be stored in the fancy dress box of a costume room, as part of the Mime Costume set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
3063:

3093:
Black darts are ranged throwing weapons. To wield black darts, players must have at least level 10 Ranged.

Black darts cannot be made with the Fletching skill and instead are obtained through monster drops. The only monsters to drop black darts are Burthorpe soldiers. This makes black darts rather rare and hard to obtain. Black darts can be poisoned and they can be wielded with a shield or god book for protection.
3094:
Black darts are ranged throwing weapons. To wield black darts, players must have at least level 10 Ranged.

Black darts cannot be made with the Fletching skill and instead are obtained through monster drops. The only monsters to drop black darts are Burthorpe soldiers. This makes black darts rather rare and hard to obtain. Black darts can be poisoned and they can be wielded with a shield or god book for protection.
3096:
Iron claws are a two-handed melee weapon. They are the second weakest claws available and can be wielded at 1 Attack.

Iron claws can be obtained by making them using the Smithing skill, or buying them from Martin Thwait in the Rogues' Den. The requirements for making them are completing the Death Plateau quest and 28 Smithing. To make them, use two iron bars on an anvil with a hammer in the inventory. This will grant the player 50 Smithing experience.
3097:
Steel claws are a fast two-handed melee weapon. To wield them the player must have at least level 5 Attack. They are given as a reward for completing the Death Plateau quest.

After completing the Death Plateau quest, they can be created at 43 Smithing. They require 2 Steel bars, and yield 75 Smithing experience. They can also be bought from Martin Thwait in the Rogues' Den.
3098:
Black claws are a fast two-handed melee weapon. To wield them, a player must have at least level 10 Attack. They can only be obtained as a monster drop.

As with all black and white equipment, the black claws cannot be made from raw materials using the Smithing skill.
3099:
Mithril claws are a two-handed melee weapon that are member's only. To wield them the player must have at least level 20 Attack.

Mithril claws can be created by using 2 mithril bars on an anvil with a hammer in the inventory after completing the Death Plateau quest. This requires level 63 in Smithing, and grants the player 100 Smithing experience.
3100: Adamant claws are a two-handed melee weapon. They can be made with two adamantite bars and a hammer at any anvil granting 125 Smithing experience. They can only be made by players who have completed the Death Plateau quest and have a Smithing level of at least 83. They have an Attack requirement of 30 to wield. They are not a very popular weapon due to the fact they require 2 hands to wield and provide inferior stats to that of the adamant scimitar.
3101:
Rune claws are a two-handed melee weapon, requiring 40 Attack to wield. They are the third strongest pair of claws.

Rune claws can be obtained either through smithing, as a drop from the Shellbane Gryphon, or looting ninja implings. They can be made at level 98 Smithing with two runite bars after completion of the Death Plateau quest, granting 150 Smithing experience.

As they are the cheapest and easiest to obtain claws with a special attack, they are the most accessible way to complete the combat achievement I was here first!.
3105:
Climbing boots are a low-level piece of armour used in the troll quest series, requiring the completion of the Death Plateau quest to wear. After finishing Death Plateau, players may buy climbing boots from Tenzing for 12 each.

Climbing boots are popular among players of all combat levels due to their low price, lack of negative bonuses, and the fact that they give +2 Strength bonus with no Defence requirement. They offer the same strength bonus as rune boots and mixed hide boots, which drop from Nechryael or can be crafted with 69 Crafting, respectively. By contrast, climbing boots can be obtained by most players within 30 minutes of making an account.

The boots can be taken, along with an iron bar, to the blacksmith in Burthorpe to produce spiked boots.
3107:
Spiked boots are boots that can be obtained by bringing Dunstan (the Burthorpe blacksmith) an iron bar and a pair of climbing boots. Dunstan will only help after a player completes a required portion of the Death Plateau quest.

Spiked boots cannot be used in place of climbing boots for climbing over rocks in the mountain path.

These boots are used during Desert Treasure I while trying to obtain the Ice diamond on the Ice Path segment. The spiked boots are unequipable, except during portions of Desert Treasure I. They are not needed after the quest.
3122:
The granite shield is a shield made of granite. It requires 50 Defence and 50 Strength to equip. It has defensive stats equal to the Toktz-ket-xil, minus the +5 strength bonus, and isn't commonly used for melee combat as a result.

It can be used in place of the rune kiteshield due to its superior ranged defence bonus. However, some players choose not to use it due to its weight and slightly lower melee defence bonuses.
3123:
Shaikahan bones are dropped by The Shaikahan when it is killed, which requires a Karambwan paste-poisoned spear or hasta. Note that any kills prior to Tai Bwo Wannai Trio will not yield any bones. Despite the examine text stating it glows with a yellow aura, its appearance remains akin to that of dragon bones.

Shaikahan bones give 25 Prayer experience when buried. This can be increased by offering the bones in different ways:

75 XP when casting Sinister Offering.

75 XP when offered at the Sacred Bone Burner after the appropriate faith level has been achieved.

87.5 XP when offered at a gilded altar with two burners lit or at the Chaos Temple.

100 XP when offered at the Ectofuntus in the form of Shaikahan bonemeal.
3125:
Jogre bones are bones dropped by jogres, which give 15 Prayer experience when buried. This can be increased by offering the bones in different ways:

45 XP when casting Sinister Offering.

45 XP when offered at the Sacred Bone Burner after the appropriate faith level has been achieved.

52.5 XP when offered at a gilded altar with two burners lit or at the Chaos Temple.

60 XP when offered at the Ectofuntus in the form of jogre bonemeal.

They can be lit with a tinderbox at level 30 Firemaking to make burnt jogre bones, granting 90 Firemaking experience. Burnt jogre bones are used with karambwanji paste during the Tai Bwo Wannai Trio quest to make marinated j' bones.

If a player selects "light" without level 30 Firemaking, the player will receive the message "You need a firemaking level of 30 to burn Jogre bones. You could find some other way of burning them.", hinting that you need to use a furnace to make burnt jogre bones.

Players can cast the Superheat Item spell on jogre bones for 53 Magic, and 25 Cooking experience.

Jogre bones cannot be used on the Exposed altar in The Teomat.
3128:
Pasty jogre bones are made by using burnt jogre bones with karambwanji paste. The item is used in the Tai Bwo Wannai Trio quest, where they must be marinated and given to Tinsay. They give 17 Prayer experience each if buried. There are four pasty jogre bones with the same name, but only one combination will successfully create the marinated bones.

Warning: Pasty jogre bones made from cooked karambwanji paste will explode, dealing 2 damage, when cooked. Players will receive the message: "The cooked karambwanji paste catches fire and explodes."
3129:
Pasty jogre bones are made by using burnt jogre bones with karambwanji paste. The item is used in the Tai Bwo Wannai Trio quest, where they must be marinated and given to Tinsay. They give 17 Prayer experience each if buried. There are four pasty jogre bones with the same name, but only one combination will successfully create the marinated bones.

Warning: Pasty jogre bones made from cooked karambwanji paste will explode, dealing 2 damage, when cooked. Players will receive the message: "The cooked karambwanji paste catches fire and explodes."
3130: Marinated jogre bones are a quest item that are made by cooking pasty jogre bones on a range or fire. They are used in the Tai Bwo Wannai Trio quest. They can be buried for 17 Prayer experience each.
3131:

3135:
Prison key may refer to:

Prison key (Prison Pete)

Prison key (Troll Stronghold)
3138: Potato cactus is an item that is used with the Herblore skill as a secondary ingredient when creating magic potions and battlemage potions. Potato cactus can also be selected as one of the 3 of 31 items needed for Fairytale I - Growing Pains as well as 1 of 50 items for Mourning's End Part II. They can be grown in a cactus patch by planting potato cactus seeds, requiring level 64 Farming. Eight are also used to pay Taylor to look after a player's Celastrus tree. Collecting 5 of them while inside the Kalphite Lair is a requirement for the Easy Desert Diary.
3142:
Raw karambwan are octopodes native to the tropical island of Karamja. Catching one requires 65 Fishing and a karambwan vessel using raw karambwanji as bait after completing the fishing portion of the Tai Bwo Wannai Trio quest. Each catch yields 50 Fishing experience. The karambwan fishing spots are north of the Karamja Shipyard and east of the harpie bug swarms at fairy ring code DKP, or alternatively fished at sea while on a raft.

To be able to cook a karambwan thoroughly, players must speak to Tinsay in his hut after completing the Tai Bwo Wannai Trio quest. When using a raw karambwan on a fire or cooking range, two options of cooking are given: poorly or thoroughly. Cooking poorly requires 1 Cooking, but yields a poison karambwan and 80 Cooking experience. Cooking poison karambwans is typically the fastest way to level Cooking from level 1, as Karambwans can be cooked faster than other food. Cooking thoroughly requires 30 Cooking yielding a cooked karambwan and 190 Cooking experience. Karambwan stop burning at 99 Cooking, 93 Cooking at the Hosidius Kitchen, or 86 Cooking at the Hosidius Kitchen after completing the elite Kourend & Kebos Diary.

Catching a karambwan is a medium Karamja Diary task, while cooking a karambwan thoroughly is a hard Karamja Diary task.
3144:
Cooked karambwan is a type of fish that restores 18 Hitpoints when eaten. They can be obtained by cooking raw karambwan on a fire or cooking range. Cooking a karambwan requires level 30 Cooking, and grants 190 experience when successful.

In order to produce a cooked karambwan, the player must first complete Tai Bwo Wannai Trio and afterwards talk to Tinsay in the southernmost hut in Tai Bwo Wannai. If the player has not done this, cooking a raw karambwan will instead produce a poison karambwan. Players may burn a karambwan while cooking one, resulting in a burnt karambwan; the burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 99 on both ranges and fires. It is possible to use tick manipulation to cook each raw karambwan in one tick rather than the standard four to increase Cooking experience rates.

When eaten, the message You eat the Karambwan. is displayed.

Karambwans are commonly used as a fast food, a subtype of food that incurs non-standard attack or eating delays when consumed. Karambwans may be consumed after other foods without delay; this does not work if the karambwan is eaten first, and does not work when eating two karambwan in a row. This technique (commonly referred to as combo eating) can be further enhanced by drinking a dose of Saradomin brew after your alternative food item, and before your karambwan (food>brew>karambwan).

Additionally, karambwans add a delay of two ticks before the player can attack again, while most other foods have a delay of three ticks.

Karambwans may also be used in tick manipulation to improve rates. This is only recommended for non-ironman players. For example, you can start your usual 3-tick timer using your herb and tar, then on the next cycle, you eat a cooked karambwan instead. This effectively allows you to 2.5-tick certain actions, such as barbarian fishing.
3146:
Poison karambwan is a type of untradeable food that damages the player for 5 poison damage. It can be obtained by cooking raw karambwan, granting 80 experience when successful. Prior to completing Tai Bwo Wannai Trio and speaking to Tinsay, poison karambwan will always be made when successfully cooking raw karambwan. After this event, raw karambwan can be made into either poison karambwan or into cooked karambwan, which heals for 18 Hitpoints. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt karambwan. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 99 on both ranges and fires.

Poison karambwan will only damage you if you have at least 6 Hitpoints. It applies a green poison hitsplat which is purely visual: you will not be poisoned or continue to take poison damage afterwards.

Poison karambwan can be used with a pestle and mortar, to create karambwan paste which can be used to poison spears and hastae.

Eating one will give the message You eat the Karambwan., followed by It tastes ... painful.
3147:

3150:
A raw karambwanji is a brightly coloured untradeable fish that may be caught at level 5 Fishing using a small fishing net at the Holy Lake south of Tai Bwo Wannai on Karamja (fairy code CKR). The raw version is used as bait to catch raw karambwan. It is also notable as an easily obtainable, stackable raw fish with the only requirement being 5 Fishing, making it ideal for feeding pet cats and fighting hell rat behemoths.

The amount of karambwanji caught depends on the player's Fishing level, increasing every five levels. The exact formula is ⌊FishingLevel/5⌋+1; players will catch 20 raw karambwanji at a time with a Fishing level of 95 or above and will catch 21 to 22 raw karambwanji at a time when boosting beyond 99. 5 Fishing experience is granted per catch, not per individual fish. The player can continue fishing for raw karambwanji even if their inventory is full. If there is room in the inventory, there is a chance to catch raw shrimps.

The benefits from either Rada's blessing or spirit flakes will give the player a chance to catch double the amount of raw karambwanji (for example, a player that catches 15 raw karambwanji will instead catch 30). They cannot be stored in a fish barrel. They can, however, be stored in a tackle box, as they are considered bait.

To use it to fish karambwan, players must load a raw karambwanji into a karambwan vessel and then use the vessel with one of the karambwan fishing locations in the north-east of Karamja to fish karambwan. Upon catching a karambwan, the vessel will automatically be reloaded with a new karambwanji from the inventory.

It is ground into raw karambwanji paste for Tai Bwo Wannai Trio. During the same quest, it may be cooked into karambwanji, but it cannot be cooked after completion of the quest. After completing the quest, raw karambwanji may be bought from Tiadeche for 10 coins each. He stocks 50 per world.
3162:
A Sliced banana is the result of using a knife or most weapons with a Slash attack style on a banana. The message box states You deftly chop the bananas into slices when slicing a banana.

When eaten, the sliced banana heals two hitpoints; the same amount as a whole banana. Sliced bananas are only used for the quest Tai Bwo Wannai Trio, wherein players are required to slice a banana before attempting to add it to a bottle of Karamja rum.
3164: Karamjan rum is an item used in Tai Bwo Wannai Trio quest, requested by Tinsay. It is made by using a sliced banana on a bottle of Karamjan rum. Adding the slices gives the message You add the banana slices to the Karamjan rum.. It will be confiscated by the customs officer just like regular Karamjan rum, but will not be destroyed by teleportation, entering Mor Ul Rek, or setting sail. Attempting to put the rum with banana in the crate near Luthas will give the message Pirates don't usually take sliced banana with their Karamjan rum..
3165:
Karamjan rum (banana) is an item made by using a banana on a bottle of Karamjan rum. It serves no practical purpose.

Adding the banana gives the message You stuff the banana into the neck of the bottle. You begin to wonder why.. Attempting to add a sliced banana afterwards gives the message You can't. A banana is blocking the neck of the bottle..

Attempting to hide it in the crate during Pirate's Treasure gives the message Pirates don't usually take banana with their Karamjan rum.. However, the customs officers will confiscate it if the player has started the quest and attempts to charter a ship. Unlike the regular Karamjan rum, it can be taken off the island by teleporting.

This item may result from a common mistake while completing Tai Bwo Wannai Trio, in which the player must use sliced banana with Karamjan rum. Many players forget to slice the banana first, forcing them to collect another Karamjan rum and banana.
3167: A monkey skin is produced by giving a monkey corpse to Tamayu during the Tai Bwo Wannai Trio quest. It is used to make a seaweed sandwich.
3170:
The bronze spear is a two-handed melee weapon made from bronze and is the weakest spear in Old School RuneScape. Spears are members-only weapons. Bronze spears can also be used to create a scarecrow.

Bronze spears can be easily obtained from low-level monsters such as goblins. There is a bronze spear spawn in the Haunted Mine on the second level near other assorted bronze equipment. A (kp) version can be bought from Tamayu after finishing the Tai Bwo Wannai Trio quest. Using the Smithing skill, players can create bronze spears. However, players must have begun Barbarian Smithing training to be able to smith these spears. It can also be found by digging at Level 3 digging spots at the Digsite, with a specimen brush, specimen jar and trowel in the inventory, or bought from the Fortis Blacksmith.

Like most spears, the bronze spear can be poisoned.
3171: The iron spear is a members-only two-handed melee weapon. An iron spear can be obtained by buying one from the Fortis Blacksmith, buying one from another player, or receiving it as a monster drop. The only way it can be created using the Smithing skill is through Barbarian Training after completing Tai Bwo Wannai Trio. It can be poisoned.
3172: The steel spear is a two-handed melee weapon that requires 5 Attack to wield. It can be bought from the Mount Karuulm Weapon Shop or Fortis Blacksmith, or obtained as a drop from monsters. Players who have started learning Barbarian Smithing and have level 35 Smithing may produce a spear at a Barbarian anvil from one steel bar and one willow log, receiving 75 Smithing experience. Smithing spears at the Barbarian anvil requires completion of Tai Bwo Wannai Trio. Like most spears, it can be poisoned.
3173: The mithril spear is a two-handed melee weapon made from mithril requiring 20 Attack to wield. Mithril spears are a members-only weapon. It can be bought from the Mount Karuulm Weapon Shop or Fortis Blacksmith, or obtained as a drop from monsters. Using the Smithing skill, players can create mithril spears on one of the barbarian anvils in either Otto's Grotto or Barbarian Village. However, players must have begun Barbarian Smithing training to be able to smith these spears. Like most spears, the mithril spear can be poisoned.
3174: The adamant spear is a two-handed members'-only melee weapon requiring 30 Attack to wield. It can be bought from the Mount Karuulm Weapon Shop or Fortis Blacksmith, or obtained as a drop from monsters. Using the Smithing skill, players can create adamant spears with level 75 Smithing This requires 1 adamantite bar and 1 yew log. However, players must have begun Barbarian Smithing training to be able to smith these spears. Like most spears, the adamant spear can be poisoned. Smithing an adamant spear at the anvil at Otto's Grotto is a requirement for the Kandarin Hard Diary.
3175:
The rune spear is a two-handed melee weapon requiring 40 Attack to wield. Unlike most other rune equipment, rune spears are members-only. Rune spears can be created at a barbarian anvil with 90 Smithing, requiring one runite bar and one magic log, as well as partial completion of the Barbarian Training miniquest. Like most spears, the rune spear can be poisoned.

A rune spear is also a requirement for a hard clue scroll. Ironmen can acquire it by completing Tai Bwo Wannai Trio for a rune spear (kp) then using a cleaning cloth on it, or by buying it from Mount Karuulm Weapon Shop.

This item is a rare drop from the rare drop table. Wearing a ring of wealth will increase the chances of receiving one from the rare drop table.
3176:
The dragon spear is a two-handed melee weapon that requires level 60 Attack to wield. It does not require the completion of a quest to equip. Like most spears, it can be poisoned.

The spear is a rare drop from both the rare and gem drop tables. On the gem drop table, the spear will only drop if the Legends' Quest has been completed, otherwise a talisman will be dropped in its place. However, the rare drop table does not require the quest's completion in order to be able to receive it as a drop. Wearing a ring of wealth will increase the chances of receiving one from both tables.

Goraks fought in the Gorak Plane while wearing a ring of wealth are more likely to drop the dragon spear than any other monster, with a drop rate of 1 in 325. Brutal black dragons are also frequent droppers of dragon spears, dropping it directly with a drop rate of 1 in 512 (while also having access to the rare drop table so they drop it slightly more common than this overall).

The spear is primarily used for player killing scenarios; outside of this, it is sought after by ironmen, as two elite clue steps require it.

As with most dragon equipment, the dragon spear cannot be made from raw materials using the Smithing skill.
3179:
Small ninja monkey bones are a form of monkey bones that can be obtained by killing Monkey Archers.

Zooknock is able to make a small ninja monkey greegree with the bones in the Ape Atoll Dungeon. If players want to make a medium ninja monkey greegree, they must use medium ninja monkey bones instead. After completion of Monkey Madness II, players no longer need to bring bones; they can simply claim the greegree from Zooknock in the Tree Gnome Stronghold.

Small ninja monkey bones give 16 Prayer experience when buried, which can be increased by offering the bones in different ways:

48 XP when casting Sinister Offering.

48 XP when offered at the Sacred Bone Burner after the appropriate faith level has been achieved.

56 XP when offered at a gilded altar with two burners lit or at the Chaos Temple.

64 XP when offered at the Ectofuntus in the form of small ninja bonemeal.

Small ninja monkey bones restore 2 prayer points when crushed with the Bonecrusher necklace.
3181:
Gorilla bones are the bones dropped by the level 167 Monkey Guards that inhabit the Temple of Marimbo on Ape Atoll.

Zooknock is able to make a gorilla greegree with the bones in the Ape Atoll Dungeon. If players want to make a bearded gorilla greegree, they must use bearded gorilla bones instead. After completion of Monkey Madness II, players no longer need to bring bones; they can simply claim the greegree from Zooknock in the Tree Gnome Stronghold.

Gorilla bones give 18 Prayer experience when buried. This can be increased by offering the bones in different ways:

54 XP when casting Sinister Offering.

54 XP when offered at the Sacred Bone Burner after the appropriate faith level has been achieved.

63 XP when offered at a gilded altar with two burners lit or at the Chaos Temple.

72 XP when offered at the Ectofuntus in the form of gorilla bonemeal.
3182:
Bearded gorilla bones are the remains of the bearded level 167 Monkey Guards found in the Temple of Marimbo.

Zooknock is able to make a bearded gorilla greegree with the bones in the Ape Atoll Dungeon. If players want to make a gorilla greegree, they must use gorilla bones instead. After completion of Monkey Madness II, players no longer need to bring bones; they can simply claim the greegree from Zooknock in the Tree Gnome Stronghold.

Bearded gorilla bones give 20 Prayer experience when buried. This can be increased by offering the bones in different ways:

60 XP when casting Sinister Offering.

60 XP when offered at the Sacred Bone Burner after the appropriate faith level has been achieved.

70 XP when offered at a gilded altar with two burners lit or at the Chaos Temple.

80 XP when offered at the Ectofuntus in the form of bearded gorilla bonemeal.
3185:
Small zombie monkey bones are the bones of small Monkey Zombies that are obtained from killing the level 82 zombie monkeys in the Ape Atoll Dungeon and under the Temple of Marimbo.

Zooknock is able to make a small zombie monkey greegree with the bones in the Ape Atoll Dungeon. If players want to make a big zombie monkey greegree, they must use large zombie monkey bones instead. After completion of Monkey Madness II, players no longer need to bring bones; they can simply claim the greegree from Zooknock in the Tree Gnome Stronghold.

Small zombie monkey bones give 5 Prayer experience when buried, much like standard monkey bones. This can be increased by offering the bones in different ways:

15 XP when casting Sinister Offering.

15 XP when offered at the Sacred Bone Burner after the appropriate faith level has been achieved.

17.5 XP when offered at a gilded altar with two burners lit or at the Chaos Temple.

20 XP when offered at the Ectofuntus in the form of small zombie monkey bonemeal.
3186:
Large zombie monkey bones are a form of monkey bones that can be obtained by killing level 129 Monkey Zombies in the Ape Atoll Dungeon or in the cave beneath the Temple of Marimbo.

Zooknock is able to make a big zombie monkey greegree with the bones in the Ape Atoll Dungeon. If players want to make a small zombie monkey greegree, they must use small zombie monkey bones instead. After completion of Monkey Madness II, players no longer need to bring bones; they can simply claim the greegree from Zooknock in the Tree Gnome Stronghold.

Large zombie monkey bones give 5 Prayer experience when buried, much like standard monkey bones. This can be increased by offering the bones in different ways:

15 XP when casting Sinister Offering.

15 XP when offered at the Sacred Bone Burner after the appropriate faith level has been achieved.

17.5 XP when offered at a gilded altar with two burners lit or at the Chaos Temple.

20 XP when offered at the Ectofuntus in the form of large zombie monkey bonemeal.
3187:
Skeletal gorilla bones are dropped by the skeletal gorillas in the Ape Atoll Dungeon. Unlike regular bones, if these are left on the ground for too long, another skeletal gorilla will emerge from them and begin attacking any nearby players. If there are too many skeletal gorillas already spawned, they instead turn into "burning bones", which cannot be picked up. In addition, they cannot be turned into a greegree.

When players leave the dungeon with them in your inventory, a message will appear in the chatbox stating that "The skeleton bones you are carrying crumble to dust", and they turn into ashes. However, they can be safely smuggled out via dying and reclaiming the items from Death.

Skeletal gorilla bones give 3 Prayer experience when buried, unlike standard monkey bones, which give 5 experience. This can be increased by offering the bones in different ways:

9 XP when casting Sinister Offering.

9 XP when offered at the Sacred Bone Burner after the appropriate faith level has been achieved.

10.5 XP when offered at a gilded altar with two burners lit or at the Chaos Temple.

12 XP when offered at the Ectofuntus in the form of skeleton bonemeal.
3188:
A cleaning cloth is made by using Karamjan rum (or the variant with sliced bananas) on a piece of silk, which is used to wipe the poison off a weapon or the colour off an abyssal whip or dark bow if one has used the recolouring items obtained from Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing. If used on a stackable item, such as poisoned darts, it will remove the poison from the entire stack. It can also be used to clean Blamish Oil off of an oily fishing rod or oily pearl fishing rod. The cleaning cloth can be used multiple times.

This item can also be bought with 60 coins from Tamayu in the village of Tai Bwo Wannai, located south of Brimhaven, deep in the jungle of Karamja, once the Tai Bwo Wannai Trio quest is completed.

The easiest way to make them is to use a knife to create sliced bananas, use the sliced bananas on the Karamjan rum, creating an unlabeled variant of the rum which does not get destroyed like normal, and then either teleporting to the mainland or banking the Karamjan rum in the Tzhaar caves.

A fast way to make them is to buy regular silk and bank it. Withdraw it using the bank in the Tzhaar caves. Then, exit through the volcano in Karamja, buy the rum (due east of the volcano, next to the Karamja general store), and make the cleaning cloths. Drop the rum outside the Tzhaar cave entrance as it explodes from the heat if taken in, re-enter the volcano, and bank the cleaning cloths, withdraw 26 more silk, exit the caves and pick up the rum and repeat the process.

Alternatively, you can also use an amulet of glory to teleport to Karamja to buy the Karamjan rum and drop it near the docks where the amulet of glory teleports your character. Pick up the rum and make your cleaning cloths, then teleport to Castle Wars using a ring of dueling to bank your cloths and repeat.
3190: The bronze halberd is a halberd made out of bronze. It can be purchased from the Quartermaster in the Tyras Camp or received as drops from Orks. Like all halberds, this weapon has an attack range of two squares, making it the only variety of melee weapon that can be used to safespot monsters. Halberds cannot be made with the Smithing skill. Although completion of the Regicide quest is required in order to wield the dragon halberd, it is not a requirement in order to wield any other halberds.
3192: An iron halberd is a halberd made of iron. It can be purchased from the quartermaster in the Tyras Camp or received as loot from goraks. Like all halberds, this weapon has an attack range of two squares, making it the only variety of melee weapon that can be used to safespot monsters. Halberds cannot be made with the Smithing skill. Although completion of the Regicide quest is required in order to wield the dragon halberd, it is not a requirement in order to wield any other halberds.
3196:
The black halberd is a two-handed melee weapon that is members only. To wield one the player must have at least 10 Attack and 5 Strength. To obtain a black halberd either buy one at Quartermaster's Stores in Tyras Camp or from another player. Although completion of the Regicide quest is required in order to wield the dragon halberd, it is not a requirement in order to wield any other halberds.

As with all black and white equipment, the black halberd cannot be made from raw materials using the Smithing skill.
3200: Adamant halberd is a halberd made from adamantite, requiring level 30 Attack and 15 Strength to wield. As with all halberds, the adamant halberd has one extra square of attack range while in combat, making it possible to safespot monsters. Halberds cannot be made via the Smithing skill. Although completion of the Regicide quest is required in order to wield the dragon halberd, it is not a requirement in order to wield any other halberds.
3202:
The rune halberd is a halberd made of rune. It can be purchased from the Quartermaster in the Tyras Camp for 83,200 coins. It requires 40 Attack and 20 Strength to wield. Although completion of the Regicide quest is required in order to wield the dragon halberd, it is not a requirement in order to wield any other halberds.

Like all halberds, with this weapon you can attack at a range of two squares away, making it the only variety of melee weapon that may be used to safespot monsters. The halberd has three attack styles: Controlled stab (shared exp), Aggressive slash (Strength exp), and Defensive stab (Defence exp), making it a poor choice for players who wish to train Attack, especially because of its slow attack speed.
3204:
The dragon halberd is a two-handed polearm and the third strongest halberd in Old School RuneScape, and can only be equipped with 60 Attack, 30 Strength, and completion of the Regicide quest. Like all halberds, the dragon halberd can attack at a range of 2 tiles, making it useful as a melee weapon type that can be used to safespot monsters.

Like most halberds, it has similar damage-per-second to its two-handed sword counterpart, due to bearing the same attack speed and similar combat stats. Specifically, compared to the dragon 2h sword, the dragon halberd trades 4 strength bonus in exchange for 3 additional slash attack bonus and some defensive bonuses, alongside the unique range bonus. Furthermore, its special attack, Sweep, also bears resemblance to the dragon 2h sword's special, Powerstab, because it hits multiple targets at once.

It can be purchased at Tyras Camp after completion of Regicide for 325,000 coins, looted from The Gauntlet, received as a drop from Zulrah, or obtained as an uncommon reward from Master Treasure Trails caskets.

As with most dragon equipment and all halberds, the dragon halberd cannot be made from raw materials using the Smithing skill.
3206: The King's message is a quest item that players receive from the King's messenger 4 to 12 minutes after logging in, once the player has completed the Underground Pass quest. When players receive it, it is a signal to them that they can start the Regicide quest.
3208:
Crystal pendant is an item used in Regicide. It is given to players by Lord Iorwerth so they can prove they're working for him. The crystal pendant has no uses after finishing the quest, aside from being aesthetically unique.

Warning: Pendants in the player's bank, equipped to their character, or in their inventory will be removed when speaking to Lord Iorwerth and King Lathas during Regicide. The pendant is silently taken from the player when talking to Lord Iorwerth to receive the Big book of bangs, as well as any future dialogue with Lord Iorwerth during the quest, and finally when speaking with King Lathas to complete the quest. As such, using the drop trick is necessary when talking to them for players who want to keep this pendant after the quest.
3209: Sulphur can be obtained by taking a piece of a sulphur formation, found on the northern shore of the Poison Waste. It can be ground using a pestle and mortar to make Ground sulphur, which is used in Regicide to make the Barrel bomb. All sulphur is removed from inventory and bank upon completion of Regicide.
3213:
Quicklime is made by putting limestone in a furnace while wearing gloves. If the player isn't wearing gloves, the limestone will corrode the player's skin and damage the player for 8 Hitpoints. Quicklime is used in the Regicide quest for making the barrel bomb.

With an empty pot in inventory, the quicklime is used with a pestle and mortar to make a pot of quicklime.

When attempting to crush quicklime using a pestle and mortar without an empty pot, the player will spill the dust on the ground and take a small amount of (non-lethal) damage.

Limestone can be mined in Silvarea (east of Varrock, near the house of the Odd Old Man) and in north-east Tirannwn.
3215: Ground sulphur is created by using sulphur with a pestle and mortar. It, along with a Pot of quicklime and a barrel of naphtha, are ingredients used for making the Barrel bomb. This item is made during the Regicide quest.
3221:
A barrel of naphtha is used in the Regicide and Mourning's End Part I quests. It is used as an explosive and as a solvent for a poison, respectively.

It is obtained by filling a barrel with coal tar, and then taking it together with 6-9 coal to the Chemist's house in Rimmington, before using coal to distill it.
3222:
Naphtha mix is created after mixing a pot of quicklime or ground sulphur into a barrel of naphtha. The other ingredient must be added to create a barrel bomb in the Regicide quest.

All Naphta mixes are removed from your inventory and bank upon completion of Regicide.
3223:
Naphtha mix is created after mixing a pot of quicklime or ground sulphur into a barrel of naphtha. The other ingredient must be added to create a barrel bomb in the Regicide quest.

All Naphta mixes are removed from your inventory and bank upon completion of Regicide.
3224: A strip of cloth can be made using 4 balls of wool on a loom. It is used in the Regicide quest as a fuse for the barrel bomb that players make in the quest.
3226:
Raw rabbit is a meat item with a 100% drop rate from the rabbits found in Isafdar and on Miscellania, as well as hunted from the Piscatoris Hunter area. This meat may be cooked, roasted, or added raw to make a Wild pie.

The meat may be skewered on an iron spit to make skewered rabbit, which can then be roasted on a fire to make roast rabbit. Alternately, a raw rabbit can be cooked over a fire or a range to yield cooked rabbit.

Either cooked rabbit or roast rabbit is required for the quest Regicide.
3230:
Big book of bangs is a book obtained from Lord Iorwerth and used in the Regicide quest. It is not needed after the quest, but if players want it again, they can reclaim it from a bookcase in a player-owned house or from the Grand Library in Prifddinas after completion of Song of the Elves.

It was written by Mel Achy.

3261:
Goutweed is a rare herb that is not currently used in Herblore, but rather traded to Sanfew in Taverley for random herbs at a 1:1 ratio.

Goutweed is obtained in three ways:

By sneaking past troll guards in the storeroom under Burntmeat's kitchen during (and after) the Eadgar's Ruse quest.

By growing from gout tubers in a herb patch, which are obtained occasionally from the Tai Bwo Wannai Cleanup minigame. This is not recommended, as gout tubers are valued at 592,634 on the Grand Exchange.

Rare reward from Brambickle in the Gnome Restaurant minigame.

It is an item required in the Eadgar's Ruse, Dream Mentor, and Dragon Slayer II quests. It is therefore recommended to gather at least three goutweed when you go to the storeroom for the first time, so that you do not have to go back multiple times.
3264:
Ground thistle is a quest item in the Eadgar's Ruse quest. It is made by using a Troll thistle on a fire to turn it into a dried thistle and then crushing it with a pestle and mortar.

The ground thistle is added to a ranarr potion (unf) to make a Troll potion.
3266:
The drunk parrot is a quest item used in the Eadgar's Ruse quest. It is obtained by giving alco-chunks to a parrot in Ardougne Zoo.

The player must hide the parrot underneath the rack near the prison cells in the Troll Stronghold. By doing this, the parrot listens to the sounds of humans screaming from the cells, and copies them. This makes the parrot sound like a human to the trolls.

The player must then give the drunk parrot to Eadgar in Trollheim, along with a dirty robe, 10 grain, a log, and 5 raw chicken. He will then turn them into a fake man that the player can give to Burntmeat, a troll cook, in order to obtain some information about goutweed.

Dropping the drunk parrot prints the message You release the parrot, and it flies away.. It can be reobtained by using more alco-chunks on the parrots in the zoo, or from Eadgar if the player has spoken to Eadgar about making the parrot learn to speak like a human.
3267:
The dirty robe is a quest item used in the Eadgar's Ruse quest. It can be obtained by talking to Tegid, the druid who is washing his clothes in the lake south-east of Taverley. The player has to threaten him during the conversation before he will hand them over.

The player must give the robes to Eadgar in Trollheim along with a drunk parrot, 10 grain, a log, and 5 raw chicken. He will then turn them into a fake man that the player can give to Burntmeat, a Troll cook in order to obtain some information about goutweed.
3268:
The fake man is an item used in Eadgar's Ruse. Players need to give this item to Burntmeat, the troll cook in the Troll Stronghold, in order to find the location of the rare goutweed herb. It is really made of grain, raw chicken, dirty robes, and a drunk parrot.

Players can obtain multiple fake men by drop tricking. Burntmeat will only take one from the player's inventory during the quest.
3270:
Alco-chunks are a quest item used in the Eadgar's Ruse quest. They can be created by using a knife on a pineapple to create pineapple chunks, and then mixing them with a strong spirit such as vodka.

During the Eadgar's Ruse quest the player gives alco-chunks to one of the parrots that live in Ardougne Zoo so that it can be smuggled out of the zoo. The player must give the drunk parrot to Eadgar in Trollheim, along with a dirty robe, 10 grain, a log, and 5 raw chicken. He will then turn them into a fake man that the player can give to Burntmeat, a Troll cook in order to obtain some information about Goutweed. They can't be remade after the quest, because the player says he won't need them anymore. If a player tries to make them before talking to Parroty Pete a message will appear that says "Why would you want to do that?"
3325:
Vampyre dust are remains dropped by vampyres. It is primarily used on Saradomin Braziers in the Hallowed Sepulchre to pass through holy barriers, where players can then loot the coffin past it.

It is also an item that may be asked for during the quest Forgettable Tale... Using 20 vampyre dust on an ornate undead combat dummy enables it to function as a vampyre.

It cannot be used with the ash sanctifier.
3329: The round blood'n'tar snelm is a type of helmet that reduces the damage taken from snails by 12. Its stats are similar to those of a steel med helm, but it has no requirements to equip.
3331: The round ochre snelm is a type of helmet that reduces the damage taken from snails by 4. Its stats are similar to those of a steel med helm, but it has no requirements to equip.
3337: The pointed myre snelm is a type of helmet that reduces the damage taken from snails by 4. Its stats are similar to those of a steel med helm, but it has no requirements to equip. It is a pointed version of the regular myre snelm.
3339: The pointed blood'n'tar snelm is a type of helmet that reduces the damage taken from snails by 12. Its stats are similar to those of a steel med helm, but it has no requirements to equip. It is a pointed version of the regular blood'n'tar snelm.
3341:
The pointed ochre snelm is a type of helmet created by using a chisel on a pointed blamish ochre shell. Doing so requires level 15 in Crafting, and grants 32.5 experience. Its stats are similar to those of a steel med helm, but it has no requirements to equip. It is a pointed version of the regular ochre snelm.

The pointed ochre snelm reduces the damage taken from snails by 8, and is recommended if players do not have access to Protect from Missiles.
3343:
The pointed bruise blue snelm is a type of helmet that reduces the damage taken from snails by 12. Its stats are similar to those of a steel med helm, but it has no requirements to equip. It is a pointed version of the regular bruise blue snelm.

It can be made by using a chisel on the shell dropped from a Bruise Blamish Snail with a pointed shell.
3345:
A round blamish myre shell is an item dropped by myre blamish snails with round shells in the Mort Myre Swamp.

Players with level 15 in Crafting can use a chisel on it to turn it into a myre snelm (round), which gives 32.5 experience.
3347:
A round blamish red shell is an item dropped by Blood Blamish Snails with round shells in the Mort Myre Swamp.

Players with level 15 in Crafting can use a chisel on it to turn it into a Blood'n'tar snelm (round), which gives 32.5 experience.
3349:
A round blamish ochre shell is an item dropped by Ochre Blamish Snails with round shells in the Mort Myre Swamp.

Players with level 15 in Crafting can use a chisel on it to turn it into a ochre snelm (round), which gives 32.5 experience.
3351:
A round blamish blue shell is an item dropped by Bruise Blamish Snails with round shells in the Mort Myre Swamp.

Players with level 15 in Crafting can use a chisel on it to turn it into a bruise blue snelm (round), which gives 32.5 experience.
3353:
A blamish bark shell is an item dropped by Bark Blamish Snails in the Mort Myre Swamp.

Players with level 15 in Crafting can use a chisel on it to turn it into a broken bark snelm, which gives 32.5 experience.
3355:
A pointed blamish myre shell is an item dropped by myre blamish snails with pointed shells in the Mort Myre Swamp.

Players with level 15 in Crafting can use a chisel on it to turn it into a pointed myre snelm, which gives 32.5 experience.
3357:
A pointed blamish red shell is an item dropped by Blood Blamish Snails with pointed shells in the Mort Myre Swamp.

Players with level 15 in Crafting can use a chisel on it to turn it into a pointed blood'n'tar snelm, which gives 32.5 experience.
3359:
A pointed blamish ochre shell is a 100% drop from the pointed variety of Ochre Blamish Snails in the Mort Myre Swamp.

Players with level 15 in Crafting can use a chisel on the shell to craft it into an pointed ochre snelm, granting 32.5 experience.
3361:
A pointed blamish blue shell is an item dropped by Bruise Blamish Snails with pointed shells in the Mort Myre Swamp.

Players with level 15 in Crafting can use a chisel on it to turn it into a pointed bruise blue snelm, which gives 32.5 experience.
3363:
A thin snail is a piece of raw meat dropped by snails in Mort Myre Swamp. It may be cooked on either a range or a fire, requiring level 12 Cooking. This yields 70 experience and thin snail meat, which heals 5 to 7 hitpoints in one bite.

When used on a pestle and mortar it can be used to create blamish snail slime provided you have a sample bottle in your inventory to collect it. The slime can be used to create blamish oil which is used for an oily fishing rod.

Cooking a thin snail on the Port Phasmatys range is an easy task for the Morytania Diary.
3365:
Lean snail is dropped by snails. They are made into lean snail meat with 17 Cooking yielding 80 Cooking experience. It heals 5-7 Hitpoints. These can be used for Temple Trekking.

When raw, lean snail looks like thin snail, but turns deep red when cooked.

In the activities Temple Trekking/Burgh de Rott Ramble, cooked lean snail can be given to the player's follower for the trek.

Grinding the lean snail produces blamish snail slime used in the blamish oil for Heroes' Quest. You are required to have a sample bottle in your inventory to collect it.
3369:
Thin snail meat is a type of food that restores 5 to 7 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking thin snails on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 12 Cooking and granting 70 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt snail. Thin snail meat is one of a number of foods with a reduced burn rate while using the Lumbridge Castle range with Cook's Assistant completed. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 47, or 43 when using the Lumbridge range.

Cooking thin snail meat is a task in the easy Morytania Diary.
3371: Lean snail meat is a type of food that restores 5 to 8 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking lean snails on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 17 Cooking and granting 80 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt snail. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Lean snail has an unusual burn rate, and has a reduced chance of burning on fires compared to ranges. However lean snail meat is one of a number of foods with a reduced burn rate while using the Lumbridge Castle range with Cook's Assistant completed, and will burn less than on a fire when using this range. It will stop burning entirely on fires at Cooking level 47 and on ranges at level 50, or 43 when using the Lumbridge range.
3375:
Burnt snail is the result of accidentally burning either a thin snail, lean snail, or fat snail The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels.

Thin and lean snail meat stops being burnt at level 47.

Fat snail meat stops being burnt at level 56.

The burnt snail has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.
3377:
A sample bottle can be purchased from Fidelio in the Canifis General Store or from Rasolo the Wandering Merchant. It is used to collect blamish snail slime.

The best way of obtaining a sample bottle is to go to Canifis and buy it for 10 coins from Fidelio. Although it resembles an empty vial, it cannot be used for any of a normal vial's storage functions.

A sample bottle is also obtained when using the strange potion on Sithik Ints' tea during the Zogre Flesh Eaters quest. Another sample bottle is obtained during Heroes' Quest in the process of creating Blamish oil.
3383: Burnt eel is the result of accidentally burning a slimy eel while attempting to make a cooked slimy eel. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 61.
3389:
Splitbark legs are a piece of splitbark armour worn in the legs slot. 40 Magic and 40 Defence are required to wear them. Splitbark legs can be created by using a needle and thread on three pieces of fine cloth and three bark, requiring 62 Crafting. Alternatively, they can be made without the Crafting requirement by giving three bark, three fine cloth, and 32,000 coins to Wizard Jalarast at the Wizards' Tower.

It can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player-owned house.
3395:
The Diary of Herbi Flax, titled Diary in-game, is found on the shelves in a ruined house towards the south-west side of Mort'ton during the Shades of Mort'ton quest. It describes some experiments run by Herbi Flax as he was trying to find a cure for the strange malady affecting the people of Mort'ton and describes how to make Serum 207 and Serum 208.

It can also be found in the bookcase in your house or on the same shelf of the same Mort'ton house during the Temple Trekking shades event.

If players take the Diary of Herbi Flax to the Apothecary in Varrock during or after the quest, they will get an extra 335 Herblore experience. This can only be done once.
3396:
Loar remains are an item found and used in the Shades of Mort'ton minigame. To obtain these remains, the player must kill loar shades, located around Mort'ton. To burn the loar remains, the player needs some pyre logs (see table for more info) and a tinderbox. First place the pyre logs on a funeral pyre, followed by the loar remains, then light the pyre. This will grant the player Firemaking and Prayer experience (see table).

Once burned, a bronze shade key or some coins will appear next to the pyre. The keys can be used either to enter the catacombs or to open the corresponding coloured doors to chests containing valuable items.

Coins and keys dropped by cremating these remains will not despawn for five minutes, and cannot be taken by other players during this time. When dropped by the player, they will despawn and become visible to others at the normal rate.

Olive oil is an item used in the Shades of Mort'ton minigame. It may be purchased from Razmire's general store in Mort'ton for 28 coins or from Rasolo the wandering merchant for 40 coins. It is also sometimes received from giving Serum 207 or Serum 208 to the Afflicted found wandering in the town.

To create sacred oil, an item used in the preparation of pyre logs, players must first help to restore the Temple of Mort'ton that lies to the north-east of the town. Restoration also earns points. Once the temple is rebuilt, players may light the altar in the centre of the temple and use their olive oil on the fire. This converts the ordinary olive oil into sacred oil, consuming sanctity. Each 4 dose item, when sanctified, consumes 3.6% sanctity, but requires at least 10% to sanctify.

Sacred oil is a vial of blessed olive oil that is used to make pyre logs. It is obtained from the Shades of Mort'ton minigame, by using vials of olive oil on the fire altar, once the temple has been fully repaired and the altar lit. Converting olive oil to sacred oil costs sanctity points, which are gained by repairing the temple's walls or by killing the loar shades that attack the temple. Each dose of olive oil costs about 0.9% sanctity to convert; a 4-dose vial of olive oil will cost about 3.6% sanctity to convert into sacred oil. Additionally, players must have at least 10% sanctity in order to convert olive oil into sacred oil.

Sacred oil's sole use is to create pyre logs, which may be used to cremate the remains of various shades. Pyre logs are made by adding sacred oil to logs, which grants 5 Firemaking experience per dose of oil used on the log. Different logs require different amounts of sacred oil, with low-end logs requiring 2 doses, mid-tier logs requiring 3 doses, and high-end logs requiring 4 doses.

Note: Players who haven't completed the Shades of Mort'ton quest will not be able to use sacred oil to create pyre logs. Attempting to do so gives the message This sacred oil doesn't seem fresh. You should make your own.

Cremating shade remains in Mort'ton is necessary to obtain various keys that allow access to the Shade Catacombs and the reward chests within. In both cases, Firemaking and Prayer experience are gained in the process.

3606:
A key is an item needed to unlock a chest or drawer during a Treasure Trail.

There will be a clue telling you where to get it. The key is a drop only when carrying the clue scroll. It disappears when used to open the chest or drawer. Keys are non-tradeable objects, specific to the player who finds them. They are used on all levels of treasure trails.

It is possible to obtain more than one key using the drop trick. However, after taking a clue from the chest/drawer, the key won't open it again, and the player gets a message: "The chest (or drawer) is locked." Keys obtained this way from the same clue will still remain in the bank; however, keys obtained from different clues will not stack.
