Stools are unobtainable items used while playing games in the Burthorpe Games Room, the Games Zone, or in pubs. The stools are technically wieldable items, used to display the sitting animation.

It has the appearance of a steel axe in the player's inventory, as only the equipped model is ever supposed to be seen ingame.
3894:
The awful anthem is a quest item used in the Throne of Miscellania quest. Players require a new anthem for Etceteria to replace the old one, which is the condition for the peace between Etceteria and Miscellania.

Players can obtain one from the want-to-be bard Prince Brand, the son of King Vargas. It is used to settle the war between Etceteria and Miscellania. The player must take the awful anthem to Advisor Ghrim who will then make a number of improvements to the song, turning it into a good anthem, which must be taken to Queen Sigrid. The revised version of the anthem has a lighter colouring.

Attempting to bank the awful anthem prints the message You have more urgent things to do with this anthem!. After the quest, players can no longer get the Awful anthem.
3897:
The giant nib is a quest item used in the Throne of Miscellania quest. Players must obtain it in order to construct a pen large enough for King Vargas to sign a peace treaty with Etceteria.

Derrik, the Miscellanian blacksmith, will be able to make a giant nib once provided with an iron bar. Players are then able to use the giant nib with any set of logs in order to make a giant pen.
3898: The giant pen is an item used during the Throne of Miscellania. King Vargas needs a pen to sign the peace treaty between his kingdom and Etceteria. To make it, the player must ask Derrik (near the anvil on northern Miscellania) to make them a giant nib for their pen using an iron bar. Then the player can use any type of logs on the nib to finish it off. The pen can then be given to the king, who will sign the treaty.
3899:
Iron sickles can be purchased from Gardener Gunnhild on the island of Miscellania for 15 coins each. Players must have completed the Fremennik Trials quest to get to the island of Miscellania.

The item has no uses; if you ask Gunnhild what the iron sickle is used for, she says, "I can't think of anything just now. But you can buy one if you like, Your Highness!"

The iron sickle, along with the silver sickle, were historically used during the Throne of Miscellania quest to weed the herb garden. These interactions were removed with the release of Royal Trouble.
3901:
Ghrim's book, or Managing Thine Kingdom for Noobes, is a book that details the finer workings of running your own kingdom. It was written by Advisor Ghrim.

The book is given to you after completing the Throne of Miscellania quest, and after completing Royal Trouble, it upgrades to the 2nd Edition and talks about the resources of Etceteria will let you use. After completing the quest, you can also find the book on the shelves in your house, or in the bookcases in Queen Sigrid's throne room.
4001: A Hardy gout tuber is obtained during the My Arm's Big Adventure quest from Murcaily. They can not be dug up or planted in a herb patch. One is given to the player after reaching 60% favour in Tai Bwo Wannai Cleanup, but is immediately replaced by a handful of hardy gout tubers from Murcaily after My Arm goes on a rampage.
4002:
Spare controls is an item obtained during Monkey Madness I by searching the crate near the Reinitialisation Panel in the secret Gnome glider hangar. After the quest, searching the crate results in finding nothing.

They are the spare controls for the hangar reinitialisation during the quest. When viewed, they provide the completed solution of the sliding panel puzzle that needs to be completed during Monkey Madness I.
4004:
The gnome royal seal is a quest item used in the Monkey Madness I quest. The seal is given to the player by King Narnode at the start of the quest in order to prove that the player is acting with the authority of the king. It must be shown to the employee outside the shipyard on Karamja to allow entry into the main shipyard area.

The seal is no longer needed once the quest is finished.
4005: Narnode's orders are a quest item used during the Monkey Madness I quest. They are given to the player by King Narnode near the start of the quest and the player is charged with delivering them to the Gnome Royal Guard who were last seen being blown off course on their gliders during a mission to Karamja.
4007:
The enchanted bar is a quest item used during the Monkey Madness I quest. It is obtained by taking some monkey dentures, a gold bar and the m'amulet mould to Zooknock, the Royal Guard mage, at the end of the Ape Atoll Dungeon. After Monkey Madness II, it is impossible to reobtain this item, as Zooknock will just provide players with a completed m'speak amulet.

Zooknock will then infuse the magical powers of the dentures into the gold bar and return an enchanted bar. The player should then use this bar with the m'amulet mould on the magical flame in the dungeon below the temple to create an m'speak amulet.

If you right click "Listen" on the enchanted bar without wearing the monkeyspeak amulet, the enchanted gold bar will say:

"Ah Uh Ah! Ook Ah Uh! Ook Ook!"

"Ook Ook! Ook Ah Uh! Ook Ook! Ook Ah Uh!"

If you right click "Listen" on the enchanted bar when wearing the monkeyspeak amulet, the enchanted gold bar will say:

"Argh! Get me out of here!"

"I'm stuck in this horrible gold bar!"
4008: The eye of gnome can be found in crates in the depository on Ape Atoll or purchased from Tutab's Magical Market. It is slightly larger than an eye of newt. It has no use.
4009: The eye of gnome can be found in crates in the depository on Ape Atoll or purchased from Tutab's Magical Market. It is slightly larger than an eye of newt. It has no use.
4010:
Monkey magic is an unobtainable item that presumably would have been used during Monkey Madness I. Most likely, it was intended to be another Monkey themed item, similar to monkey bar and monkey nuts. For unknown reasons, it was scrapped early in development, and therefore reuses the inventory sprite for the eye of gnome.

The item has never been obtainable in Old School RuneScape, but remains in the game files.
4012:
Monkey nuts are a food item, healing 4 hitpoints when eaten. They can be purchased at Solihib's Food Stall on Ape Atoll after starting the Monkey Madness I quest. Players who have not completed Monkey Madness II must be in the form of a monkey (by holding any monkey greegree) before talking to the stall owner or they will be thrown in jail just like in the quest. A M'speak amulet is not required in order to buy from Solihib's shop.

5 Monkey nuts are also used in farming, together with a monkey bar and a ground Suqah tooth, as the payment for protecting a spirit tree.

There is also a Monkey nut bush under the Ape Atoll agility course, however this bush only grows Tchiki monkey nuts during Recipe for Disaster.
4014:
Monkey bar is a food item that heals 5 Hitpoints when eaten. They can be purchased at Solihib's Food Stall on Ape Atoll for 50 after starting the Monkey Madness I quest. Players who have not completed Monkey Madness II must be in the form of a monkey (by holding any monkey greegree) before talking to the stall owner or they will be thrown in jail just like in the quest. A M'speak amulet is not required in order to buy from Solihib's shop.

It is used as payment along with five monkey nuts and a ground suqah tooth to protect a growing spirit tree.

Unlike chocolate bars, monkey bars cannot be used in creating chocolate dust or chocolate cake.
4016:
Banana stews can be purchased at Solihib's Food Stall on Ape Atoll for 300 coins. Banana stews cannot be made through the Cooking skill.

A banana stew heals 11 hitpoints when consumed. This can be a useful food source when training Agility at the Ape Atoll Agility Course if you are near death, since the stall is near the course.

Banana stews weigh less than bowls (0.25 kg vs 0.453 kg), meaning that upon eating one, the player's weight effectively increases.
4018:
The Monkey wrench is an unobtainable item that presumably would have been used during Monkey Madness I. Most likely, it was intended to be another Monkey themed item, similar to Monkey bar and Monkey nuts. For unknown reasons, it was scrapped early in development, and therefore reuses the inventory sprite for the Eye of gnome. It likely would have been obtained from the crate (monkey wrench), which would've been found somewhere in the warehouse with the other crates.

The item has never been obtainable in Old School RuneScape, but remains in the game files.
4020:
The m'amulet mould is used in the Monkey Madness I quest to make a m'speak amulet.

The m'amulet mould is found in the north-western corner of the dungeon underneath the house in Ape Atoll where the player gets the monkey dentures. To get into the dungeon, search the south-eastern crate in the house south of the marketplace in Marim, the village of Ape Atoll, to fall down into the dungeon and take 33% of your current hitpoints as fall damage.

Monkey dentures, a m'amulet mould and a gold bar need to be given to Zooknock, who will create an enchanted bar. The enchanted bar is then brought to the dungeon below the temple in east Ape Atoll and is used on a wall of flame, with the m'amulet mould in the inventory, to create an m'speak amulet which you then string with a ball of wool.
4021:
A m'speak amulet is an item crafted during Monkey Madness I that allows the player to communicate with monkeys. It is later used in the Recipe for Disaster Awowogei subquest as well as Monkey Madness II. After completion of Monkey Madness II, the amulet is no longer needed to speak with monkeys (however, the amulet is no longer used after Chapter III of the quest).

To make one, the player must take monkey dentures, a m'amulet mould, and a gold bar to Zooknock, who will give them an enchanted bar (and the mould back). They must then use the bar on the wall of flame in the Temple of Marimbo Dungeon with the mould in their inventory to create an unstrung m'speak amulet. The amulet can be completed using a ball of wool.

If the m'speak amulet is lost, it can be reobtained by repeating the above steps, or speaking with Zooknock after completing Monkey Madness II.

Since Zooknock returns the m'amulet mould to the player when the bar is created, only one mould is required to create two or more enchanted bars.
4022:
A m'speak amulet (unstrung) is the unfinished version of the m'speak amulet crafted during Monkey Madness I. Once strung, it allows the player to communicate with monkeys.

To make one, the player must take monkey dentures, a m'amulet mould, and a gold bar to Zooknock, who will give them an enchanted bar (and the mould back). They must then use the bar on the wall of flame in the Temple of Marimbo Dungeon with the mould in their inventory, granting them 200 Crafting experience. The amulet can be completed using a ball of wool.

If the m'speak amulet is lost, it cannot be reobtained by any means other than repeating the above steps, or it can be reclaimed from Zooknock after completing Monkey Madness II.

Since Zooknock returns the m'amulet mould to the player when the bar is created, only one mould is required to create two or more enchanted bars.
4023:
A monkey talisman is used for making greegrees until the completion of Monkey Madness II. When taken to Zooknock along with the corresponding materials, he will enchant it into a greegree.

It is first acquired by talking to the Monkey Child on Ape Atoll while wearing a M'speak amulet. The talismans sold at Tutab's Magical Market may only be bought after Zooknock enchants the original, or the player can get another one for free from the monkey child.
4024:
Ninja monkey greegree may refer to:

Ninja monkey greegree (small)

Ninja monkey greegree (medium)
4025:
Ninja monkey greegree may refer to:

Ninja monkey greegree (small)

Ninja monkey greegree (medium)
4026:
The gorilla greegree is used for transforming into a gorilla on Ape Atoll. To make one, a player must take a monkey talisman and gorilla bones to Zooknock, located at the very end of the Ape Atoll Dungeon.

There are two different gorilla greegrees. This type is made using bones from the unbearded monkey guards in the Temple of Marimbo. While transformed, a player can use a rope on a red banana tree to pick the red banana needed in the Recipe for Disaster Awowogei subquest.

A glitch exists where if the player gets caught and they try to transform back, there is a small chance they will lose their greegree; however, this glitch is not common. If the player has a full inventory, and teleports from Ape Atoll without removing their greegree, they will lose it.

After Monkey Madness II, it can be reobtained from Zooknock in the Tree Gnome Stronghold if lost. No materials are required.
4027:
The bearded gorilla greegree is used for transforming into a bearded gorilla on Ape Atoll. To make one, a player must take a monkey talisman and bearded gorilla bones to Zooknock, located at the very end of the Ape Atoll Dungeon.

There are three different gorilla greegrees. This type is made using bones from the bearded monkey guards in the Temple of Marimbo. While transformed, a player can use a rope on a red banana tree to pick the red banana needed in the Recipe for Disaster Awowogei subquest.

A glitch exists where if the player gets caught and they try to transform back, there is a small chance they will lose their greegree; however, this glitch is not common. If the player has a full inventory, and teleports from Ape Atoll without removing their greegree, they will lose it.

After Monkey Madness II, it can be reobtained from Zooknock in the Tree Gnome Stronghold if lost. No materials are required.
4028:
The ancient gorilla greegree is used for transforming into an ancient gorilla on Ape Atoll. To make one, a player must take a monkey talisman and a monkey skull to Zooknock, located at the very end of the Ape Atoll Dungeon.

Unlike the other two gorilla greegrees, this type is made using a skull found in the Temple of Marimbo Dungeon. Completion of the hard Western Provinces Diary is required to open the door to the room in which it spawns. While transformed, a player can use a rope on a red banana tree to pick the red banana needed in the Recipe for Disaster Awowogei subquest.

A glitch exists where if the player gets caught and they try to transform back, there is a small chance they will lose their greegree; however, this glitch is not common. If the player has a full inventory, and teleports from Ape Atoll without removing their greegree, they will lose it.

After Monkey Madness II, it can be reobtained from Zooknock in the Tree Gnome Stronghold, if lost, by bringing him another monkey skull.
4029:
The small zombie monkey greegree is used for transforming into a small zombie monkey on Ape Atoll. To make one, a player must either take a monkey talisman and small zombie monkey bones to Zooknock at the very end of the Ape Atoll Dungeon (pre Monkey Madness II), or get one for free from Zooknock in the Tree Gnome Stronghold (post Monkey Madness II). Materials are not required if Monkey Madness II has been completed.

There are two different zombie greegrees. This type is made using bones from the level 82 monkey zombies in the Temple of Marimbo Dungeon. While transformed, a player can use the wall of flame to create an uncut zenyte and may walk safely across the bed of hot rocks in the dungeon. The player cannot run while transformed into a zombie monkey.

A glitch exists where if the player gets caught and they try to transform back, there is a small chance they will lose their greegree; however, this glitch is not common. If the player has a full inventory, and teleports from Ape Atoll without removing their greegree, they will lose it.

Either size greegree can be used in completing the Recipe for Disaster Awowogei subquest.
4030:
The big zombie monkey greegree is used for transforming into a large zombie monkey on Ape Atoll. To make one, a player must take a monkey talisman and large zombie monkey bones to Zooknock, located at the very end of the Ape Atoll Dungeon. After Monkey Madness II, it can be reobtained from Zooknock in the Tree Gnome Stronghold if lost (listed as big zombie greegree). No materials are required.

There are two different zombie greegrees. This type is made using bones from the level 98 or 129 monkey zombies in the Ape Atoll or Temple of Marimbo dungeon. While transformed, a player can use the wall of flame to create an uncut zenyte and may walk safely across the bed of hot rocks in the temple dungeon. The player cannot run while transformed into a zombie monkey.

A glitch exists where if the player gets caught and they try to transform back, there is a small chance they will lose their greegree; however, this glitch is not common. If the player has a full inventory, and teleports from Ape Atoll without removing their greegree, they will lose it.

Either size greegree can be used in completing the Recipe for Disaster Awowogei subquest.
4031:
The Karamjan monkey greegree is used for transforming into a Karamja type monkey on Ape Atoll and at the Ardougne Zoo. To make one, a player must take a monkey talisman and monkey bones or corpse to Zooknock, located at the very end of the Ape Atoll Dungeon.

While transformed, all monsters on Ape Atoll become non-aggressive. Be aware that a greegree cannot be held while in combat.

A glitch exists where if the player gets caught and they try to transform back, there is a small chance they will lose their greegree; however, this glitch is not common.

If the player has a full inventory and teleports from Ape Atoll without removing their greegree, it will drop to the ground.

After Monkey Madness II, it can be reobtained from Zooknock in the Tree Gnome Stronghold if lost. No materials are required.

The greegree is used in the Monkey Madness I quest and the Recipe for Disaster Awowogei subquest (optional).
4033:
The monkey is a talkative animal obtained during the Monkey Madness I quest. Unlike other animals in-game, it stays in your inventory rather than following you around.

Using any form of teleportation will cause the monkey to vanish. The monkey cannot be banked.

If you drop the monkey, it wanders around for about 30 seconds before disappearing, during which time it can be picked up again by talking to it. However, if the monkey is dropped on Karamja, it becomes a monster like other Karamjan monkeys and exclaims "Yay! I'm free!," granting the player Thieving experience equal to twice their level before disappearing.

While in your inventory, the monkey can be poked, much to its annoyance, and it will often interrupt the player with forced dialogue. It can be fed bananas, monkey nuts, monkey bars, and banana stew, although it will claim to not want the latter items, despite eating them anyway. The monkey will also occasionally eat bananas in your inventory without notice.
4034:
The monkey skull is an item found in the Temple of Marimbo Dungeon beneath Ape Atoll, in the west room packed with monkey zombies. There is a bamboo door separating said room from the rest of the dungeon; the door can be opened upon completion of the hard Western Provinces Diary.

It is used to make an ancient gorilla greegree, which allows the player to transform into an ancient monkey.
4035:
The 10th squad sigil is an item used to teleport to the final boss during the Monkey Madness I quest. It will no longer teleport you to the boss fight arena after you defeat the Jungle Demon. It can be safely thrown away after the quest, however it can be kept as a cosmetic item.

If lost, the sigil may be recovered by speaking to Waymottin, the gnome mage at the end of the Ape Atoll Dungeon. However, if you have completed Monkey Madness II, it can be reclaimed by Zooknock upstairs in the house south-west of Anita's. If lost due to death, you may reclaim it by speaking to Death.

Attempting to equip the sigil in the Wilderness during the quest will result in a message saying You cannot teleport out of the Wilderness using the sigil.
4037:
The Saradomin banner is the standard of Team Saradomin in the Castle Wars minigame, in which players on Team Saradomin must defend the Saradomin flag while players on Team Zamorak attempt to capture it and return it to their base to score points. The flag can be passed to another player if it is dropped. It can be bought from the Castle Wars Ticket Exchange shop, owned by Lanthus for 100 castle wars tickets.

The Saradomin banner is a large blue standard bearing the symbol of Saradomin, attached to a long wooden pole. It plays a key role in Castle Wars. It is kept on the top floor of the Saradomin base. Its counterpart in the opposing team is the Zamorak banner.

If captured, the player doing so will automatically switch their current weapon and shield with the standard, which is held with both hands. Players can attack with the standard, but it is a very weak weapon without any accuracy or strength bonuses. If a player with the standard is killed, the standard will be dropped on the ground, allowing it to be taken by members of either team.
4039:
The Zamorak banner is the standard of Team Zamorak in the Castle Wars minigame, in which players on Team Zamorak must defend the Zamorak banner while players on Team Saradomin attempt to capture it and return it to their base to score points. The flag can be passed to another player if it is dropped. It can be bought from the Castle Wars Ticket Exchange shop, owned by Lanthus for 100 castle wars tickets.

The Zamorak banner is a large red standard bearing the symbol of Zamorak, a black W-shaped fork, attached to a long wooden pole.

If captured, the player doing so will automatically switch their current weapon and shield with the standard, which is held with both hands. Players can attack with the standard, but it is very weak weapon without any accuracy or strength bonuses. If a player with the standard is killed, the standard will be dropped on the ground, allowing it to be taken by members of either team.
4041:
The Saradomin cloak is an item used in the Castle Wars minigame to indicate a player's team. Players are given their team's cloak when they enter any of the three God portals: Zamorak, Saradomin or Guthix. Because of this cloak players are not allowed to wear anything in the cape slot.

The cloak allows the player to teleport back to their team's starting room by using the 'Surrender' option, providing their current hitpoints are below 15%. Similarly to dying, this fully replenishes the player's stats and run energy.
4043: Rock or rocks may refer to any of the following:
4047: Climbing ropes are items used in the Castle Wars minigame. They can be picked up from the tables on the ground floor of the team's castle, and can be used on the enemy castle battlements, allowing players to climb onto the castle's outer walls. Climbing ropes will disappear from the walls after a short time, and are not used often by players.
4049:
Bandages are a healing item that can only be obtained in Castle Wars. After the game has ended, or if the player left the game early, all bandages in a player's inventory will disappear.

Bandages are found on the table in the start room. They restore 10% of a player's hitpoints (rounded down) and 30% of a player's run energy. By wearing a Castle wars bracelet, the amount healed will be increased by 50%. It is possible to use bandages on other players to heal them.

On non-designed Castle Wars worlds, bandages can only heal up 18 hitpoints at a time.
4051:
The toolkit is a quest item used only in Dwarf Cannon. It is obtained from Captain Lawgof after rescuing Lollk in the Goblin Cave.

It is used to fix the broken multicannon he has set up nearby in the dwarven outpost, south of the Coal Trucks near Baxtorian Falls.

Duplicates can be banked by talking to Captain Lawgof to obtain another. After speaking to Captain Lawgof after fixing the multicannon, all copies of the toolkit in the inventory are deleted.
4053:
A barricade is an item used in the Castle Wars minigame as portable obstacles to restrict enemy movement. On the recommended Castle Wars Worlds, players need at least 500 skill total to set up barricades. Players without that requirement can use the barricades on other worlds.

The barricades have a set-up option that places the item on the ground below you, as an attackable object with 50 Hitpoints. On dedicated Castle Wars worlds, each team can have a maximum of 10 barricades set up inside their base and 7 barricades set up outside their base. If the limit is reached, players on that team cannot set up more barricades unless some of the previously set up barricades are destroyed.

Players cannot walk through barricades placed in that manner, and must destroy it by attacking, lighting it with a tinderbox, or using an explosive potion with it.

Players gain no experience from attacking barricades. Players sometimes light the barricades when an enemy player is coming, as burning barricades take some time to collapse and while burning they cannot be destroyed with an explosive potion.

If you have reached your barricade limit, a message in your chat box will inform you so. Barricades are immune to poison.

On non-designated Castle Wars worlds, barricades will always appear under players. On designated Castle Wars worlds, barricades will appear on top of players.
4055:
The Castle Wars manual details all of the special actions that a player can only perform while playing Castle Wars; it can be obtained by speaking with Lanthus. The book has details on various activities that can be done to win the game.

It cannot be stored in a bookcase of a player-owned house.
4067:
Castle Wars tickets are tickets that are awarded in the Castle Wars minigame to players who spend at least 15 minutes in the game. The amount of tickets earned are dependent on whether the player's team wins, loses or ties, as well as whether the opposing team has scored, and also on whether the player is in a dedicated Castle Wars world.

Dedicated Castle Wars worlds:

2 tickets are earned if the player's team loses.

2 tickets are earned if scores are tied at 0-0.

3 tickets are earned if scores are tied at any number other than 0.

3 tickets are earned for winning if the opposing team has scored.

4 tickets are earned for winning if the opposing team had 0 points.

Non-Castle Wars worlds:

1 ticket is earned if the player's team loses.

1 ticket is earned if scores are tied at 0-0.

2 tickets are earned if scores are tied at any number other than 0.

2 tickets are earned for winning if the opposing team has scored.

3 tickets are earned for winning if the opposing team had 0 points.

Tickets can be spent on items in the Castle Wars Ticket Exchange shop.

Items can be sold back for a full ticket refund.
4068:
Decorative swords can be purchased at the Castle Wars arena through the exchange of Castle wars tickets. They may refer to:

Decorative sword (red)

Decorative sword (white)

Decorative sword (gold)
4069:
The red decorative body can be bought in the Castle Wars area south of the observatory for 8 Castle wars tickets. They can only be bought from Lanthus. The red decorative body offers similar stats to a steel platebody but weighs less. It requires level 5 Defence to wear.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Castle Wars armour (1) set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
4075:
Glowing fungus is a quest item used in the Haunted Mine quest. It is obtained by picking the glowing fungus growing on the 4th level of the Abandoned Mine.

The fungus is used to light the way in the lower parts of the mine where fire-based light sources are extinguished and tinderboxes become damp tinderboxes when the player is dropped into a large pool, hence why a glowing fungus is needed.

Being used to growing in a very dark cave, the fungus is very susceptible to sunlight and will crumble to ashes if taken out of the confines of the mine or dropped. Additionally, random events like the Maze Random Event will also cause the mushroom to disintegrate.

If bringing a non-mushroom light source to the bottom floor, even inextinguishable light sources such as Kandarin headgear 1 or a Firemaking cape, it will not work. This is because when dropping into the pool, It's unlikely any of your light sources will dry off until you leave this dank cave., which renders everything but the fungus useless.

When trying to progress further into the cave down the stairs without the fungus the player will state: "It's kind of dark down here. I should probably find some form of light before going further." The player is taken to a separate "dark" map rather than the normal destination with the darkness mechanic, similar to the Temple of Ikov dungeon where the Boots of lightness are obtained.
4077:
The crystal-mine key is found during the Haunted Mine quest. Towards the end of the quest, an evil ghost named Treus Dayth is fought when trying to pick up the "Innocent-looking Key".

After defeating the ghost, the key can be picked up. It allows passage deeper into the mine where Salve crystal can be mined and made into Salve amulets; it also allows full access to other doors in the mine and gives access to shortcuts inside the mine. In addition, it allows access to the rich ore veins in the north-west of Mort Ridge Mine level 2.

This key can be placed on the steel key ring.

To re-obtain the key, one must first acquire a glowing fungus via the carts used in the quest, to access the lowest level of the Haunted Mine where the key can be picked up again. This can be skipped if players have unlocked the shortcut near the outcrops (immediately to the south after entering the mine from the east, "Crawl-down Cart tunnel"), which directly leads to the mine entrance.
4078:
The zealot's key is a quest item used in the Haunted Mine quest. It is obtained by pickpocketing the Saradominist Zealot guarding the entrance to the mine south of Mort'ton. The key is used to activate a water pump deep inside the mine.

This key cannot be put on a steel key ring and once the Haunted Mine quest has been completed it can be returned to Zealot by talking with him. Once the key has been returned you cannot pickpocket another.
4079:
The yo-yo can be obtained by completing one of the Christmas holiday events that occur once per year. This also rewards the player with all other holiday items associated with Christmas.

Previously, they were obtainable during the 2013 Rare Drops event (from 1 July to 8 July) as part of a rare item drop.

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room.
4081:
The salve amulet is an offensive amulet that is made upon completion of the Haunted Mine quest, granting a 16.67% increase in the wearer's Attack and Strength when fighting undead monsters.

The amulet is made by using a chisel on the crystal outcrop at the bottom level of the Abandoned Mine, then using the acquired salve shard on a ball of wool; the String Jewellery spell will also work.
4082:
A salve shard is a piece of a crystal outcrop that is obtained during the Haunted Mine quest. To extract them, a chisel must be used on one of the outcrops at the bottom level of the mine. It is used to craft a salve amulet.

If returning to mine more shards after the quest is completed, climb over the first cart, crawl down the cart tunnel leading into the Haunted Mine. Once inside, crawl through the cart tunnel immediately south in that first room. You'll arrive right next to all of the crystal outcrops.
4085:
Wax is an item that players need when completing Troll Romance. Dunstan teaches the player to make it by using swamp tar on a bucket of wax with a cake tin in their inventory.

They use it on a sled to protect the wood and to make the sled more slippery. This returns the message: "You wax the sled. You're now ready to go."
4086:
A trollweiss is a rare flower obtained and used during the Troll Romance quest. They are light blue and white in colour, and are endangered (as revealed during the quest).

Players can obtain more than one, and only use one as part of the quest. They can also be equipped, and have the same stats as regular flowers.
4087:
Dragon platelegs are a rare piece of armour that require a Defence level of 60 to be worn. They are dropped by most metal dragons, brutal black dragons, skeletal wyverns and revenants. They have the same stats as the dragon plateskirt, including weight.

Dragon platelegs can be combined with a dragon legs/skirt ornament kit to make gold-trimmed dragon platelegs (g). This cosmetic enhancement won't change the stats in any way.

As with most dragon armour, players cannot make this item using the Smithing skill.
4091: A mystic robe top is magic armour that is part of the Mystic robe set worn in the body slot. It comes in blue, light, dark, and dusk, but all offer the same bonuses. All mystic robe tops require 40 Magic and 20 Defence to wear. It can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player-owned house.
4093: A mystic robe bottom is magic armour that is part of the mystic robe set worn in the leg wear slot. All mystic robe bottoms require 40 Magic and 20 Defence to wear. It can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player-owned house.
4097:
Mystic boots are an item part of the Mystic robes set worn in the feet slot. They are a type of foot armour for mages. All mystic items require 40 Magic and 20 Defence to wear. The blue mystic boots can be bought from the Wizards' Guild in Yanille. It can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player-owned house.

Despite not being a typical magical item, silly jester boots gives a greater magic defence bonus but don't have a magic attack bonus, so mystic boots are still usually a good choice overall.
4101: A mystic robe top (dark) is magic armour that is part of the Mystic robe set worn in the body slot. It comes in blue, light, and dark, but all offer the same bonuses. All mystic robe tops require 40 Magic and 20 Defence to wear. It can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player-owned house.
4103:
A Mystic robe bottom is magic armour that is part of the mystic robe set worn in the legwear slot. All mystic robe bottoms require 40 Magic and 20 Defence to wear.

It can be stored in the magic wardrobe space in a player-owned house.
4107: Mystic boots (dark) are an item part of the Mystic robes set worn in the feet slot. They are a type of foot armour for mages. It comes in blue, white and black, but all offer the same bonuses. All mystic items require 40 Magic and 20 Defence to wear. The dark mystic boots can be bought from other players or rarely dropped by Infernal Mages, which require 45 Slayer to kill. It can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player-owned house.
4111: A mystic robe top (light) is magic armour that is part of the Mystic robe set worn in the body slot. It comes in blue, light, dark, and dusk, but all offer the same bonuses. All mystic robe tops require 40 Magic and 20 Defence to wear. It can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player-owned house.
4113: A mystic robe bottom (light) is magic armour that is part of the mystic robe set worn in the legwear slot. It comes in blue, white, black, and the special enchanted version, but all offer the same bonuses. All mystic robe bottoms require 40 Magic and 20 Defence to wear. It can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player-owned house.
4117:
Mystic boots (light) are a piece of magic armour worn in the feet slot. Like all parts of the mystic robes set, they require 40 Magic and 20 Defence to wear, and can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player-owned house.

Mystic boots are primarily used in offensive setups due to their magic attack bonus. Despite not being a magic item, silly jester boots give a greater magic defence bonus.
4121:
Iron boots are member's only armour pieces that are worn in the footwear slot. There are no requirements for wearing these boots. To obtain Iron boots the player can either obtain them as a drop from Cockatrices and Cave slimes, defeated using the Slayer skill, or from trading with another player.

As with all metal boots, this piece of armour cannot be made using the Smithing skill.
4123:
Steel boots are boots made from steel, requiring level 5 Defence to wear. To obtain steel boots, players can either obtain them as a drop from Pyrefiends and Harpie bug swarms, defeated using the Slayer skill, or from trading with another player.

As with all metal boots, this piece of armour cannot be made using the Smithing skill.
4125:
Black boots are armour pieces worn in the footwear slot. They require 10 Defence to wear.

One can obtain them as a drop from Bloodvelds and their mutated counterpart, as well as their superior variants Insatiable Bloodveld and Insatiable mutated Bloodveld, respectively. They may also be acquired via trading with another player.

As with all metal boots and black items, this piece of armour cannot be made using the Smithing skill.
4127:
Mithril boots are members only armour pieces that are worn in the footwear slot. Players need at least 20 Defence to wear these armoured boots.

As with all metal boots, this piece of armour cannot be made using the Smithing skill.
4129:
Adamant boots are a pair of boots made of adamantite. The player needs at least 30 Defence to wear these armoured boots. These are the first tier of metal boots to offer a strength bonus. Players without the required Defence level can choose to wear climbing boots instead, which have one more strength bonus, but lower defence bonuses.

As with all metal boots, this piece of armour cannot be made using the Smithing skill.
4131:
Rune boots are a pair of boots made of runite. They require a Defence level of 40 to equip. Players without the required Defence level can choose to wear climbing boots instead, which have the same strength bonus but lower defence bonuses.

As with all metal boots, this piece of armour cannot be made using the Smithing skill.
4151:
The abyssal whip is a one-handed melee weapon which requires an Attack level of 70 to wield. It can be obtained as a drop from abyssal demons or from sacrificing an unsired.

The whip is among the most powerful and popular non-degradable melee weapons and is capable of attacking at the same speed of daggers and scimitars at 2.4 seconds per hit. As it performs great against monsters that are weak to slash attacks and is relatively affordable, it is one of the most widely used melee weapons in the game and is a popular choice used to train the Slayer skill at higher combat levels before more powerful weapons become accessible.

While still less powerful than other weapons such as the Ghrazi rapier and blade of Saeldor, the whip is still very popular among players for its simplicity and cost. It is a good training weapon for those wishing to increase their Attack or Defence, but not Strength, as the "Lash" option only provides shared experience between all three styles. Though it falls off compared to other weapons when they are obtained, holding a whip is recommended for the purpose of Master Treasure Trails, in which two potential steps require a whip.
4153:
The granite maul is a two-handed melee weapon that requires 50 Strength and Attack to wield. They are dropped by gargoyles (75 Slayer required), which are in the Slayer Tower.

Players can use a granite clamp to cosmetically enhance the granite maul. This causes the maul to become untradeable, and the clamp is not returned upon reverting the maul back to its original state.

Players can use an ornate maul handle to enhance the granite maul into a granite maul (ornate handle), which reduces its special attack cost from 60% to 50%.

The granite clamp and ornate handle are obtained from Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing.
4155:
The enchanted gem is an item used in the Slayer skill. They are sold by all Slayer Masters for one coin. These allow a player to contact the Slayer Master that has assigned them their current Slayer task, where they can ask for tips, ask who the master is and where they are located, and check how many monsters they still have left to kill for their task. However, it will not allow players to ask Slayer masters for new Slayer tasks.

Players who have unlocked the "Ring bling" ability for 150 Slayer reward points can craft these gems into slayer rings at 75 Crafting. Players who have unlocked the "Malevolent masquerade" ability for 400 Slayer reward points can craft this gem along with other components into a Slayer helmet at 55 Crafting.

The enchanted gem also has a right-click option within the "Log" menu to bring up a log recording every kill of most Slayer monsters the player has killed. Once a player reaches 65,535 kills for a particular monster, the log will say "Lots!" for that monster's entry.
4156:
A mirror shield is a piece of slayer equipment used for fighting the Cockatrice and Basilisk Slayer monsters, requiring 25 Slayer and 20 Defence to wield. When fighting these monsters, the shield must be equipped, or else the player's stats will be drastically reduced. It can be bought from any Slayer Master, or by trading with another player.

The mirror shield possesses iron-tier stats, but with an emphasis on Slash and Magic defence and no negative bonuses. Its +5 bonus in Magic defence makes the shield useful not only against Cockatrices and Basilisks, but as a magic-defence alternative to elemental shields (except against wyverns) if players haven't finished the quest Elemental Workshop I.

V's shield, which is obtainable after The Fremennik Exiles is completed, is a strict upgrade to the shield, as it retains the same ability and has higher defensive bonuses.
4161:
Bags of salt can be purchased from any Slayer Master, and are used to finish off rockslugs that have less than 5 Hitpoints. When used, the rockslug shrivels up and dies, consuming the bag of salt. Using a bag of salt on a rockslug with 5 or more Hitpoints has no effect but will still consume a bag of salt.

A bag (or pile) of salt is required during Icthlarin's Little Helper.
4162:
A rock hammer is Slayer equipment that is required to kill gargoyles. Players can buy a rock hammer from any Slayer Master for 500 coins.

While damage can be done to them with a regular weapon at 75 Slayer, the hammer must be used on gargoyles to finish them off when they have 10 hitpoints or less left, unless the player has unlocked the Gargoyle Smasher ability via spending 120 Slayer reward points, which allows players to automatically use the hammer to finish off the gargoyle.
4164:
A facemask is a Slayer item worn on the headgear armour slot, requiring level 10 Slayer to wear, which cannot be boosted. The facemask can be bought from any Slayer Master for 200 coins. There is a facemask spawn inside a locked cage on the top floor of Kourend Castle, however the only way to pick it up is with telegrab.

It must be worn when fighting dust devils and smoke devils, otherwise they will dramatically decrease players' stats.

Wearing a facemask will prevent infection from Nex's virus attack.

While mining volcanic sulphur deposits in the Lovakengj sulphur mine, wearing a facemask will significantly reduce the damage poison gas clouds inflict on players.

During Mourning's End Part II, a dwarf named Thorgel will agree to trade the player a death talisman in return for a list of items, which includes a facemask.

This item is required to craft a Slayer helmet.
4166:
Earmuffs are a piece of Slayer equipment that require 15 Slayer to wear. They are used to protect against banshees' screams and to reduce damage from warped terrorbirds and venators. They may be purchased from any Slayer Master for 200 coins.

This item is required to craft a Slayer helmet.

Earmuffs can be used as warm clothing for Wintertodt.
4170:
The Slayer's staff is a staff that requires level 50 Magic and 55 Slayer to wield. Obtained from any Slayer Master for 21,000 coins, it is required in order to cast the Magic Dart spell, which is the only way to harm turoth and kurask via Magic attacks.

The staff can only autocast the Crumble Undead, Magic Dart, wave and surge spells, and Arceuus combat spells. Due to the cheap rune cost of Magic Dart, lower-levelled players may find the spell useful for Barrows or for killing the Dagannoth Kings.

Players can upgrade the staff to a Slayer's staff (e) by using a Slayer's enchantment on it, which increases the requirement of wielding it to 75 Magic. The enchanted staff will increase the power of Magic Dart for 2,500 casts against monsters who are killed as part of the player's Slayer task.
4178: An abyssal whip can be seen during My Arm's Big Adventure, during the cutscene when Burntmeat cooks the adventurer. Like all of the adventurer's possessions, it is actually a fake item that is untradeable and has no value. Therefore, if players were ever able to obtain the item they would be unable to profit.
4179:
Stick is a troll found on Death Plateau. While not as strong as the nearby Rock, he can hit a max of 27, although this can be completely blocked with Protect from Melee. Like the rest of the "big", "bad" trolls in the area, such as Rock, Pee Hat, and Kraka, he can drop a rune warhammer or granite shield, making him a common target for ironman accounts.

Stick can be safespotted with Ranged to the south-west of his spawn location.
4180: Dragon platelegs can be seen during My Arm's Big Adventure, during the cutscene when Burntmeat cooks the Adventurer. Like all of the Adventurer's possessions, they are actually a fake item that is untradeable and has no value. Therefore, if players were ever able to obtain the item they would be unable to profit.
4181: The Mouth grip is an animation item used in the Werewolf Agility Course. It is temporarily wielded by the player during the animation for using the Zip line. Aside from this, the item cannot be obtained.
4182: Goutweed is a fake version of goutweed seen during My Arm's Big Adventure during the cutscene when Burntmeat cooks the Adventurer. Like all of the Adventurer's possessions, it is actually a fake item that is untradeable and has no value. If players were ever able to obtain the item it would not be useable as real goutweed.
4184:
The cavern key is an item obtained during the Creature of Fenkenstrain quest. It is obtained by killing a level 51 wolf-woman Experiment in the Experiment Cave. It is required to unlock the door to the Mausoleum, which is located in the north-west passage of the cave.

If the player is already carrying a key or has completed the quest, they cannot attack another wolf-woman Experiment. Attempting to do so results in the message 'You don't have the heart to kill the poor creature again.'

After the quest, the key can be obtained from the chest in the northern part of the Experiment Cave, near the ladder to the Mausoleum, but it is no longer needed to open the door.

This key cannot be put on the steel key ring.
4185: Tower key is an item used only in the Creature of Fenkenstrain quest. It is obtained from Dr Fenkenstrain after his monster has awakened (cannot be obtained after the quest.) It opens the locked door to the tower where Lord Rologarth is imprisoned. Afterwards, a key is no longer needed to pass through the door.
4187:
A marble amulet is an item used during the Creature of Fenkenstrain quest. It is found upstairs in Fenkenstrain's Castle, within the bookcase in the west room. Players can find it by searching the bookcase and choosing the Joy Of Grave Digging book. The marble amulet forms a star amulet when used with the obsidian amulet.

It can also be obtained after the quest, but if a star amulet is used on the easternmost grave again, as was done in the quest, the marble amulet will no longer be obtainable.
4188:
The obsidian amulet is an item used in the Creature of Fenkenstrain quest. It is found upstairs in Fenkenstrain's Castle, within the bookcase in the east room. Players can find it by searching the bookcase and choosing the Handy Maggot Avoidance Techniques book. The Obsidian amulet forms a star amulet when used with the marble amulet.

It can also be obtained after the quest, but if a star amulet is used on the easternmost grave again, as was done in the quest, the obsidian amulet will no longer be obtainable.
4189:
A garden cane is an item used in the Creature of Fenkenstrain quest. Players must obtain three canes from the pile in the 'garden' of Fenkenstrain's Castle, next to the Gardener Ghost. The garden canes are then used on a garden brush, along with bronze wire, to create an extended brush.

It can also be used to help a young vine grow up a cliff in the Feldip Hills so that you can access the jungle eagles from outside/in the jungle.
4190:
Garden brush is an item used only in Creature of Fenkenstrain quest. It is obtained from a cupboard within the shed near the Gardener Ghost. Initially to enter the shed, the player requires a shed key; subsequent visits do not require the key.

Before it can be used it must be used with 3 garden canes and 3 bronze wires to create the extended brush, which is used to obtain the conductor mould.
4191:
The extended brush is used in Creature of Fenkenstrain. It is created by attaching a garden cane to the garden brush with bronze wire.

Before it can be used it must be extended with two more garden canes, which are obtainable from the nearby pile. By using the longest extended brush with the fireplace located in the upstairs west room in Fenkenstrain's Castle, players can obtain the conductor mould. After the quest, the item can still be created.
4192:
The extended brush is used in Creature of Fenkenstrain. It is created by attaching a garden cane to the garden brush with bronze wire.

Before it can be used it must be extended with two more garden canes, which are obtainable from the nearby pile. By using the longest extended brush with the fireplace located in the upstairs west room in Fenkenstrain's Castle, players can obtain the conductor mould. After the quest, the item can still be created.
4193:
The extended brush is used in Creature of Fenkenstrain. It is created by attaching a garden cane to the garden brush with bronze wire.

Before it can be used it must be extended with two more garden canes, which are obtainable from the nearby pile. By using the longest extended brush with the fireplace located in the upstairs west room in Fenkenstrain's Castle, players can obtain the conductor mould. After the quest, the item can still be created.
4194: The torso is a quest item used only in the Creature of Fenkenstrain quest. It is 1 of the 5 parts of the monster that Dr Fenkenstrain is creating. It is found by digging the westernmost grave at the Mausoleum, accessible by climbing the ladder at the end of the Experiment cave.
4197:
The decapitated head is an item used only in Creature of Fenkenstrain quest. It is one of the five parts of the monster that Dr Fenkenstrain is creating. Players can find it by digging a grave where the Gardener Ghost leads.

The head was actually the Gardener Ghost's head, until Dr Fenkenstrain murdered him via decapitation. Players fill the head with a pickled brain, which originally belonged to Lord Rologarth.
4198:
The decapitated head is an item used only in Creature of Fenkenstrain quest. It is one of the five parts of the monster that Dr Fenkenstrain is creating. Players can find it by digging a grave where the Gardener Ghost leads.

The head was actually the Gardener Ghost's head, until Dr Fenkenstrain murdered him via decapitation. Players fill the head with a pickled brain, which originally belonged to Lord Rologarth.
4199:
Pickled brain is an item used only in Creature of Fenkenstrain quest. It is bought from the Hair of the Dog tavern for 50 coins (or telegrabbed), and then used with the decapitated head.

This happens to be the brain of Lord Rologarth, the ruler of Fenkenstrain's Castle.

When a player tries to pick a pickled brain up off the table the bar man says that they must buy one for 50 coins. This item can still be obtained even if the player has completed the quest, though it has no use.
4200: Conductor mould is an item used only in the Creature of Fenkenstrain quest. It is obtained by cleaning the fireplace that is located in the west room upstairs in Fenkenstrain's Castle with a garden brush. By using a silver bar with a furnace when holding a conductor mould, it is possible to make Conductors (requires level 20 Crafting). After the quest, it is still possible to smelt Lightning rods; however, the mould can no longer be acquired if lost.
4201:
A Conductor is an item that is only used in the Creature of Fenkenstrain quest. It is obtained by melting a silver bar in a furnace with a conductor mould in the player's inventory. This requires level 20 Crafting. It is used to repair the lightning conductor upstairs in Dr Fenkenstrain's castle.

Players can make these after the quest; however, they are useless once the player has completed the quest. Additionally, the mould becomes unobtainable after the quest.
4202:
The ring of Charos is a magical ring that charms certain NPCs when worn, unlocking different dialogue options and benefits. Charos, the creator of the ring, used it to enhance his prowess as a diplomat and convince the weak-minded to do his bidding. The Wise Old Man says that anyone who uses the ring must already possess some kind of diplomatic skill for it to work.

The unactivated form is awarded upon completion of Creature of Fenkenstrain. This version of the ring can only be used to deceive werewolves into believing the wearer is one of them; wearing it is necessary to access the Werewolf Agility Course. Near the beginning of the Garden of Tranquillity quest, the Wise Old Man activates it into the ring of Charos(a), allowing the player to charm and convince other people into helping you. Finishing Garden of Tranquility is NOT required to use the activated form of the ring.

The ring is lost upon death. If lost, it can be recovered by pickpocketing Dr Fenkenstrain. After Creature of Fenkenstrain, he resides on the top floor of Fenkenstrain's Castle; partway through The Great Brain Robbery, he permanently moves to the basement of the Harmony Island windmill. Note that if the player throws the ring into the Edgeville well during Garden of Tranquillity, another one cannot be claimed from Fenkenstrain during the quest, and the only way to get it back is to use a fishing rod on the well. Once the ring is activated for the first time, it will always be activated when recovered, and the original version becomes unobtainable.
4203:
A journal is an unobtainable item released alongside the Creature of Fenkenstrain quest. It can only be seen in game by searching the bookcases upstairs in Fenkenstrain's Castle, and choosing any option other than Joy Of Grave Digging and Handy Maggot Avoidance Techniques.

It is possible that the Journal may have originally intended to be an obtainable item, perhaps belonging to Dr Fenkenstrain, but was repurposed to appear in the book interface instead.
4204:
Letter may refer to one of the following:

Items simply named "Letter":

Letter obtained during Creature of Fenkenstrain

Letter obtained during Forgettable Tale...

Letter obtained during The Golem

Letter obtained during Royal Trouble

Letter obtained during The Queen of Thieves

Letter can be found in the eastern building in Auburnvale that houses the belladonna patch

Letter can be found in the eastern building in Sunset Coast

Old letter can be found upstairs in Sunrise Palace

Ancient letter, obtained during The Forsaken Tower

Hosidius letter, obtained from the Arceuus Library

Important letter, obtained during The Frozen Door miniquest

Letters obtained during Making History:

Letter (King Lathas)

Letter (Jorral)

Letters obtained during The Dig Site quest:

Unstamped letter

Sealed letter

Invitation letter

Letters obtained during What Lies Below:

Letter to Surok

Surok's letter

Mourner letter, obtained during Mourning's End Part I

Unsealed letter, obtained during The Fremennik Exiles
4205: The consecration seed is an item used to perform an elven consecration on the tomb of Glarial in the Roving Elves quest. The item can be obtained by killing one of the Moss Guardians in Glarial's Tomb. Eluned can enchant the seed to prepare it for the consecration. If you lose the seed during the quest, just go back to Eluned and you will get a new consecration seed.
4206: The consecration seed is an item used to perform an elven consecration on the tomb of Glarial in the Roving Elves quest. The item can be obtained by killing one of the Moss Guardians in Glarial's Tomb. Eluned can enchant the seed to prepare it for the consecration. If you lose the seed during the quest, just go back to Eluned and you will get a new consecration seed.
4207:
A crystal weapon seed is an elven crystal that can be turned into crystal weapons. Completing the Gauntlet will yield a chance of gaining these seeds. The crystal weapon seed can be bought from Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing for 12 Last Man Standing points.

This seed can be restored into a crystal bow, a crystal shield, or a crystal halberd, the latter only with completion of the Hard Western Provinces Diary. Before completion of Song of the Elves, Ilfeen is the only one to offer this service to the player. She can be found at either of two clearings in Isafdar, teleporting between them periodically. If the player is mid-quest, and she is occupied with the fight against Lord Iorwerth, an Elven Scout will fulfil her role. After completion of the quest, Ilfeen is found in Prifddinas, slightly south of the house portal.

After completion of Song of the Elves, players may enchant the seeds themselves at a Singing bowl, requiring 78 Crafting and Smithing.

Players can also exchange the weapon seed for 10 crystal shards by speaking to Amrod in Prifddinas' Hefin Inn. The seed can additionally be traded to Pennant in Prifddinas for one crystal acorn, which can be grown into a crystal tree that yields up to 28-32 crystal shards when harvested.

When converting a crystal seed to a crystal bow and crystal shield, they cannot be traded or be used for high alchemy.
4212:
The crystal bow was a degradable bow made from enchanted elven crystal. It required the completion of Roving Elves to wield, as well as 50 Agility and 70 Ranged. Along with the crystal shield, crystal halberd and the crystal saw, it was one of the four pieces of crystal equipment in Old School RuneScape.

These crystal bows functioned differently to the present day Crystal bow. They would degrade over time with use, and their stats would gradually decrease as the bow degraded. Furthermore, the bow could be traded when it was entirely new, and turned into banknotes.

With the release of Song of the Elves, all existing Crystal bows reverted into Crystal weapon seeds. As a result, these items are currently unobtainable; however, they remain in the game files.
4213: The New crystal bow is an unobtainable version of the historical crystal bow. Originally, the new crystal bow was tradeable and could be turned into banknotes. With the release of Song of the Elves, all crystal equipment was made untradeable. Any banknote versions of the New crystal bow would have been turned into this unique discontinued variant. However, all crystal items were reverted back to Crystal weapon seeds in the same update anyway; therefore this item has never been obtainable.

With the release of Song of the Elves, all existing Crystal bows reverted into Crystal weapon seeds. As a result, these items are currently unobtainable; however, they remain in the game files.
4223:
The crystal bow was a degradable bow made from enchanted elven crystal. It required the completion of Roving Elves to wield, as well as 50 Agility and 70 Ranged. 4235: The New crystal shield is an unobtainable version of the historical crystal shield. Originally, the new crystal shield was tradeable and could be turned into banknotes. With the release of Song of the Elves, all crystal equipment was made untradeable. Any banknote versions of the New crystal shield would have been turned into this unique discontinued variant. However, all crystal items were reverted back to Crystal weapon seeds in the same update anyway; therefore this item has never been obtainable.
4236:
The signed oak bow is obtained during the Ghosts Ahoy quest. It is identical to an oak longbow but has been signed by Robin in Port Phasmatys after the player beats him in several games of Rune-Draw. Ak-Haranu has the translation manual which the player requires, and requests the signed oak bow in exchange for it.

It is possible to obtain multiple signed oak bows through use of the drop trick, however, players are no longer able to request a signed oak bow from Robin after returning the bow to Ak-Haranu. Additionally, upon completing the quest, any duplicates will NOT be lost.

Unlike its regular counterpart, this item cannot be used to light a fire as part of the Barbarian firemaking training.
4237: Nettle-water is an item created in the process of making nettle tea. This item is made by adding nettles to a bowl of water. This requires a Cooking level of 20. Historically, this item gave 1 cooking exp per creation, however this is no longer the case. The player is healed 1 Hitpoint when drank. However, it is not advised to consume this item because it has potential to heal more when made into tea. Nettle-water can be cooked on a range or fire to produce nettle tea. This item is usually only used during the Ghosts Ahoy quest and the Skippy and the Mogres miniquest.
4238:
A puddle of slime is an unobtainable item released alongside Ghosts Ahoy and the Ectofuntus.

Presumably, the puddle of slime would have been a fake item that players could not pick up, similar to Flour. Players would have had to use a bucket on it in order to obtain a bucket of slime. Instead, buckets of slime are obtained directly from the pool of slime below the Ectofuntus instead.
4239:
Nettle tea is a hot drink that can be obtained by cooking nettle-water on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 20 Cooking and granting 52 experience when successful. Players may accidentally let the water boil over, returning an empty bowl; the rate of success while making these will increase as players reach higher Cooking levels. It will stop boiling over entirely at Cooking level 54 on both ranges and fires.

Drinking the tea heals 3 hitpoints. If you are not at full health, the tea will also refresh some run energy (5%), but if you are already at full hitpoints, run energy will not be restored. This item is used during the Ghosts Ahoy quest, as well as the miniquest Skippy and the Mogres. This item also can be used to bribe Panning guide to unlock panning instead of Cup of tea.

This particular kind of tea cannot be added to a tea flask.
4240:
Milky nettle tea is made by using a bucket of milk on nettle tea. It can be used on an empty cup to make a cup of milky tea.

Drinking the tea heals 3 hitpoints. If you are not at full health, the tea will also refresh some run energy (5%), but if you are already at full hitpoints, run energy will not be restored.

Milky nettle tea is given to the Old Crone during the Ghosts Ahoy quest to allow her to remember her time as an apprentice of Necrovarus.
4241:
Nettles are the key ingredient in nettle tea. They can be found in various locations throughout Runescape. Players must wear gloves in order to pick nettles (Beekeeper's gloves will not work). If no gloves are worn, no nettles will be obtained and the player will be dealt up to 2 Hitpoints of damage. Although the resulting hitsplat is green, similar to poison, the player will not be poisoned.

Once picked, they may be used on a bowl of water to create nettle-water, which can then be cooked on a range or fire to create nettle tea.
4242:
A Cup of tea (nettle) is a drink that restores 3 Hitpoints and 5% run energy, provided you have missing hitpoints. It can be obtained by using nettle tea on an empty cup.

A bucket of milk may also be added to the tea to create Cup of tea (milky nettle) which has the same effects and is used during the Ghosts Ahoy quest.

This particular kind of tea cannot be added to a tea flask. Nettle tea can be used in place of a regular cup of tea for the Panning guide during The Dig Site quest.
4243:
A cup of milky tea is made by using milky nettle tea on an empty cup. It must be put into a porcelain cup in order to become a cup of tea that the Old Crone will take during the quest Ghosts Ahoy.

Drinking the tea heals 3 hitpoints. If you are not at full health, the tea will also refresh some run energy (5%), but if you are already at full hitpoints, run energy will not be restored.

This particular kind of tea cannot be added to a tea flask. Nettle tea can be used in place of a regular cup of tea for the Panning guide during The Dig Site quest.
4245: A cup of tea is an item made during the Ghosts Ahoy quest. Players pour nettle tea into a porcelain cup given to them by the Old Crone. She refuses to drink the tea until the player adds milk. The player uses a bucket of milk on this item which only changes the colour of the liquid and the examine text. Once given to the Old Crone, she is able to recall some aged memories for the player.
4246: A cup of tea is an item made during the Ghosts Ahoy quest. Players pour nettle tea into a porcelain cup given to them by the Old Crone. She refuses to drink the tea until the player adds milk. The player uses a bucket of milk on this item which only changes the colour of the liquid and the examine text. Once given to the Old Crone, she is able to recall some aged memories for the player.
4247: The mystical robes are found during the Ghosts Ahoy quest. After showing Necrovarus the Petition form with 10 signatures, he burns it to ashes and then drops the key, which you use to enter the room upstairs. Once in the room, open and search the coffin to find the robes. Upon giving the Old Crone the robes, any duplicates will be removed from the inventory or bank; however, completing the quest does not eliminate any duplicates.
4249: The translation manual is received from Ak-Haranu during the Ghosts Ahoy quest. He will give it to you in exchange for an oak longbow signed by Robin, who is staying in the nearby The Green Ghost. Once obtained, give it to the Old Crone to continue the quest.
4250:
A ghostspeak amulet is an item worn in the neck slot that enables the wearer to talk to ghosts. Partial completion of The Restless Ghost is required to obtain the item, as it is given to players by Father Urhney in order to speak to the ghost haunting the Lumbridge graveyard during the quest. Normally players can only get one ghostspeak amulet as Father Urhney will not give an amulet to players who have one in their possession, although the drop trick can be used to obtain more.

An enchanted ghostspeak amulet is given to players by the old crone in order to control Necrovarus during the Ghosts Ahoy quest.

Players who have completed the Morytania Medium Diary may use Morytania legs in place of a ghostspeak amulet anywhere it is required, except during the miniquest The General's Shadow as the ghostly robes must be worn, and the miniquest Curse of the Empty Lord as armour is not allowed on Entrana.

Players who have lost their amulet may obtain another one from Father Urhney.
4251:
The ectophial is a reward for completing the Ghosts Ahoy quest. Players can empty it, causing them to be teleported to the Ectofuntus outside Port Phasmatys. Once the player teleports, they will automatically refill it. The player cannot interrupt the refilling animation themselves, and is immune to damage for the duration; on PvP worlds, an attacker will still gain experience on a successful hit, but no damage will be dealt.

When used to teleport to the Ectofuntus, the messages You empty the ectoplasm onto the ground around your feet... and ...and the world changes around you. will be displayed. When refilling the ectophial, the message You refill the ectophial from the Ectofuntus. will be shown.

If the player loses the ectophial, they can get a replacement from Velorina in Port Phasmatys (must wear a ghostspeak amulet or Morytania legs 2 or better) or purchase it from Perdu for 4,600 coins. Claiming a replacement from Velorina will give the player a full ectophial. Claiming an ectophial from Velorina if the player already has one will give an empty one instead, which the player first has to fill at the Ectofuntus before they can use it.

It can be used to quickly escape from fights because it is easy to replace, costs nothing, and is a one click teleport from your inventory.

Like most teleport items, the ectophial does not work past level 20 Wilderness.

4278: Ecto-tokens are a currency used in Port Phasmatys. In addition to being used to enter the town, they have several uses in and around the area, and can also be used to charge a bonecrusher. Players may obtain them by offering bonemeal to the Ectofuntus.
4284:
The bedsheet is obtained from the innkeeper of Port Phasmatys during the Ghosts Ahoy quest to be given to Robin in a nearby room. It is worn in the head slot.

Although it is brown when received, it can be changed to a light green colour by covering it in ectoplasm, making it an ectoplasm-covered bedsheet. To do this, players must dip it into the pool of slime on the bottom floor of the cavern beneath the Ectofuntus or dip it into a bucket of slime collected from the pool. Although this is supposed to make players resemble a ghost, when talking to residents of the port, they will merely joke at them.

When worn, the bedsheet makes the player resemble a classic "bedsheet" ghost. The bedsheet is not wearable in any other place than Port Phasmatys; attempting to do so will result in receiving a message, stating: "I'll only wear the bedsheet inside Port Phasmatys."

It is impossible to charter a ship while players are carrying a bedsheet.

4286:
Buckets of slime are filled with a slimy green glowing liquid, gathered from the basement of the Ectofuntus near Port Phasmatys. Necrovarus uses this liquid to control the ghosts of Port Phasmatys, but he is thwarted by the player during Ghosts Ahoy. It apparently has hidden magical properties regarding ghosts and the undead, which is the reason Necrovarus can control the ghosts of Phasmatys and also why he, along with his disciples, are still able to interact with living beings, even after many years of death.

They are used along with bonemeal to worship the Ectofuntus for training Prayer. If bones are ground and used with ectoplasm to worship the Ectofuntus, four times the normal amount of experience for the bones is given; which makes it a useful item that greatly impacts and cheapens training Prayer. Equipping the full set of Zealot's robes will provide a 5% chance (1.25% per piece) to save both the bonemeal and bucket of slime while worshipping the Ectofuntus.
4289: Raw chicken is an item obtained by killing undead chickens on Alice's farm in Morytania. It can be cooked into a cooked chicken (undead) on any fire or stove just like a normal raw chicken, granting 30 Cooking experience. The cooked version of this item heals 1 hitpoint.
4291:
Cooked chicken is a type of food that restores 3 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking raw chicken on a fire or cooking range, granting 30 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt chicken. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Cooked chicken is one of a number of foods with a reduced burn rate while using the Lumbridge Castle range with Cook's Assistant completed. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 34, or 31 when using the Lumbridge range.

Cooked chicken does not require a cooking level to cook, and can be used as an ingredient to make a stew or curry. It is an easily obtainable early food source, as killing chickens at the Lumbridge East Farm is a common activity for a low level player.
4293:
Cooked meat is a type of food that restores 3 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking various raw meats on a fire or cooking range, granting 30 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt meat. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Cooked meat is one of a number of foods with a reduced burn rate while using the Lumbridge Castle range with Cook's Assistant completed. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 34, or 31 when using the Lumbridge range.

Cooked meat is used in the making of stews, pies, and steak sandwiches, or as a topping on pizzas.

Unlike most food, players can deliberately burn cooked meat by using it on a fire or cooking range. One burnt meat is required for Witch's Potion.
4298:
The ham shirt is part of the H.A.M. robes uniform worn by Humans Against Monsters members. It is obtained from pickpocketing H.A.M. members or dropped by H.A.M. guards. When worn, players are slightly less likely to be kicked out of the H.A.M. Hideout when pickpocketing H.A.M. members, this increases the more pieces the player wears. Wearing this will not increase players chances of successfully pickpocketing.

It is also used in the quest Death to the Dorgeshuun.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the H.A.M. robes. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

Another player with the same team cape equipped will show up on the minimap as a blue dot rather than white, and the left-click "Attack" option will be moved to a right-click, as if the other player is of higher level than the player. If two players are wearing different team capes, then the "Attack" option for each other will both be left-click, regardless if one player has a higher combat level.

One team cape can be stored on a cape rack in a Player-owned house.

4415: The blunt axe is a quest item used in the One Small Favour quest. It is obtained by talking to the Jungle Forester in the Kharazi Jungle, south-east of Shilo Village. The player is asked to take the axe to Captain Shanks to get it sharpened, although Captain Shanks will tell the player to take it to the axe shop in Port Sarim instead.
4429:
Broken weathervane parts are a quest item used in One Small Favour. They are obtained by climbing onto the roof of Phantuwti Fanstuwi Farsight's house in Seers' Village and examining the weather vane there.

Each part must be repaired using a different metal bar - the ornament on top must be repaired with a bronze bar, the weathervane pillar needs an iron bar, and the directionals require a steel bar to repair.

Should the player lose the parts somehow, they must pay Phantuwti 1,000 coins to reclaim them. These replacement parts will not grant Smithing XP when repaired, unlike the initial pieces.

Once repaired, the parts can be returned to their position on top of the house in order to continue with the quest.
4430:
The directionals are a quest item used in the One Small Favour quest. They are obtained by climbing onto the roof of Phantuwti's house in Seers' Village and removing the broken vane parts. The directionals must then be repaired using a steel bar at an anvil and returned to the top of the house along with the repaired weathervane pillar and ornament.

Once the three repaired vane parts have been returned to their position the player can speak to Phantewti in order to complete the next step in the quest.
