4436:
An airtight pot is a quest item used in One Small Favour and Swan Song. It is made by using a pot lid on an empty pot.

An airtight pot must be given to the Apothecary in Varrock during the events of One Small Favour. In Swan Song, an airtight pot is used to hold bone seeds to create an army of skeleton mages.
4438: An unfired pot lid is made by using soft clay on a potter's wheel after partial completion of One Small Favour, requiring level 25 Crafting and granting 20 Crafting experience. Once the unfired pot lid is created, it must be fired in a pottery oven, producing a pot lid and granting 20 Crafting experience upon success. Unlike shaping the clay, firing it has no Crafting level requirement. At lower levels, an unfired pot lid can crack in the oven, destroying the pot lid and granting no experience.
4442:
Breathing salts are a quest item used in the One Small Favour quest. They are obtained by giving an airtight pot to the Apothecary in Varrock. The player must then take them to Horvik in order to complete the next step in the quest.

If players lose the breathing salts they will need to bring 200 coins and another airtight pot to the Apothecary.
4443:
The chicken cage is a quest item used in the One Small Favour quest. Seth Groats requires five chicken cages to hold the chickens in, and asks the player to give Horvik three steel bars that he owes to him. After giving Horvik five pigeon cages and the herbal tincture and breathing salts, he will create the chicken cages. The player must then take the cages to Seth Groats to complete the next step in the quest.

If the player loses a cage, it can be replaced by giving Horvik 100 coins and another pigeon cage.
4445:
Red mahogany logs are used in the One Small Favour quest. They are obtained by giving a sharpened axe to the Jungle Forester near the Kharazi Jungle, south-east of Shilo Village. More logs can be obtained for 200 coins each.

The quest is completed after delivering the log to Yanni Salika in the antiques shop in the village. Warning: Yanni Salika will take all the Red mahogany logs in the player's inventory!
4447:
Antique lamps are rewards from quests, achievement diaries and the Varrock Museum miniquest. Like regular lamps, these lamps grant a player experience in a chosen skill, and the skill chosen must usually be over a certain level which is unboostable.

Lamps that are not included in the three items kept on death will be kept inside your death's coffer, if not deleted.
4456:
A bowl of hot water can be created by using a normal bowl on a water source to turn it into a bowl of water and then heating this on a stove, a range, or a fire. When added to an empty cup, a cup of hot water is made.

A bowl of hot water is used to make Guthix rest and also used in the quest One Small Favour.
4458:
A cup of water is an item made by using an empty cup on a water source. Nettles cannot be added to this item — they must be instead added to a bowl of water, and add Nettle tea to an empty cup.

A cup of water cannot be used to counter the desert heat effect.
4460: A cup of hot water is created by using a bowl of hot water on an empty tea cup or by heating a cup of water on a range or fire. It is solely used to make a Guthix rest potion. It is not drinkable like tea is, and it can do nothing by itself.
4484: The safety guarantee is a quest item used in Mountain Daughter quest. It is given to the player by Brundt the Chieftain to guarantee Svidi safe passage into Rellekka. When you try to get two of these using the drop trick, a message appears, You don't need another one, really. but it can still be collected via Telekinetic grab.
4487:
The half a rock is a quest item used in the Mountain Daughter quest. The teardrop-shaped rock is obtained by using a pickaxe on the Ancient Rock in a tent in the Mountain Camp. The player must give the rock to Brundt the Chieftain in Rellekka to obtain a safety guarantee for Svidi.

Interestingly, when the player tries to obtain two pieces of the rock using the drop trick, they receive a message stating, "While two halves make one whole, it's better to just have half a rock." However, a player may obtain two pieces by using the drop trick and casting telekinetic grab on one of the halves. Using both halves together in the inventory will not create a whole rock.
4488:
Corpse of woman is an item that is briefly used during the quest, Mountain Daughter. It is actually the corpse of Hamal the Chieftain's daughter, Asleif. It is found in the Kendal's lair located near the Mountain Camp. During the quest the player must show the 14-year-old corpse to the Chieftain, to confirm Asleif's death. The player must then bury the skeleton at the small island in the lake.

The item has a bury option, but it may not be used until the player is on the small island. If you try to bury the corpse, a message will read, "You'd better bring this back to the chieftain instead."

If you try to get two of these, a message will yield, "This must be someone else's corpse, you already have Asleif's corpse."

Trying to bury the corpse after the quest is finished will delete the item and give a message, "You suddenly realize you don't even have the corpse."
4489:
Asleif's necklace is a quest item used in Mountain Daughter quest. It is given to the player by Ragnar toward the end of the quest to bury with Corpse of woman, which the player has to retrieve during the course of the quest.

If you try to obtain two necklaces using the drop trick, a message will yield "You only need one piece of jewelry." However, you can drop it and use the Telekinetic Grab spell.
4490:
Mud is a quest item used in the Mountain Daughter quest. It can be found in the south of the Mountain Camp, where the mudpool is. Players must "Dig-up" the mud from the mudpool. This can be done by hand, a spade is not necessary.

During Mountain Daughter, it is used to provide grip on a tree that the player is otherwise unable to climb, to the centre of the lake. This only needs to be done once, so this item becomes useless afterwards.
4492: The muddy rock is an item used in Mountain Daughter quest. It can be picked up off the ground near the mud pit and in the goat pens in the Mountain Camp. Five muddy rocks are used on the burial mound of the body of Asleif to complete the burial and the quest.
4494: A pole is a quest item used in Mountain Daughter. It can be found in the goat's pen in the Mountain Camp, east of Rellekka. It is used to catapult the player across the stones in the middle of the lake near the Mountain Camp; however, any staff will work for this as well. There is also a broken pole found on the south-western side of the lake which cannot be repaired and has no known use.
4495:
A Pole is an unobtainable version of the Pole. Poles were previously tradeable and could be turned into banknotes. However, they were made untradeable in 2007. Any player who had a noted pole was given this now discontinued item. Originally, the item was identical to the real pole, except being stackable.

As this change occurred prior to August 2007, the item has never been obtainable in Old School RuneScape.
4496: The broken pole is an item found near the lake during Mountain Daughter. It is the broken form of the pole used during the quest to jump across the stones in the middle of the lake. The broken pole is useless, only existing to hint that a pole or staff must be used to cross over the rocks to reach the lake's central island.
4498:
The Rope is an unused animation item presumably intended for use during Mountain Daughter, when using a rope to climb down the cliffside into the Mountain Camp. Although it has a model for use when equipped, it is not used in any animations.

Its inventory icon has the appearance of mud, as it was never meant to be seen outside of the animation.
4500:
The pole is an animation item used during Mountain Daughter. It is temporarily wielded by the player when using a pole to pole-vault over the rocks near the lake. Aside from this, it cannot be obtained.

Its inventory icon has the appearance of mud, as it was never meant to be seen outside of the animation.
4501:
The pole is an animation item used during Mountain Daughter. It is temporarily wielded by the player when using a pole to pole-vault over the rocks near the lake. Aside from this, it cannot be obtained.

Its inventory icon has the appearance of mud, as it was never meant to be seen outside of the animation.
4502:
A Bearhead is a piece of low level headgear that is obtained after killing The Kendal during the Mountain Daughter quest.

This piece of headgear has surprisingly high defensive bonuses given that it has no requirements to equip. It is popular amongst one-defence pures due to its defensive bonuses being comparable to a black full helm and among Abyss runecrafters due to its low weight. Its Magic defence is competitive with many other helmets with higher requirements.

If lost before completing Mountain Daughter, another can be obtained in the Kendal's Lair. If the quest is completed, it can also be reclaimed by speaking to Hamal the Chieftain. Players can also reclaim it from Perdu for 10,000 should they lose it.

The gold decorative body can be bought from Lanthus, who is located at Castle Wars. The body's defensive bonuses match those of an adamant platebody, apart from its weight, with the gold decorative body being 2.721kg lighter. It requires level 30 Defence to wear.

When unprotected upon PvP death, this item will stay in the inventory, but will become broken and will require 5,000 coins to repair. 5,000 coins will be dropped upon death for the opponent. After a regular death, the item can be retrieved from the gravestone without a fee.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Castle Wars armour (3) set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

These require level 30 Defence to wear.

4517:
Giant frog legs are dropped by giant frogs in the Lumbridge Swamp Caves, and heals six hitpoints. They can be used with a raw cave eel on the life altar in Creature Creation to make a frogeel. They can also be sold to Hudo in the Tree Gnome Stronghold for 1,000 coins each.

They can be a possible clue of where to find Solus Dellagar in the quest Wanted!.

When eaten, the message You eat the giant frog legs. They're a bit chewy. is displayed.
4522:
Oil lamps are a light source for use in dark places. Like all low-quality light sources, it is recommended that several lamps are used if this is the only option, and a tinderbox is available in case the lamp goes out.

Empty oil lamps can be made using the Crafting skill at level 12 by glassblowing molten glass, or bought from Dorgesh-Kaan or from other players. To light it, players require level 12 in Firemaking. Note that the oil lamp must be filled with lamp oil to be lit.

An oil lamp can be combined with an oil lantern frame (forged from iron) to make an oil lantern for 50 Crafting experience. Combining the lantern frame with the lamp does not require a furnace or anvil, but does require 26 Crafting.

As it is an open light source, it can set off gas explosions in certain parts of the Lumbridge Swamp Caves.

The player places the white candle in the lantern frame and lights it, using a tinderbox. No experience is received when lighting a candle lantern. They cannot be traded whilst lit.

The empty candle lantern can be filled with a black candle to give a black candle lantern.

The candle lantern is a type of members-only light source used in the Firemaking skill. To make a candle lantern, the player must first have an unlit candle, an empty candle lantern, and at least level 4 Firemaking. The player places the white candle in the lantern frame and lights it, using a tinderbox. No experience is received when lighting a candle lantern. They cannot be traded whilst lit.

The empty candle lantern can be filled with a black candle to give a black candle lantern.
4537: The oil lantern is the second best lightable light source in the game (requiring 26 Firemaking to light), only inferior to the Bullseye lantern. Combining the lantern frame with the lamp does not require a furnace or an anvil. The oil lantern must be filled with lamp oil before it can be lit.
4539: The oil lantern is the second best lightable light source in the game (requiring 26 Firemaking to light), only inferior to the Bullseye lantern. Combining the lantern frame with the lamp does not require a furnace or an anvil. The oil lantern must be filled with lamp oil before it can be lit.
4540: An oil lantern frame can be made by members with level 26 Smithing from an iron bar, giving 25 Smithing experience. It is used to make an oil lantern which can be made with level 26 Crafting by using an oil lamp with the frame then filling the resulting empty oil lantern with lamp oil at the chemist's west of Rimmington. Oil lanterns can be lit with a tinderbox at level 26 Firemaking.
4542: Lantern lens are used with a bullseye lantern (unf) to make a bullseye lantern. A cut sapphire can then be used on the lantern to extract the lantern lens and produce a sapphire lantern at the same time.
4544:
Bullseye lantern (unf) are unfinished bullseye lanterns. To make the steel frame, a Smithing level of 49 and a steel bar are required. Glass lenses for the frames can be made with level 49 Crafting by blowing glass; however, a cut sapphire can be used in place of the lens. Lamp oil, obtained by distilling swamp tar at the Chemist's House in Rimmington or at Miltog's Lamps in Dorgesh-Kaan, is used to fuel bullseye lanterns. Bullseye lanterns can be lit using a tinderbox at level 49 Firemaking - doing so at the Chemist's House is a requirement for the Falador Medium Diary.

The frame combined with a sapphire lens makes a sapphire lantern, which is required in the Tears of Guthix and While Guthix Sleeps quests. In Lunar Diplomacy, an emerald lens is used with the frame to make an emerald lantern.
4546:
A bullseye lantern (empty) is a bullseye lantern (unf) which has been fitted with a lantern lens but is empty of fuel.

The lamp oil used for fuel is obtained by distilling swamp tar in the chemist's house in Rimmington or at the Miltog's Lamps in Dorgesh-Kaan.

When filled with fuel it becomes a bullseye lantern. Level 49 Firemaking is required to light it.

Bullseye lanterns can also be stolen from chests in Dorgesh-Kaan, which require either 52 or 78 Thieving (either one yields them very often). They can also be stolen from cave goblins or purchased from Miltog in the Dorgesh-Kaan marketplace. Some of these methods will still require the use of lamp oil to complete them.

Lantern lens, sapphires, and emerald lens can be swapped with each other when the lantern is finished and unlit. Inserting the lantern lens requires 49 Crafting (cannot be boosted), inserting the sapphire lens requires 20 Crafting, and the emerald lens has no requirements.
4548:
A bullseye lantern is a light source used to illuminate dark areas with the highest brightness value of three. Lighting it with a tinderbox requires 49 Firemaking. Creating one from scratch requires 49 Smithing to make the bullseye lantern (unf) and 49 Crafting to make the lantern lens. Adding a lens to the unfinished bullseye lantern makes a bullseye lantern (empty) which must be filled up with lamp oil by distilling swamp tar in a lamp oil still at the Chemist's house in Rimmington or at Miltog's Lamps in Dorgesh-Kaan.

Lantern lens, sapphires, and emerald lens can be swapped with each other when the lantern is finished and unlit. Inserting the lantern lens requires 49 Crafting (cannot be boosted), inserting the sapphire lens requires 20 Crafting, and the emerald lens has no requirements.

Bullseye lanterns do not ignite swamp gas in the Lumbridge Swamp Caves and they will not extinguish when falling into water except in the Abandoned Mine. In the Sophanem Dungeon, the Scarab mage has a rare attack that magically extinguishes light sources including bullseye lanterns. Activating the scarab trap in the Sophanem Dungeon and falling into the trap extinguishes all light sources as well.
4550:
A bullseye lantern is a light source used to illuminate dark areas with the highest brightness value of three. Lighting it with a tinderbox requires 49 Firemaking. Creating one from scratch requires 49 Smithing to make the bullseye lantern (unf) and 49 Crafting to make the lantern lens. Adding a lens to the unfinished bullseye lantern makes a bullseye lantern (empty) which must be filled up with lamp oil by distilling swamp tar in a lamp oil still at the Chemist's house in Rimmington or at Miltog's Lamps in Dorgesh-Kaan.

Lantern lens, sapphires, and emerald lens can be swapped with each other when the lantern is finished and unlit. Inserting the lantern lens requires 49 Crafting (cannot be boosted), inserting the sapphire lens requires 20 Crafting, and the emerald lens has no requirements.

Bullseye lanterns do not ignite swamp gas in the Lumbridge Swamp Caves and they will not extinguish when falling into water except in the Abandoned Mine. In the Sophanem Dungeon, the Scarab mage has a rare attack that magically extinguishes light sources including bullseye lanterns. Activating the scarab trap in the Sophanem Dungeon and falling into the trap extinguishes all light sources as well.
4551:
A spiny helmet is a helmet designed to protect the player from the attacks of wall beasts, located in the Lumbridge Swamp Caves. It requires 5 Defence to equip and has the same stats as a steel full helm.

It can be bought from any Slayer Master for 650 coins. This is one of the six items used to craft a Slayer helmet.
4559: Deep blue sweets are remnants from the 2005 Halloween event that still exist within the game cache, but are unobtainable anywhere in-game.
4560: White sweets are remnants from the 2005 Halloween event that still exist within the game cache, but are unobtainable anywhere in-game.
4561: Purple sweets are remnants from the 2005 Halloween event that still exist within the game cache, but are unobtainable anywhere in-game.
4562: Red sweets are remnants from the 2005 Halloween event that still exist within the game cache, but are unobtainable anywhere in-game.
4565:
The Easter basket was given out as a reward by the Easter Bunny during the 2014 Easter event. It can be operated when worn to perform an emote, flinging two easter eggs randomly in a 5x5 radius.

While worn, the player's walking and running animations will be replaced with a skipping animation.

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room.
4566:
A Rubber chicken is a event reward that can be obtained by completing an Easter holiday event, which occurs once per year.

The Rubber chicken can be equipped and has the same attack styles as a warhammer. It gives very large attack penalties and is nearly useless as an actual weapon. As such it is allowed during fun weapon fights in legacy duels within the Emir's Arena. When wielded, players will see a "Whack" option on all other players. Picking that option will cause the player to hit the other player. The hit is just an animation and no damage is dealt, nor does it count as entering combat. If a player whacks a large number of other players, they may "fumble" the chicken, dropping it to the ground where it must be picked up again and re-equipped.

Players can right click the chicken, either in their Inventory or on the Worn Equipment screen, and select a dance option, making them do the chicken dance emote, which includes a short song which shares the same beat from a portion of Scape Santa. The dance and song could also be accessed by eating one of the event's Easter eggs, however once the event was concluded, this method no longer worked. Players who distract the eyes in the Abyss will sometimes perform the Chicken Dance emote, even if they do not have a Rubber chicken.

Previously, they were obtainable during the 2013 Rare Drops event (from 12 August to 19 August) as part of a rare item drop.

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room.
4567:
The gold helmet is a helmet the player must smith during the Between a Rock... quest using 3 gold bars. It requires level 30 Defence to wear. Smithing the helmet requires 50 Smithing and gives 30 Smithing experience. More than one helmet can be made by using the drop trick and casting Telekinetic Grab on any helmets dropped on the ground. The helmet must be worn to use Dondakan's cannon and to enter the massive Arzinian Mines, found in the mines south of Keldagrim.

During the quest, once in the mines, the helmet will begin to get heavy. Because of this, a player may only stay in the mines for eight minutes before the helmet becomes so heavy that they are magically forced out. After the quest, the helmet will not force players out, although it must still be worn to enter the mines. It is the heaviest piece of equipment in the game. Entering the mine after completing the quest unlocks the In Between song.

To leave the mines, a player must remove the helmet. When this is done, they will automatically be teleported outside. This costs the player one inventory space, so some players log out instead; if a player logs out in the mines, they will automatically be teleported outside while still wearing the helmet.

To make the helmet after the quest, have 3 gold bars and a hammer in your inventory and smith it on any anvil (option won't be available if you have one in your bank already).

Smithing a gold helmet in the Resource Area is a medium task in the Wilderness diary. Note: Pures do not need to complete the quest to complete this wilderness task.

This helmet is particularly useful when slaying gryphons and the shellbane gryphon boss, given that the helmet weighs nearly 32 kg, and those monsters have a special attack that is blocked by the player having high equipped weight.
4569: Book page 1 is used in the Between a Rock... quest. It is found by killing scorpions in the Dwarven Mine. When combined with book page 2 and book page 3, it creates pages, which the player must give to Rolad.
4570: Book page 2 is used in the Between a Rock... quest. It is found by searching mine carts in the Dwarven Mine. When combined with book page 1 and book page 3, it creates pages, which the player must give to Rolad.
4571: Book page 3 is a quest item in the Between a Rock... quest, found by mining rocks in the Dwarven Mine. When combined with book page 1 and book page 2, pages are created which must be given to Rolad.
4574: Base schematics are used in Between a Rock... to line up the other three schematics. They are found when reading the dwarven lore book.
4575: The schematic is used in the Between a Rock... quest along with the other schematics to find out how to modify the cannon. It must be adjusted over the base schematics. It is given to the player by Dondakan the Dwarf.
4578: The schematic is used in Between a Rock... to find out how to modify the cannon. It is made by adjusting the three other schematics over the Base schematics.
4589: The keys open the front door to the home of Ali the Mayor in Pollnivneach. Members acquire them as part of The Feud quest. They enable players to burgle the house of Ali the Mayor, stealing the jewels to impress Ali the Operator. The house of Ali the Mayor can be entered after the quest without the keys.
4590: Jewels are used in The Feud quest in order to gain the trust of the Menaphite gang. Players must steal them from Ali the Mayor's house in Pollnivneach in order to convince Ali the Operator to let the player join the Menaphites gang. The jewels used to belong to the mayor's wife before they were stolen.
4591:
The Kharidian headpiece is used during The Feud quest to form a desert disguise, by combining it with a fake beard. It can be bought from Ali Morrisane in Al Kharid or the Pollnivneach general store.

Despite having no 'Wear' option, the headpiece would delay the onset of desert heat by 12 seconds if it could be equipped.
4593: A fake beard can be bought from Ali Morrisane in Al Kharid or the Pollnivneach general store. It mainly serves as a quest item.
4595: The karidian disguise is an unobtainable item that only appears when searching the Grand Exchange. It is presumably an item intended for use during The Feud quest, but was replaced by the desert disguise during development for unknown reasons.
4598:
The note is an item that players find whilst burgling the home of Ali the Mayor in Pollnivneach during The Feud. It includes the first part of the combination to the safe in the mayor's home.

The combination is the series of Fibonacci numbers starting after zero, though the note only lists the first five, and the player must deduce the last number required. A hint is provided in the other note found during the quest.
4603:
Receipt may refer to:

Receipt (The Feud), an item obtained during The Feud

Receipt (A Kingdom Divided), an item obtained during A Kingdom Divided
4604: Hag's poison is a quest item used in The Feud quest. It is made for the player by Ali the Hag after giving her a full snake basket and a bucket of Ugthanki dung. The poison must then be slipped into a beer on the table of the inn in Pollnivneach in order to kill a traitor.
4606: A snake basket is used to store desert snakes which are lured by use of the snake charm during The Feud. When a snake is successfully charmed, the snake will go into the basket and become a full snake basket. Ali the Hag will then take the full snake basket and use it to make a poison intended for Traitorous Ali. If you have lost your basket, put one gold coin into Ali the snake charmer's money pot and select chat option "wow, a snake charmer! Can I have a go? Can I have a go? Please?". This is the only chat option to retrieve another basket.
4607: A snake basket full is obtained by using a snake charm along with a snake basket on a desert snake during The Feud. The player must take the resulting full snake basket to the hag in Pollnivneach so she can make a poison to kill Traitorous Ali.
4608:
A super kebab is a kebab that has had red hot sauce added to make it spicy. They are sold by Ali the Kebab seller for 5 coins. Much like the normal kebab, the super kebab has a 5/8 chance to restore Hitpoints by 3 + 7% of the player's Hitpoints level. It also has a 1/32 chance of reducing any stats except Hitpoints.

To make a super kebab, the player must use red hot sauce (obtained from Ali the Kebab seller) on either a normal kebab or ugthanki kebab. A strange-smelling ugthanki kebab will also work.
4611:
The desert disguise is used in The Feud quest. It can be made by combining a fake beard and a Kharidian headpiece, both of which can be bought from Ali Morrisane's stall just north of Al Kharid. Upon completing the quest, the disguise can still be created and the materials will still be obtainable.

Wearing the disguise will delay the onset of desert heat by 12 seconds.
4613:
The spinning plate is a toy bought from Diango in Draynor Village. It is a white plate with a red picture of a dragon on it. The player can click on the plate to have their character spin the plate on a stick. This has no in-game effect and is purely cosmetic.

The spinning plate is one of the items the rowdy dwarf can request from the player during Forgettable Tale of a Drunken Dwarf.
4614:
The Broken plate is an unobtainable item that appears in the game cache but cannot be obtained.

Spinning plates used to have a chance of being dropped when the player spun it, turning into a broken plate. The plate would break the majority of the time, and was impossible to repair. This feature was heavily criticised, as players had no option except to discard the now-useless item and buy a new plate. As a result, the plates were hotfixed on the same day to no longer break. Therefore, broken plates have never been obtainable in Old School RuneScape.

Despite not having an option to equip it, the broken plate has a model for use while equipped, which was used in the breaking animation.
4615:
Letter may refer to one of the following:

Items simply named "Letter":

Letter obtained during Creature of Fenkenstrain

Letter obtained during Forgettable Tale...

Letter obtained during The Golem

Letter obtained during Royal Trouble

Letter obtained during The Queen of Thieves

Letter can be found in the eastern building in Auburnvale that houses the belladonna patch

Letter can be found in the eastern building in Sunset Coast

Old letter can be found upstairs in Sunrise Palace

Ancient letter, obtained during The Forsaken Tower

Hosidius letter, obtained from the Arceuus Library

Important letter, obtained during The Frozen Door miniquest

Letters obtained during Making History:

Letter (King Lathas)

Letter (Jorral)

Letters obtained during The Dig Site quest:

Unstamped letter

Sealed letter

Invitation letter

Letters obtained during What Lies Below:

Letter to Surok

Surok's letter

Mourner letter, obtained during Mourning's End Part I

Unsealed letter, obtained during The Fremennik Exiles
4617:
The display cabinet key is used during The Golem to open a cabinet in Varrock Museum where a statuette is kept. The key can be pickpocketed from the curator within the museum. Only one copy of the key can be obtained.

This key cannot be put on the Steel key ring acquired from completion of One Small Favour. Since it opens only the one cabinet, it becomes useless after the quest.
4618:
The statuette is a small stone figure required for The Golem quest. The key for its cabinet (30) is obtained by pickpocketing Curator Haig Halen in the Varrock Museum.

After the statuette is stolen, the display case reads: "Recently this display was stolen and its whereabouts are unknown." However, if the player loses the statuette during the quest, they can get another one by using the display cabinet key with the now empty display case.

Attempting to return this item to the display it came from yields "Nothing interesting happens.".
4620:
The black mushroom is a quest item in The Golem, Shadow of the Storm and Land of the Goblins quests, found beneath the Ruins of Uzer and in the Goblin Cave by the entrance to the Goblin Temple.

When used with a pestle and mortar and a vial in the inventory, black dye is made, which is used to dye several items black.
4621:
Phoenix feathers can be grabbed from the desert phoenix north-east of the River Elid, by the clay mines. One feather at a time can be plucked from the bird's tail, but the player may fail, in which case the phoenix stuns the player and does a small amount of damage. Players do not kill the bird when plucking feathers. When a feather is successfully plucked, the player earns 26 Thieving experience points.

A phoenix feather is used in The Golem quest, where it is used on black dye to turn it into a phoenix quill pen.

Only one phoenix feather or phoenix quill pen can be owned at a time, however if neither are owned, it is possible to reobtain the phoenix feather even after quest completion.
4622:
Black dye is made by using a pestle and mortar on black mushrooms while having an empty vial in the inventory. It is used in The Golem quest to write a program containing new instructions for the Golem to run. It is also used in Land of the Goblins to dye goblin mail black.

Warning: Dyeing Silverlight black will consume all copies of the sword in your inventory, leaving you with only one dyed sword.

It functions as a black dye and can be used on several items:

Desert shirt, to create a black desert shirt.

Desert robe, to create a black desert robe.

Blue wizard hat, to create a black wizard hat.

Blue wizard robe, to create a black robe.

Any basic coloured cape, to create a black cape.

Any coloured goblin mail, to create a black goblin mail.

Orange slices, to create dyed orange, after partial completion of Freeing the Goblin generals.

Origami balloons.

Phoenix feather, to create a phoenix quill pen which does not consume the ink.

Black sails (10 are need per boat).
4623:
The phoenix quill pen is a quest item used in The Golem quest. It is created by using black dye on a phoenix feather. It can then be used to write a program that contains new instructions for the Golem, thus completing the quest.

If lost, even after quest completion, it can be remade by using black dye on a newly plucked phoenix feather.
4627:
Bandit's brew is a type of ale that restores 1 Hitpoint and temporarily boosts Thieving and Attack by 1, while draining Strength and Defence by ⌊Level×6100⌋+3 (see table below).

It can be purchased at The Big Heist Lodge in the Kharidian Desert Bandit Camp for 650 coins only after reaching the appropriate step of the quest Desert Treasure I. Unlike other ales, it cannot be made through brewing.

One bandit's brew is required for the quest Desert Treasure I.
4653: A fire is a pile of burning logs lit on fire using the Firemaking skill. Many foods can be cooked on a fire, given the player has the required Cooking level.
4654: The etchings are an item used in Desert Treasure I. The player receives them from Asgarnia Smith at the Bedabin Camp who wants the player to take them to Terry Balando, the archaeological expert located at the Digsite. After talking to him, he will give the player a translation in exchange for the etchings.
4655:
Translation (also called Four Diamonds translation and Translation Primer) is part of the Desert Treasure I quest, given to you by Terry Balando at the Digsite after you give him etchings given to you by Asgarnia Smith. It gives some information of the diamonds you use to open the pyramid and their origin.

After doing the quest, you can also find the book on the shelves in your house.
4668: Garlic powder is created by using a pestle and mortar on garlic. It is used with a blessed pot to defeat Dessous during the Desert Treasure I quest. The item can be created at anytime, regardless the player having started or completed the quest.
4670:
The blood diamond is one of four Diamonds of Azzanadra obtained during the Desert Treasure I quest. It is obtained by defeating Dessous and then talking to Malak who will give the player the diamond.

It is recommended that players deposit this gem in the bank as soon as they obtain it, along with the other Diamonds of Azzanadra, as a level 95 stranger may appear and attack them if they are holding one of them. The more diamonds you have on you, the more likely the stranger will appear and attack you.

Should the player lose the diamond or want to collect another via drop trick, speaking to Malak will allow another one to be obtained. However, all variants of the silver or blessed pot will be taken from the player and the only way to avoid this is dropping them. To keep a copy of the diamond after the quest, drop a duplicate before putting the last Diamond of Azzanadra into the pyramid's final unpowered obelisk and it will be safely kept afterwards, even upon quest completion.
4671:
The ice diamond is one of the four Diamonds of Azzanadra which must be obtained during the Desert Treasure I quest. It is obtained from the troll child by defeating Kamil and then freeing his parents from ice.

It is recommended that players deposit this gem on the bank as soon as they obtain it, along with the other Diamonds of Azzanadra, as a level 95 stranger may appear and attack them if they are holding one of them. The more diamonds you have on you, the more likely the stranger will appear and attack you.

Should the player lose the diamond or want to collect another via the drop trick, speak to the troll child to obtain another. To keep a copy of the diamond after the quest, drop a duplicate before putting the last Diamond of Azzanadra into the pyramid's final unpowered obelisk and it will be safely kept afterwards, even upon quest completion.
4672:
The smoke diamond is one of the four Diamonds of Azzanadra which must be obtained during the Desert Treasure I quest. It is obtained by defeating Fareed in the smoke dungeon.

It is recommended that players deposit this gem in the bank as soon as they obtain it, along with the other Diamonds of Azzanadra, as a level 95 stranger may appear and attack them if they are holding one of them. The more diamonds you have on you, the more likely the stranger will appear and attack you.

Should the player lose the diamond or want to collect another via the drop trick, entering the gated area, where Fareed was fought, will spawn another. To keep a copy of the diamond after the quest, drop a duplicate before putting the last Diamond of Azzanadra into the pyramid's final unpowered obelisk and it will be safely kept afterwards, even upon quest completion.
4673:
The shadow diamond is one of the four Diamonds of Azzanadra which must be obtained during the Desert Treasure I quest. It is located in the Shadow Dungeon and is obtained by killing both of Damis' forms.

It is recommended that players deposit this gem on the bank as soon as they obtain it, along with the other Diamonds of Azzanadra, as a level 95 stranger may appear and attack them if they are holding one of them. The more diamonds you have on you, the more likely the stranger will appear and attack you.

Should the player lose the diamond or want to collect another via the drop trick, crossing into the dungeon's multi-combat zone at the end of the corridor connecting to the open area where Damis was fought, will spawn another. To keep a copy of the diamond after the quest, drop a duplicate before putting the last Diamond of Azzanadra into the pyramid's final unpowered obelisk and it will be safely kept afterwards, even upon quest completion.
4675:
The ancient staff is a one-handed magical weapon that can be used to autocast spells from the Ancient spellbook and standard spellbook. It requires 50 Attack and 50 Magic to wield, along with completion of Desert Treasure I. The staff is decorated with the symbol of Zaros.

It is frequently used in high-level player-killing due to its high magical accuracy. It, along with its upgraded versions, are the only items that have negative Prayer bonus.

Similarly to bladed staves, this staff has an attack speed of 4, making it a suitable weapon for melee combat, displaying similar stats as those of the rune scimitar with slightly higher strength bonus and lower attack bonus. It is outclassed in melee combat by the granite hammer, which also requires 50 Attack to wield, with an additional requirement of 50 Strength.

The staff may be bought once from Eblis for 80,000 coins after completing Desert Treasure I. For this reason, Ironmen are not recommended to alch or drop it because it is used in a master clue step, and the only other way the staff can be acquired is either as a rare drop from several boss monsters or as a very rare drop from mummies in the Ancient Pyramid.
4677: The catspeak amulet is a special amulet that allows the wearer to speak with cats. It is received after the completion of Icthlarin's Little Helper, and is used in several subsequent quests. If players lose the amulet, the Sphinx will give them a replacement amulet, but only if they have a cat following them. During Dragon Slayer II, players gain the ability to speak to cats without needing the amulet.
4682:
A holy symbol is an amulet in the shape of a symbol of Saradomin. Holy symbols are made by having an unblessed symbol blessed by Brother Jered in the Edgeville Monastery, or by blessing it via using a holy book or book of Balance on an unblessed symbol at 50 Prayer, requiring a few prayer points. As Brother Jered is located on the upper floor of the monastery, blessing the symbol effectively requires a minimum of level 31 Prayer due to the entry requirement.

It has the third highest prayer bonus for an amulet in game (after god stoles and the dragonbone necklace). It is cheap, easy to obtain, and is commonly used in conjunction with Proselyte armour and other high prayer granting armour when using protect prayers as a form of defence while training.

Wearing a holy symbol while being attacked by a Feral Vampyre occasionally reduces their Attack, Strength, Defence, and Magic by 25%.

Wearing a holy symbol allows players to use a prayer book to cure poison.

A holy symbol will count as a Saradominist item within the God Wars Dungeon.

A holy symbol is required for the quests Animal Magnetism and The Great Brain Robbery.
4686:
The embalming manual, or The Little Book of Embalming, is a book written by Bod E. Wrapper which can be found during the Icthlarin's Little Helper quest. The manual is found in Sophanem on the 1st floor of the embalmer's house. After the quest, the manual can be found in the bookcase of a player-owned house whether or not it was obtained during the quest.

The book details how cadavers are handled in Sophanem, and contains hints as to where the player can find the items requested by the embalmer during the quest.
4687:
A bucket of sap is obtained by using a knife with some types of trees, while having an empty bucket in the player's inventory.

Contrary to popular belief that sap must be obtained from an evergreen tree, there are also many trees that give sap that are not described as 'Evergreen'. These are typically the slightly taller and pointier trees, and can be told apart by their examine text, which is "A commonly found tree.", instead of "One of the most common trees in Gielinor." Sap is used in two quests: Icthlarin's Little Helper and The Eyes of Glouphrie. In Icthlarin's Little Helper, the bucket of sap is given to the embalmer. In Eyes of Glouphrie, the bucket of sap is used with ground mud runes to create magic glue.

A fast way to get the sap is by using the nightmare zone minigame teleport, as there is a tree directly south of the teleport that will give sap. An alternative is by using the fairy ring AKQ to teleport to the Piscatoris hunter area where there are multiple evergreen trees immediately next to the fairy ring. A games necklace can also be used to teleport to the Burthorpe Games Room; from there, the player can run south until they reach the entrance where a few evergreen trees are located on the east. Most of the trees around the Grand Exchange also give sap.
4689:
A pile of salt is an item that can be made by using a bucket of saltwater on the suntrap in Sophanem. It is created during the quest Icthlarin's Little Helper.

This item cannot be used in place of a bag of salt to kill rockslugs.
4691:
The Sphinx's token is a quest item obtained from the Sphinx in Sophanem during the Icthlarin's Little Helper quest.

Upon asking for help from the Sphinx, she will give you the token and direct you to talk to the High Priest. Initially when speaking to the priest, he wishes to not communicate with you. Although when the player presents the token, the priest surprisingly says that he will listen to the player, if they have somehow received the Sphinx's approval. He then takes the token and the player is free to talk to him at any time without approval.

If the player manages to lose the token, they can ask the Sphinx for another one as long as the player hasn't given one to the high priest.
4692:
The Gold leaf is an unobtainable item that appears in the game's code but does not spawn anywhere. Despite not having an option to equip it, the gold leaf has a model for use while equipped.

While the leaf was added alongside Icthlarin's Little Helper, it does not appear to have been intended for use during the quest. It may have been related to Raetul.
4693: A bucket of saltwater is used in Icthlarin's Little Helper. It is a bucket that has been filled with salty water from the lake just north of Sophanem. If used on the suntrap south of the food shop in Sophanem, it can be dried into a pile of salt.
4694:
Steam runes are combination runes. They can be used as one fire rune and one water rune. Thus, any spell requiring one fire rune, one water rune, or both will spend only one steam rune.

They can be created with the Runecraft skill or purchased with Pizazz points from the Mage Training Arena.

When equipped, the twinflame staff, steam battlestaff and mystic steam staff provide an unlimited number of steam runes.
4695:
Mist runes are combination runes. They count as two separate runes: one water rune and one air rune. Thus, any spell requiring one water rune, one air rune, or both will spend only one mist rune.

They can be created with the Runecraft skill or purchased with Pizazz points from the Mage Training Arena.

10 lava runes and 10 mist runes are required for the completion of Swan Song.

When equipped, the mist battlestaff and mystic mist staff provide an unlimited number of mist runes.
4696:
Dust runes are combination runes. They count as two separate runes: one earth rune and one air rune. Thus, any spell requiring one earth rune, one air rune, or both will spend only one dust rune.

They can be created with the Runecraft skill or purchased with Pizazz points from the Mage Training Arena.

When equipped, the dust battlestaff and mystic dust staff provide an unlimited number of dust runes.
4697:
Smoke runes are combination runes. They count as two separate runes: one fire rune and one air rune. Thus, any spell requiring one fire rune, one air rune, or both will cost only one smoke rune.

They can be created with the Runecraft skill or purchased with Pizazz points from the Mage Training Arena.

When equipped, the smoke battlestaff and mystic smoke staff provide an unlimited number of smoke runes.
4698:
Mud runes are combination runes. They count as two separate runes: one water rune and one earth rune. Thus, any spell requiring one water rune, one earth rune, or both will spend only one mud rune.

They can be created with the Runecraft skill, purchased with pizazz points from the Mage Training Arena, or looted from essence implings with 42 Hunter.

Mud runes can be ground with a pestle and mortar to create ground mud runes. One ground mud rune is required to complete The Eyes of Glouphrie.

When equipped, the mud battlestaff and mystic mud staff provide an unlimited number of mud runes.
4699:
Lava runes are combination runes that count as two separate runes: one fire rune and one earth rune. Thus, any spell requiring one fire rune, one earth rune, or both will spend only one lava rune.

They can be created with the Runecraft skill or purchased with Pizazz points from the Mage Training Arena.

10 lava runes and 10 mist runes are required for the completion of Swan Song. In addition, crafting lava runes at the Fire Altar is a medium task in the Lumbridge & Draynor Diary.

When equipped, the lava battlestaff and mystic lava staff provide an unlimited number of lava runes.
4700:
A sapphire lantern is a bullseye lantern that has a sapphire in place of its more usual glass lens. Making the lantern from scratch requires level 49 Smithing (Frame) and 20 Crafting (Cut Sapphire).

Note: Lamp oil needs to be added before the lantern can be lit if crafted with a Bullseye lantern (empty). This can be accomplished by either bringing swamp tar to the chemist in Rimmington, or using swamp tar on the Lamp Still at Miltog's market stall within Dorgesh-Kaan while the lantern is still in your inventory.

To make the Sapphire Lantern, the player must use a cut sapphire on a normal or unlensed bullseye lantern. If the lantern used had a lens, the player will receive a lens in their inventory. After the player is finished using the sapphire lantern, they may use a bullseye lantern lens to convert it back into a normal bullseye lantern and retrieve the sapphire.

The lantern is a light source and is used for attracting light creatures in the Chasm of Tears. Players need to use these creatures to traverse the cavern in the Tears of Guthix and While Guthix Sleeps quests.

When extinguished, the message You extinguish the lantern. is displayed.

The lantern can be made at any time, independent of quests and activities. The lantern is kept in the inventory on death.

4703:
Magic stones are used in the quest Tears of Guthix to make the stone bowl, using a Chisel. It is mined from magical rocks near Juna within the Chasm of Tears.

You must have a sapphire lantern with you to access the stones. Use the sapphire lantern on a light creature and select to go "across the chasm" and you will see the magical rocks. Without starting the Tears of Guthix quest, one can still mine the stone, but upon completing the quest it becomes unobtainable (along with the ability to craft stone bowls). The stone can be kept after the quest by dropping one before completing the quest and picking it back up after completing the quest.
4710:
Ahrim's staff is a one-handed magic weapon that is part of Ahrim the Blighted's set. To wield Ahrim's staff, the player must have 70 Magic and 70 Attack. It increases Magic damage by 5%.

If Ahrim's staff is wielded along with all of the other pieces of equipment in Ahrim's barrows set, the player's successful magic attacks have a chance of temporarily lowering the opponent's Strength level. This is cumulative with other effects that lower strength, namely the spell Enfeeble.

It is able to autocast Standard combat spells as well as being one of the few weapons able to autocast Arceuus combat spells. Additionally, wearing Ahrim's set with an Amulet of the damned will allow players to autocast Ancient Magicks, and also grant players a 25% chance of dealing a hit with 30% increased damage.
4716:
Dharok's helm is melee armour worn in the headwear slot that is part of Dharok the Wretched's set of barrows equipment. To wear Dharok's helm, a player must have 70 Defence.

As it is part of Dharok's barrows set, if Dharok's helm is worn along with all of the other pieces of equipment in Dharok's barrows set, the player gains a special effect. Attacks do more damage as the player's hitpoints decrease, up to 98.9% bonus damage with 1 hitpoint remaining with 99 max.

For more details on the mechanics and strategies for this equipment, see the set page.

4722:

4724:
Guthan's helm is melee armour worn in the headwear slot that is part of Guthan the Infested's set of barrows equipment. To wear Guthan's helm, a player must have 70 Defence.

If Guthan's helm is wielded together with all other pieces of Guthan's armour set, then successful melee attacks have a 25% chance of restoring health to the user equal to the damage dealt to the target. This set has the potential to be extremely useful in a variety of combat situations, due to its healing reducing the need to bring food. While the set has strong combat stats, its durability can be conserved through only equipping it when a player needs to heal, and carrying alternative non-degradable armour and weaponry.

For more details on the mechanics and strategies for this equipment, see the set page.
4726:

It is the second most accurate spear in game, surpassed only by the Zamorakian spear/hasta, which has +85 Stab. However, it is slower than most spears, having an attack rate of 5 ticks, rather than 4 ticks, and it cannot be poisoned.

4732:
Karil's coif is ranged armour worn in the headwear slot that is part of Karil the Tainted's set of barrows equipment. To wear Karil's coif, a player must have 70 Defence and 70 Ranged.

Being part of Karil's barrows set, if Karil's coif is worn along with the other three pieces of Karil's set, the player's attacks gains a special effect: on successful attacks with Karil's crossbow against another player, there is a 25% chance that it may temporarily lower that player's Agility level by 20%. Additionally, if an amulet of the damned is worn alongside the set, there is also a 25% chance for each attack to deal a second hit for half the damage of the first.

For more details on the mechanics and strategies for this equipment, see the set page.
4734:
Karil's crossbow is a two-handed ranged weapon that is part of Karil the Tainted's set. It requires 70 Ranged to wield. It fires bolt racks, which break upon firing. When equipped with the other three pieces of Karil the Tainted's set the wearer will receive the set effect, which has a chance to temporarily lower their target's Agility level. Additionally, if an amulet of the damned is worn alongside the set, there is also a 25% chance for each attack to deal a second hit for half the damage of the first.

Unlike standard crossbows, it is wielded in both hands. Furthermore, regular crossbows fire fewer, more powerful shots, meaning Karil's crossbow is actually similar in function to a shortbow; this gives it a potentially higher damage per second, at the expense of the shield slot. The crossbow has an attack range of 8. Longrange increases attack range by 2.

This weapon is comparable to a magic shortbow and its imbued counterpart. While Karil's offers a longer range, a +15 or +9 greater ranged attack bonus respectively, and a passive chance to hit twice when using the full Karil set and amulet of the damned, the magic shortbow variants offer identical strength when using amethyst arrows, which are not guaranteed to be consumed with each shot. In addition, the magic shortbows do not degrade. Players on a budget or fighting monsters with low ranged defence may find the magic shortbow to be the preferable option.
4736:
Karil's leathertop is a degradable piece of ranged armour worn in the body slot that is part of Karil the Tainted's set of barrows equipment. To wear Karil's top, a player must have 70 Defence and 70 Ranged.

4738:
Karil's leatherskirt is Ranged armour worn in the legwear slot that is part of Karil the Tainted's set of Barrows equipment. To wear Karil's leatherskirt, a player must have 70 Defence and 70 Ranged.

Karil's leatherskirt gives the third highest magic defence for the leg slot at +35, following Armadyl chainskirt's +40, and Masori chaps (f)'s +46. The skirt has the same offensive bonuses as the black d'hide chaps, while offering higher defence in all but Slash in which it is on par.

Being part of Karil's barrows set, if Karil's leatherskirt is worn along with the other three pieces of Karil's set, the player's attacks gains a special effect: on successful attacks with Karil's crossbow against another player, there is a 25% chance that it may temporarily lower that player's Agility level by 20%. 4740:
Bolt racks are ammunition exclusively used by the Karil's crossbow. They are a reward from Barrows with at least 881 reward potential, purchased from Ak-Haranu's Exotic Shop on the Port Phasmatys docks, or purchased from the Last Man Standing shop.

Unlike other bolts, they always disappear after being fired and cannot be retrieved by Ava's devices.
4745:
Torag's helm is melee armour worn in the headwear slot that is part of Torag the Corrupted's set of Barrows equipment. To wear Torag's helmet, a player must have 70 Defence.

Being part of Torag's barrows set, if Torag's helmet is worn along with all of the other pieces of equipment in Torag's barrows set the player gains a set effect. Damaging melee attacks have a chance of lowering the victim's run energy by 20%.

Torag's helmet is not commonly used due to its lack of Strength or Prayer bonuses. Furthermore, the set effect is considered mediocre. As a result, it is inexpensive compared to the other barrows helmets. However, it is often used in PKing, especially by ranged tanks, as there are few other inexpensive helm options for rangers and the negative ranged attack bonus is small.

For more details on the mechanics and strategies for this equipment, see the set page.
4747:
Torag's hammers are a two-handed blunt weapon that is part of Torag the Corrupted's set of barrows equipment. To wield Torag's hammers, a player must have 70 Attack and Strength.

Being part of Torag's barrows set, if Torag's hammers are wielded along with all of the other pieces of equipment in Torag's barrows set the player gains a special effect: damaging melee attacks have a chance of lowering the victim's run energy by 20%.

Torag's hammers have lower popularity and value compared to other Barrows weapons, as the hammers have a lower strength bonus and Torag's special effect is not as useful in combat. However, they have a high crush bonus and can be one of the more likely out of the melee Barrows weapons to hit as most armours have less crush defensive bonus than slash.

Like the glacial temotli, sulphur blades, and Earthbound tecpatl, the hammers perform two independently rolled hits per attack. The maximum damage of each hit is determined by calculating the combined max hit as normal and dividing it by two. If the combined max hit is odd, one max hit is rounded up while the other is rounded down (e.g., 45 → 22 + 23). This unique effect is useful when fighting NPCs with negative flat armour, such as the Blue Moon, as the flat damage increase gets applied to each hitsplat separately.

4753:
Verac's helm is melee armour worn in the headwear slot that is part of Verac the Defiled's set of Barrows equipment. To wear Verac's helmet, a player must have 70 Defence.

Verac's helm has a lesser magic penalty compared to other helmets at +0 magic defence but slightly less ranged defence bonuses compared to Guthan's or Torag's helm, which are equal bonuses. This helmet is often used in 'tank' combat due to the high defensive bonuses as well as a prayer bonus. This helmet is commonly used during the TzHaar Fight Cave minigame because of its good melee and ranged defence and prayer bonus.

If Verac's helm is worn along with all of the other pieces of equipment in Verac's set, the player receives the Defiler set effect. With this set effect active, player attacks have a chance (averaging 1/4) of hitting through an opponent's defence and prayer entirely. This effect can be devastating towards tank opponents who rely on high defence. With this set effect, Verac's flail can be considered one of the best weapons for certain PvM situations.
4757:
Verac's brassard is melee armour worn in the body slot that is part of Verac's equipment. To wear Verac's brassard, a player must have 70 Defence.

Verac's brassard offers significantly less melee and ranged protection than Guthan, Torag and Dharok's platebodies (which all have equal stats), however it is better than the Rune platebody, with the exception of having -1 stab defence bonus. Because of this, Verac's brassard is rarely seen being used outside of the full set. However, Verac's brassard does not penalise ranged and magic attack bonuses nearly as much as regular melee armour.

If Verac's brassard is worn along with all of the other pieces of equipment in Verac's set, the player receives the Defiler set effect. With this set effect active, player attacks have a chance (averaging 1/4) of hitting through an opponent's defence and prayer entirely. 4759:

Verac's plateskirt provides the same amount of melee protection as Dharok and Torag's platelegs with a marginally lower amount of ranged protection. However, it does not penalise the wearer's magic defence, provides a substantial prayer bonus (+4) and weighs less than most leg armour.

4803: Rune brutal arrows can be used to effectively kill zogres and skogres at Jiggig, as well as chompy birds. They are made with flighted ogre arrows and rune nails. 4808:
The black prism can be obtained during Zogre Flesh Eaters quest. During the quest, it can be found in the coffin to the west of the skeleton on the floor. If you look-at it, there is a description which suggests that it was involved in the explosion that hit the area, and was blasted into the coffin. Zavistic Rarve identifies it as a tool of necromancy.

This artefact has been used to resurrect the dead ogres in Jiggig as Zogres and Skogres. Later in the quest, the player discovers that it was Sithik Ints who has used to do so out of his hatred toward ogres. After the quest, you can sell it to Zavistic Rarve for 2000 coins or Yanni Salika for 5000 coins.
4811:
The dragon inn tankard is one of the items which players take out of the ruined backpack during the Zogre Flesh Eaters quest. It has the "look at" option. Doing so reveals that it has the dragon emblem and the words "Ye Olde Dragon Inn" on it, a clue to seek further evidence at the Dragon Inn.

Showing it to the bartender in Yanille prompts him to tell the player that it belonged to Brentle Vahn, a fighter with a reputation for selling his skills unwisely. The bartender then remarks that he's seen Brentle in the company of a shady wizard; since the player found the tankard among skeletal human remains, it becomes clear that Brentle met his end while on some errand for this wizard.

It is used again at a later stage of the same quest to persuade Zavistic Rarve that Brentle was the body in the Zogre cave. In combination with other evidence, this leads Zavistic to help the player catch the culprit.

This is the only item during Zogre Flesh Eaters which disappears from both the player's bank and inventory when the quest is finished, including all duplicates.
4814:
The Sithik portrait is an item used in the quest Zogre Flesh Eaters. During the quest, the player must create the Sithik portrait by using a piece of papyrus on Sithik Ints with a piece of charcoal in the inventory.

If successful, the player can then take the portrait to the Bartender at the Dragon Inn to have it signed, affirming that Sithik was present at that bar.

If the player fails to produce the portrait, they will be left with a bad Sithik portrait, which is useless, and the player must try again.
4815:
The Sithik portrait is an item used in the quest Zogre Flesh Eaters. During the quest, the player must create the Sithik portrait by using a piece of papyrus on Sithik Ints with a piece of charcoal in the inventory.

If successful, the player can then take the portrait to the Bartender at the Dragon Inn to have it signed, affirming that Sithik was present at that bar.

If the player fails to produce the portrait, they will be left with a bad Sithik portrait, which is useless, and the player must try again.
4816:
The signed portrait of Sithik Ints is an item used in Zogre Flesh Eaters. During the quest, the player must take a Sithik portrait to the Bartender to be signed, in order to charge Sithik Ints with leading Brentle Vahn to his death.

If players use the signed portrait on Sithik, Sithik will offer to bribe the player with 2 million gold, in order to buy the signed portrait. Whether the player accepts or rejects, Sithik will not buy the portrait, instead insisting that no one would believe the player anyway.

If players produce a bad Sithik portrait during their attempt, he will not sign it and the player will have to attempt to create the portrait again.
4818:
The ogre artefact is a sacred item to the ogres of Gu'Tanoth, and is requested to be retrieved by Grish during the Zogre Flesh Eaters quest. It is dropped by a level 111 undead ourg named Slash Bash, who appears to be wearing the artefact as a helmet prior to being slain.

If lost during the quest, it can be found by searching the stand again. Slash Bash cannot be refought.
4819:
Bronze nails are nails made with a bronze bar on an anvil with a hammer in the player's inventory, requiring level 4 Smithing, yielding 15 bronze nails and granting 12.5 Smithing experience per bar. They can also be bought from a few shops, most notably the Sawmill, as well as the Shipyard, which can be teleported to for free by any Shipwright NPC found in major ports.

Bronze nails can be used to construct certain types of wooden furniture, however, they bend and break very easily. With 7 Fletching, they can be used on flighted ogre arrows to create bronze brutal arrows, granting 1.4 Fletching experience per arrow. With 41 Crafting, fifteen bronze nails can be used with an oak shield and two pieces of hard leather to craft a hard leather shield, granting 70 Crafting experience per shield. One bronze nail is required in The Fremennik Isles quest in order to make a Neitiznot shield.

Since nails cannot be bent while constructing STASH units, bronze nails are the most economical option for them.
4821:
Black nails are nails which, unlike other nails, cannot be made by players. Black nails can be obtained from thieving Ogre coffins or as a drop from zombies in Tarn's Lair. They may also be obtained while clearing rubble during the In Aid of the Myreque quest.

Black nails can be used to construct certain types of wooden furniture. With 38 Fletching, they can be used on flighted ogre arrows to create black brutal arrows, granting 6.5 Fletching experience per arrow.
4822:
Mithril nails are nails made with a mithril bar on an anvil with a hammer in the player's inventory, requiring 54 Smithing, yielding 15 mithril nails and granting 50 Smithing experience per bar.

Mithril nails can be used to construct certain types of wooden furniture. With 56 Construction, five mithril nails can be used along with two oak planks to repair broken bridges in the Hallowed Sepulchre, granting 300 Construction experience; without a hallowed hammer in the player's inventory, there is a chance of failing to repair the bridge and breaking nails in the process. With 49 Fletching, they can be used on flighted ogre arrows to create mithril brutal arrows, granting 7.5 Fletching experience per arrow. With 69 Crafting, fifteen mithril nails can be used with a yew shield and two pieces of blue dragon leather to craft a blue d'hide shield, granting 140 Crafting experience per shield.
4823:
Adamantite nails are nails made with an adamantite bar on an anvil with a hammer in the player's inventory, requiring 74 Smithing, yielding 15 adamantite nails and granting 62.5 Smithing experience per bar.

Adamantite nails can be used to construct certain types of wooden furniture. With 56 Construction, five adamantite nails can be used along with two teak planks to repair broken bridges in the Hallowed Sepulchre, granting 450 Construction experience; without a hallowed hammer in the player's inventory, there is a chance of failing to repair the bridge and breaking nails in the process. With 62 Fletching, they can be used on flighted ogre arrows to create adamant brutal arrows, granting 10.2 Fletching experience per arrow. With 76 Crafting, fifteen adamantite nails can be used with a magic shield and two pieces of red dragon leather to craft a red d'hide shield, granting 156 Crafting experience per shield.
4825: An unstrung comp bow is made by using a knife on Achey tree logs with wolf bones in the inventory. Stringing it with a Bow string creates a Comp ogre bow. Level 30 Fletching and partial completion of Zogre Flesh Eaters is required.
4834:
Ourg bones are bones obtained by killing Slash Bash, the boss from Zogre Flesh Eaters, stealing them from ogre coffins via the Thieving skill, or using keys dropped by zogres and skogres on nearby chests. As Slash Bash cannot be respawned after he has been killed once, ourg bones cannot be farmed from the boss.

Ourg bones give 140 Prayer experience when buried. This can be increased by offering the bones in different ways:

420 XP when casting Sinister Offering.

420 XP when offered at the sacred bone burner after the appropriate faith level has been achieved.

490 XP when offered at a gilded altar with two lit burners.

560 XP when offered at the Ectofuntus in the form of ourg bonemeal.

560 XP when blessed and broken down into blessed bone shards and offered at the libation bowl.

672 XP when blessed and broken down into blessed bone shards and offered at the libation bowl with jug of blessed sunfire wine. Virilis outside the altar will exchange noted bones for 10 coins each.

980 XP on average when offered at the Chaos Temple in the Wilderness. Each offering gives 490 XP, which is the same as the gilded altars with two burners lit, but with an additional 50% chance to not consume the bones.

Due to only being able to obtain them once from Slash Bash, and ogre coffins being slow to loot, Ourg bones are relatively rare, and as a result are generally much pricier than bones that provide similar Prayer experience.

Ourg bones provide the second most Prayer experience of all bones in the game, surpassed only by superior dragon bones. Unlike superior dragon bones, they do not have a Prayer level requirement to offer them, and grant almost as much experience.
4836:
The strange potion is a quest item obtained during Zogre Flesh Eaters. After the player convinces Zavistic Rarve that Sithik Ints might be involved in the curse on Jiggig, Zavistic gives the player the strange potion with instructions to find some way to use the potion on Sithik and then question him.

The player must use the potion on the cup of tea in Sithik's room, then leave and return. The player will then find that Sithik has been transformed into an ogre. The potion can not be used on any other object or character.
4838:
The Cup of tea is an unobtainable item encountered during Zogre Flesh Eaters. It is found in the room of Sithik Ints in Yanille, but cannot be picked up.

During the quest, the strange potion should be used on the cup of tea to turn Sithik into an ogre, whereupon he reveals the secret to making Relicym's balm and brutal arrows.

When the "take" option is selected, Sithik Ints yells at the player, Hey! What do you think you're doing? Leave my tea alone!. When a telegrab is attempted, he will say Hey! What do you think you're doing? Don't go casting that kind of spell anywhere near my tea! Leave my tea alone you telegrabbing fiend!
4839:
The ogre gate key is obtained from Grish toward the end of the quest Zogre Flesh Eaters to gain entrance to the Ogre's ceremonial chamber in Jiggig.

If lost during the quest, the player can get another key from Grish. This key cannot be placed onto the steel key ring.
4840:
An unfinished rogue's purse potion is an unfinished potion made via the Herblore skill. Players make it by using a rogue's purse on a vial of water, earning no experience.

It is used to make the Relicym's balm at level 8 by adding a snake weed. This requires completion of Zogre Flesh Eaters.
4842:
Relicym's balm is a potion that can cure disease. To do so, multiple doses of relicym's balm must be drunk, with each dose weakening the strength of the disease. However, the potion does not offer any temporary immunity, unlike Sanfew serum.

The potion is made by mixing rogue's purse and snake weed in a vial of water, giving 40 Herblore experience. It requires level 8 Herblore and completion of the Zogre Flesh Eaters quest to the point where Sithik Ints tells the player how to cure the Zogre disease.

Players may purchase 3 dose potions from Uglug Nar for 200 coins once they've learned how to make the potion. To open Uglug Nar's store, simply give him a Relicym's balm potion of any dosage, for which he will pay 100 (1 dose), 300 (2 doses), 650 (3 doses) or 1000 (4 doses) gold. Note that Uglug will buy these potions from players for 120 gold as well if he has none in stock, but it must be a 3 dose potion for him to make an offer.

After Barbarian Herblore Training, roe or caviar can be added to a 2 dose relicym's balm, requiring 9 Herblore, yielding a Relicym's mix and 14 Herblore experience.

Relicym's balm is the preferred weapon to use against yellow broodoo victims during the Tai Bwo Wannai Cleanup minigame, as it can deal over 25 damage to them. Relicym's balm can also be used as a cheaper alternative to Sanfew serums to reduce the damage caused by parasites when fighting The Nightmare.

Six Relicym's balm are needed to construct an innoculation station on a ship, which provides immunity to fetid waters when sailing the seas.

4850:
Ogre coffin keys are items which open the locked coffins in the Jiggig cave, which first becomes available during the quest Zogre Flesh Eaters. The keys are dropped by zogres and skogres, who always drop one key upon death.

Coffins are primarily opened due to their chance of providing different types of ogre bones, as they otherwise mostly provide low-value loot like iron and steel equipment.
4855: Ourg bonemeal is an item that is used for worship at the Ectofuntus. It consists of a pot filled with ourg bones that have been crushed in the bone grinder at the Ectofuntus.
4862:
Ahrim's staff is a one-handed magic weapon that is part of Ahrim the Blighted's set. To wield Ahrim's staff, the player must have 70 Magic and 70 Attack. It increases Magic damage by 5%.

If Ahrim's staff is wielded along with all of the other pieces of equipment in Ahrim's barrows set, the player's successful magic attacks have a chance of temporarily lowering the opponent's Strength level. This is cumulative with other effects that lower strength, namely the spell Enfeeble.

It is able to autocast Standard combat spells as well as being one of the few weapons able to autocast Arceuus combat spells. Additionally, wearing Ahrim's set with an Amulet of the damned will allow players to autocast Ancient Magicks, and also grant players a 25% chance of dealing a hit with 30% increased damage.

Dharok's helm is melee armour worn in the headwear slot that is part of Dharok the Wretched's set of barrows equipment. To wear Dharok's helm, a player must have 70 Defence.

As it is part of Dharok's barrows set, if Dharok's helm is worn along with all of the other pieces of equipment in Dharok's barrows set, the player gains a special effect. Attacks do more damage as the player's hitpoints decrease, up to 98.9% bonus damage with 1 hitpoint remaining with 99 max.

For more details on the mechanics and strategies for this equipment, see the set page.

4904:
Guthan's helm is melee armour worn in the headwear slot that is part of Guthan the Infested's set of barrows equipment. To wear Guthan's helm, a player must have 70 Defence.

If Guthan's helm is wielded together with all other pieces of Guthan's armour set, then successful melee attacks have a 25% chance of restoring health to the user equal to the damage dealt to the target. This set has the potential to be extremely useful in a variety of combat situations, due to its healing reducing the need to bring food. While the set has strong combat stats, its durability can be conserved through only equipping it when a player needs to heal, and carrying alternative non-degradable armour and weaponry.

For more details on the mechanics and strategies for this equipment, see the set page.

However, it is slower than most spears, having an attack rate of 5 ticks, rather than 4 ticks, and it cannot be poisoned.

If Guthan's warspear is wielded together with all other pieces of Guthan's armour set, then successful melee attacks have a 25% chance of restoring health to the user equal to the damage dealt to the target. This set has the potential to be extremely useful in a variety of combat situations, due to its healing reducing the need to bring food. While the set has strong combat stats, its durability can be conserved through only equipping it when a player needs to heal, and carrying alternative non-degradable armour and weaponry.

Karil's coif is ranged armour worn in the headwear slot that is part of Karil the Tainted's set of barrows equipment. To wear Karil's coif, a player must have 70 Defence and 70 Ranged.

4934:
Karil's crossbow is a two-handed ranged weapon that is part of Karil the Tainted's set. It requires 70 Ranged to wield. It fires bolt racks, which break upon firing. When equipped with the other three pieces of Karil the Tainted's set the wearer will receive the set effect, which has a chance to temporarily lower their target's Agility level. Additionally, if an amulet of the damned is worn alongside the set, there is also a 25% chance for each attack to deal a second hit for half the damage of the first.

Unlike standard crossbows, it is wielded in both hands. Furthermore, regular crossbows fire fewer, more powerful shots, meaning Karil's crossbow is actually similar in function to a shortbow; this gives it a potentially higher damage per second, at the expense of the shield slot. The crossbow has an attack range of 8. Longrange increases attack range by 2.

This weapon is comparable to a magic shortbow and its imbued counterpart. While Karil's offers a longer range, a +15 or +9 greater ranged attack bonus respectively, and a passive chance to hit twice when using the full Karil set and amulet of the damned, the magic shortbow variants offer identical strength when using amethyst arrows, which are not guaranteed to be consumed with each shot. In addition, the magic shortbows do not degrade. Players on a budget or fighting monsters with low ranged defence may find the magic shortbow to be the preferable option.

4952:
Torag's helm is melee armour worn in the headwear slot that is part of Torag the Corrupted's set of Barrows equipment. To wear Torag's helmet, a player must have 70 Defence.

Being part of Torag's barrows set, if Torag's helmet is worn along with all of the other pieces of equipment in Torag's barrows set the player gains a set effect. Damaging melee attacks have a chance of lowering the victim's run energy by 20%.

Torag's helmet is not commonly used due to its lack of Strength or Prayer bonuses. Furthermore, the set effect is considered mediocre. As a result, it is inexpensive compared to the other barrows helmets. However, it is often used in PKing, especially by ranged tanks, as there are few other inexpensive helm options for rangers and the negative ranged attack bonus is small.

For more details on the mechanics and strategies for this equipment, see the set page.

For more details on the mechanics and strategies for this equipment, see the set page.
4958:
Torag's hammers are a two-handed blunt weapon that is part of Torag the Corrupted's set of barrows equipment. To wield Torag's hammers, a player must have 70 Attack and Strength.

Being part of Torag's barrows set, if Torag's hammers are wielded along with all of the other pieces of equipment in Torag's barrows set the player gains a special effect: damaging melee attacks have a chance of lowering the victim's run energy by 20%.

Torag's hammers have lower popularity and value compared to other Barrows weapons, as the hammers have a lower strength bonus and Torag's special effect is not as useful in combat. However, they have a high crush bonus and can be one of the more likely out of the melee Barrows weapons to hit as most armours have less crush defensive bonus than slash.

Like the glacial temotli, sulphur blades, and Earthbound tecpatl, the hammers perform two independently rolled hits per attack. The maximum damage of each hit is determined by calculating the combined max hit as normal and dividing it by two. If the combined max hit is odd, one max hit is rounded up while the other is rounded down (e.g., 45 → 22 + 23). This unique effect is useful when fighting NPCs with negative flat armour, such as the Blue Moon, as the flat damage increase gets applied to each hitsplat separately.
