6465:
The ring of Charos is a magical ring that charms certain NPCs when worn, unlocking different dialogue options and benefits. Charos, the creator of the ring, used it to enhance his prowess as a diplomat and convince the weak-minded to do his bidding. The Wise Old Man says that anyone who uses the ring must already possess some kind of diplomatic skill for it to work.

The unactivated form is awarded upon completion of Creature of Fenkenstrain. This version of the ring can only be used to deceive werewolves into believing the wearer is one of them; wearing it is necessary to access the Werewolf Agility Course. Near the beginning of the Garden of Tranquillity quest, the Wise Old Man activates it into the ring of Charos(a), allowing the player to charm and convince other people into helping you. Finishing Garden of Tranquility is NOT required to use the activated form of the ring.

The ring is lost upon death. If lost, it can be recovered by pickpocketing Dr Fenkenstrain. After Creature of Fenkenstrain, he resides on the top floor of Fenkenstrain's Castle; partway through The Great Brain Robbery, he permanently moves to the basement of the Harmony Island windmill. Note that if the player throws the ring into the Edgeville well during Garden of Tranquillity, another one cannot be claimed from Fenkenstrain during the quest, and the only way to get it back is to use a fishing rod on the well. Once the ring is activated for the first time, it will always be activated when recovered, and the original version becomes unobtainable.
6466:
Rune shards can be made by using rune essence or pure essence with a hammer to crack them into small pieces. The shards can then be ground down into rune dust.

Rune shards and rune dust feature in the Garden of Tranquillity quest, where it is revealed that adding the essence to a plant cure potion enhances its potency. This potion is then used to successfully treat the badly diseased vines in Bernald's garden behind his house in Taverley.
6467:
Rune dust can be made by using a hammer or a chisel on a rune essence or pure essence stone to crack them into rune shards, and then grinding these down in a pestle and mortar.

Rune shards and rune dust appear in the Garden of Tranquillity quest, when rune dust must be added to a plant cure potion to revive some badly damaged vines in Bernald's garden behind the bar in Burthorpe.
6468:
A plant cure potion is used on diseased plants, during Farming, to restore the plant to a healthy state so it continues to grow. Farming shops and GAG farmers at farming patches sell them for 40 coins each.

Note: This will not work on dead plants. To ensure that your plant does not die, consider using an amulet of nature to monitor it, or pay a gardener to protect your crops automatically (gardeners will not protect herbs or flowers).
6469:
White tree fruit is a food item acquired by picking the white tree in the garden at Varrock Palace, after completion of the Garden of Tranquillity quest. The tree grows one fruit approximately every 5 minutes and can hold up to 4 fruit at a time. Picking one grants 12 Farming experience.

When eaten, white tree fruit restore 5-10% run energy and heal 3 health.

Due to being non-tradeable unlike other fruit, they cannot be turned into banknotes neither by tool leprechaun nor at a bank.

White tree fruit can be used as an ingredient when making supercompost. It can also be fed to the raccoon on Vatrachos Island in exchange for a medallion fragment.
6479:
The list is a quest item given to the player by Queen Ellamaria at the start of the Garden of Tranquillity quest. It contains a list of flowers the plants that the player must grow in her garden behind Varrock Palace.

To grow all of the plants the player must obtain the following seeds:

4 Delphinium seeds

3 Yellow orchid seeds

3 Pink orchid seeds

4 Snowdrop seeds

4 Vine seeds

1 White tree shoot

3 Red rose seeds

3 Pink rose seeds

3 White rose seeds

The seeds are given to the player by various NPCs for performing tasks during the quest. See the main Garden of Tranquillity walkthrough for complete instructions on each task.
6522:
Toktz-xil-ul, also known as obsidian throwing rings, are a one-handed thrown weapon that require level 60 Ranged. They are quite powerful, having stats equivalent to a magic shortbow in conjunction with rune arrows, making them one of the more powerful thrown weapons. Because of this, and the fact that they can be equipped with a shield, they are seen in PvP scenarios quite often even after the introduction of dragon knives. However, they are significantly more expensive than rune arrows, making them less practical for general use. It is part of the set of obsidian weapons.

25 of these are required to build an obsidian fence at level 83 Construction in the Superior garden of a player-owned house.

This weapon has an attack range of 7 on rapid, and 9 on long range.
6523:
The toktz-xil-ak, also known as the obsidian splitsword or obby sword, is a one-handed stab sword requiring an Attack level of 60 to wield. It has stats similar to a rune longsword but with a faster attack speed of 4 ticks. It is part of the set of obsidian weapons.

When correctly used, the obsidian sword is one of the best weapons used for training Strength, especially for those who do not want to complete the master quest Monkey Madness I for use of the dragon scimitar.

When a berserker necklace is equipped, this weapon gains a 20% damage boost. It is also affected by the obsidian armour (helmet, platebody, and platelegs) which will increase the melee attack and melee strength by 10%. The damage bonus does stack with the berserker necklace.
6524: The toktz-ket-xil is an obsidian shield requiring 60 Defence to wield. Its defensive stats are equal to a granite shield's stats with an additional +5 Strength bonus; it also weighs less. It has lower Melee defence bonuses than a rune kiteshield, but higher Ranged defence. Compared to the rune defender, it has the same strength bonus but swaps Melee accuracy bonuses for higher defensive bonuses.
6525:
The toktz-xil-ek (also known as the obsidian knife or obsidian dagger) is a one-handed slash sword that requires 60 Attack to wield. Despite often being referred to as a dagger, the toktz-xil-ek is not a stab sword, has no magic attack bonus, and cannot be poisoned. It is part of the set of obsidian weapons.

Players can buy the toktz-xil-ek at the weapons store in Mor Ul Rek for 37,500 Tokkul. This weapon cannot be made using the Crafting and/or Smithing skills.

When a Berserker necklace is equipped, this weapon gains a 20% damage boost. It is also affected by the Obsidian armour (helmet, platebody and platelegs) which will increase the melee attack and melee strength by 10%. The damage bonus does stack with the Berserker necklace.

Buying this item from the store does not unlock the collection log. The drop must be obtained via TzHaar-Xil.
6526:
A toktz-mej-tal (also known as an obsidian staff) is a two-handed staff wielded by the TzHaar-Mej, and can be obtained as a very rare drop from them. Level 60 Magic and Attack are required to equip it. As well as being able to cast Magic spells, it can be sufficiently used as a melee weapon due to its significant crush and strength bonuses. It is part of the set of obsidian weapons.

It is one of the only magic weapons that requires two hands to equip, the others being the Gauntlet-exclusive Crystal and Corrupted staves, the Blue moon spear, and Tumeken's shadow.

Ten of these are used to build an obsidian fence at level 83 Construction in a player's Superior garden.
6527:
The Tzhaar-ket-em (also known as the obsidian mace) is a one-handed blunt weapon requiring an Attack level of 60 to wield. Though it's commonly thought of as mace, it is not a spiked weapon and has no prayer bonus. It is slightly stronger and more accurate than the dragon mace, but has a slower attack speed and lacks any special attack. It is part of the set of obsidian weapons.

When a Berserker necklace is equipped, this weapon gains a 20% damage boost. It is also affected by the Obsidian armour (helmet, platebody, and platelegs) which will increase the melee attack and melee strength by 10%. The damage bonus does stack with the Berserker necklace.

Unlike other obsidian weapons, Tzhaar-ket-em can only be obtained from TzHaar-Hur-Tel's Equipment Store.
6528:
The Tzhaar-ket-om, also known as the obsidian maul, is a two-handed blunt weapon that requires a Strength level of 60 to wield. It is affected by the Berserker necklace, receiving a 20% damage increase when the necklace is worn. It is also affected by the Obsidian armour (helmet, platebody and platelegs) which will increase the melee attack and melee strength by 10%. These damage bonuses do stack with each other. It is part of the set of obsidian weapons.

Two of these are used to build an obsidian fence at level 83 Construction in a player's superior garden.

The maul is used commonly by Obsidian maulers in player-killing because the only requirement is a Strength level of 60, which makes it possible to have a low Combat level while being able to deal high amounts of damage. However, one major drawback of this weapon is its poor attack speed.

With Karamja Gloves 1 or higher, players can purchase the maul by selling 7223 chaos runes to TzHaar-Mej-Roh's Rune Store.

Players can attach a Tzhaar-ket-om ornament kit, obtained from hard Treasure Trails, to create a Tzhaar-ket-om (t). This is only cosmetic, and does not affect the maul's stat bonuses. It can be dismantled, returning the maul and ornament kit.
6529:
TokKul is the currency of Mor Ul Rek. It is made from obsidian and cannot be created by players. As it is a currency, TokKul dropped by monsters can be automatically collected if the player is wearing a ring of wealth.

TokKul is made out of the corpses of the TzHaar, as stated in the 17th Postbag from the Hedge letter. When asked why players cannot trade TokKul, TzHaar-Hur-Lek responded:
6541:
The mouse toy is a fun weapon obtained from Bob the Cat after completion of the quest A Tail of Two Cats. Occasionally, if the player wields the toy and has a pet cat following them, the cat will perform a pouncing animation at it.

The attack animation is similar to the abyssal whip. When it is used to attack, it makes the same noise as a rubber chicken "whacking" someone. This item is not commonly seen, as its damage and accuracy bonuses are noticeably poor.

If lost after the completion of A Tail of Two Cats, the mouse toy can be re-obtained by talking to Bob the Cat with an amulet of catspeak equipped. A quick way to find Bob is to hop worlds at the anvils south of the west bank in Varrock, as he can often be found there.

If lost after the completion of Dragon Slayer II, the mouse toy can be re-obtained by searching the closed chest in Unferth's house east of the castle in Burthorpe.
6542: The present is an item obtained upon completion of the A Tail of Two Cats quest. The present, when opened, yields a mouse toy, which can be used to play with your cat, and two antique lamps, which grant 2,500 experience each in a chosen skill that is above level 30.
6543:
Antique lamps are rewards from quests, achievement diaries and the Varrock Museum miniquest. Like regular lamps, these lamps grant a player experience in a chosen skill, and the skill chosen must usually be over a certain level which is unboostable.

Lamps that are not included in the three items kept on death will be kept inside your death's coffer, if not deleted.
6544:
The enchanted catspeak amulet is an amulet worn in the neck slot obtained during A Tail of Two Cats by handing over a regular catspeak amulet and 5 death runes to Hild in Burthorpe. Like the unenchanted version, you can speak to cats while wearing it. The main difference is that it can also be used to locate Bob the Cat's general direction. To do so, right click the amulet, use the "Open" option (or the "Locate" option if equipped) which will open a compass-like interface in the shape of a cat, and turn the compass clockwise or anti-clockwise by clicking on the whiskers until the eyes are lit and the cat's mouth starts moving.

After the events of Dragon Slayer II, opening the amulet simply results in the message, "You look at the amulet and take a moment to remember your fallen friend."

If the amulet is lost, you will have to visit the Sphinx in Sophanem if you don't have a spare regular amulet (your cat must be following you when you talk to the Sphinx), and pay Hild another 5 death runes and your catspeak amulet to get it enchanted again. Unlike the regular amulet, you can only hold one enchanted catspeak amulet at any time.
6546: Recipe is an item that players can find in Unferth's bookcase during A Tail of Two Cats. The recipe is for a chocolate cake, and serves as a hint that this is the food players should provide him with.
6547:
The doctor's hat is used during A Tail of Two Cats to convince Unferth that you are a doctor. It is obtained from the Apothecary.

If a player gets a nurse hat during the quest and later wants to get the doctor's hat, or vice versa, they can destroy their current hat and talk to the Apothecary to choose which hat they want. Players cannot own both hats at the same time.
6555:
A wily cat is a special variant of a pet cat, which players gain access to by completing the Ratcatchers quest. After completion, players can speak to Felkrash to have her train their overgrown cat into a wily cat. (Warning: After training your overgrown cat to be a wily cat, you will start from zero for the number of rats caught for the cat training medal. Wily cats are also ineligible for the medal.)

Wily cats are the best hunters of any cat, with a base success rate of 50% plus an additional success roll which increases based on their activity level, capping at an additional 50% success roll. When fighting hell-rat behemoths, they have higher health, get hit less often, and have twice the DPS of a regular cat. In addition, they can also catch kalphite larvae and butterflies (as well as Hunter butterflies, though this yields no experience). Wily cats do not require food of any kind (except when fighting hell-rat behemoths).

Players are only allowed to have one wily or lazy cat at a time, in addition to one kitten or adult cat, and as many overgrown cats as they wish. You may have multiple wily cats if you first store your existing wily cat in your menagerie before training another.

Wily cats have a hidden "happiness" status, which can result in 3 different sets of standard dialogue depending on whether the cat is happy, content, or unhappy. A wily cat's happiness decreases when it is not given attention for an extended period of time, similarly to raising kittens. A content or unhappy cat's mood can be improved through stroking and playing with the cat. It can also be improved by taking the cat rat catching.

Players are only allowed to have one wily or lazy cat at a time, in addition to one kitten or adult cat, and as many overgrown cats as they wish. You may have multiple wily cats if you first store your existing wily cat in your menagerie before training another.

Wily cats have a hidden "happiness" status, which can result in 3 different sets of standard dialogue depending on whether the cat is happy, content, or unhappy. A wily cat's happiness decreases when it is not given attention for an extended period of time, similarly to raising kittens. A content or unhappy cat's mood can be improved through stroking and playing with the cat. It can also be improved by taking the cat rat catching.
6558:

After completion, players can speak to Felkrash to have her train their overgrown cat into a wily cat. (Warning: After training your overgrown cat to be a wily cat, you will start from zero for the number of rats caught for the cat training medal. Wily cats are also ineligible for the medal.)

When fighting hell-rat behemoths, they have higher health, get hit less often, and have twice the DPS of a regular cat. 6562:
A mud battlestaff is a mud elemental staff which provides unlimited amounts of water and earth runes as well as the autocast option when equipped. It requires 30 Attack and 30 Magic to wield.

The mystic mud staff is an even stronger alternative, providing better melee and magic stat bonuses. It is obtained by taking the mud battlestaff and 40,000 to Thormac. (Reduced to 30,000 or 20,000 with completion of the hard and elite Kandarin diaries respectively.)

Wielding a mud battlestaff is ideal for curse spells, as almost all of them use both water and earth runes.

The staff is only obtainable as a potential drop from Dagannoth Prime. For ironmen unable or unwilling to farm this boss until (and if) the staff is dropped, there are two alternatives in order to have infinite water & earth runes at the same time: using an earth staff with a tome of water that is charged with at least one soaked page, or a using a water staff with a tome of earth that is charged with at least one soiled page. Given that only combat spells drain charges from the tomes, the staff + tome combo will provide unlimited water and earth runes when casting spells such as Bones to Peaches or Lvl-5 enchant (e.g. for training Magic at the Mage Training Arena) without the need for recharging the tome.
6563:
The mystic mud staff is an elemental staff requiring 40 Attack and 40 Magic to wield. In addition to increased Melee and Magic Attack bonuses, the staff provides unlimited amounts of earth and water runes as well as the autocast option when equipped.

Wielding a mystic mud staff is ideal for curse spells, as almost all of them use both water and earth runes. The precursor to this staff (Mud battlestaff) is only obtainable as a potential drop from Dagannoth Prime. For ironmen unable or unwilling to farm this boss until (and if) the staff is dropped, there are two alternatives in order to have infinite water & earth runes at the same time: using an earth staff with a tome of water that is charged with at least one soaked page, or using a water staff with a tome of earth that is charged with at least one soiled page. Given that only combat spells drain charges from the tomes, the staff + tome combo will provide unlimited water and earth runes when casting spells such as Bones to Peaches or Lvl-5 enchant (e.g. for training Magic at the Mage Training Arena) without the need for recharging the tome.

This staff can be created after the completion of the quest Scorpion Catcher by taking a mud battlestaff and 40,000 to Thormac. After completion of the Hard Kandarin Diary and Elite Kandarin Diary, Thormac will only require 30,000 or 20,000 respectively.
6568:
The obsidian cape is a piece of the Obsidian armour. Due to its lack of requirements and high defensive bonuses, it is a popular choice for players who lack a fire cape or a Cape of Accomplishment. It is one of few capes to count as warm clothing at the Wintertodt, although for this purpose some players may instead opt for the free, easily obtainable clue hunter cloak.

A reversed colour version may be obtained as a master clue scroll reward from Treasure Trails, which is statistically identical but the colours are inverted; it is red with black trim, as opposed to black with a red trim.

The cape of skulls provides equal bonuses while having the advantage of weighing 1.361 kg less, with the expense of a higher cost and that it gives the player a PK skull when equipped. The Tortugan shield is another good defensive cape that is considerably easier to acquire, particularly for ironman players.

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room.
6571:
An uncut onyx is the second rarest gem in Old School RuneScape, behind zenyte. It can be cut with a chisel at level 67 Crafting, granting 167.5 experience. This makes a cut onyx, which can be used to make very powerful jewellery. The cut onyx can also be used with a zenyte shard to create an uncut zenyte.

It can be purchased from TzHaar-Hur-Lek's Ore and Gem Store for 300,000 Tokkul (or 260,000 with any pair of Karamja gloves). Purchasing an uncut onyx does not register as a drop for the collection log. A common method to obtain this Tokkul as an ironman involves selling chaos runes to TzHaar-Mej-Roh's Rune Store; assuming a fully overstocked shop, this requires 28,889 chaos runes or 14,445 death runes with Karamja gloves.

There is also an extremely small chance of getting it from a bag full of gems. Each bag has 40 gems with each individual one having a 1/100,000,000 chance of being an onyx, making the chance per bag approximately 1/2,500,000.
6573:
An onyx is the second rarest gem in Old School RuneScape, behind zenyte (which is created from an onyx and a zenyte shard). Cutting an uncut onyx with a chisel requires level 67 Crafting and yields 167.5 experience. It can then be made into onyx jewellery by using a furnace along with a gold bar and a mould. Onyx can also be cut into 24 onyx bolt tips, though this is not recommended due to the bolt tips being worth significantly less than the onyx.

In order to create an uncut zenyte, a cut onyx must be fused with a zenyte shard in the wall of flames of the Temple of Marimbo Dungeon while holding a zombie monkey greegree (either variant). Doing so grants 15 crafting experience and gives the message: You reach into the extremely hot flames and fuse the zenyte and onyx together, forming an uncut zenyte.

Using a zenyte shard on a cut onyx gives the message: Only the intense heat of the flame pits beneath Ape Atoll can fuse the zenyte and onyx together.

Six of these are used to build a volcanic theme at level 85 Construction in a player's superior garden. In addition, one is used to build an obsidian decorative bench at level 98 Construction.
6575:
The onyx ring is made by using a gold bar, an onyx, and a ring mould on a furnace. It requires a Crafting level of 67 and provides 115 Crafting experience when made.

The onyx ring can be enchanted into a ring of stone through the use of the Lvl-6 Enchant spell at level 87 Magic, requiring 20 fire runes, 20 earth runes, and 1 cosmic rune.
6577:
An onyx necklace is a necklace made by using a gold bar, an onyx, and a necklace mould on a furnace. This requires 82 Crafting and yields 120 Crafting experience.

An onyx necklace can be enchanted into a berserker necklace with the Lvl-6 Enchant standard spell which requires 87 Magic, a cosmic rune, 20 earth runes, and 20 fire runes.
6579:
An onyx amulet (u) is the unstrung version of the regular onyx amulet. It is made by using a gold bar on a furnace, while having a cut onyx and an amulet mould in the inventory.

Level 90 Crafting is required to make one, and it grants 165 experience. When used with a ball of wool, it becomes an onyx amulet, giving 4 experience. After it is strung, it can be enchanted into an amulet of fury, which requires level 87 Magic and yields 97 experience.
6581:
The Onyx amulet is made by using an onyx and a gold bar on a furnace with an amulet mould in your inventory to create an onyx amulet (u). This requires a Crafting level of 90 and provides 165 Crafting experience when made. The amulet must then be strung before wearing by using a ball of wool or the String Jewellery spell from the Lunar spellbook. Stringing provides an additional 4 Crafting experience.

The Onyx amulet can be enchanted into an amulet of fury through the use of the Lvl-6 Enchant spell which requires level 87 Magic, or an enchant onyx tablet made from a lectern in a player-owned house.
6583: The ring of stone is an enchanted onyx ring. It can change the avatar of the player to look like that of a stone or empty Mining rock. If the player moves while under the effect, the effect will end. If another player mouses over or right-clicks on the player-turned-rock, the normal options will appear ("Walk here (Player name)," "Follow (Player name)," etc.).
6585:
The amulet of fury is one of the most powerful amulets available in Old School RuneScape, having equivalent attack bonuses to the amulet of glory with superior defensive, strength, and prayer bonuses, but without the ability to teleport the player. It can be made by enchanting an onyx amulet using Lvl-6 Enchant, requiring a Magic level of 87.

While it is generally regarded as the most versatile amulet with the best all-around bonuses, several amulets surpass it in certain areas.

A blood shard can be combined with the amulet to create an amulet of blood fury, which has a 20% chance of passively healing the player 30% of the damage they deal only while using melee. Its stats remain the same.

The amulet of fury can be decorated with a fury ornament kit. This produces an amulet of fury (or) but does not change its bonuses.

6636: Solus's hat is a trophy obtained by defeating the mage Solus Dellagar during the Wanted! quest. The player must give the hat to Sir Amik Varze in Falador to complete the quest. If the hat is lost, another can be obtained by asking Savant.
6638:
The colour wheel is a quest item in Mourning's End Part II and Song of the Elves. Although it plays no direct part in the quests, it can be used as a guide to the crystal puzzles in the Temple of Light and the library of Prifddinas as it provides clues to what colour of light needs to be sent to what part of the temple in order to unlock various doors there.

Red, green, and blue are the primary colours of the additive (projected) colour system, while cyan, magenta, and yellow are subtractive (reflected) colours. In the quest you will find various doors which have two colours attached to them, you are required to use prisms, mirrors and coloured crystals to direct a beam of light which is the correct colour to the various doors to unlock them. The doors will only unlock when they are hit with a beam of light which is complementary on the colour wheel. So for instance, the magenta door must be unlocked with a green beam of light.

The complements used in this spectrum of light are Magenta and Green, Cyan and Red, and Yellow and Blue.

If lost, it can be re-obtained by searching the dead guard slumped against the wall by the crystal dispenser in the temple of light, or by searching the pack by the crystal dispenser in the library.
6639: The hand mirror is a quest item used in the Mourning's End Part II and the Song of the Elves quest. It is obtained by pulling a lever in the Temple of Light near the start of the quest and is needed to solve the light puzzle in the Temple. As the player progresses through the puzzle they are rewarded with more mirrors in order to unlock more complicated parts of the puzzle. The mirrors redirect light to the place it needs to go if you put it at the right angle.
6640:
The red crystal is an unobtainable crystal released alongside the Mourning's End Part II quest. It was likely intended to be used during the light puzzle to recolour the light beams red.

It was presumably scrapped as it would make the puzzles requiring a red beam of light too easy. In the actual puzzle, red light can only be formed by passing yellow light through the magenta crystal.
6642:
Green crystal may refer to:

Green crystal (Mourning's End Part II)

Green crystal (Song of the Elves)

Green crystal (unobtainable)
6645:
The magenta crystal is an unobtainable item released alongside the Mourning's End Part II quest. Presumably, it would have been used in one of the light puzzles in the Temple of Light.

One of the pillars of light has a magenta crystal stuck inside it; however, it is inaccessible and cannot be inspected, unlike the green crystal pillar.
6646:
The horizontal fractured crystal is an item used in Mourning's End Part II. It is the first fractured crystal obtained in a chest during the quest. It splits a southbound light into a west-, south- and east-bound light. It used to open the magenta and yellow doors.

The vertical fractured crystal is the second fractured crystal obtained in a chest during the quest. It splits a west-bound light into a north-, west- and south-bound light. It is used to open the cyan and black doors.

The fractured crystals act like beam splitters and allow a beam of light to be split into three separate beams. Each crystal splits the light in different directions and must be used in a specific combination in order to be able to solve the puzzle.
6647:
The horizontal fractured crystal is an item used in Mourning's End Part II. It is the first fractured crystal obtained in a chest during the quest. It splits a southbound light into a west-, south- and east-bound light. It used to open the magenta and yellow doors.

The vertical fractured crystal is the second fractured crystal obtained in a chest during the quest. It splits a west-bound light into a north-, west- and south-bound light. It is used to open the cyan and black doors.

The fractured crystals act like beam splitters and allow a beam of light to be split into three separate beams. Each crystal splits the light in different directions and must be used in a specific combination in order to be able to solve the puzzle.
6648:
The item list is a quest item given to the player during the Mourning's End Part II quest by a dwarf named Thorgel at the end of the puzzle in the Temple of Light. Thorgel will give the player a Death talisman if the player delivers all of the items on the list to him.

There are 50 items on the list in total, so players must make a minimum of two trips to deliver them all. Players should remember to turn the mirror towards the cyan door if they're travelling through the Temple of Light to Thorgel, otherwise they will lock themselves out.

Note that it's possible to completely skip having to get the death talisman, and therefore having to do Thorgel's item list, by utilizing a Catalytic talisman to access the death altar instead. This is especially useful for ironmen, who may want to grind Guardians of the Rift in hopes of obtaining the catalytic talisman before doing the quest.
6649:
Edern's journal, or Journal of Nissyen Edern, can be found by searching the dead guard that is located outside the Temple of Light.

Through nine daily entries, the mourner Nissyen Edern wrote about joining the Death Guard, being deployed to West Ardougne, participating in the plague hoax, and investigating the tunnel to the Temple of Light.

After the quest, it can be found in the bookcase of your player-owned house or in the Grand Library in Prifddinas after completion of Song of the Elves.
6650: The blackened crystal is a quest item used in the Mourning's End Part II quest. It is obtained by using a chisel on a large black rock in the Temple of Light at the start of the quest. The player must give the crystal to Arianwyn, who will then turn it into a newly made crystal, which is needed to complete the final part of the quest. If a player has lost their blackened crystal, they must carve a new piece from the giant black crystal in order to get it back.
6651:
The newly made crystal is a quest item used in the Mourning's End Part II quest. It is obtained by using a chisel on a large black rock in the Temple of Light at the start of the quest and then giving this to Eluned after talking to Arianwyn. He will then turn it into an uncharged crystal which must be charged on the Death Altar in order to be able to seal the Temple for 1,000 years.

If lost, it can be reobtained directly from Arianwyn without needing to chisel the rock again.
6652:

6653:
The crystal trinket is a reward from Arianwyn after completing Mourning's End Part II. It is used to enter the Temple of Light after the quest. For players who have not completed Song of the Elves, this also requires mourner gear or a slayer ring since the entrance is via the Mourner headquarters' basement in West Ardougne. Players will still need the trinket after completing Song of the Elves.

If players lose it, they can obtain another from Arianwyn in Lletya. During and after Song of the Elves, it is instead found in a chest on the east side of the ground floor in Lletya in the main building.

If you try to enter the temple after completing the quest without the trinket, players will be bounced back and get the message "A strange force blocks your path." This is not necessary when crafting death runes through the Abyss, the Underground Pass, or through Guardians of the Rift.

6656:
The camo helmet is a possible reward from the Drill Demon random event.

This item can be stored in the fancy dress box of a costume room, as part of the camo outfit set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
6657:
The Camo top is an unobtainable version of the Camo top obtained from the Drill Demon random event. Originally, all pieces of Camo were tradeable, and could be turned into banknotes. However, due to players selling the pieces for very expensive prices (some up to several million) they were made untradeable 2 weeks later. Any noted versions existing ingame were transformed into this unique stackable variant.

As this change occurred prior to August 2007, the item has never been obtainable in Old School RuneScape.
6658:
The Camo bottoms are an unobtainable version of the Camo bottoms obtained from the Drill Demon random event. Originally, all pieces of Camo were tradeable, and could be turned into banknotes. However, due to players selling the pieces for very expensive prices (some up to several million) they were made untradeable 2 weeks later. Any noted versions existing ingame were transformed into this unique stackable variant.

As this change occurred prior to August 2007, the item has never been obtainable in Old School RuneScape.
6659:
The Camo helmet is an unobtainable version of the Camo helmet obtained from the Drill Demon random event. Originally, all pieces of Camo were tradeable, and could be turned into banknotes. However, due to players selling the pieces for very expensive prices (some up to several million) they were made untradeable 2 weeks later. Any noted versions existing ingame were transformed into this unique stackable variant.

As this change occurred prior to August 2007, the item has never been obtainable in Old School RuneScape.
6662: A broken fishing rod is found at Mudskipper Point, near the forlorn boot. At this time it has no use and cannot be repaired. It is possible that the rod may have belonged to a Mogre victim, (such as Skippy), given that the Mogres live nearby.
6664:
A fishing explosive is a consumable piece of Slayer equipment purchased from any Slayer master. It can lure mogres out of the water by using it on any of the three Ominous Fishing Spots in Mudskipper Point.

It can also be used to instantly awaken the Kraken boss by using it on the large whirlpool.
6665:
The mudskipper hat is an uncommon cosmetic item dropped by Mogres, which require 32 Slayer and completion of the mogre miniquest, or ocean Mogres in order to obtain. It is worn in the head slot and gives no bonuses. They are occasionally worn with flippers, another uncommon item dropped by both types of Mogres.

It can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player's costume room.
6666:
Flippers are an uncommon drop from mogres and sea mogres, which require 32 Slayer to kill. They are worn in the footwear slot and allow players to 'run' while in the underwater area beneath Fossil Island. Once the player enters the water wearing flippers, the ability to run remains active even if the player switches to other footwear.

If a weapon is equipped, you will not be able to 'run' while swimming. You must also be under 28 kg.

They can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player's costume room. They can also be stored in a tackle box.

Flippers can be made into dark flippers by talking to Patchy on Mos Le'Harmless while carrying a dark claw and 500 coins.
6668:
A fishbowl is an item that can be created with level 42 Crafting or received as a drop from Mogres. It can be filled with water and then with seaweed. With a filled fishbowl in the inventory, a tiny net can be purchased from Harry in Catherby for 10 gold which can then be used to catch a fish in the aquarium to get a pet fish. This is one of the tasks in the Easy Kandarin Diary.

It is also used in the Recipe for Disaster quest, in which players make it into a fishbowl helmet. This is worn in the helm slot and allows the player to go diving near Port Khazard.

It is also used in the Rum Deal quest, in which players receive a Fishbowl and net, which can be dismantled into a Fishbowl and a Big fishing net in order to obtain a fishbowl without having to go obtain molten glass first, which can be convenient for ironmen.

Fishbowls are sometimes used to train Magic with the Lunar spell Humidify, which fills any container in the player's inventory with water. Because the left-click option for a water-filled fishbowl is to empty it, the spell can be repeatedly cast with ease.

6673:
A fishbowl and net is created by using a big fishing net with an empty fishbowl. You can then untangle the fishbowl from the net, to get the separate components. It is used during Rum Deal to catch sluglings.

It cannot be stored in the tackle box.
6674: A tiny net is used to obtain a pet fish, can be stored in a tackle box, and can be purchased from Harry in Catherby for 10 gold, provided the player has a fishbowl filled with both water and seaweed in their inventory. When meeting this criteria, a dialogue option about getting a fish and buying a tiny net becomes an option. A Fishing level of 10 or higher is required. Obtaining a pet fish from Harry is required for the Easy Kandarin Diary.
6677: Guam in a box is made by adding ground guam to an empty fish food box. To obtain an empty box, players must talk to Harry in Catherby with a filled fishbowl in their inventory. To make the ground guam, the player must use a guam leaf with a pestle and mortar. Adding ground seaweed then turns it into fish food which can be fed to a player's pet fish. This is currently the only way to obtain fish food, other than picking it up in Draynor Manor. Making it provides no experience in any skills.
6678:
Guam in a box? is an unobtainable item added to the game with the release of pet fish. It is identical to the real Guam in a box, except with a different name and usable by free to play players.

It is unknown what purpose, if any, the item was intended to serve.
6681:
Ground guam is made by using a pestle and mortar on a guam leaf. It is used to make fish food by combining it with ground seaweed on an empty box.

Ground guam cannot be used to make potions, such as attack potions.

With a pestle and mortar in your inventory and a Herblore level of 19, you can use a ground guam on a stack of (at least 15) swamp tar to make 15 guam tar, granting 30 Herblore experience.
6683: Ground seaweed is seaweed that has been ground with a pestle and mortar. It may then be combined with ground guam by using both on an empty fish food box to make fish food. The fish food is for pet fish.
6696:
Ice coolers can be purchased from any Slayer master, and are used to finish off desert lizards that have less than 5 Hitpoints. When used, the lizard shudders and collapses from the freezing water, consuming the ice cooler. Using an ice cooler on a desert lizard with 5 or more Hitpoints has no effect but will still consume an ice cooler. It is recommended to bring an excess due to the possibility of wasting coolers.

They can also be used to craft empty fish crates, used in Sailing deep sea trawling.

Sulphur Lizards and Grimy Lizards do not require ice coolers to finish off.
6697:
A pat of butter is a food ingredient made with a Cooking skill of 38. Players can make one by churning a bucket of milk, which gives 40.5 Cooking experience, or a pot of cream, which gives 22.5 Cooking experience, in a dairy churn.

A pat of butter is used by adding it to a baked potato to make a potato with butter. After adding the butter, players can then add additional toppings.
6699:
Burnt potato is the result of accidentally burning a raw potato while attempting to make a baked potato. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 41.

The burnt potato has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.
6701:
A baked potato is a type of food that heals 4 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by baking a potato on a cooking range, requiring level 7 Cooking and granting 15 experience when successful. Potatoes cannot be cooked on fires.

Players may burn the potato, resulting in a burnt potato. Players burn potatoes less at higher levels, and will stop burning them entirely at Cooking level 41.
6703:
A potato with butter is a food item and cooking ingredient that heals 14 Hitpoints when eaten and is consumed in one bite. It can be made with a Cooking level of 39 by using a baked potato on a pat of butter or a pat of not garlic butter. Doing so grants 40 Cooking experience and does not require use of a fire or range.

A potato with butter can be combined with various other toppings like tuna and corn or mushroom & onion to make food that restores more hitpoints.
6705:
Potato with cheese is a food item that heals 16 Hitpoints when eaten and is consumed in one bite. It can be made with a Cooking level of 47 by using a piece of cheese on a potato with butter. Doing so grants 40 Cooking experience and does not require the use of a fire or range.

They are also sold by Lidio in the Warriors' Guild who has a stock of 10.

It is a popular food choice among mid-level players due to its low cost, alongside reasonable accessibility at the Warriors' Guild.
6707:
Camulet is a reward from Enakhra's Lament. When equipped, its wearer can speak to certain camels found in Al Kharid and throughout the Kharidian desert.

The Camulet has four charges to teleport to the desert, inside Enakhra's Temple near Lazim. With the hard Desert Diary completed, the teleport destination can be switched to the temple entrance near the quarry.

Using the Camulet to teleport to Enakhra's Temple is a requirement for the Medium Desert Diary.

To recharge the Camulet, players must use a bucket of Ugthanki dung on it, which will fully recharge the amulet. Players can receive dung by speaking to certain camels (after partial completion of My Arm's Big Adventure) while wearing the Camulet, such as Al the Camel, who can be found outside the bank in Al Kharid. You'll also need a bucket to collect the dung.

If lost, it can be retrieved by speaking with Lazim. Multiple Camulets may be obtained using the drop trick, but when a charge on one is consumed it is subtracted from all Camulets in the player's possession (similar to the way ring of recoil charges work).

The player can pay Lazim 1,000,000 coins to have him enhance the Camulet to grant unlimited teleport charges instead of just 4. The upgrade is permanent and will take effect on other Camulets in the player's possession and on replacements given by Lazim should the player lose one.
6710:
Blindweed seed is a quest item that the player must grow during the Rum Deal quest. It is planted in the Blindweed farming patch on the south-eastern part of Braindeath Island. Players do not need a watering can or a form of compost after planting the blindweed seed.

A nearby gardener will not watch over your growing blindweed, but blindweed cannot become diseased.

When harvested it yields blindweed, which is the first ingredient of the unsanitary swill that the player must make during the quest. Planting a blindweed seed grants 32 Farming experience and harvesting the blindweed grants 45 Farming experience.
6711: Blindweed is a quest item grown by the player during the Rum Deal quest, and is grown by planting a blindweed seed in the Farming patch on Braindeath Island. The plant is one of the ingredients of the unsanitary swill, which the player must make during the quest.
6712:
The Bucket of water is a quest item used during the Rum Deal quest. It is different to an ordinary bucket of water in that it must be filled from a stagnant lake near Braindeath Island Volcano, on Braindeath Island. The symbol of the stagnant lake is the normal symbol for a water source but has a bit of grey in it.

The bucket of water is then used to make the unsanitary swill that the player needs to continue the quest. Trying to obtain it after the quest will result in the message You do not need any more of that stuff!.
6715:
Sluglings are a quest item used during the Rum Deal quest. They are believed to be young sea slugs, as confirmed by Captain Braindeath.

Players catch sluglings by using a fishbowl and net in a fishing spot on Braindeath Island. They are one of the ingredients of the unsanitary swill that the player must make during the quest. Players are not awarded any Fishing experience when catching sluglings.

After the quest, any sluglings remaining in inventory will disappear, and an attempt to fish for sluglings triggers the response, "You have no need to do that any more."

They appear to have mind-controlling properties. Using them on Captain Braindeath triggers dialogue where the player says the sluglings are telling them to do "bad things", prompting Braindeath to stomp on them to release the player from their hypnotic trance.
6716:
Karamthulhu are a squid-like species that are sometimes obtained while fishing for slugs during the Rum Deal quest. They are also dropped by zombie pirates and zombie swabs on Braindeath Island.

Karamthulhus can be used during Rum Deal in addition to sluglings to make unsanitary swill. After the quest, any Karamthulhus remaining in the inventory will disappear, and an attempt to fish for them triggers the response, "You have no need to do that any more." Players will still be able to obtain a Karamthulhu as a drop from the aforementioned zombie pirates and swabs after having completed the quest.
6717: Karamthulhu is an unobtainable item released alongside the Rum Deal quest. It is very similar to the obtainable karamthulhu item, but has a different inventory icon, value, and examine text. While its examine text suggests it was intended to be linked to the unreleased Karamthulhu pet, the pet NPC was linked to the obtainable karamthulhu item instead, leaving the purpose of this one unknown.
6718:
The fever spider body is a quest item used during the Rum Deal quest. It can only be obtained by killing a fever spider in the basement of the rum factory on Braindeath Island and is one of the ingredients of the unsanitary swill that the player must make during the quest.

This cannot be used on an arrow shaft or thatch spar to produce a spider on shaft or spider on stick.
6719: Unsanitary swill, sometimes referred to as 'rum', is a player made quest item brewed during the Rum Deal quest. It is made by adding blindweed, stagnant water, sluglings, and a fever spider body to a brewing device on Braindeath Island. It is used on Captain Donnie who doesn't become drunk, but he does tell you the name 'Rabid Jack'.
6720:
Slayer gloves are a piece of Slayer equipment used to fight fever spiders, and require a Slayer level of 42 to be worn. If the gloves are not equipped, the spiders will damage the player for 12.5% of their base hitpoints, as well as inflict disease. When worn, they resemble a lighter brown hue similar to that of normal leather gloves.

They can be purchased from any Slayer Master for 200 coins.
6722:
Zombie heads can be obtained by completing one of the Halloween events that occur once per year. This also rewards the player with all other holiday items associated with Halloween.

Previously, they were obtainable during the 2013 Rare Drops event (from 26 August to 2 September) as part of a rare item drop.

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room. A lost zombie head can also be recovered by digging in the Lumbridge Swamp with a spade.
6724:
The seercull is a Fremennik bow that requires a Ranged level of 50 to wield, and fires arrows up to Amethyst. Compared to a magic shortbow, it has a slower rate of fire and a different special attack which is more effective against mages. In addition, its normal and rapid fire attacks have one more range than that of a shortbow, and its long range attack is equivalent to that of a composite bow. It is a comparable weapon to the Magic comp bow.

The name can be attributed to the combination of the word seer (another word for "mage" or "wizard") and the word cull (another word for "kill"), in other words, the mage-killer. This is a fitting name because of the effect of its special attack and its examine text.
6728: Dagannoth-king bonemeal is an item that is used for worship at the Ectofuntus. It consists of a pot filled with dagannoth bones that have been crushed in the bone grinder at the Ectofuntus.
6729:
Dagannoth bones are bones dropped by Dagannoth Rex, Dagannoth Prime, and Dagannoth Supreme. They are not obtained as drops from regular Dagannoth, who only drop standard bones.

Dagannoth bones give 125 Prayer experience when buried. This can be increased by offering the bones in different ways:

375 XP when casting Sinister Offering.

375 XP when offered at the sacred bone burner after the appropriate faith level has been achieved.

437.5 XP when offered at a gilded altar with two burners lit.

500 XP when offered at the Ectofuntus in the form of dagannoth bonemeal.

500 XP when blessed and broken down into blessed bone shards and offered at the libation bowl, or 600 XP when offered with a jug of blessed sunfire wine. Virilis outside the altar will exchange noted bones for 10 coins each.

875 XP on average when offered at the Chaos Temple in the Wilderness. Each offering gives 437.5 XP, which is the same as the gilded altars with two burners lit, but with an additional 50% chance to not consume the bones.

Dagannoth bones cannot be turned into peaches via the Bones to Peaches spell.

If players have completed the elite Fremennik Diary, the bones will be dropped as bank notes. This can be disabled or re-enabled by talking to Thorodin.
6731:
The Seers ring is one of the four Fremennik rings, and is dropped by the Dagannoth Prime in the Waterbirth Island Dungeon.

It can be imbued using 650,000 Nightmare Zone reward points or 325,000 with the hard tier of Combat Achievements, 260 Soul Wars Zeal Tokens, or a Scroll of Imbuing, purchased for 200 Emir's Arena reward points, which doubles the magic attack and defence bonuses, and increases the magic damage bonus from 0.2% to 0.5%.

Players can use a chisel on the seers ring to create a seers icon after completing Desert Treasure II. This process requires 80 Crafting (boostable), and is part of the process for creating the magus ring.
6733:
The archers ring is one of the Fremennik rings and is dropped by the Dagannoth Supreme in the Waterbirth Island Dungeon. It increases the player's ranged accuracy and ranged defence when worn.

It can be imbued using 650,000 Nightmare Zone reward points or 325,000 with the hard tier of Combat Achievements, 260 Soul Wars Zeal Tokens, or a Scroll of Imbuing, purchased for 200 Emir's Arena reward points, which doubles its bonuses.

Players can use a chisel on the archers ring to create an archer icon after completing Desert Treasure II. This process requires 80 Crafting (boostable), and is part of the process for creating the venator ring.
6735:
The warrior ring is one of the four Fremennik rings and is dropped by Dagannoth Rex. The Fremennik rings are among the few rings that provide combat stat bonuses.

It can be imbued using 650,000 Nightmare Zone reward points or 325,000 with the hard tier of Combat Achievements, 260 Soul Wars Zeal Tokens, or a Scroll of Imbuing, purchased for 200 Emir's Arena reward points, which doubles its bonuses.

Players can use a chisel on the warrior ring to create a warrior icon after completing Desert Treasure II. This process requires 80 Crafting (boostable), and is part of the process for creating the bellator ring.
6737:
The berserker ring is the strength bonus variant of the Fremennik rings and is dropped by Dagannoth Rex in the Waterbirth Island Dungeon. The Fremennik rings are some of the very few rings to give stat bonuses. Group Ironmen who do not have individual prestige require at least 1 Dagannoth Rex kill before they are able to wear this item.

It can be imbued into a berserker ring (i), doubling its bonuses, by using 650,000 Nightmare Zone reward points or 325,000 with the hard tier of Combat Achievements, 260 Soul Wars Zeal Tokens, or a scroll of imbuing purchased for 200 Emir's Arena reward points.

The berserker ring is one of a handful of rings that provide a strength bonus. Thus, it is commonly used in melee setups because strength bonus raises the player's maximum hit, which is usually more beneficial than accuracy for lowering kill times.

The ring makes the biggest difference when facing monsters with low Defence, but in general even against higher defence targets it will provide better DPS than rings which only provide accuracy bonuses. In specific situations where long-term DPS is not a concern (for example special attacks or boss mechanics), if crush accuracy is needed the Tyrannical ring should be used; for slash accuracy a warrior or bellator ring should be used.

Players can use a chisel on the berserker ring to create a berserker icon after completing Desert Treasure II. This process requires 80 Crafting (boostable), and is part of the process for creating the ultor ring.
6739:
The dragon axe is the second best axe in the game after its direct upgrade, the crystal axe, and is tied with the 3rd Age axe. It is 10% more efficient at chopping logs than the rune axe.

Like all axes, it is both a weapon (requiring 60 Attack to wield) and a tool (requiring 61 Woodcutting to use).

As with most dragon equipment, the dragon axe cannot be made from raw materials using the Smithing skill.
6743:
The dragon axe head is an unobtainable item that was originally used in the axe handle random event. The axe head would become detached from the player's axe while Woodcutting. To fix their axe, players had to collect the axe head off the ground and reattach it to the axe handle.

As dragon axes were worth over 2 million at the time, players who were not paying constant attention risked substantial losses. Curiously, although a special version of the Dragon axe handle was added in 2006, it was still possible to combine a Dragon axe head and a regular Axe handle.

A similar event used to happen to players while Mining, but with a pickaxe head and pickaxe handle.

Axe heads were removed in an update on 17 July 2007, prior to the release of Old School RuneScape, so have never been obtainable.
6745:
Silverlight is a magical sword used in Demon Slayer and Shadow of the Storm. It is a demonbane sword that is very effective against demonic creatures. As it is a silver weapon, it is also effective against most vampyres. It is obtained by bringing the three Silverlight keys to Sir Prysin during Demon Slayer.

In Demon Slayer, it is used to defeat Delrith. In Shadow of the Storm, it is dyed black using black dye, and later transforms into Darklight when it gets stained with the blood of Agrith-Naar.

It can be mounted on the wall in the quest hall of a player-owned house.
6746:
Darklight is a quest item used in Shadow of the Storm. It is a demonbane weapon created from the sword Silverlight. In that quest, it transformed into Darklight after being used to slay the demon Agrith-Naar, which coats it in his blood.

Both Silverlight and Darklight can be mounted on the wall of a Quest Hall in a player-owned house at 42 Construction.

If lost, Darklight can be reclaimed from Sir Prysin for a cost of 1,000 coins.
6750:
A black desert shirt is an item of clothing that players may find useful when doing the Shadow of the Storm quest. They can make it by using black dye on a normal desert shirt. This can also be done with a desert robe to create a black desert robe.

The quest requires players to be wearing at least three black garments, in order to look evil. Players may already be wearing a desert shirt (since the main part of the quest takes place in the Kharidian Desert), and black mushrooms can be found locally.

This makes it a convenient choice to make the ink and use it to dye the shirt, though players will also need an empty vial and a pestle and mortar with them.

The black desert robes will not protect players from the desert heat effect. This is stated in a warning message shown when attempting to dye them.
6752:
A black desert robe is an item of clothing that players may find useful when doing the Shadow of the Storm quest. They can make it by using black dye on a normal desert robe. This can also be done with a desert shirt to create a black desert shirt.

The quest requires players to be wearing at least three black garments, in order to look evil. Players may already be wearing a set of desert robes (since the main part of the quest takes place in the Kharidian Desert), and black mushrooms can be found locally.

This makes it a convenient choice to make the ink and use it to dye the robes, though players will also need an empty vial and a pestle and mortar with them.

The black desert robes will not protect players from the desert heat effect. This is stated in a warning message shown when attempting to dye them.
6754:
The enchanted key is a quest item that is used to locate treasure rather than unlocking things. This key is featured in the Making History quest. It is also used in The Enchanted Key miniquest to locate additional rewards after completing the quest. Once the miniquest is completed, the key disappears.

If the key is destroyed before completing all the treasures, another key can be obtained from the Silver Merchant for 500 coins. However, if the player has received and since destroyed the steel key ring, they will need to re-obtain the ring before the merchant will sell them the key.

This key can be placed on the steel key ring. Note, if placed on your key ring its name changes to "Key" with the description "Key to find hidden treasure!".
6755:
Drozal's Journal is a book that players find in a chest during the quest Making History. After completing the quest, they can find it in the bookcase of their player-owned houses.

The journal details the private thoughts of a Zamorakian individual called Drozal, who never appears in the game. His entries span a period of at least 60 days (see below), and give an overview of his somewhat evil behaviour. This includes poisoning the drinking water of the people of Ardougne (this seems to refer specifically to West Ardougne), causing them to break out in boils.

Since the entries are dated, this journal in itself also tells us the names of two (probably consecutive) months in the world of Gielinor. These are "Bennath" (which has at least 32 days) and "Raktuber" (which has at least 28 days).
6756:

6762:
The Saradomin mjolnir is a two-handed weapon. There are no level requirements to wield this item. To obtain one, a player can either find it during The Enchanted Key miniquest or trade with another player.

Each mjolnir can only be obtained once per account, as the Enchanted key will disintegrate after the player finds all of the treasure. Once this happens, the key cannot be re-obtained.

As its name implies, the Saradomin mjolnir is affiliated with the god Saradomin. It is tipped with a symbol associated with Saradomin.

It can be equipped for protection against the Saradomin followers in the God Wars Dungeon.

6766:
Cat antipoison is created by the Apothecary from a bucket of milk, marrentill and unicorn horn dust. It is used in the Ratcatchers quest for curing Pox's poison. This item can only be obtained during the quest.

This potion uses the same ingredients as normal antipoison, except that milk replaces the vial of water.
6767:
Books are items obtained in quests and elsewhere in Old School RuneScape. Most books can be read by players, which provides information ranging from lore to information on game mechanics.

When a player reads a book, an interface will appear to display the book's contents, and their character will be seen reading a green (sometimes yellow) book.
6768:
Poisoned cheese is used in the Ratcatchers quest to poison rats in 4 rat holes in the warehouse in the south-west corner of South-east Varrock. It is created by using rat poison on cheese.

When attempting to eat it, the player's character will state: "Um... let me think about this one. No! That would be stupid." Due to it not being consumable, it has no use outside of the quest.

Attempting to place the poisoned cheese in a rat hole after the completion of the quest would result in the message "Putting things in poisoned rat holes isn't my idea of fun."

Using it on a Rat trap (near the Rat Pits) will yield a message in your chatbox saying that it's an over kill and normal cheese will work fine.
6770:
Directions are an item given to the player by Jimmy Dazzler during the Ratcatchers quest. They are used to locate a house in which the player must deal with a rat problem. Choosing to follow them results in the player being teleported instantly to their current checkpoint, initially just inside the garden gates. They cannot be used outside of Ardougne, with your character saying, "These directions are from Ardougne, it would be much easier to find the place if I left from there."

After completion of the quest, players can no longer gain access to the house again, with your character saying, "I don't want to go there again. I barely managed to get out unseen."
6771: A pot of weeds is a quest item used during the Ratcatchers quest. It is made by adding normal farming weeds to an empty pot. Using a tinderbox on the pot will turn it into a smouldering pot, which can then be used to smoke out rats from their holes during the Smokin' Joe section of the quest.
6772:
A smouldering pot is a quest item used in the Ratcatchers quest. It is created by using a tinderbox on a pot of weeds. The player can then use it to help Smokin' Joe clear out rats from their holes.

Smokin' Joe offers his own pot for the player to use. But due to the green phlegm that Joe has coughed up into the pot, the player refuses and decides to make their own smouldering pot for use.

After helping Smokin' Joe, the smouldering pot becomes useless and can be safely disposed of.
6785:
The Statuette is an icon of the goddess Elidinis and is obtained during the Spirits of the Elid quest. The statuette is said to have been made by Elidinis herself and was given to Nardarine, future founder of Nardah who swore loyalty to Elidinis, after Elidinis offered to save her from the desert heat.

The statuette must be retrieved from the evil genie in the crevice to the west of Nardah. The genie will give the player the statuette if they present him with the sole of the mayor of Nardah.

Once the statuette is returned to the Elidinis Statuette, players may recharge their Prayer there to receive +2 bonus Prayer points as well as a boost to hitpoints, and their special attack energy and run energy will be fully restored as well. Any poison or venom the player has will also be cured.
6786:
The Robe of Elidinis (top) is a robe top that is required in the Spirits of the Elid quest. The robes are created by using a needle on the torn robes found in the shrine in Nardah during or after the quest. The player must wear the robes in order to enter the Water Ravine Dungeon farther north along the River Elid. After the quest, players may use the robes to continue to access the dungeon, although few do.

You can get a new set of robes by searching the cupboard again for the torn robes and then remaking them with needle and thread. You cannot get another set of torn robes if you already have a set of torn robes or Robes of Elidinis in your possession (including in the bank). However, you can use the Drop trick to get extra sets by dropping your robes before searching the cupboard. This gets you a new set of torn robes, which you can mend when you wish.

Wearing the robe top will delay the onset of desert heat by 12 seconds.

6794:
Choc-ice can be bought from a local vendor named Rokuh in Nardah, who runs Rok's Chocs Box. They are sold for 30 coins each, and heal 7 Hitpoints when eaten. If a bar of choc-ice is brought while venturing through the desert, it will automatically be consumed when the desert heat sets in, providing both its healing effect as well as quenching the player's thirst. That said, manually eating choc-ice does not reset nor delay the onset of desert heat. Choc-ice can nevertheless come in handy as an alternative to bringing waterskins to the desert. Although waterskins are refillable and provide up to 4 uses each, choc-ice has the advantages of being essentially weightless and serving a dual purpose as a food. This can be particularly useful when scaling the Agility Pyramid.

Waterskins have priority over choc-ices when under the influence of desert heat, and will be consumed first if the player is carrying both in their inventory. Bars of choc-ice can also occasionally melt while in the desert, regardless of any other measures taken to combat the heat, prompting the message: Your choc ice evaporates in the desert heat.

Choc-ices were invented by Rokuh, who sold them to the people of Nardah when their town had become cursed and they could no longer draw water from its wells. Rokuh bought a box imbued with a powerful ice spell, ensuring its contents would never melt, even under the harsh desert sun. He used this magical box (possibly an ice cooler) to store his new invention: a confection made of an iced cream coated with a layer of chocolate, which he called choc-ice. Even after the curse has been lifted from Nardah upon completion of the Spirits of the Elid, its inhabitants remain eager consumers of the treat.

Karamel, an enemy from Recipe for Disaster, drops a choc-ice when she is killed.
6796:
The lamp is a reward obtained from several random events or by opening an Intricate Pouch that differs from those awarded by quests. While these lamps cannot be traded or banked, rubbing one gives the option of adding experience to any skill a player chooses. The amount given is ten times their skill level of choice (e.g. a skill at level 21 would give 210 experience).

Lamps always go to your gravestone on death unless protected.
6798:
The earth warrior champion scroll is an extremely rare drop from earth warriors. It contains a challenge from the Earth Warrior Champion. In order to be eligible to receive the scroll, players must have at least 32 quest points and be on a members world.

Bring this scroll to Larxus in the basement of Champions' Guild. Go down the Champion Statue and through the portcullis to fight the Earth Warrior Champion as part of the Champions' Challenge minigame. During the fight, players cannot use prayers of any kind. Once defeated, you may exit through the same entrance. The scroll will be consumed upon defeat of the earth warrior champion.

Like all champion scrolls, this scroll will be removed from the player's inventory once the challenge has been completed. It is however possible to keep the scroll by dropping it before entering the arena and defeating the champion, then picking it up after the challenge has been completed.

6806:
The skeleton champion scroll is an extremely rare drop from skeletons. It contains a challenge from the Skeleton Champion. In order to be eligible to receive the scroll, players must have at least 32 quest points and be on a members world.

By bringing this scroll to Larxus in the basement of Champions' Guild, players may fight the Skeleton Champion as part of the Champions' Challenge minigame. During the fight, players can only use ranged attacks.

Players wanting to obtain this scroll may wish to prioritise getting the Lesser demon champion scroll first, because when cannoning demons in the Crandor and Karamja Dungeon, occasionally skeletons may be killed as well. It is recommended to turn on collection log notifications in the settings, as to not miss these drops. Additionally, this champion scroll may also be obtained by killing Skeletons in the Barrows dungeons, meaning that collection log hunters may wish to prioritise the Barrows collection log over the Skeleton log. The same applies to Vet'ion and Calvar'ion, which are also able to drop the scroll. It should be noted that both Barrows and the mentioned Wilderness bosses make grinding for this challenge scroll significantly longer, though.

Some of the best locations for cannoning skeletons include the Bone Yard, which is a multicombat area with 14 spread out skeleton spawns in the Wilderness, or the Digsite Dungeon, which is a single-combat area with 10 skeleton spawns. Alternatively, for players wishing to train their Magic or Ranged, the Ape Atoll Dungeon may serve as a useful location for obtaining this scroll, by killing them with Chinchompas or Barrage spells.

Like all champion scrolls, this scroll will be removed from the player's inventory once the challenge has been completed. It is however possible to keep the scroll by dropping it before entering the arena and defeating the champion, then picking it up after the challenge has been completed.
6807:
The zombie champion scroll is an extremely rare drop from Zombies. It contains a challenge from the Zombies Champion. In order to be eligible to receive the scroll, players must have at least 32 quest points and be on a members world.

By bringing this scroll to Larxus in the basement of Champions' Guild, players may fight the Zombies Champion as part of the Champions' Challenge minigame. During the fight, players can only use melee or ranged attacks.

The Graveyard of Shadows in the Wilderness is the best spot for obtaining the scroll, due to the amount of zombies that reside there. While the area is not multicombat, a cannon may be used to speed up kills. Avoid carrying decent gear/cannonballs as player killers may appear.

A good place outside the Wilderness to collect this scroll is the basement of the Wizards' Guild in Yanille (requires level 66 Magic; boosts allowed). The zombies are in an inaccessible cage and need to be fought with magic or ranged. Runes for Telekinetic Grab are also needed to collect the scroll if it drops here. Players also looking for hard clues can leverage the aggressive and burst-able armoured zombies in Zemouregal's Base, or the stronger variants in Zemouregal's Fort.

If getting collection logs is a priority, the zombie champion scroll can be obtained from multiple monsters that also have other collection log unlocks possible from them, namely:

The Mask of Ranul from Undead Druids.

The Zombie axe and Zombie helmet from Armoured zombies.

The Teleport anchoring scroll from Zombie pirates.

Additionally, the Shades of Mort'ton minigame may spawn Undead Zealots that can also drop a challenge scroll, although these do not need to be killed during the activity.

Like all champion scrolls, this scroll will be removed from the player's inventory once the challenge has been completed. It is however possible to keep the scroll by dropping it before entering the arena and defeating the champion, then picking it up after the challenge has been completed.
6809:
Granite legs are platelegs which require 50 defence and 50 strength to be worn. They can only be obtained by killing Skeletal Wyverns.

Compared to dragon platelegs and rune platelegs, they have a greater ranged defence bonus at the cost of worse melee defences. They also have 10 more negative magic attack bonus compared to metal platelegs and plateskirts, which can be beneficial for splashing.
6810: Wyvern bonemeal is an item that is used for worship at the Ectofuntus. It consists of a pot filled with wyvern bones that have been crushed in the bone grinder at the Ectofuntus.
6812:
Wyvern bones are dropped by Wyverns, which give 72 Prayer experience when buried. This can be increased by offering the bones in different ways:

216 XP when casting Sinister Offering.

216 XP when offered at the sacred bone burner after the appropriate faith level has been achieved.

252 XP when offered at a gilded altar with two burners lit.

288 XP when offered at the Ectofuntus in the form of wyvern bonemeal.

290 XP when blessed and broken down into blessed bone shards and offered at the libation bowl, or 348 XP when offered with a jug of blessed sunfire wine. Virilis outside the altar will exchange noted bones for 10 coins each.

504 XP on average when offered at the Chaos Temple in the Wilderness. Each offering gives 252 XP, which is the same as the gilded altar with two burners lit, but with an additional 50% chance to not consume the bones.
6818:
The bow-sword is required in the Devious Minds quest, for the monk at the Paterdomus Temple on the way to Canifis. According to the monk, they learned of the weapon from someone came from the "lands to the far east", as the design originated from there.

Although the bow sword offers a wield option, the player unfortunately can't wield it, as attempting to do so produces an exclamation that "It's a bow and a sword...how am I supposed to use this?!" Asking the monk to teach the player how to use it produces the comment that "it's a foreign weapon" and "perhaps later" one of their warriors can teach them.

To make the bow-sword, players need to use a mithril 2h sword on Doric's whetstone, directly east of Taverley to produce a slender blade, then adding a bow string to it. This entire process requires 65 Smithing and 50 Fletching. Players should take care not to die with this item, as it is lost on death and must be created again.

The bow-sword is later used by the assassin to kill several Monks of Entrana and snatch the relic.

The assassin makes further appearances during Secrets of the North and Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire, using the bow-sword to fend off his opponents.
6819: The large pouch is created when using the orb on a regular large pouch during the Devious Minds quest. It is used as a teleport beacon for a mysterious character later known as the Assassin to steal a relic from the Entrana church. This item is lost on death.
6820:
The relic is an unobtainable item seen in the cutscene during Devious Minds. Players doing the quest unwittingly help an assassin reach Entrana, at which point he slays the monks who were protecting it and steals it. After the theft, the High Priest tells the player to inform Sir Tiffy Cashien of the events. Sir Tiffy tells the player that he will be "in touch" later. It appears to have a star of Saradomin carved on it.

The item briefly appears on the floor during the cutscene after being dropped by a Monk, before it is taken by the Assassin. However, it cannot be taken by the player.

It is revealed during Desert Treasure II that the relic is one of the three artefacts Azzanadra had been searching for in order to contact Zaros, alongside the Strange icon and the Frostenhorn. The relic has presumably been destroyed by Sliske after the events of Devious Minds.
6821:
An orb is given to the player by the hooded monk near Paterdomus during the Devious Minds quest. The player must put it into a large or colossal pouch to be able to smuggle it to Entrana, and even then they must use the Abyss to enter the Law Altar to be able to enter Entrana. While it is possible to remove the orb from the pouch on Entrana (or elsewhere), the player will not be able to place it on the altar except in the pouch.

Late towards the end of the quest, the player discovers that the orb is, in fact, a teleport beacon used by an assassin to infiltrate Entrana and attack a congregation of Monks of Saradomin during a special ceremony.

The orb is always lost upon death.

A peach is an untradeable fruit that restores 8 Hitpoints when eaten. It can only be created by casting Bones to Peaches or a bones to peaches tablet on bones. To cast Bones to Peaches, players must unlock the spell as a reward from the Mage Training Arena.

Due to offering a technically-unlimited food source, peaches are commonly used on long training or bossing trips far from a bank, such as in the God Wars Dungeon.

Peaches can also be used in place of bananas in the Creature Graveyard, giving double the amount of pizazz points.

When creating 27 peaches at once using a mud staff and buying bones, the resulting food costs 48.37 per peach and 6.05 per hitpoint healed.

The player can talk to the hat to check the number of points they have in each activity. It replies with a grumpy attitude but will tell the player anyway. The hat has a maximum point storage limit, as follows:

8,000 Graveyard Pizazz Points

8,000 Telekinetic Pizazz Points

16,000 Alchemist Pizazz Points

32,000 Enchantment Pizazz Points

Note that destroying the hat will not cause the player to lose their pizazz points.

A mage's book is a book in the shield slot, requiring 60 Magic to wield. It is tied with the ancient wyvern shield for the third-best Magic attack bonus in the shield slot, behind the arcane spirit shield and the Elidinis' ward (f), but it has no Melee or Ranged defensive bonuses. The mage's book is popular among combat pures because there is no required Defence level. It gives a Magic damage bonus of 2%.

It can be obtained by playing the Mage Training Arena minigame for:

It is the most expensive reward available from the Mage Training Arena minigame. It takes 5.3 hours on average to acquire the mage's book when playing efficiently and using the best spells. Acquiring the book yields a profit of 3,356,160 while using the appropriate staves.

For every 100 coins inserted in the coin collector, players will gain 1 alchemist's pizazz point.

They can be made by casting an enchant jewellery spell on icosahedrons, cylinders, cubes, pentamids, and dragonstones found within the chamber. Orbs can be deposited in the hole in the centre of the chamber. Every 20 orbs deposited will reward the player with three blood, death, or cosmic runes.

Dragonstones can be found in the Enchanting Chamber of the Mage Training Arena. They cannot be taken outside of the chamber. They provide pizazz points when any enchantment spell is used on them.

Six dragonstones spawn around the room every five minutes, which players can enchant at any level. Additionally, there is a 1/32 chance of finding a dragonstone when searching a pile of shapes. The stones give more bonus pizazz points depending on the level of enchantment the player uses. Points gained per dragonstone is equal to two times the enchantment level used; therefore, the maximum points available for enchanting one of the six dragonstones is 14 (using Lvl-7 Enchant).
