Pink dye is a members-only dye. It is initially created as part of The Hand in the Sand quest by using redberries and white berries on bottled water. It can then be used on a lantern lens to make a rose-tinted lens, which is also required for the While Guthix Sleeps quest.

After completing The Hand in the Sand, players can buy more of it from Betty in the Magic Shop in Port Sarim for 20 coins each. The dye does not appear in her usual store, and can only be bought through dialogue with her.

Pink dyes can be used as an ingredient to train Construction and Farming through building Zen themes, costing only 3GP/XP and giving up to 252k experience per hour in both Construction and Farming. Buying a full inventory of pink dyes from Betty and depositing at the Port Sarim deposit box takes between 1 minute and 45 seconds up to 2 minutes, obtaining up to 800-925 pink dyes per hour.

Pink dye cannot be used to dye a blue or black skirt into a pink skirt.

Coins (also referred to as gold pieces, gp, gold, or simply money) are the most common form of currency in Gielinor. They are used among players and non-player characters alike to exchange for items and services.

Players often refer to one thousand (1,000) coins as 1k and one million (1,000,000) coins as 1m or 1mil. Both can be applied to larger numbers, for example, 10m refers to ten million coins (10,000,000). 1b or 1bil refers to one billion coins (1,000,000,000).

Alchemy spells, which create coins, cannot be cast on coins. If a player attempts it, a message will inform the player that Coins are already made of gold. Curiously, other items made of gold, such as gold ore and gold bars, can be turned into coins with Alchemy spells.

Wearing a ring of wealth will automatically pick up coins dropped by NPCs upon killing them as long as the player has inventory space available.

7001: The Camel mould (p) is a quest item used during the Enakhra's Lament quest. The (p) means positive mould. It is obtained by using a piece of soft clay in a cavity on the pedestal on the upper floor of the underground temple south of the Bandit Camp. The mould can then be used to carve a new stone head from a block of granite. The player should then insert the head into the cavity on the pedestal in order to continue the quest.
7002:
The stone head is a quest item used during the Enakhra's Lament quest. It is made by using a chisel on a piece of granite while the camel mould (p) is in the player's inventory.

The head can then be inserted into the cavity on top of the pedestal on the upper floor of the underground temple south of the Bandit Camp.
7003:
The camel mask is a hat that can be made during and after the Enakhra's Lament quest, although it plays no role in the quest itself. It gives no stat bonuses, and is merely worn for aesthetic purposes.

Players can make one by going to the middle floor of Enakhra's Temple and using a single piece of soft clay on the pedestal in the middle of the room. There is no limit to how many masks you can own.
7004: The Chisel is an animation item released with Enakhra's Lament. It is temporarily wielded during several animations in which the player holds a chisel in their right hand. Aside from this, it cannot be obtained.
7051:
The lit bug lantern is an item used in the Slayer skill. It requires level 33 Slayer to wield and must be equipped in order to fight Harpie Bug Swarms.

Level 33 Firemaking and a tinderbox are required to light the unlit lantern. Bug lanterns are worn in the shield slot, but only lit lanterns are effective against Harpie Bug Swarms for completing slayer tasks.

Only the extinguished lantern is tradeable. The version purchased from Slayer masters is unlit by default.

The bug lantern does not qualify as a light source, however it does count as warm clothing while fighting Wintertodt. It can also be used as a lantern for lantern harpooning.
7053:
The lit bug lantern is an item used in the Slayer skill. It requires level 33 Slayer to wield and must be equipped in order to fight Harpie Bug Swarms.

Level 33 Firemaking and a tinderbox are required to light the unlit lantern. Bug lanterns are worn in the shield slot, but only lit lanterns are effective against Harpie Bug Swarms for completing slayer tasks.

Only the extinguished lantern is tradeable. The version purchased from Slayer masters is unlit by default.

The bug lantern does not qualify as a light source, however it does count as warm clothing while fighting Wintertodt. It can also be used as a lantern for lantern harpooning.
7060:
The tuna potato is a type of food that restores 22 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by following the steps to combine various items (listed below). To follow all the preparation steps requires level 68 Cooking and grants 10 Cooking experience for a grand total of 309.5 Cooking experience (all the necessary steps).

The tuna potato is the second highest instant-health single consumption food, behind the marlin, alongside the dark crab, anglerfish, bluefin and manta ray. The tuna potato has the lowest Cooking requirement of these, but has the highest weight and is tedious to mass-produce. For a comparison to other items that provide healing, see food.
7066:
Mushroom & onion can be created by players with level 57 Cooking. The full process of making mushroom & onion gives 120 experience, but the final step gives none. Eating Mushroom & onion restores 11 hitpoints.

To make mushroom and onion, obtain a knife, mushroom, onion, and two bowls:

Use a mushroom with a bowl and cook it on a range to make fried mushrooms.

Use an onion with another bowl and cook it on a range to make fried onions.

Finally use one bowl on the other bowl.

Mushroom and onion may be added to a potato with butter to make mushroom potato.
7068:
Tuna and corn is food and a cooking ingredient that can only be created by members with a Cooking level of 67. It can be created by using a bowl of sweetcorn on cooked tuna with a Fletching knife equipped, or while a knife is in your inventory, or by adding cooked sweetcorn to a bowl of chopped tuna, or by using a bowl of sweetcorn on chopped tuna.

It heals 13 hitpoints. Making all ingredients for tuna and corn from scratch provides you with 204 Cooking experience.

It is mostly used as one of the final ingredients for a tuna potato, which heals 22 hitpoints. To make a tuna potato, use a tuna and corn with a potato with butter at level 68 Cooking.
7070: Minced meat is made by using cooked meat on a bowl while having a knife in your inventory. It can be eaten to restore 2 Hitpoints. Minced meat can be made into spicy minced meat by using a shaker of gnome spice or spice on it, which can then be used as bait for catching carnivorous chinchompas. Alternatively, spicy sauce can be used on minced meat to make chilli con carne.
7076:
An uncooked egg is a cooking ingredient that players can make by using an egg on a bowl. This food item cannot be eaten.

At level 13 Cooking, a player can cook an uncooked egg on a range or fire. This produces a scrambled egg and grants 50 Cooking experience. The scrambled egg can either be eaten or combined with a tomato to make egg and tomato topping, used in making an egg potato.
7080:
Sliced mushrooms are a cooking ingredient made by using a bowl with a mushroom while a knife is in inventory. This grants no Cooking experience but requires no Cooking level.

They can be cooked on a fire or range at a Cooking level of 46 to make Fried mushrooms for 60 Cooking experience. If burnt, the sliced mushrooms instead become worthless burnt mushrooms.
7082:
Fried mushrooms are a type of food that can be obtained by cooking sliced mushrooms on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 46 Cooking and granting 60 experience when successful. Players may burn the mushrooms while cooking one, resulting in a burnt mushroom; the burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels. It will stop burning entirely at level 90 Cooking on both ranges and fires. When eaten, fried mushrooms heals 5 Hitpoints.

As a cooking ingredient, they can be combined with fried onions to create mushroom & onion at level 57 Cooking. Mushroom and onion can be used at level 64 with a potato with butter to create mushroom potatoes for 55 experience.
7084:
Fried onions are a type of food that can be obtained by cooking chopped onions on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 42 Cooking and granting 60 experience when successful. Players may burn the onions while cooking one, resulting in a burnt onion; the burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 77 on both ranges and fires. When eaten, fried onions heal 5 hitpoints.

It is more commonly used as an ingredient to create mushroom & onion topping by combining it with fried mushrooms at a Cooking level of 57. This does not grant any Cooking experience, but in turn mushroom & onion can be used at level 64 with a potato with butter to create a mushroom potato for 55 experience.
7088:
A bowl of sweetcorn (in game name "Sweetcorn") is both food and a cooking ingredient. It can be made by using a bowl on a cooked sweetcorn; this does not require a knife, nor does it provide any Cooking experience. As food, when eaten, it provides healing identical to cooked sweetcorn, namely 1+10% of total hitpoints, rounded down. A bowl of sweetcorn is called "Sweetcorn" in-game. This may cause confusion among players as raw sweetcorn has the same in-game name.

Its primary use is as an ingredient in making tuna and corn. At level 67 Cooking, with a knife in inventory, members can use a bowl of sweetcorn with cooked tuna to create tuna and corn. This mixture heals 13 hitpoints when eaten, but is usually added to a potato with butter at level 68 Cooking to create a tuna potato that heals 22 hitpoints.
7090:
Burnt egg is the result of accidentally burning an uncooked egg while attempting to make scrambled egg. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 48.

The burnt egg has no use whatsoever, although it can be emptied to reclaim a bowl. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.
7092:
Burnt onion is the result of accidentally burning a chopped onion while attempting to make a fried onions. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 77.

The burnt onion has no use whatsoever, although it can be emptied to reclaim a bowl. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.
7094:
Burnt mushroom is the result of accidentally burning sliced mushrooms while attempting to make fried mushrooms. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 90.

The burnt mushroom has no use whatsoever, although it can be emptied to reclaim a bowl. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.
7096:

Regular runes could not be used for this purpose since they are stackable, and therefore stack quantities would display next to each piece on the board.

The actual items cannot be obtained by players.

7108: Gunpowder is used during the Cabin Fever quest. It is obtained from the powder barrel next to the cannon that must be fired at the enemy pirates, after which it must be put into the cannon, followed by several other items, to fire the cannon and blast the enemies away.
7109:
The fuse is an item used in the Cabin Fever quest to light a keg of gunpowder while battling an enemy ship. It can be found in the Gun Locker on The Adventurous.

The fuse is identical in appearance to the fuse used during the sequel quest The Great Brain Robbery.
7110: The beige stripy pirate shirt is a shirt that can be purchased from Dodgy Mike's Second-hand Clothing on Mos Le'Harmless, south-east of the bank.
7116: The beige pirate leggings are a pair of legwear that can be purchased from Dodgy Mike's Second-hand Clothing on Mos Le'Harmless, south-east of the bank.
7118: A canister is a can filled with anti-personnel shrapnel used in the Cabin Fever quest instead of a cannonball. It is found in the Gun Locker on Bill Teach's ship.
7120: A ramrod is used in the Cabin Fever quest to load gunpowder into the barrel of the cannon, and to clean out the cannon after a successful shot. It can be found in the Gun Locker under Bill Teach's ship.
7122: The red stripy pirate shirt is a shirt that can be purchased from Dodgy Mike's Second-hand Clothing on Mos Le'Harmless, south-east of the bank.
7126: The red pirate leggings are a pair of legwear that can be purchased from Dodgy Mike's Second-hand Clothing on Mos Le'Harmless, south-east of the bank.
7128: The blue stripy pirate shirt is a shirt that can be purchased from Dodgy Mike's Second-hand Clothing on Mos Le'Harmless, south-east of the bank.
7132: The blue pirate leggings are a pair of legwear that can be purchased from Dodgy Mike's Second-hand Clothing on Mos Le'Harmless, south-east of the bank.
7134: The brown stripy pirate shirt is a shirt that can be purchased from Dodgy Mike's Second-hand Clothing on Mos Le'Harmless, south-east of the bank.
7138: The brown pirate leggings are a pair of legwear that can be purchased from Dodgy Mike's Second-hand Clothing on Mos Le'Harmless, south-east of the bank.
7140:
The lucky cutlass can be bought from Smith on Mos Le'Harmless for 2,560 coins after completing the quest Cabin Fever, and requires 30 Attack to wield. A Book o' Piracy is required to purchase from Smith.

According to the dialogue when purchasing the cutlass from Smith, the sword was previously owned by a pirate named Unlucky Jenkins, who died after a long series of improbable and very unlucky calamities. After his gruesome demise, his cutlass was discovered, untouched. The other pirates concluded that, having survived so much terrible bad luck already, it would be impossible for it to go through any more bad luck.

Among one-handed weapons buyable in shops, this cutlass provides the highest stab and slash defence, and its crush defence is only beaten by the willow and maple blackjack(d). Because of this, it can be an accessible addition to tank armour when in the Wilderness.
7141:
Harry's cutlass is a special weapon sold by Smith on the docks of the island of Mos Le'Harmless. It originally belonged to a pirate named Brass Hand Harry, who lost his right hand in a battle off the coast of Karamja. He had Smith create a cutlass with a gauntlet fixed to the hilt in order to continue fighting. Smith will sell one to the player for 1,040 coins. It requires an Attack level of 20 to wield. It has stats similar to those of a Mithril scimitar.

The gauntlet fits over the equipment on the player's hand slot and offers a small defensive bonus. To be able to understand Smith and purchase the cutlass, the player must have a Book o' Piracy in inventory. Talk to Smith and select the 'cutlasses' option in the dialogue box.
7142:
The rapier is a very thin sword that requires an Attack level of 40 to wield. Its stats are the same as the rune scimitar but with the stab and slash attack bonuses swapped. Prior to the addition of the Brine sabre, the rapier and rune scimitar were tied for best-in-slot melee weapon for 40 attack-tier weaponry.

It was used by Gentleman Mallard until his disappearance at sea. The sword was later found by Smith of Mos Le'Harmless, who will sell it to players for 25,600 coins. Cabin Fever must be completed to reach the island, making it an indirect requirement for this weapon.

To be able to understand Smith and purchase the rapier, the player must have a Book o' Piracy in their inventory. Talk to Smith and select the cutlasses option in the dialogue box. If player possesses (in bank or in inventory) more than one rapier, Smith won't sell another one claiming that player already has one. Dropping rapiers allows player to purchase more than two rapiers.
7143: Plunder is used during the Cabin Fever quest. You need to take 10 plunder from the chest, crate, and barrel on the opponent's ship to the plunder storage in Bill Teach's ship, The Adventurous. You may store plunder collected in the plunder storage.
7144:
The Book o' Piracy (full title The Little Book o' Piracy) is a book that players receive after completing the Cabin Fever quest. Players can click on the book to read it and find out a bit about pirate life (from the pirate view) and pirate slang. The first page of this book reveals that it is "an AMCE product" by Cap'n Hook-Hand Morrisane (likely Ali Morrisane under a pseudonym).

After gaining access to the pirate town of Mos Le'Harmless, players must be carrying this book in their inventory to understand what other pirates are saying. Otherwise, the pirates will respond with a fixed script of incomprehensible pirate slang. Note that using trading shops on the island requires carrying the book.

Players who have completed Cabin Fever can obtain another copy from bookshelves in their houses. Bill Teach (aboard The Adventurous, docked at Port Phasmatys and Mos Le'Harmless) will also give them a copy before taking them to Mos Le'Harmless if they do not have one in their bank, inventory, or house.
7145: Cannon barrels are the third part of the dwarf multicannon set up on top of the cannon base after placing the cannon stand and before the cannon furnace. They shoot the enemy with a barrage of steel cannonballs or granite cannonballs. It is purchased from Multicannon parts for sale for 200,625 coins.
7149: A canister is a can filled with anti-personnel shrapnel used in the Cabin Fever quest instead of a cannonball. It is found in the Gun Locker on Bill Teach's ship.
7155:
The pile of rope is an unobtainable item seen during Cabin Fever. It can be found on the enemy pirate ship, allowing players to return to The Adventurous.

The item has a "Take" option - however, this will give the standard rope instead, and the item will not despawn. Therefore, it is designed to serve as an infinite source of rope.
7156:
The tinderbox is an unobtainable item seen during Cabin Fever. It can be found on the south-east corner of The Adventurous.

The item has a "Take" option - however, this will give the standard Tinderbox instead, and the item will not despawn. Therefore, it is designed to serve as an infinite source of tinderboxes.

It can later be found on the wrecked ship at Harmony Island. Attempting to cast Telekinetic Grab gives the message "You can't cast this spell on that object."
7158:
The dragon 2h sword is one of the strongest two-handed swords in Old School RuneScape, requiring level 60 Attack to wield. Due to its slow attacking speed and the fact that it cannot be used with a shield or defender, many players prefer using other dragon weaponry instead, such as the dragon scimitar.

It is dropped by most Wilderness bosses and the Kalphite Queen.

As with most dragon equipment, the dragon 2h sword cannot be made from raw materials using the Smithing skill.
7159:
Insulated boots are a piece of Slayer equipment worn in the feet slot, requiring a Slayer level of 37 to wear them. They can be purchased from any Slayer Master.

Wearing the boots will protect the player against a variety of electric-based attacks, including:

Reducing the max hit of a Killerwatt's ranged attack from 13 to 6

Reducing the damage dealt by a rune dragon's electric attack from 2-5 to 0-2

Reducing damage taken from the electric ball attack by 40% if it does not pass through Verzik Vitur during the second phase of the fight

Nullifying the 10 damage taken during Darkness of Hallowvale, when improperly using the large ornate key directly on the door to the Meiyerditch Laboratories, rather than suspending it from the nearby vampyre statue
7162: The Pie recipe book is a members-only item that gives recipes and instructions on making all of the pies in the game. It can be purchased from Romily Weaklax on the bottom floor of the Cooks' Guild for 5 coins. It can also be stored on the shelves of a bookcase in your player-owned house.
7164: Part mud pie is made by adding compost to a pie shell. Water must then be added to it to create a part mud pie (water).
7166: A Part mud pie (water) is made by adding water to a part mud pie (compost). Clay must then be added to it to create a raw mud pie.
7170:
A mud pie is a special type of pie that does not restore Hitpoints, and instead can be used as an equipable weapon for PvP. The pie does no damage and is not stackable, but can be thrown at other players to reduce the target's current run energy by 25%, rounded down. Mud pies have no effect on NPCs. When throwing a mud pie, a pie dish will drop underneath the target. As mud pies are considered a thrown weapon, a player targeted by mud pies should wear armour with high Ranged defence to lower their accuracy.

It can be obtained by baking a raw mud pie on a cooking range, requiring level 29 Cooking and granting 128 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt pie. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 63. Alternatively, casting the Bake Pie spell from the lunar spellbook will always create a pie without burning it.

Mud pie is a possible task from Romily Weaklax in the Cooks' Guild.
7172: Part garden pie is made by adding Tomato to a Pie shell. Onion must then be added to it to create a Part garden pie (onion).
7174: Part garden pie is made by adding an onion to a part garden pie (tomato). A cabbage must then be added to it to create a raw garden pie.
7176:
A Raw garden pie is made by adding cabbage to a part garden pie (onion). Cabbage from Draynor Manor will not work. It can be cooked on a range to give either a Garden pie or a Burnt pie.

In total to make a raw garden pie a pie dish, pastry dough, onion, tomato, and cabbage are needed.
7178:
Garden pie is a type of pie that restores 12 Hitpoints in total, 2 bites each healing for 6. It also temporarily boosts Farming by 3. A pie dish will remain after both bites are consumed.

It can be created by baking a raw garden pie on a cooking range, requiring level 34 Cooking and granting 138 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt pie. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 68. Alternatively, casting the Bake Pie spell from the lunar spellbook will always create a pie without burning it.

Garden pie is a possible task from Romily Weaklax in the Cooks' Guild.

7182: A part fish pie is made by adding trout to a pie shell. Cod must then be added to it to create a part fish pie (cod).
7184: A part fish pie is made by adding cod to a part fish pie (trout). It can be created into a raw fish pie by adding a raw potato to it.
7186: Raw fish pie is made by adding potato to a part fish pie (cod). It can then be cooked on a range which gives either a fish pie or a burnt pie.
7198:
Admiral pie is a type of pie that restores 16 Hitpoints in total, 2 bites each healing for 8. It also temporarily boosts Fishing by +5. A pie dish will remain after both bites are consumed.

It can be created by baking a raw admiral pie on a cooking range, requiring level 70 Cooking and granting 210 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt pie. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 94. Alternatively, casting the Bake Pie spell from the lunar spellbook will always create a pie without burning it.

Admiral pie is a possible task from Romily Weaklax in the Cooks' Guild.
7202: Part wild pie is made by adding raw bear meat to a pie shell. Raw chompy must then be added to it to create a part wild pie (raw chompy).
7204: Part wild pie is made by adding Raw chompy to a Part wild pie (raw bear meat). Raw rabbit must then be added to it to create a Raw wild pie.
7208:
Wild pie is a type of pie that restores 22 total Hitpoints in 2 bites, with each bite healing for 11. It also temporarily boosts Slayer by 5 levels, the highest boost available, and Ranged by 4 levels. A pie dish will remain after both bites are consumed.

It can be created by baking a raw wild pie on a cooking range, requiring level 85 Cooking and granting 240 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt pie. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Wild pies never stop burning altogether even at level 99, unless the player is wearing a Cooking cape. Alternatively, casting the Bake Pie spell from the lunar spellbook will always create a pie without burning it.

The Slayer boost can be used to kill higher level Slayer monsters, but the boost does not enable you to receive a Slayer task from a Slayer Master above your level.

Wild pies are popular for fighting the chaos elemental or chaos fanatic as the empty pie dish prevents their special attacks from un-equipping Worn Equipment due to a full inventory.

Baking a wild pie at the Nardah clay oven is a requirement for the Elite Desert Diary.

7212: A part summer pie (strawberry) is made by adding a strawberry to a pie shell. A watermelon must then be added to it to create a part summer pie (watermelon).
7214: A part summer pie (watermelon) is made by adding watermelon to a part summer pie (strawberry). A cooking apple must then be added to it to create a raw summer pie.
7218:
Summer pie is a type of pie with two bites that restores 11 Hitpoints, 10% run energy, and grants a +5 temporary skill boost to Agility per bite. A pie dish will remain after consumption.

It can be created by baking a raw summer pie on a cooking range, requiring level 95 Cooking and granting 260 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt pie. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Summer pies never stop burning altogether even at level 99, unless the player is wearing a Cooking cape. Alternatively, casting the Bake Pie spell from the lunar spellbook will always create a pie without burning it.

Summer pies are a type of 1 tick (0.6 seconds) fast food, meaning you can eat them in succession with less delay than standard food which adds a 3-tick (1.8 second) penalty. Because of this short eat delay, summer pies can restore health quicker than manta rays, making them more efficient for healing up a lot of lost health in the same amount of ticks. However, as each half adds 3 ticks of attack delay, they are less efficient in combat than other high-healing foods.

The +5 Agility boost makes summer pies a great food for use in Agility training, increasing the chance to pass obstacles while restoring Hitpoints lost from failing any. It may also be used to pass Agility level requirements in quests, Agility courses, shortcuts or any other activities with an Agility requirement. Not all requirements can be boosted, such as Dragon Slayer II, the Ape Atoll Agility Course or Saradomin's Encampment in the God Wars Dungeon. The Preserve prayer may be used to extend the duration of the boost.

Summer pies are popular for fighting the Chaos Elemental or Chaos Fanatic as the empty pie dish prevents their special attacks from un-equipping Worn Equipment due to a full inventory.

Successfully baking a summer pie inside of the Cooks' Guild is an elite Varrock Diary task.

Not all requirements can be boosted, such as Dragon Slayer II, the Ape Atoll Agility Course or Saradomin's Encampment in the God Wars Dungeon. The Preserve prayer may be used to extend the duration of the boost.

Summer pies are popular for fighting the Chaos Elemental or Chaos Fanatic as the empty pie dish prevents their special attacks from un-equipping Worn Equipment due to a full inventory.

Successfully baking a summer pie inside of the Cooks' Guild is an elite Varrock Diary task.
7222:
Burnt rabbit is the result of accidentally burning a skewered rabbit while attempting to make roast rabbit. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 99.

The burnt rabbit has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.
7223:
Roast rabbit are a type of food that can be obtained by cooking a skewered rabbit on a fire, requiring level 16 Cooking and granting 72.5 experience when successful. Players may burn the meat while cooking one, resulting in burnt rabbit; the burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 99.

When eaten, roast rabbit heals 7 hitpoints.

Either roast rabbit or cooked rabbit is required for the quest Regicide.
7225:
Iron spits are made with the Smithing skill by using an iron bar on an anvil (a hammer is required) with a Smithing level of at least 17. This provides 25 Smithing experience. They can be used to cook raw bird meat, raw beast meat, raw chompy, and raw rabbits. You can get the raw food by using the Hunter skill to catch animals, or chompy bird hunting to get chompies. To cook the raw meat, be sure to have at least a Firemaking level of 20 and then use the meat on the iron spit, and then on a fire.

One is needed to make a skewered chompy for the Recipe for Disaster/Freeing Skrach Uglogwee subquest. Raw jubbly cannot be cooked with an iron spit, and instead must be cooked on an ogre spit-roast.
7226:
Burnt chompy is an unobtainable variant of the ruined chompy that was released alongside the iron spit.

Presumably, it was intended to be the result of failing to successfully roast raw chompy on an iron spit, with the ruined chompy remaining a quest item only obtainable from using an ogre spit-roast. For whatever reason, it was decided to make the iron spit give the quest variant everywhere.
7228:
Cooked chompy is an ogre delicacy obtained by skewering a raw chompy with an iron spit, then cooking the skewered chompy on a fire, requiring level 30 Cooking and granting 100 experience when successful. Players may burn the chompy while cooking one, resulting in a ruined chompy; the burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 99.

Cooked chompy heals 10 Hitpoints. If hunting chompy birds, due to the meat's weight of 10 kg, it is recommended to do so south-west of Castle Wars. Big Chompy Bird Hunting is required to hunt them.

7297:
A key is an item needed to unlock a chest or drawer during a Treasure Trail.

There will be a clue telling you where to get it. The key is a drop only when carrying the clue scroll. It disappears when used to open the chest or drawer. Keys are non-tradeable objects, specific to the player who finds them. They are used on all levels of treasure trails.

It is possible to obtain more than one key using the drop trick. However, after taking a clue from the chest/drawer, the key won't open it again, and the player gets a message: "The chest (or drawer) is locked." Keys obtained this way from the same clue will still remain in the bank; however, keys obtained from different clues will not stack.

7409:
Magic secateurs are obtained during the quest Fairytale I - Growing Pains from Malignius Mortifer, south of Falador.

They are most commonly used for increased harvest yield when farming (see below for more information).

It is the only weapon in game that is capable of damaging Tanglefoot. Despite having a higher slash stat, the magic secateurs are considered a stab weapon.

If players lose their magic secateurs before defeating Tanglefoot, they must reacquire them by taking the required items back to the Nature Spirit; otherwise, after defeating Tanglefoot, additional pairs may be purchased from Malignius Mortifer for 40,000 coins each. Tool Leprechauns located at each Farming patch can store magic secateurs in the normal secateurs slot.

To understand the overall effects of having the secateurs on saving harvest lives, see here.
7410:
Queen's secateurs are used in Fairytale I - Growing Pains and Fairytale II - Cure a Queen quests. They are first obtained as a drop from Tanglefoot. In part 2, you need to pickpocket Fairy Godfather to get them, which requires a level of 40 Thieving. The secateurs from A Fairy Tale I and A Fairy Tale II quests are two different items.

These secateurs cannot be wielded, or used as normal secateurs; they are purely a quest item.

You cannot obtain multiple secateurs while one is in your inventory or bank. However, through the drop trick, it is possible to obtain multiple secateurs during Fairytale II.

If the Queen's secateurs are lost before talking to the Fairy Godfather at the end of Fairytale I - Growing Pains, they can be reobtained by entering the gap in the wall next to the Cosmic Altar into the tunnels where you fought Tanglefoot. The secateurs will appear in your inventory upon squeezing through the gap.
7411: The symptoms list is a quest item used in the Fairytale I - Growing Pains quest. It can be obtained by talking to Fairy Nuff in the Queen's chamber in Zanaris. The player is then charged with delivering the list to a wizard named Zandar Horfyre in order to identify the illness that the Fairy Queen is suffering from.
7414:
A paddle is an animation item released alongside canoes. While it is unobtainable by players, it can be seen equipped by non-player characters such as Hari and Tarquin. It can also be seen held by players during the cutscene in which players are rowing their canoes.

Finally, it can also be seen in the Woodcutting skill guide to represent canoes.
7416:
Mole claws are dropped by the Giant Mole that lurks below Falador Park. It is also dropped by molanisks and experiment No.2s. Players who have completed the Falador hard achievement diary will receive mole claws and mole skins from the Giant Mole in noted form. Like the mole skins, mole claws can be traded to Wyson the gardener for bird nests.

Unlike nests received through Woodcutting, Bird house trapping or Managing Miscellania, these nests never contain bird's eggs but often contain allotment and herb seeds.

Mole claws can be used to change the Baby Mole pet to the Baby Mole-rat. This can then be undone by using a mole skin on the baby mole-rat.
7418:
Mole skins are dropped by the Giant Mole that lurks below Falador park. Players who have completed the Falador hard achievement diary will receive mole skins and mole claws in noted form. Like the mole claw, mole skins can be traded to Wyson the gardener for bird nests. Unlike nests received through Woodcutting, Bird house trapping, or Managing Miscellania, these nests never contain bird's eggs but often contain allotment and herb seeds.

Mole skin can be used on a Baby mole-rat to revert a Baby Mole pet to its original state. Using a Mole claw on the regular baby mole will turn it into a baby mole-rat again.
7432: Fungicide is a Slayer equipment purchasable from Slayer masters for the price of 10 coins, and is also dropped by Mutated Zygomites as a fairly common drop. They are used to refill empty Fungicide sprays, which are used to kill Mutated Zygomites. Each fungicide fills the fungicide spray with 10 charges.
7433: The wooden spoon is a melee kitchen weapon that can be bought from the Culinaromancer's chest. To buy it, the player must have started the Recipe for Disaster quest, and is the first weapon available after completing the beginning portion of the quest. To wield the weapon, the player must have completed one subquest. This weapon has stats similar to the bronze longsword.
7435: The egg whisk is kitchen weaponry purchased from the Culinaromancer's Chest after completing one Recipe for Disaster subquest. Wielding it requires two subquests. This weapon has the same stats as the iron dagger.
7437: A spork is a melee kitchen weapon that can be bought from the Culinaromancer's chest. To wield it the player must have completed three Recipe for Disaster subquests. This weapon has stats identical to the Steel sword. It has a requirement of 10 Attack to wield.
7439: A spatula is a melee kitchen weapon that can be bought from the Culinaromancer's chest. To wield, the player must have completed three Recipe for Disaster subquests and have an Attack level of 10. This weapon has stats equal to a Black 2h sword.
7441: The frying pan is a melee kitchen weapon that can be bought from the Culinaromancer's chest. To wield it the player must have completed four Recipe for Disaster subquests and have 20 Attack. Despite having the same stats as the mithril warhammer, it was not updated in the first 2021 equipment rebalance to have a Strength level requirement.
7445: The rolling pin is a melee kitchen weapon that can be bought from the Culinaromancer's chest. To purchase, the player must have completed 6 of the Recipe for Disaster subquests. To wield, in addition to having 40 Attack, 7 subquests must be completed. This weapon has the same stats as the rune mace, including the prayer bonus. However, unlike the mace, it did not get updated to an attack speed of 4 along with the first stage of the 2021 equipment rebalance.
7449:
The meat tenderiser is a melee kitchen weapon that can be bought from the Culinaromancer's Chest. To wield it, the player must have completed all 8 Recipe for Disaster subquests, and the final battle (it may be purchased, but not wielded, before completing the final battle).

The weapon has almost the same stats as a rune warhammer, but it requires level 40 Attack instead of Strength, being left out in the first 2021 equipment rebalance. Although it is held over the player's shoulder similarly to a two-handed sword, it is a one-handed weapon and can be used with a shield.
7451:
The cleaver is a melee kitchen weapon that can be bought from the Culinaromancer's chest. To wield it, the player must have completed the entire Recipe for Disaster quest, including the final boss battles, and have 40 Attack.

It has the same stats as the Rune scimitar.
7453:

As with all Culinaromancer's gloves, this piece of armour cannot be made using the Crafting skill.

As with all Culinaromancer's gloves, this piece of armour cannot be made using the Smithing skill.
7455:

7457:
Black gloves are special gloves that can be bought from the Culinaromancer's chest after completion of four Recipe for Disaster subquests.

7459:
Adamant gloves are culinaromancer's gloves, requiring 13 Defence to equip, and can be purchased from the Culinaromancer's Chest after completion of six Recipe for Disaster subquests. These are the lowest tier of gloves that are superior to the combat bracelet for melee.

As with all Culinaromancer's gloves, this piece of armour cannot be made using the Smithing skill.
7460:
Rune gloves are special gloves that can be bought from the Culinaromancer's Chest after completion of seven Recipe for Disaster subquests.

These gloves are a great option for high risk activities such as PvP, as they only cost 6,500 whilst still providing higher bonuses than a combat bracelet. When lost in a PvP death, they turn into 3,900 coins.

While only 1 Defence is required to wear these gloves, and they can be acquired at a minimum of 13 Defence, it is impossible to equip them at this level. Specifically, the gloves are only equipable if the player has already completed Daero's training OR Defeating the Culinaromancer. Attempting to wear the gloves before one of these requirements is met results in the message: "Your Defence level is not sufficient to let you use those gloves without completing your unfinished business with Daero". This effectively makes 34 Defence the minimum required level to wear rune gloves legitimately, assuming completion of Nature Spirit, and acceptance of 20,000 Defence experience from Daero after the completion of Monkey Madness I.

As with all Culinaromancer's gloves, this piece of armour cannot be made using the Smithing skill.
7461:
Dragon gloves are a pair of Culinaromancer's gloves that can be purchased from the Culinaromancer's Chest after completion of all eight Recipe for Disaster subquests.

Dragon gloves cost the same as Barrows gloves, but have significantly lower stats. However, obtaining dragon gloves only requires 107 quest points, compared to the 175 needed to complete the quest and unlock the Barrows variant.

As with all of the Culinaromancer's gloves, they cannot be made using the Smithing skill.
7462:
Barrows gloves are gloves that can be purchased for 130,000 coins (or 104,000 coins after completing the Elite Lumbridge & Draynor Diary) from the Culinaromancer's Chest in the Lumbridge Castle cellar after completing the entire Recipe for Disaster quest.

Of all gloves in Old School RuneScape, Barrows gloves provide the second highest Melee offensive bonuses behind the ferocious gloves, the second highest offensive bonuses for Ranged behind the zaryte vambraces, and the third highest Magic offensive bonuses behind the tormented bracelet and confliction gauntlets. For these reasons they work very well for all types of combat (and especially where multiple attack styles are necessary, such as the Dagannoth Kings or Royal Titans), and many players recommend completing Recipe for Disaster and acquiring these gloves as a long-term goal that every beginner should work toward.

While these gloves lack a Defence requirement, they cannot be acquired at 1 Defence due to the levels required to complete and experience gained from completing the necessary quests to complete Recipe for Disaster. The minimum Defence level a player can have to acquire and equip these gloves is 35 when all quest requirements and experience rewards are calculated, assuming the player did not accept Daero's training at the end of Monkey Madness I. In limited time modes like Deadman Mode, these gloves can be used by accounts with level 1 Defence after completing Recipe for Disaster via a quest lamp bought with Skull points.

As with all Culinaromancer's gloves, this piece of armour cannot be made using the Smithing skill.

Purchasing a pair of Barrows gloves is a requirement for the Hard Lumbridge & Draynor Diary.

When lost in a PvP death, they turn into 78,000 coins.
7463:
Cornflour is an unobtainable item released alongside Recipe for Disaster. It is assumed to be made by using Sweetcorn on a Windmill, but this requires a pot, and results in a pot of cornflour instead.

It was presumably created as a parallel to the discontinued item Flour, as the method of using a pot on a dropped heap of flour still existed ingame.

A second version of the item exists, which is flagged as a quest version of the item. Bizarrely, this version is tradeable, and remains listed on the Grand Exchange.
7464:
The Book on chickens, titled The Origins of the Bird of Evil, is a book about the Evil Chicken found randomly on the bookshelves in the Wise Old Man's house in Draynor Village, along with the strange book and the book of folklore. Players can return the book by using it on the Wise Old Man.

This book cannot be stored in a player-owned house bookcase.

7470: Cornflour mixture is made by using milky mixture with a pot of cornflour. This item is used in the Sir Amik Varze part of Recipe for Disaster. If used with a vanilla pod, it will make an incomplete brulee.
7472: Cinnamon is used to make a creme brulee supreme during the Recipe for Disaster subquest "Freeing Sir Amik Varze" where Sir Amik Varze is freed. It is obtained by using a dramen branch with a pestle and mortar. If used with a brulee (egg), it will make a brulee (raw).
7477:
The Evil chicken's egg is a quest item for the Sir Amik Varze sub-quest of Recipe for Disaster. It can be obtained by killing the Evil Chicken. It is used with the incomplete brulee to make a brulee missing cinnamon.

To find the Evil Chicken, players must speak to the Wise Old Man in Draynor Village. The Book on chickens, found on one of his shelves, has further information about the beast. The Evil Chicken's Lair can then be accessed by using a raw chicken (an undead raw chicken won't work) on the chicken shrine in northern Zanaris, near the fairy ring. Players should be prepared to be attacked by level 227 black dragons guarding the lair and should wear or use a protection against its breath. The Evil Chicken can be found in the back of the lair, and will drop the Evil chicken's egg when it is killed.

While the destroy prompt may insinuate otherwise, all a player needs to do is enter the lair again and search the Evil Chicken's nest to get another egg; the Evil Chicken will not reappear nor will the player have to fight him again.
7478:
The dragon token is obtained by killing a Black dragon in the Evil Chicken's Lair. It is used to summon K'klik the fairy dragon in the Freeing Sir Amik Varze subquest of Recipe for Disaster. When you rub it, K'klik appears. You need to ask the dragon to flambé your brulee to turn it into a brulee supreme in the quest.

When used, you are transported away to another plane and removed from where you were standing.

It can only be used within Lumbridge or Zanaris. Attempting to use the token elsewhere will result in the message, "The dragon's token doesn't seem to work here. Try it in Lumbridge town or Zanaris."

It can no longer be obtained after completing the subquest.
7484:
Orange spice is one of four spices used on stew to make spicy stew. Completion of the Freeing Evil Dave subquest of Recipe for Disaster is required to obtain the spices in Evil Dave's Basement of Doom in Edgeville. The simplest method to obtain these spices is to send your cat to catch Hell-Rats, which will yield between 1 to 4 doses of any of the spice colours. Another option is to kill the Hell-Rat Behemoth in the north-western room, which will always drop a 4 dose of the orange spice. It is possible to combine lower doses of the orange spice on each other to create 4 dose shakers. Once all doses are used it becomes an empty spice shaker.

Spicy stews containing orange spice can temporarily boost or drain the stats of Cooking, Crafting, Construction, Firemaking, Fletching, Runecraft, and Smithing. It is possible to use 1 to 3 doses on a stew yielding, -1 to +1, -3 to +3 and -5 to +5 respectively. Orange spice is considered the most useful due to its ability to boost Runecraft up to 5 levels and is the only way to visibly boost Firemaking +2 or more.

Orange spicy stew is a common way for players to complete the Karamja Elite Diary with 86 Runecraft and build various high level objects in their POH.

7496: An empty spice shaker is what remains of red spice, orange spice, yellow spice, or brown spice after using up all the doses. The empty shaker cannot be refilled, traded, nor sold. It is a useless item. While they cannot be withdrawn in noted form, stacks of them can be destroyed with the item incinerator.
7497:
A dirty blast is a drink used in the first subquest of Recipe for Disaster. It can be made during and after the quest by adding ashes to a fruit blast, requiring 10 Cooking. The pre-made fruit blast obtained from Blurberry Bar will NOT work to make it. Additionally, you cannot add the ashes until after the quest begins. Creating a dirty blast gives 5 Cooking experience.

It is needed along with a rotten tomato, an eye of newt, and a Greenman's ale for the Recipe for Disaster quest as part of a powerful food-magic (as explained by Aris) wherein the Lumbridge cook inadvertently frees the Culinaromancer.
7498:
Antique lamps are rewards from quests, achievement diaries and the Varrock Museum miniquest. Like regular lamps, these lamps grant a player experience in a chosen skill, and the skill chosen must usually be over a certain level which is unboostable.

Lamps that are not included in the three items kept on death will be kept inside your death's coffer, if not deleted.
7508:
Asgoldian ale is a quest item used in the Recipe for Disaster quest's Freeing the Mountain Dwarf subquest. It is made by adding a single coin to an Asgarnian ale after learning the recipe from Emily in the Rising Sun Inn in Falador, once the Mountain Dwarf in Lumbridge Castle's dining hall has been inspected.

Players cannot consume the drink; if attempted, they will receive the message: I don't think I'd like gold in beer thanks. Leave it for the dwarves.
7511:
The slop of compromise is used in Recipe for Disaster to free General Bentnoze and General Wartface. It is obtained by taking soggy bread, dyed orange, and spicy maggots to the Goblin Cook in the Goblin Village.

The in-game text describes it as an "indescribable grey mush" and it cannot be truly categorised as food, since players cannot eat it.
7515:
Breadcrumbs are a quest item in the Freeing Pirate Pete subquest of the Recipe for Disaster quest. They are made by using a knife on a loaf of bread, requiring starting the quest, and used as an ingredient to make a raw fishcake.

Breadcrumbs are also used as payment to a bellshroom plant in order to enter and exit a secluded area in the Tar Swamp on Fossil Island.
7517: Ground kelp is one of the ingredients used to make fishcakes to save Pirate Pete in Recipe for Disaster. It is made by using a pestle and mortar on some kelp. Kelp can be obtained by speaking to Murphy while wearing a fishbowl helmet and diving apparatus and then going diving and picking from the plant underwater.
7518:
Giant crab meat is a 100% drop from crabs. It is used in Recipe for Disaster to make a cooked fishcake to give to Pirate Pete. Giant crab meat requires level 21 Cooking to cook, and will give 100 Cooking experience. When cooked, it will become cooked giant crab meat. This provides 5 bites of 2 Hitpoints each.

There is a chance when cooking to burn the crab meat, creating burnt giant crab meat. This chance reduces to zero at level 62 Cooking.

When used with a pestle and mortar, it becomes ground giant crab meat.
7521:
Cooked giant crab meat is a type of food that restores 5 bites of 2 Hitpoints each, for a total of 10 healing.

It can be obtained by cooking giant crab meat on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 21 Cooking and granting 100 experience when successful. When cooking, there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt giant crab meat. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. It will stop burning entirely at level 62 (58 if the easy Kourend & Kebos Diary is completed while cooking at the city kitchens).

The small amounts of hitpoints given per bite can be used to "fine tune" the hitpoints of someone using Dharok the Wretched's equipment. However, it is not recommended for general healing, as tuna is one-bite, heals just as much, and costs significantly less.

7527:
Ground giant crab meat is an ingredient in fishcakes, and is used in Pirate Pete's part of Recipe for Disaster.

Players can make this item by using giant crab meat on a pestle and mortar. Giant crab meat is obtained by killing crabs in the crab pen in the Mogre Camp.
7528: Ground cod is an ingredient used to make fishcakes when freeing Pirate Pete in the Recipe for disaster quest. It is created by using a raw cod with a pestle and mortar.
7529:
A raw fishcake is a quest item needed to complete the Pirate Pete section of Recipe for Disaster.

It is made with breadcrumbs, ground cod, ground kelp, and ground giant crab meat. Players should use any one ingredient with any other whilst they have the other ingredients in their inventory.

Players can then use the raw fishcake on a fire or a range to make a cooked fishcake. This requires level 31 Cooking to make, and heals 11 hitpoints if eaten.
7530:
Cooked fishcakes are a type of food that can be obtained by cooking a raw fishcake on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 31 Cooking and granting 100 experience when successful. Players may burn the fishcake while cooking one, resulting in burnt fishcake; the burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 62 on both ranges and fires.

The cooked fishcake heals 11 hitpoints when eaten, and is needed to complete the Pirate Pete subquest of Recipe for Disaster. It is made with breadcrumbs, ground cod, ground kelp, and ground crab meat, creating a raw fishcake that is then cooked.
7531:
Burnt fishcake is the result of accidentally burning a raw fishcake while attempting to make a cooked fishcake. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 62.

The burnt fishcake has no use whatsoever. Unlike most burnt food, it is not tradeable.
7532:
Mudskipper hides are given to Nung, at the Mogre Camp during Recipe for Disaster, in order to gain access to the crab pen.

The hide is a drop from mudskippers. Contrary to popular belief Mudskipper hides are not used to create mudskipper hats or flippers, you must kill Mogres to obtain these items.

If taken out of water a message appears saying "The Mudkipper Hides all dry out and crumble on contact to air."

Players who wish to bring this item outside the area may do so by using an Imp-in-a-box. It is not necessary to collect all mudskipper hides at once, they may be handed in one at a time to Nung who will tell you how many remaining hides you need to deliver to him.
7533: Rock or rocks may refer to any of the following:
7534:
The fishbowl helmet is obtained from Murphy during the Freeing Pirate Pete subquest of the Recipe for Disaster quest in exchange for a fishbowl. After the quest it can be obtained for free. It can be equipped alongside the diving apparatus as a source of unlimited oxygen to explore the Mogre Camp and other underwater areas. After completion of the Freeing Pirate Pete subquest, it and the diving apparatus can be stored in the cargo hold of a player's boat for use in sea charting with mermaid guides.

In The Great Brain Robbery, this helmet is used with the diving apparatus, to dive in the underwater tunnel on Harmony Island. It is useful in the underwater area of Fossil Island as well.

If you lose the fishbowl helmet, Murphy will give you a new one if you choose the diving option when talking to him. He will not give the helmet if the player has one stored in the bank, but he does not check the player's boat or tackle box.

It can be stored in a tackle box.
7535:
The diving apparatus is used for diving into the Mogre Camp in the waters of Port Khazard, during the Freeing Pirate Pete subquest of the Recipe for Disaster quest. It is used to get to the sea floor. It is also used in the underwater tunnel on Harmony Island during The Great Brain Robbery, as well as the underwater area of Fossil Island and the Coral Nurseries of The Great Conch. After completion of the Freeing Pirate Pete subquest, it can be stored in the cargo hold of a player's boat for use in sea charting with mermaid guides.

It is worn in the cape slot, and if worn alongside the fishbowl helmet, players' oxygen will not deplete while underwater.

If the apparatus is lost, Murphy will provide another one upon choosing the diving option when talking to him. He will not give the apparatus if the player has an apparatus stored in the bank, but he does not check the player's boat or tackle box.

It can be stored in a tackle box.
7540:
A broken crab claw is an item obtained when a player fails to craft a fresh crab claw into a crab claw.

The chance of successfully crafting a crab claw scales from 15% at level 1 Crafting to 94% at level 99 Crafting.
7541:
A broken crab shell is an item obtained when a player fails to craft a fresh crab shell into a crab helmet.

The chance of successfully crafting a crab helmet scales from 15% at level 1 Crafting to 94% at level 99 Crafting.
7543: The raw guide cake is a quest item that can be cooked into a Cake of Guidance with 40 Cooking. The cooked cake is used to free the Lumbridge Guide in the Recipe for Disaster quest. It is made in a cake tin from an enchanted egg, enchanted milk, and enchanted flour - the same ingredients used to make a regular cake, but each ingredient is enchanted with knowledge by the wizard Traiborn, who lives on the 1st floor of the Wizards' Tower.
7544: The enchanted egg is a quest item used to free the Lumbridge Guide in the Recipe for Disaster quest. It is one of the three ingredients of a Cake of Guidance, the others being enchanted milk and enchanted flour. It is made by having a regular egg enchanted by Wizard Traiborn, who lives on the 1st floor of the Wizards' Tower. The player must complete a small test in which they guess the names of three NPCs who appear from giant eggs.
7545: Enchanted milk is a quest item used to free the Lumbridge Guide in Recipe for Disaster. It is one of the three ingredients of a Cake of Guidance, the others being the enchanted egg and enchanted flour. It is made from a bucket of milk by Wizard Traiborn, who lives on the 1st floor of the Wizards' Tower. The player must first complete a small test where they answer three general questions about Old School RuneScape in order to have it enchanted.
7546: Enchanted flour is a quest item used to free the Lumbridge Guide in Recipe for Disaster. It is one of the three ingredients of a Cake of Guidance, the others being the enchanted egg and enchanted milk. Enchanted flour can be made from a pot of flour by completing a memory test given by Wizard Traiborn in the Wizards' Tower, who will then enchant the flour.
7566:
A raw jubbly is obtained by killing a jubbly bird or jubster during, or after, the Recipe for Disaster quest (after having begun saving Skrach Uglogwee).

It can be cooked with 41 Cooking on the spit located near Rantz or the one located at Jiggig. Cooking a raw jubbly yields 160 experience and produces a cooked jubbly. There is no level that Jubbly will "stop burning" except indirectly at 99 Cooking via a Cooking skill cape or a Max Cape.

Raw jubbly is also used in Creature Creation together with a raw lobster to make a jubster.
7568:
Cooked jubbly is an ogre delicacy obtained by cooking raw jubbly on the spitroast located near Rantz in Feldip Hills or the one located at Jiggig, requiring level 41 Cooking and granting 160 experience when successful. Players may burn the jubbly while cooking one, resulting in burnt jubbly; the burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels.

Eating cooked jubbly will heal 15 Hitpoints, and one is required to complete the Skrach Uglogwee subquest for Recipe for Disaster.
7572:
A red banana is a type of banana found on a tree on the west side of the Ape Atoll. The only way to pick a red banana is to use a rope on the red banana tree while wearing a gorilla greegree. It is used for Freeing King Awowogei in the Recipe for Disaster quest to make a stuffed snake dish fit for a monkey king. It also heals 5 hitpoints if eaten.

After freeing King Awowogei, you can no longer pick the red bananas. When you eat a red banana, you get a message, "You eat the red banana. It's tastier than your average banana."

The red banana can be turned into a sliced red banana by using a knife or any bladed weapon on it. The sliced red banana is used in the Recipe for Disaster quest to stuff the snake used to free King Awowogei. It has no other purpose than to stuff the king's snake, or to use for food while fighting an enemy.

You can only pick a red banana after investigating King Awowogei in the Lumbridge dining room. You are only allowed to pick one at a time, but more can be obtained through the drop trick.
7573:
Tchiki monkey nuts are used in, and only available during, the Freeing King Awowogei subquest of Recipe for Disaster. They are picked from a Tchiki nut bush on the Ape Atoll Agility Course. There is a hole in the ground, inside a partial hut after the rope swing. Climb down the rope to the nut bush, you may only pick one at a time.

They are different from regular monkey nuts. They can be helpful to those who need to heal when doing the Ape Atoll Agility Course. They heal 5 hitpoints, and can be ground with a pestle and mortar to create Tchiki nut paste.

If you return to the three wise monkeys with the nuts and speak to them, Mizaru will swiftly take and eat them, forcing you to go obtain more (this only happens once).

They are considered a delicacy amongst Monkeys, and many legends surround them. One such legend suggests that they are the thing that gave monkeys their superior intelligence, another suggests that they are the food of choice of the Monkey Gods.
7574:
A sliced red banana is the result of using a knife or any bladed weapon on a red banana. When eaten, the sliced red banana heals 5 Hitpoints; the same amount as the original fruit. The message box also states "You eat the sliced red banana. Yum.".

Sliced red banana used in preparing the snake for King Awowogei during Recipe for Disaster. After the quest is complete, there is no further use for red bananas, nor can any more of them be obtained.
7575:
Tchiki nut paste is made by grinding tchiki monkey nuts with a pestle and mortar. Tchiki nut paste is one of the ingredients of stuffed snake, made in the Freeing King Awowogei subquest of Recipe for Disaster.

Tchiki nut paste heals 5 hitpoints when eaten, giving a message "You eat the Tchiki monkey nut paste. It sticks to the roof of your mouth."
7579:
A stuffed snake is made during the Freeing King Awowogei subquest of Recipe for Disaster, and requires level 70 Cooking to make. It is made from stuffing a snake corpse (obtained by killing a Big Snake) with a sliced red banana and tchiki nut paste to obtain a raw stuffed snake and then cooked on the snake-shaped rock in dungeon below Temple of Marimbo. A stuffed snake heals 20 Hitpoints. After completion of Freeing King Awowogei, players can no longer procure the ingredients for a stuffed snake, but can cook more from those left over from the quest.

It is suggested to prepare at least three since there is approximately a 1/4 chance to burn the snake on each attempt at level 70 Cooking. The cooked snake is given to King Awowogei to complete his portion of the quest.

When eaten a message in the chatbox will appear, stating You eat the stuffed snake—it's quite a meal! It tastes like chicken.
7587:

To do this, players have to:

Check the coffins to see their contents.

Check the grave markers to see the respective "owners" of the graves.

7592:
A zombie shirt is a possible reward from the Gravedigger random event and is part of the Zombie outfit. The shirt offers no stat bonuses and is purely cosmetic.

This item can be stored in the fancy dress box of a costume room, as part of the Zombie Outfit set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
7593:
Zombie trousers is a possible reward from the Gravedigger random event and is part of the Zombie outfit. It gives no stat bonuses and is purely cosmetic.

This item can be stored in the fancy dress box of a costume room, as part of the Zombie Outfit set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
7594:

7622:
The bucket of rubble is a quest item made by the player during the In Aid of the Myreque quest. It is made by mining the rubble using a pickaxe in the basement of the bar in Burgh de Rott, and then using a spade or a pot on the remaining bits of rubble with a bucket in the player's inventory. To empty it, players either have to empty it next to the rubble pile outside the bar, or anywhere outside Burgh de Rott. It has no use after the quest.

There are 15 rubble rocks in the basement and a single bucket can hold three bits of rubble, meaning it will take 5 buckets filled in total to clear all of the rubble.

If the player has no room for it, they will put it into a bucket of rubble and will have to find it in the rubble pile outside of the pub. This item depicts the slaying of a vampyre by somebody using the rod of Ivandis, and gives the player a hint of the ingredients required for a Guthix balance potion.
7629:
Dusty scroll may refer to:

Dusty scroll (In Aid of the Myreque), an item obtained during the quest In Aid of the Myreque.

Dusty scroll (Secrets of the North), an item used during the quest Secrets of the North.
7630:
The crate is an item that players use while doing the In Aid of the Myreque quest, specifically while restocking the general store in Burgh de Rott. It is obtained from Aurel to hold the items he requires. Those items are ten bronze axes, ten raw mackerel or raw snails and three tinderboxes.

Despite having a destroy option, it can be placed on a table.
7633: The sleeping seven is a book found during In Aid of the Myreque, written by Keorgius Feryis. After the quest, it is available in the bookcase of a player-owned house, or from a bookcase in the Paterdomus Temple Library.
7634:
Histories of the Hallowland is a book found during In Aid of the Myreque. As its name implies, the content of this book is mostly a history of Morytania. It does also raise questions about the origin of Lord Lowerniel Vergidiyad Drakan.

After the quest, players can find this book in the bookcase of a player-owned house, or in a bookcase in the Paterdomus Temple Library.
7636: Rod dust is what is left behind after using up the 10 charges of a Rod of Ivandis. It remains equipped when the Rod of Ivandis loses its final charge, however after unequipping it cannot be re-equipped. It has no equipment stats, and functions identically to barehanded combat. It has no use at all.
7637:
A silvthrill rod is an item made by using a silver bar, mithril bar, and a sapphire on a furnace with a rod mould in the inventory. It is then enchanted with Lvl-1 Enchant, and dipped it into the River Salve, with a rope, via the well underneath Paterdomus and it will become a rod of Ivandis.

An Enchant sapphire or opal tablet cannot be used to enchant the rod; the Standard spellbook spell must be cast by the player.

As a rod of Ivandis, the weapon has 10 charges in the form of a special attack used to freeze vampyres, allowing you to use a Guthix balance potion on them. If a Guthix balance potion is used, the vampyre will either be destroyed, become angry (stronger, but vulnerable to all attacks) or they will be returned to human form.

It is used during the In Aid of the Myreque quest.

7652:
A Guthix balance (unf) is an unfinished Guthix balance. To make Guthix balance, players must have started In Aid of the Myreque and have at least level 22 Herblore.

They are made by adding garlic to a restore potion (which is made adding harralander and red spider's eggs to a vial of water). This gives 25 Herblore experience. Silver dust should be added to the unfinished potion to make a Guthix balance, also giving 25 experience.

Garlic can be added to restore potion of any dosage; i.e., 1-4 doses. The dosage of the unfinished potion, and finished guthix balance, will be dependent on the original dosage of the restore potion. The number of doses for these unfinished potions is not shown in their names, although it will be for the finished potion. The experience for adding the ingredients is the same, independent of the dosage.

For maximum efficiency, it is recommended that restore potions are decanted into 4-dose potions before Guthix balance potions are created. Alternatively, if being made from scratch for the experience, decanting the potions into 1-dose potions would earn more experience at the cost of more materials. It is generally recommended to only make the unfinished variant if one is an ironman, as garlic is trivial to obtain compared to silver dust, which can drastically increase the time it takes to finish. Rather than a "Make-x" menu like most potions, Guthix balance can be made as fast as the player can click. Despite the low XP per potion, one can gain upwards of 125k Herblore XP/hr with moderate focus and a good stockpile of materials.

7660:
Guthix balance potions are modified restore potions used against frozen Vampyre Juveniles and Juvinates. After freezing the vampyre with the Rod of Ivandis, Ivandis flail, or blisterwood flail and using a dose of the potion on them, one of three outcomes may happen: the vampyre will either be destroyed (16% chance), become feral (16% chance), or be returned to human form (68% chance). The player cannot drink the potion; it is used exclusively against vampyre juveniles and juvinates.

To make this potion, add garlic to a restore potion (made from harralander and red spiders' eggs) to make the unfinished potion. Then add some silver dust (made by using a silver bar on the grinder at the Ectofuntus) to complete the potion. This costs 790 coins if buying the 4 dose restore potion, garlic, and silver dust. The potion cannot be made until the player defeats Gadderanks in In Aid of the Myreque and talks to him to learn how to create the potion.

Rather than a "Make-x" menu like most potions, Guthix balance can be made as fast as the player can click. Despite the low XP per potion, one can gain upwards of 125,000 Herblore experience per hour with moderate focus and a good stockpile of materials.

It is a medium task in the Morytania Diary to make a Guthix balance potion while in Morytania.

7668:
The gadderhammer is a two-handed members-only maul. There are no combat requirements for wielding the gadderhammer. To obtain the gadderhammer the player must defeat Gadderanks during In Aid of the Myreque. Even though it can be purchased from another player or the Grand Exchange, it cannot be wielded until Gadderanks is defeated.

This weapon cannot be made using the Smithing skill. It has a very similar appearance and combat animation to the granite maul, and stats similar to an Adamant warhammer.

If lost, the gadderhammer can be bought from Burgh de Rott's general store owner, Aurel, for 3,000 coins.

The gadderhammer does extra damage against shades (similar to the keris versus kalphites), possessing a 25% damage bonus against shades as well as a 5% chance to deal double damage. The bonus damage when employed against shades stacks with the benefits provided by a salve amulet (e) and Void Knight equipment.

Despite its name, the gadderhammer does not act as a replacement for a hammer, unlike the Imcando hammer.
7671:
Boxing gloves are items that can only be obtained from a glove rack in a player-owned house. They come in two different colours: red and blue. They are categorically a claw weapon, and deal a max hit of 12 to other players in the boxing ring. Other gloves cannot be worn while wielding the boxing gloves, and anything worn in the glove slot will be automatically unequipped when putting them on.

When walking with these equipped your character holds them up to their face in a typical boxing stance. They are the only weapon that can be used in a boxing ring in a player's Combat Room, and they are destroyed if a player tries to leave a house with them. Fighting with them in a player-owned house is their only use.

7675:
Wooden sword is a basic weapon that can only be obtained and used within player-owned houses. They are found on the weapons rack in a player's Combat Room for use in that room. Its stats are identical to those of a bronze sword.

Upon leaving the house with a wooden sword, it will disappear.
7676:
A wooden shield can be found in the weapons rack of a player-owned house. It provides no bonuses.

This shield is obtainable through the Construction skill. Players require at least 35 Construction to build a fencing ring, and subsequently need to be able to construct a 'Level 2 Weapons rack' (44 Construction) to obtain this shield from their own house. However, it may be retrieved from another player's weapons rack.

Upon dropping or leaving the player's house, it is destroyed.
7678: A prize key is obtained after a player wins a game in a Player-owned house (if prizes are offered in the game). It is used to open prize chests that may be found in Games rooms.
7679:
A pugel is the weapon you use on the balance beam, a form of the combat ring in player-owned houses.

It has no wield option, but when stepping on a balance beam, a second pugel will be wielded while the original remains in the player's inventory. The pugel provides no bonuses, and its attack options are the same as when the player is unarmed.

A pugel stick can be obtained by searching an extra weapons rack in a player-owned house. The pugel is a tradeable item within the POH, but disappears once a player leaves the house.
7681:
The Game book, titled Party Pete's Bumper Book of Games, is found on the bookshelves in player-owned houses. It features guides to all of the games the player can make and play if they have a Games room or Combat Room.

The guides include:

Hangman

Fairy Treasure Hunt

Mimic-the-Jester

Elemental balance

Attack stone

Ranging Games (including stick-and-hoop, dartboard and archery game)

Combat (on combat rings)

Prizes (on treasure chests)
7684:
Darts are one of the standard groups of metal ranged weapons. They are a members only thrown weapon that target a monster's light ranged defence. They can be fletched by members with the required Fletching level. However, in order to smith dart tips, the player must have the required Smithing level and completed the Tourist Trap quest. They are made from dart tips and feathers and have an attack range of 3 tiles, 5 with longrange. They can be poisoned and are one-handed, so they can be wielded along with a shield or god book for protection.

Darts, alongside throwing knives, are the quickest ranged weapons in the game making them a fairly popular weapon for Ranged training. The only difference between darts and throwing knives is that knives have small ranged accuracy bonuses, have a slightly longer attack range (4/6 tiles), and are stronger than their dart counterparts; however knives are generally more expensive and traded less often compared to darts.

Darts may be used to load blowpipes as ammunition, which increases ranged accuracy and ranged strength. Unpoisoned darts may be used to load a toxic blowpipe which, as well as increasing ranged accuracy and ranged strength, has a 25% chance to envenom the target.
7686:
The Bow and arrow is an unobtainable item that would have been added alongside Construction. Presumably, it would have been used for the Archery target in the Games room. Its player model and examine description are conflicting, as while the player view model and the name features an actual bow and arrow, the examine and the inventory appearance describe an arrow only.

Most likely it was designed to be an obtainable item, that players would have to collect before they could use the Archery target. This was removed, and players are required to bring their own bow and arrows instead.

Unlike the Hoop or Dart, which can still be seen in the animations for their respective games, the bow and arrow does not appear at all in Old School RuneScape.
7688: A kettle is an item used to make a cup of tea in the kitchen of a player-owned house, allowing the player to temporarily boost Construction by up to 3 levels. An infinite number can be taken from any type of kitchen shelf. Players may use this item on a water source to produce a full kettle. If the player leaves the house this item will disappear from their inventory.
7690:
A full kettle is an item used to make a cup of tea in the kitchen of a player-owned house, allowing the player to temporarily boost Construction by up to 3 levels. To make this item, players must use a kettle on a sink or other water source inside a player-owned house. Players can then use this item on a range to produce a hot kettle. Complete directions on how to make tea can be found here.

Note: If a player leaves the house in any way, the item will disappear from their inventory.
7691:
A hot kettle is an item used to make a cup of tea in the kitchen of a player-owned house allowing the player to temporarily boost Construction by up to 3 levels. A player can obtain this item by placing a full kettle on a range and then removing the kettle from the range. Requiring level 20 Cooking, players can use a hot kettle with a teapot with leaves in order to make a pot of tea and gain 52 experience. Complete directions on how to make tea can be found here.

Note: If a player leaves the house in any way, then this item will disappear from their inventory.
7700:
A teapot with leaves is an item used to make tea in the kitchen of a player-owned house allowing the player to temporarily boost Construction by up to 3 levels. A player can obtain this item by using a teapot with tea leaves. Requiring a Cooking level of 20, players can use this item on a hot kettle, producing a pot of tea and gaining 52 experience. The contents can then be poured into up to 4 empty clay, porcelain, or trimmed porcelain cups.

Regardless of the teapot used in the tea-making process, the boost only depends on the style of cup used.

Note: Leaving the player-owned house will cause all tea-related items to disappear from the inventory.
7702:
A teapot is an item used to make tea in the kitchen of a player-owned house allowing the player to temporarily boost Construction by up to 3 levels. To obtain this item, a player may take an infinite number from any type of kitchen shelf. Teapots come in three different styles depending on the shelf that they are taken from. This item can be used with tea leaves to create a teapot with leaves, which can be brewed after adding water from a hot kettle in order to produce 4 cups of tea.

Regardless of the teapot used in the tea-making process, the boost only depends on the style of cup used.

Note: Leaving the player-owned house will cause all tea-related items to disappear from the inventory.

A cup of tea is a drink made in a player-owned house by using a pot of tea on an empty clay cup. This requires 20 Cooking and gives 52 experience. The tea gives a 1 level Construction boost when drunk. The following shelves contain empty clay cups:

Wooden shelves 1

Wooden shelves 2

Oak shelves 1

Players can also ask their servant to serve tea, and if the best shelves in your kitchen are one of those, the servant will serve this type of tea.

A bucket of milk can be added to the tea to make a milky cup of tea. This has no effect besides changing the colour of the tea and the message when drunk.

Tea from player-owned houses can not be put into a tea flask. If a player leaves the house in any way, then this item will disappear from their inventory.

A bucket of milk can be added to the tea to make a milky cup of tea. This has no effect besides changing the colour of the tea and the message when drunk.

7734:

Wooden shelves 3

Oak shelves 2

Teak shelves 1

7736:
A cup of tea is a drink which restores 3 Hitpoints and temporarily boosts Attack by 2 + 2% (rounded down); it will also instantly cancel the effect of the goading potion. Upon drinking a cup of tea, the player will exclaim Aaah, nothing like a nice cuppa tea! and an empty cup will remain in the player's inventory.

Tea may be purchased at Ye olde Tea Shoppe in Varrock or stolen at the nearby Tea stall with 5 Thieving.

A tea flask may be used to store up to five cups of tea, which will have the standard effect when consumed.
