7738:
Tea leaves is an item used to make a cup of tea in the kitchen of a player-owned house allowing the player to temporarily boost Construction by up to 3 levels. To obtain this item, players may take an infinite number from any type of kitchen larder. Players can then use tea leaves with a teapot producing a teapot with leaves. Complete directions on how to make tea can be found here.

Note: If a player leaves the house in any way then this item will disappear from their inventory.
7744:
Asgarnian ale is a type of ale that restores 1 Hitpoint and temporarily boosts Strength by 2 while draining Attack by ⌊Level×5100⌋+2 (see table below). It can be obtained through brewing at level 24 Cooking granting 248 experience. It is brewed using 2 buckets of water, 2 barley malt, 4 asgarnian hops, and a pot of ale yeast. The stronger, mature version of the ale is the Asgarnian ale(m).

4 Asgarnian ales are required during the Recipe for Disaster Dwarf subquest, where they are turned into Asgoldian ale by using a coin on them. One is also required for the Death Plateau quest.
7746:
Greenman's ale is a type of ale that restores 1 Hitpoint and temporarily boosts Herblore by 1 while also draining Attack, Strength, and Defence by 3 when consumed. It can be obtained through brewing at level 29 Cooking, granting 281 experience per batch. It is brewed using 2 buckets of water, 2 barley malt, 4 harralander, and a pot of ale yeast. The stronger, mature version of the ale is the Greenman's ale (m).

One is required for the quest Recipe for Disaster/Another Cook's Quest.
7748:
Dragon bitter is a variant of dragon bitter that can be obtained in a player-owned house. Players can obtain it by using an empty beer glass on a dragon bitter barrel, which can be built in the kitchen of a player-owned house.

It functions the same as the regular drink, but will disappear from the player's inventory upon leaving the house. It also cannot be used to make a dragon bitter (flatpack).
7750:
Moonlight mead is an unobtainable item intended for use in Construction. It is a variant of moonlight mead that would have been obtained in a player-owned house. Players could have obtained it by using an empty beer glass on a moonlight mead barrel.

For unknown reasons, the Moonlight mead barrel was never added to the game, so the item it produces is unobtainable.
7752:
Cider is a variant of cider that can be obtained in a Player-owned house. Players can obtain it by using an empty beer glass on a cider barrel, which can be built in the kitchen of a player-owned house.

Unlike regular cider, the cider obtained via a barrel will boost the player's Farming level by 2 instead of 1. Additionally, this version of cider will disappear from the player's inventory upon leaving the house.

It also cannot be used to make a cider barrel (flatpack).
7754:
Chef's delight is a type of ale that restores 1 Hitpoint and temporarily boosts Cooking by 5% + 1 while draining Attack and Strength by 5% + 2 (see table below). It can be obtained through brewing at level 54 Cooking granting 446 experience. It is brewed using 2 buckets of water, 2 barley malt, 4 chocolate dust, and 1 pot of ale yeast. The stronger, mature version of the ale is the Chef's delight(m).

A Chef's delight (Player-owned house) can be obtained from a chef's delight barrel, but it cannot be taken out of the player-owned house.
7759: The toy soldier is a wind-up toy made at a Crafting table 3 or 4 in the Workshop of a player-owned house, requiring a clockwork and a regular plank. Level 13 Crafting is needed to assemble the soldier, granting 15 experience. Once wound up, he can be released to walk around the immediate area.
7761: The toy soldier is a wind-up toy made at a Crafting table 3 or 4 in the Workshop of a player-owned house, requiring a clockwork and a regular plank. Level 13 Crafting is needed to assemble the soldier, granting 15 experience. Once wound up, he can be released to walk around the immediate area.
7763:
The toy doll is a clockwork toy. Players can make it at a crafting table 3 in the Workshop of a player-owned house, requiring a clockwork mechanism and a regular plank. A Crafting level of 18 is needed to construct the doll, giving 15 experience points.

Once wound up, the doll may be released to wander around the immediate area. Catching it will yield the player 2.5 Agility experience, though only the player who released it is able to do this. The toy doll also turns around at walls most of the time, while the toy soldier hits the wall and falls over.

Warning: This item is commonly used for scamming, as there are certain areas in the game which do not allow clockwork toys to be released. If a player has an inventory full of toy dolls which cannot be released, they are unable to pick up any more items, effectively locking their inventory.

7767:
The toy mouse is a clockwork item that players can wind up and release, whereupon it will move around on the floor. If the player can catch it before it stops moving, they will gain 3 Agility experience. Despite being a members item, members used to be able to use it on a non-members server. However, this is no longer possible.

Members can make a toy mouse at a crafting table 4 (Construction level 42) in the workshop of a player-owned house. They need level 33 Crafting to construct the mouse, and gain 15 experience in doing so. The raw materials needed are a clockwork (made from a steel bar at any crafting table) and one ordinary plank. Toy mice can also be picked up by Ava's accumulator; the chance of this occurring is 1/2,000.

Cats can chase these clockwork mice. If they catch them they will eat them and the clockwork mouse will be lost.

7771:
The toy cat or clockwork cat is made at a Crafting table 4 in the workshop of a player-owned house, from a clockwork and a regular plank. The toy cat differs from the wooden cat, a quest item which can also be made in the workshop.

A Crafting level of 85 is needed to construct the cat, giving 15 experience points.

The cat may be "released" to follow players around like any regular cat. However, it cannot be fed, catch rats, be petted, be spoken to or be used as a substitute for a real cat in quests. Similarly, the cat may be stored in a pet house in the menagerie of a player-owned house. The clockwork cat does not require any maintenance and will only disappear in the event of the owner's death. If the player attempts to release the cat on a free to play world, they will receive a game message stating "Toy cats do not function on free worlds. If you drop it it will break." and prompt the player to "Drop the cat anyway" or "Keep hold of it". Dropping the cat results in "The toy cat smashes onto the ground".

Toy cats are the only type of pet which can be traded with another player. In addition, players do not have to complete the Gertrude's Cat quest in order to have the clockwork cat follow them.
7774:
Reward tokens are unobtainable items that could originally be obtained from the Temple Trekking minigame. They provided similar rewards to the present day Reward token, but could only be obtained by escorting villagers from Burgh de Rott to the Paterdomus. Players would then have to travel back to Burgh de Rott bank to exchange the token.

In 2007, the minigame was updated with the addition of Burgh de Rott Ramble. They were superseded by new reward tokens which can be exchanged anywhere. As this change occurred prior to August 2007, the original tokens have never been obtainable in Old School RuneScape.

7777: A long vine is a player-made item used to cross a river in Temple Trekking. To make this, players must use a knife on a nearby set of hanging vines to obtain three short vines. The three vine sections are combined by using them on each other, forming a long vine which is then lassoed over a swamp tree to form a rope swing to cross the river. The long vine is lost in process, and therefore cannot be taken outside of the minigame.
7778: A short vine is a player-made item used to cross a river in Temple Trekking. Using a knife on a nearby set of hanging vines yields three short vines. The three vine sections are combined to form a long vine which is then lassoed over a swamp tree to form a rope swing to cross the river.
7779:
A Fishing tome is potential reward from the Temple Trekking minigame, in which players bring followers to Paterdomus or Burgh de Rott.

At the end of a trek, players receive a reward token, which can be exchanged for a number of rewards; should players select the "XP tome" reward option, they will receive a tome granting experience in either Agility, Firemaking, Fishing, Mining, Slayer, Thieving, or Woodcutting, with an equal (one in seven) chance of receiving each tome.

The Fishing tome grants Fishing experience once read. The colour of the tome depends upon the level of the reward token. A higher level reward token will give more Fishing experience.

7800:
Snail shells are dropped by giant snails during the Temple Trekking minigame. These are the default shells; there's also a small chance the snails will drop the perfect snail shell.

This type of snail shell cannot be used to create a snail helmet, and can instead be sold to Barlak in Dorgesh-Kaan for 600 coins.
7803:
The yin yang amulet is a cosmetic amulet that can be purchased from the Makeover Mage for 100 coins. The amulet is a replica of the one the Makeover Mage uses to change the gender of players.

According to the Makeover Mage, they found the amulet after killing a nest of gazulibirds, and asked Doric to make non-magical copies of the amulet as a result of player requests to obtain the amulet as an item.
7804:
The ancient mjolnir is an unobtainable item that was released alongside A Soul's Bane. Although the name would suggest that it was intended as a reward for treasure hunting with the enchanted key, it is most likely that the mjolnir was supposed to be either a reward from the quest, or a fifth Anger weapon.

It is possible that A Soul's Bane was originally intended to serve as a sequel to The Dig Site. Tolna's Rift is located very close to Senntisten, while Tolna states that he encountered the ruins of an ancient civilisation who used to worship a god, watched over by an evil power. The pattern on the ancient mjolnir matches the one found in the Senntisten temple; therefore it is possible that the mjolnir would have been the original reward from the quest.

For unknown reasons, the mjolnir was ultimately not released, and therefore has never been obtainable in Old School RuneScape.
7807: Anger battleaxe is an item that is used only during A Soul's Bane quest. It is used to kill Angry goblins, and the apparent damage it does is the player's normal damage multiplied by 10, meaning that you will hit three digits frequently. Unfortunately the player won't get any experience when using it. It is found from the weapon rack in the rage room, and cannot be taken out of the room.
7808: An anger mace is an item that is used only during A Soul's Bane quest. It is used to kill angry giant rats, and the apparent damage it does is the player's normal damage multiplied by 10, meaning that you will hit three digits frequently. Unfortunately the player won't get any experience when using it. It is found from the weapon rack in the rage room, and cannot be taken out of the room.
7810:
A jug of vinegar can be bought from Fortunato in Draynor Village for 1 coin after starting the Rag and Bone Man I quest (Note: If you do not see Jug of vinegar in his shop, talk to Fortunato and ask about vinegar). When decanted into an empty pot it becomes a pot of vinegar and an empty jug. Bones from various creatures around Gielinor can then be added to the pot (one bone per pot) and boiled over the fire outside the Odd Old Man's house. This will clean the bones and they can then be given to the old man to complete the quest.

A total of 35 jugs of vinegar are needed for Rag and Bone Man I (8) as well as Rag and Bone Man II (27).
7811: A pot of vinegar can be made by pouring a jug of vinegar into an empty pot. During the Rag and Bone Man I quest various bones that are dropped from creatures around Gielinor can be added to the pot (one bone per pot, 8 pots total) and boiled over the fire outside the Odd Old Man's house. This will clean the bones and they can then be given to the old man to complete the quest (you don't have to bring them all together in the quest though).
7813:
Bone in vinegar is an item that players use during the Rag and Bone Man I and Rag and Bone Man II quests. It is made by using certain one-time drop bones (such as a wolf bone) with a pot of vinegar. Due to the fact that each bone in vinegar contains a different bone, they do not stack in the inventory or bank.

All the bones in vinegar look identical, but the examine text differs for each one. For example:

There is a cave goblin skull in here.

There is a seagull wing in here.

There is a ghoul bone in here.

Take care not to accidentally empty the pot during your quest or when cleaning the bones. You will be left with only the empty pot, forcing you to retrieve the bone all over again.
7815:
Bear ribs are a bone dropped by bears that are on the Odd Old Man's wish-list during the Rag and Bone Man I quest. They must be put in a pot of vinegar, making a bone in vinegar, which then must be boiled on the pot-boiler to produced polished bear ribs. The polished bones can then be handed in to the Odd Old Man.

After the quest is complete, it is no longer possible to obtain this item.

Due to the fact that each bone in vinegar contains a different bone, they do not stack in the inventory or bank.

All the bones in vinegar look identical, but the examine text differs for each one. For example:

There is a cave goblin skull in here.

There is a seagull wing in here.

There is a ghoul bone in here.

Take care not to accidentally empty the pot during your quest or when cleaning the bones. You will be left with only the empty pot, forcing you to retrieve the bone all over again.
7916: The jackal bone is an item on the Odd Old Man's wish list during Rag and Bone Man II. It is dropped by jackals. After the quest is completed you can no longer obtain this as a drop. The bone must be put into a pot of vinegar and boiled to create a polished jackal bone before giving it to the Odd Old Man.
7917:
The ram skull helm is a helmet given as a reward, alongside the bonesack, for completing Rag and Bone Man II. If lost, the Odd Old Man will offer a replacement for free.

It requires 30 Defence to wear. The helmet's stats are nearly identical to those of an adamant full helmet, the only differences being the lack of negative Magic attack and defence bonuses, and a slightly higher Ranged accuracy.
7918:
The bonesack is a large sack filled with bones worn in the cape slot. Alongside the ram skull helm, it is given to the player as a reward for completing Rag and Bone Man II. If lost, the Odd Old Man will offer a replacement for free.

Despite appearing to hold bones, the bonesack cannot store any bones.

Due to the item's defensive bonuses it's considered to be armour and you will be denied passage to Entrana while possessing it.
7921:
An empty wine bottle is the by-product of drinking a bottle of wine. It cannot be refilled in any way, so therefore it is essentially a useless item.

Fortunato in Draynor Market buys back all empty wine bottles for 2 coins a piece. This option, however, does not come up in any dialogue; you must use the empty wine bottle on him.
7922:
The Al Kharid flyer is an item given by Ali the Leaflet Dropper. He is located at the northern entrance of Al Kharid just above the Al Kharid mine.

On free-to-play worlds, it can be used to access the shop of Ali Morrisane by using the flyer on him. When opening the store this way, one sees members items, but is not able to buy those. Besides this, the flyer is useless.
7934:
Field rations can be bought from the Void Knight General Store in the Pest Control hub or Jennifer's General Supplies in Shayzien. They can be eaten to restore 10 hitpoints, making them effectively equivalent to tuna.

Field rations are not commonly used by players either in Pest Control or beyond. Healing is not typically a priority in Pest Control because there is no penalty for death and players respawn immediately with their health and prayer replenished. Outside of Pest Control, there are simply cheaper and more effective alternatives available in greater quantities.
7936:
Pure essence is a raw material used in the Runecraft skill to make all types of runes. They can create the same runes as rune essence as well as cosmic, chaos, astral, nature, law, death, blood, wrath, and any combination runes. Pure essence does not provide any bonus over rune essence when crafting runes lower than cosmic runes; they are however much cheaper.

Unlike runes, pure essence does not stack. Essence pouches can be used to transport additional essence, when collecting or using pure essence to craft runes. Pure essence is one of the most commonly traded items in Old School RuneScape, due to its very high demand by runecrafters.
7938:
Dark essence fragments are items created by using a chisel on dark essence blocks, providing 8 Crafting experience per block. Each block will create 4 pieces of essence, which are used to runecraft blood and soul runes. Players cannot hold more than 108 fragments at a time, with 111 at a maximum if a stack of 108 is picked up while holding a stack of 4+. The fragments cannot be stored in a bank. Dark essence fragments vanish upon death.

Blood runes can be made at Kourend's Blood Altar at 77 Runecraft (can be boosted) and will provide 23.8 experience per dark essence fragment.

Soul runes can be made at 90 Runecraft and will provide 29.7 experience per dark essence fragment.
7939:
Tortoise shells are dropped by tortoises, who can drop up to three shells at a time per kill. They can be sold to Barlak in Dorgesh-Kaan for 600 coins. The shells must be unnoted in order to sell them to Barlak.

Barlak does NOT grant any Crafting experience for this item. He will only grant Crafting experience for perfect shells, a rarer counterpart to tortoise shells.
7941: An iron sheet is made by placing an Iron bar into the press at the Piscatoris Fishing Colony furnace building. It is used to repair the colony wall during the quest Swan Song. It has no further uses after the quest, and can be sold to Franklin Caranos for 20 coins after the quest. It can be made using the Smithing skill, which grants 20 Smithing experience.
7942:
Fresh monkfish are caught during Swan Song. Fresh monkfish heal 1 hitpoint when successfully cooked and then consumed.

Like regular monkfish, players need a Fishing level of 62 to catch fresh monkfish, but using boosts such as a fishing potions at 59 or an admiral pie at 57 may be used.

During the quest, Arnold Lydspor asks players to refill the fishing colony's food stocks. Players must catch and successfully cook five fresh monkfish. Catching a few extra in case some burn while cooking is not a bad idea, as even players with 99 Cooking may burn them. However it is not recommended that players train Fishing during the quest, as these quest-specific fresh monkfish only provide 1 experience for catching and 10 experience for cooking. If eaten players will heal 1 hitpoint and receive the message: It's so fresh that it's got no flavour, and it doesn't heal much health either.
7943:
Fresh monkfish are caught during Swan Song. Fresh monkfish heal 1 hitpoint when successfully cooked and then consumed.

Like regular monkfish, players need a Fishing level of 62 to catch fresh monkfish, but using boosts such as a fishing potions at 59 or an admiral pie at 57 may be used.

During the quest, Arnold Lydspor asks players to refill the fishing colony's food stocks. Players must catch and successfully cook five fresh monkfish. Catching a few extra in case some burn while cooking is not a bad idea, as even players with 99 Cooking may burn them. However it is not recommended that players train Fishing during the quest, as these quest-specific fresh monkfish only provide 1 experience for catching and 10 experience for cooking. If eaten players will heal 1 hitpoint and receive the message: It's so fresh that it's got no flavour, and it doesn't heal much health either.
7946:
Monkfish is a type of fish that restores 16 Hitpoints when eaten.

It can be obtained by cooking raw monkfish on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 62 Cooking and granting 150 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt monkfish. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 90 on ranges and level 92 on fires.

When eaten, the message You eat the monkfish.

It heals some health. is displayed.

While the Swan Song quest must be completed to fish raw monkfish, there is no such requirement for cooking them.

Catching and cooking a monkfish is a requirement for the hard Western Provinces Diary.
7948:
Burnt monkfish is the result of accidentally burning a fresh or raw monkfish while attempting to make a monkfish. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 92; wearing cooking gauntlets will stop them from burning at level 87 instead.

The burnt monkfish has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.
7950:
Bone seeds are obtained during and after the Swan Song quest. To obtain the item, one must talk to Malignius Mortifer with an airtight pot (consists of a pot and a pot lid) in the inventory. When opened a non-attackable Skeleton Mage will appear, perform a random emote, and then die. The animation occurs randomly on 1 tile away from the player.

Players may only own one pot of bone seeds at a time. Dropping the pot of bone seed will result in the magic of the bone seeds escaping from the pot. They cannot be used around Malignius Mortifier, as he will request the player move further away before opening them.
7954:
Burnt shrimp is the result of accidentally burning a raw shrimp while attempting to make a shrimp. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 34.

The burnt shrimp has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.
7956:
A casket is an item occasionally dropped by monsters that are near oceans or bodies of water. It can also be obtained via big net fishing, at a rate of about 1/128 at lower levels and 1/85.3 at higher levels. The fishing spot in Civitas illa Fortis has around a 1 in 5 chance of rewarding a casket, making this one of the most reliable places to obtain them. It can be opened to receive a small amount of treasure. Wearing a skills necklace with at least one charge while big net fishing will slightly increase the chance of finding a casket.

For ironmen, these can be a good early source of a Cosmic talisman.
7957:
The White apron is an unobtainable item that can be seen hanging on the wall of Gerrant's Fishy Business. If the player picks it up, they will be given a regular white apron instead. It is therefore designed to serve as an infinite source of aprons, but the actual hanging apron cannot be obtained by the player.

Trying to obtain the white apron via telekinetic grab does not work, with a message stating "It seems to be firmly on the hook. I cannot get that this way."
7958: The Mining prop is a quest item found during the Royal Trouble quest. It is given to the player by a dwarf called Donal in the dungeons of Miscellania castle. The player must use the prop to hold open a crack in the rocks that allows passage deeper into the dungeons. If you use a Tinderbox with it, the message "The tunnel will collapse if you do that!" will appear.
7959: The heavy box is a quest item found during the Royal Trouble quest. It is obtained by killing the Giant Sea Snake encountered at the end of the quest. The box must then be taken to Queen Sigrid to receive a letter that has to be delivered to King Vargas. The box will then stay in your inventory as an empty box - which has no further use.
7961:
The burnt diary is a book that acts as a quest item in the Royal Trouble quest. The title of the book (visible when reading it) may variably be Charred diary, Armod's Charred Diary, or Armod's Burnt Diary. It seems to change as the quest progresses, though the item name remains the same.

Players find the pages of the book in the remains of fires in the tunnels beneath Miscellania and Etceteria during the quest. Players put them together to make this book. The item's examine text also seems to change to reflect how many of the five pages the player has found so far.

The diary reveals that Armod and his friends have been causing all the trouble between the two kingdoms. He and his friends intended to cause a war, and then act as peacemakers in reconciling them. This is because they have been unable to complete The Fremennik Trials.

If lost, the book can be reclaimed from a bookcase within a player-owned house.
7962:
The burnt diary is a book that acts as a quest item in the Royal Trouble quest. The title of the book (visible when reading it) may variably be Charred diary, Armod's Charred Diary, or Armod's Burnt Diary. It seems to change as the quest progresses, though the item name remains the same.

7966:
Letter may refer to one of the following:

Items simply named "Letter":

Letter obtained during Creature of Fenkenstrain

Letter obtained during Forgettable Tale...

Letter obtained during The Golem

Letter obtained during Royal Trouble

Letter obtained during The Queen of Thieves

Letter can be found in the eastern building in Auburnvale that houses the belladonna patch

Letter can be found in the eastern building in Sunset Coast

Old letter can be found upstairs in Sunrise Palace

Ancient letter, obtained during The Forsaken Tower

Hosidius letter, obtained from the Arceuus Library

Important letter, obtained during The Frozen Door miniquest

Letters obtained during Making History:

Letter (King Lathas)

Letter (Jorral)

Letters obtained during The Dig Site quest:

Unstamped letter

Sealed letter

Invitation letter

Letters obtained during What Lies Below:

Letter to Surok

Surok's letter

Mourner letter, obtained during Mourning's End Part I

Unsealed letter, obtained during The Fremennik Exiles
7969:
The pulley beam is a quest item found during the Royal Trouble quest. It is used to repair the lift that takes the player further into the dungeons beneath Miscellania castle.

Combining a beam with a pulley beam turns it into a long pulley beam, and combining this with another beam turns it into a longer pulley beam.
7970:
The long pulley beam is a quest item found during the Royal Trouble quest. It is used to repair the lift that takes the player further into the dungeons beneath Miscellania castle.

Combining a beam with a pulley beam turns it into a long pulley beam, and combining this with another beam turns it into a longer pulley beam.
7971:
The longer pulley beam is a quest item obtained during the Royal Trouble quest. It is used to repair the lift that takes the player further into the dungeons beneath Miscellania castle.

Combining a beam with a pulley beam turns it into a long pulley beam, and combining this with another beam turns it into a longer pulley beam.
7972:
A lift manual, or AMCE Lift-In-A-Box User Manual, is obtained during the Royal Trouble quest. It is a guide to using the Lift-In-A-Box system, which is being used by a number of dwarves in their efforts to expand the caves beneath Miscellania. The Lift-In-A-Box is a product of Ali Morrisane Commercial Enterprises Ltd., one of the many projects of famed entrepreneur Ali Morrisane.

It can be obtained again from the table in the dungeon if lost.

It cannot be stored in nor retrieved from the bookcase of a player-owned house.
7977:
A basilisk head is a rare drop from basilisks and basilisk knights, requiring 40 and 60 Slayer to kill respectively. It can be stuffed at the Taxidermist in Canifis by using the item on her and paying 4,000 coins, returning a stuffed basilisk head. When players take it to her, she will tell players "My, he's a scary-looking fellow, isn't it? He'll look good on your wall!"

Once stuffed, it can be mounted at a teak, mahogany, or gilded display within the skill hall in a player-owned house, granting 63 Construction and 343 Slayer experience.

The head can alternatively be sacrificed to the Dark Altar north of Arceuus, granting 2,500 Prayer experience.
7978:
A kurask head is a rare drop from kurasks, requiring 70 Slayer to kill. It can be stuffed at the Taxidermist in Canifis by using the item on her and paying 6,000 coins, returning a stuffed kurask head. When players take it to the taxidermist, she will tell players "A kurask? Splendid! Look at those horns!"

Once stuffed, it can be mounted at a mahogany or gilded display within the skill hall in a player-owned house, granting 77 Construction and 657 Slayer experience. Alternatively, the head can be sacrificed to the Dark Altar north of Arceuus, granting 2,500 Prayer experience.

Lastly, the kurask head or stuffed kurask head can be used to enhance the ornate undead combat dummy, enabling it to act as a monster that can only be damaged by leaf-bladed weapons.
7979:
An abyssal head is a rare drop from abyssal demons, requiring 85 Slayer to kill. Players may also obtain an abyssal head by placing an unsired at the Font of Consumption; this has a 5/64 chance, and as an unsired is a 1/100 drop, this effectively makes it a 1/1,280 drop per Abyssal Sire kill.

Abyssal heads can be stuffed at the Taxidermist in Canifis by using the item on her and paying 12,000 coins, returning a stuffed abyssal head. When players take it to her, she will tell players "Goodness, an abyssal demon! See how it's still glowing? I'll have to use some magic to preserve that."

Once stuffed, it can be mounted at a mahogany or gilded display within the skill hall in a player-owned house, granting 109 Construction and 889 Slayer experience. Alternatively, the head can be sacrificed to the Dark Altar north of Arceuus, granting 2,500 Prayer experience.

Lastly, the head can be combined with a slayer helmet or slayer helmet (i) to create a red slayer helmet or red slayer helmet (i), respectively. Doing so requires purchasing the ability Unholy Helmet for 1,000 Slayer reward points.
7981:
The Kq head is a rare drop from the Kalphite Queen. It can be stuffed at the Taxidermist in Canifis by using the item on her and paying 50,000 coins, returning a stuffed kq head. When players take it to her, she will tell players "That must be the biggest kalphite I've ever seen! Preserving insects is always tricky. I'll have to be careful..."

Once stuffed, it can be mounted at a gilded display within the skill hall in a player-owned house, granting 223 Construction alongside 200 Attack, Strength, Defence, Magic, and Ranged experience, with players being given the option to decline the combat experience before mounting the heads. Talking to a mounted kalphite queen head in your POH is a task in the Elite Desert Diary. Alternatively, the head can be sacrificed to the Dark Altar north of Arceuus, granting 2,500 Prayer experience.

Lastly, the head can be combined with a slayer helmet or slayer helmet (i) to create a green slayer helmet or green slayer helmet (i), respectively. Doing so requires purchasing the ability Kalphite Khat for 1,000 Slayer reward points.
7986:
A stuffed abyssal head is obtained by bringing an abyssal head and 12,000 coins to the taxidermist in Canifis; this process is reversible by selecting the "Unstuff" option on the item.

Once stuffed, it can be mounted at a mahogany or gilded display within the skill hall in a player-owned house, granting 109 Construction and 889 Slayer experience.
7989:
A big bass is an abnormally large bass caught while fishing at any big net/harpoon fishing spot, requiring 46 Fishing to catch. Players have a 1/1,000 to receive a big bass in place of a raw bass; catching one results in the game message You catch an enormous bass! instead of the usual You catch a raw bass. If fishing with a fish barrel, a big bass will be placed into the inventory. Additionally, big bass cannot be cooked.

It can be stuffed at the taxidermist in Canifis by using the item on her and paying 1,000 coins, returning a stuffed big bass. When players take it to her, she will tell players "That's a mighty fine sea bass you've caught there." Once stuffed, it can be mounted at an oak, teak or mahogany display within the skill hall in a player-owned house, granting 31 Construction and 151 Fishing experience.

The benefits of Rada's blessing and spirit flakes will cause two big basses to be caught at once if either item activates. The extra big bass will not be counted in the collection log if this happens.
7991:
A big swordfish is an abnormally large swordfish caught while fishing for swordfish at any cage/harpoon fishing spot, requiring 50 Fishing to catch (or 70 Fishing and 50 Strength for barehanded fishing). Players have a 1/2,500 chance to receive a big swordfish in place of a raw swordfish; catching one results in the game message You catch an enormous swordfish! instead of the usual You catch a raw swordfish. If fishing with a fish barrel, a big swordfish will be placed into the inventory. Additionally, big swordfish cannot be cooked.

It can be stuffed at the taxidermist in Canifis by using the item on her and paying 2,500 coins, returning a stuffed big swordfish. When players take it to her, she will tell players "Don't point that thing at me!" Once stuffed, it can be mounted at a teak or mahogany display within the skill hall in a player-owned house, granting 50 Construction and 230 Fishing experience.

The benefits of Rada's blessing and spirit flakes will cause two big swordfish to be caught at once if either item activates. The extra big swordfish will not be counted in the collection log if this happens.
7993:
A big shark is an abnormally large shark caught while fishing at any harpoon/big net fishing spot, requiring 76 Fishing to catch (or 96 Fishing and 76 Strength for barehanded fishing). Players have a 1/5,000 chance to receive a big shark in place of a raw shark; catching one results in the game message You catch an enormous shark! instead of the usual You catch a shark! If fishing with a fish barrel, a big shark will be placed into the inventory. Additionally, big shark cannot be cooked, nor will catching one complete the elite clue scroll step given by Sherlock.

It can be stuffed at the taxidermist in Canifis by using the item on her and paying 5,000 coins, returning a stuffed big shark. When players take it to her, she will tell players "That's quite a fearsome shark! You have done everyone a service by removing it from the sea!" Once stuffed, it can be mounted at a mahogany display within the skill hall in a player-owned house, granting 70 Construction and 350 Fishing experience.

The benefits of Rada's blessing and spirit flakes will cause two big sharks to be caught at once if either item activates. The additional big shark will not be counted in the collection log if this happens.
7995: The Arthur portrait, depicting King Arthur of Camelot, is available in Falador from Sir Renitee for 1,000 coins. Completion of the Holy Grail quest is necessary to purchase this portrait. It may be framed in a player's Player-owned house with 35 construction, two teak planks and hung in the Quest Hall. The result of doing so is the King Arthur portrait.
7996:
Elena portrait is a portrait of Elena from the Plague City quest series, which can be hung in the Quest Hall of a Player-owned house. This portrait is sold by Sir Renitee, in Falador castle, for 1,000 coins. Hanging this portrait requires the completion of Plague City quest, level 35 Construction, and 2 Teak planks. The result of doing so is the Elena portrait.

Not to be confused with the Picture (of Elena) used in the Plague City quest, which cannot be hung on a wall. Likewise, the Elena portrait cannot be used as a substitute for the Picture during Plague City.
7998: This picture of the Prince Brand and Princess Astrid is available in Falador, bought from Sir Renitee for 1,000 coins. Completion of Throne of Miscellania is necessary to purchase this portrait. It may be framed in one's player-owned house with 55 Construction, two mahogany planks and hung in the Quest Hall. The result of doing so is the Miscellanians portrait.
7999:
The desert painting is an item that players can buy from Sir Renitee in White Knights' Castle for 2,000 coins, provided that they have completed Prince Ali Rescue, Tourist Trap, The Feud, and The Golem.

It is used in the Quest Hall of a player-owned house (along with three teak planks) to build The desert in the landscape painting hotspot. Doing so requires level 44 Construction, and grants 314 experience.
8000:
The Isafdar painting is an item that players can buy from Sir Renitee in White Knights' Castle for 2,000 coins by asking him for a painting of a landscape, provided that they have completed Roving Elves.

It is used in the Quest Hall of a player-owned house (along with a hammer, saw, and three mahogany planks) to build Isafdar in the landscape space. Doing so requires level 65 Construction, and grants 464 experience.

Building an Isafdar painting in your POH is a requirement for the Hard Western Provinces Diary.
8001:
The Karamja painting is an item that players can buy from Sir Renitee in White Knights' Castle for 2000 coins, provided that they have completed Pirate's Treasure, Tai Bwo Wannai Trio, and Shilo Village.

It is used in the Quest Hall of a player-owned house (along with three mahogany planks) to build Karamja in the landscape painting hotspot. Doing so requires level 65 Construction, and grants 464 experience.
8004:
The small map is an item that players can buy from Sir Renitee in White Knights' Castle for 1000 coins, provided that they have at least 51 quest points.

It is used in the Quest Hall of a player-owned house (along with two teak planks) to build the small map in the map hotspot. Doing so requires level 38 Construction, and grants 211 experience.
8006:
The large map is an item that players can buy from Sir Renitee in White Knights' Castle for 1000 coins, provided that they have at least 151 quest points.

It is used in the Quest Hall of a player-owned house (along with four mahogany planks) to build the large map in the map hotspot. Doing so requires level 78 Construction, and grants 591 experience.
8009:
The Falador teleport is a magic tablet that can be broken by players to teleport to Falador.

Players can create this item on an eagle lectern, a teak eagle lectern, or a mahogany eagle lectern. To make it, level 37 Magic, 1 law rune, 3 air runes, 1 water rune, and 1 soft clay is required, which grants 48 experience. A single Falador tablet can be obtained from Marlo's crate, a reward from the Daddy's Home miniquest.

This tablet can be made and used regardless of the player's current spellbook. The user does not need the relevant Magic level to use the tablet, which shares the same rule with all tablets not including Ardougne tablet, house tablet, and Watchtower teleport, as they require quests or having a player-owned house.
8010:
The Camelot teleport is a magic tablet that can be broken by players to teleport to Camelot.

Players can create this item on a Teak eagle lectern, a Mahogany eagle lectern, or a Marble Lectern as long as they have 1 law rune, 5 air runes, and 1 soft clay and at least level 45 Magic, granting 55.5 experience. In addition to using air runes, a player may also use a staff of air to reduce the cost and allow for an extra inventory slot.

This tablet can be made regardless of the player's current spellbook. As with all tablets, the user does not need to have the relevant Magic level to use this tablet.
8011:
The Ardougne teleport is a magic tablet that can be broken by players to teleport to East Ardougne. Using the tablet requires completion of Plague City, however, players do not have to read the Ardougne teleport scroll to use the tablet.

Players with level 51 Magic can create this item on a Teak eagle lectern or better in a player-owned house. This requires 2 law runes, 2 water runes, and 1 soft clay. Creating a tablet grants 61 Magic experience, the same as casting the Ardougne Teleport spell. Elemental staves can be substituted for runes and are recommended when making teleport tablets in large groups at a time.

As with all teleport tablets, using an Ardougne teleport tablet does not grant any experience.
8016:
An enchant sapphire or opal tablet is the magic tablet version of the Lvl-1 Enchant spell. It can be used by any player to enchant sapphire or opal jewellery. Players with 7 Magic can create this item on any lectern with 1 cosmic rune, 1 water rune, and 1 soft clay, granting 13.2 Magic experience. This tablet can be made regardless of the player's current spellbook.

As with all magic tablets, using this tablet does not have a Magic level requirement and grants no experience.

The tablet cannot be used to enchant the silvthrill rod during In Aid of the Myreque, nor can it be used to enchant portal frames within the Hallowed Sepulchre.
8017:
The enchant emerald or jade tablet is an item that can be used by any player to enchant emerald or jade jewellery. Players can create this item on either a demon lectern, a teak demon lectern, or a mahogany demon lectern as long as they have 1 cosmic rune, 3 air runes, and 1 soft clay, and at least level 27 Magic. This tablet is built using the Construction skill and works regardless of your Magic level. This single-use enchantment tablet enchants emerald jewellery.

This tablet can be made regardless of the player's current spell book. Using a Staff of air can reduce the cost of casting the spell.
8018:
The enchant ruby or topaz tablet is an item that can be used by any player to enchant ruby and red topaz jewellery. Players can create this item on either a teak demon lectern or a mahogany demon lectern as long as they have 1 cosmic rune, 5 fire runes, and 1 soft clay, and at least level 49 Magic.

This tablet can be made regardless of the player's current spell book. Using a staff of fire or lava battlestaff can reduce the costs of casting the spell.
8019:

Banners, also referred to as flags, are a category of melee weapons. They are essentially wieldable signs. Categorically they are similar to spears, but their lack of combat bonuses suggests they aren’t intended for combat.

Players cannot wield banners when on a PvP world, as their large clickbox could be used to grief other players. If the player already has a banner equipped when switching to one of these worlds, it will automatically be unequipped and moved to the player's inventory if it has space, or to their bank if it does not. In case both are full, the banner will be sent to Perdu, from whom it can be reclaimed at no cost. There are some exceptions to the banner ban: players can still hoist a trailblazer, shattered, or protest banner on a PvP or target world.

8778:
Oak planks are a type of plank in the Construction skill. Each plank gives 60 Construction experience when used.

A single oak plank is worth on average of ~175 experience when used in novice Mahogany Homes contracts (including completion bonus), and 150 experience when used to fix the broken bridges in the Hallowed Sepulchre, also requiring mithril nails.

Oak planks are most commonly obtained from hunting Eclectic implings, fighting Vet'ion/Calvar'ion, and as a common reward from elite clue scrolls.
8782:
Mahogany planks are the highest level planks used in the Construction skill, used to make some of the highest-level furniture. Each plank gives 140 experience when used in a player-owned house, 105 experience when used to build mahogany repair kits, an average of 346.1 experience when used in expert Mahogany Homes contracts (including completion bonus), and 350 experience when used to fix the broken bridges in the Hallowed Sepulchre.

The lowest construction level required to build something in your player-owned house is 40, for either a tip jar or mahogany bookcase.
8784: Gold leaf is an item used in Construction, yielding 300 Construction experience per leaf used when building many decorative items for a player-owned house. It is also used for master STASH units. It can be bought from the Stonemason in south-western Keldagrim or Metla in Stonecutter Outpost for 130,000 coins. It cannot be made by players.
8786: Marble blocks are used in the Construction skill. They can only be bought in Keldagrim from the Stonemason, or in Stonecutter Outpost from Metla for 325,000 coins. Unlike limestone bricks, marble blocks cannot be made by players. Marble blocks are commonly used to build high-level furniture and decorations in a player-owned house, yielding 500 experience per block used.
8788:
A Magic stone is used in the Construction and Sailing skills to build very high level items in player-owned houses and boats; it is also used in the construction of bank chests on various islands accessible through Sailing.

It is available from the Stonemason in south-western Keldagrim or Metla in Stonecutter Outpost for 975,000 coins each.
8790:
A bolt of cloth is used in the Construction skill to build objects such as wooden beds, curtains, and also rugs. Bolts of cloth can be purchased from a Sawmill Operator for 650 coins and provide 15 Construction experience each when used.

One bolt of cloth is used in the quest Making Friends with My Arm, and five are used in the Daddy's Home miniquest.
8792: Clockwork can be made on a Crafting table 2 or better in the Workshop of a Player-owned house. A Clockwork requires a steel bar and level 8 Crafting to make and gives 15 Crafting experience.
8837: Timber beams are used in the Shades of Mort'ton quest and Shades of Mort'ton minigame. The beams can be used in place of planks during the minigame. They have no further use outside the quest and minigame.
8839:
The Void Knight top is a piece of Void Knight equipment. It can be bought from a Void Knight for 250 Void Knight commendation points through the Pest Control mini game, although a player must have at least 42 Attack, Strength, Defence, Hitpoints, Ranged, and Magic, along with 22 Prayer to buy and wear one.

It is worn in combination with the other pieces of Void Knight Armour to achieve the designated set effect, depending on which helm is worn. This chestpiece does not interfere with Ava's devices. Unlike the Void knight robe, the Void knight top doesn't have more Magic Defence than its blessed d'hide counterparts (+45, as opposed to a blessed d'hide body's +50).

It can be upgraded into an Elite void top for 200 Void Knight commendation points, although a player must have completed the hard Western Provinces Diary tasks to be able to upgrade it. The top can also be given to the Dodgy Squire in exchange for 200 Void Knight commendation points.

If the player dies a PvP death at level 20 Wilderness or below and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 180,000 coins.

If the player dies a PvP death above level 20 Wilderness and the item is unprotected, it will be converted to coins. To prevent this, a Trouver parchment and a payment of 500,000 coins can be given to Perdu in order to permanently lock the item. The locked item will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a mangled, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 500,000 coins.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Void Knight armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
8840:
The Void Knight robe is a piece of Void Knight equipment. It can be bought from a Void Knight for 250 Void Knight commendation points through the Pest Control minigame, although a player must have at least 42 Attack, Strength, Defence, Hitpoints, Ranged, and Magic, along with 22 Prayer to buy and wear one.

It is worn in combination with the other pieces of Void Knight Armour to achieve the designated set effect, depending on which helm is worn.

It can be upgraded into an Elite void robe for 200 Void Knight commendation points, although a player must have completed the hard Western Provinces Diary tasks to be able to upgrade it. The robe can also be given to the Dodgy Squire in exchange for 200 Void Knight commendation points.

The robe is notable for having a high magic defence bonus, higher than that of blessed and black dragonhide chaps, without having any negative attack bonuses in addition to being non-degradable. The void robe bottom can therefore be a decent alternative to Karil's leatherskirt in melee gear setups aiming to maximise defence against magic.

If the player dies a PvP death at level 20 Wilderness or below and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 180,000 coins.

If the player dies a PvP death above level 20 Wilderness and the item is unprotected, it will be converted to coins. To prevent this, a Trouver parchment and a payment of 500,000 coins can be given to Perdu in order to permanently lock the item. The locked item will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a mangled, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 500,000 coins.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Void Knight armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
8841:
The Void Knight mace can be bought from a Void Knight for 250 commendation points, although a player must have 42 Attack, Strength, Defence, Hitpoints, Ranged, and Magic, along with 22 Prayer. The mace can be used to autocast Claws of Guthix, Crumble Undead, and the Wave and Surge spells. To cast Claws of Guthix, the player must have cast the spell 100 times in the Wilderness Mage Arena.

Note that the Void knight mace does not count towards the four pieces needed for the void set effect.

Its stats are relatively close to that of the rune mace, with the main difference being its 20% slower attack speed. It also has +2 bonus in Stab, Slash, and Crush attack, as well as Stab, Slash, Crush, Magic, and Ranged defence, as well as a relative +2 Strength and Prayer bonus compared to the rune mace. Due to its role as one of the weapons to cast Claws of Guthix, it also has a +8 Magic attack bonus. These stats make it one of the only melee weapons in game to have a positive ranged defence bonus, other than the Lunar staff, with +1, and the dragon spear and Zamorakian spear, with +5 and +13, respectively. Unlike other maces, it only has crushing attack styles. Alongside croziers, the hallowed flail, and the 3rd Age druidic staff, it has the highest Prayer bonus of all one-handed weapons.

While Claws of Guthix can be cast and autocast while wearing an imbued Saradomin cape or imbued Zamorak cape, an appropriate cape (Guthix cape or its imbued variant) must still be worn to receive the damage boost from Charge.

If the player dies a PvP death and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 20,000 coins.

The mace can also be given to the Dodgy Squire in exchange for 200 Void Knight commendation points.
8844:
The bronze defender is the weakest defender. It is similar to a dagger, but held in the off-hand in place of a shield. The bronze defender is dropped by cyclopes on the top floor of the Warriors' Guild. Entry to the Cyclops room requires a minimum of 100 Warrior guild tokens.

If the player dies to a PvP death and the bronze defender is not one of the player's protected items, it will remain in the player's inventory, but will become broken, which means the item is unusable and must be repaired with 1,000 coins by using the item on Perdu.
8846:
The steel defender is the third weakest defender. It is similar to a dagger, but held in the off-hand in place of a shield. It requires 5 Attack and 5 Defence to wield. The steel defender is dropped by Cyclopes on the top floor of the Warriors' Guild, but only once you have obtained an iron defender.

If the player dies to a PvP death and the steel defender is not one of the player's protected items, it will remain in the player's inventory, but will become broken, which means the item is unusable and must be repaired with 2,500 coins by using the item on Perdu.
8847:
The black defender is a defender made of black metal. It is similar to a dagger, but held in the off-hand in place of a shield. It requires 10 Attack and 10 Defence to wield. The black defender is dropped by Cyclopes on the top floor of the Warriors' Guild, but only once you have obtained a steel defender.

If the player dies to a PvP death and the black defender is not one of the player's protected items, it will remain in the player's inventory, but will become broken, which means the item is unusable and must be repaired with 5,000 coins by using the item on Perdu.

The black defender does not count as an "evil" item in Shadow of the Storm despite its colour.
8849:
The adamant defender is a defender made out of adamant. It can be obtained by killing cyclopes on the top floor of the Warriors' Guild with a mithril defender in the inventory or after you have shown a mithril defender to Kamfreena. It is held in the shield slot and requires 30 Attack and Defence to wield.

If the player dies to a PvP death and the adamant defender is not one of the player's protected items, it will remain in the player's inventory, but will become broken, which means the item is unusable and must be repaired with 25,000 coins by using the item on Perdu.
8850:
The rune defender is the 3rd strongest defender. It is used for its attack bonus and is held in the off-hand in place of a shield. It requires 40 Attack and 40 Defence to wield. The rune defender is dropped by cyclopes on the top floor of the Warriors' Guild after showing an adamant defender or better as the player enters the room.

The rune defender's slash and crush defensive bonuses are the same as a black kiteshield, but its stab defence bonus is slightly less than an adamant square shield. However, it is much more commonly used for its melee bonuses, as it gives the same bonus to strength as the toktz-ket-xil (obsidian shield) and has melee attack bonuses. A rune defender is commonly combined with weapons such as a dragon scimitar or an abyssal whip as a result.

The defender is popular among players of higher combat levels due to its offensive stats. It can be considered to be the third best off-hand item for melee training, only beaten by the dragon defender and Avernic defender, and is commonly used in PvP situations as re-obtaining a rune defender is easier than re-obtaining a dragon or Avernic one.

If the player dies to a PvP death and the rune defender is not one of the player's protected items, it will remain in the player's inventory, but will become broken, which means the item is unusable and must be repaired with 35,000 coins by using the item on Perdu. Any ornament kit on the item will also be lost on death.

Players can attach a Rune defender ornament kit, obtained from hard Treasure Trails, to create a Rune defender (t). This is only cosmetic, and does not affect the defender's stat bonuses. It can be dismantled, returning the defender and ornament kit.
8851:
Warrior guild tokens are obtained by participating in various activities found in the Warriors' Guild. They are used to gain entry to the 2nd floor Cyclops chamber and basement areas, where they can be killed for a chance to drop defenders. To enter the area, players need a minimum of 100 tokens in their inventory.

Upon entry, 10 tokens are taken from your inventory immediately. With every minute spent inside one of the cyclops rooms, 10 tokens will crumble away. When you run out of tokens, you are asked to leave, and if you stay, you will be forcefully teleported out in another minute.
8856:
The defensive shield is a two-handed Shield used during the Warriors' Guild catapult activity. It is acquired by talking to Gamfred on the 1st floor of the Warriors' Guild. It can only be equipped while standing on the target in the activity room, and moving away from that square will unequip the shield. This activity is a slower tactic of obtaining warrior guild tokens compared to killing Animated Armour.

The shield has 4 defensive options: stab, blunt, slash and magic. Successfully defending against the correct attack type awards a player with 10 Defence experience and 1 warrior guild token. While the shield is equipped, the defensive options interface will appear automatically. The quest, prayer, magic, options, emotes, and music menus will be hidden.
8857: The Shot is an animation item used in the Warriors' Guild. When taking part in the shot put activity, the item is temporarily wielded by the player during the animation for launching the shot. Aside from this, it cannot be obtained.
8858:
An 18lb shot is an item used in the shot put room, one of the activities that can be found in the Warriors' Guild. The shot put room is located on the 1st floor in the north-east corner of the guild. The northern lane in this room contains a pile of 18lb shot, while the southern lane contains a pile of 22lb shot. For each shot made with these balls, players will receive tokens equal to the distance plus one, whereas shots made with the 22lb shot will reward tokens equal to the distance plus three.

The actual 18lb shot item appears on the ground after being thrown by the player. However, it cannot be obtained; when trying to pick it up, the referee will say "Hey! You can't take that, it's guild property. Take one from the pile." Attempting to cast telekinetic grab on it results in a message I can't use Telekinetic Grab on this object.

Ground ashes are obtained by using ashes on a pestle and mortar. These are used in the Warriors' Guild in the shot put room to improve the distance of a thrown shot put slightly.

Generally, using this item to gain this slight advantage is not recommended, since the additional time spent running back and forth to the bank in order to re-stock on ashes would be better spent putting more shots. Energy-restoring items such as energy potions are a much more efficient use of inventory space than these ashes.

The Bronze key is an item that players can steal from H.A.M. guards in the store rooms (lower level) of the H.A.M. Dungeon. It is used to open the Small chest in the south-west store room, which can be entered by picking the lock on the door. It can also be entered by squeezing-through the crevice in the wall.

After using the key to unlock the chest, the player receives a message in the chatbox saying: "Your bronze key breaks in the lock." and the key disappears from the inventory.

All of the H.A.M. keys (bronze, iron, steel and silver) can be obtained at the lowest level of the H.A.M. Dungeon by pickpocketing the H.A.M. guards. Rewards from the chests include:

Coins (small amount)

1-5 pieces of random jewellery (ranging from sapphire to diamond)

Cut gems (also ranging from sapphire to diamond)

The iron key is a quest item used only in Priest in Peril. It is obtained by using a golden key on the southern Monument in the Paterdomus mausoleum.

It is used to unlock the cell Drezel is detained in. Once used, the key disappears.

Duplicates can be obtained by using another golden key on the monument even if there is already a golden key on it. This can only be done before using the blessed water on the coffin. The iron key also cannot be added to a steel key ring.

Zanik is a cave goblin who is called up to explore the surface during the Death to the Dorgeshuun quest. Being the first of her kind to view the surface above, she's a curious and eager sort. Her preferred weapon is the Dorgeshuun crossbow.

Before starting Land of the Goblins, she can be found in various places across Dorgesh-Kaan: her house, the council building with Ur-tag, Oldak's lab, the building with the goblin scribe, two places in the Dorgesh-Kaan Agility Course, and next to the entrance to the Dorgesh-Kaan–Keldagrim train system. About every five minutes, she uses a teleport sphere and teleports to another location. You cannot talk to her while she is teleporting, and it's possible for her to teleport to the same place she already was at.

8880:
The Dorgeshuun crossbow is a crossbow requiring level 28 Ranged to equip. It is often used to train Ranged at low to medium levels, due to it having several advantages over similar crossbows with the same level requirements. It has the same attack bonus as an iron crossbow. It has an attack speed that is one tick faster than most other crossbows, and it is able to fire bone bolts, which are significantly cheaper than most other ammunition of similar strength. The fact it is a crossbow also gives it an advantage over shortbows, allowing the use of the shield slot for defensive or offensive purposes. Despite the bone bolts being roughly equivalent to iron bolts in ranged strength, the Dorgeshuun crossbow's faster attack speed means that its damage-per-second output when firing bone bolts is comparable to that of a regular crossbow firing steel or even mithril bolts (depending on the player's exact Ranged level).

It can be bought from Nardok in the Dorgeshuun Mines after the completion of The Lost Tribe quest. Completion of this quest is not required to equip it, however, meaning it can be purchased from other players and used without completing this quest. It can fire metal bolts up to iron, except silver bolts, and is the only crossbow that can use bone bolts. Note, however, that bolts containing unique tips and their (e) variants are not able to be fired from it.

This crossbow is the only crossbow with an attack speed of 5. This makes it 1 tick faster than most crossbows - it is only slower than the Karil's crossbow, the hunters' crossbow, and its upgraded variant, the hunter's sunlight crossbow, which all have an attack speed of 4. It should be noted that the Karil's crossbow is two-handed.

Weighing only 2.267kg, it is also the lightest crossbow in the game, making it ideal to use along with the mithril grapple when conservation of run energy is necessary, such as in the Hallowed Sepulchre.
8882:
Bone bolts are ammunition that can be bought after completion of The Lost Tribe quest. They can only be used with the Dorgeshuun crossbow, a popular choice for training ranged due to its faster speed than regular crossbows. Unlike other ammunition, it requires 28 Ranged to equip.

Due to their low price and ease of access from Nardok's Bone Weapons, having a base price of only 3 coins each, bone bolts are generally considered a very cost-effective method of training Ranged at lower levels. Assuming non-stop use of the Dorgeshuun crossbow on rapid, the player can fire 1,500 bolts per hour, which only costs 10,500 coins per hour if buying the bolts from the Grand Exchange.

Despite the bone bolts being roughly equivalent to iron bolts in ranged strength, the Dorgeshuun crossbow's faster attack speed means that its damage-per-second output when firing bone bolts is comparable to that of a regular crossbow firing steel or even mithril bolts (depending on the player's exact Ranged level).

If not buying the bolts from the Grand Exchange, buying bone bolt packs is recommended in order to save costs, since the cost per bolt can rapidly increase when buying the bolts individually. As with other bolts, their ranged strength is higher than most arrows with similar level requirements. The Dorgeshuun crossbow is 1 tick (0.6 seconds) slower to fire than shortbows, which balances out the higher strength of the bolts.

Despite not being made of metal, bone bolts do function with Ava's devices obtained from the completion of Animal Magnetism.

8890:
Coins (also referred to as gold pieces, gp, gold, or simply money) are the most common form of currency in Gielinor. They are used among players and non-player characters alike to exchange for items and services.

Players often refer to one thousand (1,000) coins as 1k and one million (1,000,000) coins as 1m or 1mil. Both can be applied to larger numbers, for example, 10m refers to ten million coins (10,000,000). 1b or 1bil refers to one billion coins (1,000,000,000).

Alchemy spells, which create coins, cannot be cast on coins. If a player attempts it, a message will inform the player that Coins are already made of gold. Curiously, other items made of gold, such as gold ore and gold bars, can be turned into coins with Alchemy spells.

Wearing a ring of wealth will automatically pick up coins dropped by NPCs upon killing them as long as the player has inventory space available.
8923:
The witchwood icon is a piece of Slayer equipment used to decrease the effectiveness of the screams of Cave horrors found in the Mos Le'Harmless Cave. The icon is worn around the neck and requires a Slayer level of 35 to equip, although players must have 58 Slayer to be able to kill cave horrors.

If the icon is not worn, the special scream attack from cave horrors is guaranteed to deal 10% of the player's total Hitpoints. Wearing the icon does not negate all damage from the scream, it instead causes the scream attack to roll as a regular attack. Jungle horrors do not use the special scream attack, as such, the icon is not necessary to fight them.

It can be purchased from any Slayer Master for 900 coins but cannot be traded with other players. The Slayer Masters created these from witchwood trees, an extinct species of tree that once grew in Gielinor.

Protect from Melee also provides complete protection against screams, serving as an acceptable substitution for the icon.

8932:
The lumber patch is used in the Trouble Brewing minigame to repair hoppers which have been burnt by other players. It can take up to three patches to repair a hopper, depending on how long it was on fire for. At the start of each game, 10 lumber patches are stocked in the tool workbench, and crafted lumber patches can be used on the workbench to store them within it.

Lumber patches can be crafted by using a regular log on the large workbench. Logs can be gathered from the log store within your team's base, or by chopping down the various trees around your base with an axe. Scrapey tree logs cannot be crafted into lumber patches. Creating a lumber patch rewards 12.5 crafting experience, and using it to repair a hopper rewards the same amount.
8934: Scrapey tree logs are items used in the Trouble Brewing minigame. They can be obtained by chopping the scrapey trees found within the brewing area. To use the logs to produce rum, players must use a knife on them, which will yield scrapey bark. Doing so has a 1/50 chance to cause the player to become diseased.
8936:
Blue flowers are an item obtained within the Trouble Brewing minigame. Blue flowers and red flowers are found in the minigame outside the opposite team's base. Team members must collect their team's coloured flowers and place them in the kettle in order to make their team's coloured water which is then used as an ingredient in the rum.

Players can only carry 5 flowers at a time, attempting to gather more will yield the message: You have plenty of those.

These flowers cannot be taken out of the minigame but are tradeable within, and have a trade value of 1 coin. This item cannot be picked up using Telekinetic Grab, attempting to do so will yield the message: I can't use Telekinetic Grab on this object.
8942:
A monkey is used in Trouble Brewing to gather bitternuts. They are found in the island in between the two bases, and they can be caught awarding the player with 15 Agility and Hunter experience. To use it to obtain bitternuts, a bowl of red water or a bowl of blue water must be used on the monkey, making it a red monkey or a blue monkey. The dyed monkey can then be used on a Bitternut Tree, and it will throw down a bitternut to the player after some time if the player is within range of the tree. If a monkey from the opposing team is in the tree as well, the two monkeys will fight, only one will throw down a bitternut, and the other will disappear.

With completion of Monkey Madness II or a m'speak amulet, the player can "Anger the monkey" or "Caution the monkey" when talking to it. An angry monkey will grab the nut quickly, but will always lose a fight if there is one. A cautious monkey will take longer to grab the nut, but will always win the fight. A player can have a maximum of two monkeys, and a team can have a maximum of twelve. If the player chooses to release the monkey, a level 1 Monkey will spawn.

Pieces of eight were a currency earned from the Trouble Brewing minigame used to buy rewards from Honest Jimmy's House of Stuff. During a game of Trouble Brewing, each resource deposited (i.e. buckets of water, bowls of coloured water, etc.) and opponent equipment burned (i.e. pipes, pump, etc.) would result in a piece of eight being awarded at the end of the game, up to 100 pieces of eight. Each bottle of rum deposited by the player's team gave 2 extra pieces to each player on the team at the end of the game. Pieces of eight awarded for bottling rum did not count towards the 100 pieces of eight limit for resources and sabotage, making it possible for players to earn more than 100 pieces of eight in a single game.

The amount received at the end of a game was not dependent on who was winning.

It took approximately 8 hours to complete a full outfit, the average amount earned was 100+ with each match being 20 minutes long.

In total, 39,590 pieces of eight were required to buy everything in the shop. It was not possible to sell items back to the store, so in order to fill out the collection log, at least this amount of pieces of eight were needed.

Pieces of eight were discontinued in an update on 23 May 2024, and any players with the original pieces of eight had it automatically converted to a virtual currency also named pieces of eight that is stored as a variable on a player's account. A "Count" option was also added to the original item to convert any leftover pieces into the new virtual currency.

8972: A bowl of red water is an item obtained within the minigame Trouble Brewing. It is made by using a bowl on the kettle with red flowers in it. It is an ingredient to make rum and can be put in the hopper; doing so will result in gaining 100 Cooking experience. It is also used on a monkey to make the monkey into a Red monkey who can collect a bitternut.
