It is also used on a monkey to make the monkey into a Blue monkey who can collect a bitternut.
8977: Scrapey bark is used in the Trouble Brewing minigame. Players may obtain bark by using a knife with the scrapey tree logs obtained from chopping scrapey trees, granting 50 Fletching experience. Doing so has a 1/50 chance to cause the player to become diseased. They must then be placed in their corresponding factory hopper, and doing so will provide the player with 100 Cooking experience.
8979:
A bridge section is an item used in the Trouble Brewing minigame that will repair bridges damaged by fires. It can take up to three bridge sections to repair a bridge, depending on how long it was on fire for. At the start of each game, 10 bridge sections are stocked in the tool workbench, and crafted bridge sections can be used on the workbench to store them within it.

Bridge sections can be crafted by using a regular log on the large workbench. Logs can be gathered from the log store within your team's base, or by chopping down the various trees around your base with an axe. Scrapey tree logs cannot be crafted into bridge sections. Creating a bridge section rewards 12.5 crafting experience, and using it to repair a bridge rewards the same amount.
8981:
Sweetgrubs are insects used during Trouble Brewing, and are a key ingredient in the brewing of rum within the minigame, serving as a substitute to the sluglings that Braindeath 'rum' uses. They have a "gag-inducing" aftertaste, but are otherwise quite sweet, hence the name. Sweetgrubs live in large Sweetgrub Mounds found on both sides of the Trouble Brewing facility.

Raw rat meat can be used on the mounds to collect sweetgrubs, with 40 Hunter experience being awarded for each sweetgrub successfully collected. When attempting to draw out some sweetgrubs from a mound, there is a 1/5 chance that the mound will empty out and collapse. Players will have to find another mound or wait for it to fill again.

If the mound does not collapse after the player uses their meat on it, there is a further 1/5 chance that a swarm of sweetflies will be drawn out instead. The sweetflies will continue to attack the player until they run away, as they cannot be attacked in retaliation. No one can gather more sweetgrubs from the mound while there are still sweetflies present.
8987: The Torch is an animation item released with Trouble Brewing. It is temporarily wielded by the player during an animation. Aside from this, it cannot be obtained.
8988:
The stuff is purchased from Honest Jimmy's House of Stuff with 50 pieces of eight from the Trouble Brewing minigame on Mos Le'Harmless. Access to the minigame and shop requires completion of the Cabin Fever quest. "The stuff" apparently contains some questionable and/or toxic content, as it has been banned by the Cooks' Guild of Varrock. However, it does not actually cause any negative side effects when used in brewing.

The stuff is used in brewing when making ales after placing two buckets of water and two barley malt into the fermenting vat. After adding it, the specific ale ingredient and ale yeast are also put in. The odds of brewing a mature ale increases. The chances of ale maturing naturally is 5%, but adding the stuff increases this chance to 64%. However, using it can cause brewing to take up to 7 days instead of the usual 1-1½ days.
8989: The brewin' guide can be obtained near the Trouble Brewing minigame and describes how to play the game. Once obtained, it can be reclaimed from a bookcase within a player-owned house.
8990: Brewin' guides are an unobtainable item. They can be found around Trouble Brewing and have a "Take" option. However, when taken they will give a copy of the real Brewin' guide instead, and the item will not despawn. Therefore, while they serve as an infinite source of Brewin' guides, the item itself is unobtainable. On March 30th 2022 there was a brief glitch that allowed players to telegrab the books, however this was shortly hotfixed.
8991:
Blue navy slacks can be purchased from Honest Jimmy for 1,000 Pieces of eight. It is for decoration only, and has no combat bonuses. It cannot be sold back to the shop.

Navy slacks can also be stored in the Player-owned house Costume room along with a Naval shirt and a Tricorn hat of the same colour, as part of the blue naval set.
8993:
Red navy slacks can be purchased from Honest Jimmy for 1,000 Pieces of eight. It is for decoration only, and has no combat bonuses. It cannot be sold back to the shop.

Navy slacks can also be stored in the Player-owned house Costume room along with a Naval shirt and a Tricorn hat of the same colour, as part of the red naval set.
8995:
Black navy slacks can be purchased from Honest Jimmy for 1,000 Pieces of eight. It is for decoration only, and has no combat bonuses. It cannot be sold back to the shop.

Navy slacks can also be stored in the Player-owned house Costume room along with a Naval shirt and a Tricorn hat of the same colour, as part of the black naval set.
8996:
Purple navy slacks can be purchased from Honest Jimmy for 1,000 Pieces of eight. It is for decoration only, and has no combat bonuses. It cannot be sold back to the shop.

Navy slacks can also be stored in the Player-owned house Costume room along with a Naval shirt and a Tricorn hat of the same colour, as part of the purple naval set.
8997:
Grey navy slacks can be purchased from Honest Jimmy for 1,000 Pieces of eight. It is for decoration only, and has no combat bonuses. It cannot be sold back to the shop.

Navy slacks can also be stored in the player-owned house costume room along with a naval shirt and a tricorn hat of the same colour, as part of the grey naval set.
9004:
The Stronghold notes give some information about the floors in the Stronghold of Security. It is a green and brown book with a green 'S' on it.

It is found just inside the Stronghold of Security in Barbarian Village west of Varrock by searching a dead explorer, or on the shelves in a house.

This dead explorer is Litara's brother, Solztun, who is found at the very end of the stronghold. His corpse can be found immediately from the entrance to the stronghold.
9005:
Fancy boots are a pair of low level boots with stats identical to bronze boots (except weighing significantly less), fighting boots and fancier boots. They are obtained from the Cradle of Life on the fourth level of the Stronghold of Security dungeon provided the player's account has two-factor authentication enabled. They are used by new or free-to-play players, as the centre of each level rewards a combined total of 10,000 coins along with the choice between fancy boots, fighting boots or fancier boots (at the fourth and final level).

If the player dies (including in PvP) and the boots are unprotected, it will be sent to the gravestone. When lost, they can be reclaimed for free from the Cradle of Life. Multiple pairs can be claimed and owned at the same time.

They used to be the best melee boots in free-to-play, but have since been surpassed by all of the Castle Wars decorative boots, especially the decorative boots (gold) due to their Strength bonus. The high requirement of 400 castle wars tickets causes the fancy boots to still be popular, due to its nonexistent cost.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room.
9006:
Fighting boots are a pair of low level boots with stats identical to bronze boots (except weighing significantly less), fancy boots and fancier boots. They are obtained from the Cradle of Life on the fourth level of the Stronghold of Security dungeon provided the player's account has two-factor authentication enabled. They are used by new or free-to-play players, as the centre of each level rewards a combined total of 10,000 coins along with the choice between fancy boots, fighting boots or fancier boots (at the fourth and final level).

If the player dies (including in PvP) and the boots are unprotected, it will be sent to the gravestone. When lost, they can be reclaimed for free from the Cradle of Life. Multiple pairs can be claimed and owned at the same time.

They used to be the best melee boots in free-to-play, but have since been surpassed by all of the Castle Wars decorative boots, especially the decorative boots (gold) due to their Strength bonus. The high requirement of 400 castle wars tickets causes the fighting boots to still be popular, due to its nonexistent cost.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room.
9007:
A right skull half is one of 4 parts needed to make a skull sceptre, and can be found by killing a minotaur on the first level of the Stronghold of Security, the Vault of War. These minotaurs can be either low or high level and are not aggressive. It is combined with a left skull half to make a strange skull. Doing so will result in a chatbox message stating: "The two halves of the skull fit perfectly, they appear to have a fixing point, perhaps they are to be mounted on something?" It cannot be traded, bought or sold. It is a fairly uncommon drop, as are the other pieces of the sceptre. It seems to have the highest drop rate of any of the pieces of the sceptre. You can also get more than one skull half at a time, without using the drop trick. Interestingly, the skull half looks like that of an ankou, while the left skull halves dropped by Ankou seem to be minotaur skulls.

Skull sceptre pieces can be crushed with a chisel to yield bone fragments, or used on a skull sceptre (i) to add to its current charges. When chiseled, the right skull half will provide a base quantity of three bone fragments, increasing by one for each Varrock diary tier the player has completed.
9009:
The Strange skull is an item that players can use with a runed sceptre to make a skull sceptre. It appears to be half an animal skull attached to half a human skull.

Players make the strange skull by combining a right skull half with a left skull half. Right halves, which resemble and most likely are halves of ankou skulls, are dropped by minotaurs, while left halves, resembling half of a minotaur's skull, are dropped by ankou. Minotaurs are found only in the Stronghold of Security, while ankou can be found in the Stronghold of Security, the Stronghold Slayer Cave and The Forgotten Cemetery.

The skull sceptre, when formed from its 4 components, teleports the user to the mines in Barbarian Village, just above the Stronghold of Security. A new sceptre may be formed by combining the right skull half, left skull half, bottom of sceptre, and top of sceptre. Only one skull sceptre may be created at one time, but a player may own as many strange skulls, runed sceptres, skull halves and sceptre halves as one wishes.

Skull sceptre pieces can be crushed with a chisel to yield bone fragments, or combined to a skull sceptre (i) to add to its current charges. When chiseled, the strange skull will provide a base quantity of eight bone fragments, increasing by two for each Varrock diary tier the player has completed.
9012:
The runed sceptre is obtainable by combining a bottom of sceptre and a top of sceptre. They are both dropped from monsters in the Stronghold of Security. Combining this item with a strange skull results in a skull sceptre. It can not be equipped until you have added the strange skull onto it. The bottom is dropped from Flesh Crawlers and the top is dropped by catablepons.

When combined with the strange skull, the pieces form the skull sceptre. The skull sceptre, when completed, teleports the user to the mines in Barbarian Village, just above the Stronghold of Security. The sceptre will initially have five charges, or more if the Varrock Diary has been completed.

Skull sceptre pieces can be crushed with a chisel to yield Bone fragments, or combined to a Skull sceptre (i) to add to its current charges. When chiseled, the runed sceptre will provide a base quantity of six bone fragments, increasing by two for each Varrock diary tier the player has completed.
9016:
Gorak claws are common drops by goraks. Using a set of claws with a pestle and mortar creates gorak claw powder, which is the secondary ingredient used in making the magic essence potion.

Because both ingredients of the magic essence potion are free, gorak claws could theoretically be useful for players who cannot afford to make potions with expensive ingredients, or who don't have access to herbs. However, because goraks are so powerful and prayer cannot be used against them, this method is rarely feasible.
9018:
Gorak claw powder is gained during Fairytale II - Cure a Queen by grinding a Gorak claw using a pestle and mortar, and is used in the production of a magic essence. It can also be obtained and used the same way after the quest.

Gorak claws are obtained by killing Goraks, which can be found through the fairy rings (code DIR) or in the God Wars Dungeon.
9019: A Magic essence (unf) is an unfinished potion made at 57 Herblore by using a star flower on a vial of water. Adding gorak claw powder to it creates magic essence, granting 130 Herblore experience. Unlike other unfinished potions, this cannot be stored in the Potion storage of a player's Bank.
9020:
Queen's secateurs are used in Fairytale I - Growing Pains and Fairytale II - Cure a Queen quests. They are first obtained as a drop from Tanglefoot. In part 2, you need to pickpocket Fairy Godfather to get them, which requires a level of 40 Thieving. The secateurs from A Fairy Tale I and A Fairy Tale II quests are two different items.

These secateurs cannot be wielded, or used as normal secateurs; they are purely a quest item.

You cannot obtain multiple secateurs while one is in your inventory or bank. However, through the drop trick, it is possible to obtain multiple secateurs during Fairytale II.

If the Queen's secateurs are lost before talking to the Fairy Godfather at the end of Fairytale I - Growing Pains, they can be reobtained by entering the gap in the wall next to the Cosmic Altar into the tunnels where you fought Tanglefoot. The secateurs will appear in your inventory upon squeezing through the gap.
9025:
Nuff's certificate an item obtained by searching the shelves in Fairy Nuff's grotto during the quest Fairytale II - Cure a Queen. According to this certificate, Nuff got her degree at the PoxStead College, and got this certificate from the Head of Magical Healing at the college, Dr Foster.

It needs to be in the player's inventory during the quest in order to access the Fairy Queen's hideout using the Fairy ring code sequence AIR, DLR, DJQ, AJS. If lost, it can be re-obtained by searching the wrecked shelves in Fairy Nuff's cottage in the north-west of Zanaris. After the quest has been completed, Nuff's certificate no longer needs to be in the inventory to access the hideout and can be destroyed to save space.

The inscription on the back of the certificate translates to:
9026:
The ivory comb is one of the nine artefacts found during the Pyramid Plunder minigame in Sophanem. It is the lowest value loot that may be discovered, and is found only in the first two rooms of the pyramid. It can be sold to Simon Templeton at the Agility Pyramid for 50 coins.

24 ivory combs can be used to recharge the pharaoh's sceptre, costing 43,440 if purchased from the Grand Exchange. Due to its low trade volume, players are recommend to recharge sceptres with a different artefact.
9030:
The stone scarab is one of the nine artefacts found during the Pyramid Plunder minigame in Sophanem. It can be sold to Simon Templeton at the Agility Pyramid for 175 coins.

12 stone scarabs can be used to recharge the pharaoh's sceptre, costing 2,088 if purchased from the Grand Exchange.
9032:
The pottery scarab is one of the nine artefacts found during the Pyramid Plunder minigame in Sophanem. It can be sold to Simon Templeton at the Agility Pyramid for 75 coins.

24 pottery scarabs can be used to recharge the Pharaoh's sceptre, costing 2,352 if purchased from the Grand Exchange.
9036:
The pottery statuette is one of the nine artefacts found during the Pyramid Plunder minigame in Sophanem. It can be sold to Simon Templeton at the Agility Pyramid for 100 coins.

24 pottery statuettes can be used to recharge the Pharaoh's sceptre, costing 2,064 if purchased from the Grand Exchange.
9038:
The stone statuette is one of the nine artefacts found during the Pyramid Plunder minigame in Sophanem, in the rooms requiring a Thieving level of 31 or higher. It can be sold to Simon Templeton at the Agility Pyramid for 200 coins.

12 stone statuettes can be used to recharge the Pharaoh's sceptre, costing 2,160 if purchased from the Grand Exchange.
9040:
The gold seal is one of the nine artefacts found during the Pyramid Plunder minigame in Sophanem, in the rooms requiring a Thieving level of 41 or higher. It can be sold to Simon Templeton at the Agility Pyramid for 750 coins.

6 gold seals can be used to recharge the Pharaoh's sceptre, costing 4,542 if purchased from the Grand Exchange.
9042:
The stone seal is one of the nine artefacts found during the Pyramid Plunder minigame in Sophanem. It can be sold to Simon Templeton at the Agility Pyramid for 150 coins.

12 stone seals can be used to recharge the Pharaoh's sceptre, costing 1,764 if purchased from the Grand Exchange.
9052:
Locust meat is dropped by locusts in the city of Sophanem. It heals three hitpoints. Locust meat may not be cooked using the Cooking skill, but can be eaten right after killing a locust.

This can possibly be used as quick food for Pyramid Plunder. Having high combat skills to quickly kill these may make them a complete replacement for food, but since they heal less than the poison damage received it is still recommended to take antipoison.

Eating it yields the message Juices spurt into your mouth as you chew. It's tastier than you were expecting. in the chat box.
9055:
Black goblin mail is made by using black dye on goblin mail. Like all goblin mail, it is too small for players to normally wear as armour.

During the Land of the Goblins quest, the player can turn into a goblin using a transmogrification potion and wear the black goblin mail in order to access the Huzamogaarb tribal room of the Goblin Temple.
9057:
Green goblin mail is made by using green dye on goblin mail or by killing the goblins with red armour at Goblin Village. Like all goblin mail, it is too small for players to normally wear as armour.

During the Land of the Goblins quest, the player can turn into a goblin using a transmogrification potion and wear the green goblin mail, although it serves no purpose in the quest.

Green goblin mails cannot be sold nor traded, and therefore has no value. It can only occupy space in the inventory or bank. However, the dye and the goblin mail are tradeable.
9064:
The emerald lantern is a light source. It is used during the Lunar Diplomacy quest and is created by using the emerald lens with a bullseye lantern or a bullseye lantern (unf).

If created from a bullseye lantern (unf), it will require lamp oil to be lit with a tinderbox. To fix this mistake during the quest, there is an easy way to pull the Emerald Lens back out of the lantern by using a Sapphire (with completion of Tears of Guthix) or a Lantern lens on the bullseye lantern.

Level 49 Firemaking is required to light it. It is similar to the sapphire lantern, but unlike the sapphire lantern it is not made using a cut gem. If lost, the emerald lens can be recovered by speaking to the Cabin boy who can be found slightly north-west of the Lunar Isle bank.
9065:
The emerald lantern is a light source. It is used during the Lunar Diplomacy quest and is created by using the emerald lens with a bullseye lantern or a bullseye lantern (unf).

If created from a bullseye lantern (unf), it will require lamp oil to be lit with a tinderbox. To fix this mistake during the quest, there is an easy way to pull the Emerald Lens back out of the lantern by using a Sapphire (with completion of Tears of Guthix) or a Lantern lens on the bullseye lantern.

Level 49 Firemaking is required to light it. It is similar to the sapphire lantern, but unlike the sapphire lantern it is not made using a cut gem. If lost, the emerald lens can be recovered by speaking to the Cabin boy who can be found slightly north-west of the Lunar Isle bank.
9066:
The emerald lens is a quest item obtained from the Cabin boy during Lunar Diplomacy and is used to expose all the markings left on the ship by the Moon Clan.

It is used on a bullseye lantern or bullseye lantern (unf) to receive an emerald lantern, similar to a sapphire lantern. After Lunar Diplomacy is completed, this item can be discarded.
9068: The Moonclan helm is part of the Moonclan robes set. It can be purchased from the clothing store on Lunar Isle during or after the Lunar Diplomacy quest. It can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player-owned house.
9069: The Moonclan hat is part of the Moonclan robes set. It can be purchased from the clothing store on Lunar Isle during or after Lunar Diplomacy. It can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player-owned house.
9070: The Moonclan armour is part of the Moonclan robes set. It can be bought from the clothing shop on Lunar Isle during or after Lunar Diplomacy. It can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player-owned house.
9072: Moonclan gloves are part of the Moonclan robes set. They can be purchased from the clothing store on Lunar Isle during or after Lunar Diplomacy. It can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player-owned house.
9073: Moonclan boots of the Moonclan robes set are purchased from the Moon Clan Fine Clothes clothes shop on Lunar Isle during or after Lunar Diplomacy. They can be stored in a magic wardrobe in the costume room of a player-owned house.
9074: The Moonclan cape is part of the Moonclan robes set. It can be purchased from the clothing store on Lunar Isle during or after Lunar Diplomacy. It is currently the only cape to have a negative defence bonus for any style, and one of two capes to have a negative attack bonus in any style (the other being the mixed hide cape). It can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player-owned house.
9075:
Astral runes are runes used in all Lunar Spells. Astral runes require level 40 Runecraft to craft. They may be crafted by using pure essence at the Astral Altar on Lunar Isle after the completion of Lunar Diplomacy. 8.7 Runecraft experience is gained per essence used. At level 82 Runecraft, players will receive two astral runes per pure essence used.

Astral runes may not be crafted via the Abyss. There is no talisman needed to access the Astral Altar, making it and the Soul Altar the only runic altars that do not have a talisman associated with them. However, the Soul Altar can be reached through the Abyss, unlike the Astral Altar.

Astral runes may also be purchased at Baba Yaga's Magic Shop after completion of Lunar Diplomacy, located north of the bank on Lunar Isle. The shop stocks 250 astral runes. Players must have a Seal of passage equipped or in their inventory when attempting to trade with Baba Yaga or they'll be thrown off the island unless they have completed the Elite tier of the Fremennik Diary.
9078:
The Moonclan manual, or The Basics of Magic, tells the history of how the Astral Altar came to exist and some of the history of the origin of magic in Gielinor.

It also tells the story of the Fremennik V------- who discovered the rune essence. Unfortunately, some of the words have been omitted by the Moon Clan in an effort to keep some things secret.

A player can buy the book for one coin from Baba Yaga on the Lunar Isle. Afterward, it is in a bookcase in a player's house.

It is worth noting that wearing a Seal of passage is required to buy a Moonclan manual prior to the completion of the Fremennik Elite Diary.
9082: A ground tooth is made by using a suqah tooth with a pestle and mortar. It is used in farming as part of the payment for protecting a spirit tree, along with five monkey nuts and a monkey bar. Ground tooth is also used in the making of the Waking sleep vial during the Lunar Diplomacy quest. The ground tooth is not tradeable and suqah teeth may only be obtained by killing suqah on Lunar Isle. According to Yulf Squecks, many gnomes enjoy eating this item.
9083:
A seal of passage is a neckwear slot item that is required to be worn or held in the inventory in order to talk to or trade with anyone on Lunar Isle, except for 'Birds-Eye' Jack, the banker available after Dream Mentor. Without it, players attempting to speak with anyone will be forcibly teleported from Lunar Isle back to Rellekka.

The seal of passage is obtained at the beginning of the Lunar Diplomacy quest by talking to Brundt the Chieftain in the longhall in Rellekka. He will replace it for free if the player destroys it or loses it. If the seal is lost during the Fremennik Exiles quest, players must talk to Brundt in the woods south-east of Rellekka (rather than in the longhall) to reobtain it.

It is always lost on death. Because of this, it is recommended for players planning to return to Lunar Isle via Rellekka to destroy their seal of passage after each visit, as they can get a free replacement from Brundt if they do not have one banked (Rellekka is a long way from a bank if a player forgets their seal). If The Fremennik Isles is started, Maria Gunnars will transport the player to Neitiznot where there is a bank to use.

Players who have completed the Fremennik Elite Diaries will no longer need to hold or wear a seal of passage in order to speak to the residents of Lunar Isle.
9085: The empty vial is an item obtained during the Lunar Diplomacy quest, from Baba Yaga. It is the only vial that can contain a Waking Sleep Potion. This vial can only be used during Lunar Diplomacy, not for the Potion of Shared Dreaming or any other potion made during Herblore. The vial has no further use once the quest is completed.
9086: A vial of water is a quest item obtained during the Lunar Diplomacy quest. It is made by using an empty vial on a water source. A guam leaf or marrentill is used on it to make a guam vial or marr vial respectively.
9087:
The waking sleep vial is made by using ground tooth with a guam-marr vial. It is a potion used to access the Dream World in the Lunar Diplomacy quest by pouring it on the magic kindling yielding a soaked kindling. When that is lit on fire it transports the player to the Dream World. Pouring it out leaves an empty vial and has no further use once the quest is completed.

Before completing Lunar Diplomacy, collecting empty vials allows for affordable, but time consuming, Herblore training. After giving the lunar equipment set and waking sleep vial to the Oneiromancer, and getting back with magic kindling, use the potion on the kindling, drop the kindling and ask for another potion and kindling. The resulting empty vials can only be filled with water during the quest, however, Guam and Marrentill can still be added to filled vials of water after the quest has been completed.
9089:
A marr vial is made by using a marrentill on a vial of water (Lunar Diplomacy), yielding 84 Herblore experience. It is an early step in creating the waking sleep potion in the Lunar Diplomacy quest. Then a guam leaf can be added to make a guam-marr vial.

Alternatively, a guam vial can be made and a marrentill can be added to make the same product.
9090: The guam-marr vial is made by using a marrentill on a guam vial or a guam leaf on a marr vial, yielding a guam-marr vial and 84 Herblore experience. Adding a ground tooth is the next step in making the waking sleep potion required for the Lunar Diplomacy quest.
9094:
Kindling is used in the Lunar Diplomacy quest. The Oneiromancer gives the player magic kindling to use in the ceremony to travel to the Dream World.

The Oneiromancer tells the player the magic kindling is from the first magic tree that ever grew.

The player uses the Waking Sleep Potion on the kindling to make Soaked kindling. The player then places the Soaked kindling on the lit Ceremonial Brazier to enter the land of dreams. If the player leaves the Dream World or has to log out, more kindling can be obtained from the Oneiromancer. If the player has an extra set of Lunar equipment stored in their house, they may enter a dialogue loop where they ask for another set of armour and the Oneiromancer refuses them before they can ask for more kindling. This is resolved by removing the armour and having it in your inventory while speaking to the Oneiromancer.

Using the potion on the kindling prints the message You soak the kindling with the potion..
9106:
The astral tiara is an unobtainable item that was released alongside Lunar Diplomacy. As the Astral Altar did not require a talisman or tiara to enter, it was never made obtainable.

Bizarrely, no astral talisman was created to accompany it. It is possible therefore that the astral tiara would have been included as a purely cosmetic item, but the idea was scrapped before launch.
9139:
Blurite bolts are the second weakest type of bolts. They are stronger than bronze bolts but weaker than iron bolts. They can only be fired from at least a blurite crossbow or better. As with most bolts, they can be poisoned, however this will prevent the addition of bolt tips.

Blurite bolts cannot be bought, and can only be created by players. First, in order to make blurite bolts, a player must smith unfinished blurite bolts. This requires a Smithing level of 8, and for each blurite bar that player smiths they will get 10 unfinished blurite bolts and 17 Smithing experience. Then a player must attach flights to the bolts. Attaching flights to each bolt requires a Fletching level of 24 and 1 feather, granting 1 Fletching experience per bolt.

Blurite bolts may be tipped with jade. A player must first have a Fletching level of 26 and take a cut jade and use a chisel with it to make 12 jade bolt tips, granting 2 Fletching experience. Attaching jade bolt tips also requires a Fletching level of 26, and for each jade bolt tip attached to a blurite bolt, a player is granted 2.4 Fletching experience. Once the jade bolt tips have been attached, the blurite bolts become jade bolts. Jade bolts can then be enchanted to become jade bolts (e).
9140:
Iron bolts are the third-weakest bolts, stronger than blurite bolts. Iron bolts may be shot from iron or better crossbows. As with most bolts, they can be poisoned, however this will prevent the addition of bolt tips.

Iron bolts may be created by players. First, a player must smith unfinished iron bolts. This requires a Smithing level of 18, and for each iron bar a player smiths they will get 10 unfinished iron bolts and 25 Smithing experience. Then a player must attach flights to the bolts. Attaching flights to each bolt requires a Fletching level of 39 and 1 feather, granting 1.5 Fletching experience per bolt.

Iron bolts may be tipped with pearl. To tip the bolts with pearl, a player must have a Fletching level of 41 and use pearl bolt tips with the iron bolts, granting 3.2 Fletching experience for each pearl bolt tip attached and making the iron bolts into pearl bolts. Pearl bolts can then be enchanted; more information on enchanting them is available under pearl bolts.
9141:
Steel bolts are the fourth available bolt, just after iron bolts and before mithril bolts. Steel bolts may be shot from a steel crossbow or better. As with most bolts, they can be poisoned, however this will prevent the addition of bolt tips.

Steel bolts may be smithed by first making steel bolts(unf). This requires a Smithing level of 33 and a steel bar. Each bar will make 10 unfinished steel bolts and grant 37.5 Smithing experience. Attaching feathers to each bolt requires a Fletching level of 46, and will grant 3.5 Fletching experience per bolt. At 48 Fletching, red topaz bolt tips can be attached to create red topaz bolts.
9142:
Mithril bolts are a ranged projectile which are fired from a mithril crossbow or higher. Level 36 Ranged is required to equip them. As with most bolts, they can be poisoned, however this will prevent the addition of bolt tips.

To create mithril bolts, a player must first smith unfinished mithril bolts by using a mithril bar on an anvil while carrying a hammer. This requires a Smithing level of 53, and for each mithril bar that player smiths, they will get 10 unfinished mithril bolts and 50 Smithing experience. Then, a player must attach feathers to the bolts. Attaching feathers to each bolt requires a Fletching level of 54 and 1 feather, granting 5 Fletching experience per bolt.

Mithril bolts may be tipped with sapphire, emerald, or a grapple. To tip the bolts with sapphire, a player must have a Fletching level of 56 and use sapphire bolt tips with the mithril bolts, granting 4.7 Fletching experience for each sapphire bolt tip attached and making the mithril bolts into sapphire bolts. To tip the bolts with emerald, a player must have a Fletching level of 58 and use emerald bolt tips with the mithril bolts, granting 5.5 Fletching experience for each emerald bolt tip attached and making the mithril bolts into Emerald bolts. To tip a bolt with a grapple, a player must use a mithril grapple tip on the mithril bolt, granting 11 Fletching experience, and also a rope, making a mithril grapple.

They are commonly used for Ranged training due to them being modestly priced with a good damage output.
9145:
Silver bolts are ranged ammunition that can be fired from iron crossbows or better. They have a Ranged Strength bonus higher than blurite bolts but lower than iron bolts.

To produce silver bolts, players with at least 21 Crafting must use a silver bar on a furnace with a bolt mould in their inventory. This will return 10 unfeathered silver bolts and 50 Crafting experience. Attaching feathers to the bolts with 43 Fletching will complete them and grant the player 25 Fletching experience.

They are a type of silver weaponry and are one of the few ammo types able to be used to effectively kill Vampyre Juvinates.
9176:
A blurite crossbow is a crossbow stronger than the bronze crossbow but weaker than the iron crossbow. It requires 16 Ranged to wield and can only fire bronze or blurite bolts. It has an attack range of 7, increased to 9 with long range.

Blurite crossbows require 24 Fletching to be made. An oak stock must be fletched from oak logs, yielding 16 Fletching experience, then blurite limbs must be attached to the stock with a hammer, yielding 32 Fletching experience and an unstrung blurite crossbow. Finally, the crossbow must be strung with a crossbow string, yielding 16 experience. In total, making a blurite crossbow yields 64 Fletching experience.

The Knight's Sword quest must be completed before a player can create this crossbow.
9177:
An iron crossbow is a crossbow stronger than the blurite crossbow but weaker than the steel crossbow. It requires a Ranged level of 26 to wield, and can use bolts up to and including iron bolts. It has an attack range of 7, increased to 9 with long range.

Iron crossbows can be made through the Fletching skill at level 39; a player must first cut a willow stock for the crossbow from willow logs, granting 22 Fletching experience. Then, a player must add iron limbs to the stock with a hammer in their inventory, granting 44 experience and making an unstrung iron crossbow. Finally, a player must string the crossbow with a crossbow string, granting 22 experience. Creating an iron crossbow from raw materials grants 88 Fletching experience in total.
9179:
A steel crossbow is a crossbow stronger than the iron crossbow but weaker than the mithril crossbow. It requires a Ranged level of 31 to wield, and can use bolts up to and including steel bolts. It has an attack range of 7 increased to 9 with longrange.

Steel crossbows can be made through the Fletching skill at level 46; a player must first cut a teak stock for the crossbow from teak logs, granting 27 Fletching experience. Then, a player must add steel limbs to the stock with a hammer in their inventory, granting 54 experience and making an unstrung steel crossbow. Finally, a player must string the crossbow with a crossbow string, granting 27 experience. Creating a steel crossbow from raw materials grants 108 Fletching experience in total.
9181:
A mithril crossbow is a crossbow that is stronger than the steel crossbow but weaker than the adamant crossbow. It requires a Ranged level of 36 to wield, and can fire bolts up to and including mithril bolts. It has an attack range of 7 increased to 9 with longrange.

Mithril crossbows can be made through the Fletching skill at level 54; a player must first cut a maple stock for the crossbow from maple logs, granting 32 Fletching experience. Then, a player must add mithril limbs to the stock with a hammer in their inventory, granting 64 experience and making an unstrung mithril crossbow. Finally, a player must string the crossbow with a crossbow string, granting 32 experience. Creating a mithril crossbow from raw materials grants 128 Fletching experience in total.
9183:
An adamant crossbow is a crossbow that is stronger than the mithril crossbow but weaker than the rune crossbow. It requires a Ranged level of 46 to wield, and can fire bolts up to and including adamant bolts. It has an attack range of 7 increased to 9 with longrange.

Adamant crossbows can be made through the Fletching skill at level 61; a player must first cut a mahogany stock for the crossbow from mahogany logs, granting 41 Fletching experience. Then, a player must add adamantite limbs to the stock with a hammer in their inventory, granting 82 experience and making an unstrung adamant crossbow. Finally, a player must string the crossbow with a crossbow string, granting 41 experience. Creating an adamant crossbow from raw materials grants 164 Fletching experience in total.
9185:
The rune crossbow is a crossbow that is stronger than the adamant crossbow but weaker than the dragon crossbow. It requires a Ranged level of 61 to wield, and can fire up to and including runite bolts. It is one-handed so it can be equipped alongside a shield, such as an anti-dragon shield or god book. It has an attack range of 7 increased to 9 with longrange.

Rune crossbows can be made through the Fletching skill at level 69; a player must first cut a yew stock for the crossbow from yew logs, granting 50 Fletching experience. Then, a player must add runite limbs to the stock with a hammer in their inventory, granting 100 experience and making an unstrung rune crossbow. Finally, a player must string the crossbow with a crossbow string, granting 50 experience. Creating a rune crossbow from raw materials grants 200 Fletching experience in total, and doing so within Witchaven and/or Yanille is a task for the elite Ardougne Diary.

Ironmen may obtain a rune crossbow by defeating the crazy archaeologist. The rune crossbow is commonly used among ironmen and low-level players for Slayer tasks, and for TzHaar Fight Cave, due to the ease of obtaining broad bolts and the ability to equip a shield. For Slayer tasks, a magic shortbow with rune or amethyst arrows is often a stronger weapon.

The rune crossbow is commonly used even for high-level content due to its ability to fire ruby and diamond bolts. The dragon, Armadyl, Zaryte, and dragon hunter crossbows are stronger alternatives.

Using a Shattered relics variety ornament kit on the crossbow will change its appearance into that of an rune crossbow (or).
9187:
Jade bolt tips are attached to the tips of blurite bolts or dragon bolts and can then be enchanted. Once jade bolt tips have been attached to the bolts, they become jade bolts and jade dragon bolts respectively.

Jade bolt tips can be created through the Fletching skill. A player must have a Fletching level of 26 and take a cut jade and use a chisel with it to make 12 jade bolt tips, granting 2 Fletching experience.

Attaching jade bolt tips to blurite bolts requires a Fletching level of 26, and for each jade bolt tip attached to a blurite bolt, a player is granted 2.4 Fletching experience. Attaching jade bolt tips to dragon bolts requires a Fletching level of 84, granting 2.4 Fletching experience per bolt.
9190:
Emerald bolt tips are attached to the tips of mithril and dragon bolts, which can then be enchanted. Once emerald bolt tips have been attached to mithril or dragon bolts, they become emerald bolts and emerald dragon bolts, respectively.

Emerald bolt tips can be created through the Fletching skill. A player must have a Fletching level of 58 and take a cut emerald and use a chisel with it to make 12 Emerald bolt tips, giving 5.5 experience.
9191:
Ruby bolt tips are attached to the tips of adamant and dragon bolts, which can then be enchanted. Once ruby bolt tips have been attached to adamant or dragon bolts, they become ruby bolts and ruby dragon bolts, respectively.

Ruby bolt tips can be created through the Fletching skill. A player must have a Fletching level of 63 and take a ruby and use a chisel with it to make 12 ruby bolt tips, yielding 6.3 experience per gem.
9192:
Diamond bolt tips can be attached to adamantite bolts or dragon bolts, and can then be enchanted. Once diamond bolt tips have been attached, the bolts become diamond bolts or diamond dragon bolts, respectively.

Diamond bolt tips can be created through the Fletching skill. A player must have a Fletching level of 65 and take a cut diamond and use a chisel with it to make 12 diamond bolt tips, giving 7 experience.
9193:
Dragonstone bolt tips are attached to the tips of runite and dragon bolts, which can then be enchanted. Once dragonstone bolt tips have been attached to runite or dragon bolts, they become dragonstone bolts and dragonstone dragon bolts, respectively.

Dragonstone bolt tips can be created through the Fletching skill. One must have 71 Fletching and take a cut dragonstone and use a chisel with it to make 12 dragonstone bolt tips, granting 8.2 Fletching experience per dragonstone. To avoid misclicking, players will receive a message to confirm cutting the dragonstone into bolt tips. There is a "Make - x" option for this, and it takes about 70 seconds per inventory of cut gems chiselled into tips.

Attaching dragonstone bolt tips to runite bolts to make dragonstone bolts also requires 71 Fletching, and gives 8.2 experience for each dragonstone bolt tip attached to a runite bolt.
9194:
Onyx bolt tips are attached to the tips of runite bolts to create onyx bolts, or to dragon bolts to create dragon onyx bolts, which can then be enchanted to make onyx bolts (e) and onyx dragon bolts (e), respectively.

Onyx bolt tips can be created through the Fletching skill. A player must have a Fletching level of 73 and take a cut onyx and use a chisel with it to make 24 onyx bolt tips. This is not recommended because the gem itself is worth far more than the bolt tips. Instead, it's recommended to collect them as drops from various monsters, or fish infernal eels.

Attaching onyx bolt tips also requires a Fletching level of 73, and for each onyx bolt tip attached to a runite bolt, the player is granted 9.4 Fletching experience.

Onyx bolt tips can also be obtained from stone chests, ninja implings, infernal eels, and elite Treasure Trails.
9236:
Opal bolts (e) are opal bolts which have been enchanted through use of the Enchant Crossbow Bolt (Opal) spell, which requires level 4 Magic, 1 cosmic rune, 2 air runes, and 10 opal bolts which to enchant per cast of the spell.

Opal bolts are crafted by gem-tipping bronze bolts with opal bolt tips.
9237: Jade bolts (e) are blurite bolts tipped with enchanted jade. Jade bolts can be enchanted into enchanted jade bolts through the spell Enchant Crossbow Bolt (Jade) by a player with level 14 Magic. The spell enchants 10 jade bolts at a time. These bolts are untradeable.
9238: Enchanted pearl bolts are iron bolts tipped with enchanted Pearl bolt tips made from Oyster pearls. Pearl bolts can be enchanted into enchanted pearl bolts through the spell Enchant Crossbow Bolt (Pearl) by a player with 24 Magic. The spell enchants 10 pearl bolts at a time and requires 1 Cosmic rune and 2 Water runes to be present in their inventory.
9241: Emerald bolts (e) are mithril bolts tipped with enchanted emerald. Emerald bolts can be enchanted through the spell Enchant Crossbow Bolt (Emerald) by a player with level 27 Magic. The spell enchants 10 emerald bolts at a time. Like mithril and emerald bolts, firing them requires a mithril crossbow, or better.
9242: Ruby bolts (e) are adamant bolts that have been enchanted after having been tipped with ruby bolt tips. Ruby bolts can be enchanted with the spell Enchant Crossbow Bolt (Ruby) by a player with level 49 Magic, requiring 46 Ranged to wield. The spell enchants 10 ruby bolts at a time and uses 1 blood rune, 1 cosmic rune, and 5 fire runes.
9243: Diamond bolts (e) are adamant bolts tipped with enchanted diamond. Diamond bolts can be enchanted by using the spell Enchant Crossbow Bolt (Diamond) by a player with 57 Magic. The spell enchants 10 diamond bolts per cast and uses 2 law runes, 1 cosmic rune, and 10 earth runes.
9244: Dragonstone bolts (e) are runite bolts tipped with enchanted dragonstone. Dragonstone bolts can be enchanted through the spell Enchant Crossbow Bolt (Dragonstone) by a player with level 68 Magic. The spell enchants 10 dragonstone bolts at a time. They require 61 Ranged to wield. Dragonstone bolts (e) can be purchased from Justine located at the Last Man Standing Minigame in Ferox Enclave, who sells 20 for 3 points.
9245: Onyx bolts (e) are rune bolts tipped with enchanted onyx. Onyx bolts can be enchanted through the spell Enchant Crossbow Bolt (Onyx) by a player with level 87 Magic. The spell enchants 10 onyx bolts at a time. These bolts are rarely used due to their cost, but are often fletched and enchanted by ironman players for their High Level Alchemy value. Additionally, they require a Ranged level of 61 to wield.
9286:
Blurite bolts are the second weakest type of bolts. They are stronger than bronze bolts but weaker than iron bolts. They can only be fired from at least a blurite crossbow or better. As with most bolts, they can be poisoned, however this will prevent the addition of bolt tips.

Blurite bolts cannot be bought, and can only be created by players. First, in order to make blurite bolts, a player must smith unfinished blurite bolts. This requires a Smithing level of 8, and for each blurite bar that player smiths they will get 10 unfinished blurite bolts and 17 Smithing experience. Then a player must attach flights to the bolts. Attaching flights to each bolt requires a Fletching level of 24 and 1 feather, granting 1 Fletching experience per bolt.

Blurite bolts may be tipped with jade. A player must first have a Fletching level of 26 and take a cut jade and use a chisel with it to make 12 jade bolt tips, granting 2 Fletching experience. Attaching jade bolt tips also requires a Fletching level of 26, and for each jade bolt tip attached to a blurite bolt, a player is granted 2.4 Fletching experience. Once the jade bolt tips have been attached, the blurite bolts become jade bolts. Jade bolts can then be enchanted to become jade bolts (e).
9287:
Iron bolts are the third-weakest bolts, stronger than blurite bolts. Iron bolts may be shot from iron or better crossbows. As with most bolts, they can be poisoned, however this will prevent the addition of bolt tips.

Iron bolts may be created by players. First, a player must smith unfinished iron bolts. This requires a Smithing level of 18, and for each iron bar a player smiths they will get 10 unfinished iron bolts and 25 Smithing experience. Then a player must attach flights to the bolts. Attaching flights to each bolt requires a Fletching level of 39 and 1 feather, granting 1.5 Fletching experience per bolt.

Iron bolts may be tipped with pearl. To tip the bolts with pearl, a player must have a Fletching level of 41 and use pearl bolt tips with the iron bolts, granting 3.2 Fletching experience for each pearl bolt tip attached and making the iron bolts into pearl bolts. Pearl bolts can then be enchanted; more information on enchanting them is available under pearl bolts.
9288:
Steel bolts are the fourth available bolt, just after iron bolts and before mithril bolts. Steel bolts may be shot from a steel crossbow or better. As with most bolts, they can be poisoned, however this will prevent the addition of bolt tips.

Steel bolts may be smithed by first making steel bolts(unf). This requires a Smithing level of 33 and a steel bar. Each bar will make 10 unfinished steel bolts and grant 37.5 Smithing experience. Attaching feathers to each bolt requires a Fletching level of 46, and will grant 3.5 Fletching experience per bolt. At 48 Fletching, red topaz bolt tips can be attached to create red topaz bolts.
9289:
Mithril bolts are a ranged projectile which are fired from a mithril crossbow or higher. Level 36 Ranged is required to equip them. As with most bolts, they can be poisoned, however this will prevent the addition of bolt tips.

To create mithril bolts, a player must first smith unfinished mithril bolts by using a mithril bar on an anvil while carrying a hammer. This requires a Smithing level of 53, and for each mithril bar that player smiths, they will get 10 unfinished mithril bolts and 50 Smithing experience. Then, a player must attach feathers to the bolts. Attaching feathers to each bolt requires a Fletching level of 54 and 1 feather, granting 5 Fletching experience per bolt.

Mithril bolts may be tipped with sapphire, emerald, or a grapple. To tip the bolts with sapphire, a player must have a Fletching level of 56 and use sapphire bolt tips with the mithril bolts, granting 4.7 Fletching experience for each sapphire bolt tip attached and making the mithril bolts into sapphire bolts. To tip the bolts with emerald, a player must have a Fletching level of 58 and use emerald bolt tips with the mithril bolts, granting 5.5 Fletching experience for each emerald bolt tip attached and making the mithril bolts into Emerald bolts. To tip a bolt with a grapple, a player must use a mithril grapple tip on the mithril bolt, granting 11 Fletching experience, and also a rope, making a mithril grapple.

They are commonly used for Ranged training due to them being modestly priced with a good damage output.
9292:
Silver bolts are ranged ammunition that can be fired from iron crossbows or better. They have a Ranged Strength bonus higher than blurite bolts but lower than iron bolts.

To produce silver bolts, players with at least 21 Crafting must use a silver bar on a furnace with a bolt mould in their inventory. This will return 10 unfeathered silver bolts and 50 Crafting experience. Attaching feathers to the bolts with 43 Fletching will complete them and grant the player 25 Fletching experience.

They are a type of silver weaponry and are one of the few ammo types able to be used to effectively kill Vampyre Juvinates.

Jade bolts are blurite bolts tipped with jade. Jade bolts can be created through the Fletching skill. A player must first have a Fletching level of 26 and take a cut jade and use a chisel with it to make 12 Jade bolt tips, granting 2 Fletching experience. Attaching jade bolt tips also requires a Fletching level of 26, and for each jade bolt tip attached to a blurite bolt, a player is granted 2.4 Fletching experience. Once the jade bolt tips have been attached, the blurite bolts become jade bolts.

Jade bolts can be enchanted through the spell Enchant Crossbow Bolt (Jade) by a player with level 14 Magic. The spell enchants 10 jade bolts at a time, and once they are enchanted they become enchanted jade bolts and gain a special ability.
9338:
Emerald bolts are mithril bolts tipped with emerald bolt tips, requiring level 36 Ranged to use.

Emerald bolts can be created through the Fletching skill. A player must first have a Fletching level of 58 and take a cut emerald and use a chisel with it to make 12 emerald bolt tips. The emerald bolt tips can then be attached to mithril bolts to make emerald bolts. Attaching 10 emerald bolt tips to 10 mithril bolts grants 55 Fletching experience. Note that these bolts require a crossbow of level 36 to fire.

Emerald bolts can be enchanted through the spell Enchant Crossbow Bolt (Emerald) by a player with level 27 Magic. The spell enchants 10 emerald bolts at a time, and once they are enchanted they become emerald bolts (e) and gain a special ability.
9339:
Ruby bolts are adamant bolts tipped with ruby bolt tips that require 46 Ranged to wield. Ruby bolts can be created with 63 Fletching granting 6.3 experience per bolt.

Ruby bolts can be enchanted through the spell Enchant Crossbow Bolt (Ruby) by a player with level 49 Magic. The spell enchants 10 ruby bolts at a time, and once they are enchanted, they become enchanted ruby bolts and gain a special ability.
9340:
Diamond bolts are adamant bolts tipped with diamond bolt tips. They are the fourth strongest gem tipped bolt in the game. These bolts can be created using the Fletching skill. 65 Fletching is required to make these bolts, and 7 Fletching experience is rewarded per bolt created.

Diamond bolts can be enchanted with the Enchant Crossbow Bolt spell, producing Diamond bolts (e). This requires 57 Magic. The spell enchants 10 bolts at a time.
9341:
Dragonstone bolts are runite bolts tipped with dragonstone. Dragonstone bolts can be created at level 71 Fletching skill by attaching dragonstone bolt tips to runite bolts. For every dragonstone bolt tip attached to a runite bolt, a player is granted 8.2 Fletching experience.

Players can enchant dragonstone bolts by using the spell Enchant Crossbow Bolt (Dragonstone), producing dragonstone bolts (e). The spell itself requires a soul rune, cosmic rune, and 15 earth runes. The spell requires 68 Magic and enchants 10 dragonstone bolts at a time.
9342:
Onyx bolts are runite bolts tipped with onyx bolt tips. Onyx bolts can be created through the Fletching skill. 73 Fletching is required to use a chisel on a cut onyx to make 24 onyx bolt tips, granting 9.4 Fletching experience. Onyx bolt tips can be attached to runite bolts to make onyx bolts, granting 9.4 experience per bolt. They require 61 Ranged to equip.

Onyx bolts can be enchanted through the spell Enchant Crossbow Bolt (Onyx), producing Onyx bolts (e). This spell requires 87 Magic and enchants 10 bolts at a time.
9376: Blurite bolts (unf) are unfinished bolts made from using a blurite bar on an anvil with a hammer, requiring 8 Smithing and the completion of The Knight's Sword quest, yielding 10 blurite bolts (unf) and 17.5 Smithing experience. Using a feather on one makes a blurite bolts, requiring 24 Fletching, and yielding 1 Fletching experience per bolt.
9377: Iron bolts (unf) are unfinished bolts made from using an iron bar on an anvil with a hammer, requiring 19 Smithing, yielding 10 iron bolts (unf) and 25 Smithing experience. Using a feather on one makes an iron bolt, requiring 39 Fletching, and yielding 1.5 Fletching experience per bolt.
9378: Steel bolts (unf) are unfinished bolts made from using a steel bar on an anvil with a hammer, requiring 33 Smithing, yielding 10 steel bolts (unf) and 37.5 Smithing experience. Using a feather on one makes a steel bolt, requiring 46 Fletching, and yielding 3.5 Fletching experience per bolt.
9379:
Mithril bolts (unf) are unfinished bolts made from using a mithril bar on an anvil with a hammer, requiring 53 Smithing, yielding 10 mithril bolts (unf) and 50 Smithing experience. Using a feather on one makes a mithril bolt, requiring 54 Fletching, and yielding 5 Fletching experience per bolt.

These are popular for Smithing training with good rates at a fair price and for power-levelling Smithing at the Blast Furnace, where you can buy mithril ore and coal from Ordan, then smith mithril bars using the Blast Furnace. A profit can be made making bolts from the bars, adding feathers, then selling them.
9382: Silver bolts (unf) are unfinished bolts made from using a silver bar on a furnace with a bolt mould, requiring 21 Crafting, yielding 10 silver bolts (unf) and 50 Crafting experience. Using a feather on one makes a silver bolt, requiring 43 Fletching, and yielding 2.5 Fletching experience per bolt.
9415: The Grapple is an animation item released with Crossbows. It is intended to be used in an animation related to grapple shortcuts, although this animation is unfinished and does not appear ingame. Aside from this, the item cannot be obtained.
9418:
The mith grapple is an item carried in the ammunition slot, used together with any crossbow (excluding the love crossbow, light, and heavy ballistae) to grapple across certain Agility shortcuts. Both items must be equipped. Using these crossbow shortcuts is a requirement for a number of achievement diary tasks. As well as the required Agility level, players will also need a certain Ranged and Strength level to use them. Armadyl's section of the God Wars Dungeon is the sole exception, as it only requires 70 Ranged.

There is a 1/25 chance of the grapple being destroyed upon usage; when this occurs, the message box states "After untying the rope, you find that your grapple is broken and useless.". The mith grapple will never be destroyed within the Hallowed Sepulchre or while doing the Shayzien Agility Course.

The grapple can be made by attaching a mith grapple tip to a mithril bolt to create a mith grapple (unf), requiring 59 Fletching, then using the unfinished grapple on a rope. The tip can be smelted using a mithril bar, requiring 59 Smithing.

The grapple is also dropped by a number of monsters found in the Ancient Cavern, which may be accessed after completing the first part of Barbarian Firemaking, requiring level 35 Firemaking.

An unlimited supply of mith grapples can be found via a crate located in Armadyl's Eyrie, due south of the grapple spot. A mith grapple is required to access this crate. The "drop trick" can be utilised here to obtain multiple grapples, as players can only retrieve a mith grapple from this crate if they do not already have one equipped or in their inventory.

A Fletching cape or max cape can be searched for a mith grapple and bronze crossbow three times a day.

The achievement diary tasks requiring a mith grapple are as follows:

Ardougne Medium - Grapple over Yanille's south wall. (39 Agility, 38 Strength, 21 Ranged)

Falador Medium - Grapple up and then jump off the north Falador wall. (11 Agility, 37 Strength, 19 Ranged)

Kandarin Medium - Use the grapple shortcut to get from the water obelisk to the Catherby shore. (36 Agility, 22 Strength, 39 Ranged)

Karamja Hard - Use the crossbow shortcut south of the volcano. (53 Agility, 42 Ranged, 21 Strength)

Lumbridge Medium - Grapple across the River Lum. (8 Agility, 19 Strength, 37 Ranged)

Lumbridge Elite - Grapple across a pylon on the Dorgesh-Kaan Agility Course, (70 Agility, 70 Ranged, 70 Strength, Death to the Dorgeshuun)

9433:
A bolt pouch allows a player to carry multiple kinds of bolts in one inventory slot, including bolt racks, as well as mith grapples, and swap between two types of bolts mid-combat. It can be purchased for 1,500 from Hirko, who runs the crossbow shop in Keldagrim on the east side of the river. Players must ask Hirko about ammo in order to be given the option to purchase a pouch; it cannot be bought in Hirko's normal shop.

Within the bolt pouch, there are four slots that can each hold 10,000 bolts of a single type, or one mith grapple. To store items in the pouch, players must use them on the pouch. Left-clicking on the pouch will open an interface showing what bolts are in the pouch and what the player has equipped in their ammo and extra ammo slots. Bolts can be moved between slots via left click and dragging.

In addition to storing ammo, the bolt pouch allows players to seamlessly swap between their equipped ammo and one extra ammo slot. This can be done via left click from the Worn Equipment tab without interrupting the player's current action, including attacking enemies. This does not work with non-ammo items, such as Ghommal's penny or Rada's blessing - these items can only be equipped in the primary ammo slot, and switching ammo from the extra slot into the primary slot will unequip them.

If the player has Dizana's quiver equipped or in their inventory it will disable the bolt pouch's functionality to swap between their equipped ammo and the extra ammo in the bolt pouch. The Worn Equipment tab will not show the extra ammo in the bolt pouch—only the ammo in the quiver. If the player attempts to move ammo from the bolt pouch into their ammunition slot using the bolt pouch interface, it will not work, and a message will warn the player You cannot change ammo from your bolt pouch with Dizana's quiver on your person.

Attempting to use an alchemy spell on the bolt pouch fails and results in the message The dwarven pouch resists your magic. appearing in the chatbox.

The bolt pouch is never one of protected items kept in the inventory on death. In PvM death it always goes to the gravestone where it may be reclaimed with its contents preserved. In PvP death, it is always destroyed and its contents are dropped to the killer.

If an Ultimate Ironman loses the bolt pouch on death, either through despawning from a pve deathpile or being wiped from an item retrieval service, its contents will be preserved and can be reclaimed by buying a new bolt pouch from Hirko.

The bolt pouch is not obtainable on Deadman Mode worlds.

9470: The gnome scarf is a possible reward from the Gnome Restaurant activity. Players have a 1/17 chance of receiving this from Captain Daerkin and Captain Ninto. The scarf has no stats, but it can function as warm clothing in Wintertodt reducing damage taken, and is the only tradeable neck slot item to do so. It is often used for fashion purposes.
9472:
Gnome goggles are a possible reward from the Gnome Restaurant minigame. Players have a 1/17 chance to obtain them as a reward from Captain Daerkin or Captain Ninto, which are accessible with hard deliveries. The gnome goggles are part of the gnome pilot set which also includes the gnome scarf.

Goggles can be combined with the Bomber cap from the Enlightened Journey quest by talking with Auguste, resulting in a Cap and goggles. As the cap and goggles can be stored, though not the goggles themselves, this provides a means of storing the goggles in the armour case (as part of the bomber jacket costume).
9474:
Reward tokens are received for gaining at least 12 credits in the Gnome Restaurant minigame. It can be used at any time to summon a mounted terrorchick gnome bearing gnome cuisine. A player may only have one reward token at a time, but when used, it grants the player one food item for every 12 credits the player has, for up to 10 free items of gnome food. This makes it useful for exploring dungeons and other dangerous areas as it provides up to 10 pieces of food in just one inventory slot. Depending on which food you get, you can heal 5 to 15 HP per food for a potential total of 50 to 150 HP (although the drinks can have negative effects on skills such as strength and attack). While it can be brought to the Barbarian Assault minigame, it can not be used there.

If a reward token is destroyed, the credits are not destroyed and a player can talk to Gianne jnr. to get a new token. If the mounted terrorchick gnome cannot reach the player and eventually despawns, the amassed credits will still be retained.

Once the player has filled their reward token by obtaining a total of 120 credits, the dialogue from Gianne jnr. will change while getting a new job. This (unintentionally) allows players to recycle their newly given job without penalty by right-clicking Gianne jnr.'s "Get job" option before moving on to subsequent dialogue.

A mint cake can be obtained as a tip from Brambickle, Wingstone, and Penwie in the Gnome Restaurant minigame. A one-off mint cake can also be obtained during or after The Path of Glouphrie by giving Longramble a tangled toad's legs, though receiving one this way does not register it in the collection log.
