9625:
A crystal saw is an item made from a crystal saw seed by invoking a singing bowl in either Brimstail's cave or Prifddinas. The seed is awarded to players who complete The Eyes of Glouphrie quest.

When in the inventory, the saw allows the player to build furniture up to 3 levels higher than their current Construction level. Note that this boost only works on furniture that requires both a saw and a hammer to make (STASH units, Fire Pits, and Shipbuilding included); as such, the saw cannot assist in building new rooms or planting flowers in a garden. This bonus stacks with all other visible boosts to Construction, making it possible to build items up to 8 levels higher than the player's current Construction level when used in conjunction with a +5 boost from spicy stew. However, given the erratic nature of spicy stew boosts, it is more common for players to combine it with a trimmed cup of tea for a +6 boost.

If players lose or destroy the saw, they can get it back by talking to Brimstail in his cave and selecting his first dialogue option. He will not give players a seed if they have either the seed or the saw in the bank or inventory. The saw is destroyed upon death.

The saw can be used to boost your construction level for Sailing Facilities and core boat parts, despite the latter not requiring a saw. When used to construct core boat parts the crystal saw will not lose any charges.

The saw cannot be used to get higher-level contracts in Mahogany Homes.
9626:
The crystal saw seed is an item given to the player by King Narnode in the Tree Gnome Stronghold as a reward for completing The Eyes of Glouphrie quest. The seed can be enchanted into a crystal saw by using it on the singing bowl in Brimstail's cave in the south-west area of the Gnome Stronghold or in Prifddinas.

If the player loses the seed or the saw, they can speak to Brimstail and select the "Hello, just wanted a chat." chat option to obtain another seed.
9627: A handwritten book is a book written by Oaknock the Engineer that is found in the drawers near Brimstail in his cave. It is a word-for-word transcription of the book Crystal singing for beginners that players receive from Ilfeen.
9629: The tyras helm is a helmet that can be worn with a Defence level of 5. It is nearly identical in statistics to the steel full helm, although it provides a slightly better ranged attack bonus. To obtain a Tyras helm, the player can either buy one from Trader Stan's Trading Post or from another player. The helm cannot be smithed.
9632:
Daeyalt ore is a rare ore that can only be mined from daeyalt rocks by players with 20 Mining during and after the Darkness of Hallowvale quest. It cannot be smelted into a bar using the Smithing skill.

Daeyalt ore is found in the Meiyerditch mine in north-western Meiyerditch in the Sanguinesti region and in the Daeyalt essence mine in Darkmeyer. A player gets 3 ores from each rock wall.

If players are sent to the Meiyerditch mine by the Vyrewatch in Meiyerditch, they must mine 15 ores and place them in the mine cart, then ask a nearby vampyre juvinate to be released from the mine. This can be skipped by talking to the juvinate while wearing a vyre noble outfit, requiring partial completion of Sins of the Father.
9634:
A Vyrewatch top is a piece of the Vyrewatch clothing set that can be bought from Trader Sven's Black Market Goods in Meiyerditch and reduce the chances of being spotted by the Vyrewatch patrols when worn.

In the quest, Sins of the Father, the Vyrewatch top is upgraded to the Vyre noble top by Polmafi Ferdygris
9636:
Vyrewatch legs are a part of the Vyrewatch clothing set. They may be bought from Trader Sven in Meiyerditch and reduce the chances of being spotted by the Vyrewatch patrols when worn.

In the quest, Sins of the Father, the Vyrewatch legs are upgraded to the Vyre noble legs by Polmafi Ferdygris.
9638:
Vyrewatch shoes are a part of the Vyrewatch clothing set. They may be bought from Trader Sven in Meiyerditch and reduce the chances of being spotted by the Vyrewatch patrols when worn.

In the quest, Sins of the Father, the Vyrewatch shoes are upgraded to Vyre noble shoes by Polmafi Ferdygris.
9640: Citizen top is part of the citizen outfit, and can be bought from Trader Sven in Meiyerditch. It has no quest or level requirements to wear.
9642: Citizen trousers is part of the citizen outfit, and can be bought from Trader Sven in Meiyerditch. It has no quest or level requirements.
9644: Citizen shoes are part of the citizen outfit, and can be bought from Trader Sven in Meiyerditch. It has no quest or level requirements to wear.
9646: The castle sketch 1 is a quest item made during the Darkness of Hallowvale quest. It is made by using a piece of charcoal on a sheet of papyrus while standing on the north side of the castle at the north end of Meiyerditch. The sketch must be given to Safalaan along with castle sketch 2 and castle sketch 3 to complete the intelligence-gathering part of the quest.
9647:
The castle sketch 2 is a quest item made during the Darkness of Hallowvale quest. It is made by using a piece of charcoal on a sheet of papyrus while standing on the west side of the castle at the north end of Meiyerditch. The sketch must be given to Safalaan, along with the castle sketch 1 and castle sketch 3, to complete the intelligence-gathering part of the quest.

When the player attempts to make this sketch for the first time, they will be interrupted by a cutscene with Vanstrom Klause, Vanescula Drakan and her brother, Ranis Drakan. After this, the player will finish their sketch.
9648:
The castle sketch 3 is a quest item made during the Darkness of Hallowvale quest. It is a sketch of the southern part of Castle Drakan. It is made by using a piece of charcoal on a sheet of papyrus while standing on the South side of the castle (just a few steps west from where Safalaan give you the mission to sketch out the castle) at the north end of Meiyerditch. The sketch must be given to Safalaan along with castle sketch 1 and castle sketch 2 to complete the intelligence-gathering part of the quest.

When the player attempts to make this sketch for the first time, they will be interrupted by a cutscene with Vanstrom Klause. After this, Vanstrom attacks the player, but they are saved by Sarius Guile. Note that the player still has not finished the sketch after this cutscene as they were interrupted.
9650:
The blood tithe pouch is an unobtainable item released with Darkness of Hallowvale. It presumably would have been an item that players would have obtained during the quest.

A similar item can be seen served by a vyrewatch to Vanescula Drakan and Ranis Drakan during a cutscene in Darkness of Hallowvale. It is not possible to obtain the item in-game.
9652:
Haemalchemy volume 1 is a book that gives details on what the Vampyres are experimenting with. It must be telegrabbed in the Meiyerditch Laboratories to be obtained. It is given to Safalaan at the end of the Darkness of Hallowvale quest.

Haemalchemy, when broken down by definition, is the study of transmuting or modifying blood.

If a player attempts to read the book on haemalchemy, they will get the message, "This book seems far too complex to you at the moment." While the exact contents of the book are a mystery, it is known that a majority of the book is written in the vampyric language and that it details their usage of haemalchemy in an attempt to increase the amount of blood received from tithing a human and in strengthening their immunity to conventional weaponry.
9653:
The sealed message is obtained during the Darkness of Hallowvale quest. It is a sealed letter written by Safalaan to be delivered to Veliaf. Attempting to read it gives the message "The message is sealed and addressed to Veliaf. It would be rude of you to open it."

Once delivered, the player discovers that it is really a commendation letter from the "highest ranking member of the Myreque", and Veliaf then makes the player a full member of the Myreque.
9654:
Door key can refer to the following:

Door key (Darkness of Hallowvale) - A key acquired during the Darkness of Hallowvale quest.

Door key (Witch's House) - A key acquired during the Witch's House quest to open said house. May also be required for Mourning's End Part II.
9655: The ladder top is a quest item found during the Darkness of Hallowvale quest while trying to cross Meiyerditch without being spotted by the Vyrewatch. It is used to extend a broken ladder to allow the player access to the upper level of a building which is on the route through the town.
9659:
Buckets of water are unobtainable items that can be found throughout Meiyerditch. Attempting to take them results in the chatbox message I really do not want to go anywhere near that! It stinks!, and attempting to cast Telekinetic Grab results in the chatbox message I really don't want to waste runes grabbing this item.

Based on the message given in the chatbox, it can be assumed that the bucket contains urine or stagnant liquids.
9662:
The useless key is an unobtainable item released alongside A Taste of Hope, created to replace the discontinued shortcut key. Two versions of the key were created to replace the standard and bank placeholder versions of the shortcut key. While the useless key was never meant to be seen by players, it inadvertently became visible as the bank placeholders were not wiped from the game. Therefore, any players who had created a bank placeholder of the shortcut key saw the useless key takes its place.

The placeholders were removed over a year later in an update on 13 June 2019.
9665: The torch is an animation item released with the rework of the Sea Slug. It is temporarily wielded by the player in an animation where they scare away a Fisherman or a Sea Slug with a lit torch. Aside from this, the item cannot be obtained.
9668: An initiate harness m can be obtained after completing the Recruitment Drive quest by buying it from Sir Tiffy Cashien in Falador. It may be opened to obtain initiate armour. Once opened it cannot be recreated by a Grand Exchange Clerk.
9680: Sea slug glue is a quest item used in The Slug Menace quest. It is made by giving a dead sea slug to Bailey on the Fishing Platform near Witchaven. The glue is used to join together the three fragments of Page 3 of Maledict's holy book, which is used later in the quest.
9682:
The door transcription is a quest item used in the Slug Menace quest. It is given to the player by Savant after using the Commorb v2 to scan the markings on a mysterious door in the newly discovered shrine underneath Witchaven.

If you happen to lose your door transcription, you can get it back by using the Playback option on the Commorb v2 and looking at your current assignment.
9684:
Page 1 is a quest item used in the Slug Menace quest. It is found by searching the study desk in the Mayor's house in Witchaven. The page is used in conjunction with Page 2 and Page 3 of Brother Maledict's holy book in order to determine how to make the special runes needed to open a mysterious door in the newly discovered shrine beneath Witchaven.

In the quest, the player was tricked by sea slug possessed citizens that it will help shut Mother Mallum's door, but in reality, frees her.
9685: Page 2 is a quest item used in the Slug Menace quest. It is given to the player by Ezekial Lovecraft, the owner of the fishing store in Witchaven. The page is used in conjunction with Page 1 and Page 3 of Brother Maledict's holy book in order to determine how to make the special runes needed to open a mysterious door in the newly discovered shrine beneath Witchaven.
9686: Page 3 is a quest item used in the Slug Menace quest. It is given to the player by Col. O'Niall in the form of three Fragments which the player must glue together using sea slug glue. The page is used in conjunction with Page 1 and Page 2 of Brother Maledict's holy book in order to determine how to make the special runes needed to open a mysterious door in the newly discovered shrine beneath Witchaven.
9687: Fragment 1 is a quest item used in the Slug Menace quest. It is given to the player by Col. O'Niall, along with Fragment 2 and Fragment 3. The player must glue the fragments together using sea slug glue and doing a small jigsaw puzzle to form Page 3 of Maledict's holy book. This page is used in conjunction with Page 1 and Page 2 of the book in order to determine how to make the special runes needed to open a mysterious door in the newly discovered shrine beneath Witchaven.
9688: Fragment 2 is a quest item used in the Slug Menace quest. It is given to the player by Col. O'Niall, along with Fragment 1 and Fragment 3. The player must glue the fragments together using sea slug glue and doing a small jigsaw puzzle to form Page 3 of Maledict's holy book. This page is used in conjunction with Page 1 and Page 2 of the book in order to determine how to make the special runes needed to open a mysterious door in the newly discovered shrine beneath Witchaven.
9689: Fragment 3 is a quest item used in the Slug Menace quest. It is given to the player by Col. O'Niall, along with fragment 2 and fragment 1. The player must glue the fragments together using sea slug glue and doing a small jigsaw puzzle to form Page 3 of Maledict's holy book. This page is used in conjunction with page 1 and page 2 of the book in order to determine how to make the special runes needed to open a mysterious door in the newly discovered shrine beneath Witchaven.
9690:
The blank water rune is a quest item used in The Slug Menace. It is made by right-clicking on Page 2 of Brother Maledict's holy book and choosing the "shape water" option with a rune essence or pure essence in the inventory. During this process the player must also make a blank air rune, a blank earth rune, a blank fire rune, and a blank mind rune using page 1 and page 3. The player needs a chisel in their inventory to make these runes.

Make more than one blank because you can fail while chiselling the shape of the rune and/or binding it with the element of the rune.

When used on the Water Altar in the usual way it turns into a special water rune, which is needed later in the quest. This item is lost upon death with all the others blank runes aswell.
9691: A water rune is a special type of water rune used during The Slug Menace. It is made by using a blank water rune on the Water Altar in the normal way and is used to unlock a mysterious door in the newly discovered shrine beneath Witchaven. Sometimes the blank water rune can break while trying to fuse it with the Water Altar. In order to unlock the door the player must also have made a special air rune, a special earth rune, a special fire rune, and a special mind rune. Unlike normal water runes, this cannot be used to cast a spell.
9692:
The blank air rune is a quest item used in The Slug Menace. It is made by right-clicking on Page 1 of Brother Maledict's holy book and choosing the "shape air" option with a rune essence or pure essence in the inventory. During this process the player must also make a blank water rune, a blank earth rune, a blank fire rune, and a blank mind rune using page 2 and page 3. The player needs a chisel in their inventory to make these runes.

Make more than one blank because you can fail while chiselling the shape of the rune, and/or binding it with the element of the rune.

When used on the Air Altar in the usual way it turns into a special air rune which is needed later in the quest. This item is lost upon death with all the others blank runes aswell.
9693:
Air runes are one of the four elemental runes. They are used in every combat spell and most teleportation spells in the standard spellbook, as well as in many spells from other spellbooks. Because they are used very often, players are recommended to purchase an item that can provide infinite air runes while equipped, such as a staff of air.

A common way for beginning players to obtain air runes is to talk to the magic tutor in Lumbridge. She will give you 30 air and mind runes if you don't have any in your inventory or bank. Air runes or packs can be bought from Magic shops, such as Aubury's Rune Shop in Varrock. Non-ironman players can also purchase them from the Nightmare Zone using 25 reward points.
9694:
The blank earth rune is a quest item used in The Slug Menace. It is made by right-clicking on Page 1 of Brother Maledict's holy book and choosing the "shape earth" option with a rune essence or pure essence in the inventory. During this process the player must also make a blank air rune, a blank water rune, a blank fire rune, and a blank mind rune using page 2 and page 3. The player needs a chisel in their inventory to make these runes.

Make more than one blank because you can fail while chiselling the shape of the rune, and/or binding it with the element of the rune.

When used on an Earth Altar in the usual way it turns into a special earth rune which is needed later in the quest. This item is lost upon death with all the others blank runes aswell.
9695: An earth rune is a special type of earth rune used during The Slug Menace. It is made by using a blank earth rune on the Earth Altar, yielding 2 Runecraft experience regardless of whether the essence is successfully empowered or not. This experience is given even if It is used to unlock a mysterious door in the newly discovered shrine beneath Witchaven. In order to unlock the door the player must also have made a special air rune, a special fire rune, a special mind rune and a special water rune. It is made by using one of the three pages that are found during the quest. You must have one or more rune essence as there is the chance that you might shatter the essence creating "rune shards". Unlike normal earth runes, this cannot be used to cast a spell.
9696:
The blank mind rune is a quest item used in The Slug Menace. It is made by right-clicking on Page 3 of Brother Maledict's holy book and choosing the "shape mind" option with a rune essence or pure essence in the inventory. During this process the player must also make a blank air rune, a blank earth rune, a blank fire rune, and a blank water rune using page 1 and page 2. The player needs a chisel in their inventory to make these runes.

It is recommended that players make more than one blank because players can fail while chiselling the shape of the rune, as well as when binding it with the element of the rune.

When used on a Mind Altar in the usual way it turns into a special mind rune which is needed later in the quest. This item is lost upon death with all the others blank runes aswell.
9697: A mind rune is a special type of mind rune used during The Slug Menace. It is made by using a blank mind rune on the Mind Altar in the normal way and is used to unlock a mysterious door in the newly discovered shrine beneath Witchaven. In order to unlock the door the player must also have made a special air rune, a special earth rune, a special fire rune and a special water rune. Unlike normal mind runes, this cannot be used to cast a spell.
9698:
The blank fire rune is a quest item used in The Slug Menace. It is made by right-clicking on Page 2 of Brother Maledict's holy book and choosing the "shape fire" option with a rune essence or pure essence in the inventory. During this process the player must also make a blank air rune, a blank earth rune, a blank water rune, and a blank mind rune using page 1 and page 3. The player needs a chisel in their inventory to make these runes.

Make more than one blank because you can fail while chiselling the shape of the rune, and/or binding it with the element of the rune.

When used on a Fire Altar in the usual way it turns into a special fire rune which is needed later in the quest. This item is lost upon death with all the others blank runes aswell.
9702:
Stick is a troll found on Death Plateau. While not as strong as the nearby Rock, he can hit a max of 27, although this can be completely blocked with Protect from Melee. Like the rest of the "big", "bad" trolls in the area, such as Rock, Pee Hat, and Kraka, he can drop a rune warhammer or granite shield, making him a common target for ironman accounts.

Stick can be safespotted with Ranged to the south-west of his spawn location.
9703:
A Training sword is a beginner weapon. It has identical stats to a bronze sword.

It is obtained for free along with a training shield from the Melee combat tutor, just south of the Lumbridge General Store. It can be replaced if lost, but only one can be obtained at a time. Due to the accessibility, this sword is ideal for players who are new to the game and have just finished Tutorial Island.
9704: The training shield is a beginner's item. The shield has an appearance similar to a white decorative shield and has the same bonuses as a wooden shield, though it weighs significantly more. It can be obtained for free from the melee combat tutor east of Lumbridge Castle. Players are only allowed one shield at any time.
9705: The training bow can be obtained from the Ranged combat tutor in Lumbridge. As it only requires a Ranged level of 1 to wield, it can be used by all players. It can only fire training arrows, which are given to players in sets of 25 by the tutor. It has the same stats as a shortbow.
9706:
Training arrows are arrows given by the ranged combat tutor. They can only be fired using a training bow. The combat stats of the arrows are equivalent to bronze arrows but are less used due to the fact that they can only be fired by a training bow.

Training arrows can be collected from the ranged combat tutor (east of Lumbridge Castle), along with a training bow, every 30 minutes. Although technically the player cannot claim more than 25, arrows on the ground do not count towards that limit. This means that a player can shoot the arrows without picking them up, claim an extra 25 arrows, and then pick up the fired ones from the ground, obtaining more than 25 in total.

The time limit is shared with the magic combat tutor, meaning runes must not have been collected from the magic combat tutor in the past 30 minutes to be able to receive training arrows.
9715:
The slashed book is a quest item used in Elemental Workshop I. It is made by using a knife or any slashweapon on a battered book. Additionally, it can be found by searching the bookcase where the battered book was originally found, only after creating a slashed book for the first time.

It is used to make elemental shields or mind shields.

The slashed book (or the battered book) may be one of the items on the item list, given by Thorgel, that is needed to receive a death talisman during or after Mourning's End II; however, it is not needed to finish the quest as long as you already have a death talisman or catalytic talisman.

Duplicates can be drop tricked by searching the bookcase to obtain another only after the player has created a slashed book. Duplicates can be obtained after completing the quest.
9716: Rock or rocks may refer to any of the following:
9717:
The Beaten book or the Book of the Elemental Helm begins the Elemental Workshop II quest. It can be found in the Digsite's Exam Centre library south-east of Varrock, or in your POH bookcase after completing the quest (Book of the Elemental Helm), and has a scroll inside it as a bookmark. This scroll helps find the key to get into a lower level of the workshop.

To make a mind helmet for the quest you must have this book in your inventory after which the book serves no purpose beyond reading (other than use for Kandarin Medium Diary). If the book is lost or destroyed prior to completion of the quest, another may be obtained by searching the Exam Centre's library again after dropping the scroll obtained from the book.
9718: The crane schematic is an item used in the Elemental Workshop II quest. It includes instructions on how to make a crane claw from elemental metal. This item is gained by searching one of two crates near the entrance to the Elemental Workshop II quest room.
9719:
The lever schematic is an item that can be obtained during the Elemental Workshop II quest from the same crate as the claw schematic.

This is a clue as to the correct solution to the pipe connection puzzle in the junction box. It shows that the middle pipe going to the lever, top-right in the interface of the junction box, provides incoming water that is then directed by the lever down one of the other 2 pipes and on to the press. In combination with how the pipes are plumbed into the back of the junction box, this means that the top-right pipe end in the interface must be connected to the large water supply pipe, top-middle in the interface and that the other 2 pipes coming from the lever, bottom-right and bottom-middle in the interface must be connected to the 2 pipes going to the press, top-left and bottom-left in the interface. Given these constraints, there is only one possible solution.
9720: The crane claw is a quest item made in the Elemental Workshop II quest. It is made from elemental metal, requiring 20 Smithing, yielding 20 Smithing experience. It is used to repair the crane.
9724: A large cog is an item used in the Elemental Workshop II quest. It is found by searching the catwalk and downstairs in the secondary Elemental Workshop, and the location is random for each player. It can be used, along with the small cog and medium cog, to repair the wind tunnel, by placing it on the right-hand pin on the east side of the room.
9725: Medium cog is an item used in the Elemental Workshop II quest. It is found by searching upstairs and downstairs in the secondary Elemental Workshop, and the location is random for each player. It can be used, along with the large cog and small cog, to repair the wind tunnel by placing it on the lower-left pin on the east side of the room.
9726: A small cog is an item used in the Elemental Workshop II quest. It is found by searching upstairs and downstairs in the second area of Elemental Workshop, and the location is random for each player. It can be used, along with the large cog and medium cog, to repair the wind tunnel, by placing it on the upper-left pin on the east side of the room.
9727: A primed bar is an elemental metal that has undergone several processes making it receptive to magical forces formed by machines in the basement of the Elemental Workshop. They can be turned into primed mind bars.
9728:
Primed mind bars are made during and after the Elemental Workshop II quest in the Elemental Workshop in Seers' Village. The bar may be created by placing a primed bar into the extractor gun found in the mind room and operating the machinery. Doing so will temporarily reduce the player's Magic level by 20.

The bar may be smithed into a mind shield with a slashed book or a mind helmet with a beaten book, by using it on the workbench in the first level of the Elemental Workshop.
9729:
The elemental helmet is magical headwear that can be made after completing the Elemental Workshop II quest. The helmet is created by using an elemental metal on a workbench within the Elemental Workshop with a beaten book in the player's inventory. This requires level 20 Smithing and grants 20 experience.

Although the helmet can be traded between players, it can only be equipped by those who have completed Elemental Workshop II.
9731:
A mind shield is an upgraded version of the elemental shield, offering an additional +3 magic defence bonus over the latter. It is made during and after the Elemental Workshop II quest in the elemental workshop dungeon.

Making the shield requires 30 Smithing, a primed mind bar, a hammer, and a slashed book in the inventory. Right-click the "Smith" option on a workbench in the elemental workshop to smith the shield, which grants the player 30 Smithing experience. Equipping a mind shield requires completion of Elemental Workshop II.

Warning: When attempting to smith a mind shield, having a beaten book, but no slashed book, will automatically create a mind helmet, not a mind shield.

A mind shield can be used as partial protection against the icy breath of skeletal wyverns and wyverns. When worn, it reduces the maximum damage of wyvern icy breath attacks to 10.
9733:
A mind helmet can be made during and after the Elemental Workshop II quest in the Elemental Workshop dungeon from a primed mind bar while having a beaten book in your inventory.

Creating a mind helmet is a medium achievement in the Kandarin Diary.
9735:
Goat horn is an item dropped by goats, billy goats, and Wyrmscraig goat.

When used with a pestle and mortar, the goat horn becomes goat horn dust, which can be mixed with harralander and a vial of water at level 36 Herblore to make a combat potion.
9736: Goat horn dust is made by grinding goat horns with a pestle and mortar. It is combined with a harralander potion (unf), requiring 36 Herblore, and yielding a combat potion(3) and 84 Herblore experience.
9747:
An Attack cape is a Cape of Accomplishment that can be bought for 99,000 coins from Ajjat at the Warriors' Guild by any player who has achieved level 99 in the Attack skill.

Like all skill capes, the Attack cape gives +9 to all defensive stats, and also a +4 bonus to prayer if it is trimmed, which requires a separate skill at level 99. The cape is automatically trimmed if this condition is met.

When the Attack cape is equipped, it will negate the need for warrior guild tokens when accessing the basement and 2nd floor in the Warriors' Guild, allowing players to stay within the Cyclopes area for as long as they please. However, if the player removes the cape to replace it with something else, they will be pulled out of the area once out of combat.

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room, as part of the Attack cape set, along with the hood. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

As of 1 August 2026, there are 518,396 players that have achieved level 99 in Attack.

9749:
The Attack hood is the skillcape hood associated with having achieved skill mastery in the Attack skill. Players may buy the hood alongside the Attack cape from Ajjat at the Warriors' Guild for 99,000 coins, providing that they have level 99 in Attack. The hood itself provides absolutely no offensive or defensive bonuses and may be worn for purely aesthetic purposes.

While the hood is bought with the skillcape, it is not needed to perform the emote associated with it; the skillcape is the only essential item.

Should players lose the hood, they may reclaim it from Ajjat for free.

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room, as part of the Attack cape set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
9750:
The Strength cape is a Cape of Accomplishment, obtainable by players with 99 Strength. The Strength cape can be bought with the hood from Sloane (or Yadech Strongarm after the completion of While Guthix Sleeps) in the Warriors' Guild for 99,000 coins. Sloane is located on the 1st floor, after passing through two heavy doors.

Like all skill capes, the Strength cape gives +9 to all defensive stats, and also a +4 bonus to prayer if it is trimmed, which requires a separate skill at level 99. The cape is automatically trimmed if this condition is met.

The strength cape has a teleport to the Warriors' Guild, with unlimited uses, and unlike the combat bracelet, it will teleport players inside the guild.

It also has a right-click "boost" option, also activating upon equipping the cape, that temporarily boosts Strength by 1, to 100.

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room, as part of the Strength cape set, along with the hood. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

As of 1 August 2026, there are 791,091 players that have achieved level 99 in Strength.
9751:

The Defence cape is a Cape of Accomplishment that players can purchase only when they've reached level 99 in the Defence skill. It can be bought from Harlan, the Melee combat tutor, for 99,000 coins from where he resides, close to the Lumbridge general store.

Like all skill capes, the Defence cape gives +9 to all defensive stats, and also a +4 bonus to prayer if it is trimmed, which requires a separate skill at level 99. The cape is automatically trimmed if this condition is met.

When the defence cape is equipped, players can enable the cape to act as a ring of life. This option is toggle-able, and can be enabled/disabled by the player at any given time. As it acts like a ring of life, it is one of the few items whose teleports will work up to level 30 Wilderness, while most other means of teleportation will not work above level 20 Wilderness.

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room, as part of the Defence cape set, along with the hood. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

The ranging cape is a Cape of Accomplishment awarded to players who have achieved 99 Ranged. The skillcape and its respective hood can be bought from Aaron the Armour salesman in the Ranging Guild for 99,000 coins.

Like all skill capes, the Ranging cape gives +9 to all defensive stats, and also a +4 bonus to prayer if it is trimmed, which requires a separate skill at level 99. The cape is automatically trimmed if this condition is met.

When the ranging cape is equipped, it grants players the ammo-saving effects of Ava's accumulator. Completion of Animal Magnetism is not required to benefit from this perk. By default, the cape will only provide the 72% ammo-saving effect of the accumulator, not the improved 80% savings of Ava's assembler. However, Vorkath's head can be used on the cape to increase its ammo-saving rate to 80% to match the assembler (an assembler cannot be used as a substitute). This consumes the head, and will upgrade all ranging and max capes currently in possession or purchased in the future. Note that upgrading the cape does not give it the ranged strength and accuracy bonuses of Ava's assembler.

Like Ava's devices, the ranging cape is affected by metallic interference.

The ranging cape will also collect miscellaneous steel items (or mithril items after it has been upgraded with a Vorkath's head) into the player's inventory; as with the Ava's devices this can be disabled with the right-click Commune option.

It also has a right-click "Boost" option, only shown when the cape is equipped, that temporarily boosts Ranged by 1, to 100.

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room, as part of the Ranging cape set, along with the hood. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

The Hitpoints cape is a Cape of Accomplishment that can be bought from Surgeon General Tafani in the Emir's Arena hospital after achieving level 99 in the Hitpoints skill. The skillcape and its corresponding hood can be purchased for 99,000 coins. The skillcape has a white colour and red stripes if trimmed.

Like all skill capes, the Hitpoints cape gives +9 to all defensive stats, and also a +4 bonus to prayer if it is trimmed, which requires a separate skill at level 99. The cape is automatically trimmed if this condition is met.

When the Hitpoints cape is equipped, the player's natural Hitpoints regeneration rate is doubled to 2 Hitpoints per minute instead of the natural rate of 1 Hitpoint per minute. This does not stack with the Rapid Heal prayer, but does stack with the regen bracelet to regenerate 4 Hitpoints per minute.

Utilising the worn boost effect on the cape will instantly give you +1 health point. This can be used once per minute.

On the mobile and Official Client the effect is visible in the form of a second blue sector around the player's hitpoints orb. This blue sector is only visible when its cooldown is less than that of the natural regeneration segment (otherwise it will be hidden behind it). The blue regeneration bar is functionally independent from your natural regeneration bar, and cannot be influenced by external factors such as Rapid heal (though Rapid Heal can still be used to offset your natural regeneration to better match that of the blue regeneration bar for optimal healing). Despite not stacking with the Rapid Heal prayer, the prayer causes the blue regeneration bar to completely disappear, though it does not reset.

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room, as part of the Hitpoint cape set, along with the hood. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

The models used during the emote slightly change depending on if your player character is body type A or B.

The Agility cape is the only piece of the graceful set that can be purchased with coins.

The cape can be purchased for 99,000 coins from Duradel (or Kuradal after completion of While Guthix Sleeps), in Shilo Village. Slayer capes are black in colour, and have a red trim if the player has more than one level 99 skill. As Duradel is in Shilo Village, players must have completed the Shilo Village quest in order to buy the cape.

Like all skill capes, the Slayer cape gives +9 to all defensive stats, and also a +4 bonus to prayer if it is trimmed, which requires a separate skill at level 99. The cape is automatically trimmed if this condition is met.

When the Slayer cape is equipped or in the inventory, there is a 10% chance of being given the option to have their previous Slayer task reassigned by the same Slayer Master the player got their last task from, either in person or through the Astral Contact spell. If activated on a boss task, the assigned boss can potentially be a different one.

When the cape effect activates on Konar quo Maten's tasks, she will retain the same location as with the old task. On Mortimer's tasks, the modifier of the task is retained.

The quest point cape is a cape of accomplishment that can be obtained by players who have completed all quests (excluding miniquests). The cape, along with the quest point hood, can be purchased from the Wise Old Man in Draynor Village for 99,000 coins. To trim the cape, players must complete all achievement diaries, thus earning them the achievement diary cape as well.

Should a new quest be released, the cape will be unequipped, and the player will not be able to equip or operate it until the new quest is completed. If the player's inventory is full, the cape will be banked instead. In the event that their inventory and bank are both full, the cape will be lost, and will have to be re-purchased from the Wise Old Man.

The cape is a popular goal for ironmen due to its quick teleport to a fairy ring. Additionally, performing the quest cape emote in the Wise Old Man's house is an elite task in the Lumbridge & Draynor Diary. The emote can also be used at the top of Falador Castle for a task in the elite Falador Diary.

Unlike skill hiscores, there is no official way to track the number of players who currently own the cape; it must be shared by Jagex. In February 2020, there were 61,766 current members who had obtained the quest point cape.

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room, as part of the Quest point cape set, along with the hood. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored. Players who own a quest cape but no longer have all quests completed will find they cannot store the cape until they re-complete all quests. However, quest capes that were already mounted on the cape rack prior to new quests becoming available will remain on the rack. Quest capes on cape racks therefore represent that the home owner at one point or another had attained all available quest points at the time of mounting.

Auguste's sapling is given during the Enlightened Journey quest by Auguste to grow into a willow tree in order to obtain Willow branches to build the basket of the balloon for the Balloon transport system. The branches can also be cut off any existing willow tree in a farming patch or obtained by trading with other players. If the sapling is lost before it is planted, another can be purchased from Auguste for 30,000 coins. However, as a willow seed costs 58 coins, this option is only reasonable for ironmen who are unwilling or unable to obtain a seed by other methods.

Auguste gives the player the sapling for free, only the first time. With it, he also gives the player a basket of apples, to pay a gardener to watch over it. Growing this sapling to a willow tree takes 4 hours. The sapling cannot be re-obtained after completing the quest, and cannot be stored in the seed vault.
9934:
An origami balloon is a smaller version of a hot air balloon made during the Enlightened Journey quest to test the scientific principles of a hot air balloon. It will end up being burnt.

The Origami balloon can be made by players who have reached the point in the quest in which they are made. Dyes can be applied to the balloon as well. It will produce the same result and burn after a short distance flight (if there are no obstacles in front of the balloon, it will fly farther; otherwise, it will burn down before it reaches an obstacle).

Making an origami balloon provides 35 Crafting experience.

All of the necessary parts, with the exception of papyrus, can be found in the dwarven city of Keldagrim. The city's general store, Gunslik's Assorted Items stocks candles, as well as tinderboxes. On the east side of the city, in the marketplace, the Carefree Crafting Stall stocks balls of wool. Papyrus can be bought in Shilo Village, Al Kharid or East Ardougne, found in a cupboard on the ground floor of the White Knights' Castle, and dye can be made in Pollnivneach and Draynor Village or purchased in Lletya.

To make an origami balloon:

Use a papyrus with a ball of wool, creating a balloon structure.

Use an unlit candle or black candle on the uncompleted Origami balloon.

Optionally, use a dye on the balloon to change its colour.

The finished origami balloon can be flown by using it with a tinderbox, providing 20 Firemaking experience.

Making origami balloons will result in 75,000–80,000 Crafting experience per hour which is inferior to gems experience-wise and to molten glass money-wise.
9943:
The sandbag is a quest item used during Enlightened Journey as an anchor for the air balloon. It is made by using a sack on a sand pit or a bucket of sand. Players can use a bucket on the sandbag to make it into a bucket of sand.

For non-ironmen accounts, the sandbag can be obtained quite easily with the use of the Grand Exchange. A bucket of sand can be used on the sack to make the sandbag even before starting the quest. Players can also make the sandbag after quest completion, although there is no further use for this at present.
9944:
The bomber jacket is one of two items of clothing that form the Bomber jacket costume, the other being the Bomber cap. Players obtain the set after completing Enlightened Journey. If lost, the jacket can be retrieved again from Auguste on Entrana. It can be used as warm clothing at Wintertodt.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Bomber jacket costume set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
9945:
The bomber cap and the bomber jacket form the bomber jacket costume, which is a reward for completing the Enlightened Journey Quest. If lost on death, a replacement can be claimed from Auguste in Entrana.

The bomber cap can be combined with the gnome goggles from the Gnome Restaurant minigame into a cap and goggles by talking with Auguste on Entrana.

It can be used as warm clothing for the Wintertodt.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Bomber jacket costume set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
9946:
Cap and goggles are a combination of gnome goggles, obtained during Gnome Restaurant, and the bomber cap reward from the Enlightened Journey quest. The items can be combined by talking with Auguste on the island of Entrana. To separate the combined cap and goggles, right click and choose "split".

If you die with this item, the goggles will disappear.

The cap and goggles can be used as warm clothing for the Wintertodt.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Bomber jacket costume set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
9947: The old red disk is a quest item used in The Fremennik Trials quest. It is found during Peer the Seer's part of the quest while searching upstairs in his house. It is found by studying the mounted unicorn head. The disk is used on an abstract mural downstairs in his house in order to obtain a vase lid needed to complete Peer's challenge.
9948:
The Hunter cape is the Cape of Accomplishment for the Hunter skill and can be purchased for 99,000 coins alongside the Hunter hood from the Hunting expert located in the Feldip Hills, by players who have achieved level 99.

Like all skill capes, the Hunter cape gives +9 to all defensive stats, and also a +4 bonus to prayer if it is trimmed, which requires a separate skill at level 99. The cape is automatically trimmed if this condition is met.

The cape provides five teleports per day which can be used to travel to the carnivorous chinchompas in the Feldip Hunter area or the black chinchompas in the Wilderness Hunter area. A third teleport to the Hunter Guild can be unlocked by bringing a cape, worn or in the inventory, to Guildmaster Apatura at the guild. Unlike the previous teleports, the guild teleport has no limit on the number of daily teleports.

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room, as part of the Hunter cape set, along with the hood. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

This item can also be stored in the Huntsman's kit.

As of 1 August 2026, there are 152,479 players that have achieved level 99 in Hunter.

9980:
Roast bird meat are a type of food that can be obtained by cooking skewered bird meat on a fire, requiring level 11 Cooking and granting 62.5 experience when successful. Cooking the skewered bird meat also requires level 20 Firemaking, though it does not give any Firemaking experience.

Players may burn the meat while cooking one, resulting in burnt bird meat; the burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 99.

When eaten, roast bird meat heals 6 hitpoints.
9988:
Roast beast meat are a type of food that can be obtained by cooking a skewered beast on a fire, requiring level 21 Cooking and granting 82.5 experience when successful. Players may burn the meat while cooking one, resulting in burnt beast meat; the burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 99.

When eaten, roast beast meat heals 8 hitpoints.
10008:
A box trap is a type of trap used in the Hunter skill to catch ferrets, embertailed jerboas and chinchompas. Using a box trap requires the specific Hunter level needed for the prey, as well as partial completion of the Eagles' Peak quest.

Whenever prey passes a trap, it has a chance of either being caught in the trap or evading it. If the prey is successfully caught, the box trap will close in around the animal and start shaking, at which point the player will have the option to "check" the trap for loot and experience. If the prey evades the trap, the trap will simply close, at which point the player will have to reset it.

Box traps may be bought from Aleck's Hunter Emporium in Yanille, the Nardah Hunter Shop in Nardah, or Imia's Supplies in the Hunter Guild. One can also be obtained for free by searching the crate adjacent to the bookcases in the north-western house at Land's End. They can also be obtained from Hunter kits.
10010:
A butterfly net is an item used in the Hunter skill. It is wielded to capture implings, and butterflies or moths throughout Gielinor and Puro-Puro, and bats in the Chambers of Xeric. Catching an impling without an impling jar will automatically loot it, and catching a butterfly or moth without a butterfly jar will automatically release it. A jar is required to keep them for later use.

The magic butterfly net is an upgraded butterfly net that requires 17 Hunter to obtain, and increases the player's chances of capturing butterflies, implings, and bats by about 7.8%.

Butterfly nets and jars may be bought from Aleck's Hunter Emporium. in Yanille, the Nardah Hunter Shop in Nardah, or Imia's Supplies in the Hunter Guild. Alternatively, they can also be obtained from a hunter kit, which is obtained by casting the Hunter Kit spell on the Lunar spellbook, requiring a Magic level of 71. A butterfly net can also be obtained for free from a crate in the north-east corner of Lan the Butcher's house at Land's End.

Elnock Inquisitor located inside Puro-Puro will give you a starter set consisting of 1 butterfly net, 7 impling jars, and an impling scroll.

Players can right-click this net to open the Impling Tracker, which tracks how many implings they've caught both in Puro-Puro and the surface world.
10012: A butterfly jar is used to contain captured butterflies or moths with the Hunter skill. These jars can also be turned into impling jars by treating them with imp repellent. Butterfly jars cannot be used to hold implings. They can be created by using one charge of a jar generator or bought in four different Hunter shops in Gielinor (in Yanille, Nardah, the Hunter Guild, and The Great Conch).
10020:
A ruby harvest is a members-only item that is made by catching a ruby harvest with a butterfly jar in the inventory. This requires level 15 Hunter with a butterfly net or a magic butterfly net or level 25 Hunter without, and gives 24 experience. These butterflies can be found near the Piscatoris Hunter area (fairy ring code AKQ).

Once caught, they can be released to boost the player's Attack level by 4 + 15% of their Attack level (rounded down). In a multi-combat zone, the item may be used on another player to share the effect with them and up to three players within a 5x5 area of the target. Players must have Accept Aid toggled on to receive the boost. The empty butterfly jar will remain in the inventory after use.

With a pestle and mortar, players can combine the moth with raw hunter meat to create ruby harvest mix (2).
10023:
The Falconer's glove is used in the Hunter skill in the falconry hunting technique in the Piscatoris falconry area, which is located east of the Piscatoris Hunter Area. While wearing the glove, a player has a gyr falcon on their hand which they can send to catch spotted kebbits, dark kebbits and dashing kebbits. While wearing the glove, players cannot wear any other gloves, bracelets, weapons or shields.

A player can temporarily borrow the glove and falcon from Matthias for a fee of 500 coins, and it will be taken away from the player when they leave the fenced area. The fee must be paid every time the player returns to the area later to hunt more kebbits. Alternatively, players may pay a one-time fee of 500,000 coins for unlimited free glove rentals in the future. Players don't need to worry about logging out with the glove on, it will remain with them when they log back in.

When attempting to leave the area with the glove equipped, the player will state "I should return the glove I borrowed from the falconer before leaving.". Attempting to remove the glove yourself, will give the message You should speak to Matthias to get this removed safely.. Teleporting bypasses this restriction with the text As you leave, Matthias' falcon flies back to him.

10027:
An imp-in-a-box is made by catching an imp with a magic box. It can be used to send items from anywhere to the bank.

It is used by right-clicking on it and choosing "Bank Imp-in-a-box"; then, a window will come up where the items to be sent to the bank can be selected (be careful to not click twice quickly, because items can move after clicking on the first one). Alternatively, simply use an item on the box for it to be sent to your bank. This method is a quick way for players with higher Hunter levels (71 required to catch imps) to quickly bank items. The imp will agree to take two items or stacks from the player to the bank in exchange for its freedom; however, it will refuse to do so in the following areas or scenarios:

In PvP areas (e.g. PvP worlds, the Wilderness) whilst in combat

Above level 30 Wilderness, even when not in combat

While under the effect of Tele Block

Chambers of Xeric

Theatre of Blood

The imp will also refuse to bank a player's looting bag, even outside of the Wilderness. If it is not one of the protected items, the imp-in-a-box is converted to a magic box upon death in the Wilderness.

Imps-in-boxes can be stored in the huntsman's kit. Having an imp-in-a-box in your inventory prevents you from entering the Puro-Puro mini-game.

Note that while the box can be used to send two items to the bank, it will be labelled Imp-in-a-box(2); when one has already been used, it will be labelled Imp-in-a-box(1) and when both have been used, it will revert to magic box.

A Teasing stick is used in Hunter to catch Spined larupia, Horned graahk, Sabre-toothed kyatt, sunlight antelope, and moonlight antelope. While carrying the teasing stick, players are able to "tease" these animals. This makes them aggressive toward the player, allowing players to lure them into a Pitfall trap.

Players with low combat levels should be wary of damage taken from the animals.

The teasing stick can first be used at level 31 Hunter to catch spined larupia, but there is no hunter requirement for having one. It can be purchased from Aleck's Hunter Emporium. in Yanille, Nardah Hunter Shop in Nardah, or Imia's Supplies in the Hunter Guild.

A teasing stick is one of several items that can be obtained from a Hunter kit, which is created by casting the Lunar spell Hunter Kit (spell).

A teasing stick also spawns on the west coast of Karamja, near the horned graahk area.

A Hunter's spear also functions as a teasing stick and can be equipped to save an inventory space.
10033:
Chinchompas are one-handed, multi-target, stackable Ranged weapons requiring level 45 Ranged to wield. Chinchompas can be obtained by box trapping grey chinchompas in the Piscatoris Hunter area, the Kourend Woodland, or on the Isle of Souls. This requires 53 Hunter and completion of the Eagles' Peak quest, and will give the player 198.4 Hunter experience per catch. They have a catch rate of about 146/255 at 53 Hunter and a guaranteed chance to catch at 95 Hunter. To use chinchompas in combat, they must be wielded in the weapons slot. Chinchompas are thrown like darts or throwing knives; however, they explode on impact. In PvM, they can hit up to 11 targets in a 3x3 area. In PvP, the cap is 9 targets. They cannot be picked up again from the ground after being thrown, and Ava's device does not return them.

When throwing a chinchompa at a group, the accuracy roll is based on the targeted NPC. If you miss on this target, you will miss on all targets. If you hit on this target, you will hit on all targets. The damage rolls are done independently per target. The max hit for the targeted NPC is calculated normally, however the max hit used for the damage roll on the additional targets is the max hit for the initial target with the boosts from Salve and Avarice removed. The accuracy roll made on the initial target uses the 'heavy' ranged defence for determining the opponent's defence roll.

Fuses are used to describe the attack speed for throwing chinchompas. It is just another name for the conventional styles of ranged training.

Short fuse (accurate): 4 ticks

Medium fuse (rapid): 3 ticks

Long fuse (longrange): 4 ticks
10034:
Red chinchompas are one-handed multi-target stackable Ranged weapons requiring level 55 Ranged to wield. Red chinchompas can be obtained by box trapping carnivorous chinchompas, requiring 63 Hunter and completion of the Eagles' Peak quest.

To use chinchompas in combat, they must be wielded in the weapons slot. Red chinchompas are thrown like darts or throwing knives; however, they explode on impact. In PvM, they can hit up to 11 targets in a 3x3 area. In PvP, the cap is 9 targets. They cannot be picked up again from the ground after being thrown and Ava's device does not return them. In multiple target attacks, the chinchompa simply rolls at the target's defence values; if it hits, then all other nearby targets are also hit, regardless of their Defence level and ranged defence bonuses. If it misses, then none of the targets take damage. The accuracy roll made on the initial target uses the 'heavy' ranged defence for determining the opponent's defence roll.

Using red chinchompas is widely regarded as the second fastest way to train Ranged and Hitpoints; however, this method is very costly. Catching red chinchompas is also popular among high-level Hunters as it gives fast experience and is profitable.

Fuses are used to describe the attack speed for throwing chinchompas. It is just another name for the conventional styles of ranged training.

Short fuse (accurate): 4 ticks

Medium fuse (rapid): 3 ticks

Long fuse (longrange): 4 ticks
