This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Camouflage gear: Jungle set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
10061:
The desert camo top is a members only piece of Desert camouflage gear that requires 10 Hunter to wear. To make one, bring two desert devil furs and 20 coins to the Fancy Clothes Store in Varrock, to Pellem in the Hunter Guild, or to Prifddinas' Seamstress.

When worn, it reduces weight by 3 kg. Additionally, though the examine claims so, it does not affect the trapping of hunter creatures.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Camouflage gear: Desert set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
10063:
Desert camo legs are a members only piece of the Desert camouflage gear that requires 10 Hunter to wear. To make a pair, bring two desert devil furs and 20 coins to the Fancy Clothes Store in Varrock, to Pellem in the Hunter Guild, or to Prifddinas' Seamstress.

When worn, it reduces weight by 2 kg. Additionally, though the examine claims so, it does not affect the trapping of hunter creatures.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Camouflage gear: Desert set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
10065:
The polar camo top is a members only piece of the polar camouflage gear. To make one, bring two polar kebbit furs and 20 coins to the Fancy Clothes Store in Varrock, to Pellem in the Hunter Guild, or to Prifddinas' Seamstress.

When worn, it reduces weight by 3 kg. Additionally, though the examine claims so, it does not affect the trapping of hunter creatures.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Camouflage gear: Polar set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
10067:
Polar camo legs are a members-only piece of Polar camouflage gear. To make a pair, a player will need to bring two polar kebbit fur and 20 coins to the Fancy Clothes Store in Varrock, to Pellem in the Hunter Guild, or to Prifddinas' Seamstress.

When worn, it reduces weight by 2 kg. Additionally, though the examine claims so, it does not affect the trapping of hunter creatures.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Camouflage gear: Polar set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
10069:
A spotted cape is a weight-reducing item requiring 40 Hunter to be equipped, reducing weight by 2.267 kg. To make it, two spotted kebbit furs and 400 coins must be brought to the Fancy Clothes Store in south-east Varrock, to Pellem in the Hunter Guild, or to Prifddinas' Seamstress.

Catching spotted kebbits at the Piscatoris falconry area requires 43 Hunter.

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room.
10071:
A spottier cape is a weight-reducing item requiring 66 Hunter to be equipped (unboostable), reducing weight by 4.535 kg. While this item provides a greater weight-reduction than the graceful cape, it does not boost the player's run energy restoration rate.

To make it, two dashing kebbit furs and 800 coins must be brought to the Fancy Clothes Store in south-eastern Varrock; doing so and then equipping the cape is a hard Varrock Diary task. Alternatively bring two dashing kebbit furs and 800 coins to Pellem in the Hunter Guild or to Prifddinas' Seamstress.

Catching dashing kebbits at the Piscatoris falconry area requires 69 Hunter.

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room.
10073:
A spotted cape is a weight-reducing item requiring 40 Hunter to be equipped, reducing weight by 2.267 kg. To make it, two spotted kebbit furs and 400 coins must be brought to the Fancy Clothes Store in south-east Varrock, to Pellem in the Hunter Guild, or to Prifddinas' Seamstress.

Catching spotted kebbits at the Piscatoris falconry area requires 43 Hunter.

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room.
10074:
A spottier cape is a weight-reducing item requiring 66 Hunter to be equipped (unboostable), reducing weight by 4.535 kg. While this item provides a greater weight-reduction than the graceful cape, it does not boost the player's run energy restoration rate.

To make it, two dashing kebbit furs and 800 coins must be brought to the Fancy Clothes Store in south-eastern Varrock; doing so and then equipping the cape is a hard Varrock Diary task. Alternatively bring two dashing kebbit furs and 800 coins to Pellem in the Hunter Guild or to Prifddinas' Seamstress.

Catching dashing kebbits at the Piscatoris falconry area requires 69 Hunter.

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room.
10075:
Gloves of silence are a pair of thieving gloves requiring 54 Hunter to wear. When worn, the gloves increase your success chance while pickpocketing by 5%, eventually breaking after 62 failed pickpockets.

To make the gloves, players must bring two unnoted Dark kebbit furs from the Piscatoris falconry area (level 57 Hunter) and 600 coins to the Fancy Clothes Store in Varrock, to Pellem in the Hunter Guild, or to Prifddinas' Seamstress. Before they break, the gloves can be repaired by using one dark kebbit fur on them, while having one spool of thread, a knife, and a needle in your inventory; repairing them requires level 64 Crafting but does not grant any experience.

After completing the medium Ardougne diaries, the gloves become ineffective when used in Ardougne and will not degrade, as the 10% increased chance of success the diary provides is higher than that of the gloves and both bonuses do not stack. Upon completion of the hard Ardougne diaries, this extends to the rest of Gielinor and the gloves become completely obsolete. This effect does not require an Ardougne cloak of any tier to be worn.

Players with access to rogue equipment (minimum of 50 Agility and 50 Thieving to obtain) may choose to forgo using the gloves of silence, as wearing the full rogue set guarantees double rewards for pickpocketing. If wearing the gloves instead of the Rogue gloves with the rest of the rogue set, you instead have a 60% chance to double pickpocketing loot (since you lose both the 15% chance from the gloves and the 25% full set bonus), and therefore receive ~20% less loot, while gaining more XP per hour due to less failures. Due to stun timers on failed pickpocketing being longer than the action of pickpocketing itself, the 5% increased success rate results in 7-25% increased XP rates from pickpocketing, depending on base pickpocketing chance.
10077:
Spiky vambraces are leather armour worn on the forearms, most commonly by low-level warriors, and often rangers (as there is no magic penalty), in place of leather vambraces. They have the same stats as leather vambraces, except for a +2 Strength bonus. To make spiky vambraces, use kebbit claws on leather vambraces. This grants 6 Crafting experience. Level 32 Crafting is required to make any vambraces into spiked vambraces.

Like the leather vambraces they are created from, this variant also has no skill requirements to be worn.
10083:
Red spiky vambraces are red dragonhide vambraces with kebbit claws attached, which requires 32 Crafting to do and grants 5.8 Crafting experience. Kebbit claws can be gained using the Hunter skill. Red spiked vambraces can also be obtained by looting an eclectic impling that has been caught. The difference in stats between spiked and non-spiked vambraces is a bonus to strength of +2 and a slight increase in physical defence for the spiked ones.

Like the red dragonhide vambraces they are created from, this variant also requires 60 Ranged to be worn.
10087:
A stripy feather is a drop from the tropical wagtail bird caught using the Hunter skill. Level 19 Hunter and at least one bird snare are needed to catch these birds in the Feldip Hunter area. These feathers may be used with a fly fishing rod to catch rainbow fish, with 38 Fishing, in rivers of Gielinor, and in place of regular feathers in Fletching. It can be stored in a tackle box.

They can be sold to the Fancy Dress Shop for 8 coins each.
10089:
A blue feather is a drop from the Cerulean twitch bird caught using the Hunter skill. Level 11 Hunter and at least one bird snare are needed to catch these birds in the Rellekka Hunter area.

Blue feathers, along with all coloured feathers gathered from the Hunter skill, can be used in place of regular white feathers with the Fletching skill. Despite the difference, the arrows still come out with white feathers and are used as normal arrows. They can be sold to the Varrock Fancy Clothes Store for 6 coins each. They cannot be used for fly fishing.
10091:
Orange feathers are a drop from the Copper longtail bird caught using the Hunter skill. Level 9 Hunter and at least one bird snare are needed to catch these birds in the Piscatoris Hunter area.

Orange feathers, along with all coloured feathers gathered from the Hunter skill, can be used in place of regular white feathers with the Fletching skill. Despite the difference, bolts and arrows created still come out with white feathers and have no extra properties. These feathers cannot be used for fly fishing. They are colourful and can be sold at the Varrock Fancy Dress Shop.
10092:
A ferret is an item used with a rabbit snare in order to hunt white rabbits in the Piscatoris Hunter area. Players can obtain a ferret by catching a wild ferret using a box trap slightly south-west of the southern rabbit holes. Once caught, the player can use a ferret to flush out a white rabbit from its hole and towards a waiting rabbit snare. A ferret is caught during the quest Eagles' Peak to be given to Charlie.

There is a small chance of a ferret escaping from the player once caught, forcing the player to catch another one to continue hunting rabbits. The chance to keep the ferret scales with Hunter level, ranging from around an 80.9% chance at level 27, up to a 100% chance at level 99.
10093:
Tatty larupia fur is obtained when trapping a spined larupia, found in the Feldip Hunter area. This fur, along with 200 coins, can be turned into either the larupia top and larupia legs by one of the Custom Fur Clothing vendors. It cannot be made into a larupia hat, which requires normal larupia fur. Level 28 Hunter is required to wear the larupia hunter gear set.

Tatty larupia fur, like all tatty furs, cannot be stored in a fur pouch or used during Golem crafting.
10095:
Larupia fur is a common item obtained by hunting Spined larupias (requires Level 31 Hunter) in the Feldip Hunter area. It can be used to create all pieces of larupia hunter gear. Only the full larupia fur may be used to make the headgear of larupia hunter gear. It can be used to dress golems in the golem crafting activity.

Although it can be used for any piece of larupia hunter gear, tatty larupia fur also works for the body and legs but drops more often and is far less expensive. As a result, players often only use the full fur for headdresses.
10097:
Tatty graahk fur is obtained when trapping a horned graahk, found in the Karamja Hunter area. This fur, along with 200 coins, can be turned into either a graahk top or graahk legs by one of the Custom Fur Clothing vendors. It cannot be used to make the graahk headdress, which requires normal graahk fur. Level 38 Hunter is required to wear the graahk hunter gear set.

Tatty graahk fur, like all tatty furs, cannot be stored in a fur pouch or used during Golem crafting.
10099:
Graahk fur can be obtained by trapping Horned graahks on Karamja. The fur comes in two variants; perfect and tatty. Both variants can be taken to the Fancy Dress Shop in Varrock, to Pellem in the Hunter Guild, or Prifddinas' Seamstress in Prifddinas to be made into various articles of clothing. The tatty fur can only be made into Graahk tops and Graahk legs, and the perfect fur is used for the Graahk headdress. It can be used to dress golems in the golem crafting activity.

Furs can also be sold to merchants in East Ardougne and Rellekka.

The ratio of getting graahk fur to tatty graahk fur is based on one's Hunter level.
10101:
Tatty kyatt fur is obtained when trapping a sabre-toothed kyatt, found in the Rellekka Hunter area. This fur, along with 200 coins, can be turned into either a kyatt top or kyatt legs by one of the Custom Fur Clothing vendors. It cannot be used to make the hat, which requires normal kyatt fur. Level 52 Hunter is required to wear the kyatt hunter gear set.

Tatty kyatt fur, like all tatty furs, cannot be stored in a fur pouch or used during Golem crafting.
10103: Kyatt fur is sometimes obtained by pit trapping a Sabre-toothed kyatt in the polar/snow hunting region, although Tatty kyatt fur is more often obtained. Level 55 Hunter is required. The fur can be taken to the Fancy Clothes Store owner in Varrock, who will turn it into a hat, top, or legs for some coins. Wearing the set of kyatt camouflage does not increase the player's hunting abilities, however when wearing the full set you receive 60% less damage from hunter creatures. Level 52 Hunter is required to wear the set. It can be used to dress golems in the golem crafting activity.
10107:
Long kebbit spikes are loot obtained from tracking Razor-backed kebbits, which requires a Hunter level of 49. With a Fletching level of 42, a chisel can be used on a spike to create 12 Long kebbit bolts. Long kebbit bolts can only be fired from a hunters' crossbow.

Players can also bring a long kebbit spike and 40 coins to Leon, located inside Aleck's Hunter Emporium in Yanille, who will exchange it for 12 long kebbit bolts.
10115:
Dark kebbit fur is a type of fur obtained from dark kebbits, which are caught using the Hunter skill. Dark kebbits can be hunted with level 57 Hunter in the Piscatoris falconry area after renting a falcon from Matthias for 500 coins.

Two dark kebbit furs can be taken to the Fancy Clothes Store in Varrock or Pellem at the Hunter Guild, where the shop owner will charge 600 coins to turn the furs into a pair of gloves of silence, or used along with a needle and thread to repair an existing pair of the gloves, requiring 64 Crafting. The gloves require level 54 Hunter to wear, and lower the wearer's chance of getting caught while pickpocketing by 5%, however this is rendered obsolete after completing and claiming the rewards from the hard Ardougne Diary, or when using Rogue equipment to thieve. It can be used to dress golems in the golem crafting activity.
10117: Polar kebbit fur is an item obtained after successfully tracking a polar kebbit and catching it with a noose wand. Polar kebbit fur may be used to make polar camouflage gear by taking two furs and 20 coins per piece to the Fancy Dress Store in south-east Varrock. However, it cannot be used with needles and thread. It can be used to dress golems in the golem crafting activity.
10119:
Feldip weasel fur is dropped by feldip weasels, which are found south of the Feldip Hills. Players require a Hunter level of 7 in order to capture these creatures. The fur may be made into jungle camouflage gear at Tailor's Fancy Clothes Store in south-eastern Varrock. It takes 2 of these furs and 20 coins in order to make one part of the two piece outfit. A total of 4 pieces of fur and 40 coins will make the full set.

Hunter camouflage gear is mostly cosmetic and does not increase catch rates. However, it is weight-reducing clothing. It can be used to dress golems in the golem crafting activity.
10123: Desert devil fur is the fur from a dead Desert Devil used to make Desert camouflage gear. This outfit does not decrease your chances of being seen by animals while hunting. It can be used to dress golems in the golem crafting activity.
10125:
Spotted kebbit fur is a type of fur obtained from spotted kebbits, which are caught using the Hunter skill. Spotted kebbits can be hunted with level 43 Hunter in the Piscatoris falconry area after renting a falcon from Matthias for 500 coins.

Two spotted kebbit furs can be taken to the Fancy Clothes Store in Varrock or Pellem at the Hunter Guild, where the shop owner will charge 400 coins to turn the furs into a spotted cape. The cape requires level 40 Hunter to wear, reduces the wearer's weight by 2.267 kg. It can be used to dress golems in the golem crafting activity.
10127:
Dashing kebbit fur is a type of fur obtained from dashing kebbits, which are caught using the Hunter skill. Dashing kebbits can be hunted with level 69 Hunter in the Piscatoris falconry area after renting a falcon from Matthias for 500 coins.

Two dashing kebbit furs can be brought to the Fancy Clothes Store in Varrock or Pellem at the Hunter Guild, where the shop owner will charge 800 coins to turn the furs into a spottier cape; doing so is a task for the hard Varrock Diary. The cape requires level 66 Hunter to wear, and reduces the wearer's weight by 4.5 kg.

It can be used to dress golems in the golem crafting activity.
10132:
A strung rabbit foot is made by using a ball of wool with a rabbit foot, which requires level 37 Crafting and gives 4 experience; players must have level 24 Hunter to wear the strung rabbit foot. Rabbit feet can be obtained by snaring rabbits. Players must have completed the Eagles' Peak quest to be able to snare rabbits.

If worn whilst woodcutting, bird nest drops are slightly less likely to contain seeds, and slightly more likely to contain bird's eggs or rings (changing the rate from 3/100 to 3/95). If worn whilst looting bird houses, bird nest drops are slightly less likely to be empty nests, and slightly more likely to contain eggs or rings. In practice, wearing the strung rabbit foot lowers the average coin value of a bird nest, so it is only recommended to wear it if actively hunting for egg nests.

For activities that can directly award empty nests, e.g. bird house trapping, up to 10 nest rolls are performed with a chance of getting an empty nest. For successful rolls, the chance is 65/100 for an empty nest. Wearing a strung rabbit foot removes 5 empty nest slots, making the chance 60/95, and improving the chance of getting ring or egg nests instead.

The benefits of wearing a strung rabbit foot stack with the effect of wearing a pair of twitcher's gloves.

Since redwood trees and sulliusceps only drop clue nests, wearing the strung rabbit foot has no effect when chopping these trees.
10134:
A rabbit foot is received through the hunter skill by snaring a rabbit. It can be made into a strung rabbit foot at level 37 Crafting by using a ball of wool on it.

When worn, the rabbit foot increases the chance that nests received from cutting trees or emptying birdhouses will contain a bird's egg, from the usual chance of 3/100 to 3/95.
10136: Rainbow fish is a type of fish that restores 11 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking raw rainbow fish on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 35 Cooking and granting 110 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt rainbow fish. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 63.
10138:
A raw rainbow fish can be caught by players with 38 Fishing. They are caught with a fly fishing rod at a river fishing spot (such as the one near Barbarian Village or in Shilo Village), using stripy feathers (obtained via the Hunter skill) as bait. Each one caught grants 80 Fishing experience.

Raw rainbow fish can be used in the Hunter skill as optional bait for barb-tailed kebbits in the Feldip Hunter area. Catching a barb-tailed kebbit requires level 33 Hunter and yields 168 Hunter experience.

Players can also cook it on a range or a fire to make a cooked rainbow fish, which heals 11 Hitpoints when eaten. Doing so requires 35 Cooking and grants 110 Cooking experience. With 63 Cooking or higher it is impossible to burn the fish.

Although they reward more Fishing experience when caught than salmon or trout, they are much slower to catch and as such are not recommended to be caught purely for experience.
10140:
Burnt rainbow fish is the result of accidentally burning a raw rainbow fish while attempting to make a rainbow fish. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 64.

The burnt rainbow fish has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.
10142:
Guam tar is an item used as food, or "ammunition", for swamp lizards when used as a weapon. It is also optionally used as bait for hunting swamp lizards to increase the catch rate by 3%.

Guam tar can be made at level 19 Herblore by using 15 swamp tar on a guam leaf or ground guam, whilst having a pestle and mortar in the inventory. This process yields 15 guam tar, and grants 30 Herblore experience.
10143:
Marrentill tar is an item used as food, or "ammunition", for orange salamanders when used as a weapon. It is also optionally used as bait for hunting orange salamanders to increase the catch rate by 3%.

Marrentill tar can be made at level 31 Herblore by using 15 swamp tar on a marrentill, whilst having a pestle and mortar in the inventory. This process yields 15 marrentill tar, and grants 42.5 Herblore experience.
10144:
Tarromin tar is an item used as food, or "ammunition", for red salamanders when used as a weapon. It is also optionally used as bait for hunting red salamanders to increase the catch rate by 3%.

Tarromin tar can be made at level 39 Herblore by using 15 swamp tar on a tarromin, whilst having a pestle and mortar in the inventory. This process yields 15 tarromin tar, and grants 55 Herblore experience.
10145:
Harralander tar is an item used as food, or "ammunition", for black salamanders when used as a weapon. It is also optionally used as bait for hunting black salamanders to increase the catch rate by 3%.

Harralander tar can be made at level 44 Herblore by using 15 swamp tar on a harralander, whilst having a pestle and mortar in the inventory. This process yields 15 harralander tar, and grants 72.5 Herblore experience.
10146:
The orange salamander is the fourth strongest salamander weapon. Once the Hunter creature is caught using the Hunter skill, they become weapons. The orange salamander requires level 50 Ranged, 50 Attack, and 50 Magic to wield and is a two-handed weapon. Marrentill tar is used as ammunition for the salamander.

Despite being able to perform Magic and Ranged attacks, this weapon requires the user to be in the opponent's melee distance to attack, potentially reducing the practicality of the two attack styles. However, it can be used to attack enemies from behind fences, and can also attack enemies in diagonal squares, meaning that safespotting is still possible.

They require 47 Hunter to catch, and give 224 Hunter experience when caught. A small fishing net and a rope is used to set up the traps that catch salamanders. They can be caught in the Uzer hunter area, the Necropolis hunter area, and the Great Conch's Abalone Cliffs.

When using the Scorch (Slash) and Blaze (Magic) attack styles, the attack speed is 5. When using the Flare (Range) attack style, the attack speed is 4, which is similar in concept to the Rapid style of most ranged weapons, and it will use standard ranged defence, similar to bows.

Warning: This is a live creature; if unprotected it will run away when you die. Should this happen, you will need to buy or catch a new one.
10148:
The black salamander is the second strongest salamander that can be caught using the Hunter skill at level 67 Hunter, giving 319 experience per catch. They can be found north-east of the Chaos Temple.

It is a two-handed weapon that requires level 70 Attack, Magic, and Ranged to wield, and can be used to train Strength, Magic, and Ranged. Harralander tar is used as ammunition for the salamander.

Despite being able to perform Magic and Ranged attacks, this weapon requires the user to be in the opponent's melee distance to attack, potentially reducing the practicality of the two attack styles. However, it can be used to attack enemies from behind fences, and can also attack enemies in diagonal squares, meaning that safespotting is still possible.

When using the Scorch (Slash) and Blaze (Magic) attack styles, the attack speed is 5. When using the Flare (Range) attack style, the attack speed is 4, which is similar in concept to the Rapid style of most ranged weapons, and it will use standard ranged defence, similar to bows.

Warning: This is a live creature; if unprotected it will run away when you die. Should this happen, you will need to buy or catch a new one.
10149:
The swamp lizard is a two-handed Ranged weapon requiring level 30 in Attack, Ranged, and Magic to wield. The required ammunition for the swamp lizard is Guam tar.

Despite being able to perform Magic and Ranged attacks, this weapon requires the user to be in the opponent's melee distance to attack, potentially reducing the practicality of the two attack styles. However, it can be used to attack enemies from behind fences, and can also attack enemies in diagonal squares, meaning that safespotting is still possible.

Swamp lizards may be obtained by trapping swamp lizards east of Canifis using net traps, requiring level 29 Hunter, or by trading with other players. Successfully catching a Swamp Lizard grants 152 Hunter experience.

When using the Scorch (Slash) and Blaze (Magic) attack styles, the attack speed is 5. When using the Flare (Range) attack style, the attack speed is 4, which is similar in concept to the Rapid style of most ranged weapons, and it will use standard ranged defence, similar to bows.

In its melee mode, the swamp lizard has a chance of inflicting poison starting at 6 damage.

Warning: This is a live creature; if unprotected it will run away when you die. Should this happen, you will need to buy or catch a new one.
10156:
The hunters' crossbow is a crossbow that requires 50 Ranged to wield. It possesses a firing speed of 3 ticks on rapid, equivalent to that of a shortbow. It can only use kebbit bolts and long kebbit bolts as ammunition. Players with at least 74 Fletching can upgrade the hunters' crossbow into the hunters' sunlight crossbow by using a sunlight antelope antler on it while having a chisel in their inventory.

The hunters' crossbow can be bought from Leon for 1,300 coins at the Leon's Prototype Crossbow shop in Yanille. It cannot be crafted by players.

Like the Armadyl crossbow, it has an attack range of 8 tiles. Longrange increases the attack range by 2.
10159: Long kebbit-tipped hunting bolts are ranged ammunition for the hunters' crossbow. They are made from long kebbit spikes. Use a chisel on a long kebbit spike to create twelve long kebbit bolts. This requires 42 Fletching and gives 7.9 Fletching experience per long kebbit spike.
10172: A fake beak is an item needed for Eagles' Peak quest along with the eagle cape to make a convincing disguise. It is made by taking Yellow dye and Swamp tar to the Fancy Dress Shop. It is used to prevent players from taking damage from the mother eagle. Additional eagle cape and fake beak combos can be obtained from the fancy-dress shop owner when he is supplied with 5 eagle feathers, 1 swamp tar, yellow dye and 25 coins.
10175:
The golden feather is a quest item used in the Eagles' Peak quest. It is found on a pedestal inside the caves under Eagles' Peak.

The player must use the golden feather along with a bronze feather and silver feather in order to open a locked door that leads deeper into the caves. The feather can also be obtained after the quest and multiple copies can be obtained by banking the duplicates.
10177:
The bronze feather is a quest item used in the Eagles' Peak quest. It is found on a pedestal inside some caves under Eagles' Peak. When a player attempts to take it, a net trap will lift the feather upwards. The player must then operate the winches in order to lower it. It is not possible to obtain it without setting off the trap.

The player must use the bronze feather along with a silver feather and a golden feather in order to open a locked door that leads deeper into the caves. The feather can be reobtained after the quest and multiple copies can be obtained by banking the duplicates.
10186:
Clue scroll (easy) is an emote clue obtained from easy Treasure Trails.

The items can be stored in a STASH rock on the south side of the limestone mine. It requires 27 Construction, a hammer, saw, 2 planks and 10 Nails to build. Building the STASH rewards the player with 150 Construction XP.
10194:
Clue scroll (easy) is an emote clue obtained from easy Treasure Trails.

The items can be stored in a STASH rock on the south-eastern wall of the Al Kharid mine. It requires 27 Construction, a hammer, saw, 2 planks and 10 Nails to build. Building the STASH rewards the player with 150 Construction XP.
10196:
Clue scroll (easy) is an emote clue obtained from easy Treasure Trails.

The items can be stored in a STASH rock south-east of the fountain. It requires 27 Construction, a hammer, saw, 2 planks and 10 Nails to build. Building the STASH rewards the player with 150 Construction XP.
10214:
Clue scroll (easy) is an emote clue obtained from easy Treasure Trails.

The items can be stored in a STASH bush near the south-east corner of the beehive field. It requires 27 Construction, a hammer, saw, 2 planks and 10 Nails to build. Building the STASH rewards the player with 150 Construction XP.
10218:
Clue scroll (easy) is an emote clue obtained from easy Treasure Trails.

The items can be stored in a STASH rock north of the crossroads. It requires 27 Construction, a hammer, saw, 2 planks and 10 Nails to build. Building the STASH rewards the player with 150 Construction XP.
10226:
Clue scroll (easy) is an emote clue obtained from easy Treasure Trails.

The items can be stored in a STASH rock south-west of the crossroads. It requires 27 Construction, a hammer, saw, 2 planks and 10 Nails to build. Building the STASH rewards the player with 150 Construction XP.
10234: Clue scroll (hard) is an emote clue obtained from hard Treasure Trails.
10240: Clue scroll (hard) is an emote clue obtained from hard Treasure Trails.
10242: Clue scroll (hard) is an emote clue obtained from hard Treasure Trails. An amulet of glory (t) cannot be used to complete this step.
10246: Clue scroll (hard) is an emote clue obtained from hard Treasure Trails.
10250:
Clue scroll (hard) is an emote clue obtained from hard Treasure Trails.

The items can be stored in a STASH unit, requiring 55 Construction, 2 teak planks, 10 nails and a hammer and saw to build.
10258: Clue scroll (medium) is an emote clue obtained from medium Treasure Trails.
10260: Clue scroll (medium) is an emote clue obtained from medium Treasure Trails.
10262: Clue scroll (medium) is an emote clue obtained from medium Treasure Trails.
10268: Clue scroll (medium) is an emote clue obtained from medium Treasure Trails.
10270: Clue scroll (medium) is an emote clue obtained from medium Treasure Trails.
10274: Clue scroll (medium) is an emote clue obtained from medium Treasure Trails.
10282:
The yew composite bow is a bow that requires level 40 Ranged to equip. Yew comp bows can be obtained from completing a medium difficulty Treasure Trail. The yew comp bow is essentially an upgraded yew longbow with a one tick faster attack speed and slightly improved accuracy.

This item can be stored in the treasure chest of a costume room, provided that the interface of the corresponding clue tier is opened before attempting to store the item. Alternatively, the item can be used on the opened treasure chest to insert it without viewing the interface.
10284:
The magic comp bow requires level 50 Ranged to wield, and can fire arrows up to amethyst. It is slightly quicker and more accurate than a magic longbow, and features the same special attack. Magic comp bows can be obtained as a reward for completing a hard Treasure Trail. This item can be stored in the treasure chest of a costume room, provided that the interface of the corresponding clue tier is opened before attempting to store the item. Alternatively, the item can be used on the opened treasure chest to insert it without viewing the interface.

Composite bows can be fired from 10 squares away at both rapid and long range styles; this combination of speed and distance is matched only by the crystal bow, scorching bow, and bow of Faerdhinen. Where long attack distance is ideal, a magic comp bow could suffice as a non-degradable alternative to the crystal bow.

White firelighters are a possible reward from Treasure Trails. They create white logs when used with regular logs.

In addition, players can use 250 white firelighters on a Phoenix to recolour it white.
10328:
White logs are created by using logs with a white firelighter, a possible reward from any tier of clue scroll. When burned they create a white fire, yielding 50 Firemaking experience, which is 10 more than regular logs. Additionally, every attempt to make a white fire is successful, unlike with regular fire.

These logs are not logs cut from a white tree.

White logs can be added to the Odd Old Man's pot-boiler, but the resulting fire will be normal and the logs will be lost.

Note: Purple logs can be added to the Odd Old Man's pot-boiler, but the resulting fire will be normal and the logs will be lost.

10354:
The amulet of glory (t) (or trimmed amulet of glory) is a cosmetic variant of the regular amulet of glory. Players can receive this item as a reward from hard Treasure Trails at a chance of 1/1,625 per slot. Aside from appearance, it has the same functions and stat bonuses as a regular amulet of glory (including gem mining as long as it is charged).

This item can be stored in the treasure chest of a costume room, provided that the interface of the corresponding clue tier is opened before attempting to store the item. Alternatively, the item can be used on the opened treasure chest to insert it without viewing the interface. However, unlike its regular counterpart, it cannot be mounted in a Quest Hall.

For Ironmen completing treasure trails, this can NOT be used as an uncharged amulet of glory - only a regular amulet of glory may be used, obtained either through crafting one at level 80, catching a dragon impling at level 83 Hunter, or by completing other treasure trails.

Heroes' Quest is required to charge the amulet at the Fountain of Rune. Like the regular amulet of glory, there is a 1 in 25,000 chance that it will transmute into an amulet of eternal glory when charged at the Fountain of Rune, causing it to provide unlimited teleports rather than the usual six. This will cause it to lose its trimmed status.

Alternatively, the item can be used on the opened treasure chest to insert it without viewing the interface, as part of the Saradomin vestment set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

It should be noted that despite being obtained from a Reward casket (hard), it is stored in the easy rewards section of the treasure chest.

10476:
Purple sweets are a stackable food item that are earned from all levels of Treasure Trails, except beginner. They are the only stackable food item in the game, restoring 1–3 Hitpoints and 10% run energy per sweets eaten.

Due to their high price and low amount healed, they are rarely used as conventional food. Due to being stackable, they are often used for activities with constant tick eating and to restore run energy instead of stamina potions to save inventory space.

When eaten, the message You eat the sweets. The sugary goodness heals some energy. is displayed.
10486:
The Empty sack is an animation item added to the game with Animal Magnetism. It is wielded by Malcolm during a cutscene in which he attempts to catch an Undead chicken for the player.

It may have originally been intended for players to obtain this item first, then give it to Malcolm to use.
10487:
An undead chicken is obtained during the quest Animal Magnetism from Malcolm who lives just west of the Ectofuntus by paying him 10 ectotokens per chicken. It is widely considered a 'fun' weapon, and shares its stats with a range of other such weapons.

This weapon can be bought during or after the quest for 10 Ecto-tokens.

Equipping the weapon causes the chicken to emit a short scream.
10488: Selected iron is a quest item used in the Animal Magnetism quest. The player must give the Witch in Draynor Manor five regular iron bars and she will then return the bar that is most suitable for turning into a bar magnet. The player must then take this bar to the mine near Rimmington and hit the bar with a hammer, making sure to face in the north direction, to turn it into a bar magnet. This will grant the player a token amount of Smithing experience.
10490:
Undead twigs can be obtained by chopping undead trees outside Draynor Manor with a blessed axe during or after the Animal Magnetism quest. They have no use outside of this quest. It may take several attempts before some twigs are acquired, as there is a chance of failing to cut the tree properly.

Ordinary woodcutting axes will not be able to cut the undead tree, as they will "bounce off the bark" of the undead tree.

Each twig procured gives 5 Woodcutting experience.
10491:
The blessed axe is an axe made by Turael by giving him a mithril axe and a holy symbol, which requires completing the Animal Magnetism quest up until the point Ava suggests talking to him. Talking to Turael after this step will then make it. It is used to chop undead twigs from the undead trees within the vicinity of Draynor Manor. Turael will make additional blessed axes if the required materials are brought to him again in Burthorpe.

As the axe possesses a silver blade, it can damage vampyres.

The blessed axe does not retain the functionality of the mithril axe used to create it; it cannot be used to chop anything but undead trees. It does not require an Attack level to wield. The only statistical difference is the blessed axe has a +2 Prayer bonus the mithril axe does not.

Despite being made with a holy symbol, the blessed axe does not count as a Saradomin item for God Wars Dungeon when equipped.
10493: Translated notes are used in the Animal Magnetism quest. They are made by decoding the research notes by doing a puzzle. Ava uses them to make an accumulator or attractor.
10495: A container is an item that players create as part of Animal Magnetism. They make it by combining a pattern with polished buttons and hard leather. They then give it to Ava, who turns it into Ava's attractor. The container is important in finishing the quest and is the structure of the whole attractor.
10496:
Polished buttons are obtained by polishing regular buttons. When polished, one receives 5 Crafting experience.

One may get the buttons by pickpocketing H.A.M. members, digging in the Level-1 or Level-3 digsite east of Varrock, opening Ogre coffins, or by inspecting the Port Khazard trawler net after participating in the Fishing Trawler.

They are used in the Animal Magnetism quest.
10499:
Ava's accumulator is an item awarded to the player by completing the quest Animal Magnetism if the player is level 50 Ranged or above (players below 50 Ranged will instead receive Ava's attractor). It is equipped in the cape slot, can pick up a player's ranged ammunition after they fire it, and every 3.5 minutes, will attract an assortment of metal ammunition. The accumulator gives the fourth best Ranged attack bonus for the cape slot.

Like all of Ava's devices, the accumulator will not work when metal torso armour (Ahrim's top included) is worn, as this will cause 'interference'. A list of metal torso armour that does not interfere with Ava's accumulator can be found here.

Ava (found in Draynor Manor) will upgrade the attractor for anyone who obtains 50 Ranged after the quest for a price of 75 steel arrows, along with either 999 coins or an attractor (If you bring both coins and an attractor, the attractor will be used). It can also be purchased from Perdu after getting level 50 Ranged, even without first obtaining one from Ava. After that, it can be upgraded to Ava's assembler (upon completion of Dragon Slayer II) for Vorkath's head and 75 mithril arrows, as well as 4,999 coins or an Accumulator.

Upon dying, if it is not an item kept on death, it will be stored in the player's grave until reclaimed. If not reclaimed within an hour, it can be reacquired by speaking with Ava and purchased for 999 coins and 75 steel arrows. Multiple devices may be possessed at the same time.

As with Ava's other devices, Ava's accumulator can be used on both Lanthus in the Castle Wars lobby and Nomad in the Soul Wars lobby to permanently activate the effect in the minigames.

The Ava's accumulator can also be combined with the max cape to change its appearance by turning it into the accumulator max cape.

Lastly, the breakdown of the ammo recovery rate is as listed:

Break on impact: 20%

Drop onto floor: 8%

Recovered automatically: 72%
10500:
The crone-made amulet is an altered ghostspeak amulet used in Animal Magnetism.

Players obtain it by talking to the Old Crone with a ghostspeak amulet and at least one empty slot in their inventory. The old crone will use a hair from Alice (which players do not need to obtain - the old crone finds it on their clothes) to create a special copy of the ghostspeak amulet.

Only Malcolm (the farmer north-west of Port Phasmatys) can use it, and even then he can only talk to his wife Alice. The purpose of all this is so Alice could get his bank PIN and receive her inheritance.

Players attempting to equip this amulet on themselves receive the message: "Your ghostliness isn't ethereal enough to wear this. Perhaps you should wait a few hundred years or so?"
10507:
The reindeer hat is an untradeable cosmetic item obtained by completing one of the Christmas holiday events that occur once per year. This also rewards the player with all other holiday items associated with Christmas.

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room.

An emote is performed by using the "prance" option on the hat while it is worn. This spawns a snow pile under the player, which snowballs can be picked from, and melts soon after. It is commonly used in free to play for tick-manipulation.

In snow-restricted areas, the message in the chatbox will instead state This is not an appropriate place to play with your hat!. The hat cannot also be operated while sitting down prompting the message You can't operate the hat while you're sitting down..

Previously, they were obtainable during the 2013 Rare Drops event (from 14 July to 21 July) as part of a rare item drop.
10508:
A wintumber tree is a holiday item that can be planted in a player-owned house. It can be obtained by completing one of the Christmas holiday events that occur once per year. This also rewards the player with all other holiday items associated with Christmas. The tree is untradeable and may be planted on any free non-hotspot space in the Garden or on any free outdoor space of a player-owned house. If lost or destroyed, the player can obtain another from Diango in Draynor Village.

Attempting to plant the tree anywhere besides the garden of your player-owned house prints the message You can only plant the wintumber tree in the garden of your player-owned house. Attempting to dig up a wintumber tree in someone else's house prints the message You can't dig up the owner's wintumber tree! How unfestive!

Previously, they were obtainable during the 2013 Rare Drops event (from 5 August to 12 August) as part of a rare item drop.

10531:
A green egg is used in Barbarian Assault to damage penance monsters. If loaded into the egg launcher and shot at penance creatures, it will deal 1 damage and poison the target. If shot at a Penance Runner, Penance Fighter, or Penance Ranger, the poison will hit every 3 seconds a total of 5 times unless healed. If shot at a Penance Healer, the poison will hit every 18 seconds a total of 5 times. Green egg poison is in addition to poisoned food damage, and will not reset, reduce, or delay damage. A maximum of five green eggs may be loaded into the egg launcher at any given time. Both egg launchers share the same reserve of eggs.

Green eggs tend to be used when no red eggs are available, as they deal less damage and can only damage one enemy at a time.
10533:
Blue eggs are used in Barbarian Assault to stun penance monsters. If loaded into an egg launcher and shot at penance creatures, a blue egg will stun its target for 6 seconds. During this time, the monster will not move, and cannot be targeted with food, weapons or the egg launcher. A maximum of five blue eggs may be loaded into the egg launcher at any given time. Both egg launchers share the same reserve of eggs.

Blue eggs are rarely used in the minigame due to the fact that firing one will render its target temporarily unattackable (and, in the case of healers, unable to be poisoned). However, they can still be useful for slowing down Penance runners from reaching the southern cave entrance should they manage to get past the player(s) who are assigned the Defender role.
10535: A poisoned egg is used in the final wave of Barbarian Assault. It is made by using a yellow egg, which is dropped by the Penance Queen in the 10th wave, on the poison crater. The yellow egg must be received from the collector and dunked in poison craters by the healer. It must then be passed on to the attacker to make a spiked/pois. egg.
10536: A spiked/pois. egg is used in the final wave of Barbarian Assault. It is made by using spikes on a poisoned egg. The poisoned egg must be received from the healer and have spikes added by the attacker. It must then be passed on to the defender to make an omega egg.
10537:
The omega egg is used during the last wave of the Barbarian Assault minigame to defeat the Penance Queen. The omega egg is launched using the egg launcher. This is the only way the queen can be damaged and defeated. Each hit with the omega egg deals 30-39 damage.

The omega egg can only be shot if the wave's runners, fighters, healers, and rangers have been defeated.

10540: Poisoned worms are used in Barbarian Assault to hurt Penance Healers. The healer needs to use the poisoned worms on the penance healer. This will cause 4 damage, and poison the healer for 4 damage. Unlike regular monsters, the Penance Healer ticks poison damage every 3 seconds.

10547:
The healer hat is a possible reward item from Barbarian Assault and requires 45 Defence to wear. Players who have killed the Penance Queen and have 275 Honour points in each of the four roles can purchase the hat from Commander Connad, located on the main floor of the Barbarian Outpost. The hat is part of the penance set, all parts of which are available from Barbarian Assault.

Its stats are very similar to the farseer helm. Both require 45 Defence and offer +6 magic attack bonus with attack penalties of -5 to all other styles. However, the healer hat has a slightly higher (+1) magic defence bonus at the cost of lower melee defence (-2 to stab, slash, and crush).

If the player dies a PvP death and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 45,000 coins.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room.
10548:
The fighter hat is a piece of members-only armour that requires 45 Defence to wear, and is obtained through the Barbarian Assault minigame. Players with 275 honour points in each role and who have killed the Penance Queen can purchase the hat from Commander Connad, located on the ground floor of the Barbarian Outpost.

The fighter hat is sometimes used in place of the warrior helm and berserker helm. The warrior helm provides slightly better defensive bonuses, but offers an attack bonus to slash only, while the fighter hat also provides attack bonuses to stab and crush. In fact, the +5 stab attack bonus makes the fighter hat the best-in-slot item for stab attack. The berserker helm has slightly better defensive bonuses and provides a strength bonus (+3), but provides no melee attack bonuses. The fighter hat is a popular choice among obsidian maulers that are unable to obtain the Inquisitor's great helm.

If the player dies a PvP death and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 45,000 coins.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room.
10550:
A ranger hat is a piece of headgear available as a reward from Barbarian Assault. It resembles the head of a Penance Ranger.

Equipping the hat requires level 45 Defence. Players who have killed the Penance Queen and have 275 honour points in all four roles can purchase a Ranger hat from Commander Connad, who is located on the ground floor of the Barbarian Outpost. In terms of Ranged attack bonus, it has 2 more than a Snakeskin bandana, the same as a Spined helm, and 2 less than a Robin Hood hat.

If the player dies a PvP death and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 45,000 coins.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room.
10551:
The fighter torso (called the Penance torso in the Barbarian Assault Reward Shop) is armour that requires 40 Defence to equip and is a reward from the Barbarian Assault minigame. It can be purchased from Commander Connad for 375 honour points in all four roles, and one Penance Queen kill. It can be sold back to Connad for 300 honour points in all four roles by using it on him.

If the player dies a PvP death at level 20 Wilderness or below and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 150,000 coins.

If the player dies a PvP death above level 20 Wilderness and the item is unprotected, it will be converted to coins. To prevent this, a Trouver parchment and a payment of 500,000 coins can be given to Perdu in order to permanently lock the item. The locked item will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a mangled, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 500,000 coins.

Note: It is possible to obtain at any level, but low level players may struggle specifically with the attacker role.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room.
10553:

Players with 150 honour points in each of the four roles can purchase the gloves by speaking to Commander Connad, located on the main floor of the Barbarian Outpost. Players do not have to kill the Penance Queen to obtain the gloves.

Penance gloves provide 4.535 kg in weight reduction, along with modest defensive bonuses.

These gloves can be taken to Entrana.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room.

Attacker icon is an item worn in the jaw slot, a back-end Worn Equipment slot system where facial hair is placed while playing Barbarian Assault. It shows that the player is an attacker indicated by the red circle around them with the attacker symbol. When a game of Barbarian Assault finishes, the icon is removed.

Having a higher level in the Attacker role, which can be done via Commander Connad or choosing to do so immediately after a game, allows players to deal bonus damage to penance monsters.

It shows that the player is a collector indicated by the yellow circle around them with the collector symbol. When a game of Barbarian Assault finishes, the icon is removed.

Having a higher level in the Collector role, which can be done via Commander Connad or choosing to do so immediately after a game, allows the collection bag to hold more eggs, and an increased chance of success when converting eggs.

Having a higher level in the Defender role, which can be done via Commander Connad or choosing to do so immediately after a game, allows players to have an increased luring range when luring Penance Runners.

Having a higher level in the Healer role, which can be done via Commander Connad or choosing to do so immediately after a game, allows players to heal more hitpoints per healing vial dose.

After the miniquest, players can quickly reclaim the diary from a bookcase in a player-owned house under the name The Diary of Tarn Razorlor.
10589:
Granite helm is a helmet that can be obtained by killing terror dogs or from High Level Gambles at Barbarian Assault. 50 Strength and 50 Defence are required to equip the helm. It has slightly better stats than the rune full helm but slightly worse stats than the dragon med helm.

The granite helm has superior ranged defensive stats compared to rune and dragon (but inferior to the dragon full helm). This also applies to other pieces of granite equipment.
10594:
A clockwork book can be found in the bookcase of a player-owned house. It is given to you by Larry during the Cold War quest.

The book itself contains notes and instructions on making clockwork toys and a note from Larry on how to make the penguin suit. It is needed if you wish to build the penguin suit in Cold War.

If lost, it can be reclaimed from Larry at Ardougne Zoo, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house.
10597:
Mission reports are three different items, all used in the Cold War quest. They are:

Mission report (Ardougne), given to the player by a Penguin in Ardougne Zoo after greeting him.

Mission report (Lumbridge), given to the player by the penguins dressed as a sheep after giving them the secret phrase.

Mission report (Fake), given to the player by Noodle after trading him swamp tar and 5 feathers.
10598:
Mission reports are three different items, all used in the Cold War quest. They are:

Mission report (Ardougne), given to the player by a Penguin in Ardougne Zoo after greeting him.

Mission report (Lumbridge), given to the player by the penguins dressed as a sheep after giving them the secret phrase.

Mission report (Fake), given to the player by Noodle after trading him swamp tar and 5 feathers.
10599:
Mission reports are three different items, all used in the Cold War quest. They are:

Mission report (Ardougne), given to the player by a Penguin in Ardougne Zoo after greeting him.

Mission report (Lumbridge), given to the player by the penguins dressed as a sheep after giving them the secret phrase.

Mission report (Fake), given to the player by Noodle after trading him swamp tar and 5 feathers.
10600:
The KGP ID card is an item used during Cold War. During the quest, it is obtained from Noodle the penguin after giving him five feathers and one lump of swamp tar. The card is used to gain access to the Killer Gentoo Penguins Headquarters on the Iceberg during the quest. Players do not need the card to access the headquarters afterwards.

For collectors, be cautious after the quest's end. Noodle, who trades you this, is no longer present afterward, making this item unobtainable if lost.
10808: Arctic pyre logs may be used during the Shades of Mort'ton minigame to cremate the remains of Loar, Phrin, and Riyl Shades. They require level 47 Firemaking to light and grant 158 Firemaking experience when used to cremate a shade (237 with Morytania Diary 4 complete).
10810:
Arctic pine logs are cut from arctic pine trees, found on the island of Neitiznot and south-west of Rellekka. A Woodcutting level of 54 is required to cut them, giving 40 experience per log; 42 Firemaking is needed to make a fire using these type of logs, granting 125 experience per log. A Woodcutting level of 56 is required to split these logs.

They are also used to make Neitiznot shields, requiring a level of 56 in Woodcutting. Two of these logs, a bronze nail, and a rope are required to make one, granting 34 Crafting experience.

Players can also use the logs on a woodcutting stump to make split logs for the quest The Fremennik Isles.
10814:
Hair is a drop obtained by killing yaks outside the village of Neitiznot. Players can use it on a spinning wheel to make rope using the Crafting skill. Making a rope requires level 30 Crafting and grants 25 Crafting experience.

The players who paid Vanligga Gastfrihet's taxes during or after The Fremennik Isles can buy them from her shop (located north of the longhall in Jatizso) for a price starting at 2 coins each with a stock of 50. She is very close to a bank, so purchasing hair from her is a faster method of obtaining than killing yaks.
10818:
Yak-hides are a 100% drop from yaks. They can be cured for 5 coins by Thakkrad Sigmundson on Neitiznot. Cured yak-hide can be crafted into yak-hide legs and yak-hide bodies with the use of a needle and thread.

After partially completing The Fremennik Isles quest, players can also buy yak-hides from Contraband yak produce in central Jatizso.
10820:
Cured yak-hides are obtained by taking a yak-hide to Thakkrad Sigmundson on Neitiznot and paying him 5 coins to cure it. They can also be bought from the Contraband yak produce store on Jatizso starting at 110 coins each.

Cured yak-hides can be crafted into yak-hide legs and yak-hide bodies with the use of a needle and thread. Yak-hide legs require one cured yak-hide and 43 Crafting, while yak-hide bodies require two cured yak-hides and 46 Crafting. Each item gives 32 Crafting experience upon creation, which is unusual, as usually when crafting with hides the experience granted is based on the amount of hides used.
10822:
The Yak-hide armour is a piece of member's only armour. A Defence level of 20 is required to wear the top. It is part of the Yak-hide armour set, with the other part being the legs.

Yak-hide armour counts as warm clothing for the Wintertodt.
10824:
Yak hide armour are pieces of members only armour. Level 20 Defence is required to wear them. Yak hide legs have a +2 Ranged attack bonus compared to green d'hide chaps. It is part of the Yak-hide armour set, with the other part being the top.

Yak-hide armour counts as warm clothing for the Wintertodt.
10826:
The Neitiznot shield, also commonly called the Fremennik roundshield, is a shield made of wood that requires level 25 Defence to wield. It can be made during and after completion of The Fremennik Isles quest with level 56 Woodcutting on the woodcutting stump near the bank in Neitiznot. This requires two arctic pine logs, a bronze nail, a rope, and a hammer in the inventory. Making the shield grants 34 Crafting experience.

Although this shield can only be created after reaching a certain point in The Fremennik Isles quest, it is not a wielding requirement, and it can be worn by players who have not started the quest.

It has a slightly higher ranged and crush defence compared to the adamant kiteshield, but much lower slash and stab defence. It also lowers ranged attack and magic attack more than the adamant kiteshield. Therefore, it is not commonly used by players with 30 or higher Defence. It is, however, a safe alternative to players who have 25 Defence, as its defensive stats are comparably higher than those of the mithril kiteshield.

This shield also reduces the maximum damage taken from rocks thrown by ice troll females and thrower trolls from 6 to 2, as well as reducing the maximum hit of the Ice Troll King's throwing rock attacks from 7 to 2.
10829:
The Documents are an unobtainable item added to the cache alongside The Fremennik Isles. They have an option to "Open", while their examine states they must be taken to Ali Morrisane in Al Kharid.

The documents' internal name suggest they formed part of a trade agreement, while the Royal decree is referred to as a "receipt", despite not serving this purpose. At the same time, many unused models can be found depicting crates of armour, swords, and battleaxes. It is possible therefore that there was a cut subplot in the quest which involved trading Jatizso products with Ali Morrisane.
10831: The empty tax bag is used during The Fremennik Isles quest for collecting taxes from the shopkeepers and more inhabitants of Jatizso. While collecting taxes, it will become a light tax bag, then a normal tax bag, and finally a hefty tax bag. Tax bags cannot be banked, as "a magical force prevents you from banking this item!"
10832: The light tax bag is used during The Fremennik Isles quest for collecting taxes from the shopkeepers and more inhabitants of Jatizso. It is originally an empty tax bag, then as more taxes are collected it becomes a light tax bag, then a normal tax bag, and finally a hefty tax bag.
10835:
The bulging taxbag is an item that is unobtainable via normal gameplay. During The Fremennik Isles, in the part of the quest where players collect taxes for King Gjuki Sorvott IV, the tax bag becomes bulging when they collect at least 33,000 coins in taxes from the citizens of Jatizso. However, players can only collect a maximum of 29,000 coins in taxes, resulting in a hefty tax bag.

For the tax bag to become bulging, players must perform an exploit:

Destroy the tax bag, and filling the inventory entirely.

Attempt to collect taxes from Vanligga Gastfrihet, and offer to pay her taxes with your own coins. As you have no space in your inventory, a tax bag is placed in your bank containing the taxes you paid for her.

As the flag that tracks whether Vanligga's taxes has been paid or not is not set when paying her taxes in this manner, players can keep paying her taxes until the tax bag in the bank is bulging.
10836:
The silly jester hat is part of the silly jester costume, which is obtained and used during The Fremennik Isles quest. Unique to the silly jester costume, a bell jingle can be heard when the hat is equipped or unequipped.

If lost, a replacement can be obtained by searching the king's chest on Jatizso.
10837:
The silly jester top is part of the silly jester costume, which is obtained and used during The Fremennik Isles quest. Unique to the silly jester costume, a bell jingle can be heard when the top is equipped or unequipped.

If lost, a replacement can be obtained by searching the king's chest on Jatizso.
10838:
Silly jester tights are part of the silly jester costume, which is obtained and used during The Fremennik Isles quest. Unique to the silly jester costume, a bell jingle can be heard when the tights are equipped or unequipped.

If lost, a replacement can be obtained by searching the king's chest on Jatizso.
10839:
The silly jester boots are part of the silly jester costume, which is obtained and used during The Fremennik Isles quest. They offer the third highest Magic defence bonus of any pair of boots, tied with infinity boots, pegasian boots, bloodbark boots, and boots of brimstone, only beaten by the Eternal boots and Avernic treads. Unique to the silly jester costume, a bell jingle can be heard when the boots are equipped or unequipped.

If lost, a replacement can be obtained by searching the king's chest on Jatizso.
10840:
A jester stick is an unobtainable item that is wielded during a cutscene in The Fremennik Isles. During the quest, the player is required to act as the jester for Mawnis Burowgar, in order to eavesdrop on the guards' conversation. When choosing the "Talk to puppet" option, the jester stick appears during the animation.

It can also be seen wielded by Slug Hemligssen.
10841: The apricot cream pie is an unobtainable item that is wielded during a cutscene in The Fremennik Isles. During the quest, the player is required to act as the jester for Mawnis Burowgar, in order to eavesdrop on the guards' conversation. When choosing the "Pie" option, the apricot cream pie appears during the animation.
10842:
The Decapitated head is the severed head of the Ice Troll King, whom players slay as part of The Fremennik Isles.

Players must decapitate the Ice Troll King after killing him - they do not gain the head in their inventory automatically. They should then take the head to Mawnis Burowgar in Neitiznot.

Unusually (even for a quest item), players cannot deposit this item in a bank. If the head is lost prior to completion of the quest, another can be obtained by reentering the Ice Troll Caves. In this scenario, upon entering the caves the player will be returned to the location of the Ice Troll King's corpse without having to pass through the first part of the cave.
10844:
Spring sq'irks are obtained through the Sorceress's Garden minigame. They are picked off of the sq'irk tree in the spring maze, requiring 25 Thieving to enter. Picking a spring sq'irk gives 40 Farming experience, and teleports the player to the fountain in the inner garden.

Players can use a pestle and mortar and an empty beer glass with 4 spring sq'irks to make spring sq'irkjuice. The spring sq'irkjuice gives 1,350 Thieving experience when given to Osman (or Selim after completing Beneath Cursed Sands), or can be consumed to boost Thieving by 1.
10845:
Summer sq'irks are obtained through the Sorceress's Garden minigame. They are picked off of the Sq'irk tree in the Summer maze. Doing so gives 60 Farming experience and teleports the player to the fountain in the inner garden.

With 2 summer sq'irks in your inventory along with a pestle and mortar and an empty beer glass you can make Summer sq'irkjuice.

Summer sq'irkjuice gives 3,000 Thieving experience when given to Osman (or Selim after completing Beneath Cursed Sands).
10846:
Autumn sq'irks are obtained through the Sorceress's Garden minigame. They are picked off of the Sq'irk tree in the Autumn maze. Doing so gives 50 Farming experience and teleports the player to the fountain in the inner garden.

With 3 autumn sq'irks in your inventory along with a pestle and mortar and an empty beer glass, you can make Autumn sq'irkjuice.

Autumn sq'irkjuice gives 2,350 Thieving experience when given to Osman (or Selim after completing Beneath Cursed Sands).
10847:
Winter sq'irks are obtained through the Sorceress's Garden minigame. They are picked off of the Sq'irk tree in the Winter maze. Doing so gives 30 Farming experience and teleports the player to the fountain in the inner garden.

With 5 winter sq'irks in your inventory along with a pestle and mortar and an empty beer glass you can make Winter sq'irkjuice.

Winter sq'irkjuice gives 350 Thieving experience when given to Osman (or Selim after completing Beneath Cursed Sands).
10848:
Spring sq'irkjuice is made from spring sq'irks, found in the Sorceress's Garden minigame. Level 25 Thieving is required to access the spring garden. To make the juice, pick 4 spring sq'irks and use them with a pestle and mortar while having a beer glass in your inventory.

Picking the spring sq'irk gives 40 Farming experience.

Drinking the spring sq'irkjuice will restore 10% of your energy and give you a Thieving bonus of +1.

You can also give the spring sq'irkjuice to Osman (or Selim after completing Beneath Cursed Sands) for 1,350 Thieving experience.

Players wishing to gain fast levels in Thieving need only give Osman 40 glasses of spring sq'irkjuice to go from level 25 to level 45 Thieving. Progressing to the next available sq'irkjuice provides better experience with fewer required sq'irks per drink.
10849:
Summer sq'irkjuice is made from summer sq'irks, found in the Sorceress's Garden minigame. Level 65 Thieving is required to access the summer garden. To make the juice, pick 2 summer sq'irks and use them with a pestle and mortar while having a beer glass in your inventory which can be obtained on the shelves in the Sorceress's house.

Picking the summer sq'irk gives 60 Farming experience.

Drinking the summer sq'irkjuice will restore 20% of your energy and give you a Thieving bonus of +3.

You can also give the summer sq'irkjuice to Osman (or Selim after completing Beneath Cursed Sands) for 3,000 Thieving experience.

Turning in summer sq'irkjuice provides 84,000 Thieving experience per inventory, the highest of all sq'irkjuices.
10850:
Autumn sq'irkjuice is made from autumn sq'irks, found in the Sorceress's Garden minigame. Level 45 Thieving is required to access the autumn garden. To make the juice, pick 3 autumn sq'irks and use them with a pestle and mortar while having a beer glass in your inventory. In the autumn garden, you will also find a herb bush that allows you to pick two herbs at a time.

Picking the autumn sq'irk gives 50 Farming experience.

Drinking the autumn sq'irkjuice will restore 15% of your energy and give you a Thieving bonus of +2

You can also give the autumn sq'irkjuice to Osman (or Selim after completing Beneath Cursed Sands) for 2,350 Thieving experience.
10851:
Winter sq'irkjuice is made from winter sq'irks, found in the Sorceress's Garden minigame. No Thieving level is required to access the winter garden. To make the juice, pick 5 winter sq'irks and use them with a pestle and mortar while having a beer glass in your inventory. In the winter garden, you will also find a herb bush that allows you to pick two herbs at a time.

Picking the winter sq'irk gives 30 Farming experience.

Drinking the winter sq'irkjuice will restore 5% of your energy.

You can also give the juice to Osman (or Selim after completing Beneath Cursed Sands) for 350 Thieving experience.

The winter sq'irkjuice does not provide a temporary boost to Thieving unlike other sq'irkjuice variants, which makes drinking it almost entirely pointless over handing it in for experience.
10856: Sin seer's note is given by Sin Seer in Seers' Village during The General's Shadow miniquest. The note attests to the fact that the player has committed many sins and atrocities in their life, and it is used by the player to gain General Khazard's trust. To obtain the note, Sin Seer needs to be bribed with 40 coins.
10857: A severed leg is an item given by General Khazard during The General's Shadow miniquest. It is used to distract Bouncer after getting him to low health so the player can kill him at the end of the miniquest.
10858:
The shadow sword is a two-handed sword obtained as a reward from The General's Shadow mini-quest. The sword matches the ghostly robes set, though it cannot be stored alongside the robes in the costume room of a player-owned house.

The shadow sword has the same stats as a black 2h sword, with additional Magic attack and defence bonuses.

If lost, the sword can be reclaimed by speaking to the ghost in the room where you fought Bouncer's ghost (accessible through a crack on the south wall of the north-eastern room in the Goblin Cave, just east of the Fishing Guild entrance). A ghostspeak amulet (or Morytania legs 2 or better) must be worn in order to talk to the ghost.

The ghost will not give you a second copy if you already have one in your inventory or bank. The only way to obtain multiple copies at the same time is to first deposit one in the master STASH unit in the south-east corner of Zamorak's Fortress.

Note: Despite being untradeable, the shadow sword will always be lost on death, unless it's one of the three (or four with Protect Item) items protected on death. It will also not appear on the ground, meaning you will have to reclaim it.
10859:
A tea flask is a container item that can store up to 5 cups of plain tea. Tea may be drunk directly from the flask restoring 3 Hitpoints and temporarily boosting Attack by 2 + 2% (rounded down). Upon consuming the tea, the player will exclaim Ahhh, tea is so refreshing.. The tea flask may also be used on an empty cup to fill it. Tea flasks cannot be filled with damiana tea, nettle tea, or tea from a player-owned house.

Tea flasks can be obtained through Creature Creation, a solo activity that involves creating unique hybrid monsters and killing them for their drops. The tea flask may be obtained from any of the hybrid monsters.

Like satchels, they do not stack in the bank even if they have matching contents, and cannot be placed in Group storage.
10863:
Builder's shirt is obtained during the Tower of Life quest. This item is part of the builder's costume.

After completing the quest Tower of Life, the builder's costume is not necessary to enter the Tower of Life and may be destroyed if wanted. A new set can be obtained within the Tower of Life. If you have destroyed or lost your builder's shirt, talk to 'The Guns'. He will tell you he wants you to go to Yanille and buy him a cheap beer and then you can get your shirt back by talking to him again.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Builder's costume set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
10864:
Builder's trousers is obtained during the Tower of Life quest. This item is part of the builder's costume.

If you have destroyed or lost your builder's trousers, search the plants to the south-east of the tower. (If none found, search plants in south-west as well.) Failing that, search the crates within the tower of life itself.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Builder's costume set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
10865:
Builder's boots are obtained during the Tower of Life quest. This item is part of the builder's costume.

If you have destroyed or lost your builder's boots, pickpocket 'No fingers' for another pair.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Builder's costume set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
10866:
The rivets is a quest item found during the Tower of Life quest. It is found in a crate inside the tower on the north-east side.

The player must use 4 pipes, 5 pipe rings and 6 rivets to repair the broken pipework on the 2nd floor floor of the tower. Additional rivets can be obtained before the pipework is fixed, and fixing the pipework will only remove 6 rivets.
10870:
Binding fluid is an item found during the Tower of Life quest. It is found in a crate inside the tower on the south side.

A player must use 5 metal bars and 4 bottles of binding fluid to repair the broken cage on the 3rd floor floor of the tower. Additional bottles of binding fluid can be obtained before the broken cage is fixed, and fixing the broken cage will only remove 4 bottles of binding fluid.
10874:
The coloured ball is a quest item found during the Tower of Life quest. It is found in a crate inside the tower on the south-west side.

The player must use 4 coloured balls, 3 metal sheets and 4 valve wheels to repair the broken pressure machine on the ground floor of the tower during the quest. Additional balls can be obtained before the machine is fixed, and fixing the machine will only remove 4 balls.
10875: The valve wheel is a quest item found during the Tower of Life quest. It is found in a crate inside the tower on the south-east side. The player must use 4 coloured balls, 3 metal sheets and 4 valve wheels to repair the broken pressure machine on the 1st floor of the tower. Additional wheels can be obtained before the machine is fixed, and fixing the machine will only remove 4 wheels.
10880:
A black satchel is a drop from swordchicks, which can be created in the basement of the Tower of Life after completing the Tower of Life quest. When equipped, it will also enhance the beckon emote.

It can hold a banana, a cake, and triangle sandwich, which heal a total of 20 Hitpoints. It takes multiple bites to consume the food, but it is much cheaper than most food that heals a similar amount.

Multiple satchels of the same type do not stack in the bank, no matter what their contents are. It also cannot be placed into Group storage, despite being a tradeable item.
10881:
A gold satchel is a drop from jubsters, which can be created in the basement of the Tower of Life after completing the Tower of Life quest. When equipped, it will also enhance the beckon emote.

It can hold a banana, a cake, and triangle sandwich, which heal a total of 20 Hitpoints. It takes multiple bites to consume the food, but it is much cheaper than most food that heals a similar amount.

Multiple satchels of the same type do not stack in the bank, no matter what their contents are. It also cannot be placed into Group storage, despite being a tradeable item.
10882:
Rune satchels are a drop from newtroosts, which can be created in the basement of the Tower of Life after completing the Tower of Life quest. When equipped, it will also enhance the beckon emote.

It can hold a banana, a cake, and triangle sandwich, which heal a total of 20 Hitpoints. It takes multiple bites to consume the food, but it is much cheaper than most food that heals a similar amount.

Multiple satchels of the same type do not stack in the bank, no matter what their contents are. It also cannot be placed into Group storage, despite being a tradeable item.
10884: A fuse is used during The Great Brain Robbery to blow open the door of the monastery. The fuse is found in a locker on the ground floor of the ship beached on Harmony Island. It is identical to the fuse used in Cabin Fever.
10886:
The prayer book is a reward from the The Great Brain Robbery quest. By right clicking on it while wearing a holy symbol or hallowed symbol, the player can use Prayer to cure poison at the cost of some prayer points (see #Usages). This can also be done via clicking the hitpoints orb, though potions will be prioritised. Sometimes the poison will only be partially cured if you run out of prayer points.

If lost, the prayer book can be reclaimed in the Edgeville Monastery on the ground floor on the south-western bookcase. The book can also be found on the bookcase in a player-owned house under the title, "Prayer of Deliverance from Poisons".

Although this book has a 'destroy' option, it is possible to get more than one copy. This can be done by keeping the book in your bank while you obtain a new one from your player-owned house bookcase.

The prayer book is always lost on death.
10887:
The barrelchest anchor is a two-handed spiked weapon and quest item acquired in The Great Brain Robbery. 60 Attack and 40 Strength are required to wield it. It is obtained after killing Barrelchest.

Players receive this item in a broken state and must pay Smith on the docks of Mos Le'Harmless a fee of 230,000 coins to repair the anchor (Book o' Piracy is needed to properly speak with Smith). If the anchor is lost, players can retrieve another damaged anchor from Brother Tranquility or purchase a repaired one from Perdu for 290,000 coins. Similar to the Bearhead, players do not need to complete The Great Brain Robbery in order to use or reclaim the Barrelchest anchor.

The anchor has a soft requirement of 50 Prayer in order to start The Great Brain Robbery. Many combat pures may still opt to complete the quest as Smite requires 52 Prayer.

The barrelchest anchor's stats are almost equal to those of Dharok's greataxe. It is well known as a PKing weapon, used in combos such as anchor to Granite maul specials.

It can be upgraded to the Barrelchest anchor (bh) with a Barrelchest anchor imbue scroll, which has a +10 increased crush and strength bonus and a +15% increase to the special attack's damage. The upgraded version can only be used for PvP in the Bounty Hunter minigame, Castle Wars, Clan Wars and Soul Wars however.
10888:
