11677:
The Explorer's notes are written by Nestor Peregrine, a famous dwarven explorer who used to live in Keldagrim. The book details his journey beyond Trollheim, where he discovered the God Wars Dungeon. It can be found in the northern bookcase on the 1st floor in the Keldagrim Library, located on the west side of the northern bridge.

Once taken from the library, it can be retrieved from the bookcase in a player-owned house, in which the book's title is Memoirs of a Dwarven Explorer.
11679:
Antique lamps are rewards from quests, achievement diaries and the Varrock Museum miniquest. Like regular lamps, these lamps grant a player experience in a chosen skill, and the skill chosen must usually be over a certain level which is unboostable.

Lamps that are not included in the three items kept on death will be kept inside your death's coffer, if not deleted.
11680: The address form is an item that is used in the King's Ransom quest. The address form is received as a piece of evidence when the player breaks into the Sinclair Mansion near Seers' Village. It is taken from the library on the 1st floor of the mansion and cannot be telegrabbed. It proves that the Sinclair family had left for good and wasn't going to tell anybody where or why they were going. Once obtained from the house the player must then take the form back to the guard they talked to near the start of the quest. It has no other real use.
11681: The scrap paper is a quest item used in the King's Ransom quest. To obtain it the player must search the dining room in the Sinclair Mansion near Catherby. It must then be taken to the guard at the mansion along with an address form and a black knight helm in order to convince the guard that further investigation is required.
11682:
A hair clip is used in the King's Ransom quest to unlock a gate. It can be obtained by casting the Telekinetic Grab spell on one of the guards of the gate. If players lose it after the quest they can speak to Merlin in Camelot to receive another. Players may use the drop trick to obtain several. He won't give you any if you have some stored in the bank.

It can be used just like a lockpick, unlocking many kinds of doors; however, it doesn't work with chests, other than the chest on the 2nd floor of Oldak's house in Dorgesh-Kaan, the chest in the Bandit Camp in the Kharidian Desert, and the Seers' Village chest required for medium Kandarin Diary. As it functions like a lockpick, that means it can also break when failing to pick lock specific things, like the Secure chest in the Bandit Camp.
11687: Water runes are a variant of normal water runes which can be obtained from the Attacker item machine when playing the Attacker role in Barbarian Assault. To prevent any glitches where players may be able to take runes outside of the minigame and sell them for profit, the machine gives untradeable runes that have no value. Normally, they will disappear if the player attempts to take them outside.
11688:
Air runes are one of the four elemental runes. They are used in every combat spell and most teleportation spells in the standard spellbook, as well as in many spells from other spellbooks. Because they are used very often, players are recommended to purchase an item that can provide infinite air runes while equipped, such as a staff of air.

A common way for beginning players to obtain air runes is to talk to the magic tutor in Lumbridge. She will give you 30 air and mind runes if you don't have any in your inventory or bank. Air runes or packs can be bought from Magic shops, such as Aubury's Rune Shop in Varrock. Non-ironman players can also purchase them from the Nightmare Zone using 25 reward points.

11695: The law rune is a rune used in all teleportation and telekinesis spells, as well as in many of the supportive and utility spells on the Lunar Spellbook. For non-members, the main source of law runes is from monster drops, as most monsters that drop runes may occasionally drop law runes. For members, they may be purchased in the Mage Arena Rune Shop or in the Wizards' Guild, requiring 66 Magic and completion of The Hand in the Sand. They can also be purchased from Ali Morrisane after partial completion of the Rogue Trader miniquest (after completing The Feud quest), from the magic store on Ape Atoll after obtaining the greegree as part of the Monkey Madness I quest, or from the magic store in Prifddinas after completing Song of the Elves. Guardians of the Rift offers an efficient and affordable way of acquiring law runes.
11696:
The cosmic rune is a rune used primarily in enchanting spells. Enchanting spells enchant jewellery, such as rings and amulets, into something that has an effect when worn or operated. For example, when the player casts Lvl-4 Enchant on a diamond ring, the ring will become a ring of life. Cosmic runes are also used for the Lunar spells Astral Contact, Cure Me, Cure Group, and Spellbook Swap and for the resurrection spells in the Arceuus spellbook.

They can be crafted at the Cosmic Altar in Zanaris through the Runecraft skill at level 27 for 8 experience per pure essence after the Lost City quest. They can also be purchased at Lundail's Arena-side Rune Shop in the Mage Arena in the Wilderness, Amlodd's Magical Supplies in Prifddinas after completing Song of the Elves, or from Ali Morrisane after completing The Feud and the Rogue Trader miniquest. At level 59 Runecraft, the amount crafted doubles to two cosmic runes per pure essence. Twisted extracts can also be used to increase the quantity of crafted cosmic runes by 60 per pure essence, requiring partial completion of Desert Treasure II and access to the Scar essence mine.

There is a cosmic rune spawn in the north-western part of Wilderness, on the icy area just south of the members' gate. A total of three cosmic runes spawn here with a respawn time of 1 minute and 53 seconds. This is a dangerous area due to player killers and aggressive ice warriors and ice giants.
11697: Blood runes are one of the runes used to cast spells in the Magic skill. They are used in some of the highest level spells, the lowest of which is Ruby Crossbow Bolt Enchant, and the highest is Heal Group. Blood runes are also used in charging the scythe of Vitur, Sanguinesti staff, ring of shadows, and soul bearer.
11698: Soul runes are unobtainable runes released alongside the Barbarian Assault minigame that would have been obtained from the Attacker item machine when playing the Attacker role. To prevent any glitches where players may be able to take runes outside of the minigame and sell them for profit, untradeable versions of each rune were added. However, the machine only gives runes that are directly used in combat spells. As a result, Soul runes cannot be obtained by players.
11699: Astral runes are unobtainable runes released alongside the Barbarian Assault minigame that would have been obtained from the Attacker item machine when playing the Attacker role. To prevent any glitches where players may be able to take runes outside of the minigame and sell them for profit, untradeable versions of each rune were added. However, the machine only gives runes that are directly used in combat spells. As a result, Astral runes cannot be obtained by players.
11700:
The bronze arrow is an arrow made of bronze. These arrows are the weakest type of arrows in Old School RuneScape and are compatible with most bows. As with most arrows, they can be poisoned.

In order to create this item players must first smelt bronze bars. Then using a hammer and anvil, the player must turn the bar into bronze arrowtips. Creating the bronze bar has no Smithing requirement, while a player must have level 5 Smithing to create the arrowheads. Then players should cut logs, and using a knife, turn them into arrow shafts. After attaching feathers to the arrow shafts (creating headless arrows) players can then use the arrowheads on the headless arrows to create bronze arrows. This entire process requires level 1 Fletching.

In addition, arrows can be purchased from a variety of general and archery stores.
11701:
Iron arrows were an item formerly obtained while playing Barbarian Assault. They could be received from the Attacker item machine, and could not be taken out of the minigame. Players using ranged had to use a different type of arrow to kill Penance Fighters and Penance Rangers, depending on which style was called out by the collector.

As players using Ranged were limited to using low-level gear as a result of this mechanic, Barbarian Assault was updated in 2018 to use four new types of arrows instead. These are twice as strong as Dragon arrows.

11704:
A raw pheasant is obtained by killing a pheasant in the Freaky Forester random event. A raw pheasant must be given to the Freaky Forester to complete the event. The meat from any pheasant can be given to the Freaky Forester despite him asking for the meat of a specific bird.

Raw pheasants disappear if dropped. Attempting to attack another pheasant with one in the inventory results in the message You already have a pheasant carcass. You don't need to kill another. If the player kills two pheasants (so there are two carcasses on the ground) and picks one up, attempting to pick up the second one results in the message You already have a pheasant carcass in your inventory, you don't need to kill another. After handing in a raw pheasant and being told to leave, attempting to attack a pheasant results in the message You don't need to attack any more pheasants. You're allowed to leave. A second raw pheasant can be picked up after giving the first one to the Freaky Forester, but it is removed from the inventory when leaving the event area.
11710:
An anti-dragon shield (nz) is a Nightmare Zone exclusive version of an anti-dragon shield, and shares its combat stats. It spawns on the ground if Elvarg is present in a Nightmare Zone session, as protection against her dragonfire attack.

As with all items with the (nz) suffix, it cannot be taken outside of the Nightmare Zone, and if discarded, can be retrieved from the same place it spawned.
11711:
Magic secateurs (nz) are a Nightmare Zone exclusive version of the magic secateurs, and share its combat stats. They spawn on the ground if Tanglefoot is present in a Nightmare Zone session, as they are the only possible means of damaging the boss.

As with all items with the (nz) suffix, they cannot be taken outside of the Nightmare Zone, and if discarded, can be retrieved from the same place it spawned.
11712:
A chaos rune (nz) is a Nightmare Zone exclusive version of a chaos rune. It spawns on the ground if either the Dagannoth mother or Gelatinnoth mother is present in a Nightmare Zone session, as their combat mechanics require the use of all four types of elemental spells to damage them.

As with all items with the (nz) suffix, they cannot be taken outside of the Nightmare Zone, and if discarded, can be retrieved from the same place it spawned. Runes with the (nz) suffix cannot be used to cast non-combat spells (except for Bones to Bananas and Bones to Peaches), and all spells cast have heavily reduced Magic experience (though this does not apply to experienced gained from damage dealt.)

11721:
An iron pickaxe (nz) is a Nightmare Zone exclusive version of the iron pickaxe, and shares its combat stats. It spawns on the ground during a Nightmare Zone session only if Slagilith is present and the player's Attack is lower than 20. This is because a pickaxe is the only way to damage Slagilith.

As with all items with the (nz) suffix, it cannot be taken outside of the Nightmare Zone, and if discarded, can be retrieved from the same place it spawned.
11722:
A super ranging is a potion only usable in the Nightmare Zone, costing 250 reward points per dose. It boosts one's Ranged stat by 15% + 5. At 99 Ranged, this potion will boost Ranged to 118, which is 6 higher than the regular ranging potion.

Unlike an overload potion, this potion does not reapply every 15 seconds and works the same way as a normal Ranging potion, but with a higher boost.

A super magic potion is a potion only usable in the Nightmare Zone, costing 250 points per dose. It boosts one's Magic stat by 15% + 5. Because of this, it makes spells a great deal more accurate while providing lower levels the ability to use spells far above their Magic level. For example, one with 78 Magic could sip this potion to be able to cast Ice Barrage. At 99 Magic, this potion will boost one's Magic level to 118. You cannot use this to enchant jewellery.

Compared to the Saturated heart, it grants a stronger Magic boost, but it decays over time unlike the boost from the saturated heart.

An overload is a potion purchased from Dom Onion's Reward Shop for 1,500 Nightmare Zone points per dose. Overloads cannot be used outside the Nightmare Zone. Drinking an overload raises a player's Attack, Strength, Defence, Ranged, and Magic levels by 5-19 (5 + 15% of the player's level, rounded down) for five minutes, while causing them to take 50 hitpoints worth of damage over the course of several seconds. This damage is not absorbed if the player has used an Absorption potion.

It is not possible to use an overload if the player currently has less than 51 Hitpoints. However, if a player drinks an overload and lowers their Hitpoints (such as by using a dwarven rock cake or locator orb) before the overload has finished causing damage, the resulting damage will kill them.

Level boosts from an overload are reapplied every 15 seconds until the 5 minute duration ends, at which point the player is healed for 50 Hitpoints and the boosts wear off. Boosts from overloads do progressively decay over time, but given the 15 second reapplications, they effectively remain near or at full effect until the potion wears off.

Scrolls of redirection are a reward from the Nightmare Zone, costing 775 reward points per scroll. Based on the expected value of spending Nightmare Zone points on herb boxes, they have a value of 831 coins. Each scroll redirects a single Teleport to house tablet to one of the following locations, provided that the player has the Construction level to have their house moved there: Rimmington, Taverley (level 10), Pollnivneach (level 20), Hosidius (level 25), Rellekka (level 30), Aldarin (requires completion of Children of the Sun and level 35), Brimhaven (level 40), Yanille (level 50), Trollheim (requires completion of Eadgar's Ruse), and Prifddinas (requires completion of Song of the Elves and thus level 70).

If the player redirects a tablet and wishes to revert it back to its original form, the player will not get their scroll back; however, an unused scroll can be refunded without loss of points.

If the player obtains a redirected tablet without having the requirements to make the tablet in the first place, the reward points can be completely refunded by reverting the tablet.

Players can save an inventory space when going to the God Wars Dungeon by redirecting two tablets to Trollheim, teleporting, and reverting the other back to a house tablet instead of carrying multiple teleports.
11741: The Rimmington teleport is a magic tablet that can be broken by players to teleport just outside the Rimmington house portal. It can be created by using a scroll of redirection on a teleport to house tablet.
11742:
The Taverley teleport is a magic tablet that can be broken by players to teleport just outside the Taverley house portal. It can be created at level 10 Construction by using a scroll of redirection on a teleport to house tablet.

This tablet is the only method (outside of a normal House Teleport with a house in Taverley) of teleporting directly to Taverley. Other nearby teleports (Falador, Burthorpe via games necklace/Minigame Teleport and Camelot) all require a considerable walk to get to the village.

Alternatively, players can teleport directly to Taverley (south of its tree patch) using the balloon transport system.

The black mask (i) is an upgraded version of the black mask. It requires 20 Strength, 10 Defence, and 40 Combat to equip. It can be imbued as a reward from the Nightmare Zone, costing 1,250,000 reward points or 625,000 with the hard tier of Combat Achievements, at Soul Wars for 500 Zeal Tokens, or by using a scroll of imbuing purchased from the Emir's Arena. 16.67% bonus to Melee accuracy and Strength on Slayer targets.

When this item is imbued at Nightmare Zone and subsequently uncharged, it will refund 100% of the cost. 1,250,000 reward points by default and 625,000 when the hard tier of Combat Achievements are complete.

11787:
A steam battlestaff is a steam elemental staff which provides unlimited amounts of water and fire runes as well as the autocast option when equipped. It requires 30 Attack and 30 Magic to wield.

The mystic steam staff is an even stronger alternative, providing better melee and magic stat bonuses. It is obtained by taking the steam battlestaff and 40,000 to Thormac. (Reduced to 30,000 or 20,000 with completion of the hard and elite Kandarin diaries respectively.)

The staff is only obtainable as a potential drop from K'ril Tsutsaroth.

Players can use a steam staff upgrade kit, obtained from Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing, to cosmetically enhance their steam battlestaff, creating a steam battlestaff (or). This only alters its appearance, and becomes untradeable. It can be reverted, but the kit will not be retained.
11789:
The mystic steam staff is an elemental staff requiring 40 Attack and 40 Magic to wield. In addition to increased Melee and Magic Attack bonuses, the staff provides unlimited amounts of water and fire runes as well as the autocast option when equipped.

This staff can be created after the completion of the quest Scorpion Catcher by taking a steam battlestaff and 40,000 to Thormac. After completion of the Hard Kandarin Diary and Elite Kandarin Diary, Thormac will only require 30,000 or 20,000 respectively.

It can also be obtained through other players and bought on the Grand Exchange.

Players can use a steam staff upgrade kit, obtained from Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing, to cosmetically enhance their mystic steam staff, creating a mystic steam staff (or). This only alters its appearance, and it becomes untradeable. It can be reverted, but the kit will not be retained.
11791:
The staff of the dead is a one-handed bladed staff that requires 75 Magic and 75 Attack to wield. It is dropped by K'ril Tsutsaroth, and counts as a Zamorakian item while in the God Wars Dungeon and in the desert Bandit Camp. It is one of several one-handed staves which boost magic damage by 15%.

When a combat spell is cast with the staff, there is a 1/7 (~14.2%) chance that the staff will negate the rune cost for that spell.

The staff can autocast Flames of Zamorak, Crumble Undead, Magic Dart, elemental combat spells from the Standard spellbook, and combat spells from the Arceuus spellbook. It is not, however, able to autocast ancient magicks.

Being a bladed staff, it is notable for its offensive melee stats, which are unusually high for a Magic weapon. Its stats slightly surpass that of a dragon scimitar while having the same attack speed when using melee. However, when using magic spells, it offers an attack speed of 5.

The staff may be upgraded into the toxic staff of the dead, the staff of light, or the staff of balance.
11806:
The Saradomin godsword is one of the five variants of the godsword that was fought over during the God Wars. Requiring 75 Attack to wield, it is created by adding the Saradomin hilt to a completed godsword blade. If not purchasing it from another player, the hilt must be obtained by defeating Commander Zilyana in the God Wars Dungeon.

Players can attach a Saradomin godsword ornament kit, obtained from master clue scrolls, to the godsword. Doing so will cosmetically enhance the godsword, creating a Saradomin godsword (or); this only alters its appearance, and gives no stat enhancements. The godsword will become untradeable, but it can be dismantled, returning both the godsword and the kit.
11810: The Armadyl hilt is a rare drop from Kree'arra, in the God Wars Dungeon. Its design resembles a bird or winged being. When attached to a completed Godsword blade, which can be created by combining the three Godsword shards, it creates the Armadyl godsword.
11812: The Bandos hilt is dropped by General Graardor, in the God Wars Dungeon. When attached to a completed Godsword blade, it creates the Bandos godsword.
11814: The Saradomin hilt is a rare drop from Commander Zilyana, in the God Wars Dungeon. When attached to a completed Godsword blade, which can be created by combining the three Godsword shards, it creates the Saradomin Godsword.
11816: The Zamorak hilt is dropped by K'ril Tsutsaroth, in the God Wars Dungeon as a rare drop. When attached to a completed godsword blade, which can be created by combining the three godsword blade shards, it creates the Zamorak godsword.
11824:
The Zamorakian spear is a two-handed spear obtained from the God Wars Dungeon as a drop from K'ril Tsutsaroth and his bodyguards, requiring an Attack level of 70 to wield. Unlike other spears, it cannot be poisoned, and has its highest bonus in stab, while other spears have the same bonus on all melee attack styles. The Zamorakian spear offers the fourth highest stab bonus of all weapons at +85, shared with the Zamorakian hasta, dragon hunter lance, and crystal halberd. It is outmatched by the Ghrazi rapier with a stab bonus of +94, the Belle’s folly with a stab bonus of +100 and the Osmumten's Fang with a stab bonus of +105.

The Zamorakian spear is currently the strongest spear in the game. It is popular among players because of its versatility; it has stab, slash and crushing options, making it useful on a wide array of monsters, including the Corporeal Beast, to which it deals full damage as a Corpbane weapon. Most dragons, drakes, and wyrms are also weak to the stab attack type, but as a two-handed weapon it is incompatible with an anti-dragon shield; it is only advisable to use it in combination with a super antifire potion (except against wyrms).

Overall, this weapon's total defence bonuses are the highest for any melee weapon, and the second highest for any weapon after the Zaryte crossbow. Many players consider this weapon to be an upgraded dragon spear because both of these spears have the same special attack, though the Zamorakian spear cannot be poisoned. Additionally, the Zamorakian spear's stab bonus outweighs its other bonuses, unlike the dragon spear's balanced stats.

Otto Godblessed can convert the spear into a Zamorakian hasta for 300,000 coins, or 150,000 coins if the player has completed the Elite Kandarin Diary. Reversing the hasta into a spear can be done for free by talking to Otto Godblessed again. The hasta has the exact same stats as the spear, but it is one-handed and thus can be used with a shield or defender. This makes the spear inferior to its hasta variant in virtually every situation, except when fighting the Corporeal Beast, as it is weak to spears but not hastae. The hasta can then further be modified to a dragon hunter lance by combining it with the hydra's claw, faring exceptionally well against draconic creatures and allowing the aforementioned anti-dragon shield to be equipped.
11826:
The Armadyl helmet is an item that can be obtained from Kree'arra and his bodyguards in the God Wars Dungeon, or as an extremely rare drop from an Armadylean/Bandosian guard from elite coordinate clues. Along with the Armadyl chestplate and chainskirt, it is part of the Armadyl armour set, and requires 70 Defence and Ranged to wear.

The helmet has the second highest ranged attack bonus of any item in the headwear slot behind the Masori mask, however, it penalises both melee and mage attack bonuses and lacks any ranged strength bonuses which makes the helm somewhat undesirable.
11828:
The Armadyl chestplate is an item that can be obtained from Kree'arra and his bodyguards in the God Wars Dungeon. Along with the Armadyl helmet and chainskirt, it is part of the Armadyl armour set, and requires 70 Defence and Ranged to wear.

It penalises melee attack bonuses which may make it undesirable in situations where multiple attack styles are used.
11830:
The Armadyl chainskirt is an item that can be obtained from Kree'arra and his bodyguards in the God Wars Dungeon. Along with the Armadyl helmet and chestplate, it is part of the Armadyl armour set, and requires 70 Defence and Ranged to wear.

The chainskirt is light in weight, however, it penalises melee attack bonuses which may make it undesirable in situations where multiple attack styles are used.
11832: The Bandos chestplate is a part of the Bandos armour set, which requires 65 Defence to wear. It is dropped by General Graardor and his bodyguards in the God Wars Dungeon. The Bandos chestplate provides a +4 Strength bonus, and more defensive bonuses than comparable body armours such as the fighter torso and inquisitor's hauberk. Despite seemingly being made of metal, the Bandos chestplate does not interfere with Ava's devices.
11834: Bandos tassets are a part of the Bandos armour set, requiring 65 Defence to wear. They are dropped by General Graardor and his bodyguards in the God Wars Dungeon. Bandos tassets are widely used by experienced players as they offer high stats compared to other leg slot items, including the second highest strength bonus, tied with the Inquisitor's plateskirt, blood moon tassets, and oathplate legs. It's beaten only by Torva platelegs.
11836:
Bandos boots are part of the Bandos armour set, which requires 65 Defence to wear. They have the second highest ranged defence bonus for boots (beaten only by its upgraded variants, the guardian boots and the echo boots).

Bandos boots can be combined with a black tourmaline core to create a pair of guardian boots, which have increased stats. The process cannot be reversed.

A Slayer helmet is a piece of headgear made by combining a nose peg, facemask, earmuffs, spiny helmet, enchanted gem, and a black mask together. Reinforced goggles are additionally required only if the quest A Porcine of Interest is completed. The helmet can be created by players with level 55 Crafting (boosts work) and who have unlocked the "Malevolent masquerade" ability for 400 Slayer reward points. It requires 10 Defence to equip. Despite the helmet requiring a nose peg, which requires 60 Slayer to equip, the Slayer helmet requires no particular Slayer level to wear.

The helmet has the same defensive bonuses as a rune full helm. Additionally, while worn, the helmet provides the special effects of all of the Slayer equipment from which it was made. It will prevent infection from Nex's virus attack, and can be used as warm clothing for Wintertodt.

When worn on a Slayer assignment, the helmet provides an Attack and Strength boost of 16.67% (from the black mask used to make it) against monsters assigned as the player's Slayer task. This does not stack with the boosts given by the Salve amulet or its enchanted/imbued variants against undead Slayer assignments. It does however stack with the 20% damage boost of a berserker necklace when using obsidian weapons. The helmet can be imbued through Soul Wars, the Nightmare Zone, or Emir's Arena (with a scroll of imbuing) to provide a 15% boost to Ranged and Magic damage and accuracy as well, as detailed below.

A lone exception to the boost application are the Awakened variants of Vardorvis, Duke Sucellus, The Leviathan, and The Whisperer if assigned them as a slayer task. Additionally, the Slayer helmet's accuracy and damage bonuses do not apply to monsters outside of the designated assigned area (applicable when receiving tasks from Krystilia or Konar quo Maten), even if the monster type matches the task.

When killed by another player, and the helmet is not one of the items protected on death, the Slayer helmet is converted to a black mask and dropped for that player. It does not drop coins and leave the owner with a broken Slayer helmet, like other untradeable gear would.

Players can own more than one Slayer helmet at a time.
11865:
The Slayer helmet (i), requiring a Defence level of 10 to wear, is a piece of equipment that is worn in the helmet slot. It provides the bonuses of multiple pieces of protective and beneficial Slayer equipment. It functions in the same manner as its unimbued variant (with the 16.67% Melee bonus), except that it also provides an extra 15% boost to Ranged accuracy and Ranged damage, and a 15% boost to Magic accuracy and Magic damage, against monsters assigned as the player's Slayer task.

It has defensive bonuses equivalent to the rune full helm, with the exception of providing +11 higher relative magic defence (+10 vs. -1) as well as positive Magic and Ranged attack bonuses. It will prevent infection from Nex's virus attack, and can be used as warm clothing for Wintertodt.

Players can imbue the Slayer helmet using either 1,250,000 Nightmare Zone reward points (625,000 when the hard tier of Combat Achievements are complete), 500 Soul Wars Zeal Tokens, or by using a scroll of imbuing purchased from the Emir's Arena. The scroll can be used on the black mask before assembling the Slayer helmet or on the Slayer helmet itself.

If an imbued Slayer helmet is disassembled, then it will return an imbued black mask, along with the other components. The black mask (i) can be uncharged to return (depending on the original imbuing method) the scroll of imbuing, or a full refund of the Nightmare Zone reward points or Soul Wars zeal tokens used to purchase it.

For players with undead Slayer tasks, the boosts given by the Salve amulet or Salve amulet (e) do not stack with the effects of a Slayer helmet (i), and the amulet's boosts will take priority over the helmet's.

When using obsidian weapons the effect of a berserker necklace does stack with the effects of a Slayer helmet (i).

The ranged damage bonus from crystal armour pieces is multiplied by the 15% damage boost from the helmet. Assuming players are wearing both the crystal body and legs, this results in a damage bonus of approximately 29.375% (1.15 * 1.125).
11866:
The Slayer ring (or Ring of slaying) can be used to teleport players to various locations related to Slayer.

Players can purchase Slayer rings from Slayer masters for 75 Slayer reward points each. Alternatively, they can purchase the Ring bling unlock for a one-time cost of 150 points, giving them the ability to craft slayer rings. Making a slayer ring requires level 75 Crafting. Players must bring an enchanted gem, a gold bar, and a ring mould to a furnace to make the ring. This yields 15 Crafting experience, the same as an ordinary gold ring.

Each ring has 8 charges when crafted for teleportation. When they are all depleted, the ring crumbles, leaving an enchanted gem behind. Charges can be transferred between rings by using them on each other or by decanting them via Murky Matt. When decanting, the enchanted gems from the empty rings are not left behind. Casting High Level Alchemy on a slayer ring produces 600 coins at full (8) charge, dropping by 6 coins per charge expended.

Unlike most teleports, which stop working above level 20 Wilderness, the Slayer ring is among the few items whose teleports can still be used up to level 30 Wilderness.

The slayer ring also allows players to contact the most advanced Slayer master they are eligible to receive tasks from, consuming no charges. However, players cannot be assigned tasks, spend slayer reward points or purchase slayer equipment from a master when contacting them this way.

The slayer ring (eternal) is an upgraded version of the Slayer ring, made with an eternal gem instead of an enchanted gem. It has identical functions but provides unlimited teleport charges.

11877: Empty vial pack is an item pack containing 100 vials. They can be purchased from various herblore shops and general stores.
11879:
Water-filled vial pack is an item pack containing 100 vials of water.

These packs can solely be bought from the below mentioned store locations.
11883: Bait pack is an item pack containing 100 fishing bait. They can be bought from various fishing shops.
11889:
The Zamorakian hasta is a one-handed spear made by taking a Zamorakian spear to Otto Godblessed after completing the Fishing and Smithing parts of the Barbarian Training miniquest, along with a payment of 300,000 coins (only 150,000 if the player has completed the Elite Kandarin Diary). Like the Zamorakian spear, the hasta requires an Attack level of 70.

As with other hastae, the Zamorakian hasta does not deal full damage when fighting the Corporeal Beast.

It is a popular weapon against enemies weak to stab, such as dragons. Due to its reasonable crush bonus, it is also often used against enemies weak to crush, such as Vet'ion. All of the stat bonuses remain the same as a Zamorakian spear, and it retains its special attack. As the hasta can be wielded with off-hand equipment such as a shield or defender, it is preferable over the spear in all instances except when fighting the Corporeal Beast. As it can also function as a slash weapon it may be useful in some encounters where several attack styles are needed, such as against the Moons of Peril.

It can be upgraded to the dragon hunter lance by combining it with a hydra's claw, obtained from the Alchemical Hydra. The lance has 20% higher accuracy and damage against dragons and many other draconic creatures, but in the process it loses its defensive and prayer bonuses and some of its strength bonus.

Otto Godblessed can turn the hasta back into a spear for free.
11891:
The Saradomin banner is the standard of Team Saradomin in the Castle Wars minigame, in which players on Team Saradomin must defend the Saradomin flag while players on Team Zamorak attempt to capture it and return it to their base to score points. The flag can be passed to another player if it is dropped. It can be bought from the Castle Wars Ticket Exchange shop, owned by Lanthus for 100 castle wars tickets.

The Saradomin banner is a large blue standard bearing the symbol of Saradomin, attached to a long wooden pole. It plays a key role in Castle Wars. It is kept on the top floor of the Saradomin base. Its counterpart in the opposing team is the Zamorak banner.

If captured, the player doing so will automatically switch their current weapon and shield with the standard, which is held with both hands. Players can attack with the standard, but it is a very weak weapon without any accuracy or strength bonuses. If a player with the standard is killed, the standard will be dropped on the ground, allowing it to be taken by members of either team.
11892:
The Zamorak banner is the standard of Team Zamorak in the Castle Wars minigame, in which players on Team Zamorak must defend the Zamorak banner while players on Team Saradomin attempt to capture it and return it to their base to score points. The flag can be passed to another player if it is dropped. It can be bought from the Castle Wars Ticket Exchange shop, owned by Lanthus for 100 castle wars tickets.

The Zamorak banner is a large red standard bearing the symbol of Zamorak, a black W-shaped fork, attached to a long wooden pole.

If captured, the player doing so will automatically switch their current weapon and shield with the standard, which is held with both hands. Players can attack with the standard, but it is very weak weapon without any accuracy or strength bonuses. If a player with the standard is killed, the standard will be dropped on the ground, allowing it to be taken by members of either team.
11895:
The Gold decorative skirt can be bought in the Castle Wars area south of the observatory for 600 Castle Wars tickets. They can only be bought from Lanthus. The gold decorative skirt and their legs counterpart offers the same stats as an adamant plateskirt, including the reduced weight compared to adamant platelegs. It requires level 30 Defence to wear.

When unprotected upon PvP death, this item will stay in the inventory, but will become broken and will require 5,000 coins to repair. 5,000 coins will be dropped upon death for the opponent. After a regular death, the item can be retrieved from the gravestone without a fee.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Castle Wars armour (3) set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
11896:
The decorative magic robe top can be bought from the Castle Wars lobby for 40 Castle wars tickets. The item set can be purchased from Lanthus. It requires level 20 Magic to wear.

The decorative magic robe top is a good option for 1 defence pures as it provides good defence bonuses for only requiring 20 Magic. It provides the same bonuses (and costs the same amount of tickets) as the Decorative armour (ranged top).

If the player dies a PvP death and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 5,000 coins.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Castle Wars mage armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
11897:

11900:

11901:

11904:
The Entomologist's diary belongs to an entomologist named Buggie, who is located in the Kalphite Cave, found east of the Shantay Pass.

The book details the origin of the kalphites in the cave, and it is inferred that the entomologist succumbed to the poison of the kalphites he raised.

If lost, it can be reclaimed by searching Buggie, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house.
11905:
The trident of the seas is a one-handed powered staff requiring 75 Magic to wield. Once charged with runes and coins, it can be used to attack with a built-in magic spell regardless of the player’s current spellbook.

It is available as a task-only drop from cave krakens (or the kraken boss) with level 87 Slayer; normal cave krakens can drop an uncharged trident, whereas the kraken boss can drop a fully charged one. Similar to Barrows equipment, the trident is only tradeable when either uncharged or fully charged.

The trident of the seas has the same effect in drift net fishing as the merfolk trident, though it does not have the ability to hold pufferfish charges (convenient for breathing underwater).

The staff's charge cannot be used against another player in dangerous PvP, only safe minigames.

11910: Chocolate strawberries were food obtainable during the 2014 Valentine's Day event by opening a box of chocolate strawberries given by another player. Eating the strawberries heals two hitpoints. All chocolate strawberries were removed on 20 February 2014 to prevent creating a discontinued tradeable item.
11912:
A box of chocolate strawberries was obtainable during the 2014 Valentine's Day event after giving the Lumbridge Cook a chocolate bar. All boxes were removed on 20 February 2014 to prevent creating a discontinued tradeable item.

To open the box, players have to receive it from someone else; players cannot open their own boxes. The box contains three chocolate strawberries. Opening the box given by another players results in the message: "To (player name), with love - Your secret admirer."
11914:
A box of chocolate strawberries was obtainable during the 2014 Valentine's Day event after giving the Lumbridge Cook a chocolate bar. All boxes were removed on 20 February 2014 to prevent creating a discontinued tradeable item.

To open the box, players have to receive it from someone else; players cannot open their own boxes. The box contains three chocolate strawberries. Opening the box given by another players results in the message: "To (player name), with love - Your secret admirer."
11920:
The dragon pickaxe is the second strongest and second fastest pickaxe in-game, tied with the 3rd Age pickaxe and behind the crystal pickaxe. It requires 61 Mining to mine with the pickaxe and 60 Attack to wield it. However, as its special attack temporarily boosts the player's Mining level by 3, players with at least 60 Attack can start mining with the pickaxe at 58 Mining.

Excluding waiting for ores to respawn or having to move to a new resource, the dragon pickaxe is effectively a 5.88% increase in overall mining speed compared to a rune pickaxe. By default, the dragon pickaxe provides a chance to mine an ore every three ticks, and there is an additional 1/6 chance to reduce this to two ticks, leading to an average of 2.83 ticks per roll.
11922: Lava dragon bonemeal is an item that is used for worship at the Ectofuntus. It consists of a pot filled with lava dragon bones that have been crushed in the bone grinder at the Ectofuntus.
11923:
A broken dragon pickaxe was a dragon pickaxe that had been broken by an exploding rock. It could be fixed at Nurmof's Pickaxe Shop in the Dwarven Mine.

If the broken pickaxe was equipped before being broken, it would remain in the weapon slot. Once unequipped, it could not be equipped again.

After an update on 11 September 2014 making random events optional, all existing broken pickaxes were automatically repaired.
11924:
The malediction ward is a mage-class shield that requires at least 60 Defence to wield. It offers the fifth best Magic attack bonus for the off-hand slot in the game, exceeded by the mage's book, the ancient wyvern shield, the arcane spirit shield and the Elidinis' ward (f).

In terms of stats, the ward provides melee defence identical to that of a dragon square shield but provides a moderate amount of Magic defence instead of providing Ranged defence. The shield carries a substantial Magic attack bonus but negative melee and Ranged attack bonuses. Because of this the shield is ideal for mages, but unsuitable for other combat. The shield also has a Magic damage bonus of 2%.

Players can use a ward upgrade kit, obtained from Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing, to cosmetically enhance the malediction ward, creating a malediction ward (or). This only alters its appearance, and becomes untradeable. It can be reverted, but the kit will not be returned.
11926:
An odium ward is a Ranged shield requiring 60 Defence to wield. It provides the third best Ranged Attack and Ranged Strength bonus in the shield slot, succeeded by the dragonfire ward and the twisted buckler. It is created at the Volcanic Forge in the Wilderness with an odium shard 1, odium shard 2, and odium shard 3, dropped by the Chaos Fanatic, Crazy archaeologist, and Scorpia, respectively.

The ward upgrade kit, purchased from Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing, cosmetically enhances the odium ward, creating an odium ward (or). This only alters its appearance and makes it untradeable. This can be reverted but the kit will not be returned.
11930: The odium shard 3 is an item dropped by Scorpia. When the two other shards, the odium shard 1 and 2 are obtained, they can be forged into an odium ward on the Blighted Volcano on the most north-east part of the Wilderness.
11931: The malediction shard 1 is an item dropped by the Chaos Fanatic. When the two other shards, the malediction shard 2 and 3 are obtained, they can be forged into a malediction ward on the Blighted Volcano on the most north-east part of the Wilderness.
11932: The malediction shard 2 is an item dropped by the Crazy archaeologist. When the two other shards, the malediction shard 1 and 3 are obtained, they can be forged into a malediction ward on the Blighted Volcano on the most north-east part of the Wilderness.
11933: The malediction shard 3 is an item dropped by Scorpia. When the two other shards, the malediction shard 1 and 2 are obtained, they can be forged into a malediction ward on the Blighted Volcano on the most north-east part of the Wilderness.
11934:
A raw dark crab is a members-only fish found in the Wilderness. Dark crabs require a Fishing level of at least 85 and give 130 Fishing experience per catch. A lobster pot is used to catch dark crabs, along with dark fishing bait. Dark fishing bait can be obtained as a drop from various monsters in the Wilderness or bought from other players at the Grand Exchange.

They require a Cooking level of at least 90 to cook and give 215 Cooking experience per fish. It is advised to cook raw dark crabs at the Hosidius Kitchen due to their high burn rate, as they are still possible to burn even at 99 Cooking. Alternatively, wearing a Cooking cape will ensure 100% cook-success rate due to its perk.

Completion of the Elite Wilderness Diary greatly increases the catch rate of these fish, from 16% to 34% at 99 Fishing -- a 112.5% increase, more than doubling the base rate. As such, it is highly recommended that players complete the Elite diary prior to fishing dark crabs. If staying in the area for extended trips, these fish and any other items can be turned into banknotes using Piles in the Resource Area for a fee of 50 coins per item.

Dark Crab fishing spots in the Resource Area are some of the few fishing spots in Gielinor that do not relocate and can be fished in perpetuity, encouraging low-effort skill training. However, this method of training is ill-advised, as player killers may enter the Resource Area to catch fishers off-guard. If a player utilizes the Fishing Barrel and it is kept on death, any fish stored in the barrel will be kept. Players also may utilize the Looting Bag to store their raw or cooked crabs for very low risk and doubling their inventory without utilizing Piles, where both the bag and crabs within will be consumed if the player is killed.
11936:
The dark crab is a type of food that restores 22 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking raw dark crab on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 90 Cooking and granting 215 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt dark crab. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. It will only stop burning entirely if the player is wearing a Cooking cape. The chance to burn is decreased by using the city kitchens when the easy or elite Kourend & Kebos Diary has been completed (5 and 10% respectively).

The dark crab is the second highest instant-health single consumption food, behind the marlin, alongside the tuna potato, anglerfish, bluefin and manta ray. The dark crab has the lowest weight, while the tuna potato has the lowest Cooking requirement, but highest weight. The anglerfish will only heal 22 if Hitpoints are level 93 or higher, but has the added benefit of being able to heal the player above their base Hitpoints. Cooked moonlight antelope and cooked dashing kebbit heals 26 and 23 health respectively, but part of the healing is delayed, making them not always practical in the same situations.

Catching and cooking a dark crab in the Wilderness Resource Area is a requirement for the Elite Wilderness Diary.
11938:
Burnt dark crab is the result of accidentally burning a raw dark crab while attempting to make a dark crab. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels. There is no level where dark crabs stop being burned, although wearing a cooking cape will prevent players from burning any food.

The burnt dark crab has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.
11940:
Dark fishing bait is dropped by various monsters found in the Wilderness. It is needed as bait for dark crabs, along with a lobster pot. A minimum of 85 Fishing is required to use this bait.

Each catch uses up one piece of bait, although since dark crabs can only be found in the Wilderness, it is only recommended to bring enough for just an inventory of caught crabs. If the player is fishing in the Resource Area, they can make longer trips by using Piles to note the caught crabs for a fee of 50 coins each.
11941:
The looting bag is a storage bag that can hold up to 28 stacks of any item. Only one looting bag can be in a player's possession at a time.

Tradeable items can only be stored whilst in the Wilderness, including the Ferox Enclave, by using them on the looting bag or via the looting bag's "Deposit" option. Stackable items like runes, arrows, or noted items stack in the looting bag as they would in the inventory. The bag may also be used in certain locations outside the Wilderness on PvP worlds. The contents of a looting bag cannot be recovered outside of a bank without destroying it or dying.
11942:
An ecumenical key is an item dropped by all monsters in the Wilderness God Wars Dungeon, east of the Forgotten Cemetery, which can be used to instantly access the boss room of any one of the five Godwars bosses (General Graardor, Kree'arra, Commander Zilyana, K'ril Tsutsaroth, and Nex) without having to obtain the kill count normally required.

The keys are only recommended for trips at Kree'arra or Commander Zilyana, as their soldiers take longer to kill. They are not recommended for General Graardor, K'ril Tsutsaroth, and Nex, due to the former two having weak soldiers that can be quickly killed, and the latter's counting for multiple essence per kill.

Players are limited to having three (3) keys at a time; completing the Medium and Hard Wilderness Diary increases this limit to four (4) and five (5) keys, respectively. If players receive additional key drops, they will be unable to pick them up as they are deleted; a message appears in the player's chatbox stating, "You already have enough of these".

Once the key has been used, it will disappear from the player's inventory. If the player has both sufficient kill count and a key, the kill count will be consumed first.

Players who have completed the Hard Wilderness Diary may also sell ecumenical keys to the Lesser Fanatic in Edgeville for 61,500 coins per key.
11943:
Lava dragon bones are dropped exclusively by lava dragons located on Lava Dragon Isle in the Wilderness. They give 340 Prayer experience when buried at the Lava Dragon Isle, or 85 when buried elsewhere. This can be increased by offering the bones in different ways:

255 XP when casting Sinister Offering.

255 XP when offered at the sacred bone burner after the appropriate faith level has been achieved.

297.5 XP when offered at a gilded altar with two burners lit.

340 XP when buried on Lava Dragon Isle, or when offered at the Ectofuntus in the form of lava dragon bonemeal.

340 XP when blessed and broken down into blessed bone shards and offered at the libation bowl, or 408 XP when offered with a jug of blessed sunfire wine. Virilis outside the altar will unnote noted bones for 10 coins each.

595 XP on average when offered at the Chaos Temple in the Wilderness. Each offering gives 297.5 XP, which is the same as the gilded altars with two burners lit, but providing a 50% chance to not consume the bones.

Additionally, Zealot's robes will provide a 5% chance to not consume the bones each time they are used, regardless of the method chosen.
11959:
Black chinchompas are one-handed multi-target stackable Ranged weapons requiring level 65 Ranged to use. Black chinchompas can be obtained by box trapping black chinchompas in the Wilderness Hunter area. This requires 73 Hunter, and will give the player 315 Hunter experience per catch. To use chinchompas in combat, they must be wielded in the weapon slot. Black chinchompas are thrown like darts or throwing knives; however, they explode on impact.

In PvM, they can hit up to 12 (as opposed to 11 with other chinchompas) targets in a 3x3 area. In PvP, the cap is 10 (as opposed to 9 with other chinchompas). They cannot be picked up again from the ground after being thrown and Ava's attractor does not return them since they are live animals. Black chinchompas have a Ranged Strength bonus of +30, as opposed to +15 from red chinchompas and +0 from grey chinchompas.

Using black chinchompas is widely regarded as the fastest way to train Ranged and Hitpoints; however, this method is very costly. Catching black chinchompas is also popular among high-level hunters as it gives fast experience and is profitable.

Fuses are used to describe the attack speed for throwing chinchompas. It is just another name for the conventional styles of ranged training.

Short fuse (accurate): 4 ticks

Medium fuse (rapid): 3 ticks

Long fuse (longrange): 4 ticks
11964:
The amulet of glory (t) (or trimmed amulet of glory) is a cosmetic variant of the regular amulet of glory. Players can receive this item as a reward from hard Treasure Trails at a chance of 1/1,625 per slot. Aside from appearance, it has the same functions and stat bonuses as a regular amulet of glory (including gem mining as long as it is charged).

This item can be stored in the treasure chest of a costume room, provided that the interface of the corresponding clue tier is opened before attempting to store the item. Alternatively, the item can be used on the opened treasure chest to insert it without viewing the interface. However, unlike its regular counterpart, it cannot be mounted in a Quest Hall.

For Ironmen completing treasure trails, this can NOT be used as an uncharged amulet of glory - only a regular amulet of glory may be used, obtained either through crafting one at level 80, catching a dragon impling at level 83 Hunter, or by completing other treasure trails.

Heroes' Quest is required to charge the amulet at the Fountain of Rune. Like the regular amulet of glory, there is a 1 in 25,000 chance that it will transmute into an amulet of eternal glory when charged at the Fountain of Rune, causing it to provide unlimited teleports rather than the usual six. This will cause it to lose its trimmed status.

11972:
The combat bracelet is a dragonstone bracelet that has been enchanted by the Lvl-5 Enchant spell.

A combat bracelet can be recharged at the totem pole in the Legends' Guild, or at the Fountain of Uhld in the Myths' Guild, or by casting Recharge Dragonstone, giving it four charges. Players who have completed Legends' Quest can also recharge it at the Fountain of Rune, giving it six charges.

The bracelet provides useful teleports to combat-related guilds. The bracelet also informs its wearer of their current Slayer task count every 10 kills (i.e. "You still need to kill x0 monsters to complete your current Slayer assignment"). This feature only works if the bracelet is charged.

Like other dragonstone jewellery, it is one of the few items whose teleports will work up to level 30 Wilderness, while most other means of teleportation will not work above level 20 Wilderness.

The bracelet also provides combat bonuses comparable to those of mithril gloves from the Culinaromancer's Chest. Compared to mithril gloves, the bracelet has +1 attack bonuses and -1 defensive bonuses in all attack styles except magic.
11974:
The combat bracelet is a dragonstone bracelet that has been enchanted by the Lvl-5 Enchant spell.

A combat bracelet can be recharged at the totem pole in the Legends' Guild, or at the Fountain of Uhld in the Myths' Guild, or by casting Recharge Dragonstone, giving it four charges. Players who have completed Legends' Quest can also recharge it at the Fountain of Rune, giving it six charges.

The bracelet provides useful teleports to combat-related guilds. The bracelet also informs its wearer of their current Slayer task count every 10 kills (i.e. "You still need to kill x0 monsters to complete your current Slayer assignment"). This feature only works if the bracelet is charged.

Like other dragonstone jewellery, it is one of the few items whose teleports will work up to level 30 Wilderness, while most other means of teleportation will not work above level 20 Wilderness.

The bracelet also provides combat bonuses comparable to those of mithril gloves from the Culinaromancer's Chest. Compared to mithril gloves, the bracelet has +1 attack bonuses and -1 defensive bonuses in all attack styles except magic.
11976:
The amulet of glory is a dragonstone amulet that has been enchanted by the Lvl-5 Enchant spell. After completion of Heroes' Quest, it can be charged at the Fountain of Heroes and the Fountain of Rune. When charged at the Fountain of Rune they will have 6 charges instead of the normal 4. With the completion of Dragon Slayer II, it can be charged at the Fountain of Uhld below the Myths' Guild. The amulet of glory is tradeable on the Grand Exchange only when it has zero, four, or six charges.

It is a very popular amulet in members-only worlds amongst players of all levels, as it provides good damage bonuses, has no requirements to wear, is much less expensive than the amulet of fury, and offers useful teleports.

Like other dragonstone jewellery, it is one of the few items with a teleportation ability that will work up to level 30 Wilderness, while most other means of teleportation will not work above level 20 Wilderness.

A trimmed version, the amulet of glory (t), may be obtained from hard Treasure Trails, but is no different than a normal amulet of glory aside from appearance and the inability to use it for certain Treasure Trail steps.

Certain Treasure Trail clue steps in the Hard, Elite and Master tiers require having an amulet of glory equipped, which can be difficult for ironmen, given the very high Crafting level of 80 required. However, this can be somewhat alleviated by using a mushroom pie to temporarily boost Crafting by 4 levels, meaning an actual Crafting level of 76 is required for these clue steps.
11978:

11992:
Lava scales are always dropped by lava dragons at the Lava Dragon Isle located in the Wilderness. They are also dropped uncommonly by brutal black dragons. The shards are an ingredient for extended antifire and extended super antifire potions.

Lava scales themselves have no use, but when ground with a pestle and mortar, players can obtain between 3-6 lava scale shards. This amount will be increased by 50% rounded down with completion of the hard Wilderness Diary, meaning that each scale will yield either 4, 6, 7, or 9 shards when ground. The amount received is random, with high Herblore level yielding a higher average. With 99 Herblore, there is a 98% chance of receiving the maximum amount of shards.

If asking Wesley to grind them, he can only crush one scale to three shards, warning the player of this before proceeding.

Note: If attempting to obtain lava scale shards, infernal eel fishing is a viable option for players wishing to avoid the Wilderness.
11994:
Lava scale shards are the result of using a pestle and mortar on a lava scale, which is dropped by lava dragons and brutal black dragons. Grinding a scale yields between 3-6 shards, with higher Herblore levels yielding a higher average. If the hard Wilderness Diary is complete, this amount will be increased by 50%, rounded down, meaning that players can receive either 4, 6, 7, or 9 shards per scale.

They can also be obtained by using a hammer on an infernal eel, which require level 80 Fishing to catch. Each eel has a 1/8.75 chance to yield between 1-5 shards.

The shards are used as an ingredient to make extended antifires and extended super antifires, requiring levels 84 and 98 Herblore to create, respectively, with 1 shard being used per dose.
11995:
The pet chaos elemental is a pet that resembles the miniature chaotic clouds that inhabit the area where the Chaos Fanatic resides, and can be obtained by killing the Chaos Elemental or the Chaos Fanatic.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.
11996:
The holiday tool is a special spawner tool distributed by Jagex Moderators to certain players of the Old School RuneScape community.

During the reintroduction of free-to-play, it was given out to certain clan leaders, livestreamers and players focusing on hosting free to play events in order to spawn free to play starter packs. It could only spawn around ten starter packs twenty times per day.

During holiday events, Jagex Moderators or players who own the tool may use it to spawn tradeable holiday items during livestream events. It could only spawn a set amount of items twenty times per day, but Jagex Moderators can reset this by typing in ::setvar event_dailydistribution 0 in the chatbox.
11997: Easter is an unobtainable item added with the 2014 Easter event. Presumably, it would have been used by Jagex moderators to spawn Eggs during community events, similar to the community pumpkin and the holiday tool.
11998:
The smoke battlestaff is an elemental staff requiring 30 Attack and 30 Magic to wield. The staff provides unlimited amounts of air and fire runes as well as the autocast option when equipped.

The mystic smoke staff is an even stronger alternative, providing better melee and magic stat bonuses. It is obtained by taking the smoke battlestaff and 40,000 to Thormac. (Reduced to 30,000 or 20,000 with completion of the hard and elite Kandarin diaries respectively.)

The staff provides a 10% increase to Magic accuracy and damage when casting spells from the standard spellbook; this bonus also applies to curse spells.

The staff is only obtainable as a potential drop from the thermonuclear smoke devil.
12000:
The mystic smoke staff is an elemental staff requiring 40 Attack and 40 Magic to wield. In addition to increased Melee and Magic Attack bonuses, the staff provides unlimited amounts of air and fire runes as well as the autocast option when equipped.

Like the smoke battlestaff, it provides a 10% increase in accuracy and damage when casting spells from the standard spellbook; this bonus also applies to curse spells.

This staff can be created after the completion of the quest Scorpion Catcher by taking a smoke battlestaff and 40,000 coins to Thormac. After completion of the Hard Kandarin Diary and Elite Kandarin Diary, Thormac will only require 30,000 coins or 20,000 coins respectively.
12002:
The occult necklace is a magical amulet that requires 70 Magic to wear. It is dropped by the smoke devil and its boss variant. Wearing it increases the player's Magic damage by 5%, and is the only amulet to give such a bonus. This 5% bonus will also stack with existing boosts, such as the staff of the dead and the imbued slayer helmet. The salve amulet(ei) does not apply its damage bonus to other hit targets when barraging. The 3rd Age amulet possess slightly higher magic accuracy but lacks magic strength. Thus, aside from using single target magic damage against undead mobs, or in situations where landing a single spell is pivotal, it is the best neck slot item for magic damage output.

A combination of the occult necklace and staff of the dead while using Ice Barrage would increase a player's max hit to 36, from an original maximum of 30. The max hit increases to 40 if using a black mask (i) or slayer helmet (i) on a Slayer task.

Players can attach an occult ornament kit, obtained from master clue scrolls, to cosmetically enhance the necklace, creating an occult necklace (or). This only alters its appearance, and gives no stat enhancements. It can be dismantled, returning the necklace and ornament kit.
12004:
A kraken tentacle is obtained from killing cave krakens (and their boss version) in the Kraken Cove, located just south-west of the Piscatoris Fishing Colony. The tentacle is used to make abyssal tentacles, enhanced tridents of the seas, and enhanced tridents of the swamps.

When the tentacle is used on an abyssal whip, an upgraded version of the whip, the abyssal tentacle, is created. The upgraded abyssal tentacle requires level 75 Attack to wield. Once combined with the whip, the weapon will degrade after 10,000 hits, consuming the whip and leaving only the tentacle. When using the items on each other there will be a warning message that states The tentacle will gradually consume your whip and destroy it. You won't be able to get the whip out again. The combined item is not tradeable.

Ten kraken tentacles can be given to Lieve McCracken to enhance a trident of the seas or swamp to hold 20,000 charges instead of 2,500. Ten tentacles are required for every trident the player wishes to enhance.
12006:
The abyssal tentacle is a weapon which requires 75 Attack to wield. It is created by combining a kraken tentacle with an abyssal whip. It is an upgraded variant of the whip, having a +8 increase in Slash and +4 increase in Strength over its predecessor. It also has a 25% chance per hit to poison the opponent, which starts at 4 damage. With regard to 4 tick one-handed weapons, the +90 slash bonus of the abyssal tentacle is second only to the +100 slash bonus of the Blade of Saeldor.

The abyssal tentacle can be created by using a kraken tentacle on an abyssal whip. Once created, the weapon will degrade after 10,000 attacks, including misses. Afterwards the whip is consumed, leaving only the tentacle. When using the items on each other there will be a warning message notifying the player that this process is irreversible and the abyssal tentacle is not tradeable.

If the abyssal tentacle is not protected upon death, it will fully degrade into a kraken tentacle. However, if it is protected on death, it will remain in its regular state as the abyssal tentacle. In addition, the abyssal tentacle does not stack in the bank, regardless of the number of charges the abyssal tentacles have.

Using a Shattered relics variety ornament kit on an abyssal tentacle will change its appearance into that of an abyssal tentacle (or).
12011:
Pay-dirt is obtained while mining ore veins within the Motherlode Mine. Mining pay-dirt grants 60 (up to 61.5 with full prospector outfit) Mining experience and requires a minimum Mining level of 30. Pay-dirt can be cleaned by depositing them into the hopper in the centre of the mine. Once cleaned players must search a sack to claim their ores, which is dependent on the player's Mining level. Pay-dirt cannot be deposited in the bank.

Players have a 1/32 (~3.13%) chance of obtaining a golden nugget per pay-dirt, which can be used to purchase the prospector outfit and other mining-related rewards from Prospector Percy's Nugget Shop. The number of golden nuggets received is limited to 3 per batch of pay-dirt deposited into the hopper. While this limit doesn't cause issues during normal gameplay, seasonal events with boosted rates can cause golden nuggets to be deleted. To avoid this, players can deposit half of their pay-dirt at a time by dropping the other half before depositing.

Which ore the pay-dirt becomes is determined at the time it is mined. If using a temporary boost, to try to get ore above your level, use the boost while mining, as opposed to using the boost at the hopper and sack.

The double-ore bonus from Varrock armour does not apply to pay-dirt.
12012:
Golden nuggets are obtained in the Motherlode Mine by searching the sack after cleaning the pay-dirt.

They can be traded in for various rewards from Prospector Percy's Nugget Shop.
12014:
The prospector jacket is one part of the prospector outfit and is a reward from the Motherlode Mine in exchange for 60 Golden nuggets or from Volcanic Mine for 39,000 points. The jacket gives a Mining experience boost of 0.8% when worn.

Alternatively, a player can use the Varrock armour 4 from the elite Varrock Achievement diary to receive the experience bonus.

Like the rest of the Prospector kit, the jacket provides partial protection against the heat of the Kharidian desert, adding 12 seconds to the interval between required sips from a waterskin, or 34 seconds if the entire set is worn.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Prospector kit set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

Note: Any piece of the set that was purchased from the Petrified Pete's Ore Shop can't be sold for golden nuggets at the Prospector Percy's Nugget Shop. If you try to do this, you will receive the message "You can't sell this item back to Percy as you did not buy it from this shop".
12015:
The prospector legs are a part of the Prospector kit that can be bought from the Motherlode Mine in exchange for 50 golden nuggets or Volcanic Mine for 34,000 points. These leggings increase Mining experience by 0.6% when worn.

Like the rest of the Prospector kit, the legs provide partial protection against the heat of the Kharidian desert, adding 12 seconds to the interval between required sips from a waterskin, or 34 seconds if the entire set is worn.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Prospector kit set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

Note: Any piece of the set that was purchased from the Petrified Pete's Ore Shop can't be sold for golden nuggets at the Prospector Percy's Nugget Shop. If you try to do this, you will receive the message "You can't sell this item back to Percy as you did not buy it from this shop".
12017:
The Salve amulet (i) is the imbued form of the salve amulet, granting an additional 16.67% increase in the wearer's ranged accuracy and damage, as well as a 15% increase for magic, when fighting undead monsters.

The salve amulet is imbued by using either 800,000 Nightmare Zone points (halved upon completing the hard combat achievements), 320 Soul Wars Zeal Tokens, or by using a scroll of imbuing on the amulet. Amulets imbued through the latter two methods do not count for completing the Ardougne Diary task. Furthermore, amulets imbued at one location cannot be refunded at a different location.
12018:
The Salve amulet(ei) is the enchanted and imbued form of the salve amulet, granting a 20% increase in the wearer's accuracy and damage for melee, ranged, and magic when fighting undead monsters.

The salve amulet's bonuses against the undead do not stack with the black mask and slayer helmet's on-task bonuses; wearing both will only apply the bonuses of the salve amulet (ei). The salve amulet also does not have an effect on the dwarf multicannon's accuracy. However, the bonuses of Void Knight equipment do stack with the salve amulet. Additionally, the amulet's effects apply to all targets when using multi-hitting melee weapons in a multicombat area, such as the Scythe of Vitur and the special attack of the dragon 2h sword, but not for multi-hitting magic and ranged attacks (ex. chinchompas and burst spells).

12161:
Puzzle boxes can be obtained by doing hard, elite, and master Treasure Trails. Before you are able to continue with your clue scroll, you will have to complete the puzzle.

A puzzle box is always scrambled 101 times before being handed to the player, by randomly sliding a piece into the empty position starting from the solved state.

If you have a duplicate puzzle box, (obtained by a method such as the Drop trick) in your inventory or bank after completing the clue, you cannot obtain another clue.

12199:
The Ancient crozier is part of the ancient vestment set. To wield one, the player needs at least 60 Prayer.

The crozier is equipped as a staff in the weapons slot and counts as a Zarosian item within the God Wars Dungeon. Despite this fact, it cannot be used to autocast Ancient magicks.

This item can be stored in the treasure chest of a costume room, provided that the interface of the corresponding clue tier is opened before attempting to store the item. Alternatively, the item can be used on the opened treasure chest to insert it without viewing the interface, as part of the ancient vestment set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

It should be noted that despite being obtained from a Reward casket (medium), it is stored in the easy rewards section of the treasure chest.

The black pickaxe is a pickaxe that mines on a 5-tick cycle, 1-tick faster than the steel pickaxe and the same speed as the mithril pickaxe. It is a possible reward from beginner and easy Treasure Trails. This item can be stored in the treasure chest of a costume room, provided that the interface of the corresponding clue tier is opened before attempting to store the item. Alternatively, the item can be used on the opened treasure chest to insert it without viewing the interface.

Players need 10 Attack to wield the pickaxe and 11 Mining to mine with it.

It is the lightest pickaxe, making it the best for activities that require running, such as questing and training Runecraft through the Abyss or Dense Essence Mining.

Nardah teleport scrolls are consumable teleport scrolls that teleport the player to Nardah. They can be obtained from all levels of Treasure Trails except beginner.

There are no requirements to use this teleport.

If the player has completed Spirits of the Elid, they can use this item to quickly teleport to near the Elidinis Statuette to quickly replenish their prayer points, run energy, special attack energy, and hitpoints. This can be ideal for combat activities that require frequent restoration, such as Barrows.

12407:
Pest control teleport scrolls are consumable teleport scrolls that teleport the player to the Void Knights' Outpost. They can be obtained from all levels of Treasure Trails except beginner.

There are no requirements to use this teleport.

Although players can teleport directly to Pest Control every 20 minutes via Minigame Teleport, these direct teleport scrolls have a few beneficial uses.

Pest Control teleport scrolls provide the closest teleport to an anvil for those doing clues and arguably the most important aspect is they provide players with the closest bank teleport that is not diary locked. By having access to such a close bank, these scrolls are ideal for using when doing Corporeal Beast resupplying or skill related activities.

For Ultimate ironmen, an added major benefit is that it is one of the closest teleports to a rune shop and a general store that sells axes.

After an update on 11 September 2014 making random events optional, all existing broken pickaxes were automatically repaired.

This item mimics the look of the third age druidic wreath from RuneScape 3, and as such can be considered part of the 3rd age druidic robes set. Unlike the robes, however, the wreath offers no bonuses.

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room.

The ring of the gods is a ring dropped by Vet'ion and Calvar'ion.

It can be imbued, with the holy wrench in inventory, for 650,000 Nightmare Zone reward points or 325,000 with the hard tier of Combat Achievements, 260 Soul Wars zeal tokens, or a scroll of imbuing, purchased for 200 Emir's Arena reward points, giving it an additional +4 prayer bonus as well as the effect of the holy wrench when equipped.
12603:
The tyrannical ring is a ring dropped by Callisto and Artio. Callisto can be found in Callisto's Den and Artio can be found in the Hunter's End.

It is very useful when using crush weapons as the tyrannical ring is one of only three rings that provide a crush attack bonus, the others being the brimstone ring and the ring of shadows. However, unlike the brimstone ring and the ring of shadows, the tyrannical ring does not provide any strength bonus.

It is often used with dragon warhammer for its special attack, as it only reduces the enemy's defence if the player hits, which is where the tyrannical ring's accuracy bonus helps.

It can be imbued into a Tyrannical ring (i) using 650,000 Nightmare Zone reward points or 325,000 with the hard tier of Combat Achievements, 260 Soul Wars zeal tokens, or a scroll of imbuing, purchased for 200 Emir's Arena reward points, giving it a +8 crush attack and defence bonus, instead of the usual +4.
