The rotten onion is a special spawner tool distributed by Jagex Moderators to certain players of the Old School RuneScape community. During the MacMillan Cancer Support Charity Event of 2015, it was used to spawn green banners for players watching the livestreamed event.

There are two unique options for the onion:

Chew, which would spawn green banners.

Smell, which would cause the player to say, "Oh Saradomin! Who on Gielinor thought it'd be a good idea to smell a rotten onion?"
13328:
The green banner is an item that was made available during the MacMillan Cancer Support Charity Event that was hosted during the 14th and 15th of November 2015 via usage of the rotten onion, which was distributed by Jagex Moderators to certain players of the Old School RuneScape community. It was made available from Diango's Toy Store the week after.

This item cannot leave a placeholder in the bank.
13331:
The Saradomin max cape is the result of combining a Saradomin cape with a max cape, during which the max hood required to be in the player's inventory will automatically convert to the Saradomin max hood.

Like the other max cape variants (a max cape combined with another cape slot item), the Saradomin max cape does not have the max cape's stats or perks; it only acts as a cosmetic upgrade to the Saradomin cape with the following exceptions when worn:

It acts as a Cooking cape to allow access to the Cooks' Guild without a chef's hat, golden chef's hat, Varrock armour 3 or 4

It acts as a Crafting cape to allow access to the Crafting Guild without a brown apron or golden apron

It acts as a Runecraft cape to prevent essence pouches from degrading (but does not allow access to runic altars)

It acts as a Firemaking cape to work as a piece of warm clothing

It can be used to perform the Skill Cape emote.

The max cape and saradomin cape can be separated by using a knife on the cape. Mac will also buy back a max cape, along with its variants, for 1,900,800 coins each. He will return the secondary item any max cape variant was combined with upon doing so.

On a PvP death, it is always kept in the inventory, even if not protected. If the player is skulled and has the Protect Item prayer active, both the max cape and their most valuable item will be kept. Otherwise, on death from causes outside of the wilderness, if it is not one of your protected items, it goes to your grave.

If players are refunding the Saradomin max cape via Mac, the player must also have the Saradomin max hood in their inventory.

Should players lose the hood, they may reclaim it from Mac for free.

13339:
Sacred eels are members-only fish that can be caught at Zul-Andra with a fishing rod and fishing bait, requiring at least level 87 Fishing and granting 105 Fishing experience per eel caught. The village may only be accessed once players reach the Tyras Camp during Regicide. Players must also first speak to High Priestess Zul-Harcinqa, or they will be stopped by the closest worshiper and instructed to do so upon trying to fish.

With a minimum Cooking level of 72, the fish can be dissected with a knife to extract Zulrah's scales. Dissecting the fish gives 3–9 scales and 109–127 Cooking experience (100 base XP plus 3 for each scale obtained). A player's Cooking level affects how many scales are received when they are dissected. The minimum, maximum, and average scales per level can be obtained from the table below. Furthermore, the sacred eels provide a relatively high chance (around 1/500, depending on your Fishing level) of obtaining Clue bottles.

With 90 Fishing and Cooking, you can expect to gain about 21,300 Fishing experience, 23,800 Cooking experience, and about 1,200 Zulrah's scales per hour. With 97 Fishing and 99 Cooking, you can expect to gain about 23,500 Fishing experience, 26,400 Cooking experience, and about 1,500 scales per hour (about 200–225 eels). The Rada's blessing's chance to double caught fish works on sacred eels, increasing the number of eels caught per hour if used.

Players have a base chance of 1/99,000 to obtain the Heron pet while fishing Sacred Eels. On death, each sacred eel's worth counts as 16 coins.

The maximum number of scales acquired from every dissected sacred eel increases in 8-level intervals, capping at a boosted level of 104 (9 scales).
13340:
The Agility cape is a Cape of Accomplishment that may only be acquired and worn by players who have achieved the maximum level in the Agility skill, 99. Once players have trained to this level, they may purchase the cape from Cap'n Izzy No-Beard, located at the entrance of the Brimhaven Agility Arena, for a fee of 99,000 coins. When this fee is paid, the player receives both the cape and a matching hood.

Like all skill capes, the Agility cape gives +9 to all defensive stats, and also a +4 bonus to prayer if it is trimmed, which requires a separate skill at level 99. The cape is automatically trimmed if this condition is met. However, if the cape is equipped at the time of achieving level 99 in a separate skill, the cape will remain untrimmed as the game will consider it a graceful cape.

When the Agility cape is equipped, it will act as a substitute to the graceful cape, granting the same -4 kg in weight reduction and 3% increased natural run energy restoration; as a substitute, it will also grant the graceful outfit's set effect when worn with the other five graceful pieces. This allows the cape to be used for the master clue step, "Complete a lap of the Rellekka Rooftop Course while wearing the full graceful outfit." Once per day, it is also able to restore the player's run energy to 100%, and provide the effect of a stamina potion for one minute.

The Agility cape is the only piece of the graceful set that can be purchased with coins.

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room, as part of the Agility cape set, along with the hood. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

As of 1 August 2026, there are 132,537 players that have achieved level 99 in Agility.

13342:
The max cape is a cape available to players who have attained level 99 in all 24 skills. It is sold by Mac on his island, west of the Warriors' Guild, for 2,376,000 coins, equivalent to 99,000 for each skill. When purchased, it comes along with a corresponding hood.

The cape's stats are equivalent to a trimmed skillcape. It inherits all skillcape perks from skillcapes. The cape's emote shows the icons for all 24 skills flying above the character's head, and a bar-graph stylised like the skills interface icon, with the player floating over it.

To reach Mac, the player needs a pickaxe and an axe, as well as level 99 in Agility, Crafting, Construction, Defence, Mining, and Woodcutting. After purchasing, players can sell excess max capes for 1,900,800 coins. This can only be done if the player has both the hood and cape in their inventory. Other max cape variants can be refunded in the same manner.

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room, as part of the max cape set, along with the hood. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

The total level a player needs for the max cape is 2,376. The minimum amount of experience required for the cape is 312,826,344. As of 1 August 2026, there are 52,396 players that have achieved level 99 in all skills.

On a PvP death, the cape is always kept in the inventory, even if not protected. If the player is skulled and has the Protect Item prayer active, both the max cape and their most valuable item will be kept. Otherwise, on death from causes outside of the wilderness, if the cape is not one of protected items, it goes to the grave.

13353:
Gricoller's can is a reward from the Tithe Farm minigame, which is found in the south-east corner of Hosidius. Players may exchange points at Farmer Gricoller's Rewards for the can.

Gricoller's can costs 200 points and acts like a watering can, the difference being that it holds 1,000 charges instead of 8. It can be fully refilled by using it on any water source (including the Humidify spell). It can also be refilled at Farmer Gricoller's rewards shop, free of charge.

Players will find the Tithe Farm to be more convenient when using Gricoller's can as it can hold enough water to grow 333 Tithe Farm fruits by itself. Unlike regular watering cans, it can also skip its own animation when used on another plant, removing the need to alternate cans for fast watering.

The tool leprechaun is able to store Gricoller's can in the watering can slot.

A player can purchase more than 1 of these if they use the drop trick, but will find they cannot pick up the original can back up off the ground. If a player, however, stores 1 Gricoller's can at the tool leprechaun, they are able to purchase a 2nd one. Every Gricoller's can operates the same "water tank", much like how binding necklaces, bracelets of clay and other shared-stat items work. This can be useful, as you can store a can with the Leprechaun and fill the second at a bank near a water source. Having a second Gricoller's can in your bank can replace normal watering cans to be used for activities such as watering tree pots in preparation for tree runs without needing to find a tool leprechaun.
13354:
A lovakite bar is a bar of refined lovakite ore made by smelting one lovakite ore and two pieces of coal at the Lovakite furnace in the centre of Lovakengj, granting 20 Smithing experience.

It can be smelted with a Smithing level of 45.

It cannot be smelted in a normal furnace. If players try, it'll say it's not the right temperature. Players must use the Lovakite furnace just south of the blast mine bank (accessible instantly by using Xeric's talisman to teleport to Xeric's Inferno). However, the Superheat Item spell will work as normal.
13355:
Juniper logs are obtained from chopping mature juniper trees, located within Hosidius near the saltpetre deposits. Juniper trees require 42 Woodcutting to chop and give 35 Woodcutting experience per log. They cannot be used in training Firemaking.

Players can deposit up to 60 juniper logs in each charcoal furnace in the south end of Hosidius, and lighting the furnace requires a tinderbox and paying Smoggy 600 coins. After the logs have finished burning, players may obtain juniper charcoal, used to make dynamite. Each log yields 50 juniper charcoal.
13356:
Lovakite ore is a type of ore that can be obtained through Mining, and is only found in the lovakite mine in Lovakengj. Mining this ore requires 65 Mining.

Lovakite ore can be mined with a Mining level of 65 or higher, granting 60 Mining experience. Lovakite ore has a respawn time of 30–45 seconds.

It can be smelted into a lovakite bar by combining one Lovakite ore with two coal, which requires level 45 Smithing and grants 20 experience. Lovakite can only be smelted at the lovakite furnace in central Lovankengj (south of the Blast Mine) or via Superheat Item. Attempting to do so at any other furnace will state that the furnace's temperature is wrong for this ore. Lovakite bars can then be smithed into Shayzien armour.

It takes 11 bars to make one full set of armour, equivalent to 11 lovakite ores and 22 coal.

Varrock armour 2 and higher levels of Varrock armour has a chance to double the number of ores received from mining.

Mining a piece of lovakite ore is a hard Kourend & Kebos Diary task.

It is dropped by the tier 5 soldier at the Combat Ring in the Shayzien Encampment. It can also be created at an anvil with 93 Smithing and 4 lovakite bars.

In terms of defensive bonuses, it lies between the iron platebody and steel platebody.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Shayzien armour (tier 5) set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored. It can alternatively be stored in a STASH unit as it is required for an Elite clue step.
13383: Xerician fabric is a piece of fabric dropped by lizardmen, lizardman brutes, and lizardman shamans. It can also be found by thieving from stone chests found in the Molch Lizardman Temple. It is used in the Crafting skill to create Xerician robes using a needle and thread or a costume needle. The Xerician robes can be stored in an Armour case in the Costume room of a Player-owned house.
13385:
The Xerician hat is a part of the Xerician robes set, and requires 10 Defence and 20 Magic to wear.

Its stats are identical to gnome hats, Canifis hats, the ghostly hood, and the Fremennik hat. The hat is the second-lightest of the equivalent alternatives, being only slightly beaten by the ghostly hood; because of this, it's not recommended to use the hat in situations where it might be lost, as the alternatives are considerably cheaper.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Xerician robes. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
13387:
The Xerician top is part of the Xerician robes set. Equipping the Xerician top requires the player to have at least 10 Defence and 20 Magic.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Xerician robes. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
13389:

13391:
The lizardman fang is a common drop from lizardmen and their brute and shaman counterparts. They are used to charge teleports on Xeric's talisman, in which each fang provides one teleport charge.

100 Lizardman fangs can also be obtained by dismantling an inert Xeric's talisman, either via the 'Dismantle' option or by using a pet rock on it.
13392:
Xeric's talisman is an amulet that allows players to teleport to locations around Great Kourend. The talisman was once owned by Xeric, a tyrannical ruler who reigned over Great Kourend during the Age of Strife.

At level 72 Construction, the talisman can be mounted in the portal nexus room in a player-owned house. This requires an inert Xeric's talisman, 1 mahogany plank, 1 gold leaf and 5,000 lizardman fangs. A mounted talisman provides unlimited teleport charges.

13394: Gang meeting info is an item obtained from the information board near Captain Ginea. It details the location of meetings between gangsters and the gang boss. This is part of the Intelligence Gathering activity.
13396: The training manual is obtained from Captain Ginea as part of the Intelligence Gathering activity after giving her an intelligence report, dropped by gangsters and the gang boss during one of their meetings. Reading the book gives the player the option to gain experience in either Hitpoints, Attack, Strength, or Defence. This item cannot be banked. Dying with the book in your inventory will cause it to be permanently lost.
13397: Servery flour are obtained from the food cupboard in the Hosidius mess. It is used in creating servery pineapple pizza and servery meat pie.
13398: Servery pastry dough is obtained from using a bowl of water on servery flour. It is then used on a servery dish to create a servery pie shell.
13399: Servery raw meat is obtained from the meat table in the Hosidius mess. It can be cooked into servery cooked meat, granting 1 Cooking experience. It is used in creating servery stew and servery meat pie.
13400: Servery dishes are obtained from the utensil cupboard in the Hosidius mess. It is used in creating servery meat pie.
13401: Servery pie shell is obtained from using a servery pastry dough on a servery dish. It is then used on a servery cooked meat to create a servery uncooked pie.
13403: Servery meat pie is obtained from cooking a servery uncooked pie in the Hosidius mess. It is then served at the buffet table for the Shayzien soldiers. A Cooking level of 20 is required to make this meat pie.
13404: Servery pizza base is obtained from using a bowl of water on servery flour. It is then used on a servery tomato to create a servery incomplete pizza.
13406:
Servery incomplete pizzas are obtained by using servery tomato on a servery pizza base. It is used in creating servery pineapple pizza, which is served to Shayzien

soldiers in the Hosidius mess.
13407: Servery cheese is obtained from the food cupboard in the Hosidius mess. It is used in creating servery pineapple pizza.
13409: Servery plain pizza is obtained by cooking a servery incomplete pizza in a clay oven in the Hosidius mess. It is then used on servery pineapple chunks to create servery pineapple pizza, which is served at the buffet table for the Shayzien soldiers.
13410: Servery pineapple are obtained from the food cupboard in the Hosidius mess. It is used on a knife to create servery pineapple chunks.
13411: Servery pineapple chunks is obtained from using a knife on a servery pineapple. It is then used on a servery plain pizza to create a servery pineapple pizza.
13412: Servery pineapple pizza is obtained from using servery pineapple chunks on a servery plain pizza. It is then served at the buffet table for the Shayzien soldiers in the Hosidius mess. A Cooking level of 65 is required to make this pizza. This item cannot be banked.
13413:
Servery cooked meat is obtained by cooking servery raw meat in the Hosidius mess, granting 1 Cooking experience. It is used in creating servery stew and servery meat pie.

If you try to eat the servery cooked meat, Ewesey will tell you that it is not for you.
13414: Servery potato is obtained from the food cupboard in the Hosidius mess. It is used in creating servery stew.
13415: Servery incomplete stew is obtained by using either a servery cooked meat or servery potato on a bowl of water. It is used in creating servery stew, which is served to Shayzien soldiers in the Hosidius mess.

13419:
Sulphurous fertiliser can be made at level 36 Farming by combining saltpetre with regular compost. It can be used on grape vines in the Vinery to increase the yield of grapes and Zamorak's grapes by 20%.

Sulphurous fertiliser was originally used in the Kourend Favour system, where players could hand it into the Clerk in the centre of the saltpetre mine at a rate of 0.1% Hosidius favour per bucket.
13420:
Gricoller's fertiliser is an item only available within the Tithe Farm minigame.

It is automatically added to your inventory at the start of the minigame granted the player has enough space.

After being used on a planted seed, it will decrease the time it takes for the seed to grow by half.

Gricoller's fertiliser can be useful at the end of a Tithe Farm session when only a small number of fruit are needed to hit the bonus points at the 100 fruit threshold; the fertiliser will help speed up the last growth periods of the smaller batches of plants.
13424:
Bologano seeds are used to grow bologano fruit in the Tithe Farm minigame. At least level 54 in the Farming skill is required to use the seeds.

Upon leaving the minigame area through the farm door, all seeds in a player's inventory will disappear.

No experience is granted for planting the seeds. The player will receive 14 experience upon harvesting the fruit and 140 experience for depositing it into the sacks, or 14.3 and 143.5 experience respectively with the complete farmer's outfit. The player will also receive a bonus of 3,500 experience should they return 75 fruit or more at a time. This experience bonus is not boosted by the farmer's oufit. Additionally, the 75th through 100th fruit deposited will grant double experience. Up to 10,000 seeds can be obtained from the table by the entrance of the minigame.

The total experience earned from harvesting and depositing a full batch of seeds (100 fruits) is 22,540. Wearing the full farmer's outfit will boost the experience from harvesting and depositing fruit (but not the experience bonus) by 2.5%, bringing the total experience per 100 fruits to 23,011.

Leaving the Tithe Farm minigame, either through the door, teleporting, or any other means, will remove any harvested fruit from the players inventory, and reward 0 xp. However, the player can safely log out without losing any harvested fruit or seeds, as the player will be placed inside the minigame when logged back in.

13430:
A bucket of sandworms is obtained by digging sandworm castings north of Tynan's Fishing Supplies, granting 10 experience in Hunter. While digging sandworm castings, players may fail to find any sandworms, resulting in a bucket of sand instead.

In order to obtain buckets of sandworms, players require at least level 15 Hunter while carrying a spade and empty bucket. There is a 59-70% chance of obtaining a bucket of sandworm, depending on the player's Hunter level.

Each bucket holds between 1 and 5 sandworms as anglerfish bait.
13446:
A dark essence block is an item created by using dense essence blocks on the Dark Altar located in the northern area of Arceuus. Dense essence blocks are mined nearby using a chisel and a pickaxe.

Each dark essence block created gives 2.5 Runecraft experience while draining 1 prayer point. They can still be made without any prayer points remaining.

Dark essence blocks are used in the creation of Arceuus spellbook teleport tablets (instead of soft clay) at the lectern located in the Ouditor's house in Arceuus whilst being on the Arceuus spellbook.

Dark essence blocks can also be used with a chisel to create 4 dark essence fragments per block, which are runecrafted into blood runes and soul runes. When crafting blood runes, each dark essence block is worth 97.7 experience, including the 2.5 experience gained when imbuing the block at the dark altar. This increases to 121.3 when crafting soul runes.

Dark essence blocks disappear upon death.
13447:

Ensouled heads can be reanimated anywhere as long as the head is on the ground within the 31x31 area centred on its initial drop location and has not been put into the bank, trade screen, Grand Exchange, or price checker. Otherwise, it must be taken to the Dark Altar in Arceuus to be reanimated.

Killing the reanimated goblin gives 130 Prayer experience.

13570:
Juniper charcoal is made on the southern beach of Hosidius, shown on the map as Charcoal burners. To make juniper charcoal, mature juniper trees (located north of the charcoal burners) must be cut for juniper logs to add to one of the charcoal furnaces (maximum 60 per furnace), which are then lit with a tinderbox. Smoggy must be paid 600 coins (per furnace) to watch over the process for you. After 16 hours and 30 minutes, 50 juniper charcoal per log added can be collected from furnace, producing up to 3,000 juniper charcoal per furnace.

Juniper charcoal is one of the ingredients needed to make dynamite; the others being volcanic sulphur, saltpetre, a pot, and a ball of wool. Dynamite is used in the Blast Mine minigame, requiring level 43 Mining to participate.
13571:
Volcanic sulphur is a mineral that can be mined within the Lovakengj sulphur mine. Volcanic sulphur deposits require level 42 Mining and an equipped breathing filter (such as a gas mask, facemask, or slayer helmet) to mine, and grant 35 Mining experience.

Volcanic sulphur is used along with juniper charcoal, saltpetre, and a pot to create a dynamite pot. Adding a ball of wool to the dynamite pot creates dynamite, which can be used in the Blast Mine at level 43 Mining.

A breathing filter is mandatory to attempt to mine volcanic sulphur; if unequipped, a warning is shown in the chatbox stating that "You'll choke on the fumes if you try to mine without protection." In addition, moving gas clouds within the mine will deal rapid hits of 1-3 damage per tick to unprotected players instead of the usual 1 damage per tick with protection.

It is recommended to mine the volcanic sulphur deposits from the south or from the west to avoid taking excessive damage since the gas clouds cannot damage you when directly south or west of you.

Players can extend their stay at the sulphur deposits if they also wear the Hitpoints Cape and Regen Bracelet, as in combination these provide additional natural healing (+4 hp/min).

The sulphur clouds may be safespotted by luring a spider to the western-most sulphur deposit. This can be done by attacking the spider with auto-retaliate off (casting curse spells or splashing recommended). The safespot setup requires the player to stand on the west square positioned south of the western most deposit with the spider attacking from the east. This safespot works as long as you do not move, step on the spider, or others players walking on you or the spider. Mining using this safespot will not show the mining animation, but you will continue to mine.

One volcanic sulphur piece is used in A Kingdom Divided quest.
13575:
Blasted ore is obtained after detonating a hard rock face in the blast mine. Players must first excavate the hard rock using a chisel, then using a pot of dynamite on the resulting cavity. Then, players must light the dynamite and run away from it, or large amounts of damage will be taken.

Once the dynamite explodes, blasted ore will appear where the dynamite exploded. It should then be deposited in an ore sack near a blonde-haired operator. Players have three minutes before the blasted ore disintegrates, so it is encouraged to deposit the ore frequently.

Should the player pick up but not deposit the blasted ore in the Ore sack in time, the blasted ore will disappear from the inventory and a message will appear in the chat interface "Your blasted ore has disintegrated." Hopping worlds will also cause all blasted ore to disintegrate.

If a temporary boost is to be applied when blast mining, they must be activated before the blasted ore is initially spawned.

Like pay-dirt, blasted ore cannot be deposited in a bank.
13576:
The dragon warhammer is a warhammer that requires 60 Strength to wield and is currently one of the strongest warhammers available (second only to the Statius Warhammer) in Old School RuneScape. It is obtained as an extremely rare drop from Lizardman shamans.

The dragon warhammer can be used as a substitute for a regular hammer when banging the big door at the entrance of Bandos' Stronghold in the God Wars Dungeon, as well as in the Chambers of Xeric to stun Jewelled Crabs and build any storage chest (with the required mallignum root planks and Construction level). It can also be used in the Tombs of Amascut to repair the pillars in the monkey puzzle of the Path of Apmeken.

The dragon warhammer is popular for its special attack, as it can drastically reduce the opponent's defence and make them an easier target. Additionally, it is a popular weapon among strength pures due to the lack of an Attack requirement and considerable damage output.

As with most dragon equipment, the dragon warhammer cannot be made from raw materials using the Smithing skill.

The Nest box (seeds) is an item formerly obtained from Wyson the gardener in Falador Park. It could be obtained from trading in noted mole claws or mole skins. When opened, it would provide a Wyson bird nest. They were added in 2016 with an update that improved the quality of the seeds from Wyson's nests.

In an update on 17 January 2019, Wyson's nests were updated again to include the new seeds released with the Kebos Lowlands. Therefore, he now gave out new nest boxes which contained different bird nests. However, the original nest boxes remain in the game, making them a rare example of a discontinued item in Old School RuneScape.
13656:
The present was an item used during the 3rd birthday event. It was given to the player by Sir Tiffy Cashien, who assumes they were the courier he summoned. The present was intended for his grandson, Ebel Lum, whom the player was supposed to deliver to, but it was brought to the gnome child in Lumbridge instead. Attempting to open it before speaking to the gnome child resulted in the message This isn't for me to open!

The present contained a gnome child hat. Players who did not participate in the previous birthday events would have also received the cow outfit and a war ship.
13657:
Grape seeds can be planted in a vine patch at the Hosidius Vinery at level 36 Farming in order to grow a grape vine, which will yield grapes. Grape seeds can be obtained from the Tithe Farm for 2 points per seed.

Players will need to use saltpetre on the patches with a gardening trowel in order to treat the soil before planting the grape seeds. Afterwards, Gallow will watch over your grapes for free. Sulphorous fertilizer can be used on the patches to increase the yield by 20%.

Once fully grown, players can check the grape vine's health for 625 Farming experience and can harvest the grapes (or Zamorak's grapes if players have a sufficient amount of Bologa's blessings in their inventory). The amount of grapes harvested from a fully grown grape vine is random, much like harvesting herbs, but has a minimum number of five grapes per seed (five harvest lives). Players with higher Farming levels can expect substantially more grapes from each vine. After all the grapes have been harvested, the grape vine will die and players will have to clear the farming patch with a spade.
13660:
The Chronicle is an equipable book that can be used to teleport the player to just outside the Champions' Guild, making it useful for players who plant seeds in bush and hops patches as well as free-to-play ironmen. The teleport is also a short distance from Charlie the Tramp, making it useful for those doing beginner clues.

During the 2016 Easter event, players were able to acquire it for free by defeating the Chocolate Chicken during the event. It can now be purchased from Diango's Toy Store for 300 coins. If the player has a copy of the Chronicle in the inventory or bank, trying to buy another one from Diango will fail, and the user will receive the following message: "You've already got one of those." However, it is possible to own more than one Chronicle if buying them from Perdu.

In order to use the Chronicle, it must be charged with teleport cards. Players can purchase them from Diango's Toy Store at a base price of 150 coins each. The book can hold a maximum of 1,000 charges, with one being used each time the Chronicle is used to teleport. Upon death, when not an item kept on death, it is destroyed. If the Chronicle is lost or destroyed, it retains its charges if bought back.

The Chronicle's powers do not work in the Wilderness.

A bag full of gems is a bag that contains an assortment of 40 noted uncut gems. These bags are obtainable from Prospector Percy's Nugget Shop for 40 golden nuggets, from Belona's Mining Guild Mineral Exchange for 20 unidentified minerals, or from Dusuri's Star Shop for 300 stardust.

The chances of an individual gem being an uncut onyx is 1/100,000,000, making the chance per bag approximately 1/2,500,000. In terms of probability, this makes it one of the rarest drops in the game.

Obtaining the uncut onyx from a bag full of gems does produce an entry in the Collection Log.

The bags are exclusive to the stores they are bought from and therefore cannot be sold to another store in exchange for a different currency.
19476:
The achievement diary cape can be obtained by players who have completed all Achievement Diaries. It can be purchased along with its hood for 99,000 coins, from Twiggy O'Korn in Draynor Village. The cape becomes trimmed after completion of all quests, as do the quest cape and music cape after completing all diaries. The cape is notable for providing teleports to all diary masters, and offering a close bank teleport, and options that are useful for optimal Runecrafting and Farming runs.

If a new quest is released, the cape will untrim itself, and will not be able to be re-trimmed until the player completes it. Unlike skillcapes, the achievement diary cape can be trimmed and untrimmed at will, provided that the player meets the requirements. The cape provides a +4 prayer bonus, regardless of whether or not it is trimmed. Untrimmed skill capes will not be trimmed from trimming the achievement diary cape. Obtaining the music cape is not necessary to trim the diary cape.

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room, as part of the achievement diary cape set, along with the hood. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
19478:
The light ballista is a two-handed crossbow that uses javelins as ammunition, requiring level 65 in Ranged to wield.

It is created by using ballista limbs on a light frame, then using the resulting incomplete light ballista on a ballista spring, and finally adding a monkey tail on an unstrung light ballista. This process requires 47 Fletching and grants 330 experience.

Despite being classified as a crossbow, it cannot be used with a mith grapple to grapple across certain Agility shortcuts.
19481:
The heavy ballista is a two-handed crossbow that uses javelins as ammunition, requiring level 75 in Ranged and the completion of the quest Monkey Madness II to wield. Players must also accept both Duke and Daero's training in order to make use of it, unlike the light ballista. Attempting to equip the ballista without these requirements results in the message You must have completed Monkey Madness II and the advanced combat training from Duke to be able to wield this weapon.. While there is no direct Defence requirement for the heavy ballista, completing the required training from Daero after Monkey Madness I will provide a minimum of 20,000 Defence experience. This corresponds to an effective level requirement of 33 Defence.

It is created by using ballista limbs on a heavy frame, then using the resulting incomplete heavy ballista on a ballista spring, and finally adding the monkey tail on an unstrung heavy ballista. The entire process requires 72 Fletching and grants 660 experience.

The speed on accurate is one tick slower than a godsword (7 ticks), but when put on rapid it matches the speed of a godsword (6 ticks). The ballista has an attack range of 9. Longrange increases attack range by 1.

Players may combine a heavy ballista with a heavy ballista ornament kit to create a heavy ballista (or).

Despite being classified as a crossbow, it cannot be used with a mith grapple to grapple across certain agility shortcuts.

Ava's device picks up fired javelins.

Zenyte is the highest tier of gem in Old School RuneScape. Zenyte shards are dropped by tortured or demonic gorillas, then are combined with a cut onyx to produce an uncut zenyte, which can be cut to form a zenyte.

Cutting an uncut zenyte with a chisel requires level 89 Crafting and yields 50 experience. It can then be made into zenyte jewellery by using a furnace along with a gold bar and a mould.

Zenyte jewellery can be enchanted to make some of the most powerful jewellery in the game. Wearing any piece of enchanted zenyte jewellery requires level 75 Hitpoints.

Unlike other gems, zenytes do not appear to form naturally, but rather seem to have been created in some part due to Glough's mutagen being corrupted by reversing the flow of energy from the charged onyx.
19496:
An uncut zenyte is the highest tier of gem in Old School RuneScape. It can be made by combining a cut onyx with a zenyte shard at the wall of flame beneath the Temple of Marimbo on Ape Atoll, while wearing a zombie monkey greegree (small or big). This requires completion of Monkey Madness II and level 70 Crafting, and grants 15 experience. It can then be cut with level 89 Crafting into zenyte, granting 50 experience.

Cut zenyte is used to make enchanted zenyte jewellery, which are some of the most powerful in the game. These are amulet of torture, necklace of anguish, ring of suffering, and tormented bracelet.
19501:
A zenyte amulet (u) is the unstrung version of the regular zenyte amulet. It is made by using a gold bar on a furnace, while having a cut zenyte and an amulet mould in the inventory.

Level 98 Crafting is required to make one, and grants 200 experience. When used with a ball of wool, it becomes a zenyte amulet, giving an additional 4 experience. After the strung amulet is enchanted via the Lvl-7 Enchant spell, it becomes an amulet of torture, which requires level 93 Magic and yields 110 experience.
19505: The mysterious note is an item obtained during Monkey Madness II. Players will find it by searching the fire remains on the 2nd floor of Glough's house. The note contains a message written in invisible ink. After the message is decoded it becomes the scrawled note.

19529:
The zenyte shard is a rare drop received from tortured and demonic gorillas in the Crash Site Cavern, which can be accessed after completion of Monkey Madness II.

In order to create an uncut zenyte, the shard must be fused with a cut onyx in the wall of flames of the Temple of Marimbo Dungeon while holding a zombie monkey greegree (either variant). Doing so grants 15 crafting experience and gives the message: You reach into the extremely hot flames and fuse the zenyte and onyx together, forming an uncut zenyte.

Using a zenyte shard on a cut onyx gives the message: Only the intense heat of the flame pits beneath Ape Atoll can fuse the zenyte and onyx together.
19532:

19541:

This requires a Crafting level of 98 and provides 200 Crafting experience when made.

Players can cast Lvl-7 Enchant on a zenyte amulet to enchant it into an amulet of torture. This requires level 93 Magic and grants 110 Magic experience.
19544:
The tormented bracelet is an enchanted zenyte bracelet that requires a Hitpoints of 75 to equip. It is the second best magic item worn in the hand slot, behind the confliction gauntlets, providing the second greatest magic attack bonus, as well as a 5% bonus to magical damage. This effect stacks with other boosts.

Players can make a tormented bracelet by enchanting a zenyte bracelet with the Lvl-7 Enchant spell. This requires level 93 Magic, 20 soul runes, 20 blood runes, and 1 cosmic rune, and grants 110 Magic experience.

Players can attach a tormented ornament kit, obtained from master Treasure Trails, to create a tormented bracelet (or). This is only cosmetic, and does not affect the bracelet's stat bonuses. It can be dismantled, returning the bracelet and ornament kit.

A tormented bracelet can be combined with a Mokhaiotl cloth and 10,000 demon tears to create the confliction gauntlets, requiring 83 Crafting and 70 Smithing. This process is irreversible.
19550:
The ring of suffering is an enchanted zenyte ring, requiring a Hitpoints level of 75 to be equipped. It is the best-in-slot all-around defensive ring, only beaten by its imbued variant, the steel ring for melee defence, and the granite ring for ranged defence. This ring can be imbued into a ring of suffering (i) using 725,000 Nightmare Zone reward points, 300 Zeal Tokens from Soul Wars, or a scroll of imbuing (which can be purchased for 200 Emir's Arena reward points). With completion of the hard tier of Combat Achievements, these costs are halved to 362,500 Nightmare Zone reward points and 150 Zeal Tokens from Soul Wars. A ring of suffering (i) has double the bonuses of a non-imbued ring.

Players can make one by enchanting a zenyte ring with the Lvl-7 Enchant spell. This requires level 93 Magic, 20 soul runes, 20 blood runes, and 1 cosmic rune and grants 110 Magic experience.

The ring can also be charged with noted and unnoted rings of recoil to give it the recoil effect, renaming the item to ring of suffering (r). Each ring of recoil provides 40 charges. A maximum of 100,000 charges can be stored, equivalent to 2,500 rings and costing 2,350,000. Players can configure the charges while the ring is in their bank by right-clicking on Configure-Charges, as long as players have the required materials. Note that if the ring is discharged, the rings stored will not be refunded. The ring of recoil effect is toggle-able, so players may disable it as to not waste it during training and instead use it in activities such as fighting Zulrah and in PvP combat, where the effect may prove more useful. Charges are not lost upon death. While charged, the ring is untradeable.
19553:
The amulet of torture is an enchanted zenyte amulet requiring level 75 Hitpoints to equip. It is made by enchanting a zenyte amulet with the Lvl-7 Enchant spell, which requires level 93 Magic and grants 110 Magic experience.

As a purely offensive amulet, it gives the second highest melee attack and strength bonuses of any neck slot item, outclassed only by the amulet of rancour, where the amulet of torture is used in its creation.

Players can attach a torture ornament kit, obtained from master clue scrolls, to create an amulet of torture (or). This is purely cosmetic, and does not affect the amulet's stat bonuses. It can be dismantled, returning the amulet and ornament kit.
19556:
Monkey is an item obtainable after the completion of Monkey Madness II. Players can get this item by searching the westernmost crate at the Crash Site Cavern entrance. Upon doing so, a dialogue box will appear in chat stating, "There's a sweet little monkey hiding in the warm crate. You gently pick it up."

Players are able to release the monkey via right-click, prompting a dialogue box to appear stating, "The monkey scampers back to the warmth of its crate." If players wish to retrieve the monkey again, they will have to search the crate back at the Crash Site Cavern entrance. Because the monkey is classed as an item rather than a pet, it cannot be stored in the menagerie of a player-owned house.

Players are also able to transform the monkey via right-click into several other variants upon completing a number of laps at the Ape Atoll Agility Course. Note that laps are only tracked upon completion of Monkey Madness II.

If the player owns an untransformed monkey and searches the crate again, the chatbox will state, "The crate is empty." However, if the player has transformed their monkey into any other variant, they will be able to grab more monkeys and transform them into all of the other variants.
19558:
Nieve (pronounced NEEV) is the third-to-highest level Slayer master, behind Duradel. She is located in the Tree Gnome Stronghold, next to the Stronghold Slayer Cave near the magic trees and the southern bank. She only assigns tasks to players with a combat level of at least 85.

Nieve wields a Zamorakian hasta, full Bandos armour, an amulet of fury, a pirate's hook, an elysian spirit shield, and a fire cape. She made an appearance with a cave kraken in Prifddinas during Old School RuneScape's first birthday event along with other NPCs.

After completion of Monkey Madness II, she is replaced by Steve.

Blocking a task with this slayer master costs 90 Slayer reward points.
19559:
The elysian spirit shield is an item which can be retrieved from Nieve's remains during Monkey Madness II after Glough becomes mutated. The shield disintegrated as a result of Glough's devastating attack on the Slayer master.

It serves as a joke item, as the real shield is widely coveted among high level players. There are no uses for the ruined shield, and it cannot be deposited into a bank. The ruined shield is always lost on death.
19560: A charged onyx is an item obtained from a device in Glough's laboratory during Monkey Madness II. It is used with a chisel to create a deconstructed onyx, reversing the energy flow from the device and corrupting Glough's mutagen.
19562: A deconstructed onyx is an item obtained during Monkey Madness II by using a charged onyx on a chisel. It is to be placed into the device at the northern end of the laboratory, reversing the energy flow from the device and corrupting Glough's mutagen.
19564:
The royal seed pod is rewarded to the player by King Narnode Shareen after completing Monkey Madness II. Like the grand seed pod, this item can be used to teleport the player to the Grand Tree. Unlike the grand seed pod, the royal seed pod is not consumed upon use and never runs out of charges. When successfully teleporting with the royal seed pod, the message The Royal seed pod teleports you to the Grand Tree. will be displayed.

Unlike most teleports, which stop working above level 20 Wilderness, the royal seed pod is among the few items whose teleports can still be used up to level 30 Wilderness; as an easily replaceable item with a one-click teleport, many players prefer the royal seed pod for emergency escape. A 3-tick teleport delay is applied in the Revenant Caves and Wilderness boss lairs before completion of the Wilderness hard diary.

Additional pods may be purchased from King Narnode Shareen for 2 coins each.
19569: A combat damaged key is a key obtained from the closed chest found in the tank route of the Monkey Madness II maze dungeon under Ape Atoll. This key can only be obtained by players who must follow the inner route. Players who follow the outer (southern) route will instead obtain a combat scratched key. These two keys are the tank route's counterpart to the agility route's bronze key.
19570: Bronze javelin tips are items that can be made at level 6 Smithing, granting 5 javelin tips and 12.5 experience per bronze bar. They can be fletched into bronze javelins at level 3 Fletching when used with javelin shafts, which are made by using regular logs with a knife, granting 15 experience per 15 javelins made.
19572: Iron javelin tips are items that can be made at level 21 Smithing, granting 5 javelin tips and 25 experience per iron bar. They can be fletched into iron javelins at level 17 Fletching when used with javelin shafts, which are made by using regular logs with a knife, granting 30 experience per 15 javelins made.
19574: Steel javelin tips are items that can be made at level 36 Smithing, granting 5 javelin tips and 37.5 experience per steel bar. They can be fletched into steel javelins at level 32 Fletching when used with javelin shafts, which are made by using regular logs with a knife, granting 75 experience per 15 javelins made.
19580:
Rune javelin tips are items that can be made at level 91 Smithing, granting 5 javelin tips and 75 experience per runite bar. They can be fletched into rune javelins at level 77 Fletching when used with javelin shafts, which are made by using regular logs with a knife, granting 187.5 experience per 15 javelins made. However, fletching javelins decreases the resale and alchemy values significantly.

As a standalone item, rune javelin tips are a profitable way to use high alchemy due to their low cost on the Grand Exchange, which easily offsets the price of Nature runes when converting them into coins.
19582:
Dragon javelin tips are attached to javelin shafts to make dragon javelins, requiring 92 Fletching, and yielding 225 Fletching experience per 15 javelins made.

In order to obtain them as a drop from most sources (e.g dragons and dragon implings), players must have completed Monkey Madness II, or they will not be dropped at all. The only exceptions to this rule are Scorpia and the Desert Treasure II bosses.

As with most dragon equipment, dragon javelin tips cannot be made from raw materials using the Smithing skill.
19586:
A light frame is a rare drop from demonic gorillas and tortured gorillas, which can be fought after the Monkey Madness II quest in the Crash Site Cavern.

They are a component in creating light ballistae. They must be attached to ballista limbs to create an incomplete light ballista. Doing so requires level 47 in Fletching, granting 15 experience in the process.
19589:
A heavy frame is a rare drop from demonic gorillas and tortured gorillas, which can be fought after the Monkey Madness II quest in the Crash Site Cavern.

They are a component in creating heavy ballista. They must be attached to ballista limbs to create an incomplete heavy ballista. Doing so requires level 72 in fletching, granting 30 experience in the process.
19595: The incomplete light ballista is an item obtained by attaching ballista limbs to a light frame with a Fletching level of 47, granting 15 experience in the process. It is then attached with a ballista spring to create an unstrung light ballista, granting an additional 15 experience.
19598: The incomplete heavy ballista is an item obtained by attaching ballista limbs to a heavy frame with a Fletching level of 72, granting 30 experience in the process. It is then attached with a ballista spring to create an unstrung heavy ballista, granting an additional 30 experience.
19604: An unstrung light ballista is made by using a ballista spring with incomplete light ballista, requiring 47 Fletching, and yielding 15 Fletching experience. Attaching a monkey tail to it makes a light ballista, requiring 47 Fletching, and yielding 300 Fletching experience.
19607: An unstrung heavy ballista is made by using a ballista spring with incomplete heavy ballista, requiring 72 Fletching and yielding 30 Fletching experience. Attaching a monkey tail to it makes a heavy ballista, requiring 72 Fletching and yielding 600 Fletching experience.
19610:
Monkey tails are used to create heavy and light ballistae. They are dropped by demonic gorillas and tortured gorillas in the Crash Site Cavern. They can also be received as a very rare drop (1 in 5,000) from hunting maniacal monkeys with a deadfall trap in Kruk's Dungeon, prompting the message You've caught a monkey's tail. Other than the missing monkey, it's in perfect condition!

Monkey tails can be attached to an unstrung light ballista to create a light ballista, requiring 47 Fletching and granting 300 experience.

Monkey tails can be attached to an unstrung heavy ballista to create a heavy ballista, requiring 72 Fletching and granting 600 experience.
19617:
The Mind altar teleport is a magic tablet that can be broken by players to teleport to the entrance of the Mind Altar.

Players can create this item on the Arceuus lectern in the Ouditor's house with 1 law rune, 2 mind runes, and level 28 Magic while being on the Arceuus spellbook. In addition, a dark essence block is required to substitute soft clay.

The player does not need to have the relevant Magic level to use the tablet, which shares the same rule with all tablets and the player will not receive any experience, although making the teleport tablet does give 22 experience in Magic.
19629:
The Barrows teleport is a magic tablet that can be broken by players to teleport to the Barrows. To use this tablet, the user must have completed the Priest in Peril quest and must have passed through the barrier to Morytania at least once.

Players with 83 Magic and the Arceuus spellbook active can create this item on the Arceuus lectern in the Ouditor's house with 2 law runes, 2 soul runes, 1 blood rune, and a dark essence block (instead of the soft clay required for standard spellbook magic tablets). Making this tablet grants 90 Magic experience, the same as if casting the spell.

As with all magic tablets, there is no Magic level requirement to use this tablet, and no Magic experience is granted for using it.

Making a Barrows tablet is one of the challenges assigned by Sherlock for a master clue step.
19631:
The Ape atoll teleport is a magic tablet that can be broken by players to teleport to the Ape Atoll Dungeon. Completion of Monkey Madness I is required to use this tablet. Neither the post-quest 10th squad training from Daero nor Freeing King Awowogei Recipe for Disaster subquest need to be completed.

Players with level 90 Magic can create this item on the Arceuus lectern in the Ouditor's house if they have the Arceuus spellbook enabled. This requires 2 law runes, 2 soul runes, 2 blood runes, and a dark essence block instead of the soft clay required for most magic tablets. Making the tablet grants 100 Magic experience, the same as casting the Ape Atoll Teleport spell. It is not required to have Monkey Madness I completed in order to make a tablet.

As with all magic tablets, the player does not need to have the relevant Magic level to use the tablet, but using the tablet does not grant the player any experience.

Creating an Ape Atoll teleport tablet is a task for the elite Kourend & Kebos Diary.
19634:
The soul bearer is an item that sends all of the ensouled heads from their inventory to the player's bank. To use the soul bearer, the player must pick up the ensouled head(s) and select the 'Fill' option on the Soul Bearer. It is obtained from the Bear Your Soul miniquest after the Key Master repairs the damaged soul bearer.

The soul bearer is an ancient artefact that draws souls from one place to another, enabling them to travel within the River of Souls across the dimensions.

Each ensouled head costs one charge. Charging the soul bearer costs one blood rune and one soul rune per charge (738). Players can configure the charges while the soul bearer is in their bank by right-clicking on Configure-Charges, as long as players have the required materials. The soul bearer can hold 1,000 charges (738,000) and charges can be removed at any time by using the Uncharge right-click option.

If a player loses the soul bearer, they can acquire another one by using a spade to dig in the Arceuus church crypt again.

Ultimate ironmen cannot use the soul bearer.
19637:
Soul Journey is a book written by Aretha. It can be found in the Grand Library in Arceuus. Professor Gracklebone, Sam, and Villia may ask the player to find this book for them, in which their location is random and changes every 80-100 minutes. Upon handing in the book to the player's customer, a book of arcane knowledge is rewarded.

Players cannot perform a drop trick to obtain more books, as they will disappear once dropped; this is done to prevent the player from obtaining multiple copies in order to gain experience books quicker by having the book readily available after a customer asks for it.

The book speaks about the River of Souls and its role in Great Kourend's perception of the afterlife, along with excerpts from past experiences involving the Key Master's acceptance in the role of guarding Cerberus. It also mentions the soul bearer, an ancient artefact.

After reading the book for the first time, the chatbox will state The book referred to an artefact being buried in Kourend, but the author did not specify where it was buried. Maybe you could persuade her to change her mind. This begins the Bear Your Soul miniquest.
19639:
The black Slayer helmet is a piece of equipment that is worn in the helmet slot. It is a cosmetic upgrade to the Slayer helmet.

It can be created by adding an unstuffed Kbd heads after purchasing the ability King black bonnet for 1,000 Slayer reward points from any Slayer master. This is reversible, and the head will be returned to the inventory along with the slayer helmet's components. If a player loses the black slayer helmet in a PvP death, the Kbd heads will be placed in their gravestone.
19641:
The black Slayer helmet (i) is a piece of equipment that is worn in the helmet slot. It is a cosmetic upgrade to the Slayer helmet (i).

It can be created by adding an unstuffed Kbd heads after purchasing the ability King black bonnet for 1,000 Slayer reward points from any Slayer master. This is reversable, and the head will be returned to the inventory along with the slayer helmet's components. If a player loses the black slayer helmet (i) in a PvP death, the Kbd heads will be placed in their gravestone.
19651: The Hosidius teleport is a magic tablet that can be broken by players to teleport just outside the Hosidius house portal. It can be created at level 25 Construction by using a scroll of redirection on a teleport to house tablet.
19656: An uncooked botanical pie is made by adding a Golovanova fruit top to a Pie shell. It can be baked with level 52 Cooking to make a botanical pie, granting 180 Cooking experience when successfully baked.
19659:
Botanical pie is a type of pie that restores 14 Hitpoints in total, 2 bites each healing for 7. It also temporarily boosts Herblore by 4, the second highest boost available, and the highest reliable boost. A pie dish will remain after both bites are consumed.

It can be created by baking an uncooked botanical pie on a cooking range, requiring level 52 Cooking and granting 180 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt pie. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Botanical pie is one of a number of foods with a reduced burn rate while using the Lumbridge Castle range with Cook's Assistant completed. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 84, or 52 when using the Lumbridge range. Alternatively, casting the Bake Pie spell from the lunar spellbook will always create a pie without burning it.
19662:
Botanical pie is a type of pie that restores 14 Hitpoints in total, 2 bites each healing for 7. It also temporarily boosts Herblore by 4, the second highest boost available, and the highest reliable boost. A pie dish will remain after both bites are consumed.

It can be created by baking an uncooked botanical pie on a cooking range, requiring level 52 Cooking and granting 180 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt pie. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Botanical pie is one of a number of foods with a reduced burn rate while using the Lumbridge Castle range with Cook's Assistant completed. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 84, or 52 when using the Lumbridge range. Alternatively, casting the Bake Pie spell from the lunar spellbook will always create a pie without burning it.
19668:
Minecart control scrolls were instructions given to the player by Miriam. They were used to set up the Lovakengj Minecart Network. They were given to Loinur, Mogrim, Traxi, Raeli, and Stuliette to complete the network. The scrolls were removed on 10 January 2024 after an update removing any requirements to use the Lovakengj Minecart Network.

Players could use the Check option to find out the locations of the NPCs.
19675:
Arclight is a demonbane weapon requiring level 75 Attack to wield. An upgraded variant of Darklight, Arclight features an enhanced passive effect in addition to modest improvements in attack bonus and speed.

If Arclight is lost, it can be replaced by paying Sir Prysin 1,000 coins for Darklight and enhancing it with ancient shards again. Players can possess multiple copies of Arclight.

After reading Duradel's notes, at level 74 Smithing, players can use either a fully charged or infused Arclight with a tormented synapse to upgrade the weapon to Emberlight.
19677: Ancient shards are obtained from monsters found within the Catacombs of Kourend (excluding ghosts). Three shards can be used with a Darklight at the altar in the centre of the catacombs to create an Arclight, a degradeable variant of the darklight that provides stats superior to the abyssal tentacle when used against demons. Ancient shards are also used to charge Arclight. One shard provides 333 charges, three shards provide 1,000 charges; up to a maximum of 10,000. They are also used on the altar in the centre of the catacombs for quick transportation to several areas (and are consumed on use):
19679:
The dark totem base is an item obtained from monsters found within the Catacombs of Kourend (excluding ghosts). All Superior Slayer monsters encountered in the Catacombs are guaranteed to drop a dark totem piece.

This item can be combined with the dark totem middle and the dark totem top to create the dark totem, which is used to reach Skotizo, a demon that lurks beneath the Catacombs.
19681:
The dark totem middle is an item obtained from monsters found within the Catacombs of Kourend (excluding ghosts). All Superior Slayer monsters encountered in the Catacombs are guaranteed to drop a dark totem piece.

This item can be combined with the dark totem base and the dark totem top to create the dark totem, which is used to reach Skotizo, a demon that lurks beneath the Catacombs.
19683:
The dark totem top is an item obtained from monsters found within the Catacombs of Kourend (excluding ghosts). All Superior Slayer monsters encountered in the Catacombs are guaranteed to drop a dark totem piece.

This item can be combined with the dark totem base and the dark totem middle to create the dark totem, which is used to reach Skotizo, a demon that lurks beneath the Catacombs.
19685:
The dark totem is an item that can be created by combining the dark totem base, dark totem middle, and dark totem top. The totem pieces are dropped in that order and duplicates drop after all three are obtained. It is used on the altar in the centre of the Catacombs of Kourend to access the lower level of the catacombs to fight Skotizo. The totem is consumed when using it on the altar regardless of the outcome of the fight.

All three components can be found by killing monsters (excluding ghosts) in the Catacombs of Kourend and in the Giants' Den. Superior slayer monsters have a 100% chance of dropping a totem piece; all others have a chance equal to 1/(500−H), where H is the monster's Hitpoints. Since the improvement in drop rate as monster HP increases is very small, dark totem pieces can be most quickly obtained by killing low HP monsters within the catacombs, such as hill giants.

Assembling the dark totem results in a chatbox message stating You bring the totem pieces together with a click. It looks kind of like an arcane key and pulses with dark power in your hand.

A fully-assembled dark totem can also be rarely obtained from Skotizo.
19689:
The clue hunter garb is obtained from completing the second clue during the Crack the Clue! event. It is part of the clue hunter outfit. This item has the same stat bonuses as a leather body.

In order to obtain/reobtain the garb, the player must dig at the same downward right diagonal two-rocky area place just north of the Shayzien East station of the Lovakengj Minecart Network, where Mogrim resides.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Clue hunter outfit set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
19691:
Clue hunter gloves are obtained from completing the first clue during the Crack the Clue! event. It is part of the clue hunter outfit. Obtainable only once if you already have it in your inventory or bank. If you happen to accidentally destroy it, you will need to discover it again.

These items are obtained alongside the clue hunter boots.

In order to obtain/reobtain the boots and gloves, the player must dig at an oak tree south-west of the Fishing Guild and just north of East Ardougne.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Clue hunter outfit set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored. This item counts as a warm piece of clothing.
19693:
Clue hunter trousers are obtained from completing the third clue during the Crack the Clue! event. It is part of the clue hunter outfit.

The trousers provide the same bonuses as leather chaps.

In order to obtain/reobtain the trousers, the player must dig near the entrance to the Pothole Dungeon north of Tai Bwo Wannai.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Clue hunter outfit set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
19695:
Clue hunter boots are a part of the clue hunter outfit, obtained by completing the first clue of the Crack the Clue! event. Players may only have one pair in their inventory or bank at a time. If destroyed, players must dig at an oak tree south-west of the Fishing Guild and just north of East Ardougne.

The boots are obtained alongside the clue hunter gloves.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Clue hunter outfit set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
19697:
The clue hunter cloak is a cloak obtained from completing a clue during the Crack the Clue! event. It is part of the clue hunter outfit.

In order to obtain/reobtain the cloak, the player must dig between two willow trees south-east of Yanille.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Clue hunter outfit set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
19699:
The hornwood helm is an item given to the player after completing the midsummer ritual three times during the 2016 Midsummer event, as well as subsequent Midsummer events.

As there was no Midsummer event in 2018, it was made available from Diango's Toy Store for 15 coins.

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room.
19704: A compost pack is an item pack containing 100 regular compost. They can be bought from any farming shop.
19707:
The amulet of eternal glory is a special dragonstone amulet possessing identical stats and features of a regular amulet of glory, except it has unlimited teleport charges instead of the regular four or six maximum charges. However, it cannot be mounted in a player-owned house.

It is made (only after completion of Heroes Quest) while charging amulets of glory (including the trimmed variant) with fewer than six charges at the Fountain of Rune in the Wilderness. Each amulet recharged has a 1 in 25,000 chance to be turned into an amulet of eternal glory. When this occurs, a message in the chatbox will appear, stating: "The power of the fountain is transferred into an amulet of eternal glory. It will now have unlimited charges."

Like other dragonstone jewellery, it is one of the few items whose teleports will work up to level 30 Wilderness, while most other means of teleportation will not work above level 20 Wilderness.

As with the regular charged amulet of glory, it retains the passive effect which increases chance to mine gems and gem rocks.
19710:
The ring of suffering (i) is an upgraded version of the regular ring of suffering. It can be imbued as a reward from the Nightmare Zone, costing 725,000 reward points or 362,500 with the hard tier of Combat Achievements, at Soul Wars for 300 Zeal Tokens, or by using a scroll of imbuing purchased from Emir's Arena for 200 points. Its stats are double those of the ring of suffering.

The ring can also be charged with rings of recoil to give it the recoil effect, renaming the item to ring of suffering (ri). Each ring of recoil provides 40 charges, assuming the ring of recoil has not been drained prior. A maximum of 100,000 charges can be stored, equivalent to 2,500 rings, at a cost of 2,350,000 coins. Players can configure the charges while the ring is in their bank by right-clicking on Configure-Charges, as long as players have the required materials. If a player uncharged the ring, the recoil rings stored will not be refunded. The ring of recoil effect is toggle-able, so players may disable it as to not waste it during training and instead use it in activities such as fighting Zulrah, or in PvP combat, where the effect may prove more useful. Charges are not lost upon death.

If not protected, dying to another player will cause the imbued ring to lose its imbued status, however the player will be reimbursed the Nightmare Zone points, Zeal Tokens or Scroll of imbuing to re-imbue it via the aforementioned methods. Dying to a monster will not remove its imbued effect.
19712:
A clue nest (easy) is randomly obtained from Woodcutting or bird house trapping on Fossil Island if the player has not completed X Marks the Spot, otherwise they will receive a Scroll box (easy) and an empty bird nest will drop to the ground. Searching the nest gives an easy clue scroll and an empty bird nest.

If the player completes X Marks the Spot before opening the clue nest, they will instead receive an easy scroll box.

All clue nests are dropped in addition to logs.

The ring of wealth (i) doubles the rate of clue nest drops above beginner from Woodcutting in the Wilderness.
19720:
The occult necklace (or) is an occult necklace with an occult ornament kit attached to it. The attached ornament kit gives no additional bonuses, and is only used to add aesthetics to the necklace. It costs 3,338,698 for both the parts to make the occult necklace (or).

While the necklace is untradeable in its ornamented state, it can be dismantled anytime, returning the tradeable necklace and ornament kit.

Many players purchase the ornament kit for the purpose of making the item untradeable, thus allowing the player to always keep it on death against NPCs.
19722:
The dragon defender (t) is a dragon defender with a dragon defender ornament kit attached to it. The attached ornament kit gives no additional bonuses, and is only used to add aesthetics to the defender.

The trimmed defender can be dismantled anytime, returning the defender and the tradeable ornament kit.

If the player dies to a PvP death and the dragon defender is not one of the player's protected items, it will remain in the player's inventory, but will become broken, which means the item is unusable and must be repaired with 240,000 coins by using the item on Perdu. The ornament kit will be lost.
19730:
The Bloodhound is a pet that can be received as a rare reward from master Treasure Trails at a rate of 1/1,000. Using a set of bones on the bloodhound will result in the chatbox message You give the dog the bone - it eats it.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, but can be reclaimed from Probita.
19732:
The lucky impling jar is the result of successfully catching a lucky impling via the Hunter skill. This impling has the highest requirement to catch, requiring level 89 Hunter or 99 Hunter if caught barehanded.

The lucky impling is approximately ten times rarer than a dragon impling in Gielinor, and closer to nine times rarer in Puro-Puro.
19736: Clue scroll (medium) is an anagram clue obtained from medium Treasure Trails.
19742: Clue scroll (medium) is an anagram clue obtained from medium Treasure Trails.
19744: Clue scroll (medium) is an anagram clue obtained from medium Treasure Trails.
19746: Clue scroll (medium) is an anagram clue obtained from medium Treasure Trails.
19750: Clue scroll (medium) is an anagram clue obtained from medium Treasure Trails.
19756: Clue scroll (medium) is an anagram clue obtained from medium Treasure Trails.
19758: Clue scroll (medium) is an anagram clue obtained from medium Treasure Trails.
19760: Clue scroll (medium) is a cryptic clue obtained from medium Treasure Trails.
19761:
A key is an item needed to unlock a chest or drawer during a Treasure Trail.

There will be a clue telling you where to get it. The key is a drop only when carrying the clue scroll. It disappears when used to open the chest or drawer. Keys are non-tradeable objects, specific to the player who finds them. They are used on all levels of treasure trails.

It is possible to obtain more than one key using the drop trick. However, after taking a clue from the chest/drawer, the key won't open it again, and the player gets a message: "The chest (or drawer) is locked." Keys obtained this way from the same clue will still remain in the bank; however, keys obtained from different clues will not stack.

The gnomish firelighter is an item obtainable by completing medium Treasure Trails. It may be charged with any one colour of gnomish firelighters at a time. Like other firelighters, it also increases the chance of a log to be successfully burned, additionally giving an extra 10 Firemaking experience per log when charged.

The maximum number of charges is 1,000.

While charged, it can be used with any set of standard logs in the same manner as one would use a tinderbox with any other set of logs to produce the same colour of fire as the firelighters it is charged with. One charge is used up for every coloured fire created.

If another colour is desired, one may simply uncharge the firelighter at any time; this will return any unused firelighters and free the device up to be charged with another style of firelighter.

Gnomish firelighters do not function as a tinderbox when out of charges, and only standard logs may be used to create coloured fires.

Despite being a unique Treasure Trails reward, the gnomish firelighter cannot be stored in a POH Treasure Chest.

If the player dies to a PvP death and the bronze defender is not one of the player's protected items, it will remain in the player's inventory, but will become broken, which means the item is unusable and must be repaired with 1,000 coins by using the item on Perdu.

If the player dies to a PvP death and the black defender is not one of the player's protected items, it will remain in the player's inventory, but will become broken, which means the item is unusable and must be repaired with 5,000 coins by using the item on Perdu.

20459:
The adamant defender is a defender made out of adamant. It can be obtained by killing cyclopes on the top floor of the Warriors' Guild with a mithril defender in the inventory or after you have shown a mithril defender to Kamfreena. It is held in the shield slot and requires 30 Attack and Defence to wield.

If the player dies to a PvP death and the adamant defender is not one of the player's protected items, it will remain in the player's inventory, but will become broken, which means the item is unusable and must be repaired with 25,000 coins by using the item on Perdu.
20461:
The rune defender is the 3rd strongest defender. It is used for its attack bonus and is held in the off-hand in place of a shield. It requires 40 Attack and 40 Defence to wield. The rune defender is dropped by cyclopes on the top floor of the Warriors' Guild after showing an adamant defender or better as the player enters the room.

The rune defender's slash and crush defensive bonuses are the same as a black kiteshield, but its stab defence bonus is slightly less than an adamant square shield. However, it is much more commonly used for its melee bonuses, as it gives the same bonus to strength as the toktz-ket-xil (obsidian shield) and has melee attack bonuses. A rune defender is commonly combined with weapons such as a dragon scimitar or an abyssal whip as a result.

The defender is popular among players of higher combat levels due to its offensive stats. It can be considered to be the third best off-hand item for melee training, only beaten by the dragon defender and Avernic defender, and is commonly used in PvP situations as re-obtaining a rune defender is easier than re-obtaining a dragon or Avernic one.

If the player dies to a PvP death and the rune defender is not one of the player's protected items, it will remain in the player's inventory, but will become broken, which means the item is unusable and must be repaired with 35,000 coins by using the item on Perdu. Any ornament kit on the item will also be lost on death.

Players can attach a Rune defender ornament kit, obtained from hard Treasure Trails, to create a Rune defender (t). This is only cosmetic, and does not affect the defender's stat bonuses. It can be dismantled, returning the defender and ornament kit.

The dragon defender is the second strongest defender, behind the Avernic defender. It is used for its attack and strength bonus and is held in the shield slot. It requires level 60 Defence to equip.

The dragon defender can only be obtained from the stronger level 106 Cyclopes found exclusively in the Warrior Guild's basement. To enter the basement for the first time, a player must show a rune defender to Lorelai, who will then grant them permanent access. Warrior Guild tokens are still required for time spent inside the basement unless the player has an Attack Cape equipped. Players can obtain a dragon defender without having a rune defender in their bank. Players can obtain the dragon defender without having 60 Defence.

Its melee defensive bonuses are comparable to those of an adamant square shield, with slight differences. Its strength bonus is surpassed by both the dragonfire shield and the Avernic defender, which give +7 and +8 strength bonuses, respectively. However, the dragon defender is more commonly used than either of these for melee training, due to its superior melee attack bonuses over the dragonfire shield and the overall rarity of the Avernic defender.

If the player dies to a PvP death and the dragon defender is not one of the player's protected items, it will remain in the player's inventory, but will become broken, which means the item is unusable and must be repaired with 240,000 coins by using the item on Perdu.
20465:
The Void Knight top is a piece of Void Knight equipment. It can be bought from a Void Knight for 250 Void Knight commendation points through the Pest Control mini game, although a player must have at least 42 Attack, Strength, Defence, Hitpoints, Ranged, and Magic, along with 22 Prayer to buy and wear one.

It is worn in combination with the other pieces of Void Knight Armour to achieve the designated set effect, depending on which helm is worn. This chestpiece does not interfere with Ava's devices. Unlike the Void knight robe, the Void knight top doesn't have more Magic Defence than its blessed d'hide counterparts (+45, as opposed to a blessed d'hide body's +50).

It can be upgraded into an Elite void top for 200 Void Knight commendation points, although a player must have completed the hard Western Provinces Diary tasks to be able to upgrade it. The top can also be given to the Dodgy Squire in exchange for 200 Void Knight commendation points.

If the player dies a PvP death at level 20 Wilderness or below and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 180,000 coins.

If the player dies a PvP death above level 20 Wilderness and the item is unprotected, it will be converted to coins. To prevent this, a Trouver parchment and a payment of 500,000 coins can be given to Perdu in order to permanently lock the item. The locked item will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a mangled, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 500,000 coins.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Void Knight armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
