21255:
The slayer's staff (e) is an upgraded version of the slayer's staff, obtained by using a slayer's enchantment on it. It requires 75 Magic and 55 Slayer to wield. It can be used to cast Magic Dart like the normal version of the staff.

Upon enchanting the staff, it becomes untradeable and gains 2,500 charges. Once the charges run out, it will revert to a regular Slayer's staff, and an additional Slayer's enchantment must be used on it.

Using the staff increases the damage dealt by Magic Dart when attacking a Slayer monster the player is assigned to kill. Specifically, the max hit of Magic Dart when using the slayer's staff (e) increases from ⌊MagicLevel×110⌋+10 to ⌊MagicLevel×16⌋+13. This stacks with other magic-damage boosts like the occult necklace, tormented bracelet, and black mask (i)/slayer helmet (i). Each cast of Magic Dart consumes 1 charge from the staff if the spell hits. If the spell does not hit, no charges will be consumed. Charges are also not consumed (and damage is not boosted) when casting Magic Dart on a monster that is not a current Slayer assignment.
21257:
The Slayer's enchantment is a parchment that is used on a Slayer's staff to enchant it into a Slayer's staff (e) with 2,500 charges. Once the charges run out, it reverts to a basic Slayer's staff.

Using the enchantment increases the max hit of Magic Dart whilst using the staff from ⌊MagicLevel×110⌋+10 to ⌊MagicLevel×16⌋+13. The enchanted Slayer's staff requires 75 Magic and 55 Slayer to wield, which is a significant difference from the basic Slayer's staff requirement of level 50 Magic and level 55 Slayer.

It is dropped by monsters in the Wilderness while on a Slayer task given by Krystilia.
21259:
The enchanted scroll is a quest item used only in Client of Kourend. It is obtained from Veos at the start of the quest.

A feather must be used on it to obtain an enchanted quill.

Duplicates can be banked by talking to Veos to obtain another. After giving Veos the scroll and quill, all copies in the bank are deleted. This item cannot leave a placeholder.
21260:
The enchanted quill is a quest item used only in Client of Kourend. It is made by using a feather on an enchanted scroll.

It is to write on the enchanted scroll so the client can see what the player is writing without any visible writing.

Duplicates can be obtained by banking the first one to obtain another. After giving Veos the scroll and quill, all copies in the inventory and bank are deleted. This item cannot leave a placeholder. If a player tries to make another quill while already having one in their inventory, a message will appear saying that "there's no need to make another". If a player tries to use the quill on an enchanted scroll, then a message appears saying that "you can't create another quill... by using the quill on the scroll."
21261:
The mysterious orb is a quest item used only in Client of Kourend. It is obtained from Veos after returning the enchanted scroll and quill to him.

It must be taken to the Dark Altar to be activated. Once the orb is activated near the Dark Altar, it will shatter into broken glass. If a player activates the orb anywhere else, a message appears stating that the orb is unresponsive.

Duplicates can be obtained by banking the first one to obtain another. After completing the quest, all copies in the inventory and bank are deleted.
21262:
Antique lamps are rewards from quests, achievement diaries and the Varrock Museum miniquest. Like regular lamps, these lamps grant a player experience in a chosen skill, and the skill chosen must usually be over a certain level which is unboostable.

Lamps that are not included in the three items kept on death will be kept inside your death's coffer, if not deleted.
21263:
Copper's crimson collar is an item that is obtained by killing foxes, once belonging to Veos' pet wolf, Copper.

It can only be obtained once players offer to help them recover the collar after using wolf bones on Veos, and cannot be deposited into a bank. Multiple can be obtained; however, upon completing the task, duplicates are removed.
21264:
The purple Slayer helmet is a piece of equipment that is worn in the helmet slot. It is a cosmetic upgrade to the Slayer helmet.

It can be created by adding a dark claw after purchasing the ability Dark Mantle for 1,000 Slayer reward points from any Slayer master. This is reversible, and the claw will be returned to the inventory along with the slayer helmet's components. If a player loses the purple slayer helmet in a PvP death, the dark claw will be placed in their gravestone.
21266:
The purple Slayer helmet (i) is a piece of equipment that is worn in the helmet slot. It is a cosmetic upgrade to the Slayer helmet (i).

It can be created by adding a dark claw after purchasing the ability Dark Mantle for 1,000 Slayer reward points from any Slayer master. This is reversible, and the claw will be returned to the inventory along with the slayer helmet's components. If a player loses the purple slayer helmet (i) in a PvP death, the dark claw will be placed in their gravestone.
21270:
The eternal gem is an upgraded version of the enchanted gem, offering unlimited charges when crafted into a slayer ring. It has no additional benefit in its base form. It is dropped by superior slayer monsters, which are rare encounters unlocked after purchasing the unlock Bigger and Badder for 50 Slayer reward points from any Slayer master.

The eternal gem has all the functions of the enchanted gem and thus can be used to contact a Slayer master and keep track of a player's Slayer task.

Players with level 75 Crafting and who have purchased the Ring bling unlock for 150 Slayer reward points can craft this gem into an eternal slayer ring. In order to craft this ring, players must use a gold bar on a furnace with a ring mould and the eternal gem in their inventory, granting 15 Crafting experience. This process is irreversible and the eternal slayer ring is untradeable.

The eternal gem cannot be used to craft a Slayer helmet.
21275:
The dark claw is an uncommon drop from Skotizo. It can be combined with a slayer helmet or slayer helmet (i) to create a purple slayer helmet or purple slayer helmet (i), respectively. Doing so requires purchasing the ability Dark Mantle for 1,000 Slayer reward points.

It can also be combined with a pair of flippers to create dark flippers by speaking to Patchy on Mos Le'Harmless and paying 500 coins.
21279:
Obsidian armour set is an item obtained by exchanging a set of items with a Grand Exchange clerk via their right-click "Sets" option and clicking on the appropriate item set within the Item Sets interface.

It is commonly made in order to conveniently sell all three components of obsidian armour at once.
21282:
The infernal max hood is a hood created by using an infernal cape on a max cape. When the infernal max cape is created, the max hood is required as well and is automatically converted to the infernal max hood.

If players are refunding the infernal max cape via Mac, the player must also have the infernal max hood in their inventory.

Should players lose the hood, they may reclaim it from Mac for free.
21284:
The infernal max cape is the result of combining an infernal cape with a max cape, during which the max hood is required to be in the player's inventory and will automatically be converted to the infernal max hood.

Like the other max cape variants (a max cape combined with another cape slot item), the infernal max cape does not have the max cape's stats or perks; it only acts as a cosmetic upgrade to the infernal cape with the following exceptions when worn:

It acts as a Cooking cape to allow access to the Cooks' Guild without a chef's hat, golden chef's hat, Varrock armour 3 or 4

It acts as a Crafting cape to allow access to the Crafting Guild without a brown apron or golden apron

It acts as a Runecraft cape to prevent essence pouches from degrading (but does not allow access to runic altars)

It acts as a Firemaking cape to work as a piece of warm clothing

It can be used to perform the Skill Cape emote.

It is lighter, weighing 0.453kg instead of 1.814kg

The max cape and infernal cape can be separated by using a knife on the cape. Mac will also buy back a max cape, along with its variants, for 1,900,800 coins each. He will return the secondary item any max cape variant was combined with upon doing so.

If the player dies a PvP death at level 20 Wilderness or below and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 225,000 coins.

If the player dies a PvP death above level 20 Wilderness and the item is unprotected, it will be converted to coins. To prevent this, a Trouver parchment and a payment of 500,000 coins can be given to Perdu in order to permanently lock the item. The locked item will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a mangled, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 500,000 coins.

An infernal max cape cannot be gambled for a chance at Jal-Nib-Rek.

There were approximately 9,463 players who could have an infernal max cape as of 12th March 2022.

21287:

There were approximately 9,463 players who could have an infernal max cape as of 12th March 2022.
21291:
The Jal-Nib-Rek (roughly translated as Foreign Nibbler Baby/Young) is a Jal-Nib dropped by TzKal-Zuk upon completion of the Inferno. The standard drop rate is 1/100, but this is increased to 1/75 if TzKal-Zuk is defeated while on a Slayer task. Players may also exchange their infernal capes by speaking to TzHaar-Ket-Keh for a 1/100 chance of obtaining the pet. Providing a player defeats TzKal-Zuk while on a slayer task for a 1/75 chance of the pet, and hands in their cape, the overall chance of receiving the pet from either the boss or the cape is approximately 1/43.

Players can right click "Metamorphosis" to change between the Jal-Nib and TzRek-Zuk, which is a smaller version of TzKal-Zuk.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.
21293:
Infernal eels are members-only fish that can be caught within the city of Mor Ul Rek. Catching them requires a Fishing level of 80, granting 95 Fishing experience per eel caught. In order to catch infernal eels, an oily fishing rod and bait while wearing ice gloves or Smiths gloves (i) are required. With a hammer, these eels can be cracked open to extract fourteen to twenty Tokkul, one onyx bolt tip, or one to five lava scale shards. Furthermore, there is a relatively high chance of obtaining clue bottles when fishing infernal eels, ranging from approximately 1/917 to 1/829 depending on your fishing level.

Because they are located in the inner city, they can only be caught once a player has proven themselves worthy enough to enter the city by showing a TzHaar guard guarding the entrance a fire cape.

There is an "Eat" option on the eel, which results in the following message in the chatbox: Removing the eel from the lava has caused it to harden. You don't want to test your teeth against one of these.

Upon smashing an infernal eel, there is a 2/35 chance of receiving onyx bolt tips and a 4/35 chance of receiving lava scale shards. Per eel, the average profit is 495.66 coins (not including the average value of ~14.09 Tokkul at 143.77).

When using a hammer on the eels to smash them, the first eel in the inventory will be smashed regardless of which eel the hammer was used on. While this will auto-smash the entire inventory of eels one by one, rapidly using the hammer on the last eel in the inventory will speed up the smashing process immensely. It is even possible to smash multiple eels in a single tick using this method.

When compared to monkfish, no banking is required, and they provide only slightly less experience of up to 35,000/hr. They can provide profit for ironmen through onyx bolt tips when fletched and alched, as well as providing Hardcore ironmen and Ultimate ironmen a way to obtain lava scale shards without the dangers of lava dragons. Overall, for regular accounts, infernal eels give lower experience and greater profit.
21295:
The infernal cape is the most powerful melee cape in terms of overall bonuses, awarded for defeating TzKal-Zuk in the Inferno. It surpasses its predecessor, the fire cape, boasting greater melee attack and strength bonuses, along with slightly higher defensive bonuses. In spite of this, it is still surpassed by the Ardougne cloaks 3 and 4 in stab attack and prayer bonuses, and by the mythical cape in crush attack.

An infernal cape can be exchanged for a chance of obtaining the Jal-Nib-Rek pet by speaking to TzHaar-Ket-Keh. Like killing TzKal-Zuk, there is a 1/100 chance of obtaining the pet this way. If the player already has the pet, capes cannot be exchanged.

An infernal cape can be combined with the max cape to change its appearance by turning it into the infernal max cape.

As of 1 August 2026, there are 170,755 accounts that have obtained an infernal cape.

If the player dies a PvP death at level 20 Wilderness or below and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 225,000 coins.

If the player dies a PvP death above level 20 Wilderness and the item is unprotected, it will be converted to coins. To prevent this, a Trouver parchment and a payment of 500,000 coins can be given to Perdu in order to permanently lock the item. The locked item will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a mangled, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 500,000 coins.

While equipping the fire cape will grant players the fiery attribute and will therefore make them susceptible to the extra damage from the special effect of pearl bolts (e), the infernal cape does not grant this attribute.

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room.

21298:
Obsidian helmet is a piece of obsidian armour that can be purchased from TzHaar-Hur-Zal's Equipment Store for 84,480 Tokkul (73,216 with Karamja gloves). It requires level 60 in Defence to wear.

When used in conjunction with the obsidian platebody and obsidian platelegs, all obsidian weaponry will be given a 10% boost in melee accuracy and melee strength. The damage bonus does stack with the berserker necklace multiplicatively, and is applied first.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the obsidian armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
21301:
Obsidian platebody is a piece of the obsidian armour set and can be purchased in TzHaar-Hur-Zal's Equipment Store for 126,000 Tokkul (109,200 with Karamja gloves). It requires level 60 in Defence to wear.

When used in conjunction with the obsidian helmet and obsidian platelegs, all obsidian weaponry will be given a 10% boost in melee accuracy and melee strength. The damage bonus does stack with the berserker necklace.

It gives one less strength bonus than the fighter torso, and has worse defensive stats, but it is purchasable, which makes it a decent alternative for players not wanting to do Barbarian Assault for the torso.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the obsidian armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
21304:
Obsidian platelegs are a piece of the obsidian armour set and can be purchased in TzHaar-Hur-Zal's Equipment Store for 100,500 Tokkul (87,100 with Karamja gloves). It requires level 60 in Defence to wear.

When used in conjunction with the obsidian helmet and obsidian platebody, all obsidian weaponry will be given a 10% boost in melee accuracy and melee strength. The damage bonus does stack with the berserker necklace.

Obsidian platelegs are one of only nine legs slot items that give a Strength bonus, but has lower defensive stats than most alternatives.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the obsidian armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
21308: A red rainbow strand is a colour strand found south of the Wizards' Tower during the event Gilbert's Colours. It is given to Gilbert in order to progress through the event.
21309: An orange rainbow strand is a colour strand found east of the Duel Arena bank during the event Gilbert's Colours. It is given to Gilbert in order to progress through the event.
21310: A yellow rainbow strand is a colour strand found at the southern point of Mudskipper Point during the event Gilbert's Colours. It is given to Gilbert in order to progress through the event.
21312: A blue rainbow strand is a colour strand found in the ram's pen south of Varrock during the event Gilbert's Colours. It is given to Gilbert in order to progress through the event.
21313: A purple rainbow strand is a colour strand found on the top floor of the White Knights' Castle during the event Gilbert's Colours. It is given to Gilbert in order to progress through the event.
21314:
The rainbow scarf is a neck slot item originally introduced as a reward from Gilbert for completing the Gilbert's Colours event in 2017. It can either be purchased from Diango's Toy Store for 120 coins, or obtained freely from Gilbert in the flower field south-east of Barbarian Village.

There are nine unique versions of the scarf representing different variants of sexual orientation or gender identity, whose colours can be changed at any time by right-clicking the "Change" option on the scarf. When switched to another style other than the pride (rainbow) style, the item is renamed to a colourful scarf.

It can be used as warm clothing for the Wintertodt. Note that the scarf is always destroyed on death; you will need to reacquire it if you die while fighting the Wintertodt.

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room.
21316:
Amethyst broad bolts are enhanced broad bolts. They require a Slayer level of at least 65 and a Ranged level of at least 61 to equip. They can be fired only by the rune, dragon hunter, dragon, Armadyl and Zaryte crossbows.

With a Ranged Strength bonus of +115, they are the equivalent of runite bolts in combat. Amethyst broad bolts are a superior alternative to their regular and arrow equivalents for the purpose of slaying turoth and kurasks using ranged.

Players with 76 Fletching and who have unlocked the "Broader fletching" ability for 300 Slayer reward points can create these by adding amethyst bolt tips to broad bolts. Amethyst broad bolts are fletched 10 at a time and give 10.6 Fletching experience per bolt, or 106 experience per set of 10 bolts made.
21326:
Amethyst arrows can be used with any bow made with magic logs or stronger, such as the magic shortbow and its imbued variant. They can also be used by the bone shortbow. As with most arrows, they can be poisoned.

They can be crafted with a Fletching level of 82 or higher by using headless arrows on amethyst arrowtips in sets of 15, granting 202.5 Fletching experience.

Amethyst arrows have a +6 higher Ranged strength bonus compared to rune arrows. The strongest arrow type, dragon arrows, have a +5 higher Ranged strength bonus advantage over amethyst arrows. However, dragon arrows are much more costly to use.

Despite not being made of metal, amethyst arrows do function with Ava's devices obtained from the completion of Animal Magnetism.

Amethyst bolt tips are created through the Crafting skill, requiring a Crafting level of 83. Using a chisel on an amethyst and selecting the "make bolt tips" option will result in 15 amethyst bolt tips and 60 experience per gem.

21345:
Superior mining gloves are a pair of gloves purchasable from Belona's shop, Mining Guild Mineral Exchange, for 100 unidentified minerals. Despite technically only requiring level 55 Mining to equip, level 60 is required to enter the guild to purchase them.

By speaking to Belona with these gloves and the mining gloves, players can pay her 40 unidentified minerals to combine them into a pair of expert mining gloves.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room.

Ultimate ironmen do not need "the full set" to store and withdraw variations of mining gloves.
21347:
Amethyst is a type of mineral mined from amethyst crystals in the Mining Guild. Mining it requires the player to have a Mining level of 92 and grants 240 Mining experience.

Amethyst can be cut with a chisel into several Fletching materials, including arrowtips, bolt tips, dart tips, and javelin tips. Amethyst materials and ammunition made from amethyst fall between rune and dragon gear in terms of level requirements and power.

Amethyst can only be mined in the Mining Guild. There are two sections in the guild that have amethyst crystals. The mine accessed via the south part of the guild can be used by everyone, but the larger cave to the west requires completion of the Elite Falador achievement diary to use.

While wearing expert mining gloves, amethyst crystals will not deplete for one roll, allowing players to mine an additional amethyst before depleting. The Varrock armour 4 double ore effect can also trigger when mining amethyst.
21350:
Amethyst arrowtips are attached to the tips of headless arrows, creating amethyst arrows. Doing so requires level 82 in Fletching, giving 202.5 experience per 15 arrows made, or 13.5 per arrow.

Amethyst arrowtips are created through the Crafting skill. A player must have a Crafting level of 85 and take an amethyst and use a chisel on it to make 15 arrowtips, giving 60 experience per set.
21354:
The hand fan is an item given to the player obtained after completing the midsummer ritual three times (requiring a minimum of three days to obtain) during the 2017 Midsummer event, as well as subsequent midsummer events.

As there was no midsummer event in 2018, it was made available from Diango's Toy Store for 1 coin.

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room.
21356:
Minnows are members-only fish that can be caught at Kylie Minnow's fishing platform at the Fishing Guild. They require a small fishing net and 82 Fishing to be caught, which cannot be boosted, granting 26.1 Fishing experience per catch of minnow. Boosting does however increase the rate at which they are caught. These catches consist of between 10-14 minnow, dependent on the player's Fishing level.

The platform may only be accessed after showing Kylie the full angler's outfit and having completed the Fishing Contest quest.

Minnow can be exchanged for noted raw sharks by trading with Kylie Minnow at a rate of 40 minnows for one raw shark.

Minnow fishing spots move around in a consistent 1-tile clockwise rotation at a fixed rate of 15 seconds, or 25 ticks. This is more rapid than other forms of net fishing. Players can use a synced interval timer for an auditory signal notifying the player of the spot moving, or simply count a total of 10 experience drops, which is the maximum that can be received from a fishing spot before it moves.

In addition, there is a 1/10 chance that a fishing spot will spawn a flying fish instead of providing minnows after rotating; flying fish will eat 16-26 minnow directly from the player's inventory as long as they keep fishing there, forcing them to move to another spot. A flying fish appears only after a fishing spot has changed, and will continue to eat the player's minnows until the fishing spot changes position once again. Players wishing to AFK here should pay attention for 1-2 ticks after they begin fishing to ensure a flying fish does not spawn. Flying fish cannot spawn mid way through a rotation so focus is not required for the full 25 ticks.

Equipping the Rada's blessing from Kourend & Kebos Diary gives up to 8% chance to catch twice the amount of minnows (no experience is given for the additional catch). This works well with the stackable nature of minnows in the inventory.

Using spirit flakes gives a 50% chance to double whatever is caught, e.g. a 13 minnow catch becomes 26 when a spirit flake activates.

While the fishing platform can only be accessed via the Fishing Guild, Minnow fishing does not benefit from the Guild's +7 invisible level boost.

Expert mining gloves are a pair of gloves that can be obtained by asking Belona in the Mining Guild to combine a pair of mining gloves with a pair of superior mining gloves, for a fee of 40 unidentified minerals. They require 70 Mining to wear. Unlike the other pairs of mining gloves, these gloves cannot be sold back to Belona.

Gathering the 180 total required unidentified minerals will take players approximately 10 to 12 hours of power-mining iron, which is the fastest method for acquiring unidentified minerals. To minimise the amount of clicks required to obtain expert mining gloves while power-mining iron, players should purchase the basic mining gloves as soon as they have 40 minerals.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room.

The capes have 16 variants to account for possible facial hair, where fake beards are built into the item to make it appear as if they had not been removed. There are two separate versions for each team, although all the purple team's capes except the default have the same icon as the yellow team.

21439:
The champion's cape is a cosmetic cape that is rewarded after defeating all 11 champions available in the Champions' Challenge. It is worn by Leon d'Cour, the human champion, Dimintheis, a Varrockian noble, as well as Toby, the taskmaster of the Varrock Diary.

It can be mounted on a cape hanger in an Achievement Gallery of a player-owned house.

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room.

An unlimited number of additional capes can be obtained by speaking to Larxus.
21469:
A teak seedling is created by sowing a teak seed in a plant pot filled with soil with a gardening trowel. Once watered, it will grow into a teak sapling. A teak sapling requires level 35 Farming to plant in a tree patch.

Planting the sapling in a hardwood tree patch, with a spade in your inventory, will result in it growing into a teak tree after 3,840 minutes (2 days, 17 hours, and 20 minutes). Squirrels will protect the trees for 15 limpwurt roots each tree.
21471:
A mahogany seedling is created by sowing a mahogany seed in a plant pot filled with soil with a gardening trowel. Once watered, it will grow into a mahogany sapling. A mahogany sapling requires level 55 Farming to plant in a tree patch.

After planting the sapling in a hardwood tree patch found in Fossil Island and waiting for it to fully grow, which takes 5,120 minutes (85.3 hours), the plant will grow into a mahogany tree which can be cut to yield mahogany logs.

21477:
Teak saplings are saplings that can be used to grow teak trees at level 35 Farming.

They can be made by planting a teak seed in a filled plant pot, with a gardening trowel in your inventory, and then watering the teak seedling with a watering can or by using Humidify. When watered, the seedling will sprout into a sapling in one crop cycle (0-5 minutes).

Planting the sapling in a hardwood tree patch after raking it first, with a spade in your inventory, will result in it growing into a teak tree after 4,480 minutes (3 days, 3 hours).

At Fossil Island, players can ask each of the squirrel gardeners to protect their tree in the respective patch from disease whilst it grows, which requires payment of 15 limpwurt roots. This payment can be noted. At Locus Oasis, players can ask Marcellus to protect their tree. The payment is the same as the squirrel gardeners.

Players can opt to use ultracompost instead, which reduces the trees' disease rate to ~1/10, and costs less than the payment. When doing birdhouse runs, one can make a slight detour to check if one of the trees has become diseased, and prune its diseased leaves with secateurs to cure it.
21480:
Mahogany saplings are saplings that can be used to grow mahogany trees at level 55 Farming.

They can be made by planting a mahogany seed in a filled plant pot, with a gardening trowel in your inventory, and then watering the mahogany seedling with a watering can or by using Humidify. When watered, the seedling will sprout into a sapling in one crop cycle (0-5 minutes).

Planting the sapling in a hardwood tree patch, with a spade in your inventory, will result in it growing into a mahogany tree after 5,120 minutes (3 days, 13 hours, and 20 minutes).

Players can ask the gardener to protect their tree from disease whilst it grows, which requires payment of 25 Yanillian hops.

Players can opt to use ultracompost instead, which reduces the trees' disease rate to ~1/10, and costs less than the payment. When doing birdhouse runs, one can make a slight detour to check if one of the trees has become diseased, and prune its diseased leaves with secateurs to cure it.
21483:
Ultracompost is the most potent version of compost, outclassing supercompost, that is used in the Farming skill to greatly reduce the chance of a farming patch from becoming diseased per growth stage by 90% (compared to 50% for compost and 80% for supercompost). This effect stacks with the effect provided by the iasor plant. When used on a farming patch, each bucket grants 36 Farming experience.

In addition, it also increases the minimum yield and maximum number of harvests received from allotments, hops, and herbs. This also applies to giant seaweed patches underwater, Celastrus bark from a fully grown Celastrus seed, and Crystal shards from a fully grown Crystal tree.

The minimum number of herbs increases from five to six (when compared to supercompost) and the overall crop yield increases around 20% on average. The combined effects increase expected yield per patch to about 8.6 herbs at high Farming levels.

As a rule of thumb, ultracompost is nearly always worth using as it boosts the yield of valuable patches, providing additional experience and gold overall, and is typically more cost effective and easier to manage than paying to protect a patch with a gardener.

However, ultracompost does not increase the yield of trees, fruit trees, cactus, bush patches, and flower patches; using it only protects these crops from disease.
21486:
Teak seeds are seeds used in the Farming skill. At level 35 Farming, teak seeds may be planted in plant pots with a gardening trowel and watered to become teak saplings.

After planting the sapling in a hardwood tree patch and waiting for it to fully grow, which takes 4,480 minutes (74.6 hours), the plant will grow into a teak tree, which can be cut to yield teak logs (and grant Woodcutting experience).

When cut down, the tree will automatically regrow after a period of time. A nearby gardener will look after a player's teak tree in exchange for 15 limpwurt roots.

Teak seeds are also a drop from the Wintertodt reward cart and bird nests.
21488:
Mahogany seeds are seeds used in the Farming skill. At level 55 Farming, mahogany seeds may be planted in plant pots with a gardening trowel and watered to become mahogany saplings.

After planting the sapling in a hardwood tree patch and waiting for it to fully grow, which takes 5,120 minutes (8x640 minutes or 85.3 hours), the plant will grow into a mahogany tree which can be cut to yield mahogany logs (and grant Woodcutting experience).

When cut down, the tree will automatically regrow after a period of time. A nearby gardener will look after a mahogany tree in exchange for 25 Yanillian hops (noted or unnoted).
21504:
Giant seaweed are a giant version of seaweed. It can be used on a fire or range to produce soda ash. One giant seaweed produces 6 soda ash, with a chance of failing, resulting in only one soda ash. Players with 51 or higher Cooking will no longer fail, even on a fire. Note that Cooking gauntlets do not decrease the cooking fail chance, however, the Hosidius Kitchen cooking range effect still applies.

Players can pay 5 giant seaweed to Chet to look after their growing Elkhorn frag.
21521:
A teak bird house is used to set bird house traps on Fossil Island requiring 34 Hunter. It can be made at 35 Crafting using teak logs on a clockwork with a chisel and hammer yielding 30 experience.

Once placed in a bird house space, it becomes a teak birdhouse trap.

Bird houses must be baited with 10 hop seeds (5 if Wildblood), 10 allotment seeds, 10 flower seeds, 10 low level herb seeds (guam, marrentill, tarromin, harralander), or 5 high level herb seeds (ranarr and above). After approximately 50 minutes when the birdhouse is full, it can be emptied, granting 280 Hunter experience.

The sawmill proposal is an item used during the Bone Voyage quest. It is obtained from the sawmill operator in the Lumber Yard.

It is to be given to the sawmill operator in the Woodcutting Guild (or Berry if the player does not meet the requirements to enter the guild), which then becomes a sawmill agreement after he signs the proposal.

Gold ore fragments are ore fragments mined from the boulder in the Volcanic Mine. Level 50 Mining is required to receive these fragments, granting 34 points and 40 Mining experience per fragment.

They are automatically given to Petrified Pete upon exiting the mine without teleporting in exchange for Mining experience.
21536:
Mithril ore fragments are ore fragments mined from the boulder in the Volcanic Mine. Level 55 Mining is required to receive these fragments, granting 44 points and 60 Mining experience per fragment.

They are automatically given to Petrified Pete upon exiting the mine without teleporting in exchange for Mining experience.
21537:
Adamantite ore fragments are ore fragments mined from the boulder in the Volcanic Mine. Level 70 Mining is required to receive these fragments, granting 55 points and 100 Mining experience per fragment.

They are automatically given to Petrified Pete upon exiting the mine without teleporting in exchange for Mining experience.
21539:
A heat-proof vessel is a water container given to the player by Petrified Pete upon entering the Volcanic Mine. It can be equipped in the weapon slot. It has 36 uses per game, and can be used to throw water onto the lava, creating platforms which players can walk on. These platforms will melt after 90 seconds, giving players limited time to stand on them. If players remain on the hardened lava when it melts, they will fall into the lava, taking massive damage.

The water can only be thrown while the player is facing north, east, south, and west. Additionally, the water canteen can be right-clicked to open a dialogue box to throw water in a specified direction, or right-clicked while it is equipped to select the direction the player wants to throw it at.

Players can pay Petrified Pete 10,000 Volcanic Mine points to have him upgrade their vessel to hold more water, increasing the number of uses per game from 36 to 72. The Collection Log and Petrified Pete's Ore Shop interfaces refer to this upgrade as "Large water container".
21540:
A large rock is used in the Volcanic Mine to increase the gas pressure by blocking gas chambers. Should the gas pressure be too high, players should mine the blockage to reduce the pressure and maintain the mine's stability.

Players cannot take the rock out of the mine, as it will disappear upon leaving. However, should players die in the mine with the rock in their possession, it can be smuggled out of the mine by reclaiming the player's lost items from Petrified Pete, but note that the rock cannot be deposited into the bank.
21541:
The Volcanic mine teleport is a magic tablet that can be broken by players to teleport to the Volcanic Mine entrance on the Fossil Island Volcano.

They can be purchased at Petrified Pete's Ore Shop for 200 Volcanic Mine reward points.

Bone Voyage is required to use this tablet, although it is not possible to obtain it without completing the quest under normal circumstances. Attempting to use the tablet without the requirements displays the game message: You need to have completed the Bone Voyage Quest to use this spell.

Calcite is an item that is used with pyrophosphite on a mycelium pool in order to recalcify fossils into enriched bones, which are used on the eastern strange machine in the House on the Hill to gain Prayer experience.

It is dropped by monsters found on Fossil Island, and can be mined from boulders inside the Volcanic Mine. It can also be purchased for 70 points each from Petrified Pete's Ore Shop.

It is dropped by monsters found on Fossil Island, and can be mined from boulders inside the Volcanic Mine. It can also be purchased for 70 points each from Petrified Pete's Ore Shop.

Small enriched bones can be obtained by using cleaned small fossils or an unidentified small fossil obtained from Fossil Island and depositing them into the mycelium pool. Players must add 3 pyrophosphite and 3 calcite along with the fossil to begin calcifying it; more will almost certainly be needed to maintain the reaction to completion.

Small enriched bones can be used on the eastern strange machine in the House on the Hill for 500 Prayer experience each.

Medium enriched bones can be used on the eastern strange machine in the House on the Hill for 1,000 Prayer experience each.
21551:

Large enriched bones can be used on the eastern strange machine in the House on the Hill for 1,500 Prayer experience each.

21622:
Volcanic ash is obtained from mining ash piles found around the Fossil Island Volcano. Doing so requires level 22 Mining and grants 10 experience per drop, regardless of the number of ash mined at once.

They can also be obtained as drops from various monsters on Fossil Island including wyverns in the Wyvern Cave.
21626:
A sulliuscep cap is an item obtained from chopping down sulliusceps. Players have a 1/100 chance of receiving the cap while chopping sulliusceps.

They are used as an ingredient in mushroom pies, a food item that boosts Crafting by 4 levels.
21631:
The ancient diary is found inside the House on the Hill on Fossil Island. It can be found on the bottom floor of the house by searching a pile of ancient books behind the ladder. Obtaining the diary is a mini task on the Museum Camp's notice board.

The diary documents a conflict between Zorgoth and Skeka, the author of the diary. This diary gives more insight on the dragonkin.

If lost, it can be reclaimed by searching the pile of books again, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house.
21633:
The ancient wyvern shield is a magical shield requiring a Magic level of 70 and a Defence level of at least 75 to equip, as well as having started Dragon Slayer I. It is one of the best Magic shields in the game, with stats comparable to that of the arcane spirit shield when fully charged, although it only has a 2% Magic damage bonus while having negative Melee and Ranged attack bonuses. However, it provides far superior stab and slash defence.

The shield provides both dragonfire protection and greater protection against the icy breath of wyverns and frost dragons. Unlike the elemental, mind, and dragonfire shields, the ancient wyvern shield will also grant an immunity against the freezing effect from a wyvern's icy breath, as well as reducing the damage, which can make it somewhat ideal when killing wyverns despite penalizing melee and ranged. This immunity, on the other hand, does not extend to any other freezing effect (such as KBD, Vorkath, etc).

When the shield is obtained, it is uncharged and offers similar defensive bonuses to those of an adamant sq shield. When fully charged, it offers melee and magic defensive bonuses slightly higher than those of the dragonfire shield while having far worse ranged defence.

21643:
Granite boots are boots made out of granite rock. They require level 50 Defence and Strength to equip, offering strength bonus and defensive stats superior to rune boots. Unlike most melee boots, they also provide a Ranged defence bonus.

They are obtained as a drop from wyverns in the Wyvern Cave.

The boots also help to protect the wearer from the extremely hot ground of the Karuulm Slayer Dungeon. Because they offer a strength bonus, unlike the boots of brimstone and the boots of stone, they are the most powerful offensive boots for melee attack styles within the Karuulm Slayer Dungeon if the player has not completed the elite Kourend & Kebos diary.
21646:
The granite longsword is the fourth strongest longsword available in Old School RuneScape, and can only be wielded by players who have at least 50 Attack and Strength.

It is obtained as a drop from wyverns in the Wyvern Cave. Despite a high slash accuracy bonus, its 5 tick attack speed means it is outperformed by the granite hammer's 4 tick attack speed, making the hammer better for training.
21652:
A drift net is an item used to catch fish shoals in the Drift net fishing activity located underwater of Fossil Island. They can be created by using two Jute fibre on a loom.

Drift nets can be strung up on the drift net anchors underwater to catch fish shoals over time. Players can then chase fish shoals into the drift nets. Each fish shoal fills the net up by 10% and gives Hunter and Fishing experience based on a player's current levels. Upon harvesting a drift net, the drift net will be destroyed and the player will be given the option to discard, bank, or take all rewards. Players will use between 80 and 110 drift nets an hour while drift net fishing.
21655:
A pufferfish can be caught underwater on Fossil Island. They can be held in a player's inventory to reduce a player's weight by 0.5kg, and can be used via a "Puff" option to restore 15% oxygen to stay underwater for longer.

Using the Puff action produces the message You depuff the pufferfish, restoring some of your puff.. They are then released back into the water as a Puffer Fish which will retreat from the player and appear deflated for several minutes before being able to be caught again. If the player has a fishbowl helmet or a medallion of the deep equipped, it cannot be puffed, stating that You ineffectually squash the poor puffer fish against your helmet. or That didn't help. if only the medallion is equipped.

The Drop action produces the text You release the pufferfish. In this case, it will not be deflated or retreat from the player and can be caught again immediately.

Upon returning to the surface, all pufferfish in the player's possession will disappear.

Attempting to drop a pufferfish above water results in the message The poor pufferfish expires with a lack of access to the sea..
21662:
The Fossil Island note book is a book used to document any findings on Fossil Island. It is obtained from the Junior Navigator after completion of Bone Voyage.

In order to fill the notes, players must participate in a number of activities that can be done around the island, such as building utilities for the Museum Camp and unlocking the Mycelium Transportation System. In addition, inside the House on the Hill, there are a number of stone chests that the player can insert 100 numulite for a chance at receiving notes (or receiving damage). Any notes that a player receives can be added to the Fossil Island note book and will appear after the player's personal notes of their activities on the island. There is no purpose beyond world-building and completionism to fill the note book.

21684: An uncooked mushroom pie is made by adding a sulliuscep cap to a pie shell. It can be baked with level 60 Cooking to make a mushroom pie, granting 200 Cooking experience when successfully baked. Obtaining a sulliuscep cap requires level 65 Woodcutting in order to cut the Sulliusceps found in the Sticky Swamp portion of Fossil Island which can be accessed via the Bone Voyage quest.
21690:
Mushroom pie is a type of pie that restores 16 Hitpoints in total, 2 bites each healing for 8. It also temporarily boosts Crafting by 4, the second highest boost available, and the highest reliable boost. A pie dish will remain after both bites are consumed.

It can be created by baking an uncooked mushroom pie on a cooking range, requiring level 60 Cooking and granting 200 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt pie. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Mushroom pie is one of a number of foods with a reduced burn rate while using the Lumbridge Castle range with Cook's Assistant completed. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 89, or 60 when using the Lumbridge range. Alternatively, casting the Bake Pie spell from the lunar spellbook will always create a pie without burning it.
21693:
A bowl of fish is a consumable item purchased from Mairin's Market found underwater beneath Fossil Island. Players can take out a variety of fish from it depending on the player's Fishing level, whereupon the bowl will be destroyed.

A bowl of fish will give an average of one of each kind of the following items: shrimps, anchovies, sardine, tuna, lobster, swordfish, sea turtles, and manta rays. There is also a rare chance of receiving fossils.
21695:
The Runefest shield is a cosmetic kiteshield adorned with the RuneFest dragon insignia, promoting and celebrating the festivities of RuneFest 2017, which took place on the 23rd of September, 2017 at Battersea Evolution Events Centre in Battersea Park, Wandsworth, United Kingdom.

Players can claim one from Diango in Draynor Village via the right-click "Holiday-items" option.

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room.
21697: The ash covered tome is an item purchased from Petrified Pete's Ore Shop by the entrance to the Volcanic Mine on Fossil Island for 40,000 points. An enhanced Fertile Soil spell is unlocked by reading it. The enhancement gives the effect of ultracompost by casting the spell while having two volcanic ash in the player's inventory, which it consumes.
21698:

This pack can only be purchased from TzHaar-Mej-Roh's Rune Store.
21701:

21711: Murky potion was a potion made during the 2017 Halloween event. It was made by giving the Apothecary in Varrock tin ore, grain, and tomberries. It was then used on the Zamorakian altar in the southern part of Varrock to create a spectral potion.
21712:
Spectral potion was a potion created during the 2017 Halloween event. It was made by using a murky potion on the Zamorakian altar in the southern part of Varrock. When this was done, a message in the chatbox stated You feel a dark power emanating from something in your backpack.

Using it on a masked stranger triggered a cutscene, resulting in the player supposedly being killed by Jonas and being brought back to life by the Grim Reaper.
21713: Tomberries were a type of berries found just south of Varrock during the 2017 Halloween event. They were given to the Apothecary in Varrock, alongside a tin ore and grain, to create a murky potion.
21714: A tattered book was an item found in Jarvis' cabin during the 2017 Halloween event. It contained clues to open the trapdoor leading to the cellar where Jarvis was hiding.
21717:
Time bubble was a magical artefact obtained by helping Wizard Traiborn remember his dance moves for the 549th Annual Wizard Dance Off during the 2017 Halloween event.

The time bubble was used on Jonas as a means to trap him underwater, in order to complete the event.
21718:
Traiborn note was a piece of parchment obtained from Wizard Traiborn in the Wizards' Tower during the 2017 Halloween event.

Unscrambled, the letters in the note spell SPIN, HEADBANG, and BLOWKISS - to direct the player to perform the Spin, Headbang, and Blow Kiss emotes in that order. Doing this correctly prompted Wizard Traiborn to commend the player for reminding him about his dance moves for the 549th annual Wizards' Tower Dance Off. He then gave the player a time bubble.
21719:
The Jonas mask is an untradeable event item rewarded after completing the 2017 Halloween event.

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room.
21720:
The Jonas mask is an untradeable event item rewarded after completing the 2017 Halloween event.

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room.
21722: The diving helmet was obtained from Jarvis during the 2017 Halloween event. It was used, along with the diving apparatus, to dive underwater during the final part of the event.
21723:
The diving apparatus is used for diving into the Mogre Camp in the waters of Port Khazard, during the Freeing Pirate Pete subquest of the Recipe for Disaster quest. It is used to get to the sea floor. It is also used in the underwater tunnel on Harmony Island during The Great Brain Robbery, as well as the underwater area of Fossil Island and the Coral Nurseries of The Great Conch. After completion of the Freeing Pirate Pete subquest, it can be stored in the cargo hold of a player's boat for use in sea charting with mermaid guides.

It is worn in the cape slot, and if worn alongside the fishbowl helmet, players' oxygen will not deplete while underwater.

If the apparatus is lost, Murphy will provide another one upon choosing the diving option when talking to him. He will not give the apparatus if the player has an apparatus stored in the bank, but he does not check the player's boat or tackle box.

It can be stored in a tackle box.
21726:
Granite dust is dropped by the Grotesque Guardians on the Slayer Tower roof, and the Mad Angel on Wyrmscraig.

With 50 Smithing, the dust can be used on steel cannonballs to create granite cannonballs. When creating them, a message asks how many the player would like to make. The stack of granite cannonballs is made instantly regardless of quantity, and a message in the chatbox will state You apply a thick coating of granite dust to your cannonballs. No Smithing experience is granted for doing so.

Granite cannonballs are the superior ammunition for the dwarf multicannon, increasing its max hit from 30 to 35.
21728:
Granite cannonballs are ammunition used for a dwarf multicannon, as well as for a boat cannon during boat combat. They can be fired from adamant cannons or stronger. They are created at level 50 Smithing by using a steel cannonball on granite dust, granting no experience.

Granite cannonballs increase the max hit of the dwarf multicannon from 30 to 35, equating to an approximate damage per second increase of 16.67%.

When a player creates granite cannonballs, a message in the chatbox will state You apply a thick coating of granite dust to your steel cannonballs.

If a player is killed by another player in the Wilderness or a PvP world, the killer will receive steel cannonballs.
21736:
Granite gloves are a pair of melee-oriented gloves dropped by the Grotesque Guardians, requiring level 50 Defence and Strength to equip.

Stats-wise, they are similar to adamant gloves, but have superior crush bonuses and melee defences.
21739:
The granite ring is a defensive ring dropped by the Grotesque Guardians that can be found on the Slayer Tower's rooftop. Level 50 Defence and Strength are required to wear it.

It can be imbued using 500,000 Nightmare Zone reward points or 250,000 with the hard tier of Combat Achievements, 200 Soul Wars Zeal Tokens, or a Scroll of Imbuing, purchased for 200 Emir's Arena reward points, doubling its stats.
21742:
The granite hammer is a warhammer dropped by the Grotesque Guardians. Level 50 Attack and 50 Strength is required to wield it.

It acts as a rock hammer in the inventory and when equipped - it will automatically smash gargoyles even if the player does not have the gargoyle smasher perk unlocked. The granite hammer also has a 30% Golembane effect, dealing 30% extra damage and accuracy against all golem-type creatures. This stacks multiplicatively with the slayer helmet's bonuses.

Unlike standard warhammers, the granite hammer features an attack speed of 4, matching the speed of more commonly used melee weapons (such as scimitars and the abyssal whip), which results in significantly more damage over time. Thus, in terms of overall power, the granite hammer is roughly between the rune scimitar and dragon scimitar.
21752:
The granite ring (i) is an imbued version of the regular granite ring from the Nightmare Zone and Soul Wars minigames. It requires 50 Defence and 50 Strength to equip. The imbue upgrade costs either 500,000 Nightmare Zone points or 250,000 with the hard tier of Combat Achievements, 200 Zeal Tokens, or by using a scroll of imbuing purchased from the Emir's Arena.

The upgrade doubles all defensive bonuses, including the negative Magic defence bonus.

If not protected, dying to another player will cause the imbued ring to lose its imbued status, but the player will be reimbursed the Nightmare Zone points, Zeal Tokens or Scroll of imbuing to re-imbue it via the aforementioned methods. Dying to a monster will not remove its imbued effect.

On the other hand, if its wearer dies to a monster, the ring will retain its imbued status even if dropped on death.
21754:
A rock thrownhammer is slayer equipment that is required to kill gargoyles. Unlike the rock hammer, the rock thrownhammer can be used to finish off gargoyles without having to do so within melee distance. This is useful for finishing off gargoyles when ranging from a safespot, or when finishing off Dawn. Since they are consumed upon usage, players should buy enough thrownhammers for their slayer task.

While damage can be done to them with a regular weapon at 75 Slayer, the thrownhammer must be used on gargoyles to finish them off when they have 10 hitpoints or less left, unless the player has unlocked the Gargoyle smasher ability via spending 120 slayer reward points, which allows players to automatically use the thrownhammer to finish off the gargoyle.

Players can buy a rock thrownhammer from any Slayer Master for 200 coins each.
21759:
The Hosidius favour certificate was a quest reward for completing The Depths of Despair. Reading this granted the player 10% Hosidius favour, where there would be a confirmation message before doing so. Should the player have wished to use it some other time, they could destroy it (if bank space was an issue) and reclaim it from Lord Kandur Hosidius.

The certificate was removed alongside the entire Kourend Favour system on 10 January 2024 with the release of Children of the Sun.
21760:
Kharedst's memoirs is a quest item reward in Client of Kourend. The book is obtained from Veos, who bought it at an auction, and can be reclaimed by speaking to him (or Cabin Boy Herbert after partial completion of A Kingdom Divided) on the Port Piscarilius docks should players lose it.

It is an equipable book that was a gift from King Kharedst IV, the last king of Great Kourend, to his only daughter Rose. If players have lost the pages before putting them in the book, they can be reclaimed from the respective lords of each Kourend house; see the table below for the relevant quests. If the book is charged when destroyed, all charges are retained. After completion of A Kingdom Divided, the book gets upgraded to the Book of the Dead, which is reclaimed from Commander Fullore instead.

The memoirs inside can be read, containing various outings Rose experienced with her father.
21764:
The Fisher's Flute is a quest item reward in The Queen of Thieves.

It is used on Kharedst's memoirs to allow teleportation to Port Piscarilius. If lost before being added to Kharedst's memoirs, a replacement can be claimed from Lady Shauna Piscarilius in The Warrens.

Using Kharedst's memoirs after adding this page to it on the Swamp Priest results in unique dialogue, revealing that he was the man named Rey who played the golden flute in the story.
21766:
History and Hearsay is a quest reward for completing Tale of the Righteous.

It is used on Kharedst's memoirs to allow teleportation to Shayzien. If lost before being added to Kharedst's memoirs, a replacement can be claimed from Lord Shiro Shayzien in Shayzien.

After adding this page, using Kharedst's memoirs on the Grave digger results in unique dialogue, revealing that he is the grave digger who talked to Rose in the story.
21768:
Jewellery of Jubilation is a quest reward for completing The Forsaken Tower.

It is used on Kharedst's memoirs or the Book of the Dead to allow teleportation to Lovakengj. If lost before being added to Kharedst's memoirs or the book of the dead, a replacement can be claimed from Lady Vulcana Lovakengj in the Lovakengj Assembly.

Using Kharedst's memoirs after adding this page to it on the Old dwarf results in unique dialogue, revealing that he is the one who sold King Kharedst IV the cursed trinkets.
21770:
A Dark Disposition is a quest reward for completing The Ascent of Arceuus.

It is used on Kharedst's memoirs to allow teleportation to Arceuus. If lost before being added to Kharedst's memoirs, a replacement can be claimed from Lord Trobin Arceuus in the upper level of the Tower of Magic.

After completing the quest A Kingdom Divided, a replacement can be claimed from Lord Trobin's son, Asteros Arceuus, on the 1st floor of Kourend Castle. Note that Asteros will only give it to the player after talking to him twice.

Using Kharedst's memoirs after adding this page to it on Alyssa results in unique dialogue, revealing that she is the handmaid named Alyssa in the story.

21776:
The imbued Saradomin max cape is the result of combining the imbued Saradomin cape with a max cape, during which the max hood required to be in the player's inventory will automatically convert to the imbued Saradomin max hood.

Like the other max cape variants (a max cape combined with another cape slot item), the imbued Saradomin max cape does not have the max cape's stats or perks; it only acts as a cosmetic upgrade to the imbued Saradomin cape with the following exceptions when worn:

It acts as a Cooking cape to allow access to the Cooks' Guild without a chef's hat, golden chef's hat, Varrock armour 3 or 4

It acts as a Crafting cape to allow access to the Crafting Guild without a brown apron or golden apron

It acts as a Runecraft cape to prevent essence pouches from degrading (but does not allow access to runic altars)

It acts as a Firemaking cape to work as a piece of warm clothing

It can be used to perform the Skill Cape emote.

The max cape and imbued Saradomin cape can be separated by using a knife on the cape. Mac will also buy back a max cape, along with its variants, for 1,900,800 coins each. He will return the secondary item any max cape variant was combined with upon doing so.

If the player dies a PvP death and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 99,000 coins.
21778:

If players are refunding the imbued Saradomin max cape via Mac, the player must also have the imbued Saradomin max hood in their inventory.

Should players lose the hood, they may reclaim it from Mac for free.

21786:

21791:
The imbued Saradomin cape is obtained from imbuing a Saradomin cape with the items dropped by Justiciar Zachariah, Porazdir, and Derwen, during the Mage Arena II miniquest, requiring 75 Magic. Subsequent imbues will require only the Justiciar's hand, or 250,000 to purchase from the Lost Property shop.

This cape, along with the imbued Guthix and Zamorak capes, provides the best in slot magic attack and magic damage bonus for the cape slot.

The cape, like most untradeable equipment, is automatically protected upon death in dangerous PvM scenarios outside of the Wilderness, and likewise is always protected upon safe deaths and services that offer an item reclaim function (such as Zulrah via Priestess Zul-Gwenwynig and the Grotesque Guardians via the magical chest).

If the player dies a PvP death and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 96,000 coins.

The imbued Saradomin cape can be combined with the max cape to change its appearance by turning it into the imbued Saradomin max cape.

You may obtain all 3 god capes imbued at the same time. After completing the miniquest, you may return with duplicates of any dropped items by Justiciar Zachariah, Porazdir, and Derwen.

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room.
21793:
The imbued Guthix cape is obtained from imbuing a Guthix cape with the items dropped by Justiciar Zachariah, Porazdir, and Derwen, during the Mage Arena II miniquest, requiring 75 Magic. Subsequent imbues will require only ent's roots, or 250,000 to purchase from the Lost Property shop.

This cape, along with the imbued Saradomin and Zamorak capes, provides the best in slot magic attack and magic damage bonus for the cape slot.

Despite the update newspost stating that the cape is always lost upon death (excluding safe deaths and services that offer an item reclaim function, such as Zulrah via Priestess Zul-Gwenwynig and the Grotesque Guardians via the magical chest), the cape, like most untradeable equipment, is automatically protected upon death in dangerous PvM scenarios outside of the Wilderness.

The imbued Guthix cape can be combined with the max cape to change its appearance by turning it into the imbued Guthix max cape.

You may obtain all 3 god capes imbued at the same time. After completing the miniquest, you may return with duplicates of any dropped items by Justiciar Zachariah, Porazdir, and Derwen.

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room.
21795:
The imbued Zamorak cape is obtained from imbuing a Zamorak cape with the items dropped by Justiciar Zachariah, Porazdir, and Derwen, during the Mage Arena II miniquest, requiring 75 Magic. Subsequent imbues will require only the demon's heart, or 250,000 to purchase from the Lost Property shop.

Despite the update newspost stating that the cape is always lost upon death (excluding safe deaths and services that offer an item reclaim function, such as Zulrah via Priestess Zul-Gwenwynig and the Grotesque Guardians via the magical chest), the cape, like most untradeable equipment, is automatically protected upon death in dangerous PvM scenarios outside of the Wilderness.

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room.
21797:
Justiciar's hand is a drop from Justiciar Zachariah. This hand, along with the demon's heart and ent's roots from Porazdir and Derwen respectively, is required to imbue a god cape during the Mage Arena II miniquest.

Subsequent imbues will require only one item of the player's choice. In this case, this hand will imbue a Saradomin cape into an imbued Saradomin cape.

The Justiciar's hand cannot be deposited into a bank, and is always lost upon death, so it is recommended to turn it in to Kolodion as soon as possible.
21798:
Ent's roots are a drop from Derwen. These roots, along with the demon's heart and Justiciar's hand from Porazdir and Justiciar Zachariah respectively, are required to imbue a god cape during the Mage Arena II miniquest.

Subsequent imbues will require only one item of the player's choice, in which these roots will imbue a Guthix cape into an imbued Guthix cape.

The ent's roots cannot be deposited into a bank, and are always lost upon death, so it is recommended to turn them in to Kolodion as soon as possible.
21799:
Demon's heart is a drop from Porazdir. This heart, along with the Justiciar's hand and ent's roots from Justiciar Zachariah and Derwen respectively, is required to imbue a god cape during the Mage Arena II miniquest.

Subsequent imbues will require only one item of the player's choice, in which this heart will imbue a Zamorak cape into an imbued Zamorak cape.

The demon's heart cannot be deposited into a bank, and is always lost upon death, so it is recommended to turn it in to Kolodion as soon as possible.
21800:
The enchanted symbol is used in Mage Arena II miniquest to find the three god bosses. It works similarly to the strange device used for Hot & Cold clue steps, though it can only be used in above-ground parts of the Wilderness, including the safe areas just outside the Ferox Enclave.

Activating the symbol prompts players to select which god to attune it to, and upon choosing one it randomly deals up to 16 damage and indicates which direction to go in the chatbox. It is possible to die from using the symbol.

Only one enchanted symbol can be owned at a time, and if lost it may be reobtained from Kolodion in the Mage Arena bank. Dying anywhere with the symbol will always cause it to be destroyed if it is not a protected item.
21804:
The ancient crystal is a drop obtained from revenants found in the Revenant Caves.

Four of these, along with four marble blocks and level 80 Construction, are required in order to build an obelisk in the Superior garden of a player-owned house. Doing so effectively awards 250 Construction experience per crystal.
21807:
The ancient emblem is a drop obtained from revenants found in the Revenant Caves.

It can be given to the Emblem Trader wandering around in the Revenant Caves in exchange for 500,000 coins. This must be done while on the official Bounty Hunter world. The emblem cannot be given to him in Edgeville. A chisel can be used on the ancient emblem to break it into 1,000 revenant ether.

Much like the bracelet of ethereum, the emblem is always lost on death, even if it is the only item in the player's inventory.

Note that unlike other Ancient artefacts, the ancient emblem becomes rarer when skulled.
21810:
The ancient totem is a drop obtained from revenants found in the Revenant Caves.

It can be given to the Emblem Trader wandering around in the Revenant Caves in exchange for 1,000,000 coins. This must be done while on the official Bounty Hunter world. The totem cannot be given to him in Edgeville. A chisel can be used on the ancient totem to break it into 2,000 revenant ether.

Much like the bracelet of ethereum, the totem is always lost on death, even if it is the only item in the player's inventory.
21813:
The ancient statuette is a drop obtained from revenants found in the Revenant Caves.

It can be given to the Emblem Trader wandering around in the Revenant Caves in exchange for 2,000,000 coins. This must be done while on the official target worlds. The statuette cannot be given to him in Edgeville. A chisel can be used on the ancient statuette to break it into 4,000 revenant ether.

Much like the bracelet of ethereum, the statuette is always lost on death, even if it is the only item in the player's inventory.
21826:
The redundant hat was an unobtainable item that was added to the cache with the 2017 Winter Deadman finals. It originally had the name "Dmm ref hat" and was listed on the Grand Exchange. Presumably it was supposed to be used in the finals.

The item was a copy of the ancestral hat. It was removed from the Grand Exchange after a week.

21837:
Ogre artefact is an item obtained during the The Corsair Curse quest.

During the quest, it comes to light that it was stolen by Arsen the Thief and must be returned to Chief Tess to lift the curse. However, it is revealed that Arsen simply grabbed one of her many tooth-picks, and that her shamans have not actually cursed the crew.

21859:
The Wise old man's santa hat is an untradeable event item rewarded after completing a Christmas event. It appears to be a combination santa hat and blue party hat.

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room.
21861: Enchanted curtains is an item obtained from the Wise Old Man during the 2017 Christmas event. It is used on a snowball obtained outside the grotto to turn it into enchanted snowy curtains.
21862: Enchanted snowy curtains is an item obtained by using a snowball on some enchanted curtains during the 2017 Christmas event. It is given to Iffie in order to create the snow imp costume.
21863:
The Wise old man's teleport tablet is an item obtained during the 2017 Christmas event. It is given to the player so that they can return conveniently to the Land of Snow once they have made the snow imp costume.

Unlike most event items, if this item is destroyed during the event, it cannot be reobtained, and players must return to the Land of Snow by speaking to the Wise Old Man in his house.
21865:
The Fine mesh net is an item obtained in Santa's Grotto during the 2017 Christmas event. It is used to catch Snow Sprites to light up Dolph's nose.

After the event is completed, it was automatically taken away from the player. However, players could reobtain it by revisiting the Land of Snow via speaking to the Wise Old Man after completing the event. After the event ended, it was automatically deleted from every player.

It cannot be used as a net for butterflies or implings, even if it is reobtained after the event.
21866: The Santa suit is obtained from the wardrobe in Santa's Grotto during the 2017 Christmas event. It is used on the washer furnace after it has been fuelled to produce a wet Santa suit.
21867: The Santa suit (wet) is obtained during the 2017 Christmas event by using a Santa suit on the washer furnace after it has been fuelled. The wet suit is to be used on a fuelled dryer furnace to produce a dry Santa suit.
21868: The Santa suit (dry) is obtained during the 2017 Christmas event by using a wet Santa suit on the dryer furnace after it has been fuelled. The dry suit is to be given to the Wise Old Man so that he can dress up as Santa.
21869: Logs and kindling are obtained in Santa's Grotto during the 2017 Christmas event. Two are used to light up the washer and dryer furnaces in order to shrink the Santa suit for the Wise Old Man.
21870:
The promissory note is a quest item used in The Fremennik Trials. It is obtained by giving 5,000 coins to Askeladden in Rellekka. The note can then be given to Thora the Barkeep in exchange for a legendary cocktail.

The promissory note is basically a contract to stop Askeladden from entering the bar because he is underage. However, as he is Fremennik, he will be able to enter the bar after completing his trials, as he will get a new Fremennik name.
21871: Santa's seal is obtained during the 2017 Christmas event by searching the shelf within Santa's vault. It is used to sign the promissory note.
21873:
Empty sacks are used to store potatoes, onions, and cabbages (10 per sack). Players can make a sack using a loom.

Apart from being used in Farming for carrying vegetables, 8 of them are used during Enlightened Journey to make sandbags. Sacks full of vegetables can also be used as payment for a farmer watching over a player's crops. Sacks may also be used to make scarecrows, by using a sack on a haystack to make a hay sack. The hay sack can then be used with a bronze spear and a watermelon to produce the scarecrow.

The Fill Sack option will instantly fill a sack with 10 vegetables. Vegetables chosen to go automatically into the sack are cabbages first, then onions, and lastly potatoes. Cabbages from Draynor Manor cannot be stored in a sack.
21874: A bulging sack is obtained from the Foreman during the 2017 Christmas event. It is given to the Wise Old Man so that he can deliver the presents.
21882:
Dragon armour set (lg) is an item obtained by exchanging a set of items with a Grand Exchange clerk via their right-click "Sets" option and clicking on the appropriate item set within the Item Sets interface.

Sets are commonly used to reduce the amount of bank space taken up.
21885:
Dragon armour set (sk) is an item obtained by exchanging a set of items with a Grand Exchange clerk via their right-click "sets" option and clicking on the appropriate item set within the Item Sets interface.

21888:
The turquoise Slayer helmet is a piece of equipment that is worn in the helmet slot. It is a cosmetic upgrade to the Slayer helmet.

It can be created by adding Vorkath's head after purchasing the ability Undead Head for 1,000 Slayer reward points from any Slayer master. This is reversible, and the head will be returned to the inventory along with the slayer helmet's components. If a player loses the turquoise slayer helmet in a PvP death, Vorkath's head will be placed in their gravestone.
21890:

This is reversible, and the head will be returned to the inventory along with the slayer helmet's components. If a player loses the turquoise slayer helmet (i) in a PvP death, Vorkath's head will be placed in their gravestone.
21892:
The dragon platebody is an armour used in melee and the strongest of all standard platebodies. It requires 60 Defence and completion of the quest Dragon Slayer I to equip.

It offers some of the highest bonuses of any non-degradable armour in the game, providing higher slash and stab defence than the Bandos chestplate. For melee use it is a direct upgrade to the dragon chainbody in every stat except crush, with the chainbody having +1 crush defence more than the platebody. Despite its high defensive bonuses however, the dragon platebody lacks a strength bonus, making it less commonly used for general melee training.

Players with level 90 Smithing can make one by using a dragon chainbody, dragon metal lump, and dragon metal shard at the Dragon Forge, granting 2,000 experience.

A dragon platebody ornament kit, obtained from master clue scrolls, can be attached to create a gold-trimmed dragon platebody (g). This is only cosmetic, and does not affect the platebody's stat bonuses. It can be dismantled, returning the platebody and ornament kit.

It is considered a piece of the dragon armour set.
21895:
A dragon kiteshield is a kiteshield made by combining a dragon sq shield, dragon metal shard, and dragon metal slice at the Dragon Forge after the completion of Dragon Slayer II. This process requires a hammer and 75 Smithing, granting 1,000 Smithing experience. The dragon kiteshield does not require Legends' Quest to wield, despite being created from the dragon sq shield. Like other dragon equipment, it requires 60 Defence to wield.

Just like the dragon sq shield, the dragon kiteshield does not protect against dragonfire.

Players can attach a dragon kiteshield ornament kit, obtained from master clue scrolls, to create a gold-trimmed dragon kiteshield (g). This marginally increases the kiteshield's Ranged attack bonus (from -3 to -2), but is otherwise cosmetic. It can be dismantled, returning the kiteshield and ornament kit.
21898:
The Assembler max cape is the result of combining Ava's assembler with a max cape, during which the max hood required to be in the player's inventory will automatically convert to the assembler max hood.

Like the other max cape variants (a max cape combined with another cape slot item), the assembler max cape does not have the max cape's stats or perks; it only acts as a cosmetic upgrade to Ava's assembler with the following exceptions when worn:

It acts as a Cooking cape to allow access to the Cooks' Guild without a chef's hat, golden chef's hat, Varrock armour 3 or 4

It acts as a Crafting cape to allow access to the Crafting Guild without a brown apron or golden apron

It acts as a Runecraft cape to prevent essence pouches from degrading (but does not allow access to runic altars)

It acts as a Firemaking cape to work as a piece of warm clothing

It can be used to perform the Skill Cape emote.

The max cape and assembler can be separated by using a knife on the cape. Mac will also buy back a max cape, along with its variants, for 1,900,800 coins each. He will return the secondary item any max cape variant was combined with upon doing so.

Turning the Ava's assembler into an assembler max cape is the only way for ultimate ironmen to store one, as it counts as a max cape on the cape rack.

If the player dies a PvP death and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 240,000 coins.
21900:
Assembler max hood is a hood created by using Ava's assembler on a max cape. When the assembler max cape is created, the max hood that is required to be in the player's inventory during the cape's creation is automatically converted to the assembler max hood.

If players are refunding the assembler max cape via Mac, the player must also have the assembler max hood in their inventory.

Should players lose the hood, they may reclaim it from Mac for free.
21905:
Dragon bolts are a type of crossbow ammo that can only be fired from a dragon crossbow, Armadyl crossbow, dragon hunter crossbow, or Zaryte crossbow. Additionally, they require a Ranged level of 64 to wield. As with most bolts, they can be poisoned, however this will prevent the addition of bolt tips.

They can only be obtained by using feathers on unfinished dragon bolts. Doing so requires level 84 in Fletching and grants 12 experience per bolt.

Bolt tips of any kind, excluding amethyst, can be added to dragon bolts and then enchanted to obtain enchanted bolts that possess the ranged strength of dragon bolts.
21907:
Vorkath's head is an item dropped by Vorkath. The head has various uses, such as being used to upgrade Ava's accumulator, as a cosmetic upgrade to the Slayer helmet, or sacrificed for Prayer experience. For any given kill, the drop rate of the head is 1/50, with the exception of the 50th kill, when the drop is guaranteed.

Players can take the head along with 75 mithril arrows, and either Ava's accumulator or 4,999 coins (for a new device), to Ava in Draynor Manor to obtain Ava's assembler, which gives increased stats and improved ammo return. Players can also use the head on a ranging or max cape to give the enhanced ammo-returning effect to those capes. Additionally, players can bring the assembler and Dizana's quiver to Ava to grant the quiver the ammo-returning effect.
21909:
Vorkath's stuffed head is obtained by bringing Vorkath's head and 50,000 coins to the taxidermist in Canifis; this process is reversible by selecting the "Unstuff" option on the item.

Once stuffed, it can be mounted at a gilded display within the skill hall in a player-owned house with level 82 Construction, granting 223 Construction alongside 200 Attack, Strength, Defence, Magic, and Ranged experience, with players being given the option to decline the combat experience before mounting the heads.
