21975:
Crushed superior dragon bones are a secondary ingredient used to create super antifire potions, which require level 92 Herblore to make. They can be obtained by using a pestle and mortar with superior dragon bones, which in turn can be obtained by killing Vorkath or frost dragons.

They can be stored in a reagent pouch while superior dragon bones cannot, which can allow saving inventory space when fighting Vorkath repeatedly.
21990:
The rift guardian is a members-only skilling pet that can be obtained while training Runecraft. The chances of getting it are dependent on the player's Runecraft level, the rune the player is crafting, and the number of essence used. Upon using the Guardian's eye on it, which is purchased from the Guardians of the Rift reward shop for 3,000 abyssal pearls, players unlock a permanent metamorphosis option to turn it into the Greatish guardian.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

When runecrafting using dark essence fragments, the pet is given after they are removed and the runes are given back. This means if there is not already some of the runes to be crafted in the inventory, and the rest of the inventory is full, and a pet is already following the player, the rift guardian will not be given; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.
21992:
Vorki is a pet dropped by Vorkath. It is a much smaller version of Vorkath.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.
22001: Clue scroll (easy) is a cryptic clue obtained from easy Treasure Trails.
22002:
The dragonfire ward is a ranged shield requiring a Ranged level of 70 and a Defence level of 75 to equip, as well as having started Dragon Slayer I. It offers the second highest Ranged Attack and Ranged Strength bonus for the shield slot in the game, only beaten by the twisted buckler.

The ward offers two special characteristics: it acts like a regular anti-dragon shield in terms of dragonfire protection, and it provides partial protection against the icy breath of wyverns, like the elemental, mind, and dragonfire shields. This immunity does not extend to draconic creatures capable of producing a similar effect (KBD, Vorkath, etc).
22003:

A skeletal visage is an item obtained as a very rare drop from Vorkath.

22033:
Aivas' diary can be obtained in the dungeon beneath Lithkren by searching Aivas' charred corpse next to the ancient doors.

The diary describes the events that resulted in the discovery of Lithkren by the humans, which led to the battle on Lithkren, which Aivas led alongside Robert the Strong, Camorra Shayzien and Tristan Corvo.

If lost, it can be reclaimed from Aivas' corpse, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house.
22037:
Malumac's journal is a journal that can be found by searching a skeleton in the south-west corner of the Karamjan Temple found in the Kharazi Jungle.

The journal, written by Malumac, a member of an elite expeditionary group led by Skotizo and operating under Zamorak's direct orders, details the group's goal to retrieve a powerful artefact in an underground temple beneath the Kharazi Jungle.

If lost, it can be reclaimed from Malumac's corpse, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house.
22041:
Imcandoria's fall is a book found in the library of the Myths' Guild after completing Dragon Slayer II. The book can be used on Freja, who transcribed the original text, as well as Thurgo, one of the last known Imcando dwarves.

The book, written by Highseer Gulbrand of the Isle of Garmr, details the fall of Imcandoria. The text was originally inscribed in rock paper in an extremely heavy tome and was loosely translated based on old trade scrolls written by early Fremennik tribes on the isle.

If lost, it can be reclaimed from the Myths' Guild library or from a bookcase within a player-owned house.
22043:
Imafore's betrayal is a book that can be found in the library of the Myths' Guild after completing Dragon Slayer II.

The book describes the events that led to Great Kourend's declaration of war against Varlamore.

If lost, it can be reclaimed from the Myths' Guild library, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house.
22045:
Lutwidge and the Moonfly is a poem written by a bard named Shudersque that can be found in the library of the Myths' Guild after completing Dragon Slayer II.

The poem describes the encounter between Lutwidge and the Moonfly. If players speak to Lutwidge about his grand feats, he will tell players that the poem's telling of the battle is a little embellished and rife with errors. If players have the poem in their inventory, he will also tell them that the sword was actually bathed in the sap of a yew tree, rather than sheep's blood.

If lost, it can be reclaimed from the Myths' Guild library, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house.
22047:

The book speaks of the Tale of Serafina, in which she takes on the Theatre of Blood and survived all of the challenges within, and was granted freedom from the blood tithes as her reward. However, it is discovered during the quest A Taste of Hope and in her diary that the tale was simply a ruse to instill false hope into the citizens of Meiyerditch so that they could provide entertainment for the vampyres.

If lost, it can be reclaimed from the Myths' Guild library, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house.

22095:
Swamp paste is made by mixing flour with swamp tar to make raw swamp paste, and then cooking the mixture on a fire, yielding 2 Cooking experience. It cannot be cooked on a range. It is possible to burn the tar, though it is automatically discarded. Swamp tar spawns in Lumbridge Swamp and Mort Myre Swamp.

To make a large amount of swamp paste from swamp tar, use a barrel of flour at either the Sinclair Mansion or Gordon and Mary's farm. Bring as much swamp tar as needed and 26 pots, Gordon's farm also has a pot spawn. Click the barrel to fill the pots, then combine with the swamp tar to create raw swamp paste. Repeat this until the desired amount is obtained, then cook it. A permanent fire is recommended for large amounts. There is a permanent fire at the base of Mount Karuulm, very near the fairy ring and in front of the shack with a rope spawn.

Swamp paste can also be bought from the Trader crewmembers at any of the ports in the Charter ship network, the Khazard General Store (south of Ardougne), and Rasolo (west of the Fishing Guild) are very useful for some of the quests listed below. It is also sold at the Mort'ton Builder's Store.

Swamp paste also tends to be rewarded in abundance when unlocking chests within the Shades of Mort'ton minigame.

Unlike swamp tar, swamp paste cannot be combined with herbs to form ammunition for a Salamander using the Herblore skill.

22111:
The dragonbone necklace is a necklace that is dropped exclusively by Vorkath. Wearing the necklace requires level 70 in Prayer, and currently offers the highest Prayer bonus of any piece of equipment available in Old School RuneScape.

When worn, it will restore Prayer points as bones are buried (even if buried via the bonecrusher). This effect does not stack with the Catacombs of Kourend Prayer restoration effect, and does not grant Prayer points for scattering demonic ashes.

The dragonbone necklace can be combined with the bonecrusher and a hydra tail to create the bonecrusher necklace, which combines the effects of both the dragonbone necklace and the bonecrusher.

The amount of points restored are as follows:

Bones, Burnt bones, Monkey bones, Wolf bones, and Bat bones restore 1 prayer point.

Big bones, Jogre bones, Zogre bones, Wyrmling bones, Shaikahan bones, and Small ninja monkey bones restore 2 prayer points.

Baby dragon bones, Bull bones, Wyrm bones, and Strykewyrm bones restore 3 prayer points.

Dragon, Frost dragon, Wyvern, Drake, Dagannoth, Hydra, Fayrg, Raurg, and Lava dragon bones restore 4 prayer points.

Superior dragon bones, Giant bones, and Ourg bones restore 5 prayer points.
22114:
The mythical cape is a cape that can only be worn by those who have completed the Dragon Slayer II quest.

It can be purchased from Jack at the Mythical Cape Store on the top floor of the Myths' Guild for 10,000 coins. The cape provides unlimited free teleports to the guild. The mythical cape has the highest crush attack bonus of any cape slot item in Old School RuneScape, providing a +6 bonus.

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room. It may also be mounted in the Quest Hall in the Guild trophy space, or the cape hanger in the Achievement Gallery, of a player-owned house. While mounted, the player can use it to teleport to the Myths' Guild.
22116: Superior dragon bonemeal is an item that is used for worship at the Ectofuntus. It consists of a pot filled with superior dragon bones that have been crushed in the bone grinder at the Ectofuntus.
22124:
Superior dragon bones are obtained as a guaranteed drop from killing Vorkath and as an uncommon drop from killing frost dragons. They can be crushed with a pestle and mortar to create crushed superior dragon bones, which is a secondary ingredient in super antifire potions, requiring level 92 Herblore to create.

Unlike other types of bones, superior dragon bones require a Prayer level of 70 (unboostable) to use, and give 150 Prayer experience when buried. This can be increased by offering the bones in different ways:

450 XP when casting Sinister Offering.

450 XP when offered at the sacred bone burner after the appropriate faith level has been achieved.

525 XP when offered at a gilded altar with two burners lit.

600 XP when offered at the Ectofuntus in the form of superior dragon bonemeal.

605 XP when blessed and broken down into blessed bone shards and offered at the libation bowl, or 726 XP when offered with a jug of blessed sunfire wine. Virilis outside the altar will exchange noted bones for 10 coins each.

1050 XP on average when offered at the Chaos Temple in the Wilderness. Each offering gives 525 XP, which is the same as the gilded altars with two burners lit, but with an additional 50% chance to not consume the bones.

Superior dragon bones provide the most Prayer experience of any bone in the game, but they are very expensive, making them the top-tier choice for efficient training when cost is not a concern. When used at a gilded altar, they require 38.84 coins per experience, while regular dragon bones use 13.05 coins per experience. As such, the most economical use is as a secondary for making super antifire potions.

22207:
Glistening tears are a form of currency found in the Underwater Agility and Thieving training activity, located in the Underwater section of Fossil Island. Glistening tears can be exchanged with Mairin for experience in Agility, Thieving, or both, and are obtained by looting chests and clams during the activity. Glistening tears are always obtained alongside a mermaid's tear. Approximately 150 tears are obtainable per hour.

The most efficient way of exchanging glistening tears is selecting both skills. While it gives less experience in an individual skill, its value is higher than training the two skills independently, due to Agility being proportionally slower to train.

Players can only exchange a maximum of 700 glistening tears at once; if players exchange them for experience with more than 700 glistening tears in the inventory, the excess will be discarded. In addition, they cannot be deposited into a bank.

Choosing Agility and Thieving, the experience granted by each Glistening Tear is defined by the following equations; When exchanging for one skill, experience is multiplied by 1.5:

EA⌊0.1⌋=3×A2×910150=0.018×A2 ET⌊0.1⌋ =11×T2×910150=0.066×T2

EA is Agility experience; ET is Thieving experience; A is Agility level; T is Thieving level.

Based on 150 tears per hour.

The feather's colours match the colour of the magic spell element that the fighters and rangers are weak to, which makes it easy to know which arrow should be equipped once the Collector has made the correct call.

22239:

22242:
The dragon platebody (g) is a dragon platebody with a dragon platebody ornament kit attached to it, and is part of dragon gold-trimmed armour. The attached ornament kit gives no additional bonuses, and is only used to add aesthetics to the platebody. It costs 7,345,316 for both the parts to make the dragon platebody (g).

While the platebody is untradeable in its ornamented state, it can be dismantled anytime, returning the tradeable platebody and ornament kit.

This item can be stored in the treasure chest of a costume room, provided that the interface of the corresponding clue tier is opened before attempting to store the item. Alternatively, the item can be used on the opened treasure chest to insert it without viewing the interface, as part of the dragon gold-trimmed armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

To fully charge an enhanced trident, it would cost 9,520,000 coins, requiring one death rune, one chaos rune, 5 fire runes, and a Zulrah scale per charge. Players can configure the charges while the trident is in their bank by right-clicking on Configure-Charges, as long as players have the required materials.

If lost on death, any scales that were used to charge the trident will appear on the floor along with the uncharged trident.

22296:
The staff of light is a one-handed bladed staff which requires 75 Attack and 75 Magic to wield. It is created by using Saradomin's light on a staff of the dead. This process is irreversible.

The staff of light inherits all of the staff of the dead's effects. The only differences between them is that the staff of light autocasts the Saradomin Strike god spell rather than the Flames of Zamorak god spell, and is unable to autocast Arceuus combat spells. In addition, it counts as both a Saradominist and a Zamorakian item while in the God Wars Dungeon and in the Desert Bandit Camp.

The staff of light cannot be upgraded with a magic fang to provide the additional magic attack bonus and toxic effect given to the toxic staff of the dead.
22299:
The ancient medallion is a drop obtained from revenants found in the Revenant Caves.

It can be given to the Emblem Trader wandering around in the Revenant Caves in exchange for 4,000,000 coins. This must be done while on the official Bounty Hunter world. The statuette cannot be given to him in Edgeville. A chisel can be used on the ancient medallion to break it into 8,000 revenant ether.

Much like the bracelet of ethereum, the medallion is always lost on death, even if it is the only item in the player's inventory.
22302:

22308:

22316:
The prop sword is a weapon first obtained as a reward from the 2018 Birthday event. It is the iconic sword seen in the logo of RuneScape from 2001 to 2007.

While equipped, players can right-click the sword in the Equipment Stats interface to perform an emote, in which players assume a fencing position and slash the air to create the letters "RS", the acronym for "RuneScape".

Despite being a sword, its combat styles are the same as those of a warhammer. It offers very large attack penalties and is nearly useless as an actual weapon. As such, it is allowed during "fun weapon" fights in legacy duels within the Emir's Arena.

When wielded, a "Slash" option will appear on other players. Picking this option will cause the player to slash their target. The hit is just an animation and no damage is dealt, nor does it count as entering combat. There is a chance that players may "fumble" the sword, dropping it to the ground where it must be picked up.

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room.
22318:
The pet dark core is a pet dropped by the Corporeal Beast. It is the dark energy core that is summoned during the fight with the Corporeal Beast. Players can right click "Metamorphosis" to change between the dark core and the Corporeal Critter, which is a smaller version of the Corporeal Beast.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.
22319:
The Jal-Nib-Rek (roughly translated as Foreign Nibbler Baby/Young) is a Jal-Nib dropped by TzKal-Zuk upon completion of the Inferno. The standard drop rate is 1/100, but this is increased to 1/75 if TzKal-Zuk is defeated while on a Slayer task. Players may also exchange their infernal capes by speaking to TzHaar-Ket-Keh for a 1/100 chance of obtaining the pet. Providing a player defeats TzKal-Zuk while on a slayer task for a 1/75 chance of the pet, and hands in their cape, the overall chance of receiving the pet from either the boss or the cape is approximately 1/43.

Players can right click "Metamorphosis" to change between the Jal-Nib and TzRek-Zuk, which is a smaller version of TzKal-Zuk.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. 22320:
The champion's lamp is an item obtained from the Chest of Champions in the north side of the Champions' Challenge area after defeating a champion.

Rubbing the lamp awards the player ten times the experience that is given immediately after a champion's defeat. For example, rubbing a lamp obtained after defeating the Hobgoblin Champion will award players with 2,320 Hitpoints and Slayer experience. Players will receive a confirmation message before gaining the experience.

The lamp cannot be banked. If players were to somehow lose the lamp, it can be reclaimed from the Chest of Champions.
22321:
The rotten cabbage is an item available only to Jagex Moderators, similar to the rotten potato, egg and carrot. It was first seen used for spectating players during the deadman mode seasonal servers.

It is known to have four right-click options:

Control

Spectate

Info

Options
22323:
The Sanguinesti staff is a one-handed powered staff requiring 82 Magic to wield, available as a rare drop from the Theatre of Blood. Like most powered staves, it is only tradeable when it is fully uncharged. Named after the Sanguinesti region, the staff was crafted by Lord Lowerniel Drakan himself, and was given to Lady Verzik Vitur as a gift for her assistance in the Misthalin–Morytania War.

The Sanguinesti staff can be combined with a holy ornament kit to make a Saradomin-themed holy Sanguinesti staff. Though its stats do not change, it makes it usable as a Saradomin item in the God Wars Dungeon.

The staff's charge cannot be used against another player in dangerous PvP, only safe minigames.
22324:
The Ghrazi rapier is a one-handed stab weapon obtainable as a rare drop from the Theatre of Blood. It requires level 80 Attack to wield. It provides the highest strength and stab bonus out of any weapon for its attack speed. This makes the rapier tied with the blade of Saeldor and the Inquisitor's mace for the melee weapon with the highest damage output for general use, although it is outperformed by the Osmumten's fang against high defence monsters and Scythe of Vitur against large monsters.

The Ghrazi tribe was the most vicious vampyre tribe on Vampyrium. This rapier was once wielded by a fearsome Ghrazi warlord who was slain in battle by Verzik Vitur's father, who gave it to Verzik.

The rapier can be combined with a holy ornament kit to make a Saradomin-themed holy Ghrazi rapier. This cosmetic upgrade won't change the stats in any way, but it will make the rapier count as a Saradomin item in the God Wars Dungeon.
22325:
The Scythe of Vitur is a two-handed slash weapon requiring 80 Attack and 90 Strength to wield, available as a rare drop from the Theatre of Blood. The scythe is extremely valuable due to its immense power against most large monsters. It is only tradeable when fully uncharged.

The Scythe of Vitur was once wielded by the founder of House Vitur, a vampyre now worshipped as a god.

Although the Scythe of Vitur has a stab bonus, it does not have a Stab combat style.
22326:
The Justiciar faceguard is obtained as a rare drop from the Theatre of Blood. It is part of the justiciar armour set, and requires level 75 Defence to equip.

When the full set of Justiciar armour is equipped, the player gains a set effect: all combat damage taken is reduced (except in PvP). The exact formula for the amount of damage reduced is bonus3000, where bonus is the player's defence bonus for that particular style. For example, if an enemy was using a crush style attack, and the player has a crush defence bonus of +450, then 15% of the damage (450/3,000) is reduced.

The Justiciar faceguard is counted as a Saradomin item in the God Wars Dungeon.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Justiciar armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
22327:
The Justiciar chestguard is part of the justiciar armour set requiring 75 Defence to equip. It is a rare drop from the Theatre of Blood.

Wearing the full Justiciar armour set grants the passive effect: all non-PvP combat damage is reduced by bonus3000, where bonus is the player's current defence bonus being rolled against by the attacker's attack style. For example, if an enemy attacks with crush and the player has a crush defence bonus of +450, then 15% (450/3,000) of the damage is reduced.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Justiciar armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

22355:
A holy handegg is an item originally obtained during the 2018 Easter event. It was a reward for defeating the Colossal Chocco Chicken.

With the item in your inventory, you can right-click Use on it, and click another player. If the player has their right hand free, they will catch the egg, and it will end up in their weapon slot. Ironmen cannot throw the egg to other players, nor can they have the egg be thrown to them.

After the easter event was removed, they became available from Diango's Toy Store.

Being thrown an egg will cause the person that catches it to interrupt their action.

22365:
The Shayzien favour certificate was a quest reward for completing Tale of the Righteous. Reading this granted the player 10% Shayzien favour, where there would be a confirmation message before doing so. Should the player have wished to use it some other time, they could destroy it (if bank space was an issue) and reclaim it from Lord Shiro Shayzien.

The certificate was removed alongside the entire Kourend Favour system on 10 January 2024 with the release of Children of the Sun.
22367:
The Kourend favour certificate was a quest reward for completing Client of Kourend. Reading this granted the player 20% favour towards a city of their choosing, where there would be a confirmation message before doing so. Should the player have wished to use it some other time, they could destroy it (if bank space was an issue) and reclaim it from Veos in Port Piscarilius. This item could not leave a placeholder.

If the player had not started gaining Piscarilius favour, it was recommended to use the certificate to bypass the first 20% favour there, as it was costly and time consuming requiring three planks and nine nails per 0.5% favour gained.

The certificate was removed alongside the entire Kourend Favour system on 10 January 2024 with the release of Children of the Sun.
22376:
The Olmlet is a pet obtained from the Chambers of Xeric. It is a much smaller version of the Great Olm, with its body fully visible. Players have a 1/53 chance of receiving the pet when they receive an item from the unique drop table after killing the Great Olm.

The olmlet is able to metamorphose into five other pets which are smaller versions of the other bosses encountered inside the Chambers of Xeric, which requires using metamorphic dust on it. The dust can be acquired from the Chambers' Challenge Mode version and clearing it under a specific time.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.

The olmlet is able to metamorphose into five other pets which are smaller versions of the other bosses encountered inside the Chambers of Xeric, which requires using metamorphic dust on it. The dust can be acquired from the Chambers' Challenge Mode version and clearing it under a specific time.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.
22388:

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room. It can also be mounted on a cape hanger in an Achievement Gallery.

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room. It can also be mounted on a cape hanger in an Achievement Gallery.
22398:
The Ivandis flail is a one-handed staff created by the player during A Taste of Hope from a chain, an enchanted emerald sickle (b) and the rod of Ivandis. The flail requires an Attack level of 40 to wield. It is a silver weapon and can deal full damage to vampyres of all tiers and gives a 20% damage bonus against them. It can also autocast standard spellbook spells.

This flail is effective in damaging and killing the vyrewatch because, despite their sufficient mind-reading ability to predict attacks and avoid damage, the flail is incredibly unpredictable and random. The sickle head further increases the unpredictability of the weapon. Thus, attackers do not hit the Vyrewatch in the intended way, rendering their mind-reading useless.

The flail retains the ability to cast Bloom from the silver sickle (b). This versatility lets a player kill ghasts, vampyre juvinates and vyrewatch with a single weapon.

While players can make a flail themselves after the quest, it is much easier to purchase one from Vertida Sefalatis for 20,000 coins in the old Myreque Hideout under Old Man Ral's home or from Perdu for 30,000 coins from the Lost Property shop. During Sins of the Father, an Ivandis flail is used to create a blisterwood flail in the hideout.
22402: The mysterious herb is a herb obtained from Serafina's home during A Taste of Hope. It is used to create the potion and blood potion, along with some mysterious crushed meat.
22403: The mysterious meat is obtained from Serafina's home during A Taste of Hope. It is crushed with a pestle and mortar to create mysterious crushed meat, which is the second ingredient used to create the potion and blood potion.
22404: The mysterious crushed meat is obtained from Serafina's home during A Taste of Hope. It is obtained by crushing mysterious meat with a pestle and mortar. It is the second ingredient used to create the potion and blood potion.
22405:
Vials of blood are obtained as drops from the Theatre of Blood or made by squeezing 50 blood sacs into a vial. It is used as the base instead of a vial of water when creating bastion and battlemage potions.

It is also used to charge the Scythe of Vitur, with each vial of blood, along with 200 blood runes, providing 100 charges. It can be charged by depositing the items into the vyre well in Ver Sinhaza or Darkmeyer and using the Scythe of Vitur on it.

Vials of blood may also be used to pay the aranei scout near the portal to Castle Drakan to move the player's grave near to them, if they had died whilst fighting the Maggot King. Depending on the current prices of vials of blood, this may be the most cost-effective way to pay.
22407: The blood potion is obtained during A Taste of Hope by using the mysterious herb with a vial of blood, then adding mysterious crushed meat to the Unfinished blood potion. It is to be used on the door in Serafina's home, which will open this time.
22408: The unfinished potion is obtained during A Taste of Hope by using the mysterious herb with a vial of water. A mysterious crushed meat is then added to it to create a potion.
22409: The potion is obtained during A Taste of Hope by using the mysterious herb with a vial of water, then adding mysterious crushed meat to the unfinished potion. It is to be used on the door in Serafina's home.
22413: Flaygian's notes are obtained during A Taste of Hope. They are the results of Flaygian Screwte's effort to translate the Haemalchemy book that the player found during Darkness of Hallowvale. It contains some notes about the vampyre's immunities, and Screwte's theories on how to overcome them.
22414:
A chain is an item used to link two cannonballs together to create two chainshot cannonballs for boat combat. These require the same Smithing level, and gives the added bonus of halving a target's movement speed for 8 ticks (4.8s).

They are created at an anvil with one steel bar, requiring level 34 Smithing and granting 37.5 experience.

Aside from making chainshot cannonballs, they are used to create the Ivandis flail by linking the enchanted emerald sickle (b) and the rod of Ivandis together.

Chains can be freely obtained from a crate in the old Myreque Hideout under Old Man Ral's house during A Taste of Hope. After the quest, it can be obtained again from the same place, but the player can only collect one at a time without performing the drop trick.
22415:
Tome of experience may refer to:

Temple Trekking rewards:

Agility tome

Firemaking tome

Fishing tome

Mining tome

Slayer tome

Thieving tome

Woodcutting tome

Tome of experience (A Taste of Hope), reward for completing the A Taste of Hope quest

Tome of experience (The Blood Moon Rises), reward for completing the quest The Blood Moon Rises
22416:
The Turncloak can be found in upper floor of the Crombwick Manor, which is accessed through the Sisterhood Sanctuary.

The book is written from the perspective of Phosani, the Justiciar of the Wolf, and describes her and her companions Insela and Otrava surrendering their squadron, pledging allegiance to Lord Drakan and betraying Saradomin during the God Wars.

This book cannot be stored in a player-owned house bookcase.
22420:
The bloody grimoire is an old book that can be found in the Sisterhood Sanctuary. It can only be obtained by using the Telekinetic Grab spell to reach it.

The book is authored by Otrava, a member of the Sisterhood. It describes the author's discovery of a damaged version of the Senntisten Scriptures from their slain enemies, and details how they used their newfound knowledge of blood magic to create blood potions; namely, the bastion and battlemage potions.

In addition, the book lists two more recipes for a 'totality potion' and 'vigour potion' that were crossed out due to instability and a lack of ingredients, respectively.

This book cannot be stored in a player-owned house bookcase.
22422:
The Elixir of Everlasting is a scroll containing the formula to the fabled elixir created by Otrava, a high-ranking member of the Sisterhood and its divine healer. It can be obtained by using an old key on the chest on the 2nd floor of church in Slepe.

While the Elixir of Everlasting is able to extend the drinker's life indefinitely, it had the side effect of causing the drinker to sleep for longer periods of time, until they eventually become trapped in an eternal slumber, never to wake up.

Phosani, along with other high-ranking members of the Sisterhood, drank this without knowing of its side effects, and fell into a deep sleep. Realising the consequences of messing with the natural order, the people of modern-day Slepe (its original name currently unknown), in accordance to the laws set by Phosani, moved the sleeping members of the Sisterhood deep into the Sanctuary with all their possessions and hid the formula itself away to prevent others from suffering its side effects.

Despite this, several notes about the elixir remain in the Sisterhood Sanctuary, albeit most of them have been scribbled over the top with hastily written warnings. Daer Krand, who is performing research on the elixir within the Sanctuary, is currently attempting to recreate it.

During Sins of the Father, it is discovered that Kroy, a vampyre herbalist, found the formula and recreated it. Alongside Damien Leucurte, a vampyre noble, the both of them used the elixir on Slepe's townsfolk by mixing it with their local beverage, Bloody Bracer, causing the town's second Sleeper Plague, in order to perform blood tithes on them as the sleeping victims only require a fraction of the blood compared to an awake human due to an increased vampyre population and dwindling blood supply.
22424:
Buried Alive is an old piece of parchment received from Hameln the Jester in the Slepe church.

The scroll documents the high-ranked members of the Sisterhood being moved deeper into the Sisterhood Sanctuary, who did not wake after a fortnight (two weeks). This was done in accordance to the laws set by Phosani, the Sisterhood's founder.

This scroll cannot be stored in a player-owned house bookcase.
22426:
The deed is received from a table in the eastern room of the Crombwick Manor's ground floor, which is accessed through the Sisterhood Sanctuary.

The deed, signed by Lord Drakan himself on the 38th of Septober on the 661st Year of the Fourth Age, certifies that the Sleepers Manor (known today as the Crombwick Manor) is now owned by Ichabod Crombwick as a commemoration for his loyalty to the Drakans.

The deed cannot be stored in a player-owned house bookcase.
22430:
The bloody bracer is a type of ale that restores 2 Hitpoints and drains Prayer by 4% + 2. The bloody bracer may heal you above your maximum Hitpoints once. Upon drinking the ale, a message in the chatbox will state The tincture tastes great, but you feel an evil within you stir..

It is purchasable at the Rat & Bat in the town of Slepe. Unlike other ales, it cannot be created through brewing.
22435:
The enchanted emerald sickle (b) is an item obtained by using an emerald on a silver sickle (b), then casting Lvl-2 Enchant on the resulting emerald sickle (b). It is to be used on a rod of Ivandis while having a chain in the inventory to create the Ivandis flail.

The sickle retains the right-click "bloom" option from the silver sickle (b), which can be used next to rotten logs, branches, or bushes in Mort Myre swamp to obtain Mort myre fungi, stems, and pears. These items can be used to fill the Druid pouch which allows the player to fight Ghasts. Bloom can also be cast on dead vines in the Ancient Guthixian Temple to grow them into flowering vines which can be picked to obtain a vine flower.

It can also be used to harm Vampyres and Vampyre Juvinates, but this is not recommended due to its weak stats.
22437:
The rotten carrot is an item available only to Jagex Moderators, similar to the rotten potato, egg and cabbage.

Using the rotten carrot on an account will instantly kill them and show an interface with the account's bank and inventory contents, which will be teleported to the user's bank.

It is used for the Bot Busting stream on the Old School RuneScape Twitch channel, which began at 8pm BST/3pm EST on Saturday June 16th, 2018.
22438:
Justiciar armour set is an item obtained by exchanging a set of items with a Grand Exchange clerk via their right-click "Sets" option and clicking on the appropriate item set within the Item Sets interface.

It is commonly made in order to conveniently sell all three components of Justiciar armour at once.

22473:
Lil' Zik is a pet that can be obtained from completing the Theatre of Blood. It is a much smaller version of Verzik Vitur's final form. Players have a chance of receiving the pet when looting the monumental chests in Verzik's treasure vault. The drop rate is dependent on the player's performance in the raid, unaffected by that of teammates, ranging from 1/650 to 1/6,500 in regular raids and ranging from 1/500 to 1/5,000 in Hard Mode raids. The maximum rate is reached with 10 individual points (which are invisible to the players; the maximum per player is 32, or 18 if not including the MVP bonuses for each room). The highest rate is reached by dying no more than twice per raid, with more deaths allowed if the player deals the most damage in some rooms, assuming participation in each room.

Lil' Zik is able to metamorphose into five other pets which are smaller versions of the other bosses encountered in the Theatre of Blood, which requires using Sanguine dust on it. The dust can be acquired from the Theatre's Hard Mode version and clearing it under a specific time.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.
22481:
The Sanguinesti staff is a one-handed powered staff requiring 82 Magic to wield, available as a rare drop from the Theatre of Blood. Like most powered staves, it is only tradeable when it is fully uncharged. Named after the Sanguinesti region, the staff was crafted by Lord Lowerniel Drakan himself, and was given to Lady Verzik Vitur as a gift for her assistance in the Misthalin–Morytania War.

The Sanguinesti staff can be combined with a holy ornament kit to make a Saradomin-themed holy Sanguinesti staff. Though its stats do not change, it makes it usable as a Saradomin item in the God Wars Dungeon.

The staff's charge cannot be used against another player in dangerous PvP, only safe minigames.
22486:
The Scythe of Vitur is a two-handed slash weapon requiring 80 Attack and 90 Strength to wield, available as a rare drop from the Theatre of Blood. The scythe is extremely valuable due to its immense power against most large monsters. It is only tradeable when fully uncharged.

The Scythe of Vitur was once wielded by the founder of House Vitur, a vampyre now worshipped as a god.

Although the Scythe of Vitur has a stab bonus, it does not have a Stab combat style.

Players can use the right-click "Change" option to alter the cape's appearance to other tiers, providing that they have met the completion count required for them.

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room.

22502:
Sinhaza shroud tier 5 is a cosmetic cape that can be obtained from the Mysterious Stranger by the entrance to the Theatre of Blood after completing 2,000 Theatre of Blood raids.

Players can use the right-click "Change" option to alter the cape's appearance to other tiers.

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room.
22504:
Serafina's diary is an old diary that appears on the ground after defeating The Maiden of Sugadinti in the Theatre of Blood. It can also be obtained from the grand bookshelves in Verzik Vitur's treasure vault beneath her throne room, accessed after her defeat.

The book details the personal thoughts of Serafina, and explains how she was transformed into The Maiden of Sugadinti. The same story, but from her brother's perspective, can be read in his diary.

If lost, it can be reclaimed by defeating The Maiden of Sugadinti, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house.
22506:
The Butcher is a book that appears on the ground after defeating the Pestilent Bloat in the Theatre of Blood. It can also be obtained from the grand bookshelves in Verzik Vitur's treasure vault beneath her throne room, accessed after her defeat.

The book details how the Pestilent Bloat came to be, being created by an erratic vampyre known as "The Butcher" using the body parts of different races such as ogres and cyclopes.

If lost, it can be reclaimed by defeating the Pestilent Bloat, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house.
22508:
Arachnids of Vampyrium is a book that appears on the ground after defeating the Nylocas Vasilias in the Theatre of Blood. It can also be obtained from the grand bookshelves in Verzik Vitur's treasure vault beneath her throne room, accessed after her defeat.

The book gives details about the various species of nylocas, and tells how they were brought from Vampyrium, the vampyre's homeworld.

If lost, it can be reclaimed by defeating the Nylocas Vasilias, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house.
22510:
The Shadow Realm is a book that appears on the ground after defeating Sotetseg in the Theatre of Blood. It can also be obtained from the grand bookshelves in Verzik Vitur's treasure vault beneath her throne room, accessed after her defeat.

The book details the experiments performed on Sotetseg and how the author manipulated it to travel into the Shadow Realm.

If lost, it can be reclaimed by defeating Sotetseg, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house.
22512:
The Wild Hunt is a journal that appears on the ground after defeating Xarpus in the Theatre of Blood. It can also be obtained from the grand bookshelves in Verzik Vitur's treasure vault beneath her throne room, accessed after her defeat.

The journal is written by Lowerniel Drakan, and it tells of his desire to hunt down the Yarasa Xarpus from his homeworld of Vampyrium.

If lost, it can be reclaimed by defeating Xarpus, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house.
22514:
Verzik Vitur - Patient Record are a set of medical notes that appear on the ground after defeating Verzik Vitur in the Theatre of Blood. It can also be obtained from the grand bookshelves in her treasure vault beneath her throne room, accessed after her defeat.

The patient record, written by Vulcan Orvoros, contains medical notes on Verzik Vitur, detailing a sickness she was infected with after a nylocas bite. In A Night at the Theatre it is revealed that the bite was actually a result of a prototype nylocas biting her when she presented it to Ranis Drakan, which injected a parasite that eventually matured into the Nylocas Queen and killed her, before the Queen ordered him killed too.

If lost, it can be reclaimed by defeating Verzik Vitur, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house.
22517:
Escape crystals are a consumable teleport item that can be equipped in the ring slot. It can be purchased from Rick in the 1st floor of the Wizards' Tower, as well as from the Mysterious Stranger in Ver Sinhaza, for 75,000 coins.

The crystal acts similarly to a respawn teleport, teleporting players away from various activities, which Hardcore ironmen/group ironmen may consider as dangerous upon death:

Players can also use the crystal on their group members to activate them, allowing teleportation of teammates out of danger in an instant. To enable this, players must right-click the crystal and select "Configure", then choose the first option. Both players must have a crystal for this to work, and both crystals will be consumed in the process.

Additionally, the crystal can be configured to auto-activate upon taking damage (including zeros) after a specified time of inactivity (ranging from 2 to 300 seconds) via the "Configure" option; in this case, inactivity is defined as any time the player is not typing, clicking/tapping within the game, moving/zooming the camera, or moving the mouse. For example, if players configure the timer to 30 seconds, they will automatically be teleported away from the aforementioned activities upon taking damage after being inactive for at least 30 seconds. However, if the player has just logged in or hopped worlds and takes damage, the escape crystal will activate immediately even if the inactivity timer has not elapsed. This function will apply in The Gauntlet if the crystal was in the player's inventory upon entry, and is configured to auto-activate.

The crystal will NOT activate while the player is moving. If the inactive time is reached at any point during movement, the crystal will activate when the player stops moving.

The crystal can also be equipped and toggled to act in the same manner as a ring of life, although this will cause the crystal to be unable to teleport out from the aforementioned activities, so players must have it unequipped should they wish to be able to do so in those activities.

It is one of the few items whose teleports will work up to level 30 Wilderness, while most other means of teleportation will not work above level 20 Wilderness.
22521:
A coin pouch is an item obtained from pickpocketing certain NPCs, which contains several coins depending on the NPC it was obtained from. To obtain the coins from them, players can simply click their stack of coin pouches to open them all at once, or they can right-click them to open one at a time. They cannot be traded or banked.

Up to 28 coin pouches can stack in a player's inventory, after which the player must open them to collect the coins inside before being able to pickpocket more. This limit can be increased by completing the Ardougne Diary, where it increases to 56, 84, and 140 after completing the Medium, Hard, and Elite diaries, respectively.

Coin pouches have different variants depending on who the player pickpocketed it from; for example, a coin pouch from pickpocketing guards does not stack with pouches from pickpocketing Ardougne knights. NPCs who are pickpocketed via blackjacking yield coins directly while they are knocked out instead of coin pouches. If rogue equipment is used to receive double the loot from pickpocketing, only one coin pouch is obtained (containing the normal amount) while the other half is obtained directly as coins.

To obtain the coins from them, players can simply click their stack of coin pouches to open them all at once, or they can right-click them to open one at a time. They cannot be traded or banked.

Up to 28 coin pouches can stack in a player's inventory, after which the player must open them to collect the coins inside before being able to pickpocket more. This limit can be increased by completing the Ardougne Diary, where it increases to 56, 84, and 140 after completing the Medium, Hard, and Elite diaries, respectively.

Coin pouches have different variants depending on who the player pickpocketed it from; for example, a coin pouch from pickpocketing guards does not stack with pouches from pickpocketing Ardougne knights. NPCs who are pickpocketed via blackjacking yield coins directly while they are knocked out instead of coin pouches. If rogue equipment is used to receive double the loot from pickpocketing, only one coin pouch is obtained (containing the normal amount) while the other half is obtained directly as coins.

22541: The rotten strawberry is an item available only to Jagex Moderators, similar to the rotten potato, egg, cabbage, and carrot.
22542:
Viggora's chainmace is a one-handed spiked weapon that can be received as a drop from revenants found within the Revenant Caves. It was once owned by Viggora, the only human among the generals of Zaros during the Second Age. After his death, it was claimed by a follower of Zamorak, and was extensively used during the God Wars. This item counts as a Zamorakian item in the God Wars Dungeon.

The chainmace requires an Attack level of 60 to wield and has bonuses similar to the dragon scimitar, with the chainmace using crush attack styles rather than slash. Although it can be used in its uncharged form, it has a powerful passive effect within the Wilderness when charged with revenant ether.

Due to the damage increase of the passive effect, the chainmace is a popular item used for PvM within the Wilderness such as Wilderness Slayer tasks and killing revenants.

The chainmace can be upgraded to an ursine chainmace by attaching the claws of Callisto to it, requiring level 85 Smithing or paying Andros Mai 500,000 coins. Players can also dismantle an uncharged chainmace to receive 7,500 revenant ether, resulting in 1,305,000 coins and a loss of −3,105,985 coins.

22552:
Thammaron's sceptre is a powered staff requiring 60 Magic to wield, available as a drop from revenants. Like most powered staves, it is only tradeable when it is fully uncharged. It was once owned by Thammaron, a Tsutsaroth demon who was one of Zamorak's most trusted allies during the reign of Zaros, and later one of his key generals during the God Wars. This item counts as a Zamorakian item in the God Wars Dungeon.

The sceptre shares the same magic attack bonus as the trident of the seas, and has a powerful passive effect within the Wilderness when charged with revenant ether. In addition, unlike other powered staves, the sceptre can attack players outside of minigames. The sceptre also has a "Swap" option that allows players to switch it to Thammaron's sceptre (a), which is a variant that can autocast offensive combat spells from the standard spellbook (including Flames of Zamorak) and the Ancient Magicks.

The sceptre can be upgraded to an accursed sceptre by attaching the skull of Vet'ion to it, requiring level 85 Crafting or paying Phabelle Bile 500,000 coins. Players can also dismantle an uncharged sceptre to receive 7,500 revenant ether, resulting in 1,305,000 coins and a loss of −1,438,765 coins.

22557:
The amulet of avarice is an amulet that can be received as a drop from revenants found within the Revenant Caves. The amulet has the same combat bonuses as the amulet of glory, but has an additional 20% increase in accuracy and damage when fighting revenants, similar to a Salve amulet. The effects of the amulet do not stack with the Slayer helmet (i).

When worn, all drops received from NPCs within the Revenant Caves, Wilderness Slayer Cave and Chaos Temple will be in the form of bank notes, except for secondary supply rolls and uniques. However, equipping the amulet will cause the player to become skulled, similar to the cape of skulls. Attempting to equip the amulet gives a warning telling the player that this will happen. The skull cannot be removed until the amulet is unequipped, after which it behaves like a normal PK skull and disappears after twenty minutes. This behaviour is different from the cape of skulls, which will only keep the skull active for 20 minutes from the moment of equipping.

It is worth noting that while skulled (regardless of the source of the skull, except for the skull given by a high-risk PvP world), unique drops from revenants have their drop rate nearly doubled.

Wearing the amulet while looting a Zombie Pirate's Locker will note the drops other than the teleport anchoring scroll.

If the amulet is worn while killing the Revenant maledictus as a top-damaging player, they will obtain the Forinthry Surge skull for 30 minutes, a variant that provides an additional 15% accuracy and damage boost when fighting revenants. Taking off the amulet will automatically remove this buff.
22586:
The looting bag is a storage bag that can hold up to 28 stacks of any item. Only one looting bag can be in a player's possession at a time.

Tradeable items can only be stored whilst in the Wilderness, including the Ferox Enclave, by using them on the looting bag or via the looting bag's "Deposit" option. Stackable items like runes, arrows, or noted items stack in the looting bag as they would in the inventory. The bag may also be used in certain locations outside the Wilderness on PvP worlds. The contents of a looting bag cannot be recovered outside of a bank without destroying it or dying.
22589:
The reduced cadava potion is made by the Apothecary during the quest Making Friends with My Arm by giving him a cadava berry, requesting a variant of the cadava potion appropriate for the Wise Old Man's age. When given to the Wise Old Man he uses it to pretend to be dead for My Arm.

Attempting to drink the potion yields the chatbox message "However bad the day's been, drinking this is unlikely to make it better."

Once the Wise Old Man drinks the potion, he collapses, and the player puts him in a coffin to prove My Arm "killed" the Wise Old Man.
22590:
Goat dung is an item used in the quest Making Friends with My Arm. It is obtained by using a bucket on a pile of goat poo in the north-easternmost building in Weiss.

It is given to Snowflake to fertilise two herb patches in Weiss: one for the Weiss trolls to grow goutweed, and another for players to use after the quest, which, like the Troll Stronghold herb patch, will never be diseased.
22593:
Te salt is a type of salt that can be mined from te salt rocks in the Salt Mine beneath Weiss after the completion of Making Friends with My Arm. Along with Urt salt and Efh salt, it can be used to light fire pits that provide benefits (such as a permanent light source), and it is also used to create icy and stony basalts. Mining Te salt requires 72 Mining and is mined in chunks of 2-7 scaling with the player's level, granting the player 5 experience per salt mined. Mining enhancers do not work here.

A total of 1100 Te salt is required to construct all the permanent fires available (1 dehumidification, 3 eternal light, 1 nourishment, 1 unseasonal warmth). 100 Te salt is required to attune each portal to Weiss or Troll Stronghold in a Portal Chamber in a Player Owned House (for a total of 200 for both portals), and 1000 Te salt is required to attune a Portal Nexus to either (for a total of 2000 for both portals).Players will also need 250 Te, Efh, and Urt salts to build an Eternal brazier on each of their boats. Assuming the brazier is built on 5 boats (the current maximum), 1250 of each salt would be needed in total.
22597:
Urt salt is a type of salt that can be mined from urt salt rocks in the Salt Mine beneath Weiss after the completion of Making Friends with My Arm. Along with Te salt and Efh salt, it can be used to light fire pits that provide benefits (such as a permanent light source), and it is also used to create stony basalts. Mining Urt salt requires 72 Mining and is mined in chunks of 2-7 scaling with the player's level, granting the player 5 experience per salt mined. Mining enhancers do not work here.

700 Urt salt is required to construct all the available permanent fires (1 dehumidification, 3 eternal light, 1 nourishment, 1 unseasonal warmth). 250 Urt salt is required to construct an Eternal brazier on a boat. 300 Urt salt is required to attune a portal to Troll Stronghold in a Portal Chamber in a Player Owned House, and 3000 Urt salt is required to attune a Portal Nexus. Players will also need 250 Te, Efh, and Urt salts to build an Eternal brazier on each of their boats. Assuming the brazier is built on 5 boats (the current maximum), 1250 of each salt would be needed in total.
22599:
Icy basalt is an item that can be used to teleport to Weiss, near the herb patches. Using it to teleport consumes the icy basalt. It may only be used after finishing Making Friends with My Arm.

To create an icy basalt, players must use a basalt with 3 efh salt and 1 te salt.

This teleport can be incorporated into a portal within a Portal Chamber using 100 times the required resources (300 efh salt, 100 te salt, and 100 basalt), or in a Portal Nexus using 1,000 times the required resources (3,000 efh salt, 1,000 te salt, and 1,000 basalt).

Note: The resources for icy basalt (efh salt, te salt, and basalt) must be used for the portal chamber, not the created item.
22601:
Stony basalt is an item that can be used to teleport to the Troll Stronghold entrance, below the climbing rocks shortcut. The stony basalt is consumed when it is used to teleport. It may only be used after completing Making Friends with My Arm.

To create stony basalt, players must use 1 basalt with 3 urt salt and 1 te salt.

With level 73 Agility and the completion of the Hard Fremennik Diary, an option to teleport to the Stronghold roof is unlocked, past the climbing rocks shortcut. This alternate destination works like all Agility shortcuts, you may boost to pass the check, although being drained when you otherwise meet the requirement will still put you on the roof.

This teleport can be incorporated into a portal within a Portal Chamber using 100 times the required resources (300 urt salt, 100 te salt, and 100 basalt), or in a Portal Nexus using 1,000 times the required resources (3,000 urt salt, 1,000 te salt, and 1,000 basalt).

Note: The resources for Stony basalt (urt salt, te salt, and basalt) must be used for the portal chamber, not the created item.
22603:
Basalt is a rock that can be mined from basalt rocks in the Salt Mine beneath Weiss after the completion of Making Friends with My Arm. It requires level 72 Mining and grants 5 Mining experience. Mining enhancers do not work here.

It can be used with te salt, along with urt or efh salts to create icy basalt and stony basalt. 200 Basalt is required to attune a portal to both (100 each) Troll Stronghold and Weiss in a Portal Chamber in a Player Owned House, and 2000 Basalt is required to attune a Portal Nexus with both teleports (1000 each). Basalt rocks have a 1/7 chance of being depleted each time they are mined.

Snowflake, who is located just outside the mine entrance, is able to note any basalt you have mined for free.
22610:
Vesta's spear (bh) is a two-handed weapon requiring 75 Attack to wield, and is purchased from the Bounty Hunter Store for 300 points.

As with all Ancient Warriors' equipment from Bounty Hunter, it is initially purchased in inactive form, and must be charged with 5,000,000 coins before it can be used by the player. Upon dying in PvP, the coins used to activate the item are given to the killer, and players are left with the inactive item.

In addition, it can only be used within Daimon's Crater, Castle Wars, Clan Wars, Soul Wars, the TzHaar Fight Pit, and both the player-owned house and Clan Hall combat rings; attempting to attack anything outside the listed areas will result in the player being interrupted from doing so.
22613:
Vesta's longsword (bh) is a slash weapon requiring 75 Attack to wield, and is purchased from the Bounty Hunter Store for 650 points.

As with all Ancient Warriors' equipment from Bounty Hunter, it is initially purchased in inactive form, and must be charged with 50,000,000 coins before it can be used by the player. Upon dying in PvP, the coins used to activate the item are given to the killer, and players are left with the inactive item. That said, the activated form is preserved and the coins aren't lost if the longsword is one of the player's protected items.

Unlike other Ancient Warriors' weapons bought from the Bounty Hunter Store, this variant of the Vesta's longsword appears to share the same restrictions as Vesta's blighted longsword, meaning it can be used on a Bounty Hunter world while in the Wilderness, inside Daimon's Crater, Castle Wars, Clan Wars, Soul Wars, the TzHaar Fight Pit, and both the player-owned house and Clan Hall combat rings. The weapon cannot be used for PvM or PvP combat activities in other circumstances.
22616:

Statius's warhammer is a crush weapon requiring level 78 Strength and 20 Attack to wield. It is part of Statius's equipment, a set of Ancient Warriors' equipment.

On permanent Deadman Mode worlds, it is dropped by any monster found in the Wilderness as part of a global loot table, the chance being relative to the combat level of the monster. It can also be obtained from looting Deadman's chests and as a drop from breach monsters in Deadman: Annihilation.

The warhammer works in place of a regular hammer for building storage chests in the Chambers of Xeric.

22663:
The pet smoke devil is a pet dropped by the Thermonuclear smoke devil. It is a much smaller version of the (Thermonuclear) smoke devil. Players can right click "Metamorphosis" to change between the regular smoke devil and the thermonuclear smoke devil.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.
22664: The Scythe of Vitur is a tool initially used by Jagex Moderators during the RuneFest 2018. Afterwards, it was used in various bot-busting streams to help kill bots.
22666: The rubber chicken is a tool initially used by Jagex Moderators during the RuneFest 2018. Afterwards, it was used in various bot-busting streams to help kill bots.
22671:
The tattered Kalphite Queen head is an item dropped by the Kalphite Queen. Players are guaranteed to receive one for their 256th Kalphite Queen kill; players who already had 256 kills before the tattered head's release will receive it on their next kill instead.

It can be stuffed at the Taxidermist in Canifis by using the item on her and paying 50,000 coins, returning a stuffed tattered kq head. When players take it to her, she will tell players "That's not the most impressive head I've seen but I think I can just about manage this one. Preserving insects is always tricky. I'll have to be careful..."

Once stuffed, it can be mounted at a gilded display within the skill hall in a player-owned house, granting 223 Construction alongside 200 Attack, Strength, Defence, Magic, and Ranged experience, with players being given the option to decline the combat experience before mounting the heads.

Unlike the normal kq head, the tattered head's only use is to be stuffed and mounted, as talking to it is part of the Desert Elite Achievement Diary. As such, it cannot be used to create the green slayer helmet or be sacrificed to the Dark Altar.

If a player dies or teleports out while the Kalphite Queen is killed on the 256th kill, the player will not receive the drop and will be unable to obtain the Kq head (tattered).
22675:
The scroll sack is obtained after completing 100 master Treasure Trails. It is a large sack containing many clue scrolls, with a spade on the side of it.

It can be stored in the treasure chest in a player-owned house. If lost, it can be re-obtained by speaking to Watson or by completing another master clue scroll.

As of 7 August 2026, there are 37,188 players that have completed at least 100 master Treasure Trails.
22677: The crypt key is an item obtained during A Night at the Theatre, in which players kill a vyrewatch in Ranis Drakan's crypt to access the chamber containing his coffin.
22679: Hetty's empty cauldron is an item obtained during the 2018 Halloween event and is given to the player by Hetty. It is to be filled with a bucket of water and two cabbages (in any order) to create a cauldron of water & cabbages for Eric.
22680: Cauldron of cabbages is an item obtained during the 2018 Halloween event made by filling Hetty's empty cauldron with two cabbages. It is to be filled with a bucket of water to create a cauldron of water & cabbages for Eric.
22681: Cauldron of water is an item obtained during the 2018 Halloween event made by filling Hetty's empty cauldron with a bucket of water. It is to be filled with two cabbages to create a cauldron of water & cabbages for Eric.
22682: Cauldron of water & cabbages is an item obtained during the 2018 Halloween event.
22684:
Eek is a small spider that plays a part in the 2018 Halloween event. She can be found in the small graveyard north of the church next to Rimmington and Port Sarim. She understands humans, due to spiders spending much of their time in human settlements. She got her name from the scared exclamation "eek", as it was a sound she liked. After the player completes the event, Eric gives Eek to the player.

Completing any subsequent Halloween event will allow players to obtain Eek.

Eek can be wielded in the weapon slot, and is classified as a fun weapon in legacy duels within the Emir's Arena because she gives the wielding player negative bonuses. Players have the right-click option of Talk-to, in which a random conversation takes place between the player and Eek.

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room.
22687: The church lectern was an item obtainable during the 2018 Halloween event by taking it next to the altar in the Rimmington church. It was given to Eric in order for him to appear imposing when he is reading a scary story for his niece and nephew, Angel and Henja.
22710:
A curator's medallion is used to build a mounted digsite pendant within a player-owned house portal nexus room. It is obtained from Curator Haig Halen, after having discovered the digsite pendant in the Varrock Museum, in exchange for 1 digsite pendant of any charge, 250 cut rubies, 500 fire runes (combination runes will not work), and 100 cosmic runes. The clean necklace must be found before you are given the option to deposit rubies.

Curator Haig Halen accepts noted rubies and any amount of rubies up to 250. The digsite pendant and the runes will not be accepted until the rubies have been delivered or the player has enough in their inventory to satisfy the remaining quantity. The remaining rubies (minimum of 1), digsite pendant, and runes must all be delivered at the same time, as the final rubies will not be accepted without the rest of the required items. The ability to deliver rubies piecemeal mostly benefits Ultimate Ironmen who do not have access to the noting facilities of a bank.

The medallion is lost on death, even though it is an untradeable item.

The medallion will be lost permanently if destroyed. A new medallion can be claimed from Curator Haig Halen by exchanging another digsite pendant and the required rubies, fire runes and cosmic runes. As such, Ultimate Ironmen are strongly recommended to ensure they have the appropriate Construction level to add it to their player-owned house before claiming a medallion.
22711:
The collection log is a book that players can receive from The Collector near the stairs in the Varrock Museum's ground floor. It records nearly every unique drop the player has obtained from various content in Old School RuneScape. The player does not need to have claimed a collection log for it to start tracking drops.

Drops obtained prior to its release are not automatically recorded for any player, excluding untradeable items (such as pets) provided that they can be tracked by the game; for example, long bones the player had traded to Barlak or buried before the log's release were not added to it, but any long bones in the player's possession were added. Ironman players are able to add some items collected prior to the release by using the item on the collection log item; this does not apply to Group Ironman players. Using an ineligible or already logged item on the collection log gives the message Your collection log has already accounted for that item.

Each entry in the log is tracked by the item itself, not where it was obtained. This means that collection log item slots can be shared across multiple pages. For example, obtaining a dragon pickaxe from the Chaos Elemental will also log it under other bosses that drop it, such as Callisto and the King Black Dragon.

There is a cap on the amount each item can be tracked, depending on the item in question. For example, Zulrah's scales will only be tracked up to 65,535 and bracelets of ethereum up to 250.

It can be stored in a bookcase within a player-owned house, and can also be accessed from the adventurer's log within a player's Achievement Gallery and the Character Summary interface.

There are currently a total of 1,920 slots to fill in the collection log, with a total of 1,712 unique entries being tracked. Pets, gilded equipment, and 3rd age equipment account for 129 of the 201 slots containing duplicate items.

The dragon hasta is a one-handed melee weapon that requires 60 Attack and completion of the Smithing section of the Barbarian Training miniquest to be wielded. Like spears, the dragon hasta can be poisoned.

Dragon hastae are obtained as loot from the brimstone chest, which requires a brimstone key to open. The dragon hasta is obtained in broken form and can be repaired for free by showing it to Otto Godblessed (the repair does not require Barbarian Smithing).

Like most hastae, it provides negative defensive bonuses, but when equipped with a shield, the combined defence bonuses will be higher than those provided by the dragon spear.

As with most dragon equipment, the dragon hasta cannot be made from raw materials using the Smithing skill.

22754: Wyrm bonemeal is an item that is used for worship at the Ectofuntus. It consists of a pot filled with wyrm bones or strykewyrm bones that have been crushed in the bone grinder at the Ectofuntus.
22760:
The Lovakengj favour certificate was a quest reward for completing The Forsaken Tower. Reading this granted the player 10% Lovakengj favour, where there would be a confirmation message before doing so. Should the player have wished to use it some other time, they could destroy it (if bank space was an issue) and reclaim it from Lady Vulcana Lovakengj.

The certificate was removed alongside the entire Kourend Favour system on 10 January 2024 with the release of Children of the Sun.
22761: Dinh's hammer is the ancient hammer requested by Undor in The Forsaken Tower.
22763: The 8-gallon jug is an item obtained during The Forsaken Tower. It is found in a cupboard on the ground floor, and is used to solve a puzzle to obtain Dinh's hammer.
22764: The 5-gallon jug is a quest item in The Forsaken Tower quest. It is found in a cupboard on the ground floor and is used to solve the puzzle to obtain Dinh's hammer.
22775: Ancient letter is a letter found in the western crate on the ground floor of the Forsaken Tower. It is addressed to High Priest Nistirio by Xamphur, Xeric's closest comrade, regarding the tower having useful artefacts for Xeric's forces. It is an optional item for the quest, The Forsaken Tower, and it can be obtained after completing the quest.
22780:
Wyrm bones are the remains obtained from killing wyrms, which give 50 Prayer experience when buried. This can be increased by offering the bones in different ways:

150 XP when casting Sinister Offering.

150 XP when offered at the sacred bone burner after the appropriate faith level has been achieved.

175 XP when offered at a gilded altar with two burners lit.

200 XP when offered at the Ectofuntus in the form of wyrm bonemeal.

210 XP when blessed and broken down into blessed bone shards and offered at the libation bowl, or 252 XP when offered with a jug of blessed sunfire wine. Virilis outside the altar will exchange noted bones for 10 coins each.

350 XP on average when offered at the Chaos Temple in the Wilderness. Each offering gives 175 XP, which is the same as the gilded altar with two burners lit, but with an additional 50% chance to not consume the bones.

Burying them while wearing a dragonbone necklace will restore 3 prayer points.
22792:
Dragonfruit pie is a type of pie that restores 20 Hitpoints in total, 2 bites each healing for 10. It also temporarily boosts Fletching by 4, the second highest boost available, and the highest reliable boost. A pie dish will remain after both bites are consumed.

It can be created by baking a uncooked dragonfruit pie on a cooking range, requiring level 73 Cooking and granting 220 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt pie. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Dragonfruit pies never stop burning altogether even at level 99, unless the player is wearing a Cooking cape or using the Hosidius kitchen. Alternatively, casting the Bake Pie spell from the lunar spellbook will always create a pie without burning it.

As with most dragon equipment, dragon knives cannot be made from raw materials using the Smithing skill.

Cormorant's glove is an item required for Aerial Fishing that can obtained for free by speaking to Alry the Angler on Molch island. Levels 35 Hunter and 43 Fishing are required to receive the glove and begin using it to catch bluegill, common tench, mottled eel, and greater siren. Alongside the fish, players can also catch Molch pearls which can then be traded to Alry for a number of items which can assist in standard fishing.

In order to use the cormorant's glove, players must have appropriate food in their inventory to keep the bird fed. King worms can be found scattered around the island to use for this purpose. Alternatively, the player may bring a knife to the island or pick up the one that spawns there and butcher any fish caught there into fish offcuts. The player receives 1 fish offcut from butchering any of the Molch island fish. Fine fish offcuts may also be used.
