Fish chunks were a product of cutting open a bluegill, common tench, mottled eel, or greater siren using a knife. They could be stored in a tackle box. Fish chunks were used as a substitute for King worms when feeding the cormorant in aerial fishing. Cutting the fish has no skill requirements, but provides a small amount of Cooking experience. When catching fish, there is a 50% chance for a fish chunk to be consumed after every third catch. If it is not consumed on the third, it is guaranteed to be consumed on the fourth, meaning each chunk is consumed every 3.5 catches on average.

As part of the Sailing technical pre-release, all fish chunks were converted into fish offcuts, which now also function as food for the cormorant in aerial fishing.
22820:
Molch pearls are a stackable item which can be obtained while Aerial fishing. Each catch has a 1/66.6 to 1/50 chance of giving Molch pearls in addition to the player's catch, which scales based on the player's Fishing and Hunter levels. Players can also exchange a golden tench with Alry the Angler for 100 Molch pearls. They can be stored in a tackle box.

Molch pearls can be traded to Alry in his shop, Alry the Angler's Angling Accessories on Molch Island for equipable versions of fishing rods, pieces of the Angler's outfit, as well as for the fish sack.
22826:
Bluegill are fish that can be caught on Molch Island using the Cormorant's glove. Requiring 43 Fishing and 35 Hunter to catch, they provide 11.5 Fishing experience and 16.5 Hunter experience.

Before attempting to fish them, players must speak with Alry the Angler to obtain the Cormorant's glove. This item functions similarly to the Falconer's glove used in the hunter skill. Players must click on rapidly moving fishing spots and can obtain a variety of fish, including the bluegill.

Bluegill require no bait to catch directly, however King worms are initially required to feed the cormorant. Once caught, a knife can be used to cut the bluegill to obtain stackable fish offcuts which can be used as a substitute for the king worms. Cutting the fish provides 3.5 Cooking experience.

Catching a Bluegill on Lake Molch is a requirement of the medium Kourend & Kebos Diary.
22835:
Greater siren are aquatic creatures that can be caught on Molch island using the Cormorant's glove. Requiring 91 Fishing and 87 Hunter to catch, they provide 100 fishing experience and 130 hunter experience.

Before attempting to fish them, players must speak with Alry the Angler to obtain the Cormorant's glove. This item functions similarly to the Falconer's glove used in the hunter skill. Players must click on rapidly moving fishing spots and can obtain a variety of fish, including the Greater siren.

Greater siren require no bait to catch directly, however King worms or fish offcuts are initially required to feed the cormorant. When caught, a knife can be used to cut the siren to obtain stackable fish offcuts which can be used as a substitute for the king worms. Cutting the siren provides 25 Cooking experience.
22842:
A pearl barbarian rod is an item that can be purchased for 150 Molch pearls from Alry the Angler on Molch island. It is an equipable version of the Barbarian rod, and can only be purchased if the relevant part of the Barbarian Training miniquest is completed with Otto Godblessed. It can only be used in the fishing spots at Otto's Grotto, and Mount Quidamortem in the Kebos Lowlands. Since barbarian fishing gives marginal Strength and Agility experience with each catch, it is more efficient than other training methods such as fly fishing.

This item can be stored in the magic wardrobe of a costume room. It can also be stored in a Tackle box.
22844:
A pearl fly fishing rod is an equipable version of the fly fishing rod. It is purchased for 120 Molch pearls from Alry the Angler on Molch island. This rod can be used to fish for trout, salmon (both with feathers), and rainbow fish (with stripy feathers).

The pearl fly fishing rod can only be obtained by members, but can be equipped and used in a free to play world.

This item can be stored in the magic wardrobe of a costume room. It can also be stored in a Tackle box.
22846:
A pearl fishing rod is an item that can be purchased for 100 Molch pearls from Alry the Angler on Molch island. It is an equipable version of the fishing rod.

To use this fishing rod, one will need fishing bait (sandworms or Diabolic worms for anglerfish) to catch fish. Players can also add blamish oil to create an oily pearl fishing rod to catch lava and infernal eels. This process can be reverted with a cleaning cloth.

The pearl fishing rod can only be obtained by members but can be equipped and used in a free to play world.

This item can be stored in the magic wardrobe of a costume room. It can also be stored in a Tackle box.

The following fish are caught with a pearl fishing rod:
22850: Redwood seedlings are the result of planting a redwood seed in a plant pot with a gardening trowel. Once watered, these seedlings can take up to 5 minutes to grow into a redwood sapling. 90 Farming is needed to plant the seed. When it has grown, players may place it in a redwood tree patch to grow a redwood tree. Players can pay 6 dragonfruit for the farmer to look after it.
22854: Redwood seedlings are the result of planting a redwood seed in a plant pot with a gardening trowel. Once watered, these seedlings can take up to 5 minutes to grow into a redwood sapling. 90 Farming is needed to plant the seed. When it has grown, players may place it in a redwood tree patch to grow a redwood tree. Players can pay 6 dragonfruit for the farmer to look after it.
22859:
Redwood saplings are saplings that can be used to grow redwood trees at 90 Farming. They are made by planting a redwood seed in a filled plant pot, with a gardening trowel in your inventory, then watering the redwood seedling with a watering can or by casting Humidify. When watered, the seedling will sprout into a sapling in one crop cycle (0-5 minutes).

Planting the sapling in the redwood tree patch in the Farming Guild, requiring a spade, yields 230 Farming experience. It will grow into a redwood tree after 6,400 minutes (4 days, 10 hours, and 40 minutes), and yields 22,450 Farming experience when checked.

Players can ask the gardener to protect their tree from disease whilst it grows, which requires payment of 6 dragonfruits. This payment can be noted.

Once the tree has fully grown, it can be cut down like a regular redwood tree, as it will regrow unlike other self-grown log giving trees. This method of cutting redwoods may be preferable for players looking to AFK more, as you don't compete with other players and the bank deposit is closer. However; you will lose out on the Woodcutting Guild's invisible +7 boost to Woodcutting, making it slightly slower overall.

It is not possible for players to clear the redwood tree patch; Alexandra must be paid 2,000 coins to clear it.
22862: Dragonfruit seedlings are the result of planting a dragonfruit tree seed in a plant pot with a gardening trowel. Once watered, these seedlings will take approximately 5 minutes to grow into a dragonfruit sapling. 81 Farming is needed to plant the seed. When it has grown, players may place it in a fruit tree patch to grow a dragonfruit tree. Players can pay 15 coconuts for the farmer to look after it.
22864: Dragonfruit seedlings are the result of planting a dragonfruit tree seed in a plant pot with a gardening trowel. Once watered, these seedlings will take approximately 5 minutes to grow into a dragonfruit sapling. 81 Farming is needed to plant the seed. When it has grown, players may place it in a fruit tree patch to grow a dragonfruit tree. Players can pay 15 coconuts for the farmer to look after it.
22866:
Dragonfruit saplings are saplings that can be used to grow dragonfruit trees at level 81 Farming.

They can be made by planting a dragonfruit tree seed in a filled plant pot, with a gardening trowel in your inventory, and then watering the dragonfruit seedling with a watering can or by using Humidify. When watered, the seedling will sprout into a sapling in one crop cycle (0-5 minutes).

Planting the sapling in a fruit tree patch, with a spade in your inventory, will give 140 Farming experience. It will grow into a dragonfruit tree after 960 minutes (16 hours), which gives 17,335 Farming experience.

Players can ask the gardener to protect their tree from disease whilst it grows, which requires payment of 15 coconuts. This payment can be noted.
22871:
Redwood tree seeds are seeds used in the Farming skill. At level 90 Farming[boostable], redwood seeds may be planted in plant pots with a gardening trowel and watered to become redwood saplings. They can be obtained from bird nests, monster drops, the brimstone chest, Larran's big chest or by completing farming contracts.

After planting the sapling in a redwood tree patch found in the Farming Guild and waiting for it to fully grow, which takes over four days (106.7 hours), the plant will grow into a redwood tree which can be cut to yield redwood logs (and grant Woodcutting experience). Planting the redwood sapling yields 230 experience, and checking its health gives 22,450 experience. Alexandra will look after a player's redwood patch in exchange for 6 dragonfruits.

When cut down, the tree will automatically regrow after a period of time. Players cannot clear the patch on their own; they must pay Alexandra 2,000 coins to do so.

One seed can be used on the skilling pet Tangleroot to change its appearance.
22873:
Potato cactus seeds are a type of seed that can be planted in a cactus patch found in Al Kharid or the Farming Guild. They require level 64 Farming to plant and produce a potato cactus. Growth time is approximately 70 minutes. Players can harvest potato cacti from the mature plant.

Potato cactus seeds can be obtained as drops from various monsters, in seed packs awarded from farming contracts, or by pickpocketing a master farmer.

A nearby gardener will watch over your growing potato cactus plant in exchange for 8 snape grass.
22875:
Hespori seeds are a type of seed requiring level 65 Farming to plant, and that can only be planted in the Hespori patch with a seed dibber in the cave found in the west wing of the Farming Guild. They can be randomly obtained from checking the health of fully grown trees, bushes or cacti, from the last harvest of a regular plant such as herbs, hops, allotments, flowers, mushrooms, cacti, giant seaweed, coral, or from completing farming contracts.

When fully grown, it will grow into the Hespori, a demi-boss that can be defeated for 12,600 Farming experience. It is not necessary to water or compost a Hespori plant, nor does it need protection from disease. It takes 22–32 hours to grow, depending on when it was planted. The flower behind the cave entrance will be in bloom when the Hespori plant is fully grown.

Players can speak to Arno if they wish to stop randomly receiving Hespori seeds as they harvest, clear, or check the health of their crops around Gielinor.

Hespori seeds are most commonly dropped from plants grown in Special patches; players looking to fight Hespori more often should consider growing cactus, nightshade, mushrooms and giant seaweed. Giant seaweed is a popular choice as the seaweed spores are easily obtainable, grow quickly, and have a 1/15 chance to drop a Hespori seed; similar to the Tangleroot, this is rolled on the last harvesting attempt.

If the player has no room in their inventory, they will not receive a Hespori seed. In most cases, the chance of receiving a Hespori seed is 500 times the base chance of the Tangleroot. At 99 Farming, the effective chance of Tangleroot per Hespori seeds received is between 1/252.2 and 1/497.3. Note this is outside Tithe farm and does not account for Hespori seeds received from seed packs.

Unlike many other seeds, Hespori seeds cannot be used to fill birdhouses.
22877:
Dragonfruit tree seeds are the highest level fruit tree patch seeds. At 81 Farming, a dragonfruit tree seed can be planted in a plant pot to make a dragonfruit seedling, which grows into a dragonfruit sapling; the sapling can be planted in a fruit tree patch to be grown into a dragonfruit tree. Dragonfruit trees, when fully grown, bear dragonfruit.

A nearby gardener will watch over your growing dragonfruit tree at the cost of 15 coconuts.

Dragonfruit trees, like all fruit trees, ideally take six 160-minute farming cycles to fully grow, but certain factors can delay this. Dragonfruit trees are usually fully grown within 24 hours, however.

Dragonfruit tree seeds may be found rarely in a bird nest, which can be obtained randomly while Woodcutting, emptying Birdhouses or from Managing Miscellania. They can also be obtained via farming contracts from the Farming Guild, as loot from opening the brimstone chest, Larran's small or big chest or as rare drops from the Hespori, alchemical hydra, demonic gorillas, lizardman shamans, and Vorkath.

One seed can be used on the skilling pet Tangleroot to change its appearance.
22879:
Snape grass seeds can be planted at level 61 Farming. 3 seeds are sown in an allotment patch to grow snape grass plants, which yield snape grass: a Herblore secondary ingredient. They take 1 hour and 10 minutes to grow.

A nearby gardener will watch over growing snape grass plants for 5 jangerberries. Fully grown white lilies in a nearby flower patch will also protect the snape grass from disease.

These seeds can be stolen from master farmers. They may also be obtained from various monsters, Farming Guild seed packs, and the Wintertodt reward cart.

The amulet of bounty is useful for saving snape grass seeds, providing a saving of 23,274 coins per charge.

8 snape grass are needed to protect growing potato cactus.
22881:
Attas seeds are a type of anima seed requiring level 76 Farming (boostable) to plant. They are obtained exclusively from the Hespori, and can only be planted in the anima patch within the intermediate tier of the Farming Guild. Planting an attas seed gives 100 Farming experience.

From the moment the seed is planted, the attas plant will increase the yield of player's farming patches worldwide, by increasing the chance to save a harvest life by 5%. This effect stacks with other similar chance-to-save boosts, such as the magic secateurs and the Farming cape. The plant will provide this effect for approximately 3.5 days (8 x 640 mins) before dying. To maximise the duration of the plant's effects, it is recommended to plant it ~10 minutes after the Farming tick occurs in the following times (UTC):

Day 1: 12:00 AM, 10:40 AM, 9:20 PM

Day 2: 8:00 AM, 6:40 PM

Day 3: 5:20 AM, 4:00 PM

Day 4: 2:40 AM, 1:20 PM

The next growth stage will occur in approximately 4 hours and 12 minutes (refresh). After refreshing, when this timer indicates 10 hours and 40 minutes, this signifies a Farming tick just occurred. Due to the Farming tick varying between accounts, it is recommended to wait another 15 minutes, after it says 10 hours and 25 minutes.

Once the Attas plant reaches its eighth growth stage (~74 hours after planting), it will begin to take on a withered appearance, indicating the plant will die in the next growth stage, though the benefits will remain until death. In order to reap the Attas plant's benefits again, players must clear the anima patch and plant another Attas seed. The plant cannot be resurrected with the Resurrect Crops spell. Players can remove the plant before the plant dies by using a spade on the anima patch, being prompted "are you sure you want to dig up this patch?"
22887:
White lily seeds can be planted in a flower patch at level 58 Farming to yield a white lily. When fully grown, it protects all neighbouring allotments from disease.

A nearby gardener will not watch over a growing white lily plant. It is recommended to use ultracompost when planting them.

They can be obtained as a drop from the Hespori, from a seed pack bought from Tithe Farm, or bought from other players.

Using one seed on the Tangleroot pet will change its appearance to a white lily variant.
22929:
A dragonfruit is obtained from a dragonfruit tree, which can be grown from a dragonfruit sapling in a fruit tree patch, provided that one has level 81 Farming. Players can pay a gardener a fee of 15 coconuts to watch over the tree while it grows. A fully grown dragonfruit tree grows one dragonfruit per 30 minutes up to a maximum of six per tree.

When eaten, a dragonfruit heals 10 hitpoints. They are an ingredient in dragonfruit pies, which require level 73 Cooking to bake and boost a player's Fletching level by 4 when eaten.

Ten dragonfruits can also be used on a vial to create bottled dragonbreath, which can be used on a sulphur vent on Mount Karuulm to "power" it (this process will burn the player for 2 damage if they are not wearing ice gloves). Once powered, it can be used on a dragonfire shield or ward to fully charge it instantly.

Players may pay 6 dragonfruits to Alexandra in the Farming Guild to have her look after a planted redwood tree. Players can also pay a gardener 8 dragonfruits to look after a planted rosewood tree.
22932:
White lilies are flowers that can be harvested from a flower patch after planting white lily seeds. Fully grown white lilies protect all neighbouring allotments from disease.

White lilies have very limited practical uses after being harvested. The most productive use of white lilies (once harvested) is to add them to a compost bin to make supercompost.
22935:
Celastrus bark is a type of wood harvested from a celastrus tree. The bark can be fletched into a battlestaff using a knife with level 40 Fletching, granting 80 Fletching experience.

One celastrus tree produces a minimum of 3 bark, where each harvest has a chance of using up one of the "lives" of the celastrus patch, much like harvesting herb patches. Similar to other variable-yield patches, the yield of celastrus bark can be increased by using magic secateurs, supercompost, ultracompost, attas seed, and having higher Farming levels. Nature offerings do not increase the yield of celastrus bark, however.

Celastrus bark can also be used for tick manipulation training on a 4-tick cycle to receive greatly improved experience rates. An expanded explanation on tick manipulation and celastrus bark's use case can be found on that page.
22951:
Boots of Brimstone are a piece of Slayer equipment worn in the foot slot. A Slayer level of 44, along with level 70 in Defence, Magic, and Ranged is required to wear them.

They can be created by using a drake's claw on the boots of stone, and can protect the wearer from the extremely hot ground within the Karuulm Slayer Dungeon.

These boots have the second highest stab attack bonus, as well as the third-highest magic defence in the footwear slot, tied with the silly jester boots, bloodbark boots, infinity boots, and pegasian boots. Because these boots have no negative bonuses, positive attack and defence bonuses in both ranged and magic, and decent melee defensive bonuses, these boots are an excellent choice for activities that require use of mage and range styles such as Zulrah. They are a poor choice for activities which require melee due to the absence of any strength bonus.
22963: A broken dragon hasta is a broken form of the dragon hasta and can be received as loot from the brimstone chest. Players can show the broken dragon hasta to Otto Godblessed for a free repair. Players do not have to learn Barbarian Smithing via the Barbarian Training miniquest to do this. Players do however need to have completed the smithing portion of the miniquest in order to wield the repaired hasta.
22978:
The dragon hunter lance is a one-handed spear and dragonbane weapon created by using a hydra claw on a Zamorakian hasta. Equipping the lance requires level 78 Attack as well as completion of the Firemaking (not the pyre step), Fishing, and Smithing sections of the Barbarian Training miniquest.

The lance's dragonbane passive effect is its 20% increased accuracy and damage when fighting draconic creatures, such as dragons, wyverns, and the Great Olm (but excluding Elvarg and revenant dragons). This stacks multiplicatively with both Void Knight equipment and the Slayer helm (i).

Like the Zamorakian hasta, it will act as a Zamorak item within the God Wars Dungeon; though the lance lacks the hasta's prayer and defensive bonuses and special attack, while sporting a lower strength bonus.

When attempting to create the dragon hunter lance, a warning will appear in the chatbox stating that the process cannot be reversed, and a confirmation will appear afterwards asking if players would like to proceed with the alchemical combination. Should the player confirm, the chatbox will state: You successfully combine the Hydra claw and the Zamorakian hasta to create the Dragon hunter lance.
22981:
The ferocious gloves are a pair of melee gloves requiring level 80 Attack and Defence to equip. They are the best-in-slot offensive gloves for melee, surpassing Barrows gloves. However, they provide no defensive stats, and have a negative ranged and magic attack bonuses, making them less effective when using multiple attack styles.

The gloves are untradeable, but can be made from a piece of hydra leather, costing 10,077,686 on the Grand Exchange. To craft the gloves, player must bring the leather and a hammer to the northern part of the Lithkren Vault, and use the leather on the machinery south-west of the pool. In order to revert the gloves back to leather form, simply use the machinery again while holding a hammer and the gloves. Players must complete Dragon Slayer II to access the vault.
22986:
The bonecrusher necklace is a necklace that can be created by combining the bonecrusher and dragonbone necklace with a hydra tail. It requires level 70 in Prayer to equip and shares its best in slot +12 prayer bonus with the dragonbone necklace.

The necklace possesses the effects of both the bonecrusher and the dragonbone necklace, being able to automatically crush bones while restoring prayer, saving an inventory slot. Like the bonecrusher, the necklace must be charged with ecto-tokens (25 charges per token). It can be charged quickly using the free bonemeal and buckets of slime from Robin given daily as part of the hard Morytania diary rewards. The prayer restoration effect does not stack with the Catacombs of Kourend prayer restoration effect. When unequipped, the bonecrusher necklace behaves like an ordinary bonecrusher, granting Prayer experience but no restoration.

The bones crushed can include those from monsters killed traditionally, but can also include those killed using hunter methods such as deadfall traps.

When killed in PvP, the bonecrusher necklace and its charges are kept when protected. When unprotected, only the bonecrusher is kept with the charges, the hydra tail and dragonbone necklace are always dropped to the killer.

The amount of points restored are as follows:

Bones, Burnt bones, Monkey bones, Wolf bones, and Bat bones restore 1 prayer point.

Big bones, Jogre bones, Zogre bones, Wyrmling bones, Shaikahan bones, and Small ninja monkey bones restore 2 prayer points.

Baby dragon bones, Bull bones, Wyrm bones, and Strykewyrm bones restore 3 prayer points.

Dragon, Frost dragon, Wyvern, Drake, Dagannoth, Hydra, Fayrg, Raurg, and Lava dragon bones restore 4 prayer points.

Superior dragon bones, Giant bones, and Ourg bones restore 5 prayer points.

The bonecrusher necklace will not affect demonic ashes. For automatic scattering, use the Ash sanctifier. For spectral creatures that do not drop ashes or bones, use the Ectoplasmator. Neither the ash sanctifier, nor the ectoplasmator will restore prayer points.

Players cannot have a bonecrusher and a bonecrusher necklace at the same time.
22991:
The stone tablet is a tablet found in a stone chest in the south-east corner of the Lizardman Temple. It records the construction of the temple.

When read, the player will read it aloud and make their own commentary.
23007:
The tatty note can be found by searching the bed in a small shack north-east of the Farming Guild, near the fairy ring CIR.

The note is addressed to Rose, the daughter of King Kharedst IV. It is revealed during the quest A Kingdom Divided that the note was written by Liam Orson, a member of the Kourend Council. In the note, he apologises to Rose for having played a part in killing her father and indirectly causing her current comatose state, but claims that what the Council did was for the greater good.
23037:
Boots of stone are a piece of Slayer equipment worn in the foot slot. A Slayer level of 44 is required to equip them. They can be bought from any Slayer master. The boots help to protect the wearer from the extremely hot ground of the Karuulm Slayer Dungeon.

Boots of stone can be used on a drake's claw to upgrade them into boots of brimstone, which have increased stats and can also be worn as an alternative within the Karuulm Slayer Dungeon, along with granite boots.
23050: The mystic robe top (dusk) is a part of the dusk Mystic robes set worn in the body slot. Mystic robe tops come in many colours but all share the same bonuses, and all mystic items require 40 Magic and 20 Defence to wear. It can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player-owned house.
23053: The mystic robe bottom (dusk) is a part of the dusk Mystic robes set worn in the legs slot. Mystic robe bottoms come in many colours but all share the same bonuses, and all mystic items require 40 Magic and 20 Defence to wear. It can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player-owned house.
23059: Mystic boots (dusk) are a part of the dusk Mystic robes set worn in the feet slot. Mystic boots come in many colours but all share the same bonuses, and all mystic items require 40 Magic and 20 Defence to wear. It can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player-owned house.
23062:
The nest box is an item that holds bird nests. It can be obtained from trading in noted mole claws or mole skins to Wyson the gardener who can be found in Falador Park.

There are three different types of nest boxes.

Nest box (seeds) - Contains birds nests with seeds in them.

Nest box (ring) - Contains bird nests with rings in them.

Nest box (empty) - Contains bird nests with nothing in them.

Each box will contain various amounts of nests depending on what each nest contains.

If you have nest boxes on you, trading more mole parts into Wyson will not result in the bird nests being added to the existing boxes. Rather, you will get a separate additional set of boxes.
23069: The mysterious orb is an item obtained during the X Marks the Spot quest. It must be used to determine the location of the next clue, similar to using the enchanted key.
23072:
Antique lamps are rewards from quests, achievement diaries and the Varrock Museum miniquest. Like regular lamps, these lamps grant a player experience in a chosen skill, and the skill chosen must usually be over a certain level which is unboostable.

Lamps that are not included in the three items kept on death will be kept inside your death's coffer, if not deleted.
23077:
Alchemical hydra heads are a rare drop from the Alchemical Hydra. They can be stuffed at the taxidermist in Canifis by using the item on her and paying 50,000 coins, returning stuffed hydra heads. When shown the heads, she will say, "This hydra looks like it might fall to pieces soon. I'll have to be careful to preserve it properly."

Once stuffed, Alchemical hydra heads can be mounted at a gilded display within the skill hall in a player-owned house, granting 223 Construction alongside 200 Attack, Strength, Defence, Magic, and Ranged experience, although players are given the option to decline the combat experience. Alternatively, the heads can be sacrificed to the Dark Altar north of Arceuus, granting 2,500 Prayer experience.

Lastly, the heads can be combined with a slayer helmet (or imbued) to create a hydra slayer helmet; doing so requires purchasing the ability Use More Head for 1,000 Slayer reward points.
23082:
Antique lamps are rewards from quests, achievement diaries and the Varrock Museum miniquest. Like regular lamps, these lamps grant a player experience in a chosen skill, and the skill chosen must usually be over a certain level which is unboostable.

Lamps that are not included in the three items kept on death will be kept inside your death's coffer, if not deleted.
23091:
Ornate gloves are obtained from completing the first clue during the Crack the Clue II event. They are part of the ornate armour set, and are obtainable only once if you already have them in your inventory or bank. If you happen to accidentally destroy them, you will need to discover them again.

They are obtained alongside the ornate boots.

In order to obtain/reobtain the boots and gloves, the player must dig just south-east of Rimmington near Skippy with a pie dish in their inventory.

Its stats are identical to those of Leather gloves.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Ornate armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
23093:
Ornate boots are obtained from completing the first clue during the Crack the Clue II event. They are part of the ornate armour set, and are obtainable only once if you already have them in your inventory or bank. If you happen to accidentally destroy them, you will need to discover them again.

They are obtained alongside the ornate gloves, and have stats identical to leather boots.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Ornate armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
23099:
The ornate cape is obtained from completing a clue during the Crack the Clue II event. It is part of the ornate armour set, and is obtainable only once if you already have it in your inventory or bank. If you happen to accidentally destroy it, you will need to discover it again.

In order to obtain/reobtain the cape, the player must dig by the entrance to the Chaos Temple in the Wilderness with a goblin mail in their inventory.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Ornate armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

Its stats are identical to those of regular dyed capes, such as the black cape.
23101:
The ornate helm is obtained from completing a clue during the Crack the Clue II event. It is part of the ornate armour set, and is obtainable only once if you already have it in your inventory or bank. If you happen to accidentally destroy it, you will need to discover it again. Its bonuses are equal to those of the Shaman mask.

In order to obtain the helmet, the player must perform the Bow, Yes and Clap emotes in succession between some trees south of Varrock, east of the stone circle. They also must have nothing equipped and only have a plain pizza, a wooden shield and cheese in their inventory. If the correct conditions are met, the Mysterious Old Man will appear, telling the player "Here, take this. But tell no one I was here."

The ornate helm was not found until five days after the fourth clue was made available, at 16:00 GMT on 19 March 2019. An additional sentence was added to the examine text with an update the same week to commemorate the players that found it.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Ornate armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
23103: The Cook's shopping list is an item used during the 2019 Birthday event. It was given to the player by the Cook. It is a list of items that the player obtain for the party.
23104: The Cook's letter is an item used during the 2019 Birthday event. It was given to the player by the Cook, to be given to the Squire in the White Knights' Castle in exchange for Vyvin's wine.
23105:
The Brewer's folly is an ale obtained from Emily or Kaylee in the Rising Sun Inn during the 2019 Birthday event. It is to be given to the Cook for Hans.

According to the barmaids, they don't charge patrons for it because it tastes horrible, hence the name.

If a player attempts to drink the beer, the chatbox will state "Drinking the Brewer's Folly would be your folly."
23106:
Vyvin's wine is a bottle of vintage obtained from the squire during the 2019 Birthday event. It was stolen from Sir Vyvin in exchange for a baked cake for the squire's birthday party, and is to be given to the Cook for the Wise Old Man.

If a player attempts to drink the wine, the chatbox will state "The squire's risking his job by giving you this stuff. It'd be rude to drink it yourself."
23110:
Mystic set (light) is an item obtained by exchanging a set of items with a Grand Exchange clerk via their right-click "Sets" option and clicking on the appropriate item set within the Item Sets interface.

It is commonly made in order to conveniently sell all five components of light mystic robes at once.
23113:
Mystic set (blue) is an item obtained by exchanging a set of items with a Grand Exchange clerk via their right-click "Sets" option and clicking on the appropriate item set within the Item Sets interface.

It is commonly made in order to conveniently sell all five components of blue mystic robes at once.

The Mimic is an item that may be obtained when attempting to open an elite or master reward casket. In order to be eligible to obtain it, players must first speak to the strange casket upstairs in Watson's house in Hosidius to enable the chance of a reward casket turning into the Mimic; attempting to open an elite or master reward casket for the first time before speaking to the strange casket will direct players to the strange casket if they say they want Mimic encounters. An elite reward casket has a 1/35 chance of being a mimic, while master reward caskets have a 1/15 chance. There is a dry protection that guarantees your first Mimic encounter on either the 10th master reward casket or 25th elite reward casket, if you have Mimic encounters enabled.

When obtained, a message in the chatbox will state The chest turned out to be the Mimic!. Attempting to open the Mimic before defeating the Mimic boss gives the message "Visit the Strange Casket, upstairs in Watson's house in Hosidius, to attempt the Mimic's challenge.".

Once a player obtains the Mimic, they can return to the strange casket to challenge The Mimic. When the player defeats the Mimic, they must leave in order to open the mimic chest and receive their reward. If a player attempts to open the mimic chest while in the Mimic's fight area, the chatbox will state "It'd be bad taste to try opening that in here."

If a player tries to open another elite or master reward casket with a Mimic in the player's inventory, the chatbox will warn the player "You already have a Mimic, and cannot be given another one. Do you wish to open the casket anyway?" However, if the Mimic is dropped on the ground, the player may obtain more Mimics. Just like clue scrolls, Mimics can be juggled, staying on the ground for an hour before despawning. As such the player may opt to juggle Mimics if opening a lot of caskets. Once done, the player can pick up all Mimics at once, since there is no restriction against carrying several Mimics.

The Mimic cannot be deposited into a bank. If players try to bank it, the chatbox will state "A magical force prevents you from banking this item!"

When opening your first casket after defeating The Mimic you will also be given a Mimic scroll case which can be opened to let you stack 1 more Scroll box for every tier of clue scroll.

23387:
Watson teleport scrolls are consumable teleport scrolls that teleport the player to Watson's house in Hosidius. They are obtained by exchanging empty master scroll books with Watson. Each book given will reward the player with 10-20 scrolls.

There are no requirements to use this teleport. Notably, this teleport can be used without requiring the player to have visited Kourend before, unlike other teleports such as the Hosidius teleport or the games necklace teleport to the Wintertodt Camp.

Players use these scrolls to access Watson's home, where they can quickly turn in clue scrolls in exchange for a master clue scroll, or to reach The Mimic upstairs more quickly. They can also use them as a one-click stackable teleport to Hosidius in general.
23389:
Spiked manacles are a rare reward obtained from medium Treasure Trails. They are tied with aranea boots for the best-in-slot strength bonus for footwear that has no requirements to equip. It has equivalent strength bonus to dragon boots and aranea boots, all of which are only surpassed by primordial boots and the avernic treads, though without any of the defensive bonuses.

In comparison to climbing boots, which also have no Defence requirement to equip, Spiked manacles have +2 higher strength bonus. However, Spiked manacles have some negative bonuses whereas the Climbing boots have none, and Climbing boots also offer +2 Slash and +2 Crush melee defence bonuses. Aranea boots have slight Ranged and Magic attack bonuses, no negative defence bonuses, and 1 Prayer bonus, making them slightly better than spiked manacles.

This item can be stored in the treasure chest of a costume room, provided that the interface of the corresponding clue tier is opened before attempting to store the item. Alternatively, the item can be used on the opened treasure chest to insert it without viewing the interface.

23417:
Puzzle boxes can be obtained by doing hard, elite, and master Treasure Trails. Before you are able to continue with your clue scroll, you will have to complete the puzzle.

A puzzle box is always scrambled 101 times before being handed to the player, by randomly sliding a piece into the empty position starting from the solved state.

If you have a duplicate puzzle box, (obtained by a method such as the Drop trick) in your inventory or bank after completing the clue, you cannot obtain another clue.
23442:
A clue geode (beginner) is randomly obtained from Mining if the player has not completed X Marks the Spot, otherwise they will receive a Scroll box (beginner). Opening the geode gives a beginner clue scroll.

If the player completes X Marks the Spot before opening the clue geode, they will instead receive a beginner scroll box.

The ring of wealth (i) does not affect the rate of clue geode (beginner) drops from Mining in the Wilderness.
23444:
The tormented bracelet (or) is a tormented bracelet with a tormented ornament kit attached to it. The attached ornament kit gives no additional bonuses, and is only used to add aesthetics to the bracelet. It costs 20,057,866 for both the parts to make the tormented bracelet (or).

While the bracelet is untradeable in its ornamented state, it can be dismantled anytime, returning the tradeable bracelet and ornament kit.

Many players purchase the ornament kit for the purpose of making the item untradeable, thus allowing the player to always keep it on death against NPCs.
23446:
The Giant easter egg is a cosmetic reward obtained from the 2019 Easter event, as well as subsequent Easter events. When wielded, players will be given a unique animation of them struggling to carry the egg. The egg has a unique Easter dance emote that can be used by right clicking on the item.

After the event, a hammer can be used on the giant easter egg to find the bunnyman mask. Holding the giant easter egg causes the Bunny Man to have different dialogue, which hints at the use of a hammer.

If the player attempts to use the easter egg in a PvP zone they will receive the message "Perhaps you should play with your egg somewhere safer."

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room.
23448:
The bunnyman mask is an untradeable cosmetic item that is worn by the Bunny Man. During the 2019 Easter event, it was obtained by using a hammer on the giant easter egg; subsequent events simply reward the player with the mask.

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room.

When the hard Fremennik Diary is completed, the lyre can also teleport to Waterbirth Island, and gains the ability to teleport to Jatizso and Neitiznot after completion of the elite Fremennik Diary.

It shows that the player is an attacker indicated by the red circle around them with the attacker symbol. When a game of Barbarian Assault finishes, the icon is removed.

Having a higher level in the Attacker role, which can be done via Commander Connad or choosing to do so immediately after a game, allows players to deal bonus damage to penance monsters.

23489:
This Wine of Zamorak is an unobtainable variant of the Wine of Zamorak that can be found in the Deep Wilderness Dungeon. Unlike the normal item, this version is scripted to respawn much faster than normal, and to give the wine in banknote form after the completion of the Wilderness Hard diary.

The item is unobtainable, as it cannot be picked up directly from the table. Casting Telekinetic grab on it will give the regular wine of Zamorak instead.
23490:
Larran's key is a key obtained from killing monsters while on a Slayer task given by Krystilia. It is used to open Larran's small and big chests.

The exact odds of receiving a key scales with the monster's Combat level. For levels 1-80, the probability follows a curve between 1/1972 at level 1 to 1/100 at level 80. For levels 81 or higher, the odds are between 1/99 and 1/50, scaling linearly and capping at level 350, as reflected in the equation below.

If it concerns a Slayer monster (meaning it requires a certain Slayer level to kill), the drop chance is increased by 20%. In addition, any monster killed within the Wilderness Slayer Cave has a further 15% increased chance to drop a key. Superior slayer monsters that spawn as part of Krystilia's tasks will always drop a key on death.

The probability P of obtaining a key when killing a monster with combat level L is given by:

P={1⌊310×(80−L)2⌋+100if L∈(0,80]1⌊−527×L⌋+115if L∈(80,350]150L∈(350,∞)

Larran's keys are always dropped on player death, even if there are fewer than 3 items kept on death. If killed by another player, keys are lost to the killer. If killed in PvM, the keys always go to your gravestone.
23495:
Sraracha is a pet dropped by Sarachnis, and is a much smaller version of the boss. Players can right click "Metamorphosis" to change its form, providing they have used an orange or blue egg sac to unlock its other coloured forms.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.
23499:
The grubby key is a key obtained from killing monsters within the Forthos Dungeon. It is used to open the Grubby Chest.

Brother Aimeri will give the player a key in exchange for spare pristine spider silks.
23504:
The Tome of the Moon is a book obtained during the miniquest In Search of Knowledge by searching the north-eastern Temple Library bookshelves within the Forthos Dungeon. Initially empty, players must fill four Tattered moon pages that are received as drops from monsters within the dungeon.

The tome contains the teachings of Ranul, the god of the moon.

If lost, it can be reclaimed from the north-eastern bookshelves in the Temple Library, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house if the tome has been fully restored. Any pages that were previously filled before the book was lost will be present in the reclaimed book.
23506:
The tome of the Sun is a book obtained during the miniquest In Search of Knowledge by searching the south-eastern Temple Library bookshelves within the Forthos Dungeon. Initially empty, players must fill four Tattered sun pages that are received as drops from monsters within the dungeon.

The tome contains the teachings of Ralos, the god of the sun.

If lost, it can be reclaimed from the south-eastern bookshelves in the Temple Library, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house if the tome has been fully restored. Any pages that were previously filled before the book was lost will be present in the reclaimed book.
23508:
The tome of the Temple is a book obtained during the miniquest In Search of Knowledge by searching the south-western Temple Library bookshelves within the Forthos Dungeon. Initially empty, players must fill four Tattered temple pages that are received as drops from monsters within the dungeon.

The tome details the various features of the Forthos Dungeon, referred to in the tome as the Temple to Ranul/Ralos, and their original uses. The last page of the tome contains an entry by a follower of Ranul, whose followers have become corrupted and fanatical after meeting a dark wizard, who is either Xeric or one of his followers; it is purposely left open to interpretation.

If lost, it can be reclaimed from the south-western bookshelves in the Temple Library, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house if the tome has been fully restored. Any pages that were previously filled before the book was lost will be present in the reclaimed book.
23510:
The tattered moon page is a torn page obtained from monsters in the Forthos Dungeon. Four of these are used to fill the Tome of the Moon during the miniquest In Search of Knowledge, although players do not need to begin the miniquest to begin obtaining them.

Once the tome has been completed and given to Logosia in the Arceuus Library, subsequent pages can be given to her in exchange for 1,000 coins per page. Should players wish to stop receiving tattered pages from monsters in the Forthos Dungeon, they can speak to Logosia once they've completed In Search of Knowledge.

23517:
A giant egg sac is an item obtained as a drop from Sarachnis, which can be opened with a knife while standing inside a bank (right click egg sac in bank interface, then click empty) to obtain 100 red spiders' eggs, which is worth 17,500. This means opening a full giant egg sac results in a profit of 1,566.

The red spiders' eggs are placed into your inventory as items (not as notes), and the giant egg sac (full) becomes the untradeable giant egg sac.

Once opened, the untradeable giant egg sac has a Remove-eggs option which will remove red spiders' eggs from the sac and place them in free inventory slots.
23520:
A giant egg sac is an item obtained as a drop from Sarachnis, which can be opened with a knife while standing inside a bank (right click egg sac in bank interface, then click empty) to obtain 100 red spiders' eggs, which is worth 17,500. This means opening a full giant egg sac results in a profit of 1,566.

The red spiders' eggs are placed into your inventory as items (not as notes), and the giant egg sac (full) becomes the untradeable giant egg sac.

Once opened, the untradeable giant egg sac has a Remove-eggs option which will remove red spiders' eggs from the sac and place them in free inventory slots.
23522:
The Mask of Ranul is worn by the Undead Druids in the Forthos Dungeon and can be received from them as a drop.

The mask appears to be a depiction of Ranul, the god of the moon. Its combat stats are identical to a Wizard hat, while also being slightly lighter.

If worn while inspecting the campfire at Shipwreck Cove, Chosen Aluinus will appear and give the message Hmm... Such potential. Such a waste.... He seems to go on a minute cooldown before appearing again.
23528:
Sarachnis cudgel is a one-handed crush weapon dropped by Sarachnis, requiring level 65 Attack to equip. The weapon appears to be made from several of Sarachnis' legs bound together by her webs.

The cudgel has slightly better crush and strength bonuses than Viggora's chainmace and slightly lower bonuses than the Leaf-bladed battleaxe, although with a faster attack speed than the latter. This makes it a good crush weapon which does not degrade or require a charge.
23533:
Cooked karambwan is a type of fish that restores 18 Hitpoints when eaten. They can be obtained by cooking raw karambwan on a fire or cooking range. Cooking a karambwan requires level 30 Cooking, and grants 190 experience when successful.

In order to produce a cooked karambwan, the player must first complete Tai Bwo Wannai Trio and afterwards talk to Tinsay in the southernmost hut in Tai Bwo Wannai. If the player has not done this, cooking a raw karambwan will instead produce a poison karambwan. Players may burn a karambwan while cooking one, resulting in a burnt karambwan; the burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 99 on both ranges and fires. It is possible to use tick manipulation to cook each raw karambwan in one tick rather than the standard four to increase Cooking experience rates.

When eaten, the message You eat the Karambwan. is displayed.

Karambwans are commonly used as a fast food, a subtype of food that incurs non-standard attack or eating delays when consumed. Karambwans may be consumed after other foods without delay; this does not work if the karambwan is eaten first, and does not work when eating two karambwan in a row. This technique (commonly referred to as combo eating) can be further enhanced by drinking a dose of Saradomin brew after your alternative food item, and before your karambwan (food>brew>karambwan).

Additionally, karambwans add a delay of two ticks before the player can attack again, while most other foods have a delay of three ticks.

Karambwans may also be used in tick manipulation to improve rates. This is only recommended for non-ironman players. For example, you can start your usual 3-tick timer using your herb and tar, then on the next cycle, you eat a cooked karambwan instead. This effectively allows you to 2.5-tick certain actions, such as barbarian fishing.
23551: A ranging potion is a potion found in the Last Man Standing minigame. A dose of ranging potion provides a temporary skill boost to Ranged equal to 4 + 10% of the player's current Ranged level, rounded down. Unlike normal ranging potions, these lack an "Empty" option.

23567:
A super restore is a potion found in the Last Man Standing minigame that restores all player stats that have been lowered, including Prayer, but not including Hitpoints.

The restore value obtained per dose is 8 + 25% of the player's base level (round down) in each of the affected skills. For example, a player with 84 Thieving and 63 Smithing would restore both 29 points of Thieving and 23 points of Smithing for each dose consumed. The maximum amount of points that can be restored with this potion is 32 at level 96. This means that a super restore potion will restore 1 more Prayer point per dose than a prayer potion. Unlike normal super restores, these lack an "Empty" option.

23603:
The imbued Guthix cape is obtained from imbuing a Guthix cape with the items dropped by Justiciar Zachariah, Porazdir, and Derwen, during the Mage Arena II miniquest, requiring 75 Magic. Subsequent imbues will require only ent's roots, or 250,000 to purchase from the Lost Property shop.

This cape, along with the imbued Saradomin and Zamorak capes, provides the best in slot magic attack and magic damage bonus for the cape slot.

Despite the update newspost stating that the cape is always lost upon death (excluding safe deaths and services that offer an item reclaim function, such as Zulrah via Priestess Zul-Gwenwynig and the Grotesque Guardians via the magical chest), the cape, like most untradeable equipment, is automatically protected upon death in dangerous PvM scenarios outside of the Wilderness.

If the player dies a PvP death and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 96,000 coins.

The imbued Guthix cape can be combined with the max cape to change its appearance by turning it into the imbued Guthix max cape.

You may obtain all 3 god capes imbued at the same time. After completing the miniquest, you may return with duplicates of any dropped items by Justiciar Zachariah, Porazdir, and Derwen.

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room.

23613:
The staff of the dead is a one-handed bladed staff that requires 75 Magic and 75 Attack to wield. It is dropped by K'ril Tsutsaroth, and counts as a Zamorakian item while in the God Wars Dungeon and in the desert Bandit Camp. It is one of several one-handed staves which boost magic damage by 15%.

When a combat spell is cast with the staff, there is a 1/7 (~14.2%) chance that the staff will negate the rune cost for that spell.

The staff can autocast Flames of Zamorak, Crumble Undead, Magic Dart, elemental combat spells from the Standard spellbook, and combat spells from the Arceuus spellbook. It is not, however, able to autocast ancient magicks.

Being a bladed staff, it is notable for its offensive melee stats, which are unusually high for a Magic weapon. Its stats slightly surpass that of a dragon scimitar while having the same attack speed when using melee. However, when using magic spells, it offers an attack speed of 5.

The staff may be upgraded into the toxic staff of the dead, the staff of light, or the staff of balance.
23615:
Vesta's longsword (bh) is a slash weapon requiring 75 Attack to wield, and is purchased from the Bounty Hunter Store for 650 points.

As with all Ancient Warriors' equipment from Bounty Hunter, it is initially purchased in inactive form, and must be charged with 50,000,000 coins before it can be used by the player. Upon dying in PvP, the coins used to activate the item are given to the killer, and players are left with the inactive item. That said, the activated form is preserved and the coins aren't lost if the longsword is one of the player's protected items.

Unlike other Ancient Warriors' weapons bought from the Bounty Hunter Store, this variant of the Vesta's longsword appears to share the same restrictions as Vesta's blighted longsword, meaning it can be used on a Bounty Hunter world while in the Wilderness, inside Daimon's Crater, Castle Wars, Clan Wars, Soul Wars, the TzHaar Fight Pit, and both the player-owned house and Clan Hall combat rings. The weapon cannot be used for PvM or PvP combat activities in other circumstances.
23619:
Morrigan's javelin from Last Man Standing is a minigame-exclusive variant of the normal Morrigan's javelin. It can be obtained from opening the chests with a bloodier key, or looting the crates that spawn at random locations on the map. It is dropped on death to whoever killed you.

Unlike other javelins, they cannot be used with ballistae and are a standalone weapon.
23620: Statius's warhammer from Last Man Standing is a minigame-exclusive variant of the normal Statius's warhammer. It can be obtained from opening the chests with a bloodier key, or looting the crates that spawn at random locations on the map. It is dropped on death to whoever killed you.
23622:
The infernal cape is the most powerful melee cape in terms of overall bonuses, awarded for defeating TzKal-Zuk in the Inferno. It surpasses its predecessor, the fire cape, boasting greater melee attack and strength bonuses, along with slightly higher defensive bonuses. In spite of this, it is still surpassed by the Ardougne cloaks 3 and 4 in stab attack and prayer bonuses, and by the mythical cape in crush attack.

An infernal cape can be exchanged for a chance of obtaining the Jal-Nib-Rek pet by speaking to TzHaar-Ket-Keh. Like killing TzKal-Zuk, there is a 1/100 chance of obtaining the pet this way. If the player already has the pet, capes cannot be exchanged.

An infernal cape can be combined with the max cape to change its appearance by turning it into the infernal max cape.

As of 1 August 2026, there are 170,755 accounts that have obtained an infernal cape.

If the player dies a PvP death at level 20 Wilderness or below and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 225,000 coins.

If the player dies a PvP death above level 20 Wilderness and the item is unprotected, it will be converted to coins. To prevent this, a Trouver parchment and a payment of 500,000 coins can be given to Perdu in order to permanently lock the item. The locked item will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a mangled, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 500,000 coins.

While equipping the fire cape will grant players the fiery attribute and will therefore make them susceptible to the extra damage from the special effect of pearl bolts (e), the infernal cape does not grant this attribute.

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room.
23624: A seers ring (i) from Last Man Standing is a minigame-exclusive variant of the normal seers ring (i). It can be obtained from opening the chests with a bloody key or bloodier key, or looting the crates that spawn at random locations on the map. It is dropped on death to whoever killed you.

23632: Karil's leathertop from Last Man Standing is a minigame-exclusive variant of the normal Karil's leathertop. It has no requirements to wear and is part of the Max/Med starting loadout in the minigame.
23633:
Dharok's platelegs is melee armour worn in the legs slot that is part of the Dharok the Wretched's set of Barrows equipment. To wear Dharok's platelegs, a player must have 70 Defence.

As it is part of Dharok's barrows set, if Dharok's platelegs is worn along with all of the other pieces of equipment in Dharok's barrows set, the player gains a special effect. Attacks do more damage as the player's hitpoints decrease, up to 98.9% bonus damage with 1 hitpoint remaining with 99 max.

For more details on the mechanics and strategies for this equipment, see the set page.
23634: Torag's platelegs from Last Man Standing is a minigame-exclusive variant of the normal Torag's platelegs. It has no requirements to wear and is part of the Max/Med starting loadout in the minigame.
23635:
Verac's plateskirt is melee armour worn in the legwear slot that is part of Verac the Defiled's set of Barrows equipment. To wear Verac's plateskirt, a player must have 70 Defence.

Verac's plateskirt provides the same amount of melee protection as Dharok and Torag's platelegs with a marginally lower amount of ranged protection. However, it does not penalise the wearer's magic defence, provides a substantial prayer bonus (+4) and weighs less than most leg armour.

If Verac's plateskirt is worn along with all of the other pieces of equipment in Verac's set, the player receives the Defiler set effect. With this set effect active, player attacks have a chance (averaging 1/4) of hitting through an opponent's defence and prayer entirely. This effect can be devastating towards tank opponents who rely on high defence. With this set effect, Verac's flail can be considered one of the best weapons for certain PvM situations.

For more details on the mechanics and strategies for this equipment, see the set page.
23636:
Verac's helm is melee armour worn in the headwear slot that is part of Verac the Defiled's set of Barrows equipment. To wear Verac's helmet, a player must have 70 Defence.

Verac's helm has a lesser magic penalty compared to other helmets at +0 magic defence but slightly less ranged defence bonuses compared to Guthan's or Torag's helm, which are equal bonuses. This helmet is often used in 'tank' combat due to the high defensive bonuses as well as a prayer bonus. This helmet is commonly used during the TzHaar Fight Cave minigame because of its good melee and ranged defence and prayer bonus.

If Verac's helm is worn along with all of the other pieces of equipment in Verac's set, the player receives the Defiler set effect. 23640:
The amulet of fury is one of the most powerful amulets available in Old School RuneScape, having equivalent attack bonuses to the amulet of glory with superior defensive, strength, and prayer bonuses, but without the ability to teleport the player. It can be made by enchanting an onyx amulet using Lvl-6 Enchant, requiring a Magic level of 87.

While it is generally regarded as the most versatile amulet with the best all-around bonuses, several amulets surpass it in certain areas.

A blood shard can be combined with the amulet to create an amulet of blood fury, which has a 20% chance of passively healing the player 30% of the damage they deal only while using melee. Its stats remain the same.

The amulet of fury can be decorated with a fury ornament kit. This produces an amulet of fury (or) but does not change its bonuses.
23644:
Eternal boots are boots that require level 75 Magic and Defence to wear. They currently have the second highest Magic attack bonus and Magic defence of any pair of boots, behind the Avernic treads. They have a Magic damage bonus of 1%.

They can be created by using an eternal crystal with a pair of infinity boots. This process cannot be reversed, and requires level 60 in Runecraft and Magic (boosts cannot be used), granting 200 experience in both skills. Unlike the infinity boots, the eternal boots cannot be stored in the player owned house.
23646: Bandos tassets are a part of the Bandos armour set, requiring 65 Defence to wear. They are dropped by General Graardor and his bodyguards in the God Wars Dungeon. Bandos tassets are widely used by experienced players as they offer high stats compared to other leg slot items, including the second highest strength bonus, tied with the Inquisitor's plateskirt, blood moon tassets, and oathplate legs. It's beaten only by Torva platelegs.
23648:
The dragon javelin is a type of Ranged ammunition used by the light ballista and the heavy ballista. They are the strongest type of javelin. As with most javelins, they can be poisoned.

They can be fletched by attaching dragon javelin tips to javelin shafts at level 92 Fletching, granting 225 experience per 15 javelins made.
23649: Diamond bolts (e) are adamant bolts tipped with enchanted diamond. Diamond bolts can be enchanted by using the spell Enchant Crossbow Bolt (Diamond) by a player with 57 Magic. The spell enchants 10 diamond bolts per cast and uses 2 law runes, 1 cosmic rune, and 10 earth runes.
23650:
The rune pouch is an item that can store 16,000 of three types of runes (except runes found in the Nightmare Zone). Players can cast spells using the runes stored in the pouch, so a rune pouch saves inventory space. With a thread of Elidinis and level 75 crafting, the rune pouch can be upgraded (with a needle) to a divine rune pouch. Players cannot own more than one rune pouch.

If players die a PvP death while carrying a rune pouch in any level Wilderness or in a PvP world, they will lose the rune pouch, unless it has been locked via use of a trouver parchment. It should be noted that the Trouver parchment does not protect runes stored within a Rune pouch upon PvP death.

If players die a PvM death anywhere, including any level Wilderness, the rune pouch is always sent to a gravestone or item retrieval service, unless it has been locked via use of a trouver parchment. Locked rune pouches are kept in the inventory upon PvM death, instead.
23652: Mage's book from Last Man Standing is a minigame-exclusive variant of the normal mage's book. It can be obtained from opening the chests with a bloody key or bloodier key, or looting the crates that spawn at random locations on the map. It is dropped on death to whoever killed you.
23653:
Ahrim's staff is a one-handed magic weapon that is part of Ahrim the Blighted's set. To wield Ahrim's staff, the player must have 70 Magic and 70 Attack. It increases Magic damage by 5%.

If Ahrim's staff is wielded along with all of the other pieces of equipment in Ahrim's barrows set, the player's successful magic attacks have a chance of temporarily lowering the opponent's Strength level. This is cumulative with other effects that lower strength, namely the spell Enfeeble.

It is able to autocast Standard combat spells as well as being one of the few weapons able to autocast Arceuus combat spells. Additionally, wearing Ahrim's set with an Amulet of the damned will allow players to autocast Ancient Magicks, and also grant players a 25% chance of dealing a hit with 30% increased damage.
23654:
The occult necklace is a magical amulet that requires 70 Magic to wear. It is dropped by the smoke devil and its boss variant. Wearing it increases the player's Magic damage by 5%, and is the only amulet to give such a bonus. This 5% bonus will also stack with existing boosts, such as the staff of the dead and the imbued slayer helmet. The salve amulet(ei) does not apply its damage bonus to other hit targets when barraging. The 3rd Age amulet possess slightly higher magic accuracy but lacks magic strength. Thus, aside from using single target magic damage against undead mobs, or in situations where landing a single spell is pivotal, it is the best neck slot item for magic damage output.

A combination of the occult necklace and staff of the dead while using Ice Barrage would increase a player's max hit to 36, from an original maximum of 30. The max hit increases to 40 if using a black mask (i) or slayer helmet (i) on a Slayer task.

Players can attach an occult ornament kit, obtained from master clue scrolls, to cosmetically enhance the necklace, creating an occult necklace (or). This only alters its appearance, and gives no stat enhancements. It can be dismantled, returning the necklace and ornament kit.
23659:
Crystal saplings are used to grow crystal trees, with 74 Farming.

They can be made by planting a crystal acorn in a filled plant pot, with a gardening trowel in your inventory, and then watering the crystal seedling with a watering can or by using Humidify. When watered, the seedling will sprout into a sapling in one crop cycle (0-5 minutes).

Planting the sapling in the crystal tree patch in the Crwys district in north-east Prifddinas, with a spade in your inventory, will give 180 Farming experience. It will grow into a crystal tree after 480 minutes (8 hours), which gives 13,240 Farming experience.

The crystal tree cannot become diseased.

Players should use ultracompost to increase the crystal shard yield from 16-20 to 28-32 when the tree is cut down.

Crystal saplings cannot be converted into banknotes by Tool Leprechauns.
23661:
Crystal acorns are seeds used in the Farming skill. At level 74 Farming, crystal acorns may be planted in plant pots with a gardening trowel and watered to become crystal saplings. They can be obtained as a reward from the Elven Crystal Chest, by catching crystal implings or from trading crystal weapon, armour, and tool seeds to Pennant in Prifddinas. Pennant exchanges one acorn in return for any one seed, except for Enhanced crystal teleport seed.

After planting the sapling in the crystal tree patch found in Prifddinas and waiting for it to fully grow, which takes about eight hours, the plant will grow into a crystal tree which can be cut to yield crystal shards. Planting the crystal sapling yields 126 experience, and checking its health gives 13,240 experience. Crystal trees cannot become diseased.

Harvesting crystal trees grants 28-32 crystal shards if ultracompost is used. Other types of compost will yield fewer shards, down to 16-20 with no compost. Magic secateurs have no effect. Players can also receive bird nests after chopping the tree down.

One acorn can be used on the skilling pet Tangleroot to change its appearance.
23667:
The dragonstone armour set is an item obtained by exchanging a set of items with a Grand Exchange clerk via their right-click "Sets" option and clicking on the appropriate item set within the Item Sets interface.

It is commonly made in order to conveniently sell all five components of dragonstone armour at once.
23670: Iwan's flyer is an item obtained from The Gauntlet when dying after dealing minimal damage. The flyer advertises the shop Iwan's Maces, run by Iwan in northern Prifddinas. Using the item on Iwan has no effect; it has no use whatsoever.
23673:
The crystal axe is an item used in Woodcutting. It requires level 71 Woodcutting and Song of the Elves to create and use, with 50 Agility and 70 Attack required to wield it. It possesses the same special attack as the dragon axe, and gives the player a 15% increase in efficiency chopping logs over the rune axe, surpassing the 10% increase of the dragon axe. This makes the crystal axe approximately 4.5% faster than the dragon axe.

Players can create a crystal axe via a singing bowl by combining a dragon axe, 120 crystal shards and a crystal tool seed. Doing so requires level 76 Smithing[boostable] and 76 Crafting[boostable] to sing the crystal, and grants 6,000 experience in both skills. Players can configure the charges while the axe is in their bank by right-clicking on Configure-Charges, as long as players have the required materials. If the player does not meet the Smithing and Crafting requirements, they can have Conwenna or Reese sing the crystal for them for an extra 60 crystal shards, for a total of 180.

After creation, the player can revert the crystal axe into a dragon axe. This process returns the crystal tool seed and the dragon axe to the player, but all crystal shards used to create or charge the axe are lost.

A dangerous death in PvP causes the crystal axe to revert to a dragon axe, which will then be dropped for the killer. All crystal shards will be lost should this happen.

23677:
The dragon pickaxe (or) is a dragon pickaxe with a Zalcano shard added onto it. Song of the Elves does not need to be completed for players to create, equip, or use this pickaxe.

The shard gives no additional bonuses, and is only used to add aesthetics to the pickaxe. It costs 680,062 coins for both the parts to make the dragon pickaxe (or).

While the pickaxe is untradeable in its ornamented state, it can be reverted anytime, returning the dragon pickaxe and Zalcano shard.
23680:
The crystal pickaxe is a pickaxe used in Mining. It requires 71 Mining and Song of the Elves to create and use, with 50 Agility and 70 Attack required to wield it. It possesses the same special attack as the dragon pickaxe. A charged crystal pickaxe provides a chance to mine an ore every three ticks (with an additional 1/4 chance to reduce this to two ticks); excluding waiting for ores to respawn or having to move to a new resource, the crystal pickaxe is effectively a 3.03% increase in overall mining speed compared to a dragon pickaxe or 9.09% compared to a rune pickaxe. An uncharged crystal pickaxe has the same mining capabilities as a dragon pickaxe.

23757:
The Youngllef is a pet received from the reward chest in the Gauntlet. It is a smaller version of the Crystalline Hunllef. Upon completion of the Corrupted Gauntlet, players unlock the right click "Metamorphosis" option to change between the regular Youngllef and the corrupted Youngllef variant. The pet will always be received in the regular form, even if it is obtained from the Corrupted Gauntlet.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. The pet cannot be picked up and instead must be reclaimed from Probita.
23760:
Smolcano is a pet dropped by Zalcano. It is a much smaller version of Zalcano.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed.
