23768: The crystal impling jar is the result of successfully catching a crystal impling, while also having an empty impling jar. Level 80 Hunter is required to catch them.
23770: Clue scroll (elite) is a coordinate clue obtained from elite Treasure Trails.
23771: The Prifddinas teleport is a magic tablet that can be broken by players to teleport just outside the Prifddinas house portal in the Ithell Clan district. It can be created after completion of Song of the Elves by using a scroll of redirection on a teleport to house tablet.
23773: Scrawled notes are obtained by searching the dead mourner near the crystal dispenser in the Temple of Light. It directs players towards using the colour wheel that is obtained alongside the notes and the nearby dispenser to solve the light puzzles during Mourning's End Part II.
23775: The hand mirror is a quest item used in the Mourning's End Part II and the Song of the Elves quest. It is obtained by pulling a lever in the Temple of Light near the start of the quest and is needed to solve the light puzzle in the Temple. As the player progresses through the puzzle they are rewarded with more mirrors in order to unlock more complicated parts of the puzzle. The mirrors redirect light to the place it needs to go if you put it at the right angle.
23776: The red crystal is a crystal used in the light puzzle section during Song of the Elves. It can be placed on a pillar to recolour the light beam going through it.
23778:
Green crystal may refer to:

Green crystal (Mourning's End Part II)

Green crystal (Song of the Elves)

Green crystal (unobtainable)
23781: The magenta crystal is a crystal used in the light puzzle section during Song of the Elves. It can be placed on a pillar to recolour the light beam going through it.
23782: The Black crystal is an unobtainable crystal released alongside Song of the Elves. It can be seen in the chatbox when inspecting the pillar near the Seal of Ithell which has the black crystal jammed inside it.
23783:
Green crystal may refer to:

Green crystal (Mourning's End Part II)

Green crystal (Song of the Elves)

Green crystal (unobtainable)
23784: The fractured crystal is a crystal used in the light puzzle section during Song of the Elves. When it is placed on a pillar, the incoming light will be split and continue outward in multiple directions.
23785:
The Ardougne knight helm is a quest item used in Song of the Elves. It is made by using red dye on a steel full helm to emulate the equipment of a Knight of Ardougne. It has no Defence requirement to wear, and has identical stats to an iron full helm.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Ardougne knight armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
23787:
The Ardougne knight platebody is a quest item from Song of the Elves. An Ardougne knight tabard is obtained by Alrena for a purple dye and some silk, which is then combined with a steel platebody to obtain this item.

If the Ardougne knight tabard or platebody is lost, Alrena will give out a new tabard for free.

The defensive bonuses of this item are equivalent to those of an iron platebody, despite the item requiring a steel platebody to create. However, it can be equipped even at level 1 Defence.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Ardougne knight armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
23789:
The Ardougne knight platelegs is a piece of equipment used in Song of the Elves. It is obtained by the player asking Edmond to polish steel platelegs, wiping the Defence requirement and making this the only method for accounts such as one-defence pures to complete Song of the Elves. It shares the same bonuses as iron platelegs. It is impossible to obtain for players with the required Defence level to wear steel platelegs, even if deboosting Defence level.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Ardougne knight armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

If lost, a pair of steel platelegs can be used instead to store in the armour case.
23791:
The Ardougne knight tabard is a quest item from Song of the Elves. It is made by Alrena by giving her Purple dye and some Silk. The tabard is then used on a Steel platebody to make the Ardougne knight platebody.

If the Ardougne knight tabard or platebody is lost, Alrena will replace it for free.
23792: The blue liquid is one of the chemicals in Elena's cabinet during Song of the Elves. It is obtained when the player incorrectly takes the thin blue liquid. The player is supposed to take the thick clear liquid instead.
23794: The clear liquid is a vial containing sulphuric acid, obtained from Elena's cabinet during Song of the Elves. It is obtained when the player correctly chooses the thick clear liquid. Elena uses this acid to escape from her jail cell.
23795: The red powder is one of the chemicals in Elena's cabinet during Song of the Elves. It is obtained when the player incorrectly takes the dark red powder. The player is supposed to take the thick clear liquid instead.
23798: The elder cadantine is a quest item in Song of the Elves. Elena grows it with your help to make an inversion potion by mixing the herb with crystal dust in a vial of water.
23800: An elder cadantine potion (unf) is a quest item in Song of the Elves made by using an elder cadantine on a vial of water. The player must then use crystal dust on this unfinished potion to make an inversion potion.
23802: Crystal is a material used by the elves, which was gifted to them by their goddess Seren. It is infused with some of her divine power, and is an important part of elven culture. It can be shaped, formed, and magically charged into weapons, tools, or other items with magical powers by the use of crystal seeds and crystal shards. Crystal seeds and shards can be transformed via crystal singing, either by using a singing bowl with sufficient Crafting and Smithing levels, or by the service of a crystal singer. Crystal shards can also be ground into crystal dust for use in Herblore, to transform certain combat stat-boosting potions into divine potions.
23804:
Crystal dust is a Herblore tertiary ingredient used for creating divine potions. Divine potions provide the same level of stat boosts as the base potion they are made from, but stay boosted to their maximum for 5 minutes instead of the boost reducing by one level per minute as normal potions do.

Crystal dust can be made by using a pestle and mortar on crystal shards, to create 10 dust per shard. One dust is used per dose (similar to amylase crystals in stamina potions); therefore, a single shard provides enough dust to create two and a half full divine potions.
23812: The orb of light is a quest item in Song of the Elves that is recovered from the cave by Iorwerth Camp. It is used to unlock access to Seren's dark essence.
23820: The corrupted sceptre is a weak melee weapon given to players when they start the Corrupted Gauntlet. It is required to light nodes next to doorways, allowing access to adjacent rooms.
23821: A corrupted axe is a basic axe that is given to the player at the start of the Corrupted Gauntlet. It is used to obtain Phren bark from Phren roots within the Corrupted Gauntlet.
23822: A corrupted pickaxe is a basic pickaxe that is given to the player at the start of the Corrupted Gauntlet. It is used to obtain corrupted ore from crystal outcrops within the Corrupted Gauntlet.
23824:
Corrupted shards are obtained from various activities in the Corrupted Gauntlet, and are used to create most pieces of equipment within the minigame. They will be automatically placed into the inventory when dropped by monsters or resources.

They can be ground with a pestle and mortar to receive 10 corrupted dust each, which are an ingredient to create egniol potions.
23831: The corrupted spike is an item used inside the Corrupted Gauntlet. It is obtained as a drop from the Corrupted Bear miniboss. It can be used with the attuned corrupted halberd to create the perfected corrupted halberd. Players may use a pestle and mortar to crush the spike into 80 corrupted shards. The next kill of the Corrupted Bear will still provide the 50/50 chance of the corrupted bowstring and corrupted orb.
23833: The corrupted orb is an item used in the Corrupted Gauntlet. It is obtained as a drop from the Corrupted Dragon miniboss. It can be used with the attuned corrupted staff to create a perfected corrupted staff. Players may use a pestle and mortar to crush the orb into 80 corrupted shards. The next kill of the Corrupted Dragon will still provide the 50/50 chance of the corrupted bowstring and corrupted spike.
23834: A weapon frame can be obtained as a drop from any monster in the Gauntlet. The weapon frame is used to create the lowest tier crystal halberd, bow, or staff. These items can be attuned to tier 2 by using 50 crystal shards. Depending on which weapon is created, the attuned weapons can be perfected to tier 3 by using a unique item (either the crystal spike, orb or bowstring).
23835: Grym leaf is a herb that found within the Gauntlet, obtained by either picking a Grym Root or as a drop from crystalline monsters. It is used to make a grym potion (unf), which is used with 10 crystal dust to create an egniol potion.
23837: Corrupted ore is mined from crystal outcrops within the Corrupted Gauntlet. It is used alongside phren bark and linum tirinum to create and upgrade corrupted helms, bodies, and legs.
23838: Phren bark is chopped from Phren Roots within the Gauntlet. It is used alongside crystal ore and linum tirinum to create and upgrade crystal helms, bodies, and legs.
23839: Vials are typically filled up with water and are most commonly used in the Herblore skill to make potions or mixes. Upon finishing a potion, the empty vial is left in the player's inventory; however with completion of Alfred Grimhand's Barcrawl, players may speak to the barbarian guard outside of the Barbarian Outpost to learn how to automatically smash vials upon finishing a potion. This feature also works in free-to-play. The player may also toggle this feature from the settings menu.
23843:
A basic corrupted body is a piece of corrupted crystal armour created within the Corrupted Gauntlet, made from 50 corrupted shards, 1 corrupted ore, 1 phren bark, and 1 linum tirinum.

It can be upgraded into an attuned corrupted body by using 100 corrupted shards, 2 corrupted ore, 2 phren bark, and 2 linum tirinum.
23844:
An attuned corrupted body is a piece of corrupted crystal armour created within the Corrupted Gauntlet, made from 100 corrupted shards, 1 basic corrupted body, 2 corrupted ore, 2 phren bark, and 2 linum tirinum.

It can be upgraded into a perfected corrupted body by using 100 corrupted shards, 2 corrupted ore, 2 phren bark, and 2 linum tirinum.
23845:
A perfected corrupted body is a piece of corrupted crystal armour created within the Corrupted Gauntlet, made from 100 corrupted shards, 1 attuned corrupted body, 2 corrupted ore, 2 phren bark, and 2 linum tirinum.

In total, a player will require 250 corrupted shards, 5 corrupted ore, 5 phren bark, and 5 linum tirinum to create the perfected corrupted body.
23846:
Basic corrupted legs are a piece of corrupted crystal armour created within the Corrupted Gauntlet made from 50 corrupted shards, 1 corrupted ore, 1 phren bark, and 1 linum tirinum.

It can be upgraded into a pair of attuned corrupted legs by using 50 corrupted shards, 1 corrupted ore, 1 phren bark, and 1 linum tirinum.
23847:
Attuned corrupted legs are a piece of corrupted crystal armour created within the Corrupted Gauntlet, made from 50 corrupted shards, 1 basic corrupted legs, 1 corrupted ore, 1 phren bark, and 1 linum tirinum.

It can be upgraded into a pair of perfected corrupted legs by using 100 corrupted shards, 2 corrupted ore, 2 phren bark, and 2 linum tirinum.
23848:
Perfected corrupted legs are a piece of corrupted crystal armour created within the Corrupted Gauntlet, made from 100 corrupted shards, 1 attuned corrupted legs, 2 corrupted ore, 2 phren bark, and 2 linum tirinum.

In total, a player will require 250 corrupted shards, 4 corrupted ore, 4 phren bark, and 4 linum tirinum to create the perfected corrupted legs.
23852:
A basic corrupted staff is a powered staff that can be created in the Corrupted Gauntlet, made from a weapon frame. It can be upgraded into an attuned corrupted staff by using 50 corrupted shards.

The staff has a max hit of 23, regardless of Magic level.
23853:
An attuned corrupted staff is a powered staff that can be created in the Corrupted Gauntlet, made from 50 corrupted shards and a basic corrupted staff. It can be upgraded into a perfected corrupted staff by using a corrupted orb.

The staff has a max hit of 31, regardless of Magic level.
23854:
A perfected corrupted staff is a powered staff that can be created in the Corrupted Gauntlet, made from an attuned corrupted staff and a corrupted orb.

In total, a player will require 50 corrupted shards, a weapon frame, and a corrupted orb to create the perfected corrupted staff.

The staff has a max hit of 39, regardless of Magic level. This is increased to 40 when using Augury or Mystic Vigour.
23855: A basic corrupted bow is a weapon that can be created in the Corrupted Gauntlet, made from a weapon frame. It can be upgraded into an attuned corrupted bow by using 50 corrupted shards.
23856: An attuned corrupted bow is a weapon that can be created in the Corrupted Gauntlet, made from 50 corrupted shards and a basic corrupted bow. It can be upgraded into a perfected corrupted bow by using a corrupted bowstring.
23858:
Corrupted teleport crystal is a single-use item received when starting the Corrupted Gauntlet. It teleports players back to the starting room.

Additional crystals can be created with 50 corrupted shards.
23861: The crystal sceptre is a weak melee weapon given to players when they start the Gauntlet. It is required to light nodes next to doorways, allowing access to adjacent rooms.

23872: Raw paddlefish is a fish found in the Gauntlet, which can be obtained from using a crystal harpoon on fishing spots or as drops from the crystalline monsters. It can be cooked to create paddlefish, which heal 20 hitpoints. The fish can be burnt, which will create burnt paddlefish.
23873: Burnt paddlefish is the result of accidentally burning raw paddlefish while attempting to make paddlefish. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 47.
23874:

23880: The water-filled vial is a vial filled with water, which is created via the singing bowl within the Gauntlet with 10 crystal shards. It is used to create egniol potions in the Gauntlet.
23881: Grym potion (unf) is an unfinished potion that can be made in the Gauntlet by using a Grym leaf on a water-filled vial. It is used with 10 crystal dust to create an egniol potion.
23886:
A basic crystal helm is a piece of crystal armour created within the Gauntlet, made from 50 crystal shards, 1 crystal ore, 1 phren bark, and 1 linum tirinum.

It can be upgraded into an attuned crystal helm by using 50 crystal shards, 1 crystal ore, 1 phren bark, and 1 linum tirinum.
23887:
An attuned crystal helm is a piece of crystal armour created within the Gauntlet, made from 50 crystal shards, 1 basic crystal helm, 1 crystal ore, 1 phren bark, and 1 linum tirinum.

It can be upgraded into a perfected crystal helm by using 100 crystal shards, 2 crystal ore, 2 phren bark, and 2 linum tirinum.
23888:
A perfected crystal helm is a piece of crystal armour created within the Gauntlet, made from 100 crystal shards, 1 attuned crystal helm, 2 crystal ore, 2 phren bark, and 2 linum tirinum.

In total, a player will require 200 crystal shards, 4 crystal ore, 4 phren bark, and 4 linum tirinum to create the perfected crystal helm.
23889:

It can be upgraded into an attuned crystal body by using 100 crystal shards, 2 crystal ore, 2 phren bark, and 2 linum tirinum.
23890:
An attuned crystal body is a piece of crystal armour created within the Gauntlet, made from 100 crystal shards, 1 basic crystal body, 2 crystal ore, 2 phren bark, and 2 linum tirinum.

It can be upgraded into a perfected crystal body by using 100 crystal shards, 2 crystal ore, 2 phren bark, and 2 linum tirinum.
23891:
A perfected crystal body is a piece of crystal armour created within the Gauntlet, made from 100 crystal shards, 1 attuned crystal body, 2 crystal ore, 2 phren bark, and 2 linum tirinum.

23893:

23894:

23898:
A basic crystal staff is a powered staff that can be created in the Gauntlet from a weapon frame. It can be upgraded into an attuned crystal staff by using 50 crystal shards.

The staff has a max hit of 23, regardless of level.
23899:
An attuned crystal staff is a powered staff that can be created in the Gauntlet from 50 crystal shards and a basic crystal staff. It can be upgraded into a perfected crystal staff with a crystal orb.

The staff has a max hit of 31, regardless of level.
23900:
A perfected crystal staff is a powered staff that can be created in the Gauntlet from an attuned crystal staff and a crystal orb.

In total, a player will require 50 crystal shards, a weapon frame, and a crystal orb to create the perfected crystal staff.

The staff has a max hit of 39, regardless of level. This is increased to 40 by the Mystic Vigour and Augury prayers.
23901: A basic crystal bow is a weapon that can be created in the Gauntlet, made from a weapon frame. It can be upgraded into an attuned crystal bow by using 50 crystal shards.
23902: An attuned crystal bow is a weapon that can be created in the Gauntlet, made from 50 crystal shards and a basic crystal bow. It can be upgraded into a perfected crystal bow by using a crystalline bowstring.
23903:
A perfected crystal bow is a weapon that can be created in the Gauntlet, made from an attuned crystal bow and a crystalline bowstring.

In total, a player will require 50 crystal shards, a weapon frame, and a crystalline bowstring to create the perfected crystal bow.
23906: Refined tephra is obtained by using tephra mined within Zalcano's prison on the furnace in the east, granting 10 Smithing experience per refined tephra. Players must then imbue them at the altar to create imbued tephra, which is used to deal damage to Zalcano's stone armour.
23907:
Imbued tephra is obtained by imbuing refined tephra at the Seren altar in the western end of Zalcano's prison. It can also be obtained from golems that Zalcano occasionally summons.

The imbued tephra is the only item that can deal damage to Zalcano while she is still standing; the damage dealt is scaled based on the player's Smithing and Runecraft levels. In addition, if she has summoned demonic symbols around the prison, the blue symbols will increase the damage dealt. Players can either attack Zalcano directly while having the imbued tephra in their inventory to use them, or equip and throw them at her.
23908:
The Zalcano shard is an item dropped by Zalcano. It can be used on the dragon pickaxe to create the dragon pickaxe (or), which alters its appearance. It is solely a cosmetic upgrade and does not change the stats.

The shard is the second cosmetic add-on for the dragon pickaxe, after the dragon pickaxe upgrade kit. However, unlike the upgrade kit, it will not be destroyed should players revert the dragon pickaxe to its regular appearance.
23911:
The crystal crown is a purely cosmetic crown purchasable from the Lliann's Wares in Prifddinas's Ithell district for 250,000,000 coins. The crown is untradeable, and it cannot be alchemised or sold back to Lliann's shop.

It should be noted that Lliann's Wares initially carries three crowns in stock. Each crown in stock is set to resupply after as many game ticks as it costs (250 million), which can take several years. However, like all other shops, the stock refreshes back to three crowns after server restarts, such as maintenance or game updates. Due to the low number of players wishing to buy crystal crowns, the restock time should not be a concern.

The crown’s colours, based on that of the Ithell Clan, may be changed to other colours of the Elven Clans. The crystals needed to do so can be bought from the same store for 500,000 coins each. It can also be reverted to the Ithell Clan's colour by using the crystal of Ithell on any variant of the crystal crown.
23913:
The Iorwerth crystal crown is a purely cosmetic crown made by using the crystal of Iorwerth on any variant of the crystal crown.

23943:
The elven signet is a unique ring obtainable only from crystal implings. When worn, it offers a 10% chance to not use a charge when using crystal equipment, excluding the blade of Saeldor and the bow of Faerdhinen.

The signet can be combined with a celestial ring at a singing bowl, alongside 100 crystal shards and 1,000 stardust, to create the celestial signet, which combines the effects of both. Doing so requires level 70 Smithing and Crafting; if the player does not meet the Smithing and Crafting requirements, they can have Conwenna or Reese sing the crystal for them for an extra 50 crystal shards, for a total of 150.
23946:
The eternal teleport crystal is an item that can be used to teleport to Lletya and Prifddinas, in a similar fashion to the teleport crystal, but with infinite charges. You cannot obtain it before completing Song of the Elves.

Players can create an eternal teleport crystal via a singing bowl by combining an enhanced crystal teleport seed and 100 crystal shards. Doing so requires level 80 Smithing and Crafting to sing the crystal (the levels can be boosted), and grants 5,000 experience in both skills. If the player does not meet the Smithing and Crafting requirements, they can have Conwenna or Reese sing the crystal for them for an extra 50 crystal shards, for a total of 150, you are also not granted the experience if made for you.
23948:
Elven dawn is a type of ale that restores 1 Hitpoint and temporarily boosts Agility by 1 while draining Strength by 1.

It is purchasable at the Hefin Inn in Prifddinas. Unlike other ales, it cannot be created through brewing.
23953:
The crystal tool seed is an elven crystal that can be turned into the crystal axe, crystal harpoon, or crystal pickaxe, using 120 crystal shards and the dragon counterpart on a singing bowl. It can be obtained as a drop from Zalcano.

The crystal tools start off at 10,000 charges and degrades, like other crystal equipment. One charge is depleted for each time an item is obtained using the tool, with some exceptions for particular uses of the axe and pickaxe where the crystal version has no additional benefit (duplicates from items such as the Varrock armour do not deplete an extra charge). The player may add charges with crystal shards, with each shard granting 100 charges, up to a maximum of 20,000 charges. Dismantling a crystal tool will return the dragon equivalent and crystal tool seed to the player and doing so will lose all crystal shard charges that were previously loaded.

Players can also exchange the tool seed for 100 crystal shards by speaking to Amrod in Prifddinas' Hefin Inn.

A dangerous death in PvP causes the crystal tools to revert to their dragon equivalents which will then be dropped for the killer. All crystal shards will be lost as well.
23956:
The crystal armour seed is an elven crystal that can be turned into crystal armour at a singing bowl. Completing the Gauntlet will yield a chance of gaining these seeds and combining them with crystal shards can be used to create the armour pieces.

Players can also exchange the armour seed for 250 crystal shards by speaking to Amrod in Prifddinas' Hefin Inn. The seed can additionally be traded to Pennant in Prifddinas for one crystal acorn.
23964:
Crystal dust is a Herblore tertiary ingredient used for creating divine potions. Divine potions provide the same level of stat boosts as the base potion they are made from, but stay boosted to their maximum for 5 minutes instead of the boost reducing by one level per minute as normal potions do.

Crystal dust can be made by using a pestle and mortar on crystal shards, to create 10 dust per shard. One dust is used per dose (similar to amylase crystals in stamina potions); therefore, a single shard provides enough dust to create two and a half full divine potions.
23975:
A crystal body is a piece of crystal armour requiring 70 Defence and 50 Agility to equip. When equipped, a 7.5% damage bonus and 15% accuracy bonus is applied to the crystal bow or Bow of Faerdhinen when either is equipped. This bonus stacks additively with the crystal legs and crystal helm's bonuses, for a total of 15% damage and 30% accuracy. The bonus also stacks with the slayer helmet (i) and is useful for bosses similar to the Abyssal Sire.

Players can create a crystal body via a singing bowl by combining 150 crystal shards and three crystal armour seeds. Doing so requires level 74 Smithing and Crafting to sing the crystal (the levels can be boosted), and grants 7,500 experience in both skills. Players can configure the charges while the crystal body is in their bank by right-clicking on Configure-Charges, as long as players have the required materials. If the player does not meet the Smithing and Crafting requirements, they can have Conwenna or Reese sing the crystal for them for an extra 60 crystal shards, for a total of 210.

The body's colours may also be changed to other colours of the Elven Clans by buying crystals from Lliann's Wares in Prifddinas, which cost 500,000 coins each. It can also be reverted to its original colour by using the crystal of Meilyr on any variant of the body.

If lost to another player in a dangerous PVP death, the crystal body will revert to 3 crystal armour seeds, which will then be dropped for the killer. All crystal shards will be lost should this happen. If the crystal body is protected on death, the body will be kept, and will not lose any charges- similar to a blowpipe or trident.

When combined with an imbued slayer helmet, the damage bonus from crystal armour pieces is multiplied by the 15% ranged damage boost from the helmet. Assuming players are wearing both the crystal body and legs, this results in a damage bonus of approximately 29.375%.

23983:
The crystal bow is a powerful degradable bow available after a player completes the Roving Elves quest, and a possible reward from this quest along with the crystal shield. The crystal bow may be made from enchanted elven crystals. To wield the crystal bow, a player must have 70 Ranged, 50 Agility and have completed the Roving Elves quest. The crystal bow benefits from damage and accuracy boosts when crystal armour is equipped.

A crystal bow is created when an elf sings to a crystal weapon seed and enchants it into a bow. The most prominent elf with this talent is Ilfeen, who will perform this service for players for a price. However, she can only do this with a weapon seed; partially charged bows should be reverted to their seed form (using the right-click menu in the inventory) to be converted back into a bow.

Because it is blessed by the elven goddess Seren, the crystal bow does not require any arrows to use, as it generates its own when fired. The bow's fired shots are coated in a green aura, similar to Craw's bow, and rolls damage against an NPC's standard ranged defence.

The crystal bow can be considered the penultimate bow in the composite bow family, before the bow of Faerdhinen. It shares the same 10-square attack range on any style as well as a 4-tick attack speed on rapid, placing it between popular ranged weapons like the shortbow (3-tick) and crossbow (5-tick).

The crystal bow is required to complete the Hard Western Provinces Diary. It is also used for two master clue steps: an emote step and as a possible item to show Falo the Bard.

23987:
The crystal halberd is a degradable two-handed polearm made from a crystal weapon seed. It requires completion of the Hard Western Provinces Diary to wield, as well as 70 Attack, 35 Strength and 50 Agility.

In order to obtain a crystal halberd (with 2,500 charges), one must talk to Islwyn who will offer to sell a crystal halberd for 750,000 coins. Alternatively, one can take a crystal weapon seed to Ilfeen to be recharged into a crystal halberd with 2,500 charges starting at a price of 750,000 coins, lowering by 150,000 each time afterwards, eventually reaching a recharge price of 150,000 coins.

With access to Prifddinas and completion of the Hard Western Provinces Diary, the singing bowl can be used with 78 Crafting and Smithing and 40 crystal shards to turn a crystal weapon seed into a crystal halberd. Players without the stat requirements can speak to Conwenna or Reese and have them create the crystal halberd for you for 20 additional crystal shards.

The crystal halberd is significantly more powerful than a dragon halberd, making it a good choice as a melee safespot weapon.

The crystal halberd can deal full damage to the Corporeal Beast, despite not being a spear, but it must be on the stab attack style.

The crystal halberd is used for its special attack, which can deal high damage against large enemies or groups of enemies. However, its special attack is bested in DPS by the special attacks of both the dragon dagger and dragon claws against most monsters, making its use largely centred around last-hitting and AoE damage.

23995:
The blade of Saeldor is a one-handed slash sword that once belonged to Saeldor, an elite elven warrior, that can be created from an enhanced crystal weapon seed. Requiring level 80 Attack to wield, it provides the highest slash bonus out of any one-handed weapon for its attack speed, and is tied with the two-handed Saradomin's blessed sword for highest slash bonus of any weapon for its speed (although using any sort of defender makes the blade a superior choice). It is considered the best one-handed slash weapon in the game and one of the strongest one-handed melee weapons, along with the Ghrazi rapier and the Inquisitor's mace; though these weapons are weaker than Osmumten's fang against high-defence, stab-susceptible monsters.

On unprotected death in PvP, the inactive blade is dropped, and all shards used to charge it will be lost. In PvM on the other hand, all current charges will be kept upon death.

This item is purely cosmetic. When equipped, it causes the player to sway around when standing or walking to mimic drunkenness, similar to the ale of the gods.

24034:
The dragonstone full helm can be found as a rare reward upon opening the Elven Crystal Chest within Prifddinas. It has the same stats as rune full helm and requires 40 Defence to equip.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Dragonstone armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Dragonstone armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
24051:
A Dear Friend is a book found in the Grand Library in Prifddinas, which requires completion of Song of the Elves to access.

The book is written before the First Age prior to the elves' arrival on Gielinor from their homeworld Tarddiad. It describes the experiences of Caron and his wife's encounter with a Hunllef cub, the elves' natural predator, on Tarddiad.

If lost, it can be reclaimed from any bookshelf in the Grand Library, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house.
24053:
On Leprechauns is a book found in the Grand Library in Prifddinas, which requires completion of Song of the Elves to access.

The short book describes a possible sinister side to the Tool Leprechauns that hold a player's farming tools.

If lost, it can be reclaimed from any bookshelf in the Grand Library, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house.
24055:
The bloody diary is a book found in the Grand Library in Prifddinas, which requires completion of Song of the Elves to access.

The diary was written during the War of the Five Houses 200 years ago by an unnamed adventurer from Hosidius. However, most of the pages have been stained in blood and cannot be read by the player.

The few entries that remain unstained describes the adventurer's return to Great Kourend after the war, some of his adventures in Varlamore, as well as nearly discovering how to create Arclight.

If lost, it can be reclaimed from any bookshelf in the Grand Library, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house.
24057:
The Eight Clans is a hymn found in the Grand Library in Prifddinas, which requires completion of Song of the Elves to access.

The hymn sings of the eight Elven Clans and their specialties.

If lost, it can be reclaimed from any bookshelf in the Grand Library, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house.
24061:
Niff & Harry is a poem found in the Grand Library in Prifddinas, which requires completion of Song of the Elves to access.

The poem describes an encounter between Niff Delfingus, a nurse who was said to be able to cure any illness, and a human named Sir Harry the Hero. It is not known whether the Harry referred to in the poem is the same Sir Harry encountered in the Underground Pass.

If lost, it can be reclaimed from any bookshelf in the Grand Library, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house.
24065:
Ebrill's journal is a book found in the Grand Library in Prifddinas, which requires completion of Song of the Elves to access.

The journal is written by Ebrill, an elf of the Iorwerth Clan, and describes his attempts to contact his friend, Colwyn, shortly before Lord Iorwerth's bloody conquest of the city during the Fourth Age.

If lost, it can be reclaimed from any bookshelf in the Grand Library, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house.
24069:
The Truth Behind the Myth (excerpt) is a book found in the Grand Library in Prifddinas, which requires completion of Song of the Elves to access.

The excerpt written is from a book about Camorra Shayzien, a famous heroine during the Fourth Age, and ponders about why her slaying of Garak was considered a more impressive feat than her heroic acts with Robert the Strong during the Dragonkin Conflicts.

If lost, it can be reclaimed from any bookshelf in the Grand Library, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house.
24071:
The Living Statues is a book found in the Grand Library in Prifddinas, which requires completion of Song of the Elves to access.

The book is written by a Dorgeshuun goblin during the God Wars and details his involvement with the Bandosian general Snaarldor in the creation of the gargoyles and the Grotesque Guardians in Viggora's Folly.

If lost, it can be reclaimed from any bookshelf in the Grand Library, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house.
24073:
The Spurned Demon is a book found in the Grand Library in Prifddinas, which requires completion of Song of the Elves to access.

The book details how Zalcano came to be imprisoned in the volcanic caverns beneath Prifddinas by the elves.

If lost, it can be reclaimed from any bookshelf in the Grand Library, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house.
24123:
The crystal bow is a powerful degradable bow available after a player completes the Roving Elves quest, and a possible reward from this quest along with the crystal shield. The crystal bow may be made from enchanted elven crystals. To wield the crystal bow, a player must have 70 Ranged, 50 Agility and have completed the Roving Elves quest. The crystal bow benefits from damage and accuracy boosts when crystal armour is equipped.

A crystal bow is created when an elf sings to a crystal weapon seed and enchants it into a bow. The most prominent elf with this talent is Ilfeen, who will perform this service for players for a price. However, she can only do this with a weapon seed; partially charged bows should be reverted to their seed form (using the right-click menu in the inventory) to be converted back into a bow.

Because it is blessed by the elven goddess Seren, the crystal bow does not require any arrows to use, as it generates its own when fired. The bow's fired shots are coated in a green aura, similar to Craw's bow, and rolls damage against an NPC's standard ranged defence.

The crystal bow can be considered the penultimate bow in the composite bow family, before the bow of Faerdhinen. It shares the same 10-square attack range on any style as well as a 4-tick attack speed on rapid, placing it between popular ranged weapons like the shortbow (3-tick) and crossbow (5-tick).

The crystal bow is required to complete the Hard Western Provinces Diary. It is also used for two master clue steps: an emote step and as a possible item to show Falo the Bard.
24125:
The crystal halberd is a degradable two-handed polearm made from a crystal weapon seed. It requires completion of the Hard Western Provinces Diary to wield, as well as 70 Attack, 35 Strength and 50 Agility.

In order to obtain a crystal halberd (with 2,500 charges), one must talk to Islwyn who will offer to sell a crystal halberd for 750,000 coins. Alternatively, one can take a crystal weapon seed to Ilfeen to be recharged into a crystal halberd with 2,500 charges starting at a price of 750,000 coins, lowering by 150,000 each time afterwards, eventually reaching a recharge price of 150,000 coins.

With access to Prifddinas and completion of the Hard Western Provinces Diary, the singing bowl can be used with 78 Crafting and Smithing and 40 crystal shards to turn a crystal weapon seed into a crystal halberd. Players without the stat requirements can speak to Conwenna or Reese and have them create the crystal halberd for you for 20 additional crystal shards.

The crystal halberd is significantly more powerful than a dragon halberd, making it a good choice as a melee safespot weapon.

The crystal halberd can deal full damage to the Corporeal Beast, despite not being a spear, but it must be on the stab attack style.

The crystal halberd is used for its special attack, which can deal high damage against large enemies or groups of enemies. However, its special attack is bested in DPS by the special attacks of both the dragon dagger and dragon claws against most monsters, making its use largely centred around last-hitting and AoE damage.
24130: The combat path starter kit is an item obtained from Adventurer Jon for free after starting the combat path of the Adventure Paths. It contains an assortment of combat-related items.
24131: Combat path voucher is an item obtained from Adventurer Jon by completing tasks in the Adventure Paths' Combat Path. It can be used to claim rewards from various NPCs in Varrock. Players can read the voucher to see a list of items they can still claim. Upon claiming the last reward, that NPC will take the voucher from the player.
24133:
The infernal max cape is the result of combining an infernal cape with a max cape, during which the max hood is required to be in the player's inventory and will automatically be converted to the infernal max hood.

Like the other max cape variants (a max cape combined with another cape slot item), the infernal max cape does not have the max cape's stats or perks; it only acts as a cosmetic upgrade to the infernal cape with the following exceptions when worn:

It acts as a Cooking cape to allow access to the Cooks' Guild without a chef's hat, golden chef's hat, Varrock armour 3 or 4

It acts as a Crafting cape to allow access to the Crafting Guild without a brown apron or golden apron

It acts as a Runecraft cape to prevent essence pouches from degrading (but does not allow access to runic altars)

It acts as a Firemaking cape to work as a piece of warm clothing

It can be used to perform the Skill Cape emote.

It is lighter, weighing 0.453kg instead of 1.814kg

The max cape and infernal cape can be separated by using a knife on the cape. Mac will also buy back a max cape, along with its variants, for 1,900,800 coins each. He will return the secondary item any max cape variant was combined with upon doing so.

If the player dies a PvP death at level 20 Wilderness or below and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 225,000 coins.

If the player dies a PvP death above level 20 Wilderness and the item is unprotected, it will be converted to coins. To prevent this, a Trouver parchment and a payment of 500,000 coins can be given to Perdu in order to permanently lock the item. The locked item will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a mangled, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 500,000 coins.

An infernal max cape cannot be gambled for a chance at Jal-Nib-Rek.

There were approximately 9,463 players who could have an infernal max cape as of 12th March 2022.
24135:
The Assembler max cape is the result of combining Ava's assembler with a max cape, during which the max hood required to be in the player's inventory will automatically convert to the assembler max hood.

Like the other max cape variants (a max cape combined with another cape slot item), the assembler max cape does not have the max cape's stats or perks; it only acts as a cosmetic upgrade to Ava's assembler with the following exceptions when worn:

It acts as a Cooking cape to allow access to the Cooks' Guild without a chef's hat, golden chef's hat, Varrock armour 3 or 4

It acts as a Crafting cape to allow access to the Crafting Guild without a brown apron or golden apron

It acts as a Firemaking cape to work as a piece of warm clothing

It can be used to perform the Skill Cape emote.

The max cape and assembler can be separated by using a knife on the cape. Mac will also buy back a max cape, along with its variants, for 1,900,800 coins each. He will return the secondary item any max cape variant was combined with upon doing so.

Turning the Ava's assembler into an assembler max cape is the only way for ultimate ironmen to store one, as it counts as a max cape on the cape rack.

If the player dies a PvP death and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 240,000 coins.
24136:
The bronze defender is the weakest defender. It is similar to a dagger, but held in the off-hand in place of a shield. The bronze defender is dropped by cyclopes on the top floor of the Warriors' Guild. Entry to the Cyclops room requires a minimum of 100 Warrior guild tokens.

If the player dies to a PvP death and the bronze defender is not one of the player's protected items, it will remain in the player's inventory, but will become broken, which means the item is unusable and must be repaired with 1,000 coins by using the item on Perdu.
24138:
The steel defender is the third weakest defender. It is similar to a dagger, but held in the off-hand in place of a shield. It requires 5 Attack and 5 Defence to wield. The steel defender is dropped by Cyclopes on the top floor of the Warriors' Guild, but only once you have obtained an iron defender.

If the player dies to a PvP death and the steel defender is not one of the player's protected items, it will remain in the player's inventory, but will become broken, which means the item is unusable and must be repaired with 2,500 coins by using the item on Perdu.
24139:
The black defender is a defender made of black metal. It is similar to a dagger, but held in the off-hand in place of a shield. It requires 10 Attack and 10 Defence to wield. The black defender is dropped by Cyclopes on the top floor of the Warriors' Guild, but only once you have obtained a steel defender.

If the player dies to a PvP death and the black defender is not one of the player's protected items, it will remain in the player's inventory, but will become broken, which means the item is unusable and must be repaired with 5,000 coins by using the item on Perdu.

The black defender does not count as an "evil" item in Shadow of the Storm despite its colour.
24141:
The adamant defender is a defender made out of adamant. It can be obtained by killing cyclopes on the top floor of the Warriors' Guild with a mithril defender in the inventory or after you have shown a mithril defender to Kamfreena. It is held in the shield slot and requires 30 Attack and Defence to wield.

If the player dies to a PvP death and the adamant defender is not one of the player's protected items, it will remain in the player's inventory, but will become broken, which means the item is unusable and must be repaired with 25,000 coins by using the item on Perdu.
24142:
The rune defender is the 3rd strongest defender. It is used for its attack bonus and is held in the off-hand in place of a shield. It requires 40 Attack and 40 Defence to wield. The rune defender is dropped by cyclopes on the top floor of the Warriors' Guild after showing an adamant defender or better as the player enters the room.

The rune defender's slash and crush defensive bonuses are the same as a black kiteshield, but its stab defence bonus is slightly less than an adamant square shield. However, it is much more commonly used for its melee bonuses, as it gives the same bonus to strength as the toktz-ket-xil (obsidian shield) and has melee attack bonuses. A rune defender is commonly combined with weapons such as a dragon scimitar or an abyssal whip as a result.

The defender is popular among players of higher combat levels due to its offensive stats. It can be considered to be the third best off-hand item for melee training, only beaten by the dragon defender and Avernic defender, and is commonly used in PvP situations as re-obtaining a rune defender is easier than re-obtaining a dragon or Avernic one.

If the player dies to a PvP death and the rune defender is not one of the player's protected items, it will remain in the player's inventory, but will become broken, which means the item is unusable and must be repaired with 35,000 coins by using the item on Perdu. Any ornament kit on the item will also be lost on death.

Players can attach a Rune defender ornament kit, obtained from hard Treasure Trails, to create a Rune defender (t). This is only cosmetic, and does not affect the defender's stat bonuses. It can be dismantled, returning the defender and ornament kit.
24143:
The dragon defender is the second strongest defender, behind the Avernic defender. It is used for its attack and strength bonus and is held in the shield slot. It requires level 60 Defence to equip.

The dragon defender can only be obtained from the stronger level 106 Cyclopes found exclusively in the Warrior Guild's basement. To enter the basement for the first time, a player must show a rune defender to Lorelai, who will then grant them permanent access. Warrior Guild tokens are still required for time spent inside the basement unless the player has an Attack Cape equipped. Players can obtain a dragon defender without having a rune defender in their bank. Players can obtain the dragon defender without having 60 Defence.

Its melee defensive bonuses are comparable to those of an adamant square shield, with slight differences. Its strength bonus is surpassed by both the dragonfire shield and the Avernic defender, which give +7 and +8 strength bonuses, respectively. However, the dragon defender is more commonly used than either of these for melee training, due to its superior melee attack bonuses over the dragonfire shield and the overall rarity of the Avernic defender.

If the player dies to a PvP death and the dragon defender is not one of the player's protected items, it will remain in the player's inventory, but will become broken, which means the item is unusable and must be repaired with 240,000 coins by using the item on Perdu.
24144:
The staff of balance is a one-handed bladed staff which requires 75 Attack and 75 Magic to wield. It is created by bringing a Guthixian icon and a staff of the dead to Juna in the Chasm of Tears. This process is irreversible.

The staff of balance inherits all of the staff of the dead's effects. The only differences between them is that the staff of balance autocasts the Claws of Guthix god spell rather than the Flames of Zamorak god spell, and is unable to autocast Arceuus combat spells. In addition, it counts as a Zamorakian item while in the God Wars Dungeon and in the Desert Bandit Camp.

The staff of balance cannot be upgraded with a magic fang to provide the additional magic attack bonus and toxic effect given to the toxic staff of the dead.

The defensive bonuses of the halo are similar to those of a black full helm, excluding negative attack bonuses and Ranged defence bonus. In addition, the halo gives a prayer bonus and magic defence while the full helm does not.

If the player dies a PvP death and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 25,000 coins.

24169:
The Saradomin halo is an item worn in the head slot that can be bought from (or sold to) Lanthus for 75 Castle Wars tickets.

The Saradomin halo acts as a Saradomin item and thus prevents Saradomin followers from attacking its wearer in the God Wars Dungeon. It also allows players to be constantly attacked by Bandits at the Bandit Camp in the Kharidian Desert, as it is a god item.

The defensive bonuses of the halo are similar to those of a black full helm, excluding negative attack bonuses. In addition, the halo gives prayer bonus and magic defence while the full helm does not.

If the player dies a PvP death and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 25,000 coins.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room.
24172:
The healer hat is a possible reward item from Barbarian Assault and requires 45 Defence to wear. Players who have killed the Penance Queen and have 275 Honour points in each of the four roles can purchase the hat from Commander Connad, located on the main floor of the Barbarian Outpost. The hat is part of the penance set, all parts of which are available from Barbarian Assault.

Its stats are very similar to the farseer helm. Both require 45 Defence and offer +6 magic attack bonus with attack penalties of -5 to all other styles. However, the healer hat has a slightly higher (+1) magic defence bonus at the cost of lower melee defence (-2 to stab, slash, and crush).

If the player dies a PvP death and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 45,000 coins.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room.
24173:
The fighter hat is a piece of members-only armour that requires 45 Defence to wear, and is obtained through the Barbarian Assault minigame. Players with 275 honour points in each role and who have killed the Penance Queen can purchase the hat from Commander Connad, located on the ground floor of the Barbarian Outpost.

The fighter hat is sometimes used in place of the warrior helm and berserker helm. The warrior helm provides slightly better defensive bonuses, but offers an attack bonus to slash only, while the fighter hat also provides attack bonuses to stab and crush. In fact, the +5 stab attack bonus makes the fighter hat the best-in-slot item for stab attack. The berserker helm has slightly better defensive bonuses and provides a strength bonus (+3), but provides no melee attack bonuses. The fighter hat is a popular choice among obsidian maulers that are unable to obtain the Inquisitor's great helm.

If the player dies a PvP death and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 45,000 coins.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room.
24174:
A ranger hat is a piece of headgear available as a reward from Barbarian Assault. It resembles the head of a Penance Ranger.

Equipping the hat requires level 45 Defence. Players who have killed the Penance Queen and have 275 honour points in all four roles can purchase a Ranger hat from Commander Connad, who is located on the ground floor of the Barbarian Outpost. The Void Knight mace can be bought from a Void Knight for 250 commendation points, although a player must have 42 Attack, Strength, Defence, Hitpoints, Ranged, and Magic, along with 22 Prayer. The mace can be used to autocast Claws of Guthix, Crumble Undead, and the Wave and Surge spells. To cast Claws of Guthix, the player must have cast the spell 100 times in the Wilderness Mage Arena.

Note that the Void knight mace does not count towards the four pieces needed for the void set effect.

Its stats are relatively close to that of the rune mace, with the main difference being its 20% slower attack speed. It also has +2 bonus in Stab, Slash, and Crush attack, as well as Stab, Slash, Crush, Magic, and Ranged defence, as well as a relative +2 Strength and Prayer bonus compared to the rune mace. Due to its role as one of the weapons to cast Claws of Guthix, it also has a +8 Magic attack bonus. These stats make it one of the only melee weapons in game to have a positive ranged defence bonus, other than the Lunar staff, with +1, and the dragon spear and Zamorakian spear, with +5 and +13, respectively. Unlike other maces, it only has crushing attack styles. Alongside croziers, the hallowed flail, and the 3rd Age druidic staff, it has the highest Prayer bonus of all one-handed weapons.

While Claws of Guthix can be cast and autocast while wearing an imbued Saradomin cape or imbued Zamorak cape, an appropriate cape (Guthix cape or its imbued variant) must still be worn to receive the damage boost from Charge.

If the player dies a PvP death and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 20,000 coins.

The Void mage helm is a piece of Void Knight equipment. It can be bought from a Void Knight for 200 commendation points, if the player has at least 42 Attack, Strength, Defence, Hitpoints, Ranged, and Magic, and 22 Prayer to buy and wear one. It is worn in combination with the other pieces of Void Knight Armour (Void knight top, Void knight robe, and Void knight gloves) to achieve the designated set effect. The Void knight mace is not required for the bonus.

The Void mage set gives a +45% to magic accuracy. This typically provides less accuracy and defensive bonuses than Ahrim's robes, but can be easily switched with the other Void sets. If wearing Elite Void Knight robes, the set gives an additional 5% increase to magic damage.

The effective magic attack bonus can be calculated as 1.45x+28.8, where x is the total equipment magic attack bonus when wearing the Void mage set. For example, if you have a magic attack bonus of +16 while also wearing the Void mage set (which provides no bonus), the effective bonus becomes +52 taking into account the set effect. When wearing several best-in-slot pieces of magical gear, the accuracy of the Void mage set can surpass Ahrim's robes with the same gear.

24219:
The Swift blade is a one-handed weapon purchased from Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing for 350 Last Man Standing points.

It is one of the only four melee weapons with an attack speed of 3, with the other ones being the ham joint, goblin paint cannon, and mystic cards, with the latter two also being two handed weapons only. The swift blade also exclusively uses Stab and Slash attack styles whereas the others use Crush, and the mystic cards have negative combat stat bonuses whereas the others have no bonuses.

Due to having no Attack level requirement, the Swift blade is the best-in-slot weapon for training Defence pures and combines well with the stab bonus given by the Ardougne cloaks.

This item is also commonly used in the Theatre of Blood for the Nylocas room because of its fast attack speed. It is preferred over the Goblin paint cannon and the Ham joint because its attack styles are not shared with the dragon warhammer, allowing players to keep the dragon warhammer on an accurate attack style, while having the swift blade on an aggressive style. In addition, the swift blade is slightly more accurate than a ham joint when used with a defender, as defenders have +2 higher stab accuracy compared to crush.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room.
24224:
The infernal cape is the most powerful melee cape in terms of overall bonuses, awarded for defeating TzKal-Zuk in the Inferno. It surpasses its predecessor, the fire cape, boasting greater melee attack and strength bonuses, along with slightly higher defensive bonuses. In spite of this, it is still surpassed by the Ardougne cloaks 3 and 4 in stab attack and prayer bonuses, and by the mythical cape in crush attack.

An infernal cape can be exchanged for a chance of obtaining the Jal-Nib-Rek pet by speaking to TzHaar-Ket-Keh. Like killing TzKal-Zuk, there is a 1/100 chance of obtaining the pet this way. If the player already has the pet, capes cannot be exchanged.

An infernal cape can be combined with the max cape to change its appearance by turning it into the infernal max cape.

As of 1 August 2026, there are 170,755 accounts that have obtained an infernal cape.

If the player dies a PvP death at level 20 Wilderness or below and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 225,000 coins.

If the player dies a PvP death above level 20 Wilderness and the item is unprotected, it will be converted to coins. To prevent this, a Trouver parchment and a payment of 500,000 coins can be given to Perdu in order to permanently lock the item. The locked item will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a mangled, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 500,000 coins.

While equipping the fire cape will grant players the fiery attribute and will therefore make them susceptible to the extra damage from the special effect of pearl bolts (e), the infernal cape does not grant this attribute.

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room.
24225:
The ornate granite maul is a granite maul with an ornate maul handle attached to it. The handle enhances the granite maul by reducing its special attack cost from 60% to 50%. The handle is effectively consumed by this process, as while the maul can be reverted, the process will destroy the handle. The ornate handle is obtained from Justine's Stuff for the Last Shopper Standing.

A granite clamp can be added to the maul to adjust its appearance. The clamp gives no additional bonuses, and is only used to add aesthetics to the maul. While untradeable, the maul can be reverted to its tradeable state at any time using the right-click "Revert" option; however, the clamp will be destroyed upon doing so.

When this weapon is lost on death in PvP, it is converted to 90% of Grand Exchange price of the granite maul and the ornate maul handle.

If a player dies with the clamped maul and it is not one of the player's protected items, the maul will revert to its default appearance, and players must use another granite clamp to enhance its appearance again.

The imbued Saradomin cape is obtained from imbuing a Saradomin cape with the items dropped by Justiciar Zachariah, Porazdir, and Derwen, during the Mage Arena II miniquest, requiring 75 Magic. Subsequent imbues will require only the Justiciar's hand, or 250,000 to purchase from the Lost Property shop.

This cape, along with the imbued Guthix and Zamorak capes, provides the best in slot magic attack and magic damage bonus for the cape slot.

The cape, like most untradeable equipment, is automatically protected upon death in dangerous PvM scenarios outside of the Wilderness, and likewise is always protected upon safe deaths and services that offer an item reclaim function (such as Zulrah via Priestess Zul-Gwenwynig and the Grotesque Guardians via the magical chest).

If the player dies a PvP death and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 96,000 coins.

You may obtain all 3 god capes imbued at the same time. After completing the miniquest, you may return with duplicates of any dropped items by Justiciar Zachariah, Porazdir, and Derwen.

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room.
24238:
The imbued Saradomin max cape is the result of combining the imbued Saradomin cape with a max cape, during which the max hood required to be in the player's inventory will automatically convert to the imbued Saradomin max hood.

Like the other max cape variants (a max cape combined with another cape slot item), the imbued Saradomin max cape does not have the max cape's stats or perks; it only acts as a cosmetic upgrade to the imbued Saradomin cape with the following exceptions when worn:

It acts as a Cooking cape to allow access to the Cooks' Guild without a chef's hat, golden chef's hat, Varrock armour 3 or 4

It acts as a Crafting cape to allow access to the Crafting Guild without a brown apron or golden apron

It acts as a Runecraft cape to prevent essence pouches from degrading (but does not allow access to runic altars)

It acts as a Firemaking cape to work as a piece of warm clothing

It can be used to perform the Skill Cape emote.

The max cape and imbued Saradomin cape can be separated by using a knife on the cape. Mac will also buy back a max cape, along with its variants, for 1,900,800 coins each. He will return the secondary item any max cape variant was combined with upon doing so.

24255: A Venom gland is an item used in The Fremennik Exiles quest. It can be found in some crates south of the house that is south of the sandpit in Rellekka. It is given to Freygerd along with the fang and an unsealed letter as evidence of basilisks plotting to attack Rellekka.
24256: The unsealed letter is an item used in The Fremennik Exiles quest. It is obtained by killing a Basilisk Youngling that comes out after the player searches the sandpit in Rellekka. It is given to Freygerd along with the fang and venom gland as evidence of basilisks plotting to attack Rellekka, and if the player has not read it, it is returned by Brundt the Chieftain.
24257: The unsealed letter is an item used in The Fremennik Exiles quest. It is obtained by killing a Basilisk Youngling that comes out after the player searches the sandpit in Rellekka. It is given to Freygerd along with the fang and venom gland as evidence of basilisks plotting to attack Rellekka, and if the player has not read it, it is returned by Brundt the Chieftain.
24258: The V sigil is an item used in The Fremennik Exiles quest. It is obtained by using three lunar bars on an anvil along with a hammer, granting 25 Smithing experience. It can be enchanted into the V sigil (e) by bringing it to Fossegrimmen south of Rellekka.
24259: The V sigil (e) is an item used in The Fremennik Exiles quest. It is obtained by bringing a V sigil to Fossegrimmen located south of Rellekka. It can be combined with lunar glass, a polishing rock and a fremennik shield to create V's shield.
24260: Molten glass (i) is an item used in The Fremennik Exiles quest. It is obtained by bringing molten glass to Baba Yaga on Lunar Isle. It can be turned into Lunar glass by using it on the Astral Altar along with 100 astral runes.
24262: The Polishing rock is an item used in The Fremennik Exiles quest. It can be obtained by dropping a pet rock into the large geyser north-west of the Mountain Camp, then fishing it out with a fishing rod while equipping ice gloves.
24265:
V's shield is a shield created during The Fremennik Exiles quest. It is a recreation of the shield owned by the legendary warrior V. It requires 40 Defence and 60 Slayer to wield.

It acts as a mirror shield when fighting basilisks, basilisk knights, and cockatrice. It has stronger defensive stats than the mirror shield, on par with an Adamant kiteshield but positive magic defence and without negative stats.

If lost, it can be reobtained from Brundt the Chieftain in Rellekka's longhall for 50,000. Multiple shields can be obtained via the drop trick.

24268:
The basilisk jaw is a unique drop from basilisk knights. It can be combined with the helm of Neitiznot, after the completion of The Fremennik Exiles, to create an untradeable Neitiznot faceguard. Doing so requires asking Olaf the Bard for stories about basilisk jaws while having it in their inventory. Completion of The Fremennik Exiles is also required to equip the helmet.

If players are on a Slayer task for basilisks, the drop rate of the basilisk jaw is improved from 1/5,000 to 1/1,000.

Upon inspecting the jaw, a message appears in the chatbox stating "It's the jaw of a Basilisk Knight. Perhaps Olaf the Bard knows a good story about it." If a player attempts to use the jaw on the helm of Neitiznot before speaking to Olaf the Bard, a message appears in the chatbox stating "You're not quite sure how to do that. Perhaps Olaf the Bard can help. He's likely to know a good story about Basilisk Jaws."
24271:
The Neitiznot faceguard is an upgraded helm of Neitiznot that requires 70 Defence and completion of The Fremennik Exiles to wear. In addition to offering increased defensive bonuses, its strength bonus is doubled, giving it the second highest of any helmet, tied with Oathplate helm and behind the torva full helm.

It can be made by combining a helm of Neitiznot and a basilisk jaw after asking Olaf the Bard for stories about basilisk jaws while having it in their inventory.

The helmet is untradeable, but can be freely reverted at any time. If lost in PvP, it will revert to the normal helm of Neitiznot and basilisk jaw.
24277:
A mysterious emblem was an item that was purchasable from the Emblem Trader, which a player could upgrade by killing the player's assigned target on the official Bounty Hunter world whilst having a mysterious emblem in their inventory. However, their opponent must also have had a mysterious emblem of the same tier in order for it to be upgraded. If a player is holding multiple emblems, only the highest tier emblem will be upgraded.

Emblems were always lost upon death; players were willing to risk their emblem to either receive an emblem in another player's possession or to upgrade their own. For example, if a player was killed and had a tier 4 emblem in their inventory, the target's emblem will be destroyed upon death, and the victor's emblem would have been upgraded to tier 5.

Players were not able to drop Mysterious emblems. Unlike most items, mysterious emblems had a seven second timer before being destroyed, in order to prevent players from destroying them mid-combat to deny their killer the emblem as loot.

24288: The Dagon'hai hat is a piece of magic armour obtained as a rare loot from Larran's big chest. It is part of the Dagon'hai robes set, and requires level 70 Magic and 40 Defence to wear. It can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player-owned house.
24291: The Dagon'hai robe top is a piece of magic armour obtained as a rare loot from Larran's big chest. It is part of the Dagon'hai robes set, and requires level 70 Magic and 40 Defence to wear. It can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player-owned house.
24294: The Dagon'hai robe bottom is a piece of magic armour obtained as a rare loot from Larran's big chest. It is part of the Dagon'hai robes set, and requires level 70 Magic and 40 Defence to wear. It can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player-owned house.
24297:
The White bed sheets are an item used during the 2019 Halloween event. They are obtained from the bed in the house north of Bob's Axe shop. Using a knife on the bed sheets produces the 5 items in the spooky outfit.

Attempting to grab a second pair of sheets produces the message "You already have some sheets, try cutting some holes to make a costume!". After this, attempting to gather more sheets produces the message "You already have the full costume!"

Before getting to the appropriate part of the event and after completion, attempting to take the sheets from the bed causes the player to say in the chatbox "Why would I do that?"
24298:
Smoke powder is an item used during the 2019 Halloween event. It can be found in a sack of black powder directly south of the Lumbridge furnace. It is used inside the Lumbridge General Store with a tinderbox to create a Smoke Bomb on the ground. The smoke from the bomb distracts the shopkeepers so that you can steal the shiny glass from the table.

Attempting to pick up more than one provides the message "You already have some powder in your inventory." Attempting to ignite it outside the Lumbridge general store provides the message "You should plant that inside the Lumbridge general store!" Attempting to ignite it inside the Lumbridge general store without a tinderbox prompts a chatbox with the message "I need a tinderbox to light his, maybe my new friend has one."

Before getting to the appropriate part of the event and after completion, attempting to take the smoke powder from the Black powder sack causes the player to say in the chatbox "Why would I want that?"
24299:
Shiny glass is an item used during the 2019 Halloween event. It is found inside the Lumbridge General Store on a table. The shopkeeper will prevent it from being picked up unless the store has been filled with smoke from the smoke powder, and it can also not be telegrabbed. The shiny glass must be stolen and given to the goblins Snailneck and Grasslegs to complete the event.

Before getting to the appropriate part of the event and after completion, attempting to take the shiny glass from the table causes the player to say in the chatbox "Why would I steal that?"
24300:
The spooky hood is a cosmetic reward from the 2019 Halloween event. It is part of the spooky outfit, and can be obtained as a reward from the Halloween events that occur once per year. It can be used on the swampy sink outside the toolshed in the Lumbridge Swamp, or on the Ectofuntus outside Port Phasmatys to unlock the spookier hood.

It is meant to mimic the bedsheet obtained during the Ghosts Ahoy quest, which players have often requested that it be wearable outside Port Phasmatys but cannot due to restricted interaction checks in the game code.

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room, as part of the 2019: Spooky Costume set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

The rune pouch is an item that can store 16,000 of three types of runes (except runes found in the Nightmare Zone). Players can cast spells using the runes stored in the pouch, so a rune pouch saves inventory space. With a thread of Elidinis and level 75 crafting, the rune pouch can be upgraded (with a needle) to a divine rune pouch. Players cannot own more than one rune pouch.

If players die a PvP death while carrying a rune pouch in any level Wilderness or in a PvP world, they will lose the rune pouch, unless it has been locked via use of a trouver parchment. It should be noted that the Trouver parchment does not protect runes stored within a Rune pouch upon PvP death.

If players die a PvM death anywhere, including any level Wilderness, the rune pouch is always sent to a gravestone or item retrieval service, unless it has been locked via use of a trouver parchment. Locked rune pouches are kept in the inventory upon PvM death, instead.

Once belonging to Phosani, a former Saradominist Justiciar and one of the founders of Slepe, the Inquisitor's mace had remained sealed in the Sisterhood Sanctuary deep beneath Slepe until The Nightmare's arrival unearthed it.

The mace can be used to train all the combat stats (Attack, Strength, Defence) while on crush whereas most other melee weapons have singular strengths.

The Nightmare staff is a one-handed staff that can be received as a drop from The Nightmare. Requiring level 72 Magic and 50 Hitpoints to wield, it can autocast offensive standard spells as well as Ancient Magicks.

Once belonging to the shamans of Ashihama, its true name has since been lost to the world, and is now associated with The Nightmare. It gives a 15% bonus in magic damage.

Players can attach three different orbs to the Nightmare staff, giving it differing effects, increasing the magic requirement to 82, and making it untradeable:

The eldritch orb creates the eldritch Nightmare staff, granting it a prayer-restoring special attack

The volatile orb creates the volatile Nightmare staff, granting it a high-damaging special attack

The harmonised orb creates the harmonised Nightmare staff, removing its ability to autocast Ancient Magicks but increasing its casting speed to 4 ticks from 5

The upgraded staves can be reverted to their tradeable components at any time.
24423:
The harmonised Nightmare staff is a one-handed staff that is created by attaching a harmonised orb to the Nightmare staff. Requiring level 82 Magic and 50 Hitpoints to wield, it can autocast offensive standard spells, but cannot autocast any other spells (including Ancient Magicks and the Arceuus spellbook) unlike its other variants. Like the Nightmare staff it gives a 15% bonus in magic damage. The upgraded staff is untradeable, but it can be reverted to its tradeable components at any time. If lost on death in the Wilderness, the killer will receive the staff and the orb.

When casting offensive spells from the standard spellbook, the harmonised Nightmare staff reduces the cast time from 5 (3.0s) to 4 (2.4s) ticks, equal to most powered staves. The 4-tick spell speed only applies when autocasting. Manually casting spells with the staff equipped will result in a 5-tick attack speed. Unlike powered staves, the harmonised Nightmare staff can be used against other players in dangerous PvP scenarios, as it is not classified as a powered staff.

Due to the increased casting speed, the harmonised Nightmare staff allows standard combat spells to have damage output competitive with the powered staves; casting Fire Surge with the staff along with a charged tome of fire is particularly effective against monsters weak to magic, such as Zulrah, The Nightmare's pillars, and Kraken, albeit without the passive healing and venom provided by the Sanguinesti staff and trident of the swamp respectively.

In PvP, the increased attack speed is notable for enabling the stacking of damage from spells and melee weapon special attacks on the same tick, such as Fire Surge into Armadyl godsword special attack, something that slower attack speed staves cannot do.
24424: The volatile Nightmare staff is a one-handed staff that is created by attaching a volatile orb to the Nightmare staff granting it a high damaging special attack. Requiring level 82 Magic and 50 Hitpoints to equip, it can autocast either offensive standard spells or Ancient Magicks. Like the Nightmare staff it gives a 15% bonus in magic damage. The upgraded staff is untradeable, but it can be reverted to its tradeable components at any time. If lost on death in the Wilderness, the killer will receive the staff and the orb.
24425: The eldritch Nightmare staff is a one-handed staff that is created by attaching an eldritch orb to the Nightmare staff granting it a prayer restoring special attack. Requiring level 82 Magic and 50 Hitpoints to wield, it can autocast offensive standard spells as well as Ancient Magicks. Like the Nightmare staff it gives a 15% bonus in magic damage. The upgraded staff is untradeable, but it can be reverted to its tradeable components at any time. If lost on death in the Wilderness, the killer will receive the staff and the orb.

24483:
The Phoenix is a pet that can be received from looting the Reward Cart, from which rewards are obtained by subduing the Wintertodt with at least 500 points.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.

Though the Wintertodt is classified as a boss rather than a skilling activity, the phoenix is fifteen times more common at 200 million Firemaking experience.

The Little Nightmare is a pet that can be obtained by defeating The Nightmare or Phosani's Nightmare. It is a much smaller version of her. The pet has a 1/800 drop rate in the original encounter, decreasing for every additional player in the room when the fight started: 1/1600 in a duo, 1/2400 in a trio, 1/3200 in a 4-man and 1/4000 in a 5-or-higher-man encounter. At Phosani's Nightmare, the pet has a flat 1/1400 drop rate.

The Little Nightmare is able to metamorphose into a little parasite. For Little Nightmare to be able to do so, players must use the Parasitic Egg on her, a drop acquired from Phosani's Nightmare.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.
