25367:
The infernal harpoon is a special non-tradeable harpoon created by using a smouldering stone on a dragon harpoon, requiring 75 Fishing[not boostable] and 85 Cooking[not boostable] to craft. This cannot be boosted. It is non-reversible and grants 350 Cooking and 200 Fishing experience. It can be stored in a tackle box.

Fish caught with a charged harpoon have a 1/3 (33%) chance to be cooked and destroyed instantly, granting half of the Cooking experience that would normally be gained from cooking the fish otherwise. Harpoonfish caught within the Tempoross minigame are not destroyed when cooked, making it a popular upgrade that saves 3 ticks (1.8 seconds) per fish. The harpoon will not consume big fish, such as the big shark. Fishing training methods using tick manipulation also can use the infernal harpoon to avoid dropping 1/3rd of the fish caught.

Since it cannot revert to its components and cannot be traded, if lost on death in level 20 or higher Wilderness it is converted to 11,000.

If all 5,000 charges are used on raw sharks, 525,000 Cooking experience will be gained which would save about 2 hours of cooking and destroy 3,685,000 in fish.

When using the infernal harpoon at leaping harpoonfish spots at Tempoross, or when using it with Rada's blessing and/or spirit flakes, the extra fish has a separate independent chance to be cooked.
25369:
The infernal pickaxe is a special pickaxe that requires level 61 Mining to use and 60 Attack to wield. It is created by using a smouldering stone on a dragon pickaxe, requiring level 85 Smithing[not boostable] to create, and starts with 5,000 charges. Doing so grants 200 Mining experience and 350 Smithing experience.

Mining rocks with it equipped or in the inventory will give a 1/3 (33%) chance for the ore to automatically combust. This will destroy the ore, using one charge and granting roughly half of the Smithing experience based on the amount that would usually be gained when creating a bar from the ore. For rocks that cannot be smelted, Smithing experience will be gained based on the level required to mine the rock. At some mining spots, such as Motherlode Mine, Volcanic Mine, amethyst, gem rocks, crashed stars, dense runestone, or punishment rocks, the infernal pickaxe does not consume ores and acts as a regular dragon pickaxe.

Players can only use the standard, tradeable dragon pickaxe to create the infernal pickaxe; attempting to use other variants will result the chatbox stating "The cosmetically upgraded pickaxe is too beautiful to convert into an infernal pickaxe."

The infernal pickaxe possesses the same special attack as the dragon pickaxe, which will boost a player's Mining level by 3. This consumes 100% special attack energy.

When mining in the Mining Guild, unidentified minerals can still be obtained when this effect consumes an ore.

The effect can trigger alongside the bonus resource effect of the celestial ring, consuming one or possibly both ores and granting experience for each.

The infernal pickaxe cannot be reverted back to a tradeable dragon pickaxe or smouldering stone.
25373:
The dragon harpoon (or) is a dragon harpoon with a Trailblazer tool ornament kit added onto it. The kit gives no additional bonuses, and is only used to add aesthetics to the harpoon. It can be stored in a tackle box.

Players can select the "Change-Style" option to alternate between the Trailblazer Reloaded variant and the original Trailblazer variant.

While the harpoon is untradeable in its ornamented state, it can be reverted anytime, returning the dragon harpoon and kit.

The dragon axe (or) is a dragon axe with a Trailblazer tool ornament kit added onto it. The kit gives no additional bonuses, and is only used to add aesthetics to the axe. Players can additionally select the "Change-Style" option to alternate between the Trailblazer Reloaded variant and the original Trailblazer variant.

While the axe is untradeable in its ornamented state, it can be reverted anytime, returning the dragon axe and kit.

This version of the dragon axe can be used for the master clue step in the Enchanted Valley and stored in its respective STASH unit.
25389:
A swampbark body is a piece of swampbark armour worn in the body slot, requiring level 50 Magic and 50 Defence to equip. The body can be made with level 48 Runecraft by bringing a splitbark body and 500 nature runes to the Nature Altar. Doing so requires players to have first learnt the secret to infuse the armour via reading the runescroll of swampbark.

In addition to their stats, the helm, body, and legs increases the duration of bind spells by 2 ticks (1.2 seconds), with the full set increasing the duration by 6 ticks (3.6 seconds). For comparison, Ice Barrage binds players for 32 ticks (19.2 secs).

Bind: 8 ticks (4.8 secs) to 14 ticks (8.4 secs)

Snare: 16 ticks (9.6 secs) to 22 ticks (13.2 secs)

Entangle: 24 ticks (14.4 secs) to 30 ticks (18.0 secs)

It can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player-owned house.
25392:

Doing so requires players to have first learnt the secret to infuse the armour via reading the runescroll of swampbark.

They do not contribute to the swampbark armour set's effect of increasing the duration of bind spells.

25419:
Urium remains are an item found and used in the Shades of Mort'ton minigame. To obtain these remains, the player must kill urium shades, located behind a solid gold door in the Shade Catacombs.

To burn the urium remains, first place redwood pyre logs or rosewood pyre logs on a funeral pyre, followed by the urium remains, then light the pyre with a tinderbox. This will grant the player 500 Firemaking experience for redwood pyre logs and 590 Firemaking experience for rosewood pyre logs (750 and 885 respectively with elite Morytania Diary complete) and 120.5 Prayer (180.7 with hard Morytania Diary complete) experience. Neither the pyromancer outfit nor zealot's robes give any of their effects when burning shade remains.

Urium remains will always reward the player with either a gold shade key or some coins. Gold keys give unrestricted access to all areas of the Shade Catacombs and open the gold chests in the urium area of the catacombs, which give the best rewards out of all the chests.

Coins and keys dropped by cremating these remains will not despawn for five minutes, and cannot be taken by other players during this time. When dropped by the player, they will despawn and become visible to others at the normal rate.
25422:
Bleached bones are an untradeable drop from Undead Zealots. They can be offered at the Altar of the Damned to recharge a player's prayer points to full like a regular altar.

Players can bury bleached bones for 4.5 Prayer experience. Unlike long and curved bones, there is no warning that prevents the players from accidentally burying the bones. Alternatively, players can turn bleached bones into bonemeal at the Ectofuntus. Bleached bones cannot be used on the Exposed altar in The Teomat. Bleached bones can be given to a dog and they will happily gnaw on them.
25424:
Gold key red is a key and reward from the Shades of Mort'ton minigame. To obtain it, the player must burn Fiyr or Urium remains on a pyre. The key may be used to enter the Shade Catacombs and then open the correctly coloured chest. It will open a gold-framed chest with a red lock. This type of key can be used to open any door within the tombs, giving the player unrestricted access to all areas.

Unlike most items, this key will not despawn and cannot be taken by other players for 5 minutes when initially dropped from shade remains, similar to other keys from the Shades of Mort'ton minigame. When dropped by the player, they will despawn and become visible to others at the normal rate.

25434:
The zealot's robe top is a piece of the Zealot's robes set that can be obtained from looting gold chests within the Shade Catacombs.

The robe top grants a 1.25% chance to prevent various remains from being consumed whilst training Prayer; wearing the full set will increase this chance to 5%, and stacks with the bone-saving effect of the altar in the Chaos Temple. However, this does not apply at the Forthos Dungeon's Sacred Bone Burner, nor when casting Sinister Offering.

This item can be stored in the magic wardrobe of a costume room, as part of the Zealot's robes set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

The robe top grants one less prayer bonus than the easy-to-obtain Proselyte hauberk, but may be preferable as it does not have any negative attack bonuses.

Bronze locks are a potential reward from bronze chests in the Shades of Mort'ton minigame. They are used to create a bronze coffin by taking the locks and coffin to Dampe; this process is reversible via the "Remove-lock" option on the coffin.

Players cannot attach the locks on their own; attempting to do so results in a message in the chatbox stating "You don't have the knowledge to attach the lock to the coffin, Dampe should be able to help."

25457:
The broken coffin can be obtained for free from Dampe in the town of Mort'ton. The coffin can be upgraded by giving locks found from the Shades of Mort'ton minigame to Dampe. Any lock can be added to the coffin at any point; lower tier locks do not need to be added to the coffin in order to upgrade it to the next level.

You can only have one coffin at a time, i.e. if you already have one - either broken or with a lock attached - Dampe will refuse to give you another one.
25461:
The steel coffin is an item that can store up to 8 shade remains of any different type. It is obtained by bringing steel locks and a broken coffin to Dampe by the entrance to the Shade Catacombs. Shade remains cannot be burnt directly from the coffin and must be removed prior to constructing the pyre.

The coffin has several right-click options available:

Fill - Stores all shade remains in the player's inventory into the coffin, providing there is space inside.

Configure - Gives three options for the player:

Check Shade Count - Informs the player of how many shade remains are inside the coffin.

Open/Close Coffin - Opens the coffin, which will have shade remains that the player picks up be automatically placed inside the coffin, providing there is space for it. Closing the coffin will instead have shade remains placed into the inventory when picked up.

Remove lock - Prompts the player if they really want to remove the lock, and warns that any shade remains stored will be lost.

Empty - Empties remains from the coffin into the player's inventory, with highest-tier remains being withdrawn first.

25474:
The tree wizards' journal is a journal obtained from chests within the Shade Catacombs. Higher tier chests give a higher chance of obtaining the journal, as well as wearing a ring of wealth. Opening the journal for the first time gives players a runescroll of swampbark, which can be read to unlock the ability to create swampbark armour.

When the journal is first opened, a message in the chatbox will state "As you open the ancient notes, a rough scroll falls out." After having read the book once, the player will from now on receive the accompanying scroll as a reward from the chest whenever otherwise a book would have been obtained.

Written by a Zarosian warlock named Xazyd Wier, who lived during the early years of the Third Age, the journal describes their experiences with a great hollow tree after the fall of Kharyrll.

The journal can be retrieved from the bookcase in a player-owned house.
25476:
The bloody notes is a diary obtained from chests within the Shade Catacombs. Higher tier chests give a higher chance of obtaining the journal, as well as wearing a ring of wealth. Opening the notes for the first time gives players a runescroll of bloodbark, which can be read to unlock the ability to create bloodbark armour.

When the notes are first opened, a message in the chatbox will state "As you open the ancient notes, a rough scroll falls out." After having read the book once, the player will from now on receive the accompanying scroll as a reward from the chest whenever otherwise a book would have been obtained.

Written by Otrava prior to her conversion to Zamorak during the early years of the Third Age, the journal describes her experiences with a great hollow tree near the ruins of Flamtaer whom she referred to as the Chatter Tree.

The notes can be retrieved from the bookcase in a player-owned house.
25481: The runescroll of bloodbark is a scroll obtained from chests within the Shade Catacombs. Higher tier chests give a higher chance of obtaining the scroll, as well as wearing a ring of wealth. Reading the scroll unlocks the ability to craft bloodbark armour from splitbark armour.
25494: The black d'hide vambraces (beta) are a variant of the black d'hide vambraces that is available in an unrestricted world during the Equipment Rebalancing Beta, as a means to test its defence bonus reductions as proposed in the Equipment Rebalancing Changes blog. Players can obtain one within the supplies table in the Clan Wars building in Ferox Enclave.

When the full set is worn, a 20% damage bonus (compared to the current 15% in the live game) and 30% accuracy bonus is applied when using the crystal bow.

25500:
The cursed banana is an item that can be obtained from participating in any Birthday event, and was first obtained from the 2021 Birthday event. Wielding the item makes the player crouch and walk and run like a monkey.

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room.
25515:
Dharok's platebody is melee armour worn in the body slot that is part of Dharok the Wretched's set of Barrows equipment. To wear Dharok's platebody, a player must have 70 Defence.

As it is part of Dharok's barrows set, if Dharok's platebody is worn along with all of the other pieces of equipment in Dharok's barrows set, the player gains a special effect. Attacks do more damage as the player's hitpoints decrease, up to 98.9% bonus damage with 1 hitpoint remaining with 99 max.

For more details on the mechanics and strategies for this equipment, see the set page.
25517: The volatile Nightmare staff is a minigame-exclusive variant of the normal volatile Nightmare staff. It can be obtained from opening chests with a bloody key, or looting the crates that spawn at random locations on the map. It is dropped on death to whoever killed you. Upon leaving the island, it is removed from the player and thus cannot be taken out of the minigame.
25518: The ancestral hat is obtained as a rare drop from the Chambers of Xeric. It is part of the ancestral robes set, and requires level 75 in Magic and 65 Defence to wear. It can be stored in the magic wardrobe of a player-owned house.
25519:
The TzRek-Jad (translated as Baby Fire Elemental) is a pet that can be obtained via defeating TzTok-Jad in the TzHaar Fight Cave. It is a much smaller version of TzTok-Jad. Players are twice as likely to receive the pet upon defeating TzTok-Jad if they are assigned to defeat it on a Slayer task. In addition, players may exchange their fire capes by speaking to TzHaar-Mej-Jal for a 1/200 chance of obtaining TzRek-Jad. Provided a player defeats TzTok-Jad while on a Slayer task for a 1/100 chance of the pet and hands in their cape, the overall chance of receiving the pet from either the boss or the cape is approximately 1/67.

Players who have completed all six of TzHaar-Ket-Rak's Challenges can right click "Metamorphosis" to change between the TzRek-Jad and JalRek-Jad, which is a smaller version of JalTok-Jad. Attempting to change the pet's appearance before completing the challenges will result in the chatbox stating "You must have completed TzHaar-Ket-Rak's Challenges to do that."

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.
25535:
Essence packs are an unobtainable item which contain 100 pure essence when opened. There are two variants of this item, the first being a generic item pack intended to be purchased with coins, and the second intended to be purchased with stardust via Dusuri's Star Shop.

Essence packs were offered as a purchasable item from Dusuri's Star Shop in the Shooting Stars poll, though it only received 73.4% support, 1.6% short of the votes required to pass. As the developer creating Shooting Stars was unaware of the first version's existence, a second version of the item was created and subsequently removed from the shop after the item failed to pass the poll, which is why two variants of the item exist.
25537:
A bag full of gems is a bag that contains an assortment of 40 noted uncut gems. These bags are obtainable from Prospector Percy's Nugget Shop for 40 golden nuggets, from Belona's Mining Guild Mineral Exchange for 20 unidentified minerals, or from Dusuri's Star Shop for 300 stardust.

The chances of an individual gem being an uncut onyx is 1/100,000,000, making the chance per bag approximately 1/2,500,000. In terms of probability, this makes it one of the rarest drops in the game.

Obtaining the uncut onyx from a bag full of gems does produce an entry in the Collection Log.

The bags are exclusive to the stores they are bought from and therefore cannot be sold to another store in exchange for a different currency.
25549:
The golden prospector helmet is a cosmetic variant of the prospector helmet obtained by using a star fragment on it, which costs 3,000 stardust from Dusuri's Star Shop.

Like its original variant, the helmet grants 0.4% bonus Mining experience and is increased to 2.5% when wearing the full prospector kit. It can also be used as a substitute for the hard Falador diary task.

Unlike its original variant, it can not be sold back to Percy.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Prospector kit (golden) set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
25551:
The golden prospector jacket is a cosmetic variant of the prospector jacket obtained by using a star fragment on it, which costs 3,000 stardust from Dusuri's Star Shop.

Like its original variant, the jacket grants 0.8% bonus Mining experience and is increased to 2.5% when wearing the full prospector kit.

Unlike its original variant, it can not be sold back to Percy.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Prospector kit (golden) set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
25555:
The golden prospector boots are a cosmetic variant of the prospector boots obtained by using a star fragment on them, which costs 3,000 stardust from Dusuri's Star Shop.

Like its original variant, the boots grant 0.2% bonus Mining experience and is increased to 2.5% when wearing the full prospector kit.

Unlike its original variant, it can not be sold back to Percy.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Prospector kit (golden) set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
25557:
Dark flippers are a pair of footwear made by talking to Patchy on Mos Le'Harmless while carrying a dark claw and flippers. It costs 500 coins to sew together and 600 to separate them, albeit doing so will not return the dark claw; Patchy will warn players of this before sewing them together.

Like regular flippers, they can be worn in the underwater area beneath Fossil Island to swim faster.

This item can be stored in the magic wardrobe of a costume room. It can also be stored in a tackle box.
25559:
A big harpoonfish is an abnormally large harpoonfish that can be received from the reward pool in the Ruins of Unkah. It can be traded for 25 soaked pages by talking to the retired sailor inside the fishing store in the Ruins of Unkah.

It can be stuffed at the taxidermist in Canifis by using the item on her and paying 3,500 coins, returning a stuffed big harpoonfish. When players take it to her, she will tell players "Goodness me! That thing's more of a weapon than a fish!" Once stuffed, it can be mounted at a teak or mahogany display within the skill hall in a player-owned house, granting 59 Construction and 239 Fishing experience.
25564:
Raw harpoonfish are fish that can be fished from fishing spots in Tempoross Cove. During the fight with Tempoross, they are used as ammunition for harpoonfish cannons. They can be cooked at the shrine, which allows them to drain Tempoross' energy more than raw ones. Catching a harpoonfish grants 5 points during the Tempoross fight.

Note: You can use Tempoross harpoonfish in order to perform the initial bare-handed fishing task from Otto Godblessed.
25565:
Harpoonfish are obtained by cooking raw harpoonfish. They are used as ammunition for the harpoonfish cannons during the fight against Tempoross. Cooked harpoonfish drain Tempoross' energy more than raw harpoonfish, as well as giving more points. They cannot be burnt.

According to the Spirit anglers research notes, "cooking the Harpoonfish, while doing nothing for the edibility, does harden the bill, making them even more effective when used as ammunition."
25566:
Crystallised harpoonfish are fish that can be fished from fishing spots in Tempoross Cove. While fishing with a crystal harpoon, there is a 1 in 3 chance that players will catch a crystallised harpoonfish instead of a raw one.

During the fight with Tempoross, they are used as ammunition for harpoonfish cannons. Crystallised harpoonfish drains Tempoross' energy as much as raw ones, and cannot be cooked. While this means players will get fewer points over the course of the fight, players will instead receive 20% more Fishing experience from using them as ammunition.
25567:
The Desert Trout - Ship's Log is a book found by searching the book table in the small ruined building in the centre of the Ruins of Unkah.

Written by Taiman, the log contains daily entries of the ship's activities. After the crew's encounter with Tempoross, most of the pages have been soaked and are too smudged to be read by the player.
25574:
The tome of water is a book held in place of a shield that is a possible reward from Tempoross. The tome of water requires level 50 in Magic to wield.

The tome is only tradeable when empty. When it is empty its only function is its magic attack and magic defence equipment bonuses.

Empty tomes can be traded in for 25 soaked pages per tome (value of 75,900) by speaking to the retired sailor. Non-ironmen players are recommended to sell excess tomes on the Grand Exchange instead, as they are far more valuable when sold to other players.
25576:

25582:
The fish barrel is an item that can be obtained from the reward pool in the Ruins of Unkah after defeating Tempoross, or purchased from Flakes 'n' Flotsam for 6,000 spirit flakes. The barrel is able to store a combined total of 28 raw fish of any type except for harpoonfish (from Tempoross), stackable fish, trophy fish, and fish caught in the Chambers of Xeric, Ruins of Camdozaal, or Neypotzli. Players can right-click to open the barrel, which will have raw fish that the player acquires be automatically placed inside the barrel, providing there is space for it. Players can check the contents of the barrel by selecting the "Check" right-click option, which tells the amount and type of raw fish the player has inside. Note that the "Destroy" right-click option will destroy the barrel itself, not the content inside.

When the barrel is full, players can only empty it at a bank or a bank deposit box, similar to looting bags; for Ultimate Ironmen, fish can be withdrawn by using the barrel on an appropriate bank stand. When this occurs, players will get a message in the chatbox stating: "The barrel is full. It may be emptied at a bank."

Upon death to an NPC, the barrel will drop to the ground with all of its contents still stored. It is also always kept on death if killed by another player in the Wilderness. This makes the fish barrel especially useful if fishing raw dark crabs from the Resource Area, as any fish stored in the barrel will be kept on death and denied to potential player killers, since the barrel is protected above dark crabs and dark fishing bait.

Players can combine the barrel with a fish sack to create the fish sack barrel, which is an equipable version of the fish barrel. There is no confirmation message when this occurs, but it can be split apart by selecting the "Dismantle" option after right-clicking "Configure".

Players may have more than one barrel at the same time, despite the reward pool having a duplicate prevention, by purchasing them from Flakes 'n' Flotsam. However, the items will share their inventory.

25590:
A casket is an item occasionally dropped by monsters that are near oceans or bodies of water. It can also be obtained via big net fishing, at a rate of about 1/128 at lower levels and 1/85.3 at higher levels. The fishing spot in Civitas illa Fortis has around a 1 in 5 chance of rewarding a casket, making this one of the most reliable places to obtain them. It can be opened to receive a small amount of treasure. Wearing a skills necklace with at least one charge while big net fishing will slightly increase the chance of finding a casket.

For ironmen, these can be a good early source of a Cosmic talisman.
25598:
The Spirit angler boots are an upgraded version of the angler boots. They can be purchased from Gita Prymes by exchanging a pair of angler boots along with 1,200 spirit flakes. The boots grant 0.2% bonus Fishing experience. Tempoross has a skill requirement of 35 Fishing; therefore, the boots require level 35 Fishing to wear.

Wearing the complete Spirit angler's outfit acts as a rope for tethering to totem poles and masts while battling Tempoross, and grants a total of 2.5% bonus fishing experience.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the spirit angler's outfit set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored. It can also be stored in a tackle box.
25602:
Tiny Tempor is a pet obtained from the reward pool in the Ruins of Unkah. It is a much smaller version of the Tempoross.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.
25604:
Gregg's eastdoor is an item that can be obtained from participating in any Easter event, and was first obtained from the 2021 Easter event. It is a two-handed fun weapon, with a similar equipped stance to the Dinh's bulwark. However, it does not share its attack styles with the Bulwark, instead having regular blunt attack styles.

Gregg's eastdoor has the lowest attack speed out of any fun weapon, but is outclassed by the cursed goblin hammer in terms of dealing the least damage.

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room.
25608:
Gregg's iou is an item used in the 2021 Easter event. It must be given to Aggie to pay for the thick dye used to paint the doors in Draynor Village.

The IOU cannot be deposited into a bank. If players try to bank it, the chatbox will state "A magical force prevents you from banking this item!". On death, the IOU is always deleted from the player's inventory.
25609:
The Pastel flowers are an item used in the 2021 Easter event. It must be given to Aggie to create the thick dye used to paint the doors in Draynor Village.

The flowers cannot be deposited into a bank. If players try to bank it, the chatbox will state "A magical force prevents you from banking this item!". On death, the flowers are always deleted from the player's inventory.
25610:
The thick dye is an item used in the 2021 Easter event. It can be obtained from Aggie, in exchange for some pastel flowers and Gregg's iou. It is used to paint the doors in Draynor Village.

The dye cannot be deposited into a bank. If players try to bank it, the chatbox will state "A magical force prevents you from banking this item!". On death, the thick dye is always deleted from the player's inventory.
25613:
Baby Mole is a miniature version of the giant mole and is dropped by the aforementioned boss at a rate of 1/3,000. Players can change the skin of their baby mole pet to a baby mole-rat skin, which looks similar to the baby mole NPCs, by using a mole claw on their pet. Using a mole skin on the pet will turn it back into a regular baby mole.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita for no cost.
25615:
A heat-proof vessel is a water container given to the player by Petrified Pete upon entering the Volcanic Mine. It can be equipped in the weapon slot. It has 36 uses per game, and can be used to throw water onto the lava, creating platforms which players can walk on. These platforms will melt after 90 seconds, giving players limited time to stand on them. If players remain on the hardened lava when it melts, they will fall into the lava, taking massive damage.

The water can only be thrown while the player is facing north, east, south, and west. Additionally, the water canteen can be right-clicked to open a dialogue box to throw water in a specified direction, or right-clicked while it is equipped to select the direction the player wants to throw it at.

Players can pay Petrified Pete 10,000 Volcanic Mine points to have him upgrade their vessel to hold more water, increasing the number of uses per game from 36 to 72. The Collection Log and Petrified Pete's Ore Shop interfaces refer to this upgrade as "Large water container".
25625:
The Barronite mace is a crush melee weapon that can be obtained within the Ruins of Camdozaal, requiring 40 Attack to wield. Its bonuses are comparable to that of a rune mace, but it provides higher melee strength and crush accuracy bonuses at the cost of a lower prayer bonus. It also has a 15% damage and accuracy bonus against golems, including those within the dungeon. Unlike regular metal maces, the barronite mace offers blunt rather than spiked attack styles, which means it can only be used for crush attacks, despite having a notable stab accuracy bonus. For free-to-play and low level players, this mace is a good alternative to the rune scimitar when fighting golems thanks to its golembane effect and it is the second-best free-to-play weapon in most other situations, outperforming the rune sword in both strength and attack bonus. For those with membership, the golembane effect stacks with the black mask or slayer helmet effect while on a Gargoyle slayer task.

When lost during PvM, the mace goes to the gravestone and does not require repair. In a PvP death, the mace will be broken and will require 10,500 coins fee to be repaired, while the killer will receive 10,500 coins as additional loot.

The mace can be crafted by handing 3 distinct pieces of the mace to Ramarno along with 1,500 barronite shards. Note that the shards already stored in the Sacred Forge shop will not count towards these 1,500; one would have to Empty the forge to get the shards back. Activating the luck buff from Ramarno for 3,000 Barronite shards will give a 5% boost of getting the following 3 parts. The required pieces include:

Barronite guard, obtained from killing golems within the dungeon.

Barronite head, obtained from crushing barronite deposits.

Barronite handle, obtained from fishing within the dungeon.

The mace can be exchanged for 500 Barronite shards by showing it to Ramarno.
25631:
A steak sandwich is a food item that heals 6 Hitpoints and can be made during Below Ice Mountain. It is made by using bread on cooked meat with a knife in the inventory after learning the recipe from the cook in the Blue Moon Inn near Varrock's south gate.

It is given to Marley to convince him to meet up with Willow. If the player has not yet given a sandwich to Marley, there will be a confirmation dialogue if the player tries to eat it.

More sandwiches can be made during and after the quest. If the player uses the knife on the bread but has not yet learned the recipe and has started the Freeing Pirate Pete subquest of Recipe For Disaster, they will turn the bread into breadcrumbs instead of making a sandwich.
25633:
The Imcando hammer is a wieldable variant of a hammer mostly used for Smithing, Crafting, or Construction. It can be obtained through smashing barronite deposits on the barronite crusher in the Ruins of Camdozaal after completing the Below Ice Mountain quest.

When first obtained, the hammer will be in a broken state. The broken hammer can be fixed by using it on Ramarno, who will repair it for 1,250 barronite shards. Once repaired, it can be used as a hammer, both while equipped and unequipped, in any way that a normal hammer can be used.

The Imcando hammer is especially useful in a few situations:

When fighting Tempoross, it will not be destroyed by flames nor be washed away by waves.

When doing Mahogany Homes or Wintertodt, it saves an inventory slot if wielded.

In Barbarian Assault, it can be used by the Defender to repair the Penance Runner traps. In this case, the Defender will save a small amount of time that is normally spent collecting a hammer from the battlefield.

When doing Motherlode Mine, you can repair the wheels without picking up a hammer first. You are also able to repair the struts without a small tick-delay (2 - 3 ticks).

When crafting golems. While using a gem pouch and large fur pouch, a player can make 5 golems instead of 4 per inventory, increasing XP per hour and requiring less inputs.

The hammer can be swapped via the "Swap" option, converting it to its off-hand variant so that it can be equipped in the shield slot. This allows it to be equipped alongside Amy's saw, a mist battlestaff, an equippable harpoon, or a pickaxe when doing the aforementioned activities.

This item can be stored in the magic wardrobe of a costume room. Both the normal and off-hand variant can be stored in the magic wardrobe at the same time. Unwanted broken hammers can be exchanged at Ramarno for 350 barronite shards, while the fixed hammer can be exchanged for 500 barronite shards.

It can also be used in a free-to-play world, despite being a members item. Though it can only be equipped in a members' world, if it is already equipped or in the player's inventory upon logging into a free-to-play world, the hammer retains its usual functionality, regardless of the player's membership status.
25635:
The barronite head is one of the three parts of the barronite mace, obtained from smashing barronite deposits on the Barronite Crusher in the Ruins of Camdozaal's next to Ramarno. When obtained, the message There's a Barronite Head inside! will be displayed.

Alongside 1,500 barronite shards, a barronite guard, and barronite handle, it can be restored to a barronite mace by Ramarno. Alternatively, the head can be exchanged for 100 barronite shards by showing it to Ramarno, or it can be turned into coins via alchemy spells if extra shards are not needed.

Activating the Charm of Luck buff from Ramarno for 3,000 barronite shards will give a 5% boost of getting this item.
25637:
The barronite handle is one of the three parts of the barronite mace, found while fishing at a fishing spot in the Ruins of Camdozaal. When obtained, the message You fished out a Barronite Handle! will be displayed. Note that the handle cannot be obtained from the frogspawn fishing spots in Camdozaal.

Alongside 1,500 barronite shards, a barronite head, and barronite guard, it can be restored to a barronite mace by Ramarno. Alternatively, the handle can be exchanged for 100 barronite shards by showing it to Ramarno, or it can be turned into coins via alchemy spells if extra shards are not needed.

The fastest way to obtain a barronite handle is small net fishing. Offering fish to the altar does not provide any rolls on the drop table, so if only seeking the handle, it is more efficient to just drop the fish and continue fishing.

Activating the Charm of Luck buff from Ramarno for 3,000 barronite shards will give a 5% boost of getting this item.
25639:
The barronite guard is one of the three parts of the barronite mace, obtained as a drop from golems in the Ruins of Camdozaal.

Alongside 1,500 barronite shards, a barronite head, and barronite handle, it can be restored to a barronite mace by Ramarno. Alternatively, the guard can be exchanged for 100 barronite shards by showing it to Ramarno, or it can be turned into coins via alchemy spells if extra shards are not needed.

Activating the Charm of Luck from Ramarno for 3,000 barronite shards will give a 5% boost to the chance of obtaining this item.

25646:
Simple lockboxes are boxes found within the Camdozaal Vault, typically found closer towards the vault's exit. Players must exit the vault before the one minute timer runs out to keep their lockboxes; otherwise, they will lose all lockboxes they have acquired whilst inside. Lockboxes the player was carrying before entering the vault will not be lost.

Simple lockboxes have a 1/25 chance to roll the gear drop table, which contains weapons and armour ranging from iron to adamant. The gear sub-table can only be rolled once per lockbox, with any subsequent hits to it being rerolled until a "standard" item is awarded instead.

25652:
Raw guppies are a type of fish found only at fishing spots within the Ruins of Camdozaal. In order to catch this fish, players require level 7 in Fishing and a small fishing net. Each catch grants 8 Fishing experience.

Unlike other fish, guppies are not eaten and are instead prepared at the preparation table for ritual offerings at the mysterious altar, requiring level 7 Cooking and granting 12 experience when successful. Players may ruin the guppy during preparation, resulting in a ruined guppy; the chance of failure while preparing these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels.

Guppies stop being ruined at 42 Cooking. However, players can reduce this to 36 Cooking if they purchase the Preparation buff from Ramarno's Shard Exchange for 2500 Barronite shards.

Raw guppies cannot be fed to a kitten and will not be stolen by the naughty gull.
25654:
A guppy is a type of inedible fish used as an offering at the mysterious altar in the Ruins of Camdozaal, granting 4 Prayer experience.

It can be obtained by preparing a raw guppy on the preparation table whilst having a knife. This requires level 7 Cooking and grants 12 experience when successful. Players may ruin the guppy during preparation, resulting in a ruined guppy; the chance of failure while preparing these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels.

Guppies stop being ruined at 42 Cooking. However, players can reduce this to 36 Cooking if they purchase the Preparation buff from Ramarno's Shard Exchange for 2500 Barronite shards.
25658:
Raw cavefish are a type of fish found only fishing spots within the Ruins of Camdozaal. In order to catch this fish, players require level 20 in Fishing and a small fishing net. Each catch grants 16 Fishing experience.

Unlike other fish, cavefish are not eaten and are instead prepared at the preparation table for ritual offerings at the mysterious altar, requiring level 20 Cooking and granting 23 experience when successful. Players may ruin the cavefish during preparation, resulting in a ruined cavefish; the chance of failure while preparing these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels.

Cavefish stop ruining at 53 Cooking. However, players can stop ruining cavefish at 45 Cooking if they purchase the Preparation buff from Ramarno's Shard Exchange for 2500 Barronite shards.

Raw cavefish cannot be fed to a kitten and will not be stolen by the naughty gull.
25660:
Cavefish are a type of inedible fish that are offered at the mysterious altar in the Ruins of Camdozaal, granting 7 Prayer experience.

Cavefish can be obtained by preparing a raw cavefish on the preparation table whilst having a knife. Preparing cavefish requires level 20 Cooking and grants 23 Cooking experience when successful. Players may ruin the cavefish during preparation, resulting in a ruined cavefish; the chance of failure while preparing these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels.

Cavefish stop being ruined at 53 Cooking. However, players can reduce this to level 45 Cooking if they purchase the Preparation buff from Ramarno's Shard Exchange for 2500 Barronite shards.
25670:
Raw catfish is a type of fish found only from fishing spots within the Ruins of Camdozaal. In order to catch this fish, players require level 46 in Fishing and a big fishing net. Each catch grants 33 Fishing experience.

Unlike other fish, catfish are not eaten and are instead prepared at the preparation table for ritual offerings at the mysterious altar, requiring level 46 Cooking and granting 43 experience when successful. If the player is successful and offers the catfish at the mysterious altar, they get 16 Prayer experience. Players may ruin the catfish during preparation, resulting in a ruined catfish; the chance of failure while preparing these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels.

At 78 Cooking, players are no longer able to ruin catfish during preparation. However, players can stop ruining catfish at an earlier level if they purchase the Preparation buff from Ramarno's Shard Exchange for 2500 Barronite shards.

Raw catfish cannot be fed to a kitten and will not be stolen by the naughty gull.
25672:

Players may ruin the catfish during preparation, resulting in a ruined catfish; the chance of failure while preparing these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels.

At 78 Cooking, players are no longer able to ruin catfish during preparation. However, players can stop ruining catfish at an earlier level if they purchase the Preparation buff from Ramarno's Shard Exchange for 2500 Barronite shards.
25676:
Barronite shards are collected throughout the Ruins of Camdozaal, below the Ice Mountain. They are the fuel for the Sacred Forge and are thus currency for Ramarno's Shard Exchange, which has several different buffs that apply when performing actions inside the ruins.

Four to six shards are gained per mining action, which can also occasionally yield a barronite deposit that can be crushed on the anvil near Ramarno for more shards.

Barronite shards can also be stored in the Sacred Forge, either directly or by using the shards on Ramarno. While stored in the forge, the shards can be used as fuel to gain entrance to the Camdozaal Vault or spent in Ramarno's Shard Exchange. Upon entering the Camdozaal Vault, 750 Barronite shards are deducted from the Sacred Forge.

A barronite mace can be crafted by handing a barronite guard, a barronite head, a barronite handle, and 1,500 Barronite shards to Ramarno. Shards stored in the Sacred Forge will not count towards this.

Members can use a broken Imcando hammer on Ramarno to repair it at a cost of 1,250 Barronite shards. As with the mace, shards already stored in the Sacred Forge will not count towards this.

Buying all 5 permanent buffs from Ramarno's Shard Exchange, crafting one barronite mace, and repairing one Imcando hammer requires 15,750 barronite shards in total.
25684:
Barronite deposits are found whilst mining barronite rocks within the Ruins of Camdozaal. Each deposit mined yields 32 Mining experience. Mining barronite does not consume celestial ring charges, but the +4 invisible Mining boost still applies.

Using them on the Barronite Crusher anvil, near Ramarno, with a hammer yields 30 Smithing experience and various rewards, including barronite shards.
25686:
The ancient globe is a relic that may be received from breaking open barronite deposits. A relic from the Second Age, it belonged to the inhabitants of Lassar, who were destroyed by Saradominist armies after the events of the Betrayal of Zaros, which included the Imcando dwarves.

The globe can be handed to Curator Haig Halen at the Varrock Museum for 1 Kudos and 200 coins. Players will receive 100 coins for additional ancient globes. When given to the curator for the first time, he will comment "This Ancient globe seems to show new constellations. What a discovery!"
25688:
The ancient ledger is a relic that may be received from breaking open barronite deposits. A relic from the Second Age, it belonged to the inhabitants of Lassar, who were destroyed by Saradominist armies after the events of the Betrayal of Zaros, which included the Imcando dwarves.

The ledger can be handed to Curator Haig Halen at the Varrock Museum for 1 Kudos and 200 coins. Players will receive 100 coins for additional ancient ledgers. When given to the curator for the first time, he will comment "I wonder what secrets this Ancient ledger holds. It's a unique find!"
25692:
The ancient treatise is a relic that may be received from breaking open barronite deposits. A relic from the Second Age, it belonged to the inhabitants of Lassar, who were destroyed by Saradominist armies after the events of the Betrayal of Zaros, which included the Imcando dwarves.

The treatise can be handed to Curator Haig Halen at the Varrock Museum for 1 Kudos and 200 coins. Players will receive 100 coins for additional ancient treatises. When given to the curator for the first time, he will comment "I'm not even familiar with the glyphs in this Ancient treatise. It's the first time I've seen them."
25696:
Mind cores are the corrupted cores of Mind Golems, imbued with the power of the Mind Altar. They can be used in place of rune or pure essence, but only for crafting mind runes. Each core gives 55 Runecraft experience and 11 mind runes.

Like regular essence, the amount of mind runes crafted will increase with the player's Runecraft level; for example, each mind core will craft 55 mind runes at level 56 Runecraft.

Golem cores cannot be placed in essence pouches. If players attempt to store them in one, a chatbox message will appear, stating The golem core is too big to fit in an essence pouch.

The Charm of Luck buff purchasable from Ramarno's Shard Exchange does affect the drop chance of the core.
25700:
Chaos cores are the corrupted cores of Chaos Golems, imbued with the power of the Chaos Altar. They can be used in place of pure essence, but only for crafting chaos runes. They act as if the player was carrying eleven essence instead of one, meaning each core gives 85 Runecraft experience and 11 chaos runes or 2,380 Runecraft experience and 308 chaos runes for a complete inventory.

Like regular essence, the amount of chaos runes crafted will increase with the player's Runecraft level; each chaos core will craft 22 chaos runes at level 74 Runecraft.

Golem cores cannot be placed in essence pouches. If players attempt to store them in one, a chatbox message will appear, stating "The golem core is too big to fit in an essence pouch." Furthermore, cores cannot be taken through the altar portals at Guardians of the Rift.

The Charm of Luck buff purchasable from Ramarno's Shard Exchange does affect the drop chance of the core.

A chaos core is used in the quest Defender of Varrock on a Barronite deposit to create an Imbued barronite.
25702:
Ungael lab notes are a compilation of old notes obtained from the laboratory beneath Ungael. Players must have all six old notes from the laboratory in order to combine them.

Written by Zorgoth, a dragonkin, the notes contain comments on his experiments to enhance the strength and aggressiveness of dragons in order to turn the tide on the war on humanity during the Fourth Age. The notes on Ungael indicate that Zorgoth had begun switching to blue dragons for his experiments, resulting in the creation of his vorkath, a word for "pathetic failure" in the Dragonkin language. In addition, he speculates that the Stone of Jas or a similar artefact may have once been present on the island, as he could sense its residual energy.

If lost, it can be reclaimed from a bookcase within a player-owned house.
25704:
Lithkren vault notes are a compilation of old notes obtained from the Lithkren Vault. Players must have all seven old notes from the Lithkren Vault in order to combine them, four of which can only be obtained after completion of Dragon Slayer II.

Written by Zorgoth, a dragonkin, the notes were first written during the attack on Lithkren in the Dragonkin Conflicts, and more written after he became trapped inside the vault. The notes contain comments on his experiments to create his ultimate weapon, Galvek, alongside exploration of a side project that resulted in the creation of the adamant and rune dragons.

If lost, it can be reclaimed from a bookcase within a player-owned house.
25706:
The dusty note is an item found by searching the skeleton in the south-west part of the Tower of Magic prison during Tale of the Righteous. Although the item is optional, it provides instructions on how to solve the puzzle to open the gates that lead the player to the skeleton with the "investigate" option.

After investigating the skeleton, it will yield the message, "You notice some writing carved into the floor beside the skeleton: 'Lizards on the mountain. Do not trust the King. The altar is a lie.' " In a previous update, investigating the skeleton would instead give the player a dusty note with the message about the lizards being on the mountain and the king being untrustworthy instead of the current dusty note with the puzzle's instructions. The note can be kept after the quest, but it can no longer be reobtained as it serves no purpose beyond the quest.
25708:
Board game pieces are interface items used in the Burthorpe Games Room. The interfaces on which the games take place are actually inventories, with these items filling the slots on the board. Regular runes could not be used for this purpose since they are stackable, and therefore stack quantities would display next to each piece on the board.

The actual items cannot be obtained by players.
25710:
Stools are unobtainable items used while playing games in the Burthorpe Games Room, the Games Zone, or in pubs. The stools are technically wieldable items, used to display the sitting animation.

It has the appearance of a steel axe in the player's inventory, as only the equipped model is ever supposed to be seen ingame.

Bandages are a consumable item obtainable during the Theatre of Blood entry mode. They restore 20 hitpoints, 29 prayer points, and 20% run energy when consumed. They also cure poison, boost the player's combat stats, and provide the effect of a stamina potion.

Bandages act as a food item, and therefore delay the player's next attack when consumed during combat. They can be combo eaten with potions and/or cooked karambwan.

10 bandages can be claimed from the rewards chest after defeating the Pestilent Bloat and another 10 become available after defeating Sotetseg. The chest can only contain a maximum of 10 bandages, so uncollected bandages are deleted.

Stat boosts to Attack, Strength and Defence are one level lower than the corresponding super potion, and are calculated with: ⌊SkillLevel×15100⌋+4

Ranged boost is equal to a ranging potion, and is calculated with: ⌊SkillLevel×110⌋+4

Magic boost is a static +4, equal to a magic potion.
25731:
The holy Sanguinesti staff is a Sanguinesti staff with a holy ornament kit attached to it. The ornament kit gives no additional stat bonuses, but it will make the staff count as a Saradomin item in the God Wars Dungeon.

The holy Sanguinesti staff retains all the properties that the original variant has, such as its passive effect and its built-in spell, which still requires blood runes to charge.

While the staff is untradeable in its ornamented and charged state, it can be dismantled anytime, returning the ornament kit and staff. If a player loses the holy Sanguinesti staff in a PvP death, the holy ornament kit will be placed in their gravestone.

25748:
Lil' Zik is a pet that can be obtained from completing the Theatre of Blood. It is a much smaller version of Verzik Vitur's final form. Players have a chance of receiving the pet when looting the monumental chests in Verzik's treasure vault. The drop rate is dependent on the player's performance in the raid, unaffected by that of teammates, ranging from 1/650 to 1/6,500 in regular raids and ranging from 1/500 to 1/5,000 in Hard Mode raids. The maximum rate is reached with 10 individual points (which are invisible to the players; the maximum per player is 32, or 18 if not including the MVP bonuses for each room). The highest rate is reached by dying no more than twice per raid, with more deaths allowed if the player deals the most damage in some rooms, assuming participation in each room.

Lil' Zik is able to metamorphose into five other pets which are smaller versions of the other bosses encountered in the Theatre of Blood, which requires using Sanguine dust on it. The dust can be acquired from the Theatre's Hard Mode version and clearing it under a specific time.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.

Fiendish ashes are a 100% drop from imps and fiends. They give 10 Prayer experience when scattered, or 30 when offered via the Demonic Offering spell. It cannot be offered at the Chaos Temple or in player-owned house altars.

The Ash sanctifier will automatically purify these demonic ashes for 5 experience if the Hard Kourend & Kebos Diary has been completed and 10 experience if the Elite Kourend & Kebos Diary is completed. It is NOT recommended to use the Ash sanctifier on demonic creatures dropping these ashes as it is not cost effective.
25769:
Vile ashes are demonic ashes dropped by lesser demons, greater demons, hellhounds, bloodvelds, and mutated bloodvelds. The ashes give 25 Prayer experience when scattered normally. Members can get 75 experience when offered via the Demonic Offering spell. Ashes cannot be offered at the Ectofuntus, Chaos Temple, or at player-owned house altars.

The ash sanctifier will automatically purify these demonic ashes for 12.5 experience if the Hard Kourend & Kebos Diary has been completed and 25 experience if the Elite Kourend & Kebos Diary is completed.
25772:
Malicious ashes are a 100% drop from black demons, nechryael, and demonic gorillas. They give 65 Prayer experience when scattered, or 195 when offered via the Demonic Offering spell. It cannot be offered at the Chaos Temple or in player-owned house altars.

The ash sanctifier will automatically purify these demonic ashes for 32.5 experience if the Hard Kourend & Kebos Diary has been completed and 65 experience if the Elite Kourend & Kebos Diary is completed.
25781:
The ash sanctifier is a reward from completing the Hard Kourend & Kebos Diary, where players can then claim it from Tyss near the Dark Altar. To use it, it must be charged with death runes, gaining 10 charges per death rune at a cost of 19 coins per charge. The charge limit is 2,147,483,647. Players can configure the charges while the sanctifier is in their bank by right-clicking on Configure-Charges, as long as players have the required materials. Un-charging it will return the unused death runes.

When charged and carried in the inventory, the ash sanctifier will automatically purify demonic ashes that are dropped from demonic creatures upon death, granting the player half the Prayer experience they would have received from scattering the ashes themselves, or the full amount if the Elite Kourend & Kebos Diary is completed, consuming one charge in the process. This effect can be toggled with the right-click "Activity" option.

It is always kept on PvM Death. Should the player die in PvP and it is not one of their protected items, it will be sent to a gravestone. In all cases, the ash sanctifier will retain all of its charges.

The ash sanctifier will not affect bones. For this, use the Bonecrusher or Bonecrusher necklace. For spectral creatures that do not drop ashes or bones, use the Ectoplasmator.

25794:
Bones are the remains of most creatures with an animalistic or humanoid appearance.

Bones give 4.5 Prayer experience when buried. This can be increased by offering the bones in different ways:

13.5 XP when casting Sinister Offering.

13.5 XP when using the sacred bone burner after the appropriate faith level has been achieved.

15.7 XP when offered at a gilded altar with two burners lit or at the Chaos Temple. The Temple additionally has a 50% chance to not deplete the bones; effectively doubling the XP to 31.4 per bone.

18 XP when offered at the Ectofuntus in the form of bonemeal.

20 XP when blessed, broken down into blessed bone shards and offered at the libation bowl with jug of blessed wine, or 24 XP when offered with a jug of blessed sunfire wine. Virilis outside the altar will exchange noted bones for 10 coins each.

Players may also use the Bones to Bananas or Bones to Peaches spells to turn normal bones to edible bananas or peaches.

25 regular bones are used in the Demon Slayer quest.

25798:

When inspected, the chatbox message states It's a book of demonic incantations. Most of it is dedicated to summoning, but that's not really your thing.
25799:
The bloody knife is an item obtained during A Kingdom Divided, in which players help search Sophia Hughes' house in Kingstown.

When inspected, the chatbox message states It's a sharp knife covered in dried blood.
25800:

25801:

25802:
Rose's diary is an item obtained during A Kingdom Divided, in which players take it from a display case in the Library Historical Archive after pickpocketing a bluish key from Istoria.

25804: The cold key is an item obtained during A Kingdom Divided, in which players melt and smash some ice chunks in the Settlement Ruins to recover it. It is used to open the panel containing Rose's note.
25805:
Rose's note is an item that is obtained during the search for Rose during A Kingdom Divided. There are four in total, each containing a riddle that eventually leads to her whereabouts; the first is hidden in Rose's diary, and the next three are found behind panels in the Forthos Ruin, Settlement Ruins, and The Legless Faun that must be opened by solving puzzles in the vicinity.

The final note leads to the unlikely home, where she's kept in the basement in a comatose state.

25809: A lizardman egg is an item obtained during A Kingdom Divided, in which players take it from the hatching area in the Kebos Swamp. It belongs to Kaht B'alam, and is exchanged for a damp key.
25811:
The broken redirector is the device that players destroy during the quest The Ascent of Arceuus, in which it was responsible for redirecting energy from the Dark Altar, causing loss in power from the Dark Altar among the Citizens of Arceuus and the death of Thana.

It is obtained from Lord Trobin Arceuus during A Kingdom Divided, and is given to the Tasakaal in order to have them inspect it, where players discover the device was created by Xamphur, who had Councillor Andrews place the device nearby.

The broken redirector can be reclaimed from Lord Trobin Arceuus at Xeric's Lookout during the quest A Kingdom Divided.
25812:
The sulphur potion is an item obtained during A Kingdom Divided, in which players make it by adding volcanic sulphur to a defence potion with three or more doses. It is enchanted into a shielding potion by the Tasakaal.

If players attempt to drink it, they will exclaim "I really don't think I should drink this."
25813:
The shielding potion is an item obtained during A Kingdom Divided, in which players have a sulphur potion enchanted into one by the Tasakaal. It is used on the Doors of Dinh to reinforce them.

If players attempt to drink it, they will exclaim "I really don't think I should drink this."
25814: The declaration is an item obtained from Jorra during A Kingdom Divided, in which players use it to convince Lady Vulcana Lovakengj that her old friend, Councillor Unkar, conspired to betray her and take her place as ruler of Lovakengj.
25815: The dark nullifier is an item obtained from Mori during A Kingdom Divided. It is used to disrupt communications between the Voice of Yama and Yama himself, though the player's plan is foiled by a Disciple of Yama, and had their memories altered to believe that they placed the nullifier in the Chasm of Fire.
25818:
The Book of the Dead is an equipable book obtained as a reward from completing A Kingdom Divided. Having it equipped or in the player's inventory is required when casting resurrection spells.

The book is an improved version of Kharedst's memoirs, and offers the same teleports. The book offers as an additional 150 charges over the memoirs, resulting in a maximum of 250 charges if all five of the pages from the original Kourend quests have been added.

If lost, the book can be reclaimed from Commander Fullore on the ground floor of the Kourend Castle. Additional copies can be purchased from Perdu for 9,500 coins each.
25820:
Antique lamps are rewards from quests, achievement diaries and the Varrock Museum miniquest. Like regular lamps, these lamps grant a player experience in a chosen skill, and the skill chosen must usually be over a certain level which is unboostable.

Lamps that are not included in the three items kept on death will be kept inside your death's coffer, if not deleted.
25822: A protest banner is an item used during the quest A Kingdom Divided. Players can get this item by taking one from the pile outside Sophia Hughes' house in Kingstown without needing to start the quest.
25826:
The Lizardkicker is a type of ale that temporarily boosts Ranged by 4 while draining Strength and Magic by 2 + 4%. Unlike other ales, it cannot be created through brewing.

It can be purchased at The Cloak and Stagger in the city of Shayzien.

Upon drinking the ale, a message in the chatbox will state You drink the Lizardkicker. It tastes like swampwater, but you feel like your eyesight has improved slightly.
25831:
The Shayzia military orders is a letter obtained from searching the Broken altar in the Shayzia Ruin, just north-east of Shayzien.

The letter, addressed to Captain Tebell in Shayzia, is written by General Lern during the early days of the War of the Five Houses, detailing the removal of King Agata IV from the throne and the movements of the other four Houses of Kourend.
25833: Raw boar meat can be obtained by killing boars, found in the woods west of Kourend Castle and south of The Node. It can be cooked at level 1 Cooking, granting 30 Cooking experience if successful. After successfully cooking it, it will simply be cooked meat, while burning it will result in burnt meat (burning can be achieved at any level by cooking it twice). The raw boar meat can also be made into sinew at level 1 Cooking by using it on a range.
25836:
The Little Nightmare is a pet that can be obtained by defeating The Nightmare or Phosani's Nightmare. It is a much smaller version of her. The pet has a 1/800 drop rate in the original encounter, decreasing for every additional player in the room when the fight started: 1/1600 in a duo, 1/2400 in a trio, 1/3200 in a 4-man and 1/4000 in a 5-or-higher-man encounter. At Phosani's Nightmare, the pet has a flat 1/1400 drop rate.

The Little Nightmare is able to metamorphose into a little parasite. For Little Nightmare to be able to do so, players must use the Parasitic Egg on her, a drop acquired from Phosani's Nightmare.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.
25838: The parasitic egg is a reward from defeating Phosani's Nightmare. Players may use the egg on the Little Nightmare to allow it to metamorphose into a parasite version of the pet.

25844: The orange egg sac is an item obtained from looting the Grubby Chest in the south-west corner of the Forthos Dungeon. Using it on Sraracha allows it to metamorphose into the orange-coloured melee-attacking Spawn of Sarachnis.
25846: The blue egg sac is an item obtained from looting the Grubby Chest in the south-west corner of the Forthos Dungeon. Using it on Sraracha allows it to metamorphose into the blue-coloured magic-attacking Spawn of Sarachnis.
25862:
The bow of Faerdhinen is a magical bow that once belonged to Faerdhinen, an elite elven warrior. It is created from an enhanced crystal weapon seed. Requiring level 80 Ranged and 70 Agility to wield, it provides the highest Ranged Attack and Ranged Strength bonus out of any weapon for its attack speed.

Like the crystal bow, the bow of Faerdhinen does not require any arrows to use, as it generates its own when fired. The bow also benefits from improved damage and accuracy when crystal armour is equipped, with each piece granting additional bonuses - up to a total of 15% damage and 30% accuracy when the full set is equipped.

On unprotected death in PvP, the inactive bow is dropped, and all shards used to charge it will be lost. In a PvM or protected on PvP death, all current charges are kept.

25867:
The bow of Faerdhinen (c) is a corrupted version of the Bow of Faerdhinen that does not degrade, with its appearance altered to resemble the corrupted crystal seen within the Corrupted Gauntlet. The bow's colours may be changed to other colours of the Elven Clans by buying crystals from Lliann's Wares in Prifddinas, which cost 500,000 coins each. It can also be reverted to its original colour by using the crystal of Hefin on any variant of the corrupted bow.

The bow can be upgraded by bringing it and 2,000 crystal shards to a singing bowl. Doing so requires level 82 Smithing and Crafting (the levels can be boosted), and grants no experience. If the player does not meet the Smithing and Crafting requirements, they can have Conwenna or Reese sing the crystal in their stead for an extra 1,000 crystal shards. Excess charges in the bow will be taken into account; for example, a newly created bow with 10,000 charges will require 1,900 crystal shards to corrupt and a fully charged bow will only cost 1,800 crystal shards to upgrade.

Alternatively, the Bow of Faerdhinen can be corrupted passively through use: every 100 shots fired from the bow contributes 1 shard worth of progress toward the 1,900-shard corruption requirement. Once this cumulative amount is reached, the bow can be corrupted at the singing bowl with the level requirements or have Conwenna corrupt it for you for the 1000 shard price. Any combination of progress towards corruption, charges in the bow, and crystal shards can be used to meet the crystal shard requirement to corrupt the bow.

Upon creating the corrupted bow, the chatbox message states "With the help of the crystal bowl, you sing a dark song which corrupts the crystals."

While untradeable, the bow can be uncharged, but the crystal shards used to upgrade it will not be returned.

Like its regular variant, the bow requires level 80 Ranged and 70 Agility to wield, and provides the highest Ranged Attack and Ranged Strength bonus out of any weapon for its attack speed. It also benefits from damage and accuracy boosts when crystal armour is equipped. Each crystal armour piece equipped grants additional bonus accuracy and damage, adding up to a total 15% damage and 30% accuracy bonus when the full set is equipped.

When using crystal armour, the bow provides similar damage per second to the twisted bow and toxic blowpipe; however, these weapons excel against targets with high Magic level and low Defence respectively. Unlike the twisted bow or toxic blowpipe, the corrupted bow of Faerdhinen suffers no significant drawback and provides consistent performance due to its high accuracy and damage per shot, along with its moderate attack speed, long range, and unlimited ammunition.
25870:
The blade of Saeldor (c) is a corrupted version of the blade of Saeldor that does not degrade, with its appearance altered to resemble the corrupted crystal seen within the Corrupted Gauntlet. The blade's colours may be changed to other colours of the Elven Clans by buying crystals from Lliann's Wares in Prifddinas, which cost 500,000 coins each. It can also be reverted to its original colour by using the crystal of Hefin on any variant of the corrupted blade.

The blade can be upgraded by bringing it and 1,000 crystal shards to a singing bowl. Doing so requires level 82 Smithing and Crafting (the levels can be boosted), and grants no experience. If the player does not meet the Smithing and Crafting requirements, they can have Conwenna or Reese sing the crystal for them for an extra 500 crystal shards. Excess charges in the blade will be taken into account; for example, a fully charged blade (20,000 charges) will only cost 800 crystal shards to upgrade. Upon creating the corrupted blade, the chatbox message states "With the help of the crystal bowl, you sing a dark song which corrupts the crystals."

While untradeable, the blade can be uncharged, but the crystal shards used to upgrade it will not be returned.

Like its regular variant, the blade requires level 80 Attack to wield, and provides the highest slash bonus out of any one-handed weapon for its attack speed, surpassing the abyssal tentacle as the best slash weapon. It is tied with the Ghrazi rapier as the second strongest one-handed melee weapon in the game, after the Inquisitor's mace, although it is outperformed by the Scythe of Vitur against large monsters.

The bow of Faerdhinen (c) is a corrupted version of the Bow of Faerdhinen that does not degrade, with its appearance altered to resemble the corrupted crystal seen within the Corrupted Gauntlet. The bow's colours may be changed to other colours of the Elven Clans by buying crystals from Lliann's Wares in Prifddinas, which cost 500,000 coins each. It can also be reverted to its original colour by using the crystal of Hefin on any variant of the corrupted bow.

The bow can be upgraded by bringing it and 2,000 crystal shards to a singing bowl. Doing so requires level 82 Smithing and Crafting (the levels can be boosted), and grants no experience. If the player does not meet the Smithing and Crafting requirements, they can have Conwenna or Reese sing the crystal in their stead for an extra 1,000 crystal shards. Excess charges in the bow will be taken into account; for example, a newly created bow with 10,000 charges will require 1,900 crystal shards to corrupt and a fully charged bow will only cost 1,800 crystal shards to upgrade.

Alternatively, the Bow of Faerdhinen can be corrupted passively through use: every 100 shots fired from the bow contributes 1 shard worth of progress toward the 1,900-shard corruption requirement. Once this cumulative amount is reached, the bow can be corrupted at the singing bowl with the level requirements or have Conwenna corrupt it for you for the 1000 shard price. Any combination of progress towards corruption, charges in the bow, and crystal shards can be used to meet the crystal shard requirement to corrupt the bow.

Upon creating the corrupted bow, the chatbox message states "With the help of the crystal bowl, you sing a dark song which corrupts the crystals."

While untradeable, the bow can be uncharged, but the crystal shards used to upgrade it will not be returned.

Like its regular variant, the bow requires level 80 Ranged and 70 Agility to wield, and provides the highest Ranged Attack and Ranged Strength bonus out of any weapon for its attack speed. It also benefits from damage and accuracy boosts when crystal armour is equipped. Each crystal armour piece equipped grants additional bonus accuracy and damage, adding up to a total 15% damage and 30% accuracy bonus when the full set is equipped.

When using crystal armour, the bow provides similar damage per second to the twisted bow and toxic blowpipe; however, these weapons excel against targets with high Magic level and low Defence respectively. Unlike the twisted bow or toxic blowpipe, the corrupted bow of Faerdhinen suffers no significant drawback and provides consistent performance due to its high accuracy and damage per shot, along with its moderate attack speed, long range, and unlimited ammunition.

Escape crystals are a consumable teleport item that can be equipped in the ring slot. It can be purchased from Rick in the 1st floor of the Wizards' Tower, as well as from the Mysterious Stranger in Ver Sinhaza, for 75,000 coins.

The crystal acts similarly to a respawn teleport, teleporting players away from various activities, which Hardcore ironmen/group ironmen may consider as dangerous upon death:

Players can also use the crystal on their group members to activate them, allowing teleportation of teammates out of danger in an instant. To enable this, players must right-click the crystal and select "Configure", then choose the first option. Both players must have a crystal for this to work, and both crystals will be consumed in the process.

Additionally, the crystal can be configured to auto-activate upon taking damage (including zeros) after a specified time of inactivity (ranging from 2 to 300 seconds) via the "Configure" option; in this case, inactivity is defined as any time the player is not typing, clicking/tapping within the game, moving/zooming the camera, or moving the mouse. For example, if players configure the timer to 30 seconds, they will automatically be teleported away from the aforementioned activities upon taking damage after being inactive for at least 30 seconds. However, if the player has just logged in or hopped worlds and takes damage, the escape crystal will activate immediately even if the inactivity timer has not elapsed. This function will apply in The Gauntlet if the crystal was in the player's inventory upon entry, and is configured to auto-activate.

The crystal will NOT activate while the player is moving. If the inactive time is reached at any point during movement, the crystal will activate when the player stops moving.

The crystal can also be equipped and toggled to act in the same manner as a ring of life, although this will cause the crystal to be unable to teleport out from the aforementioned activities, so players must have it unequipped should they wish to be able to do so in those activities.

It is one of the few items whose teleports will work up to level 30 Wilderness, while most other means of teleportation will not work above level 20 Wilderness.

The Lightbearer is a ring obtained as a rare reward from the Tombs of Amascut. The ring was crafted by the warrior Ahmek from the unstable energy left behind from Tumeken's sacrifice that ended the Kharidian–Zarosian War.

The ring has no requirements to wear. It regenerates the player's special attack energy twice as fast at 15 seconds per 10%, or 2 minutes and 30 seconds for 100%. Equipping the ring will cause the special attack energy restoration timer to reset only if natural regeneration is below half. Unequipping the ring will always cause the special attack energy restoration timer to reset.
