The keris partisan is a one-handed partisan requiring 65 Attack to wield. It is obtained from Maisa as a reward for completing Beneath Cursed Sands. Players may own multiple partisans; additional partisans may be purchased from Selim in Al Kharid for 60,000 coins each. Weapon poisons cannot be applied to the partisan.

The keris partisan retains the effects of the keris, dealing 33% bonus damage against all kalphites and scabarites, alongside a 1/51 chance of puncturing a hole in their exoskeleton, dealing triple damage. When this special effect occurs, the chatbox will display the message: You slip your weapon through a gap in the creature's chitin, landing a vicious blow. Unlike the keris, however, the partisan provides a secondary crush bonus.

Players can attach one of four jewels, which are obtained as rewards from the Tombs of Amascut, to the keris partisan. Doing so increases the requirement to wield them to 80 Attack, and gives it differing effects within the raid.

The Breach of the Scarab creates the keris partisan of breaching, granting an additional 33% accuracy against all Kalphites and Scabarites (effect persists outside the raid).

The Eye of the Corruptor creates the keris partisan of corruption, granting a special attack that increases DPS.

The Jewel of Amascut creates the keris partisan of amascut, decreasing damage bonus against Kalphites and Scabarites but enhancing base stats.

The Jewel of the Sun creates the keris partisan of the sun, granting two passive effects and a special attack.
25981:
The keris partisan of breaching is a one-handed spear requiring 80 Attack to equip. It is made by attaching the Breach of the Scarab jewel to the keris partisan, granting an additional 33% accuracy against all kalphites and scabarites. Unlike the other three jewelled keris partisans, this partisan retains its passive effect outside the Tombs of Amascut raid. It does not possess a special attack.

The keris partisan of breaching retains the effects of the keris and keris partisan, including the 33% bonus damage against Kalphites and Scabarites, and the 1/51 chance of puncturing a hole in their exoskeleton that inflicts triple damage. When this special effect occurs, the chatbox will display the message: You slip your weapon through a gap in the creature's chitin, landing a vicious blow.

As with the keris partisan, weapon poisons cannot be applied to this partisan.

Elidinis' ward is a magical shield requiring 80 Magic, Defence, and Prayer to equip. Obtained as a rare drop from the Tombs of Amascut, the ward once belonged to the goddess Elidinis herself, who gave it to Pharaoh Osmumten before disappearing to mourn the loss of her husband Tumeken at the end of the Kharidian–Zarosian War.

The ward can be fortified by attaching an Arcane Sigil to the ward, creating the Elidinis' ward (f); doing so requires level 90 Prayer, 90 Smithing, and 10,000 soul runes, granting 260 experience in both skills in the process. Players cannot pay Abbot Langley to fortify the ward, though he can remove the sigil from an arcane spirit shield.

The fortified ward is untradeable, but it can be dismantled to return the sigil and ward. However, the soul runes will not be returned.

26231:
Nihil shards are an item dropped by all monsters in the Ancient Prison.

When used with a pestle and mortar, the nihil shard becomes nihil dust, which can be mixed with an unfinished dwarf weed potion at level 85 Herblore to make an ancient brew.

250 Nihil shards are required to create a Zaryte crossbow.
26233:
The ancient godsword is one of the five variants of the Godsword created by using an ancient hilt, obtained from Nex, on a completed godsword blade. As with all godsword variants, it requires level 75 Attack to wield.

The design of the hilt bears the Zarosian symbol and was created under Nex's orders after her escape from the Ancient Prison. Though the hilt was created, it never saw usage, as the four armies of the gods joined forces to imprison Nex once more before the weapon could be completed.

As a Zarosian item, it will also grant god protection towards Zarosian NPCs in the God Wars Dungeon.
26235:
Zaryte vambraces are a pair of vambraces requiring 80 Ranged and 45 Defence to wear. Obtained as a drop from Nex, the vambraces are the best-in-slot offensive gloves for rangers, surpassing Barrows gloves. It is also the only hands slot item to offer a Ranged Strength bonus.

As a Zarosian item, it will also grant god protection towards Zarosian NPCs in the God Wars Dungeon.
26237:
The Zaryte bow was a two-handed ranged weapon that would have required level 80 in Ranged to wield. It was one of the proposed rewards from Nex, and was only available from the supplies table in a tournament world as a test weapon for players. As a Zarosian item, it would have granted god protection towards Zarosian NPCs in the God Wars Dungeon.

The Zaryte bow has an attack range of nine, and is able to fire any type of arrow. In addition, the bow does not degrade, though it possesses a passive effect that consumes charges, similar to how an uncharged infernal axe acts as a regular a dragon axe.

The Zaryte bow was ultimately shelved and replaced by the Zaryte crossbow as a reward from Nex before being polled. With the later release of the Phantom Muspah, the venator bow was added to the game, with a similar design to the Zaryte bow.

The pumpkin pie is an unobtainable item used during the 2021 Halloween event. In order to distract the Cook in the Blue Moon Inn, the player orders this meal and loudly insults the food, causing the chef to leave the kitchen.

Although the item can be seen on a table during the cutscene, it cannot actually be obtained. Ending the cutscene with an empty inventory slot will cause the player to receive a pie dish.

The item could originally be bought and sold on the Grand Exchange due to an oversight, but was never listed on the Grand Exchange Database. Some people were able to obtain the Pumpkin pie through glitches, and sell it for very high prices. As a result of this exploit, it was made untradeable in a hotfix, then delisted from the Grand Exchange altogether.

With the end of the event, the pie was removed from the inventories of any players who still had them. However, they were not removed from any uncollected Grand Exchange offers, and are therefore still in the game.

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room.

Nexling is a pet dropped by Nex. It is a much smaller version of her.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.

26362:
The frozen key piece (Zamorak) is one of four pieces of the frozen key obtained from K'ril Tsutsaroth, or his bodyguards, during The Frozen Door miniquest.

Upon obtaining the other three pieces of the key from the other three generals of the God Wars Dungeon, players can assemble the frozen key and open the frozen door in the dungeon, which leads to the Ancient Prison containing Zaros' followers and their leader, Nex.

As with all frozen key pieces, it is always lost on death.

26366:
An important letter is given to the player by a messenger, who appears to players shortly after completing Desert Treasure I. Upon reading the letter, players will start The Frozen Door miniquest. After reading the letter, the letter cannot be reobtained once destroyed.

The author of the letter is unknown as they only identify themselves as an "admirer", but they intentionally deceive the player by tricking them into opening the Ancient Prison, where Nex, one of Zaros' most powerful generals, is imprisoned.
26368:
Nihil dust is the result of using a pestle and mortar on a nihil shard. It is combined with an unfinished dwarf weed potion, requiring level 85 Herblore, and yielding an ancient brew(3) and 190 Herblore experience.

Wesley in Nardah can crush herblore secondary items for 50 coins per item.
26370:
The ancient hilt is a rare drop from Nex, in the God Wars Dungeon. Its design bears the Zarosian symbol, and was created under Nex's orders after her escape from the Ancient Prison. Though the hilt was created, it never saw usage as the four armies of the gods joined forces to imprison Nex once more before the weapon could be completed.

When attached to a completed godsword blade, which can be created by combining the three Godsword shards, it creates the ancient godsword.
26372: The nihil horn is an item dropped by Nex. It is used to upgrade an Armadyl crossbow to a Zaryte crossbow, alongside 250 nihil shards.
26374:
The Zaryte crossbow is a ranged weapon that requires a Ranged level of 80 to wield, and can fire up to dragon bolts. The crossbow has an attack range of 8, and the longrange combat style will increase it by 2. It is only outclassed by the dragon hunter crossbow when fighting draconic monsters. This item counts as a Zaros item in the God Wars Dungeon.

The crossbow itself is crafted by attaching a nihil horn, obtained as a rare drop from Nex, with an Armadyl crossbow and 250 nihil shards. The Zaryte crossbow counts as a Zarosian item, but not as an Armadylean item in the God Wars Dungeon. In addition, the crossbow possesses a special attack as well as a passive effect, both of which synergise extremely well with the effects of enchanted bolts.

The Zaryte crossbow is primarily used for its special attack, which can deal a guaranteed 110 damage when used with ruby bolts (e) against high-health enemies. Additionally, it is the strongest weapon against non-draconic enemies weak to heavy Ranged attacks, such as the Leviathan.
26376:
The Torva full helm is part of the Torva armour set, requiring 80 Defence to wear. The helmet boasts the highest strength bonus of any helmet, being 2 higher than the Neitiznot faceguard and 3 higher than the serpentine helm. As a Zarosian-aligned item, Torva armour will give Zarosian protection within the God Wars Dungeon.

The helmet is created by combining a damaged Torva full helm, obtained as a drop from Nex, with one Bandosian component. This process requires level 90 Smithing, and is not reversible.
26378:
The Torva platebody is part of the Torva armour set, requiring 80 Defence to wear. The platebody boasts the highest strength bonus of any body slot equipment, being 2 higher than the oathplate chest, Bandos chestplate, Inquisitor's hauberk, fighter torso, and blood moon chestplate. As a Zarosian-aligned item, Torva armour will give Zarosian protection within the God Wars Dungeon.

The platebody is created by combining a damaged Torva platebody, obtained as a drop from Nex, with two Bandosian components. This process requires level 90 Smithing, drains the player's Strength and Prayer level temporarily, and is not reversible.

The platelegs are created by combining damaged Torva platelegs, obtained as a drop from Nex, with two Bandosian components. This process requires level 90 Smithing, and is not reversible.

26388:
Ecumenical key shards are an item dropped by Nex. 50 of these shards can be combined to create an ecumenical key, which allows entry to the chambers of the God Wars Dungeon bosses without having to obtain the 40 kill count normally required.

Players are limited to having three ecumenical keys at a time; completing the Medium and Hard Wilderness Diary increases this limit to four and five, respectively. As such, players who have the maximum number of ecumenical keys in their possession cannot combine additional shards until they have used a key. This does, however, mean that Ecumenical key shards are effectively a means of bypassing this restriction, since the player can have an essentially unlimited number of shards in their possession.
26390:
Blood essence is an item dropped by certain NPCs in the Ancient Prison, a possible reward from the Tombs of Amascut, as well as a potential reward when opening an intricate pouch. When one is activated, it becomes untradeable. While activated and in the inventory, it will give a 50% chance to craft an extra blood rune per pure essence, daeyalt essence, guardian essence or dark essence fragment for no additional experience. The bonus runes granted stack additively with other multipliers such as the Raiments of the Eye or runic extracts. Only one blood essence may be active at a time. If the player tries to activate a second blood essence, they will receive the message You can only have one active blood essence at a time. Each blood essence can craft an extra 1,000 blood runes before being destroyed. Blood essence works in Guardians of the Rift, however, the additional blood runes crafted will not provide additional catalytic guardian stones. Blood essence does not provide benefit nor consume charges at the Ourania Altar.

For Ultimate Ironman, the activated blood essence is destroyed upon death, and cannot be recovered from an Item Retrieval Service.

Each charge will on average last two essences. After using up all 1,000 charges, the player will have gained 47,600 experience when using dark essence, or 21,000 experience when using pure essence, and 4,200 blood runes provided the Raiments of the Eye were worn.

As a blood rune costs 356 coins, each blood essence could add an additional 356,000 coins in total. At current blood essence and blood rune prices, one can expect to earn 269,972 coins for every blood essence consumed. If using blood essence from level 77 to 99, a total of 242 blood essence would be consumed doing Zeah runecrafting for an additional 65,333,224 coins profit, while using pure essence would consume 550 blood essence for an additional 148,484,600 coins profit.

When an activated blood essence is checked by the player, they will receive the message Your blood essence has X charges remaining.

26463:
The Void knight top (or) is a Void knight top with a Shattered relics void ornament kit added onto it. The kit gives no additional bonuses, and is only used to add aesthetics to the top.

Whilst in its ornamented state, the top can be reverted anytime, returning the void knight top and kit.

If the player dies a PvP death at level 20 Wilderness or below and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 180,000 coins. The ornament kit is lost to the killer.

If the player dies a PvP death above level 20 Wilderness and the item is unprotected, it will be converted to coins. To prevent this, a Trouver parchment and a payment of 500,000 coins can be given to Perdu in order to permanently lock the item. The locked item will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a mangled, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 500,000 coins. The ornament kit is lost to the killer.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Void Knight (Shattered Relics) set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

The shattered teleport scroll is a consumable item purchased from the Leagues Reward Shop for 1,000 League points. It can be used to unlock a Shattered Relics-themed Home Teleport animation override. To enable it, players can right click "Animation" on the Home Teleport spell icon in their spellbook and select "Leagues III - Shattered Relics".

When the player reads the scroll, the chatbox message states This scroll contains an incantation which will unlock a new home teleport animation. Would you like to learn the incantation? (Warning: This will consume the scroll.)

If a player reads the scroll while already having unlocked the animation, the chatbox message will state This scroll contains an incantation which unlocks the Leagues III - Shattered Relics home teleport animation. However you have already unlocked this animation.

When equipped, the trophy can be right-clicked to perform the Trophy Emote.

The trophy can be displayed by using it on furniture built in the League hall's pedestal space.

If lost, players can reclaim it from the Leagues Tutor, or from furniture built in the League hall's trophy case space.

The Slayer helmet (i), requiring a Defence level of 10 to wear, is a piece of equipment that is worn in the helmet slot. It provides the bonuses of multiple pieces of protective and beneficial Slayer equipment. It functions in the same manner as its unimbued variant (with the 16.67% Melee bonus), except that it also provides an extra 15% boost to Ranged accuracy and Ranged damage, and a 15% boost to Magic accuracy and Magic damage, against monsters assigned as the player's Slayer task.

It has defensive bonuses equivalent to the rune full helm, with the exception of providing +11 higher relative magic defence (+10 vs. -1) as well as positive Magic and Ranged attack bonuses. It will prevent infection from Nex's virus attack, and can be used as warm clothing for Wintertodt.

Players can imbue the Slayer helmet using either 1,250,000 Nightmare Zone reward points (625,000 when the hard tier of Combat Achievements are complete), 500 Soul Wars Zeal Tokens, or by using a scroll of imbuing purchased from the Emir's Arena. The scroll can be used on the black mask before assembling the Slayer helmet or on the Slayer helmet itself.

If an imbued Slayer helmet is disassembled, then it will return an imbued black mask, along with the other components. The black mask (i) can be uncharged to return (depending on the original imbuing method) the scroll of imbuing, or a full refund of the Nightmare Zone reward points or Soul Wars zeal tokens used to purchase it.

For players with undead Slayer tasks, the boosts given by the Salve amulet or Salve amulet (e) do not stack with the effects of a Slayer helmet (i), and the amulet's boosts will take priority over the helmet's.

When using obsidian weapons the effect of a berserker necklace does stack with the effects of a Slayer helmet (i).

The ranged damage bonus from crystal armour pieces is multiplied by the 15% damage boost from the helmet. Assuming players are wearing both the crystal body and legs, this results in a damage bonus of approximately 29.375% (1.15 * 1.125).

The granite ring (i) is an imbued version of the regular granite ring from the Nightmare Zone and Soul Wars minigames. It requires 50 Defence and 50 Strength to equip. The imbue upgrade costs either 500,000 Nightmare Zone points or 250,000 with the hard tier of Combat Achievements, 200 Zeal Tokens, or by using a scroll of imbuing purchased from the Emir's Arena.

The upgrade doubles all defensive bonuses, including the negative Magic defence bonus.

If not protected, dying to another player will cause the imbued ring to lose its imbued status, but the player will be reimbursed the Nightmare Zone points, Zeal Tokens or Scroll of imbuing to re-imbue it via the aforementioned methods. Dying to a monster will not remove its imbued effect.

On the other hand, if its wearer dies to a monster, the ring will retain its imbued status even if dropped on death.

The ring of suffering (i) is an upgraded version of the regular ring of suffering. It can be imbued as a reward from the Nightmare Zone, costing 725,000 reward points or 362,500 with the hard tier of Combat Achievements, at Soul Wars for 300 Zeal Tokens, or by using a scroll of imbuing purchased from Emir's Arena for 200 points. Its stats are double those of the ring of suffering.

The ring can also be charged with rings of recoil to give it the recoil effect, renaming the item to ring of suffering (ri). Each ring of recoil provides 40 charges, assuming the ring of recoil has not been drained prior. A maximum of 100,000 charges can be stored, equivalent to 2,500 rings, at a cost of 2,350,000 coins. Players can configure the charges while the ring is in their bank by right-clicking on Configure-Charges, as long as players have the required materials. If a player uncharged the ring, the recoil rings stored will not be refunded. The ring of recoil effect is toggle-able, so players may disable it as to not waste it during training and instead use it in activities such as fighting Zulrah, or in PvP combat, where the effect may prove more useful. Charges are not lost upon death.

If not protected, dying to another player will cause the imbued ring to lose its imbued status, however the player will be reimbursed the Nightmare Zone points, Zeal Tokens or Scroll of imbuing to re-imbue it via the aforementioned methods. Dying to a monster will not remove its imbued effect.

The black mask (i) is an upgraded version of the black mask. It requires 20 Strength, 10 Defence, and 40 Combat to equip. It can be imbued as a reward from the Nightmare Zone, costing 1,250,000 reward points or 625,000 with the hard tier of Combat Achievements, at Soul Wars for 500 Zeal Tokens, or by using a scroll of imbuing purchased from the Emir's Arena. The imbued black mask can also be used to create an imbued Slayer helmet.

This version of the black mask provides the original bonus:

16.67% bonus to Melee accuracy and Strength on Slayer targets.

Plus the addition of:

15% bonus to Ranged accuracy and Strength.

15% bonus to Magic accuracy and Magic damage.

Getting rid of the -3 Magic and -1 Ranged attack penalties from the regular black mask.

If lost on death in PvP situations, the mask will lose its imbued status, but the player will be reimbursed the Nightmare Zone points, Zeal Tokens or Scroll of imbuing to imbue it again.

When this item is imbued at Nightmare Zone and subsequently uncharged, it will refund 100% of the cost. 1,250,000 reward points by default and 625,000 when the hard tier of Combat Achievements are complete.

26782:
The Salve amulet(ei) is the enchanted and imbued form of the salve amulet, granting a 20% increase in the wearer's accuracy and damage for melee, ranged, and magic when fighting undead monsters.

The salve amulet's bonuses against the undead do not stack with the black mask and slayer helmet's on-task bonuses; wearing both will only apply the bonuses of the salve amulet (ei). The salve amulet also does not have an effect on the dwarf multicannon's accuracy. However, the bonuses of Void Knight equipment do stack with the salve amulet. Additionally, the amulet's effects apply to all targets when using multi-hitting melee weapons in a multicombat area, such as the Scythe of Vitur and the special attack of the dragon 2h sword, but not for multi-hitting magic and ranged attacks (ex. chinchompas and burst spells).
26784:
The colossal pouch is the largest of the five essence pouches and can hold up to 40 rune, pure, daeyalt, or guardian essence for use in the Runecraft skill. The pouch is made by using an abyssal needle to stitch together a small, medium, large, and giant pouch, which requires the unboosted levels of 25 Runecraft and 56 Crafting. The pouches must be in their non-degraded state to be used in crafting.

Players cannot receive additional essence pouches if they own a colossal pouch. Should the player lose their colossal pouch, they must use a regular needle on the Rewards Guardian to obtain another abyssal needle, as well as reacquire the pouches.

When players create a colossal pouch, the chatbox will state You attempt to stitch together all of the pouches. It's difficult, but you eventually craft a strange, kind of gross, fleshy container. It seems capable of storing up to X essence., with X being the capacity depending on your Runecraft level. Attempting to make a colossal pouch without the required Crafting level will give the message You need level 56 Crafting to even attempt stitching these together..

During the Devious Minds quest, a colossal pouch can be used to hold an orb. The pouch is not lost when used for the quest, stating "The colossal pouch was so strong that it survived the blast from the glowing orb."

26788: A gold tiara is an item that members can create at a furnace from a gold bar along with a tiara mould and level 42 Crafting, granting 35 Crafting experience. They are a purely cosmetic head slot item, though they can be turned into an elemental or catalytic tiara, by bringing a gold tiara and either talisman to the appropriate runic altar. The talisman itself is lost in the process. Both gold and normal tiaras cannot be imbued during Guardians of the Rift.
26792:
Abyssal pearls are items obtained from the Rewards Guardian after completing a round of Guardians of the Rift. They are used to purchase items from Temple Supplies, the shop run by Apprentice Felix near the entrance to the minigame. The rewards are helpful items for training Runecraft, including the Raiments of the Eye outfit pieces costing 1,350 abyssal pearls. The average number of abyssal pearls per search is 2.14 (2.41 when exchanging lanterns and dyes), thus making 630 (or 560 when exchanging special items) the average number of searches required to complete the full Raiments of the Eye set if no duplicate items or excess dyes are traded in. While abyssal pearls cannot be traded or exchanged for coins, 400 pearls can be used to purchase a ring of the elements from Temple Supplies, which puts the value of an abyssal pearl at 1,593.57.

Players may also sell abyssal lanterns to Apprentice Felix for 100 pearls, and abyssal dyes for 50 pearls. Players may also pay Apprentice Cordelia 1 pearl to repair their essence pouches in place of the Dark Mage, after unlocking the service for an initial 25 pearls. Lastly, players can use 25 pearls on the Rewards Guardian for an additional loot roll.
26798:
The catalytic talisman is a talisman that can be received as a drop from the Rewards Guardian, using points earned while playing Guardians of the Rift. It allows players to access any catalytic runic altar, providing the player has completed the quests to access some of them.

The talisman can be combined with a gold tiara to make a catalytic tiara for 60 Runecraft experience at a catalytic altar, by using the tiara on it. This consumes the talisman, but the catalytic tiara can be used in just the same way and can be worn on the head, saving an inventory space when crafting catalytic runes. Creating the tiara cannot be done whilst playing the Guardians of the Rift minigame.

The talisman (and the tiara) can be used to access the Death Altar during Mourning's End Part II to skip completing Thorgel's item list.

Though it has a locate option, using it will give the message "Nothing interesting happens."
26801:
A catalytic tiara is a head slot item used in Runecraft. It is created at any catalytic runic altar (except for the Astral Altar, Soul Altar or Kourend's Blood Altar) by using a gold tiara or catalytic talisman on the altar with both in your inventory. This consumes the catalytic talisman and yields 60 Runecraft experience. As with all other tiaras, catalytic runic altars accessed through Guardians of the Rift cannot be used for imbuing.

The Catalytic runes are: Cosmic runes, Mind runes, Body runes, Chaos runes, Nature runes, Law runes, Death runes, Blood runes, Soul runes and Wrath runes.

While a catalytic tiara is equipped, the mysterious ruins to catalytic altars have a left-click "Enter" option, freeing up an inventory slot that the catalytic talisman would otherwise occupy.

A catalytic tiara, or any other imbued tiaras, may also be used on the Hat of the Eye in order to make the hat function as the tiara that was attuned to it.

The tiara (or the talisman) can be used to access the Death Altar during Mourning's End Part II to skip completing Thorgel's item list.
26804:
An elemental tiara is a head slot item used in Runecraft. It is created at any elemental runic altar by using a gold tiara or elemental talisman on the altar with both in your inventory. This consumes the elemental talisman and yields 40 Runecraft experience. As with all other tiaras, elemental runic altars accessed via Guardians of the Rift cannot be used for imbuement.

While an elemental tiara is equipped, the mysterious ruins to elemental altars have a left-click "Enter" option, freeing up an inventory slot that the elemental talisman would otherwise occupy.

An elemental tiara, or any other imbued tiaras, may also be used on the Hat of the Eye in order to make the hat function as the tiara that was attuned to it.
26807:
Abyssal green dye is an item that allows one piece of the raiments of the eye to be recoloured to a green variant. It is a one time use per item, therefore a total of three are needed to recolour a full set, with optionally two more for the Amulet of the Eye and the lost bag.

Excess green dyes can be exchanged for an abyssal red or abyssal blue dye by using it on Apprentice Felix; however, doing so does not count towards unlocking the respective slots in the collection log. Players may also choose to exchange the dye with Apprentice Felix for 50 abyssal pearls instead.
26811:
Abyssal red dye is an item that allows one piece of the raiments of the eye to be recoloured to a red variant. It is a one time use per item, therefore a total of three are needed to recolour a full set, with optionally two more for the Amulet of the Eye and the lost bag.

Excess red dyes can be exchanged for an abyssal blue or abyssal green dye by using it on Apprentice Felix; however, doing so does not count towards unlocking the respective slots in the collection log. Players may also choose to exchange the dye with Apprentice Felix for 50 abyssal pearls instead.
26813:
The abyssal needle is an item that can be obtained from the Rewards Guardian after completing a round of Guardians of the Rift. It can also be purchased from the Temple Supplies shop for 750 abyssal pearls.

Players with level 56 Crafting[not boostable] and 25 Runecraft[not boostable] can use the needle to stitch together the small, medium, large, and giant pouches into a colossal pouch, which stores up to 40 rune, pure, daeyalt, or guardian essence. The pouches must be in their non-degraded state to be used in crafting. Upon crafting the colossal pouch, the abyssal needle is consumed.

The maximum essence held by the pouch scales with the player's Runecraft level.

Should the player lose their colossal pouch or abyssal needle, they may use a regular needle on the Rewards Guardian to obtain another abyssal needle.
26815:
The ring of the elements is an item purchased from the Guardians of the Rift reward shop for 400 abyssal pearls. It teleports players near the elemental runic altars. It also counts as a piece of warm clothing at Wintertodt, regardless of charge. When charged, the ring is untradeable.

The ring is charged by using one of each elemental rune (air, earth, fire, water) and one law rune together on the ring, costing 148 per teleport. The ring can hold up to 10,000 charges, costing 1,480,000 to fully charge. The number of charges is tracked by player, meaning a second ring owned by the player will have the same number of charges as the first. Players can receive the runes back through the ring's right-click "Uncharge" option while at almost any bank.

26822:
The abyssal lantern is an item worn in the shield slot that can be obtained from the Rewards Guardian after completing a round of Guardians of the Rift. It can also be purchased from the Temple Supplies reward shop or Apprentice Felix via dialogue for 1,500 abyssal pearls.

Players with the appropriate Firemaking level and a tinderbox can use six logs of a certain type (normal, oak, willow, maple, yew, blisterwood, magic, or redwood) on the lantern to light it, which gives varying benefits for runecrafting when worn. The Firemaking level requirement cannot be boosted, and no Firemaking experience is gained. Coloured logs can be used in place of normal logs, though they give the same effects.

In addition to the benefits provided when runecrafting, the lit lantern serves as an equipable light source. It also works as a lantern for lantern harpooning.

Players cannot light a lantern if they already have another one lit.

Any extra abyssal lanterns the player has can be exchanged with Apprentice Felix for 100 abyssal pearls.

26850:
The Hat of the Eye is a part of the Raiments of the Eye set, purchased from the Guardians of the Rift reward shop for 400 abyssal pearls. It grants 10% more runes when Runecrafting, and is increased to 60% when the full set is worn.

The hat can be recoloured using abyssal dye (received from the Rewards Guardian) to a red, blue, or green colour scheme.

Players can attune imbued tiaras to the Hat of the Eye to allow it to function as one. This includes the catalytic tiara and the elemental tiara, allowing access to multiple altars simultaneously. All copies of the Hat of the Eye, including those of a different colour, will then be attuned to that tiara (including those stored in the magic wardrobe). The tiara is not consumed in this manner, and the attunement can be freely switched by using a different tiara. Players can use the hat's right-click "Check" option to see which type of tiara it is currently attuned to.

This item can be stored in the magic wardrobe of a costume room, as part of the Raiments of the Eye sets. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
26852:

The outfit can be recoloured using abyssal dyes (received from the Rewards Guardian) to a red, blue, or green colour scheme. Each dye recolours one piece of the outfit, so three in total are needed to recolour a set, as the boots can't be recoloured.

26876:
Atlax's diary is a book that may be received from the Rewards Guardian after a game of Guardians of the Rift.

Written by Atlax, the diary details their experiences exploring the Temple of the Eye while working for Pharana. Pharana, in turn, was asked to clear the site by Justiciar Aliya following the battle that occurred when a rift to the scar was opened. While exploring the temple, Atlax documents several discoveries, including a cache of Eye amulets and a mysterious stone guardian tasked with protecting the temple.

The book can also be found in the bookcases in a player-owned house if the player has previously read the book.
26880:
Catalytic guardian stones are items used to power-up the Great Guardian during a game of Guardians of the Rift, alongside elemental guardian stones and polyelemental guardian stones.

They are obtained by imbuing guardian essence at a catalytic runic altar, accessible directly by entering an active Portal Guardian. This is a 1:1 ratio of essence to stones. The Raiments of the Eye set does not offer additional bonuses.

Players are granted 5 Runecraft experience and 2 catalytic energy per catalytic guardian stone used to power-up the Great Guardian.

Mind, Body, Cosmic, Chaos, Nature, Law, Death and Blood Runes give Catalytic Energy.
26881:
Elemental guardian stones are items used to power-up the Great Guardian during a game of Guardians of the Rift, alongside catalytic guardian stones and polyelemental guardian stones.

They are obtained by imbuing guardian essence at an elemental runic altar, accessible directly by entering an active Portal Guardian.

Players are granted 5 Runecraft experience and 2 elemental energy per elemental guardian stone used to power-up the Great Guardian.

Air, Water, Earth and Fire Runes give Elemental Energy.
26882:
Uncharged cells are an item obtained during the Guardians of the Rift minigame. They are charged by imbuing them at a runic altar, accessible directly by entering an active Portal Guardian. The type of charge it holds is dependent on the runic altar it is charged at.

When inspected, the chatbox will state "An uncharged magical cell built to hold runic energy."
26883:
Weak cells are an item obtained during the Guardians of the Rift minigame. Players can obtain one from the table by the entrance, or by imbuing an uncharged cell at the Air, Mind, or Body Altar, which are accessible directly by entering the active Portal Guardians of that type.

The weak cell can be used alongside a chisel to create weak elemental and catalytic guardians or placed on an inactive cell tile to create weak barriers, or reinforce an existing barrier.

When inspected, the chatbox will state "A magical cell charged with a small amount of runic energy."
26884:
Medium cells are an item obtained during the Guardians of the Rift minigame. Players can obtain one by imbuing an uncharged cell at the Water, Cosmic, or Chaos Altar, which are accessible directly by entering the active Portal Guardians of that type.

The medium cell can be used alongside a chisel to create medium elemental and catalytic guardians, be placed on a weak cell tile to create medium barriers, or reinforce an existing barrier.

When inspected, the chatbox will state A magical cell charged with a moderate amount of runic energy.
26885:
Strong cells are an item obtained during the Guardians of the Rift minigame. Players can obtain one by imbuing an uncharged cell at the Earth, Nature, or Law Altar, which are accessible directly by entering the active Portal Guardians of that type.

The strong cell can be used alongside a chisel to create strong elemental and catalytic guardians, be placed on a medium cell tile to create strong barriers, or reinforce an existing barrier.

When inspected, the chatbox will state "A magical cell charged with a high amount of runic energy."
26886:
Overcharged cells are items obtained during the Guardians of the Rift minigame. Players can obtain one by imbuing an uncharged cell at the Fire, Death, or Blood Altar, which are accessible directly by entering the active Portal Guardians of that type.

The overcharged cell can be used alongside a chisel to create overcharged elemental and catalytic guardians. They can also be placed on a strong cell tile to create overcharged barriers, or reinforce existing ones.

When inspected, the chatbox will display a message similar to the cell's examine text, describing the cell as "a magical cell charged with an immense amount of runic energy."
26899:
The rift guardian is a members-only skilling pet that can be obtained while training Runecraft. The chances of getting it are dependent on the player's Runecraft level, the rune the player is crafting, and the number of essence used. Upon using the Guardian's eye on it, which is purchased from the Guardians of the Rift reward shop for 3,000 abyssal pearls, players unlock a permanent metamorphosis option to turn it into the Greatish guardian.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

When runecrafting using dark essence fragments, the pet is given after they are removed and the runes are given back. This means if there is not already some of the runes to be crafted in the inventory, and the rest of the inventory is full, and a pet is already following the player, the rift guardian will not be given; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.
26901:
Abyssal protector is a pet that can be obtained from the Rewards Guardian. It is a much smaller version of the Abyssal guardians found within the Guardians of the Rift minigame.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.
26903:
The eye amulet is obtained during the quest Temple of the Eye. The player is requested to bring this item to the Mage of Zamorak in Varrock at the Altar of Zamorak to have him trace the object. The eye on the amulet is said to be the symbol of the Order of Wizards and gives off abyssal energy. The Mage of Zamorak will tell the player more about the amulet in exchange for a bucket of water and a Strong cup of tea.

Later in the quest, the player discovers from Wizard Persten that the amulet is related to a teleportation matrix and that a Transmission Spell has been cast upon the amulet, thereby allowing the Z.M.I to track the user of the amulet. In response to this, Wizard Persten alters the spell on the amulet to provide the Z.M.I with false information.

If the amulet is lost upon death, a new one can be acquired by speaking to Wizard Persten.
26904: A strong cup of tea is an item obtained from the Tea Seller during the quest Temple of the Eye at the request of Herbert, the Mage of Zamorak. The Tea Seller tells the player the strong cups of tea that he gives Herbert are in actuality regular cups of tea, and he chooses not to tell him to keep him happy.
26905:
The abyssal incantation is an item obtained during the quest Temple of the Eye, written down by the Dark Mage. This item should be taken to Wizard Persten north of Al Kharid who then goes on to recommend you take it to Archmage Sedridor in the Wizards' Tower.

Sedridor notes that the incantation is written on thin flesh rather than parchment; when speaking to Herbert after the quest, he tells players that it is most likely flesh from an abyssal creature.
26906:
The colossal pouch is created when using the orb on a regular colossal pouch during the Devious Minds quest. It is used as a teleport beacon for a mysterious character later known as the Assassin to steal a relic from the Entrana church.

Note that unlike the large pouch, the colossal pouch is not lost during the quest. After the cutscene where the relic is stolen, the game chat will state The colossal pouch was so strong that it survived the blast from the glowing orb.
26910: The tarnished locket is an item that can be obtained from an intricate pouch, which can be received from the Rewards Guardian after completing a round of Guardians of the Rift. After inspecting it, players can give the locket to Phileas the Lumbridge Guide in exchange for the Amulet of the Eye. If the locket is lost before turning it in, it can be reclaimed from Apprentice Felix.
26912:
The lost bag is a cape slot item that can be obtained from an intricate pouch, which can be received from the Rewards Guardian after completing a round of Guardians of the Rift. It has no stat bonuses and is purely cosmetic.

The bag can be recoloured using abyssal dye (received from the Rewards Guardian) to a red, blue, or green colour scheme.

If the bag is destroyed, another can be obtained from Apprentice Felix. If the bag was recoloured before it was destroyed, then it will still be recoloured when it is reclaimed.

As it is dropped at a 1/60 rate from an intricate pouch, which in its place has a drop rate of 1/28 to 1/25, the effective drop rate of the lost bag ranges from 1/1500 to 1/1680 searches.
26914:
The amulet of the Eye is an item that allows unlimited teleportation to the Temple of the Eye, just south of the portal. It is obtained by inspecting the tarnished locket and then showing it to Phileas the Lumbridge Guide.

The amulet can be recoloured using Abyssal dye (received from the Rewards Guardian) to a red, blue, or green colour scheme.

The amulet provides unlimited teleports to the Temple of the Eye and can be used as a banking method with low requirements.

Players can reclaim the amulet from the Lumbridge Guide should it be lost. If the amulet was recoloured before it was destroyed, then it will still be recoloured when it is reclaimed. If players wish to reclaim multiple amulets, they can do so by attempting to destroy the amulet on a Free-to-play world, which drops the amulet to the ground, allowing players to reclaim another and also pick up the dropped one.

When trading the locket for the amulet, the Lumbridge Guide provides a little backstory for the item. Phileas explains that the amulet had long been in the possession of his family, whose members had been initiated into the Order of Wizards for generations. The eye-shaped amulet displays the symbol of the Order of Wizards, which long ago built and oversaw the Temple of the Eye with the aim of protecting a powerful artefact. The order had long since given up this task, leading the history of its symbol to become obscured, until the player is able to confirm its origins after re-discovering the temple.
26916: The Special hot sauce is obtained from Ali Morrisane in the 2022 Easter event. It has a right-click "Drink" option, though attempting to do so results in the player saying "I definitely do not want to drink any of this!" The special hot sauce cannot be put in the bank.
26917: The special super hot kebab is obtained from Karim after giving him the special hot sauce in the 2022 Easter event. It has a right-click "Eat" option, though attempting to do so results in the player saying "Nope, I am not going to eat that!" The special super hot kebab cannot be banked.
26919:
A big bucket is obtained from the Easter Bunny after talking to him about the choc-ice in the 2022 Easter event. It is used on a camel to obtain a Big bucket of camel milk, which is needed to create camel ice cream during the event.

The big bucket cannot be put in the bank.
26920:
Big bucket of camel milk is an item obtained during the 2022 Easter event. It is obtained by using a big bucket on either Alice, Cam, or Elly the Camel.

The bucket has a right-click "Drink" option, though attempting to do so results in the player saying "I don't think I actually want to drink that. I need it for the ice cream!"

Emptying the bucket prints the message "You empty the contents of the bucket on the floor. What a waste of camel milk!" and leaves the player with an empty big bucket. The big bucket of camel milk cannot be banked.
26921: Big bucket of frozen camel milk is an item obtained during the 2022 Easter event. It is only seen by players during a cutscene where Phoebe Kay freezes the big bucket of camel milk outside Ferox Enclave.
26924:
Magical cleaning potion is an item obtained during the 2022 Easter event. It is used to clean the dirty vat. According to Ali Morrisane, this potion is the very same one used during the 2021 Christmas event.

The bottle has a right-click "Drink" option, though attempting to do so results in the player saying "As good as this smells, I need to use this to clean the tanning vat."
26925: Cooler is an item obtained during the 2022 Easter event after asking the Suspicious crate for one. The cooler is used to hold an easter egg and ice cream easter egg in order to transport them to the Shantay Pass to perform a melting experiment. The eggs can only be removed from the cooler when standing in the Shantay Pass, which begins the experiment.
26927:
Melted easter egg is an item obtained during the 2022 Easter event. It is the result of melting an easter egg during the Shantay Pass experiment, or from the ice cream easter egg melting when talking to the Easter Bunny at the end of the event. Upon finishing the event, all remaining easter eggs in the inventory will melt.

When eaten, it heals 1 Hitpoint, resulting in the following game message:

You eat the melted Easter egg...

...It tastes lovely and heals some health.

If you eat the melted easter egg with full health, the message is slightly different:

You eat the melted Easter egg...

...It tastes lovely.

Although useless, players were able to keep melted easter eggs after completion of the event. With the end of the event, all melted easter eggs were removed from the inventories of any players who still had them.
26928: Ice cream easter egg is an item obtained during the 2022 Easter event. It is made of a normal easter egg filled with camel milk ice cream, intended to keep the chocolate from melting in the desert heat. The ice cream easter egg doesn't melt during the Shantay Pass experiment, but melts into a melted easter egg when talking to the Easter Bunny at the end of the event.
26929: Blunt scimitars can be obtained by talking to Zeke during the 2022 Easter event. They can be used to create the churning machine.
26930: Washing line is an item obtained after searching the pile of junk during the 2022 Easter event. It can be used to create the churning machine.
26934: Wooden pole is an item obtained after searching the pile of junk during the 2022 Easter event. It can be used to create the churning machine.
26935: Churning machine is an item obtained after combining the blunt scimitars, tanning wheel, cleaned vat, washing line, and wooden pole during the 2022 Easter event.
26941:
Polyelemental guardian stones are items used to power-up the Great Guardian during a game of Guardians of the Rift, alongside elemental, catalytic, and polycatalytic guardian stones.

They are obtained by crafting combination runes when imbuing guardian essence at an elemental runic altar, accessible directly by entering an active Portal Guardian.

Players are granted 5 Runecraft experience and 3 elemental energy (instead of the normal 2) per polyelemental guardian stone used to power-up the Great Guardian.

Mist, Dust, Mud, Smoke, Steam, and Lava Runes give Polyelemental Energy.
26944: Clue scroll (elite) is an coordinate clue obtained from elite Treasure Trails.
26952: The scarab mould is an item obtained from the chest during the quest Beneath Cursed Sands. It is used to craft a scarab emblem from an iron bar.
26953:
The scarab emblem is an item obtained during the quest Beneath Cursed Sands. The emblem depicts Scabaras, one of the four minor gods of the Menaphite Pantheon.

The iron emblem is obtained by using an iron bar on the furnace in the Ruins of Ullek whilst having a scarab mould, whilst the gold emblem is used to solve a puzzle to progress in the tomb below the ruins.
26954:
The stone tablet is an item obtained during the quest Beneath Cursed Sands, from searching the well in the Ruins of Ullek.

The tablet, carved during the God Wars, contains the code to the buried chest mentioned in the message.
26955:

26958:

26961: The lily of the Elid is an item obtained during the quest Beneath Cursed Sands. It is picked from the lily on a small island directly west of Nardah.
26962: The cure crate is an item obtained from Zahur during the quest Beneath Cursed Sands. It contains the cure to the plague in Sophanem.
26965: The bottle of 'tonic' is an item that can be obtained from a table at Maisa's camp between Sophanem and the Ruins of Ullek during the quest Beneath Cursed Sands. It has no apparent use.
26967:
The circlet of water is an item obtained from Maisa as a reward for completing the quest Beneath Cursed Sands. Wearing it will delay the onset of desert heat by 12 seconds.

The circlet, which acts as an equipable waterskin, is charged with five water runes per charge, and can hold up to 500,000 charges. One charge is consumed whenever the player would have needed to drink water due to the effects of desert heat. The circlet can be uncharged to regain the runes. The circlet must be equipped in order for the effects to work.

The maximum time between drinks is 132 seconds (costing 28 charges per hour).

If lost, it can be reclaimed from the High Priest of Sophanem for 10,000 coins. Additionally, if the free one was not received due to a full inventory at the end of the quest and Into the Tombs has been started, it can be claimed from the High Priest.

The desert amulet 4, which requires completion of the elite Desert Diary, also provides 100% protection against desert heat when worn but doesn't require upkeep.

26996:
An ensouled hellhound head is an item which can be dropped by hellhounds and Cerberus. It is used to gain Prayer experience by using the level 72 Magic spell Expert Reanimation from the Arceuus spellbook using 3 nature runes, 1 blood rune, and 2 soul runes. When a player reanimates an ensouled hellhound head, a reanimated hellhound will appear and grant 1,200 Prayer experience after being killed.

Ensouled heads can be reanimated anywhere as long as the head is on the ground within the 31x31 area centred on its initial drop location and has not been put into the bank, trade screen, Grand Exchange, or price checker. Otherwise, it must be taken to the Dark Altar in Arceuus to be reanimated.

27000:
The Void knight top (or) is a Void knight top with a Shattered relics void ornament kit added onto it. The kit gives no additional bonuses, and is only used to add aesthetics to the top.

Whilst in its ornamented state, the top can be reverted anytime, returning the void knight top and kit.

If the player dies a PvP death at level 20 Wilderness or below and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 180,000 coins. The ornament kit is lost to the killer.

If the player dies a PvP death above level 20 Wilderness and the item is unprotected, it will be converted to coins. To prevent this, a Trouver parchment and a payment of 500,000 coins can be given to Perdu in order to permanently lock the item. The locked item will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a mangled, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 500,000 coins. The ornament kit is lost to the killer.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Void Knight (Shattered Relics) set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

If the player dies a PvP death at level 20 Wilderness or below and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 250,000 coins. The ornament kit is lost to the killer.

If the player dies a PvP death above level 20 Wilderness and the item is unprotected, it will be converted to coins. To prevent this, a Trouver parchment and a payment of 500,000 coins can be given to Perdu in order to permanently lock the item. The locked item will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a mangled, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 500,000 coins. The ornament kit is lost to the killer.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Void Knight Elite (Shattered Relics) set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

27008:
The dragon defender (t) is a dragon defender with a dragon defender ornament kit attached to it. The attached ornament kit gives no additional bonuses, and is only used to add aesthetics to the defender.

If the player dies to a PvP death and the dragon defender is not one of the player's protected items, it will remain in the player's inventory, but will become broken, which means the item is unusable and must be repaired with 240,000 coins by using the item on Perdu. The ornament kit will be lost.
27009:
The rune defender (t) is a rune defender with a rune defender ornament kit attached to it. The attached ornament kit gives no additional bonuses, and is only used to add aesthetics to the defender.

The trimmed defender can be dismantled anytime, returning the defender and the tradeable ornament kit. Lorelai will not recognise the rune defender (t) as a rune defender for access to the basement cyclopes.

If the player dies to a PvP death and the rune defender is not one of the player's protected items, it will remain in the player's inventory, but will become broken, which means the item is unusable and must be repaired with 35,000 coins by using the item on Perdu. The ornament kit will be lost.
27010: A preform is an unfinished giant's sword made during the Sleeping Giants quest and the Giants' Foundry minigame. It is automatically equipped, and can only be unequipped by taking it to the preform storage in the northern part of the foundry. This means an unwanted preform cannot be simply gotten rid of; either the sword must be completed, damaged by messing up the process (this is the fastest method), or it must be stored forever.
27014:
Kovac's grog is a type of ale that restores 1 Hitpoint and temporarily boosts Smithing by 4 while draining Attack, Ranged, and Magic by 2. This provides the second highest Smithing boost available, surpassing the mature dwarven stout's 2-level boost. Furthermore, this is a reliable boost, unlike orange spicy stew which may boost or drain the player by up to 5 levels when 3 dashes of orange spice are added.

It can be purchased from the Giants' Foundry reward shop for 300 Foundry Reputation. Each serving of Kovac's grog is worth 100,492 coins, or 334.97 coins per Reputation point.

Upon drinking the grog, a message in the chatbox will state You drink Kovac's grog. It tastes like giants' feet.

This item cannot be traded back to the shop for Foundry Reputation. Ironman players are presented with an Easter egg message if they try to exchange the grog for Foundry Reputation.
27017:
Smithing catalyst is a consumable item purchased from the Giants' Foundry reward shop for 15 Foundry Reputation.

They are used when smelting bars at a furnace, or using the Superheat Item spell, to halve the amount of coal required per bar, whilst simultaneously providing double experience per bar consuming the catalyst in the process. The catalyst only works for bars that are produced using coal. The experience doubling effect works at the Blast Furnace, but it does not reduce the amount of coal needed any further.

Based on the opportunity cost of using Foundry Reputation to buy catalyst instead of Kovac's grog to sell on the Grand Exchange, each Smithing catalyst costs 5,024.6 coins.
27019:
Ore pack may refer to one of the following:

Ore pack (Giants' Foundry), an item purchased from the Giants' Foundry Reward Shop.

Ore pack (Volcanic Mine), an item purchased from Petrified Pete's Ore Shop.

Mineral pack, an item purchased from the Void Knights' Reward Options.
27021:
The colossal blade is a two-handed sword purchased from the Giants' Foundry reward shop for 5,000 Foundry Reputation, requiring level 60 Attack to wield.

The colossal blade's stats are similar to those of the barrelchest anchor, with a slightly higher slash bonus than the anchor's crush bonus. Although it lacks a special attack, it has a passive effect to make up for it on larger size monsters. The blade also has much lower requirements compared to the barrelchest anchor, which also requires 40 Strength, in addition to 50 Prayer and 40 Ranged for completion of The Great Brain Robbery quest. Due to this, the blade can be used as a substitute for the anchor on low Prayer, 60 Attack, player killing builds. The 16, 31, and 44 Prayer builds for example, will benefit from this.

The colossal blade only has to be unlocked once; if lost in any situation, it can be re-obtained from Perdu for 300,000 as long as you do not have another copy of this item. If lost in PVP, the item will drop as 225,000 for the killer.
27023:
The smiths tunic is a piece of the Smiths' Uniform set that can be purchased from the Giants' Foundry reward shop for 4,000 Foundry Reputation.

The tunic gives a 20% chance of speeding up anvil smithing actions by 1 tick; it also gives a 20% chance to give increased progress on preforms in the Giants' Foundry. Wearing the full set will increase this chance to 100%.

This item can be stored in the magic wardrobe of a costume room, as part of the Smiths' Uniform. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
27025:

The boots give a 20% chance of speeding up smithing actions on an anvil by 1 tick, as well as a 20% chance for increased progress on preforms in the Giants' Foundry; wearing the full set will increase this chance to 100%.

This item can be stored in the magic wardrobe of a costume room, as part of the Smiths' Uniform. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
27029:
The smiths gloves is a piece of the Smiths' Uniform set that can be purchased from the Giants' Foundry reward shop for 3,500 Foundry Reputation.

The gloves gives a 20% chance of speeding up anvil smithing actions by 1 tick; it also gives a 20% chance to give increased progress on preforms in the Giants' Foundry. Wearing the full set will increase this chance to 100%.

Smiths gloves can be combined with ice gloves to create smiths gloves (i), which combines the effects of both; this can be undone if desired.

This item can be stored in the magic wardrobe of a costume room, as part of the Smiths' Uniform. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
27031:
The smiths gloves (i) is a piece of the Smiths' Uniform set that is made from using smiths gloves and ice gloves on each other, combining the effects of both.

The gloves give a 20% chance of speeding up a smithing action performed at an anvil by 1 tick; it also gives a 20% chance to give increased progress on preforms in the Giants' Foundry. Wearing the full set will increase this chance to 100%. They also allow players to pick up hot metal bars at the Blast Furnace and preforms in the Giants' Foundry without the need for a bucket of water to cool them down.

The Dismantle option allows the player to separate the gloves back into smiths gloves and ice gloves at no cost.

This item can be stored in the magic wardrobe of a costume room. It will use the same space as the non-iced smiths gloves and count as part of the full Smiths' Uniform for Ultimate Ironmen.

The rune pouch is an item that can store 16,000 of three types of runes (except runes found in the Nightmare Zone). Players can cast spells using the runes stored in the pouch, so a rune pouch saves inventory space. With a thread of Elidinis and level 75 crafting, the rune pouch can be upgraded (with a needle) to a divine rune pouch. Players cannot own more than one rune pouch.

If players die a PvP death while carrying a rune pouch in any level Wilderness or in a PvP world, they will lose the rune pouch, unless it has been locked via use of a trouver parchment. It should be noted that the Trouver parchment does not protect runes stored within a Rune pouch upon PvP death.

If players die a PvM death anywhere, including any level Wilderness, the rune pouch is always sent to a gravestone or item retrieval service, unless it has been locked via use of a trouver parchment. Locked rune pouches are kept in the inventory upon PvM death, instead.
27098:
The elder maul ornament kit is an untradeable ornament kit purchased from the Bounty Hunter Store for 50 points. It can change the appearance of the elder maul, turning it into the elder maul (or).

The ornament kit can be removed and reattached to relevant items without penalty. When a kitted item is lost to a PvP death, the item will be lost to the killer but the kit will be sent to the gravestone. A kitted item is always protected on PvM death.
27100:
The elder maul (or) is a cosmetic variant of the elder maul with an elder maul ornament kit added to it. It can be dismantled at any time, returning both parts back to the player. It is a two-handed crush weapon that requires Attack and Strength levels of 75 to wield.

Along with the non-cosmetic variant, it is the highest tier crush weapon available. It overtakes the godswords as the weapon with the highest strength bonus. Despite the strength bonus, the abyssal bludgeon often has higher overall damage output against low-defence monsters because of its quicker attack speed, making it only useful in places such as Tekton. Because of its high strength bonus, it is often used as a finisher in player killing. The colour of the ornament kit matches that of the Bandos armour set.
27111:
Wrapped rune gloves are a pair of Culinaromancer's gloves obtainable from the equipment chests within the Emir's Arena hospital, where players can tailor their equipment and inventory to their liking in preparation for a match. Similar to rune gloves, 1 Def Pure builds cannot use these gloves; only Zerkers and Max/Med builds can add them to their loadout.

In comparison to rune gloves, the wrapped gloves possess no Defence bonuses, but in exchange has their Slash, Stab, Crush, and Ranged Attack Bonuses increased by +9, and their Magic Attack bonus increased by +3.

27157:
The dragon knife is a throwing knife that requires a Ranged level of 60 to wield. It is the most powerful type of throwing knife available. They can be obtained as a drop from wyrms, drakes, and hydras. They can be poisoned and can be wielded with a shield or god book for protection.

As with most dragon equipment, dragon knives cannot be made from raw materials using the Smithing skill.

If attacking constantly, with an Ava's assembler equipped, the dragon knife costs 2,017,800.00 per hour to throw. The average special attack costs 1,345.20.
27158: A mystic robe top (dark) is magic armour that is part of the Mystic robe set worn in the body slot. It comes in blue, light, and dark, but all offer the same bonuses. All mystic robe tops require 40 Magic and 20 Defence to wear. It can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player-owned house.
27159:
A Mystic robe bottom is magic armour that is part of the mystic robe set worn in the legwear slot. All mystic robe bottoms require 40 Magic and 20 Defence to wear.

It can be stored in the magic wardrobe space in a player-owned house.
27160: Mystic robe top (light) from Last Man Standing is a minigame-exclusive variant of the normal Mystic robe top (light). It has no requirements to wear and is a cosmetic option for the Max/Med and Zerker starting loadouts in the minigame.
27161: A mystic robe bottom (light) is magic armour that is part of the mystic robe set worn in the legwear slot. It comes in blue, white, black, and the special enchanted version, but all offer the same bonuses. All mystic robe bottoms require 40 Magic and 20 Defence to wear. It can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player-owned house.
27162:
Wizard boots are magical blue boots. These boots can be obtained from medium Treasure Trails. They require level 20 Magic to wear. They have slightly better stats than mystic boots, but are worse than Infinity boots.

This item can be stored in the treasure chest of a costume room, provided that the interface of the corresponding clue tier is opened before attempting to store the item. Alternatively, the item can be used on the opened treasure chest to insert it without viewing the interface.
27164: Zamorak halo from Last Man Standing is a minigame-exclusive variant of the normal Zamorak halo. It can be obtained from opening the chests with a bloody key, or looting the crates that spawn at random locations on the map. It is dropped on death to whoever killed you.
27165: Saradomin halo from Last Man Standing is a minigame-exclusive variant of the normal Saradomin halo. It can be obtained from opening the chests with a bloody key, or looting the crates that spawn at random locations on the map. It is dropped on death to whoever killed you.
27166:
The ghostly hood is a piece of members only armour worn in the headwear slot. Players can obtain one after speaking to Dhalak during the Curse of the Empty Lord miniquest. The hood has been claimed to serve Dhalak "well over the centuries".

There are no requirements to wear and, when worn with the other pieces, the player appears 'ghostlike' (i.e. transparent). After initially obtaining the piece, the player can talk to any of the ghosts in the same locations you were required to visit to get more pieces. The other two locations per ghost will not work, it must be the one you were required to visit during the miniquest. A lost hood may also be purchased from Perdu for 15,000 coins.

This item can be stored in the magic wardrobe of a costume room, as part of the ghostly robes set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
27169:
The berserker helm is a mid-levelled melee-based helmet. Players must have level 45 Defence and also have completed the quest The Fremennik Trials in order to wear it. It can be purchased from Skulgrimen's Battle Gear shop in Rellekka for 78,000 coins. It's also a possible reward from Barbarian Assault High Gambles or a drop from a dagannoth.

This helmet is favoured among combat pures for being the second lowest level headgear to offer a Strength bonus, which offers the same strength bonus as a helm of Neitiznot and an obsidian helmet.

The berserker helm's defensive bonuses are roughly on par with the rune full helm. More specifically, the berserker helm is slightly better than the rune full helm in both stab and crush defence, but is slightly worse in slash defence.

Skulgrimen's Battle Gear will buy this helmet from a player for 42,000 coins, which is more than the High Level Alchemy price of 36,000 coins.
27170: Infinity boots from Last Man Standing is a minigame-exclusive variant of the normal Infinity boots. It can be obtained from opening the chests with a bloody key, or looting the crates that spawn at random locations on the map. It is dropped on death to whoever killed you.
27171: Tormented bracelet from Last Man Standing is a minigame-exclusive variant of the normal Tormented bracelet. It can be obtained from opening the chests with a bloody key, or looting the crates that spawn at random locations on the map. It is dropped on death to whoever killed you.
27173: Amulet of torture from Last Man Standing is a minigame-exclusive variant of the normal Amulet of torture. It can be obtained from opening the chests with a bloody key, or looting the crates that spawn at random locations on the map. It is dropped on death to whoever killed you.
27174: Elder chaos top from Last Man Standing is a minigame-exclusive variant of the normal Elder chaos top. It can be obtained from opening the chests with a bloody key, or looting the crates that spawn at random locations on the map. It is dropped on death to whoever killed you.
27175:
The elder chaos robe is obtained as a rare drop from Elder Chaos druids. It is part of the elder chaos druid robes set, and requires level 40 in Magic to wear. It can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player-owned house.

Due to the lack of defence requirements to wield, elder chaos druid robes are best-in-slot magic armour for one-defence pures.
27176:
The elder chaos hood is obtained as a rare drop from Elder Chaos druids. It is part of the elder chaos druid robes set, and requires level 40 in Magic to wear. It can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player-owned house.

Due to the lack of defence requirements to wield, elder chaos druid robes are best-in-slot magic armour for one-defence pures.
27177:
A Fremennik kilt is a rare reward from elite Treasure Trails. It has the same bonuses as iron platelegs, except for an additional +1 strength bonus. Unlike most strength bonus providing equipment, it has no requirements to equip.

This item can be stored in the treasure chest of a costume room, provided that the interface of the corresponding clue tier is opened before attempting to store the item. Alternatively, the item can be used on the opened treasure chest to insert it without viewing the interface.
