27179: Rangers' tunic from Last Man Standing is a minigame-exclusive variant of the normal Rangers' tunic. It can be obtained from opening the chests with a bloody key, or looting the crates that spawn at random locations on the map. It is dropped on death to whoever killed you.
27181:
Zamorak chaps are a piece of Zamorak blessed dragonhide armour that require 70 Ranged to equip. It has the same offensive stats as a black dragonhide chaps, except for a +1 prayer bonus, and more defensive bonuses.

Along with other blessed dragonhide armour pieces, it cannot be made using the Crafting skill. Players can receive it as a reward from completing hard Treasure Trails.

This item does give Zamorakian protection within the God Wars Dungeon.

This item can be stored in the treasure chest of a costume room, provided that the interface of the corresponding clue tier is opened before attempting to store the item. Alternatively, the item can be used on the opened treasure chest to insert it without viewing the interface, as part of the Zamorak blessed dragonhide armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
27182: Saradomin chaps from Last Man Standing is a minigame-exclusive variant of the normal Saradomin chaps. It can be obtained only in the 1 Def Pure mode from opening the chests with a bloody key, or looting the crates that spawn at random locations on the map. It is dropped on death to whoever killed you.
27183:
The 3rd Age mage hat is a piece of the 3rd Age mage set worn in the head slot. Requiring level 65 Magic and 30 Defence to wear, it has the highest Magic attack bonus of all mage hats, tied with Virtus mask and ancestral hat. It has a Magic damage bonus of 1%.

The 3rd Age mage hat is a possible reward from hard, elite and master tier Treasure Trails and cannot be made through any skills.

This item can be stored in the treasure chest of a costume room, provided that the interface of the corresponding clue tier is opened before attempting to store the item. Alternatively, the item can be used on the opened treasure chest to insert it without viewing the interface.
27184: Ancient godsword from Last Man Standing is a minigame-exclusive variant of the normal Ancient godsword. It can be obtained from opening the chests with a bloody key, or looting the crates that spawn at random locations on the map. It is dropped on death to whoever killed you.
27185: Rune defender from Last Man Standing is a minigame-exclusive variant of the normal Rune defender. It has no requirements to wield and is part of the Zerker starting loadout in the minigame.
27186:
The Zaryte crossbow is a ranged weapon that requires a Ranged level of 80 to wield, and can fire up to dragon bolts. The crossbow has an attack range of 8, and the longrange combat style will increase it by 2. It is only outclassed by the dragon hunter crossbow when fighting draconic monsters. This item counts as a Zaros item in the God Wars Dungeon.

The crossbow itself is crafted by attaching a nihil horn, obtained as a rare drop from Nex, with an Armadyl crossbow and 250 nihil shards. The Zaryte crossbow counts as a Zarosian item, but not as an Armadylean item in the God Wars Dungeon. In addition, the crossbow possesses a special attack as well as a passive effect, both of which synergise extremely well with the effects of enchanted bolts.

The Zaryte crossbow is primarily used for its special attack, which can deal a guaranteed 110 damage when used with ruby bolts (e) against high-health enemies. Additionally, it is the strongest weapon against non-draconic enemies weak to heavy Ranged attacks, such as the Leviathan.
27187:
The bow of Faerdhinen (c) is a corrupted version of the Bow of Faerdhinen that does not degrade, with its appearance altered to resemble the corrupted crystal seen within the Corrupted Gauntlet. The bow's colours may be changed to other colours of the Elven Clans by buying crystals from Lliann's Wares in Prifddinas, which cost 500,000 coins each. It can also be reverted to its original colour by using the crystal of Hefin on any variant of the corrupted bow.

The bow can be upgraded by bringing it and 2,000 crystal shards to a singing bowl. Doing so requires level 82 Smithing and Crafting (the levels can be boosted), and grants no experience. If the player does not meet the Smithing and Crafting requirements, they can have Conwenna or Reese sing the crystal in their stead for an extra 1,000 crystal shards. Excess charges in the bow will be taken into account; for example, a newly created bow with 10,000 charges will require 1,900 crystal shards to corrupt and a fully charged bow will only cost 1,800 crystal shards to upgrade.

Alternatively, the Bow of Faerdhinen can be corrupted passively through use: every 100 shots fired from the bow contributes 1 shard worth of progress toward the 1,900-shard corruption requirement. Once this cumulative amount is reached, the bow can be corrupted at the singing bowl with the level requirements or have Conwenna corrupt it for you for the 1000 shard price. Any combination of progress towards corruption, charges in the bow, and crystal shards can be used to meet the crystal shard requirement to corrupt the bow.

Upon creating the corrupted bow, the chatbox message states "With the help of the crystal bowl, you sing a dark song which corrupts the crystals."

While untradeable, the bow can be uncharged, but the crystal shards used to upgrade it will not be returned.

Like its regular variant, the bow requires level 80 Ranged and 70 Agility to wield, and provides the highest Ranged Attack and Ranged Strength bonus out of any weapon for its attack speed. It also benefits from damage and accuracy boosts when crystal armour is equipped. Each crystal armour piece equipped grants additional bonus accuracy and damage, adding up to a total 15% damage and 30% accuracy bonus when the full set is equipped.

When using crystal armour, the bow provides similar damage per second to the twisted bow and toxic blowpipe; however, these weapons excel against targets with high Magic level and low Defence respectively. Unlike the twisted bow or toxic blowpipe, the corrupted bow of Faerdhinen suffers no significant drawback and provides consistent performance due to its high accuracy and damage per shot, along with its moderate attack speed, long range, and unlimited ammunition.
27188: The light ballista from Last Man Standing is a minigame-exclusive variant of the normal light ballista. It can be obtained from opening chests with a bloody key or bloodier key, or by looting the crates that spawn at random locations on the map. On death, it is dropped to the player who killed you.
27190:
Verac's brassard from Last Man Standing is a minigame-exclusive variant of the normal Verac's brassard. It can be obtained from opening chests with a bloody key or bloodier key, or by looting the crates that spawn at random locations on the map. On death, it is dropped to the player who killed you. Unlike the normal version of the brassard, the Last Man Standing version does not degrade.

For more details on the mechanics and strategies for this equipment, see the set page.
27191: Unholy book from Last Man Standing is a minigame-exclusive variant of the normal Unholy book. It has no requirements to wield and is a selectable offhand item in the 1 Def Pure starting loadout in the minigame.
27193: The ancestral robe top is obtained as a rare drop from the Chambers of Xeric. It is part of the ancestral robes set, and requires level 75 in Magic and 65 Defence to wear. It can be stored in the magic wardrobe of a player-owned house.
27194: The ancestral robe bottom is obtained as a rare drop from the Chambers of Xeric. It is part of the ancestral robes set, and requires level 75 in Magic and 65 Defence to wear. It can be stored in the magic wardrobe of a player-owned house.
27195:

When equipped, the great helm boosts damage and accuracy by 0.5% when using the crush attack style. In addition, it counts as a Zamorakian item in God Wars Dungeon.

Once belonging to "The Inquisitor", a former Saradominist Justiciar and one of the founders of Slepe, the Inquisitor's armour had remained sealed in the Sisterhood Sanctuary deep beneath Slepe until The Nightmare's arrival unearthed it.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Inquisitor's armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
27196:

27198:
The Inquisitor's mace is a one-handed crush weapon requiring 80 Attack to wield. Received as a drop from The Nightmare, it has bonuses nearly identical to the Ghrazi rapier and blade of Saeldor, acting as the crush variant of these weapons, with an additional +3 Strength bonus and +2 Prayer bonus.

Once belonging to Phosani, a former Saradominist Justiciar and one of the founders of Slepe, the Inquisitor's mace had remained sealed in the Sisterhood Sanctuary deep beneath Slepe until The Nightmare's arrival unearthed it.

The Inquisitor's mace, along with the pieces of Inquisitor's armour, counts as a Zamorakian item in God Wars Dungeon, providing God-related Protection. The mace can be used to train all the combat stats (Attack, Strength, Defence) while on crush whereas most other melee weapons have singular strengths.
27214:
Scarab dung is an item that is dropped by Kephri in the Tombs of Amascut, in which the player receives one if they dealt the most damage to her.

A bucket of water is used on it to obtain the dawn scarab egg, which is part of obtaining the ancient key from the Bank Camel. This requires having used the Camulet on the Bank Camel after completing the miniquest Into the Tombs.
27216:
Fossilised dung is an item that is received when searching the rewards chest within the Tombs of Amascut, only if the player has received fewer than 1,500 total reward points.

Upon using the dung on the nest at the top of the mill in Aldarin, and hopping worlds, a nasty token can be found in its place.
27221:
The big banana is an item that is dropped by Ba-Ba in the Tombs of Amascut, in which the player receives one if they dealt the most damage to her.

It is given to Awowogei after having spoken to the Bank Camel, as part of obtaining the ancient key from them. Doing so requires having completed the miniquest Into the Tombs.
27223:
Eldritch ashes are Akkha's remains that can be obtained in the Tombs of Amascut; to obtain it, the player has to deal the most damage to him.

It is given to the High Priest of Sophanem after having spoken to the Bank Camel, as part of obtaining the ancient key from them. Doing so requires having completed the miniquest Into the Tombs.
27229:
The Masori body is obtained as a rare drop from the Tombs of Amascut. It is part of the Masori armour set, and requires level 80 Ranged and 30 Defence to equip. As with the rest of the armour set, the body boasts the highest ranged attack bonus of any item in the body slot.

The body can be upgraded into a fortified variant by attaching four Armadylean plates onto it, increasing the Defence level to equip it to level 80. This process requires level 90 Crafting, and is irreversible.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Masori armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
27238:
The fortified Masori body is an upgraded variant of the Masori body. It is created by combining a Masori body with four Armadylean plates. This process requires level 90 Crafting, and is not reversible.

Part of the Masori armour set, the fortified body requires level 80 Ranged and Defence to equip, and boasts increased defence bonuses and a +1 prayer bonus in comparison to the standard variant.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Masori armour (fortified) set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
27255:
The Menaphite ornament kit is an ornament kit that can be used on Elidinis' ward (f) to create Elidinis' ward (or), which alters its appearance. It is solely a cosmetic upgrade and does not change its stats.

In order to receive one from the reward chest, players must complete a raid at level 425 (or higher) with zero deaths for all party members.

Despite having a high alchemy value of 60,000 coins, Menaphite ornament kits cannot be alched.
27257:
Icthlarin's shroud (tier 1) is a cosmetic cape that can be obtained by searching the chest across from the Grouping Obelisk in the main lobby after completing 100 Tombs of Amascut raids in Normal/Expert Mode.

Players can use the right-click "Change" option to alter the cape's appearance to other tiers, providing that they have met the completion count required for them.

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room.
27265:
Icthlarin's shroud (tier 5) is a cosmetic cape that can be obtained by searching the chest across from the Grouping Obelisk in the main lobby after completing 2,000 Tombs of Amascut raids in Normal/Expert Mode.

Players can use the right-click "Change" option to alter the cape's appearance to other tiers, providing that they have met the completion count required for them.

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room.
27267: Icthlarin's hood (tier 5) is a hood that can be obtained by searching the chest across from the Grouping Obelisk in the main lobby after completing 2,000 Tombs of Amascut raids in Normal/Expert Mode.
27272: Lily of the Sands is an item that can be obtained as a reward from the Tombs of Amascut. They are used to create Menaphite remedies at 88 Herblore by using them on an unfinished dwarf weed potion.
27275:
Tumeken's shadow is a two-handed powered staff requiring 85 Magic to wield, and is only available as a rare drop from the Tombs of Amascut. The staff is extremely valuable as, when matched with other high-end magic gear, it excels with its damage and immense accuracy even against magic-resistant monsters. Like most powered staves, it is only tradeable when it is fully uncharged.

Powered by the sun itself, the staff was created by the god Tumeken using an unknown artefact during the Kharidian–Zarosian War as a means to fight back against the invading force of the Zarosian Empire. Tumeken also used it to create Tumeken's Warden and Elidinis' Warden, two massive automata imbued with the divine essence of himself and his wife Elidinis. After Tumeken sacrificed himself to end the war, Elidinis gifted the weapon as well as her own ward to Osmumten before leaving to mourn her family.

As with all powered staves other than Thammaron's sceptre and the accursed sceptre, Tumeken's shadow is not able to use its built-in spell against other players outside of minigames.

27279:
The thread of Elidinis is an uncommon reward from the rewards chest within the Tombs of Amascut. Players with 75 Crafting[boostable] can use the thread on a rune pouch with a needle in their inventory to create a divine rune pouch, which can store four types of runes instead of three. This process can be reversed to return both items.

The base rate of receiving the thread is 1/10. To mitigate bad luck, the rate is scaled linearly with the number of raid completions, up to a maximum of 3/10 upon completing 15 raids. Once the player gets their first thread, the drop rate is decreased to 1/50. Additionally, players can buy the thread from Perdu for 350,000 coins if they have obtained it from the Tombs of Amascut at least once.

Note: This item is destroyed on death.
27281:
The divine rune pouch is an upgraded variant of the rune pouch, which holds four types of runes instead of three. Each rune can be stacked up to 16,000, the same as a normal rune pouch. The pouch is made by using a needle or costume needle to stitch together a thread of Elidinis and the rune pouch, which requires level 75 Crafting to do; boosts will work.

The pouch can be reverted to its base components, returning the thread and pouch. When reverting the pouch, if the player has a rune in the 4th slot they will be warned all of the runes in that slot will be lost, even if there are only 3 unique runes in the pouch. If players die to other players while carrying a divine rune pouch in the Wilderness or in a PvP world, they will lose it, unless it has been locked via use of a trouver parchment. It should be noted that the Trouver parchment does not protect runes stored within a Divine rune pouch upon death.
27283:
The Breach of the Scarab is an untradeable jewel that can be obtained as a reward from the Tombs of Amascut.

The jewel can be attached to the Keris partisan to create the Keris partisan of breaching, providing a 33% accuracy boost against all Kalphites and Scabarites.

Unlike the other three jeweled Keris partisans, the Keris partisan of breaching's passive effect can be used outside the Tombs of Amascut.
27285:
The Eye of the Corruptor is an untradeable jewel that can be obtained as a reward from the Tombs of Amascut.

The jewel can be attached to the Keris partisan to create the Keris partisan of corruption, whose special attack can only be used within the Tombs of Amascut.
27287:
The keris partisan of corruption is a one-handed spear requiring 80 Attack to equip. It is made by attaching the Eye of the Corruptor on the keris partisan, granting it a special attack which can only be used within the Tombs of Amascut raid. As with the keris partisan, weapon poisons cannot be applied to the partisan.

The keris partisan of corruption retains the effects of the keris partisan, dealing 33% bonus damage against all kalphites and scabarites, alongside a 1/51 chance of finding a gap in their exoskeleton, dealing triple damage. When this special effect occurs, the chatbox will display the message: You slip your weapon through a gap in the creature's chitin, landing a vicious blow.
27291:
The keris partisan of the sun is a one-handed spear requiring 80 Attack to equip. It is made by attaching the jewel of the sun to the keris partisan, granting it a special attack and two unique passive effects that only apply within the Tombs of Amascut raid:

providing a 25% increase to accuracy for targets with less than 25% health

healing the player for 12 Hitpoints upon killing a target at the cost of 5 prayer points; this effect can overheal players up to 12 Hitpoints above their base Hitpoints level

The keris partisan of the sun retains the effects of the keris partisan, dealing 33% bonus damage against all kalphites and scabarites, alongside a 1/51 chance of puncturing a hole in their exoskeleton, dealing triple damage. When this special effect occurs, the chatbox will display the message: You slip your weapon through a gap in the creature's chitin, landing a vicious blow.

As with the keris partisan, weapon poisons cannot be applied to the partisan.
27295: A water container can be found in a crate when sailing to Ungael during Dragon Slayer II. It is used to douse fires that appear on the Fremennik ship. It doesn't need to be refilled and has unlimited uses.
27296: A mirror is used in the Nature Spirit quest to prove to Filliman Tarlock that he is dead. It can be found under the washing bowl on a bench near the entrance to the Nature Grotto south of the Mort Myre Swamp. It is also obtainable after the quest, but it serves no purpose.
27297: Neutralising potions are an item obtained in the Path of Apmeken within the Tombs of Amascut. They are poured into the holes in the floor indicated by Apmeken's Sight to neutralise the dangerous fumes that can damage players if left unchecked. In groups, they are also used to cleanse a player of corruption in the challenge room.
27298:
Maisa's message is given to the player by a messenger, who appears to players who've completed the Beneath Cursed Sands quest prior to 24 August 2022, indicating the beginning of the Into the Tombs miniquest.

Players who've completed Beneath Cursed Sands after 24 August 2022 will simply be able to begin the miniquest by entering the Jaltevas Pyramid, and thus cannot ever obtain Maisa's message.
27299:
Antique lamps are rewards from quests, achievement diaries and the Varrock Museum miniquest. Like regular lamps, these lamps grant a player experience in a chosen skill, and the skill chosen must usually be over a certain level which is unboostable.

Lamps that are not included in the three items kept on death will be kept inside your death's coffer, if not deleted.
27300:
Akila's journal is a journal belonging to Akila, and is obtained from Maisa in the Tombs of Amascut raid lobby upon beginning the miniquest Into the Tombs.

The book can be reobtained by searching a crate in the Jaltevas Pyramid, or the bookcases in a player-owned house if the player has previously read the book.
27302:
Het's capture is a book dropped by Akkha upon defeating him in the Tombs of Amascut. Written by Akila, the book details how Amascut captured Het, one of the four lesser gods of the Menaphite Pantheon.

The book can be stored in and retrieved from the bookcase in a player-owned house.
27304:
Apmeken's capture is a book dropped by Ba-Ba upon defeating her in the Tombs of Amascut. Written by Akila, the book details how Amascut captured Apmeken, one of the four lesser gods of the Menaphite Pantheon.

The book can be stored in and retrieved from the bookcase in a player-owned house.
27306:
Scabaras' capture is a book dropped by Kephri upon defeating her in the Tombs of Amascut. Written by Akila, the book details how Amascut captured Scabaras, one of the four lesser gods of the Menaphite Pantheon.

The book can be stored in and retrieved from the bookcase in a player-owned house.
27308:
Crondis' capture is a book dropped by Zebak upon defeating him in the Tombs of Amascut. Written by Akila, the book details how Amascut captured Crondis, one of the four lesser gods of the Menaphite Pantheon.

The book can be stored in and retrieved from the bookcase in a player-owned house.
27310:
The wardens is a book dropped by either Tumeken's Warden or Elidinis' Warden upon defeating them in the Tombs of Amascut. Written by Akila, the book details the divine weapons that Amascut came for in Osmumten's tomb.

The book can be stored in and retrieved from the bookcase in a player-owned house.
27312:
The jackal's torch is a book found by searching the bags in the western end of Osmumten's burial chamber adjacent to the strange tablet, after defeating Tumeken's Warden and Elidinis' Warden in the Tombs of Amascut.

The book details a story of Icthlarin in the Grim Underworld, taking place some time during the Second Age.
27323:

Applying it will heal players by 5 hitpoints every 5 ticks (3 seconds) 20 times, for a total healing amount of 100 hitpoints over 100 ticks (60 seconds), and can boost the player's hitpoints up to 5 above their maximum.

As silk dressing is considered as a food item, it cannot be obtained if the "On a Diet" invocation is enabled.

Smelling salts is an item that can be obtained from the supplies bag within the Tombs of Amascut. It starts with 2 uses.

Crushing it will repeatedly restore run energy by 25% and boost the player's combat stats every 15 seconds over the course of 8 minutes, akin to an Overload, though without drawbacks.

27347:
Ambrosia is an item that can be obtained from the supplies bag within the Tombs of Amascut. Drinking it will completely restore and boost Hitpoints and Prayer, as well as replenish run energy. In addition, it also acts as a dose of antidote++ (curing venom and poison, while providing immunity to them for 36 seconds and 12 minutes respectively).

Ambrosia is a strong emergency item due to the benefits it provides in one click. It is recommended to use this item as a last resort when hitpoints, prayer, and energy are as low as possible to maximise the benefit obtained from it.

27352:
Tumeken's Guardian is a pet that can be obtained from completing the Tombs of Amascut. It is a much smaller version of Tumeken's Warden. Players have a chance of receiving the pet when looting the reward chest in the burial chamber. It is possible for it to be obtained in Entry mode, although at a much lower rate.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.
27355:
Masori armour set (f) is an item obtained by exchanging a set of items with a Grand Exchange clerk via their right-click "Sets" option and clicking on the appropriate item set within the Item Sets interface.

It is commonly made in order to conveniently sell all three components of the fortified Masori armour at once.
27358:
The tome of fire is a book held in place of a shield that is a possible reward from the reward cart upon subduing the Wintertodt. The tome of fire requires level 50 in Magic to wield.

The tome is only tradeable when empty. When it is empty, its only function is its magic attack and magic defence equipment bonuses.

Empty tomes can be traded in for 250 burnt pages per tome (value of 1,640,750) by speaking to Ignisia.

This item counts as a warm item at the Wintertodt.

If lost to another player in a dangerous PVP death, all charges inside will be converted into pages and dropped for the killer alongside the empty tome.
27359:
The Masori assembler is a cosmetic variant of Ava's assembler with a Masori crafting kit added to it. The assembler's colours are based on that of the Masori armour.

The assembler can also be combined with the max cape to change its appearance further by turning it into the Masori assembler max cape. A needle is required in order to create and dismantle the Masori assembler.

If the player dies a PvP death and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 240,000 coins. The Masori crafting kit will be placed in their gravestone.
27361:
The Masori assembler max cape is the result of combining a Masori assembler with a max cape, or by using a Masori crafting kit on an Assembler max cape, during which the max hood required to be in the player's inventory will automatically convert to the Masori assembler max hood.

Like the other max cape variants (a max cape combined with another cape slot item), the Masori assembler max cape does not have the max cape's stats or perks; it only acts as a cosmetic upgrade to Ava's assembler with the following exceptions when worn:

It acts as a Cooking cape to allow access to the Cooks' Guild without a chef's hat, golden chef's hat, Varrock armour 3 or 4

It acts as a Crafting cape to allow access to the Crafting Guild without a brown apron or golden apron

It acts as a Runecraft cape to prevent essence pouches from degrading (but does not allow access to runic altars)

It acts as a Firemaking cape to work as a piece of warm clothing

It can be used to perform the Skill Cape emote.

The max cape and masori assembler can be separated by using a knife on the cape. Mac will also buy back a max cape, along with its variants, for 1,900,800 coins each. He will return the secondary item any max cape variant was combined with upon doing so.

If the player dies a PvP death and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 240,000 coins. The Masori crafting kit will be placed in their gravestone.

The Masori assembler max cape is the result of combining a Masori assembler with a max cape, or by using a Masori crafting kit on an Assembler max cape, during which the max hood required to be in the player's inventory will automatically convert to the Masori assembler max hood.

Like the other max cape variants (a max cape combined with another cape slot item), the Masori assembler max cape does not have the max cape's stats or perks; it only acts as a cosmetic upgrade to Ava's assembler with the following exceptions when worn:

It acts as a Cooking cape to allow access to the Cooks' Guild without a chef's hat, golden chef's hat, Varrock armour 3 or 4

It acts as a Crafting cape to allow access to the Crafting Guild without a brown apron or golden apron

It acts as a Runecraft cape to prevent essence pouches from degrading (but does not allow access to runic altars)

It acts as a Firemaking cape to work as a piece of warm clothing

It can be used to perform the Skill Cape emote.

The max cape and masori assembler can be separated by using a knife on the cape. Mac will also buy back a max cape, along with its variants, for 1,900,800 coins each. He will return the secondary item any max cape variant was combined with upon doing so.

If the player dies a PvP death and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 240,000 coins. The Masori crafting kit will be placed in their gravestone.

In order to receive one from the reward chest, players must complete a raid at level 450+ with zero deaths for all party members, whilst having all invocations for Akkha enabled. Furthermore, players must defeat him at path level 4 or higher.
27386:
Tumeken's Guardian is a pet that can be obtained from completing the Tombs of Amascut. It is a much smaller version of Tumeken's Warden. Players have a chance of receiving the pet when looting the reward chest in the burial chamber. It is possible for it to be obtained in Entry mode, although at a much lower rate.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.

27416:
The speedy teleport scroll is a consumable item purchased for 600 Quest Speedrunning reward points from the Speedrunning Reward Shop, and can be freely reclaimed once purchased. It can be used to unlock a speedrunning-themed Home Teleport animation override. To enable it, players can right click "Animation" on the Home Teleport spell icon in their spellbook and select "Speedy". The speedy home teleport is slightly faster than other home teleport animation overrides, which results in a casting time of only 18 ticks (10.8 seconds) as opposed to the standard 24 ticks (14.4 seconds).

When the player reads the scroll, the chatbox message states This scroll details an incantation which unlocks the Speedy Home Teleport animation. Would you like to learn the incantation? This will consume the scroll.

If a player reads the scroll while already having unlocked the animation, the chatbox message will state This scroll details an incantation which unlocks the Speedy Home Teleport animation. However, you have already unlocked this animation.

The bronze speedrun trophy is an item that can be claimed from Eliza by beating the bronze speedrun time for all available quests in the Quest Speedrunning game mode.

Should a new quest be released for speedrunning, the trophy will be unequipped and the player cannot equip it until the new quest is completed. If the player's inventory is full, the trophy will be banked instead. If the player's inventory and bank are full, the trophy will be destroyed, with the chatbox message appearing upon logging in: "Some new quests have been made available on Speedrunning Worlds. As such, the Speedrun Trophy you had equipped has been destroyed. You can obtain another from Eliza in Varrock Square."

The divine rune pouch is an upgraded variant of the rune pouch, which holds four types of runes instead of three. Each rune can be stacked up to 16,000, the same as a normal rune pouch. The pouch is made by using a needle or costume needle to stitch together a thread of Elidinis and the rune pouch, which requires level 75 Crafting to do; boosts will work.

The pouch can be reverted to its base components, returning the thread and pouch. When reverting the pouch, if the player has a rune in the 4th slot they will be warned all of the runes in that slot will be lost, even if there are only 3 unique runes in the pouch. If players die to other players while carrying a divine rune pouch in the Wilderness or in a PvP world, they will lose it, unless it has been locked via use of a trouver parchment. It should be noted that the Trouver parchment does not protect runes stored within a Divine rune pouch upon death.
27511:
Kasonde's journal is an item found by searching the tent east of the large chasm at the southern end of the Kebos Lowlands. Receiving the journal begins The Garden of Death quest.

Written by Kasonde Shaw, the journal tells about a group named the Old Ones, who were once an ancient race that inhabited what is today the Kingdom of Varlamore, and suggests lizardmen architecture was derived from those of the Old Ones.

The notes can be stored in and retrieved from the bookcase in a player-owned house.
27513: Word translations is an item obtained during The Garden of Death by reading the stone tablet in the dungeon south-east of Mount Quidamortem.
27515: Dirty notes are items obtained throughout the dungeons visited during The Garden of Death. They are written by Kasonde Shaw.

27519:
Stone tablets are items obtained during The Garden of Death, where players find them throughout the dungeons built by the Old Ones, an ancient race who inhabited modern-day Varlamore.

The tablets can be read, and are automatically translated as players find new translations during and after the quest via the word translations scroll. When read, translated words in blue indicate that the word is incorrect in context, whilst words in green indicate the word is correct in context.

The only untranslatable phrase is "Zema-Tal" in the last tablet found. Though players infer "Tal" to mean life or soul, "Zema" is not translatable during the quest, but is instead revealed during The Heart of Darkness to mean together, people, and one. With the context of both words and the discovery of the Stranglewood during Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire, one possible meaning of Zema-Tal may be what the Old Ones called themselves (ex. Zema-Tal tepat -> We [the Old Ones are] destroyed).

27544:
Ghommal's lucky penny is an item equipped in the ammunition slot, obtained from Ghommal or Laidee Gnonock after claiming the master tier rewards from the Combat Achievements system.

When equipped, it offers a 5% chance to not use a charge when using items that consume charges (such as jewellery and weapons). When equipped in conjunction with an elven or celestial signet, both items will roll independently at a chance to not use a charge while using a piece of crystal equipment.

If you drop down to the elite tier from the master tier, the item is not deleted, but it cannot be equipped until the master tier is unlocked again. Attempting to equip it without having the master tier displays the message You need to have unlocked the Master tier of Combat Achievement rewards to use this item..

27590:
Muphin is a pet dropped by the Phantom Muspah, and is a much smaller version of it. Players can right click "Metamorphosis" to change between its ranged, melee, and shielded forms, providing they have used a charged ice on it to unlock the latter two forms.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed.

However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.

The pet uses routefinding when following the player; as such, it will path around obstacles to reach the player rather than getting stuck like most other pets.

27610:
The venator bow is a two-handed ranged weapon that was once used by the venators, who were hunters and scouts that served the Zarosian Empire. Requiring level 80 in Ranged to wield, it is made by combining five venator shards. It can fire any type of arrow, including dragon arrows, and has an attack range of 6 (8 when using the "Longrange" combat style).

The bow can be charged with ancient essence to gain a unique passive effect that consumes charges, although the uncharged version can still be used as a regular bow. The passive effect enables the bow to be used against multiple targets with one attack, with the arrow bouncing up to two other nearby monsters.

27614:
The Venator shard is a drop received from defeating the Phantom Muspah. Five shards are combined to create the Venator bow.

Players can break down venator shards using a pestle and mortar to receive 50,000 ancient essence, resulting in a loss of −12,142,272.
27616:
Ancient essence is a drop received from defeating the Phantom Muspah. It can also be obtained by mining ancient essence crystals in the Ghorrock Dungeon with 75 Mining, granting 13.5 Mining experience. It is used to create the saturated heart and forgotten brews. It is also used to charge the Venator bow to use its passive effect.

Ancient essence can also be obtained by breaking down ancient icons and venator shards. Ancient icons give 5,000 essence, while venator shards give 50,000 essence.

A total of 150,000 Ancient essence is required to saturate the Imbued heart into a Saturated heart.

When mining the essence, it can be found in one of 3 spots in the wall just south of the entrance to the Phantom Muspah fight. Only one spot will be active, switching between spots randomly with possibly 60 to 90 seconds between each movement, similar to daeyalt essence rocks. Gems can also be obtained while mining, as is the case with most mines.

Mining enhancers have no effect on crystals, however, the Crystal pickaxe's effect does, therefore mining crystals with a charged crystal pickaxe will consume charges.

The currently known rates are as follows:

At 75-77 Mining, 1-2 essence per ore mined

At 78-89 Mining, 2-3 essence per ore mined

At 90-99 Mining, 3-4 essence per ore mined

Players can expect roughly 1200-2500 essence per hour depending on mining level and type of pickaxe used. Invisible boosts such as Celestial ring will not increase the minimum amount of essence mined.
27624:
The ancient sceptre is an upgraded version of the Ancient staff that requires level 70 Magic, 60 Strength, 50 Attack, as well as completion of Secrets of the North to wield. It is made by bringing the untradeable Ancient icon and staff to Eblis. This combination process is irreversible.

The ancient sceptre, like its predecessor, can be used to autocast spells from the Ancient Magicks and standard spellbook. Unlike the ancient staff, the ancient sceptre provides a 10% Magic damage bonus, as well as a passive effect that increases the effects of Ancient Magicks by 10%. This passive effect does not increase the Magic damage bonus.

As a Zarosian item, it will also grant god protection towards Zarosian NPCs in the God Wars Dungeon.

If the player dies a PvP death and the item is unprotected, it is reverted to an ancient staff that is dropped for the killer, and the ancient icon disappears. To prevent this, a Trouver parchment and a payment of 500,000 coins can be given to Perdu in order to permanently lock the item. The locked item will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a mangled, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 500,000 coins.

The ancient icon is an untradeable drop received from defeating the Phantom Muspah, who can be fought upon completion of Secrets of the North. It can be brought to Eblis alongside the ancient staff to upgrade it to the ancient sceptre. This process is irreversible and the sceptre is untradeable.

27643:
Charged ice is a tertiary drop from the Phantom Muspah, guaranteed as a drop if it is killed in under three minutes. It is used on a Muphin to allow it to metamorphose into its melee and shielded forms. Once used on Muphin, it cannot be obtained again, even if the player gets another kill under three minutes.

One way to quicken kill times is to use only a crossbow, relying on the effects of enchanted ruby bolts during its melee and ranged phases, enchanted sapphire bolts during its shielded phase, and enchanted diamond bolts for its post-shield phase. A Zaryte crossbow or Armadyl crossbow is recommended for this, due to their special attacks affecting enchanted bolts (the Zaryte crossbow guarantees activation and passively strengthens its effects, while the Armadyl crossbow doubles base chance of activation). Players who can afford both a tumeken's shadow and twisted bow can easily make the time without having to rely on bolt activation.

Although valued at 10,000, the charged ice's clan loot broadcast values it at 500,000.
27645:
The mystic cards are an equipable set of cards obtained by redeeming the code v1r354cqu1r173und0 from Diango in Draynor Village, via the right-click "Redeem-code" option.

The cards are awarded upon completing the final step of the Runestone Basalt ARG clue-hunting event, which was released alongside the launch of the Shattered Relics League. The appearance of the mystic cards is styled after the tarot cards that could be found perched on the three runestone basalt pillars during that league, which would instantly fade away once interacted with. Diango's dialogue upon redeeming the code implies that The Sage gave him the mystic cards to hold until someone completed the event.

It is one of only four melee weapons with an attack speed of 3, with the other ones being the goblin paint cannon, swift blade, and ham joint, with the former two being two handed weapons only, and the latter two being one-handed weapons that may be equipped along with a shield-slot item. The swift blade also exclusively uses Stab and Slash attack styles whereas the others use Crush, and the mystic cards have negative combat stat bonuses whereas the others have no bonuses.

For this reason, it is a purely cosmetic item and cannot be used to train any melee combat skills. For that, players are forced to choose from the previously mentioned crush-based two-handed goblin paint cannon, or crush-based single-handed ham joint. If a stab or slash-weapon is needed then the one-handed swift blade may be used instead.

Whilst having the Mystic cards equipped, other players will have a right-click "Duel" option listed in their right-click choose option menu. Doing this will result in the player throwing a card towards the target, though of course this deals no damage.

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room.

The accursed sceptre is a powered staff requiring 70 Magic to wield. It is a direct upgrade of Thammaron's sceptre, made with level 85 Crafting by using the Skull of Vet'ion on the Thammaron's sceptre (note that this process is reversible). Players without the required level to combine the items may ask Phabelle Bile in Ferox Enclave to do so instead, for a fee of 500,000 coins. The item counts as a Zamorakian item in the God Wars Dungeon. Like most powered staves, it is only tradeable when it is fully uncharged.

Compared to Thammaron's sceptre, the accursed sceptre has a higher max hit (usually +1 or +2 higher, depending on gear), +7 extra magic accuracy, and a unique special attack.

The sceptre also has a "Swap" option that allows players to switch it to an accursed sceptre (a), which is a variant that can autocast offensive combat spells from the standard spellbook (including Flames of Zamorak) and the Ancient Magicks.

The Voidwaker is a melee weapon that requires level 75 Attack to wield. It is acquired by providing the Voidwaker blade, hilt, and gem to Madam Sikaro in the Ferox Enclave Dungeon, who will reassemble the weapon for a fee of 500,000 coins. The three parts are obtained separately as rare drops from Vet'ion, Callisto, and Venenatis (or their lesser counterparts) respectively. Its base stats are roughly comparable to an abyssal whip, and it has one of the most powerful damaging special attacks of any weapon in the game.

Attempting to combine the pieces on your own displays the message You don't think you have the skills to reassemble this weapon yourself..

Mineral pack, an item purchased from the Void Knights' Reward Options.
27695:
A broken dragon pickaxe is a rare loot from opening ore packs from the Volcanic Mine reward shop.

It can be repaired back to a dragon pickaxe by speaking to Nurmof in the Dwarven Mine, for a fee of 2,500,000 coins. Repairing a broken dragon pickaxe does not increase the count for a collection log slot for a dragon pickaxe.

Although it has a 'Wield' option, it is not wieldable; this option instead prompts the dialogue: I should get this repaired before I try and use it. Maybe Petrified Pete will know someone who can help.

When receiving the pickaxe from an ore pack, the message You find something unexpected in the ore pack... it's a broken pickaxe! will be displayed.
27697:
A crystal body is a piece of crystal armour requiring 70 Defence and 50 Agility to equip. When equipped, a 7.5% damage bonus and 15% accuracy bonus is applied to the crystal bow or Bow of Faerdhinen when either is equipped. This bonus stacks additively with the crystal legs and crystal helm's bonuses, for a total of 15% damage and 30% accuracy. The bonus also stacks with the slayer helmet (i) and is useful for bosses similar to the Abyssal Sire.

Players can create a crystal body via a singing bowl by combining 150 crystal shards and three crystal armour seeds. Doing so requires level 74 Smithing and Crafting to sing the crystal (the levels can be boosted), and grants 7,500 experience in both skills. Players can configure the charges while the crystal body is in their bank by right-clicking on Configure-Charges, as long as players have the required materials. If the player does not meet the Smithing and Crafting requirements, they can have Conwenna or Reese sing the crystal for them for an extra 60 crystal shards, for a total of 210.

The body's colours may also be changed to other colours of the Elven Clans by buying crystals from Lliann's Wares in Prifddinas, which cost 500,000 coins each. It can also be reverted to its original colour by using the crystal of Meilyr on any variant of the body.

If lost to another player in a dangerous PVP death, the crystal body will revert to 3 crystal armour seeds, which will then be dropped for the killer. All crystal shards will be lost should this happen. If the crystal body is protected on death, the body will be kept, and will not lose any charges- similar to a blowpipe or trident.

When combined with an imbued slayer helmet, the damage bonus from crystal armour pieces is multiplied by the 15% ranged damage boost from the helmet. Assuming players are wearing both the crystal body and legs, this results in a damage bonus of approximately 29.375%.

27783:
The diamond speedrun trophy is an item that can be claimed from Eliza by beating the diamond speedrun time for all available quests in the Quest Speedrunning game mode. When equipped, the trophy can be right-clicked to perform the Trophy Emote.

Should a new quest be released for speedrunning, the trophy will be unequipped and the player cannot equip it until the new quest is completed. If the player's inventory is full, the trophy will be banked instead. If the player's inventory and bank are full, the trophy will be destroyed, with the chatbox message appearing upon logging in: "Some new quests have been made available on Speedrunning Worlds. As such, the Speedrun Trophy you had equipped has been destroyed. You can obtain another from Eliza in Varrock Square."
27785:
Thammaron's sceptre (a) is the autocasting variant of Thammaron's sceptre, requiring level 60 in Magic to wield.

By selecting the "Swap" option on the sceptre, players can switch between the regular sceptre (a powered staff) and the autocasting sceptre, which can autocast offensive combat spells from the standard spellbook (including Flames of Zamorak) and the Ancient Magicks.

27790:
Nightshade, also known as belladonna, is a stackable variant of cave nightshade that can be harvested from the Draynor Manor and Auburnvale belladonna patches after planting belladonna seeds. It is used in Herblore to make weapon poison(++) or as an addition to dynamite for poison dynamite.

Players can eat nightshade, but this is not recommended in most situations. When eaten, the player will say, "Ahhhh! What have I done!" in a dialogue box, and take up to 15 damage (damage taken scales with the player's current Hitpoints). Additionally, the message You eat the nightshade...

The nightshade was highly poisonous. will be displayed. Like most self-damaging items, it is impossible for the player to kill themselves with it. (Note: It is possible for players to eat this without losing health; if the player were to accidentally eat the nightshade, they can teleport away to avoid losing any hitpoints, provided they don't click "Continue" on the dialogue text.)

Damage taken is given by the following formula:

Damage(Hitpoints)={15,if Hitpoints≥20⌊Hitpoints2⌋if Hitpoints<20

Vesta's chainbody (bh) is a piece of armour requiring 78 Defence to wear, and is purchased from the Bounty Hunter Store for 600 Bounty Hunter points. When worn alongside Vesta's plateskirt (bh), the accuracy of melee special attacks are increased by 15%. It can be converted into its corrupted variant by speaking to a Corrupted Warrior.

As with all Ancient Warriors' equipment from Bounty Hunter, it is initially purchased in inactive form and must be charged with 5,000,000 coins before it can be used by the player. In addition, it can only be used within Daimon's Crater, Castle Wars, Clan Wars, Soul Wars, the TzHaar Fight Pit, and both the player-owned house and Clan Hall combat rings; attempting to attack anything outside the listed areas will result in the player being interrupted from doing so.

Upon dying in PvP, the coins used to activate the item are given to the killer, and players are left with the inactive variant.

27853:
The dark bow (bh) is a two-handed ranged weapon that requires level 60 in Ranged to wield. It is created by using a dark bow imbue scroll on a dark bow, which is purchased as a reward from Bounty Hunter.

The imbued bow has +105 Ranged attack, instead of the regular bow's +95. In addition, the minimum hit from the special attack is increased from 5 to 7 for non-dragon arrows, and from 8 to 10 for dragon arrows. The special attack's damage also rolls between the minimum and maximum damage, rather than zero to max.

In addition, it can only be used within Daimon's Crater, Castle Wars, Clan Wars, Soul Wars, the TzHaar Fight Pit, and both the player-owned house and Clan Hall combat rings; attempting to attack anything outside the listed areas will result in the player being interrupted from doing so.

If the player dies in Bounty Hunter with the item, the imbue scroll is kept, but the weapon is lost.
27855:
The Barrelchest anchor (bh) is a two-handed weapon that requires level 50 Attack and 40 Strength to wield. It is created by using a Barrelchest anchor imbue scroll on the Barrelchest anchor, which is purchased as a reward from Bounty Hunter.

In comparison to the regular anchor, the imbued anchor has a +10 increased crush and strength bonus, and a +15% increase to the special attack's damage. The Attack level requirement to equip it is also 10 levels lower than the regular anchor.

In addition, it can only be used within Daimon's Crater, Castle Wars, Clan Wars, Soul Wars, the TzHaar Fight Pit, and both the player-owned house and Clan Hall combat rings; attempting to attack anything outside the listed areas will result in the player being interrupted from doing so.

If the player dies in Bounty Hunter with the item, the imbue scroll is kept, but the weapon is lost.

27870:
The Lightbearer is a ring obtained as a rare reward from the Tombs of Amascut. The ring was crafted by the warrior Ahmek from the unstable energy left behind from Tumeken's sacrifice that ended the Kharidian–Zarosian War.

The ring has no requirements to wear. It regenerates the player's special attack energy twice as fast at 15 seconds per 10%, or 2 minutes and 30 seconds for 100%. Equipping the ring will cause the special attack energy restoration timer to reset only if natural regeneration is below half. Unequipping the ring will always cause the special attack energy restoration timer to reset.

28067:
The fighter torso (or) is a cosmetic variant of the fighter torso with a bounty hunter ornament kit added to it.

If the player dies a PvP death at level 20 Wilderness or below and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 150,000 coins. The ornament kit will be placed in their gravestone.

If the player dies a PvP death above level 20 Wilderness and the item is unprotected, it will be converted to coins. To prevent this, a Trouver parchment and a payment of 500,000 coins can be given to Perdu in order to permanently lock the item. The locked item will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a mangled, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 500,000 coins. The ornament kit will be placed in their gravestone.

Unlike its base variant, it cannot be stored in the storage space of a costume room.

28116:
The rainbow jumper is an event item unlocked by speaking to Gilbert in the flower field south-east of Barbarian Village, after which it can be obtained from Diango or retrieved from a toy box built in the costume room. It was originally received as a reward for completing the 2023 Pride event.

There are nine unique versions of the jumper representing different variants of sexual orientation or gender identity, whose colours can be changed at any time by right-clicking the "Change" option on the jumper. When switched to another style other than the pride (rainbow) style, the item is renamed to a colourful jumper.
28126: The poet's jacket is an event item unlocked by speaking to Gilbert in the flower field south-east of Barbarian Village, after which it can be obtained from Diango or retrieved from a toy box built in the costume room. It was originally received as a reward for completing the 2023 Pride event.
28128:
The love crossbow is a fun weapon unlocked by speaking to Gilbert in the flower field south-east of Barbarian Village, after which it can be obtained from Diango or retrieved from a toy box built in the costume room. It was originally received as a reward for completing the 2023 Pride event.

Despite resembling a crossbow, it is in fact a two-handed melee weapon, and as such cannot be used to fire bolts or mith grapples. Like the goblin paint cannon, ham joint, swift blade, and mystic cards, the love crossbow is one of the few melee weapons to possess an attack speed of 3. However, due to hefty offensive penalties similar to those of the mystic cards, it is not advised to train with it.

Whilst having the crossbow equipped, other players will have a right-click "Enamour" option listed in their choose option menu. Doing this will result in the player firing a "love" bolt towards the target, causing hearts to appear around the player and their target. This deals no damage, and can only be done if the target is at least one tile away from the player.
28132:
The dusty lamp is an item obtained from the Strange Old Man after completing the miniquest His Faithful Servants. It grants 20,000 Prayer experience when rubbed; there is no minimum Prayer level required to use it.

The lamp cannot be banked. However, if the player prefers to use it at a later date, it can be destroyed and reclaimed from the Strange Old Man whenever the player wishes to do so.
28133:
The crypt map is an item obtained from the Strange Old Man after completing the miniquest His Faithful Servants.

The "Study" option on the item will permanently reveal the minimap whilst inside the Barrows crypt. After this, the crypt map is destroyed.
28140:
A log basket is an item that allows players to store a combined total of 28 logs of any type. The basket can be purchased from the Forestry Shop for 300 noted oak logs, 300 noted willow logs, and 5,000 anima-infused bark. Players (excluding Ultimate Ironmen) can sell the basket back to the rewards shop for an 80% return of the cost to purchase. The basket must be closed before being sold back.

This item can be stored in the magic wardrobe of a costume room.
28146:
The log brace is an item purchased from the Forestry Shop for 3,000 anima-infused bark, as well as 300 noted maple and yew logs. These logs can be bought on the Grand Exchange for 36,900.

It is used to craft the sturdy harness, which is used to upgrade the forestry kit into the forestry basket (alongside the log basket) in order to add the functionality of the log basket to the kit. This is reversible, meaning you will receive the sturdy harness back if you dismantle it, instead of it being a permanent upgrade like the clothes pouch and cape pouch.
28149:
The sturdy harness is an item used to combine the log basket and forestry kit into the forestry basket, combining the functionality of both items. This process can be reversed by right clicking the Forestry basket, heading into the configure options, and then choosing the dismantle option.

It is created by using the log brace with 2 ropes, 3 adamantite bars, and 45 steel nails, which requires 75 Smithing and Woodcutting to create.

To create the sturdy harness, combine the log brace with adamantite bars. The sturdy harness must be in your inventory before you can combine the log basket and forestry kit to make the Forestry Basket. The log brace alone will not work, and the combination will have no effect.

Prior to the 23 July 2025 QoL update, most players opted not to make the Forestry Basket because it had to be unequipped to bank their logs. However, this update now allows players to empty a filled log basket without clicking through multiple menus.
28154: Ritual mulch is an item purchased from the Forestry Shop for 150 anima-infused bark and 10 noted maple logs. With level 68 Woodcutting and 50 Farming, players can create nature offerings by combining ritual mulch and one of either avantoe, kwuarm, snapdragon, cadantine, lantadyme, dwarf weed, or torstol. Each set of herbs combined with ritual mulch produces 40 nature offerings.
28177:
The felling axe handle is an item used in the process of creating felling axes. Using the handle on any regular axe within a 3x3 area of an anvil, including through walls, with a hammer in the inventory will irreversibly turn it into a felling axe. The felling axe handle is available from the Forestry Shop for 10,000 anima-infused bark and 500 noted oak logs. These logs can be bought on the Grand Exchange for 20,500. While this item is free-to-play obtainable, the felling axes it creates are members-only.

Felling axes take priority over other axes when used to chop trees, even if you're wielding a normal axe.
28183:
Mulch is an item used during the Struggling sapling Forestry event, where players must create the right combination of resource piles to feed the struggling sapling. These resource piles include droppings, green leaves, rotting leaves, splintered bark, and wild mushrooms.

Players can use the mulch's "check" option to see which ingredients are currently used in it. In addition, the "History" option shows players an interface of the struggling sapling's health, as well as the best and most recent combination of mulch discovered during the event. Note that this interface is identical to the "Inspect" option on the struggling sapling.
28192: Strange pollen is an item used during the flowering tree event, where players must transfer it to a specific pair of flowering bushes to pollinate them.
28193:
An unfired cup is made by using soft clay on a potter's wheel, requiring level 3 Crafting and granting 8.5 experience. One piece of soft clay will produce four unfired cups.

It is then made into an empty cup by placing it into a pottery oven, granting 8.5 Crafting experience. Unlike shaping the clay, firing it has no Crafting level requirement. At lower levels, an unfired cup can crack in the oven, destroying the cup and granting no experience.
28196:
The bronze felling axe is a type of felling axe requiring an Attack level of 1 to be equipped, and a Woodcutting level of 1 to be used. Players can create the axe by using a felling axe handle on a bronze axe while having a hammer in their inventory and standing next to an anvil; this process is irreversible, but the felling axe itself remains tradeable.

Bronze felling axes will chop at the same speed as a normal bronze axe. If the player is carrying forester's rations however (either in the inventory or inside a forestry kit), they will receive 10% more Woodcutting experience each time they successfully chop a tree and gain a 20% chance not to receive logs when chopping trees (or tree roots in the Rising Roots forestry event), at the cost of consuming one ration. This also results in a 20% chance to not receive anima-infused bark from tree roots.

If the player has no rations on their person, the felling axe will function like a regular bronze axe.

If the player is carrying Forester's rations however (either in the inventory or inside a Forestry kit), they will receive 10% more Woodcutting experience each time they successfully chop a tree and gain a 20% chance not to receive logs when chopping trees (or tree roots in the Rising Roots Forestry event), at the cost of consuming one ration. If the player has no rations on their person, the felling axe will function like a regular dragon axe. Like all felling axes, the dragon felling axe is 2-handed.
28220:
The crystal felling axe is a type of felling axe requiring a level of 70 Attack and 50 Agility to be equipped respectively, and a Woodcutting level of 71 to be used. Players can create the axe by either using a felling axe handle on a crystal axe while standing near a singing bowl, or by using the singing bowl directly with a dragon felling axe, a crystal tool seed, and 120 crystal shards. Doing so requires level 76 Smithing[boostable] and 76 Crafting[boostable] to sing the crystal, and grants 6,000 experience in both skills. Players can configure the charges while the axe is in their bank by right-clicking on Configure-Charges, as long as players have the required materials. If the player does not meet the Smithing and Crafting requirements, they can have Conwenna or Reese sing the crystal for them for an extra 60 crystal shards, for a total of 180.

Applying the felling handle to the axe is irreversible: a one-handed axe upgraded into a felling axe can never revert to being one-handed. However, the standard process of reverting crystal to dragon does apply, meaning a crystal felling axe can be reverted into a dragon felling axe (while losing all crystal shards used to make and charge it). The crystal felling axe will start off with 10,000 charges, unless a previously used crystal axe was used in its creation, in which case it will instead inherit the remaining charges from that axe.

Crystal felling axes will chop at the same speed as a normal crystal axe, possessing the same special attack as the dragon axe, giving the player a 15% increase in efficiency over the rune axe, surpassing the 10% increase of the dragon axe. This makes the crystal felling axe approximately 4.5% faster than the dragon felling axe.

If the player is carrying forester's rations however (in the inventory or inside a forestry kit), they will receive 10% more Woodcutting experience per each log and gain a 20% chance not to receive logs when chopping trees (or tree roots in the Rising Roots forestry event), at the cost of consuming one ration. This also results in a 20% chance to not receive anima-infused bark from tree roots.

If the player has no rations on their person, the felling axe will function like a regular crystal axe.

This item can be stored in the treasure chest of a costume room, provided that the interface of the corresponding clue tier is opened before attempting to store the item. Alternatively, the item can be used on the opened treasure chest to insert it without viewing the interface.
28229:
The beaver is a members-only skilling pet that can be obtained while training Woodcutting. A strange sound is heard when you obtain the beaver while Woodcutting. The chances of getting it are dependent on the player's Woodcutting level, the base drop chance for a given tree, and the rate of successfully chopping logs.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack. This message also occurs if there is one last inventory space while the player already has a pet following them, in which case the pet will appear in the inventory instead and the resource dropped to the ground.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around for 30 seconds before disappearing completely. It can then be reclaimed from Probita in East Ardougne for no cost.

28240:
The smoke ancient sceptre is a sceptre requiring 75 Magic, 60 Strength, and 50 Attack to wield. It is made by attaching the smoke quartz, dropped by The Leviathan, to the ancient sceptre; this process can be reversed, allowing players to switch between quartzes as desired.

Like its predecessor, it will increase the effects of Ancient Magicks by 10%, with the added effect of reducing a poisoned target's healing by 20% for 6 seconds after taking damage from smoke spells.

If the player dies a PvP death at level 20 Wilderness or below and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 260,849 coins. The price is defined as 200,000 coins plus the current guide price of an ancient staff.

If the player dies a PvP death above level 20 Wilderness and the item is unprotected, it will be converted to coins. To prevent this, a Trouver parchment and a payment of 500,000 coins can be given to Perdu in order to permanently lock the item. The locked item will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a mangled, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 500,000 coins.
28242:
The ice ancient sceptre is a sceptre requiring 75 Magic, 60 Strength, and 50 Attack to wield. It is made by attaching the ice quartz, dropped by Duke Sucellus, to the ancient sceptre; this process can be reversed, allowing players to switch between quartzes as desired.

Like its predecessor, the ancient sceptre, it will increase the effects of Ancient Magicks by 10%, with an additional 10% accuracy bonus given to ice spells on targets that can be frozen and are not currently frozen.

The ice ancient sceptre finds practical use in the Inferno for an accurate and consistent option to freeze the Jal-Nibs at the start of rounds, and against other players in the Wilderness.

If the player dies a PvP death at level 20 Wilderness or below and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 260,849 coins. The price is defined as 200,000 coins plus the current guide price of an ancient staff.

If the player dies a PvP death above level 20 Wilderness and the item is unprotected, it will be converted to coins. To prevent this, a Trouver parchment and a payment of 500,000 coins can be given to Perdu in order to permanently lock the item. The locked item will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a mangled, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 500,000 coins.
28244:
The shadow ancient sceptre is a sceptre requiring 75 Magic, 60 Strength, and 50 Attack to wield. It is made by attaching the shadow quartz, dropped by The Whisperer, to the ancient sceptre; this process can be reversed, allowing players to switch between quartzes as desired.

Like its predecessor, it will increase the effects of Ancient Magicks by 10%, with the added effect of lowering the target's Attack, Strength, and Defence levels when casting shadow spells (if those levels have not already been drained).

If the player dies a PvP death at level 20 Wilderness or below and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 260,849 coins. The price is defined as 200,000 coins plus the current guide price of an ancient staff.

If the player dies a PvP death above level 20 Wilderness and the item is unprotected, it will be converted to coins. To prevent this, a Trouver parchment and a payment of 500,000 coins can be given to Perdu in order to permanently lock the item. The locked item will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a mangled, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 500,000 coins.
28246:
Wisp is a pet dropped by The Whisperer. It is a much smaller version of her.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.

The ring requires level 90 Magic and 80 Crafting to create (both being boostable), as well as having learnt how to combine Fremennik ring icons with ancient vestiges via Peer the Seer.

Unlike their predecessors, the Fremennik rings, the ancient rings cannot be imbued.

28327:
The ring of shadows is a special ring that is obtained as a reward upon completion of Desert Treasure II. As an upgrade to the ring of visibility, it retains its original effects, as well as having very similar offensive stats to the brimstone ring, making it a decent alternative. It cannot be equipped in the Lassar Undercity.

The ring may be charged by using one blood, soul, death, and law rune on the ring. When charged, the ring can teleport players to the Ancient Vault; additional teleports to the Ghorrock Dungeon, the Scar, the Lassar Undercity, and the Stranglewood can be unlocked by using tablets received as drops from Duke Sucellus, The Leviathan, The Whisperer, and Vardorvis respectively on the ring. It may contain a maximum of 1,000 charges (costing 1,054,000 coins to fully charge, or 1,054 coins per teleport). Players can configure the charges while the ring is in their bank by right-clicking on Configure-Charges, as long as players have the required materials. Uncharging the ring does refund the runes.

If lost, another can be obtained from the Mysterious Bandit in the Ancient Vault for 75,000 coins. Multiple rings can be purchased from the bandit.

Despite the ring's connections with Zaros' generals, it does not provide Zarosian god protection in the God Wars Dungeon.

In PvP death, the ring turns into 75,000 coins regardless of Wilderness location. Any charges in the ring will be lost along with the ring itself.

28334: Awakener's orbs are items dropped by the Forgotten Four bosses fought during Desert Treasure II. The orbs can be used to fight stronger variants of those bosses.
28338:
The Soulreaper axe is a two-handed axe that requires 80 Attack and Strength to wield. It is created by combining four untradeable components, obtained as drops from The Leviathan, The Whisperer, Vardorvis, and Duke Sucellus, alongside 2,000 blood runes and level 75 Magic (which cannot be boosted).

Despite being made from items dropped by prominent Zarosians, the item itself does not grant god protection towards Zarosian NPCs in the God Wars Dungeon.
28341:
Musca mushrooms are an item used during the fight with Duke Sucellus. They are picked from musca mushrooms found at the east side of the asylum, past the extremities.

They are ground into musca powder, which are mixed in the Fermentation Vat alongside arder powder and salax salt to create arder-musca poisons to wake the Duke.

You will get more powder from each mushroom with a higher Herblore level. 2 potions require 3 mushrooms below 80 herblore, and 2 mushrooms at level 80 or higher.
28342:
Musca powder is the result of using a pestle and mortar on a musca mushroom, where between five and six powders are given per mushroom with the amount being tied to your Herblore level. The amount of powder produced is based on the equation ⌊level−2010⌋, and is capped between 1 and 6 powders. Due to the required 62 Herblore for Desert Treasure II, the only amounts players will normally see are 4, 5, and 6 powders. 80 Herblore will give the player the max amount of powder. Six are mixed in the asylum's Fermentation Vat, alongside six Arder powder and six Salax salt, to create one Arder-musca poison, which are used to wake Duke Sucellus.

Musca powder can also be fed to Duke Sucellus to deal 5 damage to him, requiring 40 powder total to awaken the boss.
28343:
Holos mushrooms are a scrapped item which was originally intended to be used during the fight with Duke Sucellus. They are picked from holos mushrooms which would presumably be found in the asylum.

They are ground into holos powder, which would have been mixed in the fermentation vat alongside other ingredients to create a variety of poisons to wake the Duke.
28344:
Holos powder is a scrapped item which was originally intended to be used during the fight with Duke Sucellus. They are the result of using a pestle and mortar on a holos mushroom, where six powders are given per mushroom.

They presumably would have been mixed in the fermentation vat, alongside other types of mushroom powder, to create a variety of poisons to wake the Duke.

28349:
Salax salt is an item mined from the salt deposit in the centre of the asylum where Duke Sucellus is fought, where three to six pieces are given each time the player mines it. The amount of salt received is based on the player's Mining level:

Level 1-69 Mining yields 3 pieces.

Level 70-74 Mining yields 4 pieces.

Level 75-79 Mining yields 5 pieces.

Level 80 Mining or above yields 6 pieces.

Six pieces of salax salt are mixed in the asylum's Fermentation Vat, alongside six musca powder and six arder powder, to create one arder-musca poison, which are used to wake the Duke. There is an iron pickaxe spawn in the boss room located near the stairs half-protruding from the wall. Higher level pickaxes will produce salt at an increased rate, unless tick manipulation is used.
28350:
Musca-holos poison is a scrapped item which was originally intended to be used during the fight with Duke Sucellus. This poison would have been made by mixing musca powder, holos powder, and salax salt in the fermentation vats within the asylum.

Presumably, different types of mushroom powders would have been needed to be mixed each time the player wakes Duke Sucellus up during subsequent fights, but was scrapped in favour of only using one type of poison, the arder-musca poison.

The blackstone fragment is a modified shard of the ancient pillar found in the Lassar Undercity. It is obtained from Ketla after showing her the ring of visibility during Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire. During the quest, it is used to instantly leave the Shadow Realm within the Lassar Undercity upon activating it. It can be also used to recall the shadow blocker, revitalising idol, and anima portal back to the player's inventory from wherever they were placed.

The fragment must also be in the player's inventory during the fight against The Whisperer, as it is used at various points in the fight where her attacks must be countered from within the Shadow Realm; the player will be prompted to activate it when it begins glowing yellow. Without the fragment, the player will refuse to fight her.

If players lose the fragment, it can be re-obtained by speaking to Ketla, or from Ketla's workbench in the Residential District, located in the building just north of the Western Residential District teleporter.

It is used to destroy the shadow tentacles that block the entrances to various buildings in the Shadow Realm.

Once players give Ketla the superior shadow torch schematic, the torch will automatically be upgraded to a superior shadow torch.
28365:

It is used to destroy the shadow tentacles that block the entrances to various buildings in the Shadow Realm.

Once players are rescued by Ketla from the illusion in the Silent Choir's church, the torch will automatically be upgraded to a perfected shadow torch upon claiming it from the workbench.
