28383:
The strange potion is a quest item obtained during Zogre Flesh Eaters. After the player convinces Zavistic Rarve that Sithik Ints might be involved in the curse on Jiggig, Zavistic gives the player the strange potion with instructions to find some way to use the potion on Sithik and then question him.

The player must use the potion on the cup of tea in Sithik's room, then leave and return. The player will then find that Sithik has been transformed into an ogre. The potion can not be used on any other object or character.
28384:

During Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire, the herb, alongside argian berries, are mixed with the unfinished serum to create the strangler serum.
28385:

28388: The Strangler serum is an item used during Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire. Made by using a korbal herb and argian berries on the unfinished serum given by Kasonde, drinking it prevents The Strangler from infecting the player.

28402:
Uncharged cells are an item obtained during the Guardians of the Rift minigame. They are charged by imbuing them at a runic altar, accessible directly by entering an active Portal Guardian. The type of charge it holds is dependent on the runic altar it is charged at.

When inspected, the chatbox will state "An uncharged magical cell built to hold runic energy."
28403: Charged cells are an item obtained during Desert Treasure II. By imbuing an uncharged cell via the altar in the western room of the military installation beneath the Digsite, it can then be used to charge the golem in the central room.
28405:
Perseriya's medallion is one of the four medallions used to access the lower level of the Ancient Vault during Desert Treasure II. It is obtained by searching the debris by Perseriya's ship on the north-east side of the island, after having defeated The Leviathan.

As it cannot be deposited into a bank, it is recommended that players bring it to the Ancient Vault immediately, as the Mysterious Figure may appear and attack the player if they have it in their inventory for too long.
28406:
Sucellus' medallion is one of the four medallions used to access the lower level of the Ancient Vault during Desert Treasure II. It is found in a chest in the room west of the asylum within the Ghorrock Prison, accessed via an odd key that is obtained after defeating Duke Sucellus.

As it cannot be deposited into a bank, it is recommended that players bring it to the Ancient Vault immediately, as the Mysterious Figure may appear and attack the player if they have it in their inventory for too long.
28407:
The Whisperer's medallion is one of the four medallions used to access the lower level of the Ancient Vault during Desert Treasure II. It is obtained by searching the entrails of The Whisperer after defeating her.

As it cannot be deposited into a bank, it is recommended that players bring it to the Ancient Vault immediately, as the Mysterious Figure may appear and attack the player if they have it in their inventory for too long.

If you lose the medallion during the quest, you can recover it by returning to where you fought The Whisperer. The entrails will be there and you can grab another medallion without having to fight again.
28408: The hair clip is an item obtained during Desert Treasure II, found by searching the bed in the prison cell within Enakhra's Temple. It is used to escape from the cell, where the player can then recover their items from a chest in the eastern room.
28409:
The ancient lamp is an item obtained as a reward after completing Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire. Three are given to the player, and each one grants 100,000 experience in one of the following skills, given that it is over level 60: Attack, Strength, Defence, Hitpoints, Ranged, Magic, or Prayer.

The lamp cannot be banked. However, if the player prefers to use it at a later date, it can be destroyed and reclaimed from the Mysterious Bandit in the Ancient Vault whenever the player wishes to do so.
28412: The prisoner's letter is a letter found in the Ghorrock Prison during Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire. It is obtained by searching the skeleton in the prison cell the player was locked up in upon arrival.
28414: The chisel is an item obtained during Desert Treasure II, where it is given to the player by the prisoner in the cell next to theirs within the Ghorrock Prison.
28415:
A lockpick is an item used with the Thieving skill that can be used on certain locked objects. While some objects require a lockpick to be unlocked, certain objects are instead only made easier to open.

Lockpicks can be obtained by pickpocketing bandits (with 53 Thieving) and rogues (32 Thieving), or as drops from young implings and scavenger beasts. They can also be purchased from Martin Thwait, though this requires level 50 Thieving and Agility, or level 99 Thieving.

Lockpicks have a chance to break when performing certain actions, including: Ogre Coffins, the secure chest during Desert Treasure I, the small rune caskets during Ali Morrisane, and the first Ancient Gate during Legends' Quest. Outside of these activities, lockpicks will never break.

Scarred scraps are a consumable item that can be found within chests in The Scar. They can be consumed to restore 15 Hitpoints, 25% of the player's prayer points, and 20% run energy. It also provides the effect of a stamina potion, with the effect being doubled by the ring of endurance.

They CANNOT be taken out of the scar; furthermore, they will be removed from the player's inventory upon completion of a level during the quest. It is therefore recommended to consume them prior to finishing a level.

The stink bomb can be obtained by searching a stone chest in The Stranglewood, where players first meet Kasonde.

When set off, a stink bomb will attract the nearest strangled to the location it was set off to help keep them away from the player. A game message will state You set off a stink bomb. It smells as bad as you'd expect.

Stink bombs have a maximum range of ten squares, forming a 21x21 tile attraction area centred on the square where the bomb is set off.
28474:
The ice ancient sceptre is a sceptre requiring 75 Magic, 60 Strength, and 50 Attack to wield. It is made by attaching the ice quartz, dropped by Duke Sucellus, to the ancient sceptre; this process can be reversed, allowing players to switch between quartzes as desired.

Like its predecessor, the ancient sceptre, it will increase the effects of Ancient Magicks by 10%, with an additional 10% accuracy bonus given to ice spells on targets that can be frozen and are not currently frozen.

The ice ancient sceptre finds practical use in the Inferno for an accurate and consistent option to freeze the Jal-Nibs at the start of rounds, and against other players in the Wilderness.

If the player dies a PvP death at level 20 Wilderness or below and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 260,849 coins. The price is defined as 200,000 coins plus the current guide price of an ancient staff.

If the player dies a PvP death above level 20 Wilderness and the item is unprotected, it will be converted to coins. To prevent this, a Trouver parchment and a payment of 500,000 coins can be given to Perdu in order to permanently lock the item. The locked item will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a mangled, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 500,000 coins.

The Sigil of the Alchemaniac is a tier 1 utility Deadman Mode sigil. It is a permanent unlock that automatically recasts high or low alchemy on a stack of items. It does not remove the Magic level requirement for the spells or the runes required to cast the spells.

In Deadman: Annihilation, it can be purchased from the skull shop. It can be activated by clicking Attune and is a permanent unlock. There is no limit on how many permanent sigils can be active at once. Duplicate sigils can be sold back to the skull shop by using it on the deadman's skull.

In past Deadman Mode events, the un-attuned version was dropped by most monsters (via the Deadman Mode drop table) and was tradeable on the Grand Exchange.

In Deadman: Annihilation, it can be purchased from the skull shop. It can be activated by clicking Attune and is a permanent unlock. There is no limit on how many permanent sigils can be active at once. Duplicate sigils can be sold back to the skull shop by using it on the deadman's skull.

In past Deadman Mode events, the un-attuned version was dropped by most monsters (via the Deadman Mode drop table) and was tradeable on the Grand Exchange.

28579:

The notes can be stored in and retrieved from the bookcase in a player-owned house.
28599:
Scarred extracts are a catalyst used in runecrafting when crafting blood, soul, aether, and wrath runes, by giving 60 extra runes per extract.

The extract can be obtained in the Scar essence mine from the extract orifice by depositing tainted essence chunks into a ventriculus opening, and having 24,000 coins within Hagus' coffer to convert the tainted essence into a scarred extract.

Because using scarred extracts results in a cost of 400 coins for each rune crafted, it is not recommended to use extracts as a means of making money; rather, it is intended for ironman players who plan to use the runes for themselves.

When used in combination with a blood essence, their effects stack additively: both the essence and the extract will act on the base number of blood runes crafted.

Scarred extracts can be used at either the traditional runecrafting altars, or at the Zeah blood or soul altars.

When using scarred extracts to craft aether runes without the use of a binding necklace, extracts will only be consumed for successfully created runes. In other words, a rune that fails to combine will not also delete a scarred extract.

If players happen to make too many extracts, they can be refunded for 90% of their original cost by taking them to Hagus in the Scar.
28613:
The cape pouch is an item purchased from the Forestry Shop for 2,500 anima-infused bark. This pouch is used on the Forestry kit or Forestry basket with level 99 Woodcutting, allowing the player to store the Woodcutting cape within, to receive the skillcape benefits whilst wearing the Forestry kit instead to save an extra inventory slot.

When used on a Forestry kit or basket with level 99 Woodcutting, a message in the chatbox will state You expand your Forestry kit/basket to be able to hold a Woodcutting cape. If the player does not have level 99 Woodcutting, it will state You need level 99 Woodcutting to expand your Forestry kit/basket with this. When the cape pouch is attached to the Forestry kit, it does not change any interface options. Players can also store both the cape and the clothes pouches in their Forestry kit. To access the Woodcutting cape, use the "View" option.

Unlike the clothes pouch upgrade, the Forestry kit or basket must be equipped to receive the benefits of a Woodcutting cape stored inside; merely carrying it in the inventory is not sufficient.

Players can sell the pouch back to the shop to get 80% of its cost back (2,000 bark).
28622:
The pheasant legs are a piece of the pheasant costume, obtained by using a needle and thread on 15 pheasant tail feathers, which are a possible reward as part of the Pheasant Control Forestry event.

This item can be stored in the magic wardrobe of a costume room.
28624:
Pheasant tail feathers are an item used to create the pheasant costume. Players can use a needle and thread to create the outfit; 15 feathers are required per piece, for a total of 60 to create the full outfit.

There is a fixed 50% chance of obtaining one from Pheasant Nests as part of the Pheasant Control Forestry event. Excess feathers can be sold to the Friendly Forester for 5 anima-infused bark each.
28626:
The fox whistle is a rare reward from the Poachers Forestry event. It is used on the beaver pet to allow it to metamorphose into a fox. It is consumed in the process.

There is a 1/30 chance to retrieve a fox whistle at the end of the event, provided a player is eligible to receive the full rewards of the event (meaning the player disarmed at least 1 trap). Upon receiving one, it will be placed in the inventory (or on the ground if it is full), and a game message in the chatbox will state Well done, you've saved the fox from the poachers! The fox has left you a gift... You feel a connection to the fox as if it wishes to travel with you....

Alternatively, players can purchase the fox whistle for 75,000 anima bark from the Forestry Shop. It can also be sold to the Forestry Shop for 250 anima-infused bark.
28628:
Sawmill vouchers are an item purchased from the Forestry Shop. 10 can be purchased for 150 anima-infused bark. The voucher can be redeemed for an extra plank per log at a sawmill, or when using the Plank Make spell. Players must have sufficient space in their inventory or plank sack to do so, or the vouchers will not be used, with the excess logs that cannot be converted into 2 planks (due to lack of inventory space) being converted into 1 plank (without using a voucher) instead, which is more costly for the player.

Sawmill vouchers cannot be used by butlers when asking them to convert logs into planks.
28630:
Twitcher's gloves are an item purchased from the Forestry Shop for 5,000 anima-infused bark and 500 noted willow logs.

Whilst equipped, the player will have a 20% increased chance to receive a specific type of bird nest whenever they receive one from Woodcutting; the player can right-click "Settings" on the gloves to specify which type: Ring, Egg, Seed, or Clue. This effect stacks with the effects of a strung rabbit foot. Additionally, although redwood trees only yield clue nests when cut, the gloves can still increase the chance of getting clue nests.

The effect of the gloves does not apply during bird house trapping.

When purchasing these gloves, you receive a chatbox message stating "Remember, you must wear these gloves to receive their bonus."

Players can use the mulch's "check" option to see which ingredients are currently used in it. In addition, the "History" option shows players an interface of the struggling sapling's health, as well as the best and most recent combination of mulch discovered during the event. Note that this interface is identical to the "Inspect" option on the struggling sapling.

The Petal garland is a purely cosmetic neck slot item that can be obtained as a possible reward from the Enchantment Ritual Forestry event. Note that the petal garland cannot be stored in a player-owned house.

There is a fixed chance of 1/30 to receive the petal garland upon completing at least one step of the ritual, provided the player was eligible for the full rewards of the event. When receiving one, a game message in the chatbox will state The Dryad also hands you a Petal garland.

It can be sold to the Forestry Shop for 150 anima-infused bark.
28663:
The Golden pheasant egg is a rare reward from the Pheasant Control Forestry event. It is used on the beaver pet to allow it to metamorphose into a pheasant. It is consumed in the process.

Unlike the fox whistle, the golden pheasant egg can be obtained mid-way through the event rather than only at the end. Alternatively, the golden pheasant egg can be purchased for 75,000 anima bark from the Forestry Shop.

There is a chance to retrieve a golden pheasant egg from a pheasant nest, provided a player is eligible to receive the reward from the event; the rate is approximately 1/1500 for every regular pheasant egg retrieved. Upon receiving one, it will be placed in the inventory (or on the ground if it is full), and a game message in the chatbox will state You feel a connection to the pheasants as if one wishes to travel with you...

The golden pheasant egg can be turned in to the Friendly Forester for 250 anima-infused bark.

Only one roll for the golden pheasant egg is made upon looting a pheasant nest, after which no more rolls are given until the regular pheasant egg is turned in to the Freaky Forester. As such, repeatedly destroying regular pheasant eggs will not increase one's chance of receiving the drop.
28670: Foxes are attackable monsters found in the Fremennik Province, Hosidius, Auburn Valley, and Drumstick Isle.

If the player dies (including in PvP) and the boots are unprotected, it will be sent to the gravestone. When lost, they can be reclaimed for free from the Cradle of Life. Multiple pairs can be claimed and owned at the same time.

Upon receiving one, it will be placed in the inventory (or on the ground if it is full), and a game message in the chatbox will state The temporary beehive was made so well you take some parts for building a permanent hive.

Excess parts can be sold to the Friendly Forester for 25 anima-infused bark each.

It is obtained at a bank upon unlocking the Globetrotter relic. For an interactive map of destinations, see here.

If lost or destroyed, the Globetrotter pendant can be reclaimed from The Sage.
28767:
The banker's note is an item in the Grid Master community event from the Banker's Note relic, unlocked by completing the Corrupted Gauntlet.

It allows players to use note-able items on it to turn them into banknotes or unnote them. The "Activate" option allows players to note and un-note items in one action with a quantity of the player's choosing, though an item must first be used on the banker's note in order for this to work.

If lost or destroyed, the banker's note can be reclaimed from The Sage.

The minion whistle is an item obtained during the Demonic Pacts League, given to players who picked the tier 8 Minion relic.

The whistle allows players to summon a powerful minion which lasts for 30 minutes. The minion will cast an AoE attack if the player's target is weakest to range or magic and is in a multi-combat area.

The base minion's stats are:

Min hit: 3

Max hit: 10

Attack speed: 1.8

Accuracy: 45,000

Up to 5 equippable Zamorak-aligned items can be used on the whistle to consume them, increasing the minion's max hit by 2 per unique item, up to a total of 20.

The minion whistle can be retrieved from the Leagues Tutor in Yama's Lair if lost.
28773:
The Sage's axe is an item obtained during the Demonic Pacts League, given to players upon unlocking the Executioner relic.

With a maximum attack range of 6 tiles (8 on longrange), the Sage's axe will instantly kill targets who have less than 20% of their health remaining. However, NPCs who take reduced damage from ranged attacks will still take reduced damage when using the Sage's axe; for example, the Kraken only takes 1/7th ranged damage. Additionally, the axe does not work against Yama or the Gemstone Crab.

If lost or destroyed, the Sage's axe can be reclaimed from the Leagues Tutor in Yama's Lair.
28780:
The Trailblazer reloaded relic hunter (t2) armour set is an item obtained by exchanging a set of items with a Grand Exchange clerk via their right-click "Sets" option and clicking on the appropriate item set within the Item Sets interface.

It is commonly made in order to conveniently sell all four components of the Trailblazer Reloaded Relic Hunter (T2) outfit at once.
28783:
The Trailblazer reloaded relic hunter (t3) armour set is an item obtained by exchanging a set of items with a Grand Exchange clerk via their right-click "Sets" option and clicking on the appropriate item set within the Item Sets interface.

It is commonly made in order to conveniently sell all four components of the Trailblazer Reloaded Relic Hunter (T3) outfit at once.
28786:
The icy jumper is a cosmetic reward from the 2023 Christmas event. It can be obtained as a reward from the Christmas events that occur once per year.

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room.
28790:
The Kourend castle teleport is a magic tablet that can be broken by players to teleport to the Kourend Castle courtyard, by the statue of King Rada I. Using the tablet requires completion of the quest Client of Kourend.

Players can create this item on a teak eagle lectern, a mahogany eagle lectern, or a marble lectern with 2 law runes, 1 water rune, 1 fire rune, and 1 soft clay and at least level 48 Magic, granting 58 experience.

This tablet can be made regardless of the player's current spellbook. As with all tablets, the user does not need to have the relevant Magic level to use this tablet.
28792:
The bone mace is a weapon requiring level 50 Attack to wield. It is made by combining a rune mace with Scurrius' spine at an anvil, requiring a hammer and level 35 Smithing to do so; players without the required level can alternatively pay Historian Aldo 50,000 coins to create it on their behalf. The mace has almost identical stats to the dragon mace, missing only the 5 prayer bonus.

As a rat bone weapon, it is effective against all types of rats by adding 10 damage to the player's maximum hit. Additionally, it has no attack cooldown when attacking the giant rats that Scurrius summons. The mace cannot be used against any other type of monster (including manual cast spells); doing so will yield the game message You can only use this weapon against rats.
28794:
The bone shortbow is a weapon requiring level 50 Ranged to wield. It is made by combining a yew shortbow with Scurrius' spine, requiring a knife and level 35 Fletching to do so; players without the required level can alternatively pay Historian Aldo 50,000 coins to create it on their behalf. The bow has identical offensive stats to the magic shortbow, and can fire up to amethyst arrows.

As a rat bone weapon, it is effective against all types of rats by adding 10 damage to the player's maximum hit. The shortbow cannot be used against any other type of monster (including manually cast spells); doing so will yield the game message You can only use this weapon against rats. Additionally, this weapon has no attack cooldown when attacking the giant rats that Scurrius summons.
28796:
The bone staff is a powered staff requiring level 50 Magic to wield. It is made by combining a battlestaff with Scurrius' spine alongside 1,000 chaos runes, requiring a chisel and level 35 Crafting to do so; players without the required level can alternatively pay Historian Aldo 50,000 coins to create it on their behalf. The chaos runes are not consumed but are used to give the bone staff an initial 1,000 charges.

In order to use the staff's magic spell, it must be charged with chaos runes, holding up to 20,000 charges when fully charged. Each cast requires one chaos rune, costing 105 coins. Uncharging the staff returns all remaining runes back. Additionally, unlike other powered staves, the bone staff's built-in spell gives 35 base Magic experience on a successful hit.

As a rat bone weapon, it is effective against all types of rats by adding 10 damage to the player's maximum hit. The staff cannot be used against any other type of monster (including manual cast spells); doing so will yield the game message You can only use this weapon against rats. Additionally, this weapon has no attack cooldown when attacking the giant rats that Scurrius summons.
28798:
Scurrius' spine is an uncommon drop from Scurrius. It can be combined with various weapons to create rat bone weapons.

Excess spines can be given to Historian Aldo outside the boss area in exchange for an antique lamp giving 5,000 experience in either Attack, Strength, Defence, Hitpoints, Magic, Ranged, or 3,500 experience in Prayer.
28800:
Antique lamps are rewards from quests, achievement diaries and the Varrock Museum miniquest. Like regular lamps, these lamps grant a player experience in a chosen skill, and the skill chosen must usually be over a certain level which is unboostable.

Lamps that are not included in the three items kept on death will be kept inside your death's coffer, if not deleted.
28801:
Scurry is a pet dropped by Scurrius. It is a much smaller version of Scurrius. When spoken to, it has three distinct personalities: Scurry, the main (melee) rat, Chewy, the ranged rat, and Nibbles, the mage rat.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.
28803:
The grubby key is a key obtained from killing monsters within the Forthos Dungeon. It is used to open the Grubby Chest.

Brother Aimeri will give the player a key in exchange for spare pristine spider silks.
28804:
Bottles are obtained during Defender of Varrock within Zemouregal's Base, where they are used to collect red mist from defeated armoured zombies in order to obtain a bottle of mist.

After the quest, the item has no use and can be safely dropped.
28805:
A bottle of mist is obtained during Defender of Varrock within Zemouregal's Base, where it is used to bypass a door's security system.

It is acquired by using a bottle on red mist that appears after defeating an armoured zombie. Additional mist cannot be acquired after the quest although any in the player's bank will be kept. While the empty bottles can still be picked up, attempting to collect more mist is prevented and the following message is displayed: You don't need any more mist.
28807: Shield of Arrav is a quest where the shield of the famous Arrav of Avarrocka has been stolen by organised crime syndicates in Varrock.
28808: List of elders is obtained during Defender of Varrock, found in the Varrock Palace Library by the scrolls near the flipped table. It lists the founding elders of Avarrocka, and is cross referenced with the Varrock Census to find their living descendants.
28813: The broken zombie axe is the broken version of the zombie axe. It is dropped by armoured zombies in Zemouregal's Base, and by their higher-level variants in Zemouregal's Fort. Players with 70 Smithing can repair the axe at an anvil with a hammer in the inventory; boosts can be used. Repairing the axe grants the player 500 Smithing experience.
28816: The stone tablet is an item obtained during The Curse of Arrav in the tunnels beneath Zemouregal's Fort, and is one of four tablets made by Lamistard, who dug the tunnels in an attempt to avoid being chosen as a sacrifice in the Mahjarrat's rituals.
28817: The granite tablet is an item obtained during The Curse of Arrav in the tunnels beneath Zemouregal's Fort, and is one of four tablets made by Lamistard, who dug the tunnels in an attempt to avoid being chosen as a sacrifice in the Mahjarrat's rituals.
28818: The slate tablet is an item obtained during The Curse of Arrav in the tunnels beneath Zemouregal's Fort, and is one of four tablets made by Lamistard, who dug the tunnels in an attempt to avoid being chosen as a sacrifice in the Mahjarrat's rituals.
28819: The shale tablet is an item obtained during The Curse of Arrav in the tunnels beneath Zemouregal's Fort, and is one of four tablets made by Lamistard, who dug the tunnels in an attempt to avoid being chosen as a sacrifice in the Mahjarrat's rituals.
28820:

28822:
A coin pouch is an item obtained from pickpocketing certain NPCs, which contains several coins depending on the NPC it was obtained from. To obtain the coins from them, players can simply click their stack of coin pouches to open them all at once, or they can right-click them to open one at a time. They cannot be traded or banked.

Up to 28 coin pouches can stack in a player's inventory, after which the player must open them to collect the coins inside before being able to pickpocket more. This limit can be increased by completing the Ardougne Diary, where it increases to 56, 84, and 140 after completing the Medium, Hard, and Elite diaries, respectively.

Coin pouches have different variants depending on who the player pickpocketed it from; for example, a coin pouch from pickpocketing guards does not stack with pouches from pickpocketing Ardougne knights. NPCs who are pickpocketed via blackjacking yield coins directly while they are knocked out instead of coin pouches. If rogue equipment is used to receive double the loot from pickpocketing, only one coin pouch is obtained (containing the normal amount) while the other half is obtained directly as coins.
28824:
The Civitas illa Fortis teleport is a magic tablet that can be broken by players to teleport to Civitas illa Fortis. Using the tablet requires completion of Twilight's Promise.

Players with level 54 Magic can create this item on a Mahogany eagle lectern or better in a player-owned house. This requires 2 law runes, 1 fire rune, 1 earth rune, and 1 soft clay. Creating a tablet grants 64 Magic experience, the same as casting the Civitas illa Fortis Teleport spell. Elemental staves can be substituted for runes and are recommended when making teleport tablets in large groups at a time.

As with all teleport tablets, using a Civitas illa Fortis teleport tablet does not grant any experience.
28828:
Blessed Dizana's quiver is an upgraded variant of Dizana's quiver, made by using it on a Shrine of Ralos while having a total of 150,000 sunfire splinters and a Dizana's quiver in the player's inventory. Charging the quiver with sunfire splinters contributes to the required amount of splinters to upgrade.

The blessed quiver permanently gains the effects of Dizana's Sunfire, where an additional +1 Ranged Strength and +10 Ranged accuracy is applied to stored arrows and bolts - essentially acting as a variant of the original with unlimited charges. The upgraded variant also retains its level 75 Ranged requirement to equip.

It can also be combined with the max cape to change its appearance by turning it into Dizana's max cape.
28830:
Dizana's max cape is the result of combining blessed Dizana's quiver with a max cape, during which the max hood required to be in the player's inventory will automatically convert to Dizana's max hood.

Like the other max cape variants (a max cape combined with another cape slot item), Dizana's max cape does not have the max cape's stats or perks; it only acts as a cosmetic upgrade to blessed Dizana's quiver with the following exceptions when worn:

It acts as a Cooking cape to allow access to the Cooks' Guild without a chef's hat, golden chef's hat, Varrock armour 3 or 4

It acts as a Crafting cape to allow access to the Crafting Guild without a brown apron or golden apron

It acts as a Runecraft cape to prevent essence pouches from degrading (but does not allow access to runic altars)

It acts as a Firemaking cape to work as a piece of warm clothing

It can be used to perform the Skill Cape emote.

The cape retains the perks of the blessed Dizana's quiver.

The max cape and quiver can be separated by using a knife on the cape. Mac will also buy back a max cape, along with its variants, for 1,900,800 coins each. He will return the secondary item any max cape variant was combined with upon doing so.

If the player dies a PvP death at level 20 Wilderness or below and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 400,000 coins.

If the player dies a PvP death above level 20 Wilderness and the item is unprotected, it will be converted to coins. To prevent this, a Trouver parchment and a payment of 500,000 coins can be given to Perdu in order to permanently lock the item. The locked item will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a mangled, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 500,000 coins.
28831:
Immature tecu salamanders are young tecu salamanders that are caught as part of the Hunter skill. They have no use and cannot be used as a weapon.

Unlike other salamanders, which are caught and able to be used as weapons from the get go, tecu salamanders are often caught at this immature stage; to use one as a weapon, players must catch a fully grown tecu salamander instead, which are a much rarer catch.
28834:
The tecu salamander is the strongest salamander that can be caught using a net trap and the Hunter skill at level 79, granting 344 Hunter experience, which can be found south-east of Ralos' Rise. Catching a matured tecu salamander is rare, as players often receive immature tecu salamanders instead; when an adult is captured, a message in the game chat will state The salamander is fully grown, you could use this as a weapon.

Tecu salamanders require level 80 Attack, Magic, and Ranged to wield. Irit tar is used as ammunition for the salamander. It is the best salamander to use for the two salamander-required Combat Achievements: The Worst Ranged Weapon and More than just a ranged weapon.

Despite being able to perform Magic and Ranged attacks, this weapon requires the user to be in the opponent's melee distance to attack, potentially reducing the practicality of the two attack styles. However, it can be used to attack enemies from behind fences, and can also attack enemies in diagonal squares, meaning that safespotting is still possible.

When using the Scorch (Slash) and Blaze (Magic) attack styles, the attack speed is 5. When using the Flare (Range) attack style, the attack speed is 4, which is similar in concept to the Rapid style of most ranged weapons, and it will use standard ranged defence, similar to bows.

Warning: This is a live creature; if unprotected it will run away when you die. Should this happen, you will need to buy or catch a new one.
28845:
The jungle camo top is a members only piece of the Jungle camouflage gear that requires 4 Hunter to wear. To make one, bring two feldip weasel furs and 20 coins to the Fancy Clothes Store in Varrock, to Pellem in the Hunter Guild, or to Prifddinas' Seamstress.

When worn, it reduces weight by 3 kg. Additionally, though the examine claims so, it does not affect the trapping of hunter creatures.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Camouflage gear: Jungle set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
28848:
Jungle camo legs are a members only piece of Jungle camouflage gear that requires level 4 Hunter to wear. It is purely cosmetic and does not improve the trap-rate. To make one, bring two feldip weasel furs and 20 coins to the Fancy Clothes Store in Varrock, to Pellem in the Hunter Guild, or to Prifddinas' Seamstress.

When worn, it reduces weight by 2 kg. Additionally, though the examine claims so, it does not affect the trapping of hunter creatures.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Camouflage gear: Jungle set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

When worn, it reduces weight by 3 kg. Additionally, though the examine claims so, it does not affect the trapping of hunter creatures.

28854:

When worn, it reduces weight by 2 kg. Additionally, though the examine claims so, it does not affect the trapping of hunter creatures.

28857:

When worn, it reduces weight by 3 kg. Additionally, though the examine claims so, it does not affect the trapping of hunter creatures.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Camouflage gear: Polar set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
28860:
Polar camo legs are a members-only piece of Polar camouflage gear. To make a pair, a player will need to bring two polar kebbit fur and 20 coins to the Fancy Clothes Store in Varrock, to Pellem in the Hunter Guild, or to Prifddinas' Seamstress.

When worn, it reduces weight by 2 kg. Additionally, though the examine claims so, it does not affect the trapping of hunter creatures.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Camouflage gear: Polar set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
28872:
Sunlight antler bolts are ranged ammunition for the hunters' sunlight crossbow, requiring 66 Ranged to use. They can be created at level 62 Fletching by using a chisel on a sunlight antelope antler; each antler produces 12 bolts and 10 Fletching experience.

Unlike other arrows and bolts, weapon poison is not able to be applied to them.

Despite not being made of metal, sunlight antler bolts do function with Ava's devices obtained from the completion of Animal Magnetism.
28893:
A moonlight moth is an item that is obtained from catching moonlight moths, which require level 75 Hunter and a butterfly net and jar. Players with level 85 Hunter can catch moonlight moths barehanded.

Once caught, players can right-click "Release" the filled butterfly jar to restore 22 Prayer points. In a multi-combat zone, the item may be used on another player to share the effect with them and up to three players within a 5x5 area of the target if the players have Accept Aid toggled on. The empty butterfly jar will remain in the inventory after use. For Group Ironmen, the moonlight moth cannot be shared, while the Moonlight moth mix can.

The effect of the holy wrench does not apply to this item.

With a pestle and mortar, players can combine a Moonlight Moth with raw hunter meat to create moonlight moth mix (2).
28899:
Wyrmling bones are the remains obtained from killing wyrmlings, which give 21 Prayer experience when buried. This can be increased by offering the bones in different ways:

63 XP when casting Sinister Offering.

63 XP when offered at the Sacred Bone Burner after the appropriate faith level has been achieved.

73.5 XP when offered at a gilded altar with two burners lit or at the Chaos Temple. The Temple additionally has a 50% chance to not deplete the bones; effectively doubling the XP to 147 per bone.

105 XP when blessed and broken down into blessed bone shards and offered at the libation bowl, or 126 XP when offered with a jug of blessed sunfire wine. Virilis outside the altar will exchange noted bones for 10 coins each.

120 XP when offered at the Ectofuntus in the form of baby dragon bonemeal.
28902:
Dizana's max cape is the result of combining blessed Dizana's quiver with a max cape, during which the max hood required to be in the player's inventory will automatically convert to Dizana's max hood.

Like the other max cape variants (a max cape combined with another cape slot item), Dizana's max cape does not have the max cape's stats or perks; it only acts as a cosmetic upgrade to blessed Dizana's quiver with the following exceptions when worn:

It acts as a Cooking cape to allow access to the Cooks' Guild without a chef's hat, golden chef's hat, Varrock armour 3 or 4

It acts as a Crafting cape to allow access to the Crafting Guild without a brown apron or golden apron

It acts as a Runecraft cape to prevent essence pouches from degrading (but does not allow access to runic altars)

It acts as a Firemaking cape to work as a piece of warm clothing

It can be used to perform the Skill Cape emote.

The cape retains the perks of the blessed Dizana's quiver.

The max cape and quiver can be separated by using a knife on the cape. Mac will also buy back a max cape, along with its variants, for 1,900,800 coins each. He will return the secondary item any max cape variant was combined with upon doing so.

If the player dies a PvP death at level 20 Wilderness or below and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 400,000 coins.

If the player dies a PvP death above level 20 Wilderness and the item is unprotected, it will be converted to coins. To prevent this, a Trouver parchment and a payment of 500,000 coins can be given to Perdu in order to permanently lock the item. The locked item will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a mangled, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 500,000 coins.
28904:
Dizana's max hood is a hood created by using blessed Dizana's quiver on a max cape. When Dizana's max cape is created, the max hood is required as well and is automatically converted to Dizana's max hood.

If players are refunding Dizana's max cape via Mac, the player must also have Dizana's max hood in their inventory.

Should players lose the hood, they may reclaim it from Mac for free.

28907: Clue scroll (medium) is an anagram clue obtained from medium Treasure Trails.
28908: Clue scroll (medium) is a cryptic clue obtained from medium Treasure Trails.
28911: Clue scroll (elite) is a cryptic clue obtained from elite Treasure Trails.
28919:
The Tonalztics of Ralos is a one-handed thrown weapon that requires level 75 Ranged to equip, obtained by participating in the Fortis Colosseum. Unlike most thrown weapons, it is not stackable and effectively provides unlimited "ammo," though it has an additional effect when charged with Sunfire splinters. The weapon rolls against a monster's light ranged defence.

When charged, the weapon will hit twice, with two independent damage rolls and an attack range of 7 tiles (9 on longrange). Uncharged, the weapon hits a target once for 0-75% of the player's maximum ranged hit, with a slightly worse attack range of 6 tiles (8 on longrange). It can hold a maximum of 20,000 charges. One charge is consumed per throw, whether or not the special attack is used, and regardless of the amount of hits that land. Players can configure the charges while the weapon is in their bank by right-clicking on Configure-Charges, as long as players have the required materials.
28922:
The Tonalztics of Ralos is a one-handed thrown weapon that requires level 75 Ranged to equip, obtained by participating in the Fortis Colosseum. Unlike most thrown weapons, it is not stackable and effectively provides unlimited "ammo," though it has an additional effect when charged with Sunfire splinters. 28924:
Sunfire splinters can be obtained from participating in the Fortis Colosseum, hunting sunlight antelope, defeating the Hueycoatl and opening Chest (moon key). They are used for various items:

Charging Dizana's quiver and the Tonalztics of Ralos as well as blessing Dizana's quiver to make it permanently charged

Creating sunfire runes with rune essence (and variants) alongside fire runes (1 fire rune and 1 sunfire splinter are used per essence) and by extension making searing pages

Creating jugs of sunfire wine from a jug of wine (uses 2 splinters per jug, requires pestle & mortar)

Dizana's quivers can be exchanged for 4,000 sunfire splinters by talking to Minimus. The average number of Sunfire splinters gained per successful Colosseum run is 2,014.62, not including exchanging the additional quivers from completion.
28929:
Sunfire runes are a type of rune created by using fire runes, along with sunfire splinters and pure/daeyalt essence, at a Shrine of Ralos. Doing so requires level 33 Runecraft, with the output being doubled at level 49, and tripled at level 98.

As a superior variant of the fire rune, any successful hit with offensive fire spells will deal a minimum of 10% of the player's max hit. If the player has a source of infinite fire runes equipped (e.g. twinflame staff) and casts a fire spell with sunfire runes in their inventory, the sunfire runes are still consumed and still grant their minimum hit effect.

Though not advisable due to the cost per rune, they can be used in place of fire runes for non-combat spells such as teleporting or High Level Alchemy.

100 sunfire runes can also be used on burnt pages to create searing pages, which can be used on a tome of fire to give it the same effect.
28933:
The sunfire fanatic helm is an item that requires level 60 Prayer and 40 Defence to equip, obtained as a possible reward from participating in the Fortis Colosseum.

Part of the sunfire fanatic armour set, it provides the best in slot prayer bonus for the head slot, and also has identical defence bonuses to the rune full helm.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Sunfire fanatic armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
28936:
The sunfire fanatic cuirass is an item that requires level 60 Prayer and 40 Defence to equip, obtained as a possible reward from participating in the Fortis Colosseum.

Part of the sunfire fanatic armour set, it provides the best in slot prayer bonus for the body slot, and also has identical defence bonuses to the rune platebody. The armour does not stop Ava's devices from gathering arrows.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Sunfire fanatic armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
28942:
Echo crystals are a drop received from participating in the Fortis Colosseum. It is used on a pair of guardian boots to create echo boots, which gives it an additional +2 prayer bonus and a passive recoil effect.

Each echo crystal added to the boots gives it 6,000 recoil charges.
28945:
Echo boots are an enhanced pair of guardian boots which require level 75 Defence to wear. They are made by combining the boots with an echo crystal, a rare drop from participating in the Fortis Colosseum. Compared to its predecessor, it gives an additional +2 prayer bonus and a passive effect in which the boots deal 1 recoil damage to any target that damages the player, limited to a 3x3 square centered on the player. This effectively restricts recoiled targets to only those in melee range.

Each echo crystal will add 6,000 charges to the recoil effect (costing 481.11 per charge), up to a maximum of 60,000. The recoil effect can be toggled via the boots' "Toggle-activity" option, allowing players to disable it as to not waste it during casual training, and instead use it in activities where the effect may prove more useful. The "Revert" option reverts the echo boots back into guardian boots, though this will not return any echo crystals, regardless of whether or not any recoil charges were used. Players can configure the charges while the boots are in their bank by right-clicking on Configure-Charges, as long as players have the required materials.

Like the Bandos and guardian boots used in their creation, they will render followers of Bandos unaggressive to the wearer in the God Wars Dungeon.

28960:
Smol Heredit is a pet that can be obtained from completing the Fortis Colosseum after defeating Sol Heredit. Players have a 1/200 chance of obtaining him. Alternatively, players can exchange Dizana's quiver to Minimus for another 1/200 chance to obtain him. Unlike other boss pets, Smol Heredit is considered a main drop and will be shown accordingly on the colosseum interface upon reaching the final wave.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.

28988: The blue moon spear is a non-degradable two-handed bladed staff that requires level 70 Attack and 75 Magic to equip, which is obtained as a possible reward from the Lunar Chest in Neypotzli. It can autocast elemental spells from the standard spellbook, as well as combat spells from the Arceuus spellbook and Ancient Magicks. Despite the name, the blue moon spear is not a spear and not considered a corpbane weapon.
28991:
Atlatl darts are ammunition used exclusively by the eclipse atlatl, which is obtained as a possible reward from the Lunar Chest in Neypotzli. Alternatively the darts can be crafted, requiring level 74 Fletching, Headless atlatl dart and Atlatl dart tips. Ironmen additionally require 54 Slayer in order to obtain broken antlers, which are required to make the dart tips.

The atlatl dart has no bonuses as the eclipse atlatl uses the player's melee strength bonus to deal damage.

Despite being called darts, atlatl darts cannot be loaded into the toxic blowpipe, and they deal standard ranged damage.

Despite being equipped in the ammo slot, they can not be stored in Dizana's quiver. Attempting to do so displays the following message: "You have nothing in your worn quiver to fill your Dizana's Quiver with."

Atlatl darts are compatible with Ava's devices, however the Ranged strength bonus on them will not affect their damage, making other capes like a Fire cape more preferable if not concerned with saving the darts.
28997:
The dual macuahuitl (in English pronounced roughly mah-KUA-weetl) is a non-degradable two-handed spiked weapon that requires level 70 Attack and 75 Strength to equip, which is obtained as a possible reward from the Lunar Chest in Neypotzli.

The weapon hits twice per attack, spaced 1 game tick apart when attacking monsters, and dealing damage in two hitsplats, with both hitsplats having their max hit halved. If the player has an odd maximum hit, the first hit's maximum damage will be rounded down and the second hit's will be rounded up, e.g. a maximum hit of 25 will be split into two maximum hits of 12 and 13.

Each hitsplat has its own accuracy check. However, unlike other two-hit weapons like Torag's hammers or sulphur blades, where both checks are independent (either can hit or miss without affecting the other, equivalent to two separate hits with a single-hit weapon), the Dual macuahuitl checks the two hits sequentially, and the second check will only proceed if the first succeeds.

If the first accuracy check succeeds, damage will be rolled for the first hit, and a second accuracy check will then be performed for the second hit. If the first accuracy check fails, the second check will not proceed at all, and both hits will deal no damage. As a result, one "half" of the weapon's DPS functions normally, while the other "half" is reduced due to requiring both accuracy checks to succeed.

This is an intentional design to push the weapon into a niche against targets with lower Defence levels and mirrors the attacks of the Moons of Peril, which check accuracy in the same way.

As a slight counterbalance to this drawback, the dual macuahuitl has relatively high attack bonuses for its attack speed and level requirements. Its Crush bonus substantially exceeds that of the abyssal bludgeon and rivals the combined crush bonus of an inquisitor's mace and avernic defender.
29000:
The eclipse atlatl is a non-degradable two-handed ranged weapon that requires level 75 Ranged, 50 Attack, and 50 Strength to equip. It can be obtained as a possible reward from the Lunar Chest in Neypotzli. It uses atlatl darts as ammunition, which can be collected by Ava's devices.

Despite not being strung and using a “throwing” attack animation, the atlatl is categorically a bow and not a thrown weapon, and therefore deals standard-type damage.

Its max hit is determined by the player's melee strength bonus, while accuracy is still based on their ranged bonus, which is a unique mechanic among ranged weapons.

The atlatl's max hit mechanic means it pairs unusually with other equipment; endgame ranged gear is not best-in-slot as usual. Instead, the atlatl performs better against low-defence enemies when used in conjunction with high-strength equipment (e.g. amulet of strength, dragon boots), while end-game tribrid equipment such as Barrows gloves, amulet of fury, and aranea boots will usually outperform specialised ranged gear against high-defence enemies.

Though the atlatl's max hit is based on visible boosts to the player's Strength level (including potions), it does not benefit from melee prayers. Ranged prayers boost both accuracy and damage. Additionally, it uses the melee bonuses from the slayer helmet and salve amulets, but gains increased damage from Void Knight equipment whilst wearing the void ranger helm rather than the void melee helm.

When using the rapid attack style, up to 2,000 darts may be fired per hour. This makes the cost per hour 51,600 with Ava's assembler, 72,240 with Ava's accumulator if not picking up used ammo, or 258,000 if choosing to use a different cape for more damage, such as the Infernal cape.

The attack speed of the Atlatl varies; in player versus monster encounters, its base attack speed is 4, or equal to shortbows. During player versus player combat, its base attack speed is 5, unless the full Eclipse armour set is worn.
29004:
The eclipse moon chestplate is an item that requires level 75 Ranged and 50 Defence to equip, which is obtained as a possible reward from the Lunar Chest in Neypotzli.

As with all Moon equipment it is degradeable, much like Barrows equipment. The armour starts at 3000 charges and loses 1 charge for every 54 seconds in combat, meaning it lasts for 45 hours of continuous combat before breaking. Having an NPC such as Bob and Dunstan repair it costs 1,500,000 coins when fully broken, while repairing it yourself at an armour stand adds a discount of 7,500 coins per Smithing level, reducing the price to 757,500 coins at level 99.

The chestplate, along with all other Eclipse moon armour, functions as a very capable hybrid armour, with its strength bonuses and relatively high ranged bonuses. This is useful in situations where it is desireable to bring fewer armour switches, while still being effective in multiple styles.

29077:
Cooked moss lizard is a type of food obtained by cooking raw moss lizards at the campsites within Neypotzli after partial completion of Perilous Moons. It can be used as food whilst fighting the Moons of Peril.

Level 30 Cooking is required to cook moss lizards, and up to three cuts of meat can be obtained from cooking one, with the chance depending on the player's Cooking level.

The amount of Hitpoints restored is 1/3rd of the player's Cooking level or 1/2 of their Hunter level, whichever heals less, rounded down.

When leaving Neypotzli, this item is removed from the player's inventory with the message: The resources from Neypotzli fizzle to dust as they are severed from its magic.
29079:
Moonlight grub paste is made by using a pestle and mortar on moonlight grubs, which are picked from grubby saplings within Neypotzli. Players can sometimes receive multiple paste from one grub, depending on their Herblore level.

Moonlight grub paste can be combined with a vial of water to create moonlight potions, which can be used as a potion whilst fighting the Moons of Peril to provide melee skill boosts and prayer restoration. Players may create an extra dose of potion, with the chance depending on the player's Herblore level.

Additionally, one moonlight grub paste is requested by Eyatlalli during Perilous Moons.

When leaving Neypotzli this item is removed from the player's inventory with the message: The resources from Neypotzli fizzle to dust as they are severed from its magic.
29080:
A moonlight potion is a potion created by adding moonlight grub paste to a vial of water. A dose of the moonlight potion provides a temporary skill boost to Attack, Strength, Defence, as well as restoring prayer points; the values of the boost vary depending on the player's Herblore level.

The potion can have 2-4 doses on creation, with chances of each varying depending on the player's Herblore level.

The potion cannot be taken out of Neypotzli. Doing so will revert the potion into a vial of water and the player will receive following message: The resources from Neypotzli fizzle to dust as they are severed from its magic.

Unlike prayer potions, moonlights potions do not benefit from the effects of the Holy wrench.

29084:
Sulphur blades are a two-handed weapon that requires level 55 Attack to wield, obtained as a rare drop from sulphur nagua in Neypotzli. Like their crush and stab equivalents, the glacial temotli and earthbound tecpatl, it performs two independently rolled hits per attack. The maximum damage of each hit is determined by calculating the combined max hit as normal and dividing it by two. If the combined max hit is odd, one max hit is rounded up while the other is rounded down (e.g., 45 → 22 + 23).

Their stats are nearly identical to the dragon scimitar, trading 2 strength bonus for 5 more slash accuracy, although the scimitar paired with a defender is considerably stronger.

As sulphur blades deal damage in two hitsplats, they are very good for training combat on sulphur nagua due to them taking an additional 4 minimum damage for each hitsplat. Additionally, moonlight potions are easy to make nearby and can be used to provide prayer points and melee stat boosts.
29087:
Sulphurous essence is an item dropped by sulphur nagua in Neypotzli. They can be given to Eyatlalli for 50 Runecraft experience each after completing Perilous Moons.

Leaving Neypotzli will cause any sulphurous essence in the player's inventory to be removed, accompanied by the message The resources from Neypotzli fizzle to dust as they are severed from its magic.. However, players can drop their essence before leaving and pick it up again after returning if they are fast enough.

It is always lost on death, even if reclaiming from the gravestone within the ruins.
29088:
Calcified deposit is an item that can occasionally be obtained from mining calcified rocks in the Cam Torum mine.

It can be crushed with a hammer by using it on an anvil, producing blessed bone shards or calcified moths. This process provides 1 Smithing experience and takes 3 ticks per deposit. On average, each deposit gives 7.5 shards.
29090:
Calcified moths are a single-use item that can teleport players to Cam Torum.

They require partial completion of Perilous Moons to use, up through killing the Sulphur Nagua to receive permission to enter the city. They cannot be used beyond level 20 Wilderness. When crushed, a game message in the chatbox will state You crush the moth, releasing the energy inside...

They are obtained by using a calcified deposit on any anvil with a hammer; the rate of obtaining them from a calcified deposit is 1 in 4.

Despite having a high alchemy value of 6,000 coins, calcified moths cannot be alched. However, they can be sold to general stores for 4,000 to 6,000 coins, depending on the store.

29131:
Cooked barb-tailed kebbit is a type of hunter meat that restores a total of 12 Hitpoints when eaten, 7 are restored immediately, 5 are restored after a delay of 7 ticks (4.2s). Eating another hunter meat too quickly will waste any pending healing, as the most recent delayed heal will replace older effects that have not completed yet. Standard foods and potions do not interrupt this pending heal.

It can be obtained by cooking raw barb-tailed kebbit on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 32 Cooking and granting 106 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt kebbit. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 63 on both ranges and fires.
29134:
Cooked dashing kebbit is a type of hunter meat that restores a total of 23 Hitpoints when eaten, 13 are restored immediately, 10 are restored after a delay of 7 ticks (4.2s). The secondary heal also restores 10 points of run energy. Eating another hunter meat too quickly will waste any pending healing, as the most recent delayed heal will replace older effects that have not completed yet. Standard foods and potions do not interrupt this pending heal.

It can be obtained by cooking raw dashing kebbit on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 82 Cooking and granting 215 experience when successful. 50 Hunters' Rumours must be completed before they may be cooked. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt kebbit. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Cooked dashing kebbit never stop burning altogether even at level 99, unless the player is wearing a Cooking cape.

Dashing kebbit is the third-highest healing single consumption food, surpassing the dark crab, bluefin, anglerfish, tuna potato, and manta ray, but is surpassed by cooked moonlight antelope and marlin. Dashing kebbit heals 23 health, but part of the healing is delayed, making it not always practical. Cooked moonlight antelope also has delayed healing, heals 26 health, and also cures poison when eaten. The other foods heal the full 22 Hitpoints instantly, anglerfish can heal the player above their base Hitpoints, and bluefin also restores 5 Prayer points.
29143:
Cooked moonlight antelope is a type of hunter meat that restores a total of 26 Hitpoints when eaten, 14 are restored immediately, 12 are restored after a delay of 7 ticks (4.2s). The secondary heal also cures poison and reduces venom to poison. Eating another hunter meat too quickly will waste any pending healing, as the most recent delayed heal will replace older effects that have not completed yet. Standard foods and potions do not interrupt this pending heal.

It can be obtained by cooking raw moonlight antelope on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 92 Cooking and granting 220 experience when successful. 50 Hunters' Rumours must be completed before they may be cooked. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt antelope. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Moonlight antelope will never stop burning altogether even at level 99, unless the player is wearing a Cooking cape.

Moonlight antelope is the highest-healing single-consumption food, surpassing the marlin and cooked dashing kebbit. Moonlight antelope heals 26 health, but part of the healing is delayed, making it sometimes impractical. Dashing kebbit also has delayed healing, but heals only 23, and restores 10 run energy when eaten. Marlin heals 24 instantly, while others such as manta rays heal 22 instantly.

29186:
A ruby harvest mix is a type of hunter's mix that players can drink to boost their Attack level by 4 + 15% of their Attack level, rounded down. If drunk in a multicombat area, up to three players who are standing within two tiles of the drinker will receive the same boost, provided that they have Accept Aid toggled on.

They are made by using a jarred ruby harvest with certain meats acquired from hunter creatures; doing so requires a pestle and mortar, and does not appear to have any skill requirements associated to mix them.
29195:
A moonlight moth mix is a type of hunter's mix that players can drink to restore 22 Prayer points per dose. The effect of the holy wrench does not apply to this item.

If drunk in a multicombat area, up to three players who are standing within two tiles of the drinker will receive the same effect, provided that they have Accept Aid toggled on. This effectively works as a cheaper Prayer potion, without requiring either Herblore levels or ingredients. For Group Ironmen, the moonlight moth mix can be shared, while the non-mix variant cannot.

They are made by using a jarred moonlight moth with hunter meat acquired from hunter creatures; doing so requires a pestle and mortar, and does not have any skill requirements associated to mix them.

A quick way for Ironmen to obtain raw hunter meat is by catching dashing kebbits in the Piscatoris falconry area.

29238:
A salamander claw is a rare creature part that may be obtained from tecu salamanders as part of Hunters' Rumours.

Upon receiving a rare creature part, a game message in the chatbox will state You find a rare piece of the creature! You should take it back to the Hunter Guild.
29240:
A moonlight moth wing is a rare creature part that may be obtained from moonlight moths as part of Hunters' Rumours. The moonlight moth wing can be collected without the use of a butterfly net or butterfly jars. This requires a Hunter level of 85 for catching moonlight moths barehanded.

Upon receiving a rare creature part, a game message in the chatbox will state You find a rare piece of the creature! You should take it back to the Hunter Guild.
29242:
Basic hunters' loot sacks are a reward for successfully completing novice Hunters' Rumours assigned by Huntmaster Gilman.

Opening them rolls 5 times on the loot table; however, unlike other hunters' loot sacks, the basic sack does not drop enhanced quetzal whistle blueprints, huntsman's kits, or pieces of the guild hunter outfit.
29244:
Adept hunters' loot sacks are a reward for successfully completing adept Hunters' Rumours assigned by Guild Hunter Cervus or Ornus.

Opening them rolls 7 times for resources, and also has a chance to reward the enhanced quetzal whistle blueprint, the huntsman's kit, and pieces of the guild hunter outfit.
29246:
Expert hunters' loot sacks are a reward for successfully completing expert Hunters' Rumours assigned by Guild Hunter Aco or Teco.

Opening them rolls 9 times for resources, and also has a chance to reward the enhanced quetzal whistle blueprint, the huntsman's kit, and pieces of the guild hunter outfit. Expert and master sacks also drop perfected quetzal whistle blueprints, and rarely the Quetzin pet.
29248:
Master hunters' loot sacks are a reward for successfully completing master Hunters' Rumours assigned by Guild Hunter Wolf.

Opening them rolls 11 times for resources, and also has a chance to reward the enhanced quetzal whistle blueprint, the huntsman's kit, and pieces of the guild hunter outfit. Master and expert sacks also drop perfected quetzal whistle blueprints, and rarely the Quetzin pet.
29251:
Basic quetzal whistle blueprints are used to craft basic quetzal whistles, alongside willow logs and a knife.

Upon completing 10 Hunters' Rumours, players can obtain one for free from Soar Leader Pitri; subsequent blueprints will cost 500 coins.
29263:
The guild hunter headwear is a piece of the guild hunter outfit that can be looted from hunters' loot sacks, which are obtained upon completing Hunters' Rumours.

When worn, it increases the catch rate of hunter creatures by 0.2%, increased to 2.5% when wearing the full set. It also increases the chance of receiving a rare creature part by 0.4%, or 5% with the full set.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Hunters Outfit set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored. Alternatively, it can be stored in the huntsman's kit.

Duplicate pieces can be given to Verity for a master-level hunters' loot sack which excludes uniques.
29265:
The guild hunter top is a piece of the guild hunter outfit that can be looted from hunters' loot sacks, which are obtained upon completing Hunters' Rumours.

When worn, it increases the catch rate of hunter creatures by 0.8%, increased to 2.5% when wearing the full set. It also increases the chance of receiving a rare creature part by 1.6%, or 5% with the full set.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Hunters Outfit set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored. Alternatively, it can be stored in the the huntsman's kit.

Duplicate pieces can be given to Verity for a master-level hunters' loot sack which excludes uniques.
29267:
The guild hunter legs are a piece of the guild hunter outfit that can be looted from hunters' loot sacks, which are obtained upon completing Hunters' Rumours.

When worn, it increases the catch rate of hunter creatures by 0.6%, increased to 2.5% when wearing the full set. It also increases the chance of receiving a rare creature part by 1.2%, or 5% with the full set.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Hunters Outfit set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored. Alternatively, it can be stored in the the huntsman's kit.

Duplicate pieces can be given to Verity for a master-level hunters' loot sack which excludes uniques.
29269:
The guild hunter boots are a piece of the guild hunter outfit that can be looted from hunters' loot sacks, which are obtained upon completing Hunters' Rumours.

When worn, it increases the catch rate of hunter creatures by 0.4%, increased to 2.5% when wearing the full set. It also increases the chance of receiving a rare creature part by 0.8%, or 5% with the full set.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Hunters Outfit set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored. Alternatively, it can be stored in the the huntsman's kit.
