29271:
A basic quetzal whistle is a teleportation item that takes players to any built Quetzal Transport System landing site. When the teleport function is clicked, it will open the transport interface. It cannot be used beyond level 20 Wilderness.

The whistle is made via the right-click "Craft" option on a basic quetzal whistle blueprint, whilst having willow logs and a knife in the inventory. The blueprints are initially obtained for free from Soar Leader Pitri after completing 10 Hunters' Rumours, with subsequent blueprints costing 500 coins. Players can then craft and charge more whistles, carrying or storing away as many as they'd like.

The basic whistle can hold up to 5 charges, but can be upgraded to an enhanced quetzal whistle, which holds up to 20. The "Check" option will display a message containing the whistle's remaining charges, e.g. Your quetzal whistle has 4 charges remaining.. Lastly, the "Rumour" option on the whistle will remind players of their active rumour, e.g. Your current rumour target is a grey chinchompa. You'll need to bring back some of its fur. Cervus was the source of the rumour..

Quetzal whistles may be used to teleport to any built landing site in the Quetzal Transport System without needing to unlock Renu during Twilight's Promise.

There is an option in the game settings to configure the quetzal whether to open a map or directly teleport you to the guild. The tickbox for this can be found under the Gameplay section.
29277:
Trapper's tipple is a type of ale that temporarily boosts Hunter by 2 while draining Strength by 1 and Attack by 2.

It is purchasable from Huntmaster Gilman, who runs The Burrow pub in the Hunter Guild, requiring a minimum Hunter level of 46 (not boostable) to access. Three spawns can also be found on the tables inside the Burrow. Unlike other ales, it cannot be created through brewing.

Upon drinking the ale, a message in the chatbox will state You drink the Trapper's Tipple and feel ready to catch some creatures. You feel less able to fight said creatures.
29295:
The small meat pouch is an item that can store up to 14 pieces of hunter meat. It is made with level 35 Crafting from 4 fox fur, as well as a needle and thread; doing so grants 30 Crafting experience.

Players can right-click to open the pouch, which will have hunter meats that the player acquires to be automatically placed inside the pouch, provided there is space for it. Players can check the contents of the pouch by selecting the "Check" right-click option, which tells the number of meats the player has inside. The pouch does not store raw bird meat, despite being acquired from hunting. Players may empty the pouch by right-clicking "Empty" on the item within a bank, whilst the bank or deposit box interface is open, or on the top floor of the Hunters' Guild. However, players cannot empty their meat pouches into their inventory whilst inside both Mor Ul Rek's outer and inner parts of the city.

It can be upgraded into a large meat pouch with 65 Crafting and 3 sunlight antelope fur. If you already own a large meat pouch, the items stored by a small pouch will overwrite those pouches during this process and may delete items from the game.

The pouch shares its inventory with every small meat pouch you own. This means creating multiple pouches will not let you store more meat. If you have multiple pouches in your inventory, and destroy any of the other small meat pouches, all contents throughout your inventory and bank will be removed (You can however use a large meat pouch to store meat and craft multiple small meat pouches during a Pyre fox Hunters' Rumours and cast High Level Alchemy to make 1,800 coins every 4 fox fur you get). If you cast High Level Alchemy on a small meat pouch full of meat and then craft a new one the meat will remain in the pouch.
29297:
The large meat pouch is an item that can store up to 28 pieces of hunter meat. It is made with level 65 Crafting by upgrading a small meat pouch with 3 sunlight antelope fur as well as a needle and thread, granting 60 Crafting experience. A costume needle can also be used in place of the regular needle and thread. The small meat pouch must be closed before the player can upgrade it.

Players can right-click to open the pouch. Whilst open, hunter meats obtained from hunting will automatically go into the pouch if there is enough space. Players can check the number of meats inside with the right-click "Check" option.

The large meat pouch can only be emptied within a bank or while on the top floor of the Hunters' Guild. The meats can be emptied into the inventory or into the bank (if the bank or deposit box interface is open) via the right-click "Empty" option or by shift-clicking the pouch (if shift-click item dropping is enabled). The pouch cannot be emptied into the inventory at these banks:

Emerald Benedict in Rogues' Den, however the nearby bank chest works.

Eniola inside the Ourania Cave.

Odovacar in Tarn's Lair.

The pouch shares its inventory with every meat pouch the player owns. Creating multiple pouches will not let the player store more meat. If the player destroys any of the pouches, all the meats inside will be removed.
29299:
Small fur pouches are an item that can store up to 14 furs acquired from hunter creatures. They are made with level 35 Crafting from 4 larupia fur, as well as a needle and thread, granting 20 Crafting experience. A costume needle can also be used in place of the regular needle and thread.

Players can right-click to open the pouch, which will have furs that the player acquires from hunting to be automatically placed inside the pouch, provided there is space for it. Players can check the contents of the pouch by selecting the "Check" right-click option, which tells the number of furs the player has inside. Players may empty the pouch at a bank or a bank deposit box by right-clicking "Empty" on the item whilst the bank interface is open.

A small fur pouch is required to make a medium fur pouch, alongside level 50 Crafting and 3 graahk fur.

The pouch shares its inventory with every pouch you own. This means creating multiple pouches will not let you store more furs. If you have multiple pouches in your inventory, and destroy any of the other pouches, all contents throughout your inventory and bank will be removed.

Tatty furs cannot be stored in the pouch.
29303:
Large fur pouches are an item that can store up to 28 furs acquired from hunter creatures; non-hunter furs such as Grey wolf fur and bear fur cannot be stored in the pouch. They are made with level 65 Crafting by upgrading a medium fur pouch with 3 kyatt fur as well as a needle and thread, granting 60 Crafting experience. A costume needle can also be used in place of the regular needle and thread.

Players can right-click to open the pouch, which will have furs that the player acquires from hunting to be automatically placed inside the pouch, provided there is space for it. Players can check the contents of the pouch by selecting the "Check" right-click option, which tells the number of furs the player has inside. Players may empty the pouch at a bank or a bank deposit box by right-clicking "Empty" on the item whilst the bank interface is open.

The pouch shares its inventory with every fur pouch you own. This means creating multiple pouches will not let you store more fur. If you have multiple pouches in your inventory, and destroy any of the other pouches, all contents throughout your inventory and bank will be removed.

Tatty furs cannot be stored in the pouch.
29305:
The hunter's spear is a thrown weapon that requires level 55 Ranged and 30 Strength to equip. Compared to other ranged weapons, the player's melee strength bonuses are used when determining the amount of ranged damage dealt to a target. Ava's devices do work on these.

The hunter's spear when equipped also acts like a teasing stick and provides a 5% increased chance for teased creatures to walk into a pitfall trap. The spear must be equipped before being able to tease creatures. Teasing creatures does not consume the spear. Despite being a thrown weapon, it cannot be used to tease creatures from a distance, though it may be used to hunt stymphikes in place of makeshift spears (although it seems Ava's devices do not work while hunting stymphikes). The hunter's spear can be stored in the Huntsman's kit.

Additionally, it will not be consumed when attacking chinchompas to speed up and reset their spawns when Hunting.
29307:
Quetzal feed is a possible reward from completing Hunters' Rumours at the Hunter Guild. Ten are needed to build a landing site for the Quetzal Transport System. It may also be used to recharge the Quetzal whistle's teleports by 1. If quetzal feed is in the inventory when recharging the whistle, it may be lost.

A total of 60 quetzal feeds is required in order to build all landing sites.
29311:
Hunter spear tips are an item used in crafting hunter's spears that are obtainable from hunters' loot sacks, which are received as rewards upon completing Hunters' Rumours.

Players with level 60 Fletching (unboostable) can use a knife to create hunter's spears from five jerboa tails, a teak log, and five hunter spear tips. Spears are always crafted in batches of five, so a minimum of 5 spear tips must be used.
29317:
The tattered request note is obtained by speaking to Guildmaster Apatura after completing 50 Hunters' Rumours.

It can be reclaimed by searching the bookshelf upstairs in her quarters.
29321:
Apatura's note is a document offering information on how Apatura came to be guildmaster of the Hunter Guild.

After completing 150 Hunters' Rumours, players can speak to Apatura to receive her key, which unlocks the guildmaster's chest containing the note.
29323:
Apatura's key is obtained by speaking to Guildmaster Apatura after completing 150 Hunters' Rumours.

It is used to unlock the guildmaster's chest a floor above her quarters, which contains Apatura's note.
29325:
House keys can be obtained from pickpocketing wealthy citizens in Civitas illa Fortis at 50 Thieving. They can also be fished from the fishing spot within the park using a big fishing net.

At level 50 Thieving, house keys can be used in stealing valuables. A Thieving activity located in Civitas illa Fortis where players enter Victor's, Caius', or Lavinia's houses while they are unoccupied in order to steal valuables, after which they are consumed upon use.

Wearing a full set of rogue equipment doubles the number of house keys stolen from wealthy citizens.

Despite Oriana suggesting that the player uses them before they break, house keys do not actually break over time. They do, however, break in the door when used.
29332:
Valuables are acquired by stealing valuables from wealthy citizens' houses in Civitas illa Fortis. Found inside chests, wardrobes, and jewellery cases, valuables are stackable and will continue to be looted without clicking again for a time, granting 45 Thieving experience per valuable. Rogue equipment will not double the valuables obtained.

Occasionally, a flashing arrow will appear above one of the objects in the house, indicated by a game message in the chatbox stating You notice something shine somewhere else in the house.. These indicate that the player can get a one-time reward of 630 Thieving experience and 14 valuables from it.
29338: Blessed bone statuettes are items that may occasionally be obtained from stealing valuables. Though considered as contraband in Varlamore, players may break them down with a chisel to obtain 125 blessed bone shards (similar to that of blessed superior dragon bones at 121 blessed bone shards) and 5 Crafting experience.
29340: Blessed bone statuettes are items that may occasionally be obtained from stealing valuables. Though considered as contraband in Varlamore, players may break them down with a chisel to obtain 125 blessed bone shards (similar to that of blessed superior dragon bones at 121 blessed bone shards) and 5 Crafting experience.
29342: Blessed bone statuettes are items that may occasionally be obtained from stealing valuables. Though considered as contraband in Varlamore, players may break them down with a chisel to obtain 125 blessed bone shards (similar to that of blessed superior dragon bones at 121 blessed bone shards) and 5 Crafting experience.
29344:
Blessed bones are the blessed form of bones obtained by using them on the exposed altar on the summit of Ralos' Rise. They are broken down with a chisel to obtain 4 blessed bone shards and 5 Crafting experience, which can then be sacrificed at the libation bowl at the Teomat.

As each shard sacrificed gives 5 Prayer experience, each blessed bone gives 20 Prayer experience overall. If using a jug of blessed sunfire wine at the libation bowl instead of a regular jug of blessed wine, this is increased to 6 Prayer experience per shard, or 24 Prayer experience per bone.

Players looking to bless bones in bulk may talk to Virilis, found at the base of the exposed altar, to unnote any type of bones for a fee of 10 coins per bone.
29346:
Blessed bat bones are the blessed form of bat bones obtained by using them on the exposed altar on the summit of Ralos' Rise. They are broken down with a chisel to obtain 5 blessed bone shards and 5 Crafting experience, which can then be sacrificed at the libation bowl at the Teomat.

As each shard sacrificed gives 5 Prayer experience, each blessed bone gives 25 Prayer experience overall. If using a jug of blessed sunfire wine at the libation bowl instead of a regular jug of blessed wine, this is increased to 6 Prayer experience per shard, or 30 Prayer experience per bone.

Players looking to bless bones in bulk may talk to Virilis, found at the base of the exposed altar, to unnote any type of bones for a fee of 10 coins per bone.

Breaking-down these bones under the correct conditions will give a red token; when the player receives one, a game message will state You find a small token while breaking down bones.
29348:
Blessed big bones are the blessed form of big bones obtained by using them on the exposed altar on the summit of Ralos' Rise. They are broken down with a chisel to obtain 12 blessed bone shards and 5 Crafting experience, which can then be sacrificed at the libation bowl at the Teomat.

As each shard sacrificed gives 5 Prayer experience, each blessed bone gives 60 Prayer experience overall. If using a jug of blessed sunfire wine at the libation bowl instead of a regular jug of blessed wine, this is increased to 6 Prayer experience per shard, or 72 Prayer experience per bone.

Players looking to bless bones in bulk may talk to Virilis, found at the base of the exposed altar, to unnote any type of bones for a fee of 10 coins per bone.
29352:
Blessed babydragon bones are the blessed form of babydragon bones obtained by using them on the exposed altar on the summit of Ralos' Rise. They are broken down with a chisel to obtain 24 blessed bone shards and 5 Crafting experience, which can then be sacrificed at the libation bowl at the Teomat.

As each shard sacrificed gives 5 Prayer experience, each blessed bone gives 120 Prayer experience overall. If using a jug of blessed sunfire wine at the libation bowl instead of a regular jug of blessed wine, this is increased to 6 Prayer experience per shard, or 144 Prayer experience per bone.

Players looking to bless bones in bulk may talk to Virilis, found at the base of the exposed altar, to unnote any type of bones for a fee of 10 coins per bone.
29354:
Blessed babywyrm bones are the blessed form of wyrmling bones obtained by using them on the exposed altar on the summit of Ralos' Rise. They are broken down with a chisel to obtain 21 blessed bone shards and 5 Crafting experience, which can then be sacrificed at the libation bowl at the Teomat.

As each shard sacrificed gives 5 Prayer experience, each blessed bone gives 105 Prayer experience overall. If using a jug of blessed sunfire wine at the libation bowl instead of a regular jug of blessed wine, this is increased to 6 Prayer experience per shard, or 126 Prayer experience per bone.

Players looking to bless bones in bulk may talk to Virilis, found at the base of the exposed altar, to unnote any type of bones for a fee of 10 coins per bone.
29356:
Blessed dragon bones are the blessed form of dragon bones obtained by using them on the exposed altar on the summit of Ralos' Rise. They are broken down with a chisel to obtain 58 blessed bone shards and 5 Crafting experience, which can then be sacrificed at the libation bowl at the Teomat.

As each shard sacrificed gives 5 Prayer experience, each blessed bone gives 290 Prayer experience overall. If using a jug of blessed sunfire wine at the libation bowl instead of a regular jug of blessed wine, this is increased to 6 Prayer experience per shard, or 348 Prayer experience per bone.

Players looking to bless bones in bulk may talk to Virilis, found at the base of the exposed altar, to unnote any type of bones for a fee of 10 coins per bone.
29376:
Blessed dagannoth bones are the blessed form of dagannoth bones obtained by using them on the exposed altar on the summit of Ralos' Rise. They are broken down with a chisel to obtain 100 blessed bone shards and 5 Crafting experience, which can then be sacrificed at the libation bowl at the Teomat.

As each shard sacrificed gives 5 Prayer experience, each blessed bone gives 500 Prayer experience overall. If using a jug of blessed sunfire wine at the libation bowl instead of a regular jug of blessed wine, this is increased to 6 Prayer experience per shard, or 600 Prayer experience per bone.

Players looking to bless bones in bulk may talk to Virilis, found at the base of the exposed altar, to unnote any type of bones for a fee of 10 coins per bone.
29381:
Blessed bone shards are used to make sacrifices at the libation bowl at the Teomat, requiring level 30 Prayer. Each bone shard sacrificed gives 5 Prayer experience with blessed wine, or 6 experience with blessed sunfire wine. One jug of blessed wine will sacrifice 400 bone shards.

To make sacrifices, the libation bowl must be filled with jugs of blessed wine or jugs of blessed sunfire wine, and the player must have at least 2 Prayer points to perform it. The passive effect of Zealot's robes can be used to save some shards while sacrificing them. The chance to preserve material is calculated for each individual shard, rather than the entire set of 100 for every action taken. Up to 100 shards can be sacrificed per action at the libation bowl. Each jug of blessed (sunfire) wine poured into the libation bowl allows for 400 shards to be sacrificed.

Blessed bone shards can be obtained from various activities in Varlamore, such as breaking down sun-kissed bones and blessed bone statuettes, mining calcified rocks, blessing bones at the exposed altar, and rummaging through offerings from Vale Totems. Additionally, you have a chance at obtaining shards when opening Hunters' loot sacks after completing Hunters' Rumours, when opening the Lunar Chest, and by doing the Colossal Wyrm Agility Course.
29382:
A jug of sunfire wine is an item created by using two sunfire splinters on a jug of wine whilst having a pestle and mortar in the inventory. Sunfire splinters cannot be added to a jug of blessed wine; it must be added to an unblessed jug of wine.

It is used in the process of sacrificing blessed bone shards at the libation bowl, where one jug can sacrifice 400 shards; players will also need 2 Prayer points for each sacrifice.

When blessed at the exposed altar found south of the Teomat, the wine becomes a jug of blessed sunfire wine. This can be used at the libation bowl, in place of a regular jug of blessed wine, to increase the Prayer experience gained per blessed bone shard from 5 to 6, equivalent to an increase of 400 Prayer experience per wine used.

When buying the sunfire splinters on the Grand Exchange, this results in a cost of 2.02 gp per Prayer experience.
29384:
A jug of blessed sunfire wine is an item created by blessing a jug of sunfire wine at the exposed altar found south of the Teomat, which is made by using two sunfire splinters on a jug of wine with a pestle and mortar in your inventory. Sunfire splinters cannot be added to a jug of blessed wine; it must be added to an unblessed jug first. It is used in the process of sacrificing blessed bone shards at the libation bowl, where one jug can sacrifice 400 shards. Players will also need 2 Prayer points per sacrifice.

When used at the libation bowl, in place of a regular jug of blessed wine, the Prayer experience gained per blessed bone shard is increased from 5 to 6, equivalent to an increase of 200 Prayer experience per sunfire splinter used for a total of 2400 experience per jug.

When buying the sunfire splinters on the Grand Exchange, this results in a cost of 2.02 gp per Prayer experience.

Be aware that the jug of blessed sunfire wine cannot be stored in the bank.
29386:
A jug of blessed wine is an item created by blessing a jug of wine at the exposed altar found south of the Teomat, requiring level 30 in Prayer. It is used in the process of sacrificing blessed bone shards at the libation bowl, where one jug can sacrifice 400 shards; players will also need 2 Prayer points for each sacrifice.

Alternatively, players may use a jug of blessed sunfire wine instead, which gives each bone shard 6 Prayer experience instead of 5. This requires having added two sunfire splinters to an unblessed jug of wine; sunfire splinters cannot be added to a jug of blessed wine.

The jug of blessed wine cannot be stored in the bank.
29388:
Tokens are items that can be found from completing a variety of specific daily tasks around Varlamore. According to Cobado, these tokens, alongside the four nasty tokens and purple token, were hidden by the capybaras of Varlamore as a test to see how far someone would go in collecting them all.

Players may only gain a token from a singular source per account per day, which is based on the length of the player's character name and the day of the week (see below). For instance, on Mondays, players with 4-character long names can only get a token from the pickpocketing activity described below. A player cannot receive a token from a given source if a token from the same source is in their inventory. They can receive a duplicate if the token is in their bank, however. Whether in the bank or inventory, these tokens do not stack.

By wearing one or two (but not all three) of the required items for the easy emote clue, and yawning within the Grand Museum in Civitas illa Fortis, the Collector will appear with special dialogue related to the tokens, reacting if the player has at least one token in their inventory, responding that they need more. With all 7 tokens in the inventory, the player will be given a nice key in exchange for the tokens.

However, it is not recommended to trade the tokens in for the key until the blueberry muffin has been obtained. Bringing all 7 red tokens along with the 4 nasty tokens and the 1 purple token to Cobado will result in a one time reward for 100,000 and the blueberry muffin.

29412:
Steamforge brew is an alcoholic beverage that can be bought at The Lost Pickaxe in Cam Torum or the Stick Your Ore Inn in Mistrock for 8 coins. When drunk, the ale heals 1 Hitpoint and temporarily increases the player's Mining and Magic by 1, and temporarily decreases the player's Attack and Defence by 5% + 2, of their current level, rounded down.

Upon drinking the ale, a message in the chatbox will state You drink the Steamforge brew. It has an odd metallic taste to it.
29415:
Eclipse Red is an alcoholic drink sold at The Flaming Arrow in Civitas illa Fortis, as well as at Moonrise Wines and Sunlight's Sanctum on Aldarin. Drinking it restores 16 Hitpoints and temporarily boosts Woodcutting by 1 while draining Attack by 5 and Fletching by 1. It can also be found at the Hunter Guild, at the top floor of Guildmaster Apatura's quarters.

Upon drinking the wine, a message in the chatbox will state, You drink the Eclipse red. It tastes great, but maybe not 1,000 coins great.

These are a popular money-making method for ironmen, which consists of grabbing the single wine spawn on the second floor of the Hunter Guild and hopping worlds in order to grab more wines, then later selling them in noted form in Moonrise Wines at 700 gp apiece.

According to the book Moonrise Wines, Eclipse Red has distinct flavours of redberry, dwellberry, oak, and teak, pairing well with roasted meats and meaty pies.
29418:
Moon-lite is an alcoholic drink sold at various pubs throughout Varlamore. When drunk, the ale heals 5 Hitpoints, temporarily increases the player's Strength level by 5% + 1, and temporarily decreases the player's Attack level by 5% + 1.

Upon drinking the ale, a message in the chatbox will state You drink the Moonlite. It's very strong and leaves you feeling a bit dizzy.
29428:
Chef's notes are obtained from searching the supply crates at campsites in Neypotzli, after having built them during Perilous Moons.

The notes describe the properties of cooked moss lizards and cooked bream, as well as a possible explanation as to why certain resources gathered in the prison fizzle to dust.
29437:
The egg priest robe is an item that can be obtained from participating in any Easter event, and was first obtained from the 2024 Easter event.

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room, as part of the 2024: Egg priest vestments set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
29439:
The egg priest robe top is an item that can be obtained from participating in any Easter event, and was first obtained from the 2024 Easter event.

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room, as part of the 2024: Egg priest vestments set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
29449:
Zombie pirate keys are dropped by zombie pirates found at the Wilderness Chaos Temple. They are used to open the pirates' lockers on the shipwreck located on the coast east of the Chaos Temple.

The loot obtained from the lockers is almost completely identical to that from killing zombie pirates, but with the quantity of each drop doubled. The sole exception is the teleport anchoring scroll, with an unchanged quantity but a significantly increased drop rate.

Zombie pirate keys are always lost on death in PvP. In a non-PvP death, the keys always appear in the player's gravestone, and cannot be protected using the Protect Item prayer.
29455:
A teleport anchoring scroll is an item obtained as loot from zombie pirates and Zombie Pirate's Lockers. It can be read to become permanently impervious to teleport attacks by elder chaos druids and abyssal demons. This effect will not apply to teleport attacks from the Abyssal Sire, the Confusion attack of the Chaos Elemental, or the Tele Block spell.

Players are able to check if they have already read the scroll by right-clicking the "Check" option on the zombie pirate at the shipwreck found east of the Chaos Temple.
29462:
The small meat pouch is an item that can store up to 14 pieces of hunter meat. It is made with level 35 Crafting from 4 fox fur, as well as a needle and thread; doing so grants 30 Crafting experience.

Players can right-click to open the pouch, which will have hunter meats that the player acquires to be automatically placed inside the pouch, provided there is space for it. Players can check the contents of the pouch by selecting the "Check" right-click option, which tells the number of meats the player has inside. The pouch does not store raw bird meat, despite being acquired from hunting. Players may empty the pouch by right-clicking "Empty" on the item within a bank, whilst the bank or deposit box interface is open, or on the top floor of the Hunters' Guild. However, players cannot empty their meat pouches into their inventory whilst inside both Mor Ul Rek's outer and inner parts of the city.

It can be upgraded into a large meat pouch with 65 Crafting and 3 sunlight antelope fur. If you already own a large meat pouch, the items stored by a small pouch will overwrite those pouches during this process and may delete items from the game.

The pouch shares its inventory with every small meat pouch you own. This means creating multiple pouches will not let you store more meat. If you have multiple pouches in your inventory, and destroy any of the other small meat pouches, all contents throughout your inventory and bank will be removed (You can however use a large meat pouch to store meat and craft multiple small meat pouches during a Pyre fox Hunters' Rumours and cast High Level Alchemy to make 1,800 coins every 4 fox fur you get). If you cast High Level Alchemy on a small meat pouch full of meat and then craft a new one the meat will remain in the pouch.
29464:
The large meat pouch is an item that can store up to 28 pieces of hunter meat. It is made with level 65 Crafting by upgrading a small meat pouch with 3 sunlight antelope fur as well as a needle and thread, granting 60 Crafting experience. A costume needle can also be used in place of the regular needle and thread. The small meat pouch must be closed before the player can upgrade it.

Players can right-click to open the pouch. Whilst open, hunter meats obtained from hunting will automatically go into the pouch if there is enough space. Players can check the number of meats inside with the right-click "Check" option.

The large meat pouch can only be emptied within a bank or while on the top floor of the Hunters' Guild. The meats can be emptied into the inventory or into the bank (if the bank or deposit box interface is open) via the right-click "Empty" option or by shift-clicking the pouch (if shift-click item dropping is enabled). The pouch cannot be emptied into the inventory at these banks:

Emerald Benedict in Rogues' Den, however the nearby bank chest works.

Eniola inside the Ourania Cave.

Odovacar in Tarn's Lair.

The pouch shares its inventory with every meat pouch the player owns. Creating multiple pouches will not let the player store more meat. If the player destroys any of the pouches, all the meats inside will be removed.
29466:
Small fur pouches are an item that can store up to 14 furs acquired from hunter creatures. They are made with level 35 Crafting from 4 larupia fur, as well as a needle and thread, granting 20 Crafting experience. A costume needle can also be used in place of the regular needle and thread.

Players can right-click to open the pouch, which will have furs that the player acquires from hunting to be automatically placed inside the pouch, provided there is space for it. Players can check the contents of the pouch by selecting the "Check" right-click option, which tells the number of furs the player has inside. Players may empty the pouch at a bank or a bank deposit box by right-clicking "Empty" on the item whilst the bank interface is open.

A small fur pouch is required to make a medium fur pouch, alongside level 50 Crafting and 3 graahk fur.

The pouch shares its inventory with every pouch you own. This means creating multiple pouches will not let you store more furs. If you have multiple pouches in your inventory, and destroy any of the other pouches, all contents throughout your inventory and bank will be removed.

Tatty furs cannot be stored in the pouch.
29470:
Large fur pouches are an item that can store up to 28 furs acquired from hunter creatures; non-hunter furs such as Grey wolf fur and bear fur cannot be stored in the pouch. They are made with level 65 Crafting by upgrading a medium fur pouch with 3 kyatt fur as well as a needle and thread, granting 60 Crafting experience. A costume needle can also be used in place of the regular needle and thread.

Players can right-click to open the pouch, which will have furs that the player acquires from hunting to be automatically placed inside the pouch, provided there is space for it. Players can check the contents of the pouch by selecting the "Check" right-click option, which tells the number of furs the player has inside. Players may empty the pouch at a bank or a bank deposit box by right-clicking "Empty" on the item whilst the bank interface is open.

The pouch shares its inventory with every fur pouch you own. This means creating multiple pouches will not let you store more fur. If you have multiple pouches in your inventory, and destroy any of the other pouches, all contents throughout your inventory and bank will be removed.

Tatty furs cannot be stored in the pouch.
29474:
The prospector jacket is one part of the prospector outfit and is a reward from the Motherlode Mine in exchange for 60 Golden nuggets or from Volcanic Mine for 39,000 points. The jacket gives a Mining experience boost of 0.8% when worn.

Alternatively, a player can use the Varrock armour 4 from the elite Varrock Achievement diary to receive the experience bonus.

Like the rest of the Prospector kit, the jacket provides partial protection against the heat of the Kharidian desert, adding 12 seconds to the interval between required sips from a waterskin, or 34 seconds if the entire set is worn.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Prospector kit set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

Note: Any piece of the set that was purchased from the Petrified Pete's Ore Shop can't be sold for golden nuggets at the Prospector Percy's Nugget Shop. If you try to do this, you will receive the message "You can't sell this item back to Percy as you did not buy it from this shop".
29476:
The prospector legs are a part of the Prospector kit that can be bought from the Motherlode Mine in exchange for 50 golden nuggets or Volcanic Mine for 34,000 points. These leggings increase Mining experience by 0.6% when worn.

Like the rest of the Prospector kit, the legs provide partial protection against the heat of the Kharidian desert, adding 12 seconds to the interval between required sips from a waterskin, or 34 seconds if the entire set is worn.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Prospector kit set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

Note: Any piece of the set that was purchased from the Petrified Pete's Ore Shop can't be sold for golden nuggets at the Prospector Percy's Nugget Shop. If you try to do this, you will receive the message "You can't sell this item back to Percy as you did not buy it from this shop".
29480:
Agility Arena tickets are earned by taking part in the Brimhaven Agility Arena. One ticket and one Brimhaven voucher are earned for tagging a ticket dispenser. They are exchanged at the Agility Arena Store by talking to Pirate Jackie the Fruit for 345 Agility experience each, or 379.5 experience each with Karamja gloves 2 or higher equipped.

One ticket can be obtained per minute as the dispenser respawns every minute. Completion of the Elite Karamja Diary gives a 10% chance of receiving two Agility Arena tickets and Brimhaven vouchers when tagging a dispenser. Without the diary and never missing a dispenser, it takes at least 1 hour and 37 minutes for 100 tickets and around 16 hours for 1,000 tickets.

When doing Mourning's End Part II, Thorgel will not accept the discontinued Agility Arena Ticket. A new ticket must be obtained from the Brimhaven Agility Arena.
29486:
A cursed amulet of magic is an amulet uniquely dropped by necromancers in Great Kourend. It provides by far the lowest magic damage bonus for any item, at -80%.

The amulet's extreme penalty to magic damage has useful applications. It notably drops the maximum hit of Wind Strike above level 13 Magic from 8 to 2 and the maximum hit of Snare from 3 to 1; this allows Wind Strike or Snare to be used alongside the serpentine helm to apply venom to most NPCs, while still allowing them to regenerate to maximum Hitpoints. This technique is used to envenom while still giving kill credit to restricted accounts such as Ironmen and certain pures.

Against Olm, it can be used to keep his head turning while needing to delay dealing damage.
29489:
The rainbow cape is an event item originally unlocked by completing the 2024 Pride event. It is obtained from Gilbert in the flower field south-east of Barbarian Village, after which it can be obtained from Diango or retrieved from a toy box built in the costume room.

There are nine unique versions of the cape representing different variants of sexual orientation or gender identity, whose colours can be changed at any time by right-clicking the "Change" option on the cape. When switched to another style other than the pride (rainbow) style, the item is renamed to a colourful cape.

29518:
The unconscious broav is an item obtained during While Guthix Sleeps by catching a wild broav, using a pitfall trap and a Mort Myre fungus as bait.

It is brought to the hunting expert in order to have her train it to track scents, and is then given to the player as a broav.
29521: The dirty shirt is an item obtained from the Khazard Launderer during While Guthix Sleeps, after paying him 500 coins (or charming him with the ring of Charos(a)). Belonging to Movario, it is used on the broav to track his scent to his base.
29522: The waste-paper basket is an item found in Movario's base while investigating Movario's study for his notes during While Guthix Sleeps. The basket is picked up and searched for a ruby key to progress in the quest.
29524: Notes on pressure are an item obtained from the hidden room in Movario's study within his base. They detail his observations on weight and pressure, and is read to find a way to leave his study as teleportation is blocked within.
29525:
Movario's notes (volume 1) are the first half of Movario's documentation of his search for the Stone of Jas. He begins in the Wilderness, deeming it unworthy of further searching, and then moves to Morytania, the Temple of Ikov, the Digsite, and Lunar Isle, where he learns part of the stone's true name. He then proceeds to Shilo Village, Menaphos, and the Ancient Cavern, where he learns another name for the stone, the Eye of Saradomin, and discovers remnants of dragonkin architecture. Finally, he travels to the Lumbridge Swamp Caves and the Wizards' Tower, where he learns of another name for the stone, the Fist of Guthix.

The notes can be stored in and retrieved from the bookcase in a player-owned house.
29526:
Movario's notes (volume 2) are the second half of Movario's documentation of his search for the Stone of Jas. In them, he details how Lucien took interest in his search, detailing the events of the Temple of Ikov quest. He then mentions laying a false path to Draynor Village for Lucien's spies, as well as learning that the Temple of the Eye once held the Eye of Saradomin. He concludes by realizing the full power of the stone.

The notes can be stored in and retrieved from the bookcase in a player-owned house.
29530: Enriched snapdragon is a herb grown from an enriched snapdragon seed during While Guthix Sleeps. It must be used with the truth serum to make super truth serum during the quest.
29531:
The super truth serum is a special potion created during While Guthix Sleeps by using an enriched snapdragon on a truth serum.

It is used to interrogate the shady stranger in order to discover the possible whereabouts of Lucien.
29532: Truth serum is a special potion obtained during The Hand in the Sand quest. Players are able to make it by using a rose-tinted lens on the unfinished truth serum potion on the counter in Betty's Magic Emporium in Port Sarim.
29533: The suspect sketch is an item obtained during While Guthix Sleeps. It is a sketch of the Dark Squall, drawn from what the shady stranger tells you about his appearance while interrogating him.
29535:
The strange teleorb is an item obtained during While Guthix Sleeps by searching a desk located within the Dark Squall's inner base in the Black Knight Catacombs.

Belonging to Surok Magis, it is activated at the magic circle accessed from the ladder at the eastern side of the base, requiring one death rune and one law rune to activate. This teleports the player to Lucien's camp west of the Chaos altar. If activated anywhere else, it will say that it "doesn't seem to work here".

It can still be obtained and used after the quest from the same locations, should the player ever wish to return.
29536:
The teleorb is an item obtained from members of the Temple Knights during While Guthix Sleeps. Containing a sophisticated teleport spell, it is directly linked to the jail cell within the White Knights' Castle, allowing agents to discreetly teleport others against their will upon planting the orb on their person.

Players first receive one from Akrisae in order to interrogate one of Lucien's spies, and a second one is given by Silif after rescuing him in the Black Knight Catacombs to plant on the Dark Squall, who is later revealed as Surok Magis.

29572:
Silif is an item that may be placed into the player's inventory when Silif is following them during While Guthix Sleeps. Dropping it will cause him to follow the player, much like a pet does.

Because he cannot be picked up normally, the follower item is not intended to be received by players, but is used as a failsafe measure in the event that the Silif follower is forced into the player's backpack.
29573: A lit explosive is an item thrown by Surok Magis as part of his explosion attack during the fight against him in While Guthix Sleeps. To counter the attack, players must use Telekinetic Grab on the explosive, then cast either Low or High Level Alchemy on it; otherwise, they will take 45+ damage.
29574: A burning claw is an item rarely dropped by Tormented Demons. Two are used on each other in order to create the burning claws.
29583:
A smouldering heart is a rare untradeable item dropped by tormented demons. It is dropped on the same loot table as the smouldering gland and the smouldering pile of flesh, and acts as a one-use consumable item; unlike most items, which have a "Take" option on the ground, the Smouldering heart has a "Crush" option, and cannot be telegrabbed.

Crushing it releases energy from the heart, providing a significant stat boost to all combat stats; at level 99, the player receives a +20 level boost to Attack, Strength, and Defence, +14 to Ranged, and +11 to Magic. The smouldering heart energy will remain at their respective maximums for two minutes, after which they start decaying naturally. Note that a divine potion effect ending will reset the related stats as if they were part of the divine potion boost, and its effects carry over upon death.

Upon crushing the heart, a game message in the chatbox will state You crush the heart. Dark energy swirls around you... Players have ten minutes to crush the heart before it disappears from the ground; this timer is paused upon logging out.
29585:
A smouldering pile of flesh is an item commonly dropped by tormented demons. It is dropped on the same loot table as the smouldering gland and the smouldering heart, and acts as a multi-use consumable item; unlike most items, which have a "Take" option on the ground, the item has an "Eat-from" option, and cannot be telegrabbed.

Eating from the flesh will heal a set amount of health scaling to their Hitpoints level, capping at 18 at level 99; players can overheal from this, capping at 117 Hitpoints. If the player is at or above this cap, the player will not eat from it. The pile can be eaten from four times before disappearing (for a total of 72 Hitpoints at level 99), and does not confer the attack delay that usually occurs when eating food.

Upon consuming the flesh, a game message in the chatbox will state Even as the flesh burns your throat, you feel your wounds begin to mend. Players have ten minutes to eat from the pile of flesh before it disappears from the ground; this timer is paused upon logging out.
29587:
A smouldering gland is an item commonly dropped by tormented demons. It is dropped on the same loot table as the smouldering pile of flesh and the smouldering heart, and acts as a one-use consumable item; unlike most items, which have a "Take" option on the ground, the item has a "Crush" option, and cannot be telegrabbed.

Crushing it releases a blessing from the gland, regenerating prayer points over time in large increments (10–15 prayer points), lasting around 49 seconds. Teleporting away ends the regeneration effect.

Upon crushing the gland, a game message in the chatbox will state You crush the gland, releasing its unholy blessing. Players have ten minutes to crush the gland before it disappears from the ground; this timer is paused upon logging out.
29589:
Emberlight is a demonbane weapon requiring level 77 Attack to wield. It is made by using a tormented synapse on an anvil with an Arclight (must be fully charged, infused, or a combination of the two) and a hammer in the inventory. This requires level 74 Smithing (boostable) and having read Duradel's notes after completion of While Guthix Sleeps.

Arclight infusion and charges can be combined to reach the requirement for upgrading, with each percent of infusion being worth 100 charges (for example: 7,000 charges and 30% infusion).

Emberlight retains the same characteristics as Arclight (70% increased accuracy and damage against demons), but its primary advantages are that it no longer degrades, has higher combat stats, and has a stronger special attack against demons. However, some demons have modified demonbane effectiveness, which can either reduce or increase this bonus. For example, Duke Sucellus has 70% demonbane effectiveness, reducing the bonus to 49% accuracy and damage. Due to how max hits are calculated this would be comparable with having a weapon with a strength bonus 66 without any gear and up to 199 in maxed gear when fighting demons.

A player killer will receive the synapse from their opponent if it is not one of the protected items.
29594:
The purging staff is a one-handed magic demonbane weapon requiring level 77 Magic and 50 Attack to wield. It is made by using a tormented synapse on an anvil with a battlestaff, iron bar, and a hammer in the inventory. This requires level 74 Crafting[boostable], level 55 Smithing[not boostable], and having read Duradel's notes after completion of While Guthix Sleeps.

The purging staff can autocast offensive Arceuus or Standard spellbook spells, and its +37 magic attack and +25 magic defence bonuses are the highest of any weapon in the game, surpassing even the Kodai wand and Tumeken's shadow. In addition, the staff possesses a special attack as well as passive effects that makes it ideal for demonbane spells.

The process to create the purging staff can be reversed via the 'Revert' option, returning only the tormented synapse as a result. A player killer will receive the synapse from their opponent if it is not one of their protected items.
29596:
Duradel's notes are an item obtained from Kuradal after completion of While Guthix Sleeps. The notes can only be read once, awarding the player with Slayer experience equal to 15 times their Slayer level, similar to a book of knowledge. The player will also be able to craft high-tier demonbane weapons; emberlight, the scorching bow and purging staff after acquiring a tormented synapse, a rare drop from Tormented Demons.

The notes contain passages on demon slaying, with the player reading one specific passage on how to more easily defeat demons using body parts of other demons.

The book cannot be placed in a player-owned house bookcase. You can get another book if you lose it by talking to Kuradal.

29631:
Blighted overloads are a stat-boosting potion exclusive to Deadman Mode. Although they are listed in the Grand Exchange in all members worlds, they remain an unobtainable item outside of Deadman worlds. Players can make this potion at level 83 Herblore by combining a 4-dose super combat potion, ranging potion, and magic potion with a piece of chitin, which are obtained from killing monsters at a breach.

A dose of blighted overload, which can only be drunk in dangerous areas, will boost the player's offensive skills, reduce the player's Defence, and cause the player to take 10 damage over the course of 6 seconds (2 damage every 2 ticks). The stat boosts are re-applied every 15 seconds for five minutes until the effects wear off; for Defence, the level will decay if it is over 90% of the player's base level. The blighted overload effect will be removed if the player goes into a safezone with the effect active for longer than 11 ticks.

29651:
The Sigil of Revoked Limitation is a tier 2 Deadman Mode utility sigil. It is a permanent unlock that allows Wilderness weapons to be used to their full potential even when not in the Wilderness.

In Deadman: Annihilation, it can be purchased from the skull shop. It can be activated by clicking Attune and is a permanent unlock. There is no limit on how many permanent sigils can be active at once. Duplicate sigils can be sold back to the skull shop by using it on the deadman's skull.

In past Deadman Mode events, the un-attuned version was dropped by most monsters (via the Deadman Mode drop table) and was tradeable on the Grand Exchange.

In Deadman: Annihilation, the un-attuned version can be purchased from the skull shop. It can be activated by clicking Attune. Up to three attunable sigils can be attuned at once. Duplicate sigils can be sold back to the skull shop by using them on the deadman's skull.

29669:

In past Deadman Mode events, the un-attuned version was dropped by most monsters (via the Deadman Mode drop table) and was tradeable on the Grand Exchange.

29774:
Amy's saw (off-hand) is a variant of Amy's saw that can be equipped in the shield slot. The saw loses its combat bonuses, but otherwise functions identically to the normal variant.

The saw can be swapped back into its normal variant by using the "Swap" option.

This item can be stored in the magic wardrobe of a costume room.
29775:
Imcando hammer (off-hand) is a variant of the Imcando hammer that can be equipped in the shield slot. The hammer functions identically to the normal variant. The off-hand variant is particularly useful at Motherlode Mine as it allows the player to repair broken struts while still having a pickaxe equipped, and without taking up any inventory space.

The hammer can be swapped back into its normal variant by using the "Swap" option.

Although the main hand variant can be handed back to Ramarno for Barronite shards, attempting to return the off-hand hammer will not work.

This item can be stored in the magic wardrobe of a costume room.

It can also be used in a free-to-play world, despite being a members object. Though it can only be equipped in a members' world, if it is already equipped or in the player's inventory upon logging into a free-to-play world, the hammer retains its usual functionality, regardless of the player's membership status.
29784:
Araxyte venom sacs are items dropped by araxytes that serve as both a consumable and as a secondary ingredient used to create extended anti-venom+ potions. Each sac can upgrade one dose of anti-venom+ into a dose of extended anti-venom+, with this process requiring level 94 Herblore.

They can also be eaten to instantly cure venom and poison. Since they function as a normal piece of food, they can be combo eaten with karambwans. They provide immunity to poison for 11.7 minutes and venom for 0–18 seconds at the cost of dealing 4 venom damage a single time to the player; unlike most other sources of self-inflicted damage, this can kill the player. This is mostly done when acquired as a drop mid-trip, whilst the player has run out of anti-venom to drink. As they are stackable, they may also be used as protection from poison for very long trips whilst only taking one inventory space, such as during Dagannoth Kings tasks.

Unlike potions that cure poison or venom, the sacs will incur an attack delay of 3 ticks (1.8 seconds) when eaten, and clicking on the Hitpoints orb when afflicted does not consume one, even if it is the only form of antipoison available.
29788:
The araxyte head is a rare drop from araxytes, as well as Araxxor. It can be combined with a slayer helmet or slayer helmet (i) to create an araxyte slayer helmet or araxyte slayer helmet (i), respectively. Doing so requires purchasing the ability Eye see you for 1,000 Slayer reward points.

The araxyte head is an indirect requirement for recolouring the amulet of rancour to its silver variant, as an araxyte slayer helmet is required to obtain the recolour.

Unlike other slayer monster heads, the araxyte head is not a tertiary drop, cannot be stuffed and mounted in a skill hall, and cannot be sacrificed to the Dark Altar for Prayer experience.
29790: The noxious point is a rare drop from Araxxor. It can be combined with the noxious blade and noxious pommel to create the noxious halberd.
29792: The noxious blade is a rare drop from Araxxor. It can be combined with the noxious point and noxious pommel to create the noxious halberd.
29794: The noxious pommel is a rare drop from Araxxor. It can be combined with the noxious point and noxious blade to create the noxious halberd.
29796:
The noxious halberd is a two-handed polearm requiring level 80 Attack to wield. It is created by combining three untradeable components — the noxious point, noxious blade, and noxious pommel, all of which are rare drops from Araxxor.

As with all other polearms, the noxious halberd has a range of two tiles. Its most notable traits are that it attacks on a 5-tick cycle rather than 7, has more slash and strength bonus compared to the crystal halberd, and has a 33% chance (50% with a Serpentine helm equipped) to envenom the target (if not venom immune).

The noxious halberd will always deal the player's max hit when hitting the acidic, mirrorback, and ruptura araxytes that hatch during the fight with Araxxor. It can also deal full damage to the Corporeal Beast when on the stab attack style.
29799:
The araxyte fang is an item dropped by Araxxor. With a Crafting level of 86, it can be etched using a chisel to produce the tradeable etched araxyte fang, which is used to upgrade the amulet of torture into the amulet of rancour, giving 500 Crafting experience.

Based on Grand Exchange prices, the araxyte fang is worth 31,419,201 if used to upgrade an amulet of torture.
29801:
The amulet of rancour is the upgraded variant of the amulet of torture requiring level 90 Hitpoints to wear, providing best in slot melee strength and melee attack bonuses in all three types. It is made with level 86 Crafting by attaching the amulet of torture to an araxyte fang, which is a rare untradeable drop from Araxxor.

Compared to the amulet of torture, the amulet of rancour gains +10 melee attack bonuses and +2 strength bonus, but with negative bonuses for magic and ranged attacks.

The amulet of rancour can be recoloured to an amulet of rancour (s) by speaking to a man at the end of a series of tunnels within the Morytania Spider Cave, each of which have various requirements to pass through as alluded to in the venom-riddled note.
29804: The amulet of rancour (s) is an amulet of rancour recoloured to silver. To do so, players must navigate a series of tunnels within the Morytania Spider Cave with different requirements to reach its end, where players can then use the amulet on a man.
29806:
Aranea boots are a pair of boots dropped by araxytes. With no requirements to wear, they are currently the best-in-slot boots for one-defence pures and zerkers, due to the tribrid stats they have, with a ranged attack bonus between that of mixed hide boots and blessed dragonhide boots, a magic attack bonus equal to infinity boots, and a melee strength bonus equal to dragon boots.

The boots have a special web-negating mechanic that allows players to pass through webs in various locations without the need of a slash weapon. Additionally, the boots also negate certain special attacks once every 8 ticks (4.8 seconds) from arachnid bosses; when this occurs, a game message will state Your Aranea boots let you avoid the spider-based attack. The exception to this is Araxxor's venom cleave, which can be negated only once every 6 attacks, so every 12 seconds (20 ticks).

The following bosses can have their spider-based attacks negated:

Sarachnis' sticky web attack

Venenatis and Spindel's draining webs (The first tick is the only part of this ability negated)

Araxxor's venom cleave during his enrage phase

Araxxor's ranged auto attack; the magic auto attack is not negated.

Verzik Vitur's snapping webs during phase 3
29809:
A venom-riddled note can be found by searching a skeleton within the Morytania Spider Cave, who is found upon squeezing through the web tunnel immediately after entering the cave itself. Squeezing through the aforementioned web tunnel requires the player to wear aranea boots, otherwise the player will exclaim "Hmm there's too many webs in this tunnel, I think only a spider could get through this one!"

The note, encrypted using a Caesar shift, is a hint towards the many steps needed to acquiring an amulet of rancour (s), and can be decoded by shifting each letter right/forward 13 times in alphabetical order (ex. 13 letters after U is H). When decoded, the author is discovered to be signed by an individual named Contra, which hints at the usage of the Konami Code as directional inputs when navigating the first part of the web tunnels.
29816:
The araxyte slayer helmet is a piece of equipment that is worn in the helmet slot. It is a cosmetic upgrade to the Slayer helmet. It is required to be worn in order to proceed through the steps to recolour the Amulet of rancour to its silver variant.

It can be created by adding an araxyte head after purchasing the ability Eye see you for 1,000 Slayer reward points from any Slayer master. This is reversible, and the head will be returned to the inventory along with the slayer helmet's components. If a player loses the araxyte slayer helmet in a PvP death, the araxyte head will be placed in their gravestone.

The blue moon chestplate is an item that requires level 75 Magic and 50 Defence to equip, which is obtained as a possible reward from the Lunar Chest in Neypotzli.

When worn with all of the other pieces of the blue moon armour set, including the Blue moon spear, the player gains the Frostweaver set effect, where after casting a bind spell the blue moon spear has a 20% chance for its next melee attack to be unaffected by action delays. 29876:
The stone tablet is an item found by searching the skeleton laying by the southern pillar just west of the lift platform within the Ruins of Tapoyauik.

The tablet is notably inscripted in the common tongue by an individual named Maria, stating the Nela Tasol (Nela is an unknown word, while Tasol means Structure/Building in the Old Ones' language) has fallen, and that the Kuhu (also an unknown word, but likely referring to the Old Ones themselves) believe if her work failed, their entire legacy is lost. The stone tablet found in Mokhaiotl reveals that the work she was referring to was the creation of an archive to store the knowledge of the Old Ones.

Based on the available context, this tablet was likely inscribed sometime before the destruction of Mokhaiotl.

29889: Glacial temotli are a two-handed blunt weapon that requires level 55 Attack to wield, obtained as a rare drop from frost nagua and Amoxliatl in the Ruins of Tapoyauik. Like their slash and stab equivalents, the sulphur blades and earthbound tecpatl, it performs two independently rolled hits per attack. The maximum damage of each hit is determined by calculating the combined max hit as normal and dividing it by two. If the combined max hit is odd, one max hit is rounded up while the other is rounded down (e.g., 45 → 22 + 23). As a multi-hit weapon, it is especially useful against monsters that have negative flat armour, such as Nagua, since all successful hits will do extra damage to them.

The prop sword is a weapon first obtained as a reward from the 2018 Birthday event. It is the iconic sword seen in the logo of RuneScape from 2001 to 2007.

While equipped, players can right-click the sword in the Equipment Stats interface to perform an emote, in which players assume a fencing position and slash the air to create the letters "RS", the acronym for "RuneScape".

Despite being a sword, its combat styles are the same as those of a warhammer. It offers very large attack penalties and is nearly useless as an actual weapon. As such, it is allowed during "fun weapon" fights in legacy duels within the Emir's Arena.

When wielded, a "Slash" option will appear on other players. Picking this option will cause the player to slash their target. The hit is just an animation and no damage is dealt, nor does it count as entering combat. There is a chance that players may "fumble" the sword, dropping it to the ground where it must be picked up.

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room.

29974:
The prescription goggles are a piece of the alchemist's outfit purchased from the Mixology Rewards shop with 8,600 Mox resin, 7,000 Aga resin, and 9,350 Lye resin, which are earned from participating in the Mastering Mixology minigame. The goggles can be cosmetically changed between a focused and unfocused variant when in the inventory.

When worn, the goggles give a 10% chance to save a secondary ingredient when mixing most potions, reducing the cost of each potion by 1/9th of a secondary on average: 90 secondaries will on average be sufficient to mix 100 potions. As saved ingredients may be used in subsequent potions, the effect compounds on itself, making each secondary worth ~1.111 potions.

With stackable secondaries, the chance to trigger only occurs once per potion, saving a secondary for each dose the potion has (up to 4 equivalents for a 4-dose potion); no in-game text is displayed when secondaries are saved. When gaining an extra potion dose using a charged alchemist's amulet, you do not consume an equivalent of secondary for the extra dose. For example, when creating Anti-venom by combining Antidote++ with Zulrah's scales at 5 per dose, creating 4-dose potions will always save 20 scales when the Goggles proc. If creating 3-dose potions to take advantage of the Alchemist's amulet, the Goggles will always save 15 scales.

When making weapon poison(++), both nightshade and poison ivy berries can be saved, and when making haemostatic dressings both squid paste and cotton yarn can be saved. Additionally, the goggles can save caviar and roe when mixing barbarian potions, toadflax when mixing antidote+ (unf), irit when mixing antidote++ (unf), and torstols/torstol potions when mixing super combat potions or anti-venom+.

The goggles do not save crystal dust when mixing divine potions or ashes when making serum 207.

They can be sold back to the Mixology Rewards shop for 3,440 mox resin, 2,800 aga resin, and 3,740 lye resin.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Alchemist's outfit set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

The goggles do not save crystal dust when mixing divine potions or ashes when making serum 207.

29988:
The alchemist's amulet is an item purchased from the Mixology Rewards shop with 6,900 Mox resin, 5,650 Aga resin, and 7,400 Lye resin, which are earned from participating in the Mastering Mixology minigame. While the amulet is equipped, there is a 15% chance the player will create a potion with an extra dose when brewing potions (but with no extra experience), which consumes one charge. This effect works when adding secondaries to potions with fewer than 4 doses, such as anti-venom and stamina potions.

When first purchased, the amulet is pre-charged with 50 uses. Additional charges can be added by using amulets of chemistry on it, each giving 10 charges, up to a maximum of 5,000. On average, each Amulet of chemistry added will last for ~67 potions made, giving a fully charged Alchemist's amulet ~33,333 potions made, of which 5,000 will have an extra dose.

When the player uncharges the amulet, it returns amulets of chemistry in noted form, equal to the number of charges divided by 10 (rounded down).

Unlike the amulet of chemistry, there is no option on the amulet to stop the player from making potions once it has depleted all charges.

If killed by a player while wearing this amulet unprotected, it will appear at your gravestone with 0 charges.

29993:
Aldarium is a herblore secondary purchased from the Mixology Rewards shop with 80 Mox resin, 60 Aga resin, and 90 Lye resin, which are earned from participating in the Mastering Mixology minigame. It can also be obtained from a chest in the basement of the Alchemical Society's headquarters, by using an Alchemist's signet on the chest.

Aldarium can be combined with a harralander potion (unf) to create a goading potion, or with a huasca potion (unf) to create a prayer regeneration potion.
29996:
The reagent pouch is a storage item purchased from the Mixology Rewards shop with 13,800 Mox resin, 11,200 Aga resin, and 15,100 Lye resin, which are earned from participating in the Mastering Mixology minigame.

The pouch holds up to 26 of each Herblore secondary ingredient. When making herblore potions near a bank, the secondary ingredients will be used directly out of the bag, allowing for 26 potions to be made at a time instead of 14.

However, it is not possible to use unfinished potions directly on the pouch, necessitating a single unit of the secondary in question to make potions. For example, should the player want to make prayer potions, they would need 1 snape grass, the pouch (filled with 26 snape grass), and 26 unfinished ranarr potions in their inventory. The player would then use the snape grass on the ranarr potion with the pouch open to start making potions.

Players can fill their reagent pouch by selecting the "Fill" option, or by right-clicking the "Fill from inventory" option when the bank or deposit box interface is open. Players can right-click on the "Open" option to open the pouch, which will have secondaries that the player acquires automatically placed inside the pouch, provided there is space for them. Players can also check the contents of the pouch by selecting the "Check" right-click option, which states the number of each secondary ingredient the player has inside the pouch. Players can empty the pouch into their inventory by selecting the right-click "Empty" option, provided they are close enough to a bank. When the bank or deposit box interface is open and there are no compatible secondary ingredients in the player's inventory, the player can right-click on the "Empty to bank" option, which will empty all secondaries within the pouch into the player's bank.
30000:
The chugging barrel is a tradeable item that allows players to consume up to five potions in a single click. It is purchased from the Mixology Rewards shop at a cost of 17,250 Mox resin, 14,000 Aga resin, and 18,600 Lye resin. It is sold in a disassembled state (where it cannot store potions); players must use the 'Assemble' option in order for the barrel to become useable. The player is not required to have done the Mastering Mixology mini-game to assemble it. The barrel is only tradeable in its disassembled state. While the assembled barrel is untradeable, it is possible to dismantle the barrel at any time, although doing so will cause all potions currently stored inside to be lost.

The barrel can be filled by using up to five different potions on the item itself or via the bank loadout interface; a maximum of 100 doses per potion can be stored. Players can set up to four different loadouts in a bank for the barrel, as well as reorder the potions consumed, filling, and emptying the barrel. Potions and barbarian mixes can be stored, but hunter mixes cannot. Reordering potions allows players to consume potions in a specific order, such as Saradomin brews before super restores, allowing for stats to be boosted correctly. Vials will not be consumed after using all the contents inside the vial. When loading from presets, the barrel will pull from whichever interface is opened (i.e, if looking at potion storage when loading, the barrel will pull potions from pot storage). While it may be beneficial for certain players to place their super attack, strength, and defence potions inside the barrel and drink it as if it were a super combat potion, it is recommended to buy super combat potions since they are cheaper than the barrel.

The barrel may only be used within a bank or next to a bank chest. Certain bank interfaces do not allow the use of the barrel.

Ultimate Ironmen are able to store potion doses inside the chugging barrel and consume potions from it. However, they cannot set loadouts as it requires the use of a bank interface to do so. Its contents are also preserved even when the barrel is lost or deleted on death, able to be accessed after assembling a new chugging barrel. This allows it to be used for ghost storage, although due to the time investment to reobtain the barrel, this is not very useful.

The chugging barrel cannot be stored in Chambers of Xeric storage if accidentally brought into the raid. A disassembled chugging barrel can be stored in a Looting Bag.

30031:
Digweed can be harvested from digweed plants within the Mastering Mixology minigame. Using digweed with any potion in the minigame will double the amount of resin and Herblore experience gained when placing it on the conveyor belt.

Digweed can be obtained by picking the herb once it has matured, which happens periodically after depositing finished potions on the conveyor belt. The player will receive a notification in game chat indicating which corner of the lab has the matured plant. If not picked within 33 ticks (19.8 seconds), a mature digweed will die.

A potion can only be improved with digweed once; attempting to use multiple digweeds on the same potion returns the message This potion has already been improved with digweed.

Having any digweed in the inventory will prevent another digweed from spawning until used or destroyed, though using the drop trick, or mixing the digweed into an unfinished potion, allows the player to gather multiple digweeds.

Note: Leaving the lab will cause any digweed in the player's inventory to wither away, meaning they cannot be banked or stockpiled. When this happens, a game message appears stating Your digweed withers away as you leave the lab. However dropping the digweed while inside the minigame, leaving via teleport, and then telegrabbing it will allow you leave with the digweed.

Digweed cannot be banked; attempting to do so gives you this message A magical force prevents you from banking this item!. However, potions that have been improved with digweed can be banked.
30035:

30037:

Returning to the vineyard foreman with a full grape barrel rewards the player with 5 noted grapes.

Attempting to use the scroll without meeting the requirements displays the game message: You need to have visited Varlamore before you can teleport to the Colossal Wyrm Remains.
30042: The calcified acorn is a reward from the Colossal Wyrm Agility Course that can be purchased from Worm Tongue for 900 termites. Using it on a giant squirrel will allow it to metamorphose into a bone squirrel.

The tome of earth is a book held in place of a shield that is a possible reward from the Hueycoatl. The tome of earth requires level 50 in Magic to wield.

The tome is only tradeable when empty. When it is empty, its only function is its magic attack and magic defence equipment bonuses.

Empty tomes can be traded in for 250 soiled pages per tome (value of 651,500) by speaking to the seer at the Darkfrost.

30070:
The dragon hunter wand is a one-handed staff and wand, and dragonbane weapon requiring level 65 Magic to wield. It is obtained as a rare drop from the Hueycoatl.

The wand's dragonbane passive effect is that its accuracy is increased by 75% and damage increased by 40% when fighting draconic creatures, such as wyrms, wyverns, and hydras (but not Elvarg or revenant dragons). This stacks multiplicatively with the Slayer helm (i) or Elite Void Knight equipment, but not the salve amulet (i).

The wand can also autocast spells from the Standard spellbook and the Ancient spellbook.
30085: Hueycoatl hide is a reward dropped by the Hueycoatl. Unlike other hides, it does not need to be tanned and can be directly crafted into Hueycoatl hide armour.
30088:
Huasca seeds can be planted in a herb patch at level 65 Farming to yield grimy huasca, which is used to create prayer regeneration potions.

Nearby gardeners will not watch over herb patches, nor will a fully grown white lily plant protect them from disease.

They are obtainable from The Hueycoatl, Amoxliatl, Mature custodian stalker, Elder custodian stalker, and the chest inside the Ruins of Tapoyauik.

Huasca seeds are shown only on The Hueycoatl's Collection log. However, the seeds may also be logged in that slot if dropped by Amoxliatl or Mature and Elder custodian stalkers. The collection log slot will not be filled if obtained from the Ruins of Tapoyauik chest.
30097:
Huasca is a herb which requires level 58 Herblore to clean and yields 11.8 experience. Huasca can be grown in herb patches at level 65 Farming with a huasca seed.

They are used to create huasca potion (unf), which can be combined with aldarium to create prayer regeneration potions.

According to the book Gielinor's flora - herbs, huasca were used in rituals by the Old Ones in order to gain a deeper connection to their gods. It is believed that huasca can reveal hidden spiritual knowledge and restore balance to the soul, and is still used in Varlamore's religious traditions to this day.
30100: A huasca potion (unf) is an unfinished potion made by using a huasca on a vial of water. Using Aldarium on a huasca potion (unf) with 58 Herblore yields a prayer regeneration potion(3) and 132 Herblore experience.
30103:
Redberry antelope is an item made by Marla after giving her a raw sunlight antelope and redberries at the request of the guard Viero.

Upon giving it to him, Viero describes the meal as "interesting and complex", though the player thinks that the strong gamey flavour of the meats gives way to a tart sickly sweetness that doesn't complement it at all.
30107:
The loop half of key is an item obtained while doing specific skilling activities in Varlamore. It is used with a tooth half of key to make a moon key, which is used to open the moon chest in the Ruins of Tapoyauik. Receiving a loop half of key does not require completion of The Heart of Darkness.

It can be received through a variety of skilling activities in Varlamore:

Mining, including from the Cam Torum mine, the Ruins of Tapoyauik, and crashed stars across the region

Chopping trees

Fishing at any spot, except for the bream spots in Neypotzli.

If you receive a loop half of key while skilling and your inventory is full, it will drop to the ground under your character's feet. If lost in PvP, the item will drop as 12 coins for the killer.

Multiple loop halves can be received before finishing or using any moon keys. Note that loop halves cannot be dropped from Hunter creatures like sunlight antelope or when creating totems in the Vale Totems minigame.
30109:
The moon key is a key created by joining its loop half and tooth half together.

The loop half is received while performing skilling activities within Varlamore, such as chopping trees, fishing or mining in either the Cam Torum mine or Shooting Stars within the region. The tooth half is dropped by Amoxliatl, Hueycoatl, Doom of Mokhaiotl, and other creatures within Ruins of Tapoyauik.

The moon key can be used on the chest located within Ruins of Tapoyauik requiring completion of The Heart of Darkness to access.

Multiple moon key halves can be received before finishing or using any moon keys.
30137:
A goading potion is a potion made by using Aldarium on a harralander potion (unf), requiring 54 Herblore and granting 132 Herblore experience.

When consumed, the potion will cause any non-aggressive monsters within line of sight and a 9x9 tiled area around the player to gain aggression, including monsters which are not normally aggressive, such as dust devils. Each dose of goading potion will last for 6 minutes before wearing off.

Before drinking the potion within proximity of multiple mid to high level monsters, always be prepared. Be mindful of different monsters whose wander zone may overlap with the intended target of the goading potion. For example, a player killing warped jellies in the Catacombs of Kourend may not have the facemask needed to handle the dust devils immediately to the south. The effect of the goading potion may be cancelled at any time by drinking a cup of tea or teleporting away.

30151:
The giant squirrel is a skilling pet that can be obtained after completion of an Agility course, as well as from tagging marked ticket dispensers within the Brimhaven Agility Arena.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.
30152:

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. Since the Hueycoatl is in a pet restricted area, Huberte will always appear following the player. The pet may be kept in the encounter so long as boss arena is not exited. The Halloween scarecrow is a holiday reward received from completing a Halloween event from 2024 onwards. It can be planted on any free non-hotspot space in the Garden or on any free outdoor space of a player-owned house; the tile the player is facing must be empty in order to plant it.

The scarecrow, like the carved pumpkin head, can be customised in the same way by choosing the "Change" option when it is planted. Additionally, crows can also be summoned to perch on top of it if desired.

If lost or destroyed, the player can obtain another from Diango in Draynor Village.
