31075: Alan's blessed bones are the blessed form of Alan's bones obtained by using them on the exposed altar on the summit of Ralos' Rise. They are broken down with a chisel to obtain 5 blessed bone shards and 5 Crafting experience, which can then be sacrificed at the libation bowl at the Teomat.
31077:
On migration patterns is a book that can be found in the western end of the Stalker Den.

Written by a member of the Hunter Guild, the book details an unusually low migration season, and their discovery of a population of baby custodian stalkers. One of the reports on the topic sent to the guild, Auburn valley ecological reports, was also written by them.
31079:
Auburn Valley ecological reports is a book that can be found in the Burrow beneath the Hunter Guild, on a table in the eastern room.

Written by the same individual who wrote On migration patterns, it contains a copy of the reports they've sent relating to species migration through the Custodia Pass.
31081:
The antler guard is a tribrid shield slot item dropped by mature and elder custodian stalkers.

Requiring only level 50 Prayer to wield, its melee bonuses sit between an adamant and rune defender, ranged bonus between an unholy book and book of law, and magic bonus between that of an elemental tome and book of darkness. It shares the same strength bonus as a rune defender. Additionally, it has +2 ranged strength bonus and +5 prayer bonus. However, the main drawback of the guard is that it penalises all defence bonuses, so it is only recommended when players are not expected to be hit often.
31084: Alchemist's signet is a drop from elder custodian stalkers that can be used to open the chest next to the staircase downstairs in the Alchemical Society's headquarters, where the Mastering Mixology minigame is played. 60 Herblore[not boostable] is required to gain access to the basement. The chest contains a variety of useful Herblore supplies, including herbs, herb seeds, and secondaries. The signet is consumed once the chest is opened.
31099: Mokhaiotl waystones are consumable items used to teleport to the Ruins of Mokhaiotl. They can only be used after completion of The Final Dawn, and can be obtained as a drop from the Doom of Mokhaiotl.
31106:
The confliction gauntlets are an upgraded variant of the tormented bracelet requiring level 90 Hitpoints to wear, providing best-in-slot magic attack and magic damage bonuses. They are made with level 83 Crafting and level 70 Smithing by attaching the Mokhaiotl cloth, a rare untradeable drop from the Doom of Mokhaiotl, to a tormented bracelet alongside 10,000 demon tears. This process must be done at a bank and is not reversible.

Compared to the tormented bracelet, the gauntlets gain +10 magic attack bonus, some defensive bonuses and a +2% magic damage bonus, alongside a passive effect with one-handed magic weapons.
31109:
Mokhaiotl cloth is an item dropped by the Doom of Mokhaiotl. It is used alongside 10,000 demon tears to upgrade the tormented bracelet into the confliction gauntlets.

Based on Grand Exchange prices, the Mokhaiotl cloth is worth 46,067,188 if used to upgrade a tormented bracelet.
31111:
Demon tears are items used to charge the Eye of Ayak as an alternative to runes, or as part of the materials required to create the avernic treads and confliction gauntlets.

They are primarily obtained as drops from the Doom of Mokhaiotl. Alternatively, they can also be obtained by chopping infected roots in the Ruins of Mokhaiotl with 80 Woodcutting, providing a non-combat method of acquisition similar to that of Zulrah's scales from sacred eels. The Eye of Ayak can also be dismantled for 10,000 demon tears.

It takes 22,000 demon tears to fully upgrade both the Avernic treads (12,000 tears), including its base components, and craft the Confliction gauntlets (10,000 tears).
31113:
The Eye of Ayak is a one-handed powered staff that requires level 83 Magic to wield. It is a drop from the Doom of Mokhaiotl upon completion of delve level 3 and higher. Like most powered staves, it is only tradeable when it is fully uncharged.

It is the second strongest powered staff, placing it between the Sanguinesti staff and Tumeken's shadow in power. The maximum damage per hit is comparatively low, but it has the fastest attack speed of all powered staves, firing at a rate of 3 ticks (1.8 seconds) compared to the other staves' 4 or 5-tick speed.

The Eye of Ayak can be dismantled for 10,000 demon tears, resulting in a loss of −38,165,578 coins.

The Eye of Ayak cannot be used in Castle Wars, Clan Wars, TzHaar Fight Pit, and Soul Wars, despite all other powered staves being usable against players in those areas.

The Eye of Ayak does not lose charges on death in the Wilderness if the item is protected, even if the death occurs past level 20 Wilderness.
31115:

It is the second strongest powered staff, placing it between the Sanguinesti staff and Tumeken's shadow in power. The maximum damage per hit is comparatively low, but it has the fastest attack speed of all powered staves, firing at a rate of 3 ticks (1.8 seconds) compared to the other staves' 4 or 5-tick speed.

The Eye of Ayak can be dismantled for 10,000 demon tears, resulting in a loss of −38,165,578 coins.

The Eye of Ayak cannot be used in Castle Wars, Clan Wars, TzHaar Fight Pit, and Soul Wars, despite all other powered staves being usable against players in those areas.

The Eye of Ayak does not lose charges on death in the Wilderness if the item is protected, even if the death occurs past level 20 Wilderness.
31123:
The purple token can be obtained by completing a specific task in Varlamore centred around the capybara and pygmy hippo calf picnic located south-west of Kastori. According to Cobado, this token, alongside the seven red tokens and four nasty tokens, were hidden by the capybaras of Varlamore as a test to see how far someone would go in collecting them all.

If a player performs a Jig at the picnic, the animals will judge the player's dance moves depending on four conditions:

If all four conditions are met, the capybara will give the player the purple token. The purple token can be taken to Cobado while wearing an orange as a hat along with all 7 red tokens and all 4 nasty tokens to receive a blueberry muffin and 100,000 coins. If the player has the purple token, but not the rest of the tokens, Cobado will give the player 1 coin and tells them to find the rest if they have not yet received the blueberry muffin.

31130:
Dom is a pet dropped by the Doom of Mokhaiotl, and is a much smaller version of it. Dom can only be dropped upon completion of delve level of 6 or higher.

The first Dom players receive will cause the burrow hole to glow; subsequent Doms will not do so, even if the player loses it.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack. If the player is in a clan, the clan broadcast states [Player name] has a funny feeling like [he's/she's/they're] being followed: Dom at (number) levels. The total number of levels completed is tracked rather than kill count like most other boss pets.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.

The Battlehat was an unlock in the Grid Master community event. It was unlocked by defeating all four awakened versions of The Forgotten Four bosses.

Along with its stats, it also acted as a slayer helmet (i).

Compared to existing best-in-slot helmets, the battlehat had:

+2 Strength bonus over the Torva full helm

+10 Stab accuracy over the fighter hat

+5 Slash accuracy over the oathplate helm

+7 Crush accuracy over the Inquisitor's great helm/zombie helmet

+3 Ranged accuracy, +3 Ranged Strength, and +48 Magic defence over the Masori mask (f)

+7 Magic accuracy and +2% Magic damage bonus over the ancestral hat

Roughly equivalent melee and ranged Defence bonuses to the Justiciar faceguard (same stab defence, -3 slash defence, +1 crush defence, -7 ranged defence)

+4 Prayer over the sunfire fanatic helm

Upon loading a scene with a spooky picture in it, the picture will move in a specific way:

3 of the paintings in Draynor Manor and the one in Misthalin Manor will spin.

The rest of the paintings and the ones in Melzar's Maze will look around the room.
31223: Spooky wall lamp is an item used during the 2025 Halloween event. It is given to the player by Death after completing a short quiz. After completing the event, the spooky lamp can be seen as scenery outside Fred's house.
31224: Scarecrow is an item used during the 2025 Halloween event. The player gets the scarecrow from Sarah after dancing for the cows at the South Falador Farm. 31225:
The spooky chair is a reward from the 2025 Halloween event. It acts as a pet when dropped and will return to the inventory after 20 ticks (12s). It can be added to the menagerie in a player-owned house. As it is considered an extra rather than a pet, it counts towards the cap of 12 extras which can be stored in the menagerie at once.

Upon returning to the inventory, a message shows: The spooky chair makes its way back to you.. If the player has no inventory space, the chair will disappear, and instead a message shows: The spooky chair doesn't feel wanted and returns to Diango in Draynor Village.. If the player enters an area where followers are not allowed, the chair will disappear and a message shows: The spooky chair doesn't like this area and returns to Diango in Draynor Village.. Attempting to drop or spin the chair before completing the event gives this message: You shouldn't play with the chair yet. Fred needs it!.

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room.

31235:
Gryphon feathers are dropped by all types of gryphons. They are used to charge the horn of plenty, giving various buffs whilst training Hunter. They can be stored in a huntsman's kit.

Gryphon feathers can also be used in place of standard feathers for fletching, when making bolts, darts, and arrows, however they are not able to be used for fly fishing.
31241:
The horn of plenty is an off-hand item obtained as a drop from gryphons. Requiring level 50 Hunter to equip, the horn provides a passive invisible +2 boost to the Hunter skill. Upon equipping the horn, the player will blow the horn; this can be repeated by selecting the "Blow" option in the Worn Equipment tab.

The horn can be charged with up to 20,000 gryphon feathers, each providing one charge. The horn can be uncharged at any time, which returns any unused feathers. When charged, the invisible Hunter boost is increased from +2 to +4, consuming a charge every 25 catches. Additionally, the charged horn has a 1/10 chance to double a Hunter catch (without additional experience), consuming an additional charge whenever this occurs. This effect can be toggled on and off. This doubling effect does not work on implings, hunter meats, hunter furs (except for wyrmscraig goat fur, which works), or bones dropped by hunter creatures, nor does it work for aerial fishing or falconry as the horn needs to be equipped to receive its effects. Double hunter catches from the horn do not count towards the dry-protection on Hunters' Rumours.

As the horn provides an invisible Hunter boost, you cannot use the horn to boost for something you do not have the Hunter level for; the invisible boost only increases the player's success rates when hunting.

Charges are not lost if you die to another player in the Wilderness, assuming the item is protected on death.

31276:
The rock golem is a members-only skilling pet that can be obtained while training Mining. The chances of getting it are dependent on the player's Mining level, and the time it takes to gather a resource.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack. This message also occurs if there is one last inventory space while the player already has a pet following them, in which case the pet will appear in the inventory instead and the resource dropped to the ground.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around for 30 seconds before disappearing completely. It can then be reclaimed from Probita in East Ardougne for no cost.

When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.

31288:
The Sailing cape is the Cape of Accomplishment for the Sailing skill and can be purchased for 99,000 coins alongside the Sailing hood from Brass Hand Harry at the Pandemonium, by players who have achieved level 99.

Like all skill capes, the Sailing cape gives +9 to all defensive stats, and also a +4 bonus to prayer if it is trimmed. The cape is automatically trimmed if a second skill is levelled to 99.

The Sailing cape has the perk that allows players to rename their boats without needing to visit Sleve McDichael. Unlike Sleve, the Sailing cape allows the player to choose what name they wish to give their boat, instead of being given a random name.

The cape provides unlimited teleports to the player's boats, provided a greater teleportation focus facility is installed. Furthermore, it provides unlimited teleports to the Pandemonium for both players and boats without requiring a teleportation focus, though players must disembark before teleporting their boat and any cargo in the hold will be lost in accordance with restrictions set by the Summon Boat spell.

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room, as part of the Sailing cape set, along with the hood. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

As of 1 August 2026, there are 94,045 players that have achieved level 99 in Sailing.

31330: The mayoral fishbowl is an item used in the Current Affairs quest. It is used alongside a tiny net in order to "elect" a new fish to serve as a replacement for the late mayor.
31331:
The Mayor of Catherby is a fish found in Catherby during and after the quest Current Affairs. The fish acts as the 26th replacement for the original fish that was voted as mayor of the town, in favour of the disliked Councillor Catherine.

Players can use the mayor's consult option at any time for advice, with the mayor indicating either agreement or disagreement on the matter at hand.

Using fish food on the mayor will consume it, resulting in the message The mayor accepts your generous donation to his campaign. Poisoned fish food has no effect.

The mayor can be stored in a menagerie of a player-owned house.

Destroying the mayor will display the message You drop the fishbowl and it smashes on the floor. The Mayor of Catherby sadly dies as it does so. Another mayor can be obtained by talking to Arhein in Catherby.

31383: Camphor pyre logs may be used during the Shades of Mort'ton minigame to cremate the remains of Loar, Phrin, Riyl, and Asyn shades. They require level 71 Firemaking to light and grant 320 Firemaking experience when used to cremate a shade (480 with Elite Morytania Diary completion).

31393:

31395: Sea shells are found throughout the beaches of the Great Conch. Six are used in the Troubled Tortugans quest to repair Krill's stall, Strom's crate, and Coco's stall and crate.

31398:

One is given to the player for free during the Troubled Tortugans quest. If lost, it can be purchased from Elder Blunn's Spear and Shield Stall for 2,500 coins.

According to Elder Blunn, who crafts the shields, they were created at the suggestion of a human tourist.

Dragon nails are an item used to make various core boat parts, facilities, and rosewood repair kits. They can also be used to construct certain types of wooden furniture (although this is not advised due to their price).

They are most commonly dropped from Frost dragons, and can also be smithed from dragon metal sheets at the Dragon forge in the Ancient Cavern with level 92 smithing. Each sheet produces 15 nails.
31408:
A giant blue krill is an abnormally coloured giant krill caught while rod fishing or trawling at a krill or shimmering shoal. Upon a successful roll for a catch, players or crewmates have a 1/2,000 chance to obtain one from a krill shoal, as well as a 1/1,000 chance to roll a rare fish from a shimmering shoal (then a 45/100 chance to roll the giant blue krill), which comes out to an effective rate of ~1/2,222.22.

Catching one results in the game message You catch a giant blue krill! instead of the usual You catch a giant krill!. If a crewmate catches it, the game message will show Jolly Jim catches a giant blue krill! for example.

It can be stuffed at the taxidermist in Canifis by using the item on her and paying 5,000 coins, returning a stuffed giant blue krill. Once stuffed, it can be mounted at a teak or mahogany display within the skill hall in a player-owned house, granting 70 Construction and 250 Fishing experience.

When obtained while trawling, the collection log entry will be completed, even if the player does not collect the krill from their trawling net.
31412:

31430:
A stuffed swift marlin is obtained by bringing a swift marlin and 6,500 coins to the taxidermist in Canifis; this process is reversible by selecting the "Unstuff" option on the item.

At level 86 Construction, it can be mounted at a mahogany display within the skill hall in a player-owned house, granting 80 Construction and 360 Fishing experience.
31432:
Camphor planks are a type of plank used in the Sailing skill for shipbuilding, in various recipes for facilities and as the next tier of core boat parts above mahogany.

Additionally, camphor planks are used in various rowboat spaces to return to mooring points from the mainland without needing to use the player's own boats.
31435:

Additionally, ironwood planks are used in various bank chest spaces to build bank chests on certain islands.
31438: Rosewood planks are a type of plank used in the Sailing skill for shipbuilding, in various recipes for facilities and as the best tier of core boat parts, surpassing ironwood.
31472: A bolt of linen is an item used in building sails for a player's boat and in the creation of the gem pouch. Bolts of linen can be created with level 12 Crafting at a loom with 2 linen yarn, providing 20 Crafting experience.
31475: A bolt of canvas is an item used in building sails for a player's boat and in the creation of the gem satchel. Bolts of canvas can be created with level 39 Crafting at a loom with 2 hemp yarn, providing 75 Crafting experience.
31478: A bolt of cotton is an item used in building sails for a player's boat and in the creation of the gem tote. Bolts of cotton can be created with level 73 Crafting at a loom with 2 cotton yarn, providing 132 Crafting experience.
31481:
Elkhorn coral can be harvested from a coral nursery after planting elkhorn frags.

Using crab paste on an elkhorn coral with 49 Herblore yields anti-odour salt, an item which is automatically consumed when setting up hunter traps to smoke them; five crab paste is required per coral, giving 15 salt.

It is also used in the first step of making haemostatic dressings by adding an elkhorn coral to a vial of water to create a elkhorn potion (unf), then adding squid paste to create a haemostatic poultice, and finally adding cotton yarn for the dressing.

Lastly, five elkhorn coral can be used as a payment to protect pillar coral.
31484:
Pillar coral can be harvested from a coral nursery after planting pillar frags, and are primarily used in the making of super fishing potions and super hunter potions. To create a potion, players must add a pillar coral to a vial of water to create a pillar potion (unf), and then add the secondary ingredient.

Five pillar coral can be used as a payment to protect umbral coral.
31487: Umbral coral can be harvested from a coral nursery after planting umbral frags. They are used to make Armadyl brews by first adding one to a vial of water to create an umbral potion (unf), and then adding rainbow crab paste.
31490: A camphor seedling is created by sowing a camphor seed in a filled plant pot with a gardening trowel. Once watered, it will grow into a camphor sapling. A camphor sapling requires level 66 Farming to plant in a hardwood tree patch.
31492: An ironwood seedling is created by sowing an ironwood seed in a filled plant pot with a gardening trowel. Once watered, it will grow into an ironwood sapling. An ironwood sapling requires level 80 Farming to plant in a hardwood tree patch.
31494: A rosewood seedling is created by sowing a rosewood seed in a filled plant pot with a gardening trowel. Once watered, it will grow into a rosewood sapling. A rosewood sapling requires level 92 Farming to plant in a hardwood tree patch.
31496: A camphor seedling is created by sowing a camphor seed in a filled plant pot with a gardening trowel. Once watered, it will grow into a camphor sapling. A camphor sapling requires level 66 Farming to plant in a hardwood tree patch.
31498: An ironwood seedling is created by sowing an ironwood seed in a filled plant pot with a gardening trowel. Once watered, it will grow into an ironwood sapling. An ironwood sapling requires level 80 Farming to plant in a hardwood tree patch.
31500: A rosewood seedling is created by sowing a rosewood seed in a filled plant pot with a gardening trowel. Once watered, it will grow into a rosewood sapling. A rosewood sapling requires level 92 Farming to plant in a hardwood tree patch.
31502:
Camphor saplings are saplings that can be used to grow camphor trees at level 66 Farming.

They can be made by planting a camphor seed in a filled plant pot, with a gardening trowel in your inventory, and then watering the camphor seedling with a watering can. When watered, the seedling will sprout into a sapling in one crop cycle (0-5 minutes).

Planting the sapling in a hardwood tree patch, with a spade in your inventory, will give 88 Farming experience. It will grow into a camphor tree after 5,120 minutes (3 days, 13 hours, and 20 minutes).

Players can ask the gardener to protect their tree from disease whilst it grows, which requires payment of 10 white berries. This payment can be noted.
31505:
Ironwood saplings are saplings that can be used to grow ironwood trees at level 80 Farming.

They can be made by planting an ironwood seed in a filled plant pot, with a gardening trowel in your inventory, and then watering the ironwood seedling with a watering can. When watered, the seedling will sprout into a sapling in one crop cycle (0-5 minutes).

Planting the sapling in a hardwood tree patch, with a spade in your inventory, will result in it growing into a ironwood tree after 5,120 minutes (3 days, 13 hours, and 20 minutes).

Players can ask the gardener to protect their tree from disease whilst it grows, which requires payment of 10 curry leaves. This payment can be noted.
31508:
Rosewood saplings are saplings that can be used to grow rosewood trees at level 92 Farming.

They can be made by planting a rosewood seed in a filled plant pot, with a gardening trowel in your inventory, and then watering the rosewood seedling with a watering can. When watered, the seedling will sprout into a sapling in one crop cycle (0-5 minutes).

Planting the sapling in a hardwood tree patch, with a spade in your inventory, will result in it growing into a rosewood tree after 5,760 minutes (4 days).

Players can ask the gardener to protect their tree from disease whilst it grows, which requires payment of 8 dragonfruit. This payment can be noted.
31511:
Elkhorn frags are coral pieces that can be propagated in a coral nursery found in the Coral Nurseries, a location just off the eastern coast of the Great Conch. Compost of any type does not work on coral nursery farming patches.

Elkhorn frags require level 28 Farming to plant, producing an elkhorn coral when fully grown. Players can harvest elkhorn coral from the mature crop, which are used as an ingredient in anti-odour salts and haemostatic dressings.
31513:
Pillar frags are coral pieces that can be propagated in a coral nursery found in the Coral Nurseries, a location just off the eastern coast of the Great Conch. Compost of any type does not work on coral nursery farming patches.

Pillar frags require level 52 Farming to plant, producing a pillar coral when fully grown. Players can harvest pillar coral from the mature crop, which are used as an ingredient in super fishing potions and super hunter potions.
31515:
Umbral frags are coral pieces that can be propagated in a coral nursery found in the Coral Nurseries, a location just off the eastern coast of the Great Conch. Compost of any type does not work on coral nursery farming patches.

Umbral frags require level 77 Farming to plant, producing an umbral coral when fully grown. Players can harvest umbral coral from the mature crop, which are used as an ingredient in Armadyl brews.
31541:
Flax seeds can be planted in a hops patch at level 18 Farming to yield flax. Three seeds are required per patch.

A nearby gardener will watch over growing flax plants for 6 grain. Using compost will reduce the chances of disease and increase yield.
31547:
Camphor seeds are seeds used in the Farming skill. At level 66 Farming, camphor seeds may be planted in filled plant pots with a gardening trowel and watered to become camphor saplings.

After planting the sapling in a hardwood tree patch and waiting for it to fully grow, which takes 5,120 minutes (3 days, 13 hours, and 20 minutes), the plant will grow into a camphor tree which can be cut to yield camphor logs (and grant Woodcutting experience).

When cut down, the tree will automatically regrow after a period of time. A nearby gardener will look after a camphor tree in exchange for 10 white berries.
31549:
Ironwood seeds are seeds used in the Farming skill. At level 80 Farming, ironwood seeds may be planted in filled plant pots with a gardening trowel and watered to become ironwood saplings.

After planting the sapling in a hardwood tree patch and waiting for it to fully grow, which takes 5,120 minutes (3 days, 13 hours, and 20 minutes), the plant will grow into an ironwood tree which can be cut to yield ironwood logs (and grant Woodcutting experience).

When cut down, the tree will automatically regrow after a period of time. A nearby gardener will look after an ironwood tree in exchange for 10 curry leaves.
31551:
Rosewood seeds are seeds used in the Farming skill. At level 92 Farming, rosewood seeds may be planted in filled plant pots with a gardening trowel and watered to become rosewood saplings.

After planting the sapling in a hardwood tree patch and waiting for it to fully grow, which takes 5,760 minutes (4 days), the plant will grow into a rosewood tree which can be cut to yield rosewood logs (and grant Woodcutting experience).

When cut down, the tree will automatically regrow after a period of time. A nearby gardener will look after a rosewood tree in exchange for 8 dragonfruit.
31556:
Swordtip squid is a type of fish that restores 15 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking raw swordtip squid on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 56 Cooking and granting 150 experience when successful.

When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt swordtip squid. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will stop burning entirely at level 91, or 85 if using a cooking range.
31559:
Burnt swordtip squid is the result of accidentally burning a raw swordtip squid while attempting to cook swordtip squid. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will stop burning entirely at level 91, or 85 if using a cooking range.

The burnt swordtip squid has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange. Because of that, some players collect them or resell them to other burnt food collectors.
31561:
Raw jumbo squid is a fish caught by lantern harpooning, requiring level 69 Fishing alongside a lantern and harpoon. With lantern fishing spots exclusive to certain islands at sea, the minimum Sailing level to catch them is 47, the level required to dock at the Onyx Crest.

Raw jumbo squid can be crushed with a pestle and mortar into squid paste, an ingredient used to make haemostatic dressings. At level 71 Cooking, it can also be cooked to make jumbo squid that heals 17 Hitpoints each.

Like most raw fish, it can also be cut with a regular knife or chum facility to create fine fish offcuts to use as bait for various fishing activities. Each cutting action will also give a 1/512 chance of obtaining a squid beak, which is used to create wooden blowpipes. While using a chum facility, it is possible to obtain multiple beaks in one cutting action, depending on which chum facility is used, though the rate per action remains 1/512 regardless of how many squid are processed.
31564:
Jumbo squid is a type of fish that restores 17 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking raw jumbo squid on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 71 Cooking and granting 180 experience when successful.

When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt jumbo squid. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will only stop burning at level 98 (96 if the elite Kourend & Kebos Diary has been completed) when cooking at the Hosidius Kitchen.
31569:
Squid paste is made by using a pestle and mortar on raw swordtip or jumbo squids (obtained from lantern harpooning). It is used to make haemostatic poultice, which is the penultimate step in making haemostatic dressings.

Wesley currently does not crush raw squid.
31572:
A squid beak is an item that is used to create wooden blowpipes, obtained while cutting raw swordtip and jumbo squids at a rate of 1/1,024 and 1/512 respectively per cutting action.

If the player is cutting squids on the chum spreader and rolls to receive a squid beak, they will receive squid beaks equal to the number of squids cut on that tick (up to 4 beaks). Cutting squids with a full inventory does not reduce a player's chances, and any offcuts will drop to the ground to make room for the beak if obtained on the first cut of the inventory.

Spirit flakes and rada's blessing can be used for a chance to double catch squid.
31575:
A camphor blowpipe is a blowpipe that requires 45 Ranged to wield. Able to shoot up to mithril darts, it is made with a knife from two camphor logs and a squid beak, requiring 58 Fletching and granting 140 experience.

As with all blowpipes, the base attack speed varies; in player versus monster encounters, its attack speed is 3, or equal to darts. During player versus player combat, its attack speed is 4, or equal to a shortbow.

Like the toxic blowpipe, it must be charged with darts by using the darts on the blowpipe. Unlike the toxic blowpipe, it does not need to be charged with Zulrah's scales to use it.

31587:

It is used to create a haemostatic dressing by using cotton yarn. While the amulet of chemistry does not work with haemostatic poultices, they do work when making haemostatic dressings. Prescription goggles are able to save both squid paste and cotton yarn.
31590:
Haemostatic dressings are a potion-type item that cures bleed when applied, healing 5 Hitpoints if bleeding was stopped via its use. It is made by using cotton yarn on haemostatic poultice, requiring 56 Herblore and granting 100 Herblore experience; though not a true "potion", the amulet of chemistry acts as normal when making haemostatic dressings, and prescription goggles are able to save cotton yarns. Bob Barter will decant dressings like other potion-type items.

Haemostatic dressings can be consumed even if the player is not bleeding.

31662: Elkhorn potion (unf) is an unfinished potion made by using an elkhorn coral on a vial of water, requiring 56 Herblore. Using squid paste on an elkhorn potion (unf) with 56 Herblore yields a haemostatic poultice, which can be used alongside cotton yarn to make a haemostatic dressing.
31665: Pillar potion (unf) is an unfinished potion made by using a pillar coral on a vial of water, requiring 62 Herblore. Using a haddock eye on a pillar potion (unf) with 62 Herblore yields a super fishing potion, which boosts Fishing by 6. Using a crab paste on a pillar potion (unf) with 67 Herblore yields a super hunter potion, which boosts Hunter by 6.
31668: Umbral potion (unf) is an unfinished potion made by using an umbral coral on a vial of water, requiring 89 Herblore. Using rainbow crab paste on an umbral potion (unf) with 89 Herblore yields an Armadyl brew, which boosts Ranged and Hitpoints but lowers Attack, Strength, Defence, and Magic.
31671:
Red crabs are captured red crabs in item form, caught via crab trapping on the Pandemonium. This requires level 21 Hunter and grants 64 experience.

A red crab can be prepared with a knife to produce raw red crab meat, which can then be cooked into red crab meat at level 21 Cooking. Alternatively, it can be ground with a pestle and mortar to produce crab paste, which are used to create anti-odour salt or super hunter potions.
31677:
Rainbow crabs are captured rainbow crabs in item form, caught via crab trapping on the Crown Jewel. This requires level 77 Hunter and grants 216 experience. Rainbow crabs come in three varieties, which are identical in all but appearance.

A rainbow crab can be prepared with a knife to produce raw rainbow crab meat, which can then be cooked into rainbow crab meat at level 77 Cooking. Alternatively, it can be ground with a pestle and mortar to produce rainbow crab paste, which are used to create Armadyl brews.

If manually baiting the traps, players can expect to gain 150,000 experience per hour or more. Catch rates are static, so a player's Hunter level does not affect the experience rate.

31689:
Red crab meat is a type of food that restores 8 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking raw red crab meat on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 21 Cooking and granting 85 experience when successful.

When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt crab meat. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will stop burning entirely at level 56, or 51 if using a cooking range.
31698:
Burnt crab meat is the result of accidentally burning either raw red crab meat or raw blue crab meat. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels.

The burnt crab meat has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.
31700:
Raw rainbow crab meat is obtained by using a knife on a rainbow crab, requiring level 77 Cooking and granting 12 experience.

It can then be cooked to produce rainbow crab meat, granting 200 Cooking experience.

31710: Rainbow crab paste is made by using a pestle and mortar on a rainbow crab, which are caught via crab trapping. It is a herblore secondary used to create Armadyl brews.
31712:
Anti-odour salt is an item that is automatically consumed when setting up hunter traps to smoke them (rather than having to manually use a lit torch on the trap), which increases catch rates by 2%.

It can be made with 49 Herblore by combining elkhorn coral and crab paste while having a pestle and mortar in the inventory; five crab paste is required per coral, giving 15 salt.

Anti-odour salt cannot be stored in the huntsman's kit.
31719:
Nickel ore is an ore mined from nickel rocks at level 74 Mining, granting 80.5 experience. Alongside two copper ore, it can be smelted into a cupronickel bar at level 74 Smithing, granting 42 experience.

With the exception of Varrock armour 4 (which gives a 10% chance of mining an extra nickel ore), mining enhancers do not work for nickel rocks.

At higher Mining levels, experience rates are around 25k xp/hr. At 99 Mining and with the eastern Deepfin Mine bank chest built, experience rates can be up to 28k xp/hr.
31722:
Rubium splinters are resources that are mined from rubium rocks at level 48 Mining, found in the Charred Dungeon on Charred Island. Each rock will provide a guaranteed two splinters, and may deplete randomly on each subsequent splinter mined.

At level 68, rubium deposits can also be mined for rubium geodes which can be broken down with a hammer and chisel into splinters. The amount of splinters obtained from a geode scales with Mining level.

10 splinters and 2 of any smithable cannonball can be used at an anvil to smith 2 incendiary cannonballs every 3 ticks in batches of 56 (up to 28 actions per batch). This is done by left-clicking "Smith" on the anvil; using either the splinters or the cannonball on the anvil will not work.

When fired from a ship's cannon, the incendiaries have a chance to burn their targets.
31724:
Rubium geodes are mined rubium deposits, requiring 68 Mining. Cracking open a geode with a hammer & chisel gives rubium splinters with a quantity that scales with Mining level. Each geode has to be individually cracked open as they do not process automatically, but opening geodes will start with the first geode in the inventory, meaning that you can spam click the last geode in your inventory to quickly open them all.

Rubium deposits can be found in the Charred Dungeon, which requires 60 Sailing to reach.
31726:
Strykewyrm bones are bones dropped by lava and magma strykewyrms, which give 60 Prayer experience when buried. This can be increased by offering the bones in different ways:

180 XP when casting Sinister Offering.

180 XP when offered at the sacred bone burner after the appropriate faith level has been achieved.

210 XP when offered at a gilded altar with two burners lit.

200 XP when offered at the Ectofuntus in the form of Wyrm bonemeal. (Strykewyrm bonemeal is not obtainable as strykewyrm bones currently only create wyrm bonemeal.)

185 XP when blessed and broken down into blessed bone shards and offered at the libation bowl, or 222 XP when offered with a jug of blessed sunfire wine. Virilis outside the altar will exchange noted bones for 10 coins each.

420 XP on average when offered at the Chaos Temple in the Wilderness. Each offering gives 210 XP, which is the same as the gilded altar with two burners lit, but with an additional 50% chance to not consume the bones.

These bones can't be used with the Standard Spellbook spell "Bones to Peaches". Any attempt to do so will result in the following message: "The bones you're holding aren't suitable for peachifying."
31729:
Frost dragon bones are bones dropped by frost dragons, which give 100 Prayer experience when buried. This can be increased by offering the bones in different ways:

300 XP when casting Sinister Offering.

300 XP when offered at the sacred bone burner after the appropriate faith level has been achieved.

350 XP when offered at a gilded altar with two burners lit.

400 XP when offered at the Ectofuntus in the form of frost dragon bonemeal.

420 XP when blessed and broken down into blessed bone shards and offered at the libation bowl, or 504 XP when offered with a jug of blessed sunfire wine. Virilis outside the altar will exchange noted bones for 10 coins each.

700 XP on average when offered at the Chaos Temple in the Wilderness. Each offering gives 350 XP, which is the same as the gilded altars with two burners lit, but providing a 50% chance to not consume the bones.
31733:

The stand is used to build a keg on a player's boat, and can be used as many times as needed. If lost, it can be reclaimed from Rum-dashed Ralph in the Storm Tempor.

This item can be stored in the magic wardrobe of a costume room, as part of the Swamp cruiser's kit set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

31803:
A spyglass is a tool used in sea charting. It is used when the player or their boat is on a glowing spot, after which a short cutscene is initiated in which the player views the nearby area through the spyglass. Note that NPCs can still attack during these cutscenes. You obtain one by talking to Chartin' Charles McAtless.

If lost, another can be obtained from the cargo hold of a boat.
31805:
The current duck is a friendly floaty duck who helps the player with charting currents at sea. The ability to chart currents is unlocked upon completion of Current Affairs, which requires a Sailing level of 22.

The current duck follows currents until reaching a predetermined end point indicated with message Your current duck comes to a stop.. It will despawn two minutes after it comes to a stop. The current duck will reappear in the tools compartment of the cargo hold on a player's boat once it is placed in the water, however it will not be retrievable from there until the current one despawns or is picked up. The current duck cannot be placed in a menagerie.

Telekinetic grab does not work on the current duck.
31807:
A crowbar is a tool used to open sealed crates as part of sea charting. The ability to open sealed crates at sea is unlocked upon completion of Prying Times, which requires a Sailing level of 12.

If lost, another can be obtained from the cargo hold of a boat, or from the crate of crowbars behind the counter of the Pandemonium pub. Thurgo can also make another crowbar by speaking with him with a hammer, steel bar, and redberry pie in the inventory.
31811:
Whirlpool surprise is a type of ale that temporarily boosts Cooking by 2 and Sailing by 3, while draining Agility by 2. Drinking a whirlpool surprise results in successive game messages stating You drink the rum cocktail. It tastes great! and You feel inspired to both cook and sail!.

Two can be claimed for free from Rum-dashed Ralph upon clearing the shark rank of the Tempor Tantrum Barracuda Trial, after which it becomes available for 300 coins each at the Pandemonium pub.
31814:
Kraken ink stout is a type of ale that temporarily boosts Magic by 2 and Sailing by 1. Drinking a kraken ink stout results in successive game messages stating You drink the rich stout. It thickly coats the back of your throat. Somehow you feel more adept at magic.

The ability to purchase kraken ink stout is unlocked after completely charting 5 seas in both the Ardent Ocean and Unquiet Ocean, then showing Chartin' Charles McAtless the captain's log.

Once unlocked, players can speak to Charles again and select the chat option "What do I get from charting the sea?", then "Can you tell me about these drinks?". Players can buy one ale at a time for 300 coins, or 25 noted ales at once for 7,500 coins.
31820:
Trawler's trust is a type of ale that temporarily boosts Sailing and Fishing by 2, while draining Attack by 2. Drinking a trawler's trust results in successive game messages stating You drink the refreshing beer. It tastes foamy and salty. You feel at one with the sea!

The ability to purchase trawler's trust is unlocked after completely charting 50 seas across all oceans, then showing Chartin' Charles McAtless the captain's log.

Once unlocked, players can speak to Charles again and select the chat option "What do I get from charting the sea?", then "Can you tell me about these drinks?". Players can buy one ale at a time for 300 coins, or 25 noted ales at once for 7,500 coins.
31831:
A bottle of almost smuggled rum is an alcoholic drink acquired by prying open a sealed crate on the west side of Mudskipper Point. Doing so requires a crowbar in the inventory, which in turn requires completion of Prying Times to obtain.

Drinking the bottle grants 75 Sailing experience, and will temporarily boost Strength by ~1-5, while draining Attack by ~1-5.
31832:
A bottle of sOrodamin's bru is an alcoholic drink acquired by prying open a sealed crate in Lum Lagoon. Doing so requires a crowbar in the inventory, which in turn requires completion of Prying Times to obtain. A raft is recommended to reach this crate, although it is possible to fit a skiff through the channel to get to it.

31833:

31843:

Drinking the bottle grants 75 Sailing experience, and will deal 5 damage, as well as causing the game screen to shake briefly.
31844:

31845:

31856:

31858:

If Regicide has not been completed, then the player and their boat will remain where they were.

Drinking the bottle grants 75 Sailing experience, and will cause the camera to rock back and forth vertically (like when on the Fishing Trawler) for 20 seconds. This may be nauseating if players keep looking at the screen while the effect is ongoing, but the effect can be disabled in game settings under "Camera Effects". Alternatively, logging out after the effects have started will not cause them to resume upon logging back in.
31860:
A bottle of banker's draught is an alcoholic drink acquired by prying open a sealed crate in the Hosidian Sea, off the eastern coast of Hosidius. Doing so requires a crowbar in the inventory, which in turn requires completion of Prying Times to obtain.

Drinking the bottle grants 75 Sailing experience, and will bank all of the player's inventory items and worn equipment. If the player's bank is full, items that cannot be deposited will be dropped on the ground. Players can avoid banking their items by dropping them prior to drinking the draught and simply pick their items up after doing so.

As Ultimate Ironmen cannot use banks, drinking the bottle will instead deal damage equal to 10% of the player's Hitpoints level (rounded down).
31861:
A bottle of headless unicornman's heady beer is an alcoholic drink acquired by prying open a sealed crate in the Gulf of Kourend, to the east of Port Piscarilius. Doing so requires a crowbar in the inventory, which in turn requires completion of Prying Times to obtain.

Drinking the bottle grants 75 Sailing experience, and will fill the player's inventory with various ensouled heads. To maximise the number of heads received, the player may wish to drink this item after banking or storing any excess items in the inventory.
31863:
A bottle of crocodile tears is an alcoholic drink acquired by prying open a sealed crate in the small cove to the south of Menaphos. Doing so requires a crowbar in the inventory, which in turn requires completion of Prying Times to obtain.

Drinking the bottle grants 75 Sailing experience, and will apply desert heat damage to the player once. If the player is not carrying any full waterskins, this can deal around 5-13 damage spread across four hitsplats. Wearing the circlet of water does not prevent this damage.
31865:
Daddy's special water's special water is an item dropped by Daddy's special water, who is fought after the player is teleported upon drinking a bottle of fishier bladderier stout.

When drunk, the player receives 100 Sailing experience and a game message stating It burns.
31867:
The melted rocks is an item dropped by The rocks, who is fought after the player is teleported upon drinking a bottle of fishier bladderier stout.

When drunk, the player receives 100 Sailing experience and a game message stating It burns, but cold.
31869:
Chuck up's 'stew' is an item dropped by Chuck up, who is fought after the player is teleported upon drinking a bottle of fishier bladderier stout.

When drunk, the player receives 100 Sailing experience and a game message stating It burns, but with chunks.
31872:
A bottle of Waterbirth blue lagoon is an alcoholic drink acquired by prying open a sealed crate in the centre of V's Belt, directly east of Jatizso. Doing so requires a crowbar in the inventory, which in turn requires completion of Prying Times to obtain.

Drinking the bottle grants 75 Sailing experience, and spawns an aggressive level-100 blue dagannoth.
31875:
A bottle of exile's welcome is an alcoholic drink acquired by prying open a sealed crate just off the docks of Lunar Isle. Doing so requires a crowbar in the inventory, which in turn requires completion of Prying Times to obtain.

Drinking the bottle grants 75 Sailing experience, and will teleport the player to one of five teleport locations from the lunar spellbook: Catherby, Waterbirth Island, Port Khazard, Barbarian Outpost, or the Fishing Guild; each destination is equally likely.

Players can get back on their boat with no loss of non-courier task cargo, depending on the player's Sailing level; the boat will be docked at Lunar Isle if the player's Sailing level is at least 76 and they have completed the Lunar Diplomacy quest, or Port Sarim if not.
31878:
A bottle of black lobster ale is an alcoholic drink acquired by prying open a sealed crate in the northern part of the Fremennik Isles. Doing so requires a crowbar in the inventory, which in turn requires completion of Prying Times to obtain. Additionally, a raft is required to reach this crate, as the skiff and sloop are both too large to fit through the channel.

Drinking the bottle grants 75 Sailing experience, and will place a rare black lobster in the inventory, as well as fully drain the player's Cooking and Fishing levels.

It is one of few sailing drinks that can be sampled more than once, though subsequent drinks do not yield Sailing experience.
31881:
A bottle of dwarvern wizard's stout bomb is an alcoholic drink acquired by prying open a sealed crate in the centre of Weissmere, to the far west of Weiss. Doing so requires a crowbar in the inventory, which in turn requires completion of Prying Times to obtain.

Drinking the bottle grants 75 Sailing experience, and will temporarily boost Magic by 4, Smithing by 2, and Mining by 2, while fully draining Attack, Strength, and Defence.
31883:
A bottle graveyard corpse reviver is an alcoholic drink acquired by prying open a sealed crate just north of the large rock formations in Weissmere. Doing so requires a crowbar in the inventory, which in turn requires completion of Prying Times to obtain.

Drinking the bottle grants 75 Sailing experience, and spawns a corpse who is level-103 and aggressive. If choosing to kill it, it will fully heal upon dying up to 9 times before staying dead.
31884:
A bottle of Weiss meltwater is an alcoholic drink acquired by prying open a sealed crate in the Weiss Melt, at the north-eastern corner of the Northern Ocean. Doing so requires a crowbar in the inventory, which in turn requires completion of Prying Times to obtain.

Drinking the bottle grants 75 Sailing experience, and will visually cast Ice Barrage on the player, dealing damage equal to one-third of the player's maximum hitpoints (rounded down); this can kill the player if their health is too low. Wearing at least four pieces of warm clothing will protect the player from the drink's effects.
31885:
A bottle of ol' random's reddest rum is an alcoholic drink acquired by prying open a sealed crate just off the western coast of the Red Rock. Doing so requires a crowbar in the inventory, which in turn requires completion of Prying Times to obtain.

Drinking the bottle grants 75 Sailing experience, and will transmogrify the player as if they had worn a random transformation ring:

Pile of coins

Bush

Snowman

Rocks

Random piece of third age equipment
31887:

Drinking the bottle grants 75 Sailing experience, and spawns an aggressive level-81 angry tortugan on your boat that will attack with melee.
31888:

Drinking the bottle grants 75 Sailing experience, and will initiate a cutscene in which the screen fades to black for 75 seconds with pleasant sounds and chatbox texts guiding the player to relax and dismiss their anxieties.

Warning: Players cannot exit the cutscene and activities that occur outside of it will continue, meaning the ship can continue to move, potentially exposing players to aggressive sea creatures or inadvertently sailing into hazardous waters. As such, players should only drink this when docked at a safe area. X-logging does not speed up the cutscene and you will not be able to log back in until it is finished.

If the miniquest has not been completed, then the player and their boat will remain where they were.

As such, players who do not wish to traverse the Wilderness to reach the Abyss can do so once with this bottle, such as during the Devious Minds quest.
31891:

Drinking the bottle grants 75 Sailing experience, and will set off fireworks identical to the ones seen when reaching level 99 in a skill.
31893:
A bottle of crystal clear vodka is an item acquired by prying open the sealed crate in the Everdeep, just west of Deepfin Point. Doing so requires a crowbar in the inventory, which in turn requires completion of Prying Times to obtain.

Drinking the bottle grants 75 Sailing experience, and will deal damage equal to 20% of the player's maximum hitpoints (rounded down); this can kill the player if their health is too low. Additionally, a high-pitched ringing sound is also played; players who are sensitive to such sounds may wish to turn their volume down before drinking this bottle.
31895:

Doing so requires a crowbar in the inventory, which in turn requires completion of Prying Times to obtain. It is one of few sailing drinks that can be sampled more than once, allowing players to retake the quiz, although each of the rewards may only be received once.

Drinking the bottle grants 75 Sailing experience, and will summon the Quiz Master, who will ask five mostly nonsensical questions. Correctly answering his questions rewards the player with 5 mystery boxes. If the player has a full inventory or answers incorrectly, they will not receive any boxes, but may still retake the quiz to receive them later.

Incorrectly answering his questions will result in the player taking 10% of their Hitpoints in damage (rounded down), accompanied by a game message stating Your head aches violently as you feel braincells dying..
31897:

31900:
A bottle of lunarshine is an alcoholic drink acquired by prying open a sealed crate found in Moonshadow, to the south-west of Lunar Isle.

31902:
A bottle of mystery fruit cider is an item acquired by prying open the sealed crate in the Misty Sea, just south of the large shipwrecks.

Drinking the bottle grants 75 Sailing experience, and will result in a game message stating that the player has learnt something about the 'nature' of the mystery fruit.
31903:
Mystery fruit is an item that appears to have a very rare chance of being obtained when picking fruit or berries from farming patches, most likely requiring the bottle of mystery fruit cider to have been previously consumed. When a mystery fruit is picked, the following game message is printed: You find a mystery fruit whilst picking your crops!

Upon drinking a bottle of mystery fruit cider, a message is printed that says You feel you have learnt something about the nature of the mystery fruit by drinking this.

Eating it consumes the fruit and temporarily morphs the player into a mystery fruit, along with a message that says You feel kind of like a plum., with no other noted effects.
31908:
Iron cannonballs are ammunition used for a boat cannon during boat combat. They can be fired from iron cannons or stronger.

Four can be made from a single iron bar with level 20 Smithing, granting 17 experience per bar. Smithing cannonballs require the use of an ammo mould, which requires partial completion of Dwarf Cannon to obtain. Alternatively, a double ammo mould (requiring Foundry Reputation to purchase via the Giants' Foundry minigame) allows players to process two bars into eight cannonballs at the same speed as a regular ammo mould processes one bar into four.

Players with level 87 Sailing can further speed up smithing cannonballs by using the ancient furnace in the Grimstone Dungeon, which halves the time it takes to create cannonballs from 8 ticks to 4 ticks. Combining this with a double ammo mould, players can smith cannonballs at four times the normal speed.

31954: A narwhal horn is an item obtained from killing narwhals. It can be crafted into a narwhal horn knife with level 51 Crafting and a chisel, granting 73 experience. When carved into a knife, it becomes untradeable.
31957:

The knife can also be used in place of a regular knife for all purposes.
31959:
Ray barbs are an uncommon drop from various rays. They are used to build hemp and cotton trawling nets on a boat.

Rays can be killed as part of bounty tasks, which reward additional Sailing experience.
31961: A broken dragon hook is an item dropped by great white sharks. It is used to build a dragon salvaging hook on a boat.
31967:
An oak repair kit is an item that heals 10 health to a boat. Players can simply click the item's "Apply" option whilst on a boat to repair damage, and multiple players can do so at once to rapidly repair the boat. Additionally, crewmates can also repair the boat if instructed to, and depending on their Deckhandiness level may heal more than 10 per kit.

Players can build oak repair kits at a shipwrights' workbench with 2 oak planks, 10 iron nails, and 5 swamp paste, requiring 19 Construction and granting 90 experience, yielding 2 kits per action.

Like food, applying a repair kit incurs the same delay as eating during boat combat.

31985:

The captain's log is required to be in the player's inventory when speaking to Chartin' Charles McAtless in the Pandemonium Cave for Sailing training, as well as when speaking to Gerardus on Port Roberts for special items that unlock certain boat paints.

If lost, another can be obtained from either Junior Jim or the cargo hold of a boat.
31986:
The captain's log is an item obtained during Pandemonium from Junior Jim. Its primary use is to track courier and bounty tasks that the player has chosen to take on, as well as tracking sea charting completion.

The captain's log is required to be in the player's inventory when speaking to Chartin' Charles McAtless in the Pandemonium Cave for Sailing training, as well as when speaking to Gerardus on Port Roberts for special items that unlock certain boat paints.

If lost, another can be obtained from either Junior Jim or the cargo hold of a boat.
31989:
Boat bottles are a single-use item obtained rarely from sorting low-tier salvage from shipwrecks. It is used to "place" a player's boat into their inventory, allowing them to transport it to another port from land. This is useful for moving boats without a teleport focus built on them.

Using the "Bottle-boat" option on an empty bottle requires an empty cargo hold, as well as being at a docking point. When using the "Unbottle-boat" option on a full bottle, players will receive a confirmation message before doing so. The bottle will be lost when the player releases the boat.

Compared with the cost of recovering a boat in order to move it to a different port, using a boat bottle on a raft will result in a profit/loss of −19,956 coins, with a skiff −16,081 coins, and with a sloop 29,794 coins.

A bottle containing a boat is always kept on death and can only be destroyed using the bank incinerator. If destroyed, the boat can be recovered at a shipwright.

31996:
Dragon metal sheets are an item used in high-level shipbuilding, with some of the best facilities on a boat requiring multiple sheets to build.

With access to the dragon forge upon completion of Dragon Slayer II, players can make dragon keel parts for dragon keels as well as dragon nails (15 per sheet). Two sheets are used to make one keel part, while two keel parts are used to make one set of large dragon keel parts (requiring 4 sheets in total). As such, a total of 20 sheets are required for a dragon keel on a skiff, and 64 sheets for a sloop.

Completion of the Pandemonium quest is also required to be able to use sheets at the forge. Attempting to make something with a dragon metal sheet without having completed the quest displays the chatbox message "You probably shouldn't just go messing around with the dragon sheets without knowing what you're doing."

The best sources for these sheets are killing lava strykewyrms or frost dragons on task, however these can be quite tedious to obtain, especially if the player does not have enough slayer points to skip for them. A slower but more consistent method is completing bounty tasks for great white sharks, orcas, and high-levelled krakens (preferably armoured krakens), as one bounty task for each of these monsters are guaranteed at various notice boards across Gielinor.
31999:
Bronze keel parts are an item used to build a bronze keel on a skiff. They are created at level 10 Smithing by using 5 bronze bars at an anvil, granting 62.5 experience.

For sloops, players must instead use large bronze keel parts, which require 5 regular keel parts each for a total of 400 bronze bars.
32002:
Iron keel parts are an item used to build an iron keel on a skiff. They are created at level 22 Smithing by using 5 iron bars at an anvil, granting 125 experience.

For sloops, players must instead use large iron keel parts, which require 5 regular keel parts each for a total of 400 iron bars.
32014:
Rune keel parts are an item used to build a rune keel on a skiff. They are created at level 86 Smithing by using 5 runite bars at an anvil, granting 375 experience.

For sloops, players must instead use large rune keel parts, which require 5 regular keel parts each for a total of 400 runite bars.
32017:
Dragon keel parts are an item used to build a dragon keel on a skiff. They are created at level 94 Smithing by using 2 dragon metal sheets at the dragon forge, granting 700 experience. Accessing the dragon forge additionally requires completion of Dragon Slayer II.

For sloops, players must instead use large dragon keel parts, which require 2 regular keel parts for a total of 64 sheets.
32023:
Large iron keel parts are an item used to build an iron keel on a sloop, made with 5 iron keel parts at an anvil.

As sloop keels require 16 large keel parts, a total of 400 iron bars are required overall.
32026:
Large steel keel parts are an item used to build a steel keel on a sloop, made with 5 steel keel parts at an anvil.

As sloop keels require 16 large keel parts, a total of 400 steel bars are required overall.
32029:

As sloop keels require 16 large keel parts, a total of 400 mithril bars are required overall.
32032:
Large adamant keel parts are an item used to build an adamant keel on a sloop, made with 5 adamant keel parts at an anvil.

A sloop keel requires 16 large keel parts, totaling 400 adamantite bars.
32035:
Large rune keel parts are an item used to build a rune keel on a sloop, made with 5 rune keel parts at an anvil.

As sloop keels require 16 large keel parts, a total of 400 runite bars are required overall.
32038:
Large dragon keel parts are an item used to build a dragon keel on a sloop. It is made with 2 dragon keel parts at the dragon forge, which requires completion of Dragon Slayer II to access.

Sloop keels require 16 large keel parts, which for a dragon keel is equivalent to 64 dragon metal sheets total. However, unlike lower tier keels, they don't need to be made entirely from their base bars/sheets, as dragon keel parts and large dragon keel parts can also be sourced from drops from high level ocean monsters.
32041:
Wooden hull parts are an item used to build a wooden hull on a skiff. They are created by using 5 planks at a shipwrights' workbench, granting 72.5 Construction experience.

For sloops, players must instead use large wooden hull parts, which require 5 regular hull parts each for a total of 400 planks.

Due to skiffs already having wooden hulls upon purchasing one from a shipwright, these are only used to downgrade a skiff's hull.
32050:

32083:
Sawmill coupon (wood plank) is a type of sawmill coupon which is used to cover the 100 GP cost of converting regular logs to planks. The coupon is only redeemable at a sawmill, and cannot be substituted for coins when casting Plank Make.

25 sawmill coupons are awarded from the Pandemonium quest.
32085:
Sawmill coupon (oak plank) is a type of sawmill coupon which is used to cover the 250 cost of converting oak logs into oak planks. The coupon is only redeemable at a sawmill, and cannot be substituted for coins when casting Plank Make.

The Prying Times and Current Affairs quests each award 25 coupons. Additional coupons may be earned though various Sailing activities, such as collecting lost supplies found during The Tempor Tantrum or through shipwreck salvaging.
32093:
Inky paint is a type of boat paint used to recolour the trim of a player's skiff or sloop via the boat schematics board at the Shipyard. Trimming a boat requires level 25 Sailing and 20 Construction, granting 10 Construction experience. One paint is required for trimming skiffs, while sloops require two.

Inky paint can be received as very rare drops from krakens at sea. Along with angler's, shark, salvor's, and Barracuda paint, it can be given to Trader Stan in exchange for merchant's paint.
32099:
Salvor's paint is a type of boat paint used to recolour the trim of a player's skiff or sloop via the boat schematics board at the Shipyard. Salvor's paint is received at a rate of 1/24,000 from sorting martial salvage. Along with angler's, shark, inky, and Barracuda paint, it can be given to Trader Stan in exchange for merchant's paint.
32102:

As such, the paint requires a Sailing level of at least 78 to obtain.

As the chest is located on Charred Island, the paint requires a Sailing level of at least 60 to obtain. Players will need a rope the first time they enter the dungeon, which spawns on the southern tip of the island.
32106:

Guthixian paint can be obtained in unlimited amounts from the Elite Void Knight after having given her the void orb, which is obtained by bringing the captain's log to Gerardus once the Shrouded Ocean is fully charted. As such, the paint requires a Sailing level of at least 72 to obtain.
32307:
Fine fish offcuts are created by using a knife on certain high level raw fish, which are primarily used to bait rainbow crab traps and fish shoals whilst deep sea trawling. They can also be used in place of fish offcuts or bait for barbarian fishing and aerial fishing.

For fish shoals, baiting is not mandatory (except when rod fishing shoals, where one is used per fish), but doing so via an advanced chum station or better will grant a 20% chance to catch extra fish.

Unlike regular fish offcuts, they are not prioritised over other types of bait when barbarian fishing.
32309:
Raw giant krill is a type of fish caught from giant krill shoals whilst deep sea trawling, requiring level 69 Fishing and granting 112.5 experience per successful catch with a trawling net, or 22.5 if caught with a fishing rod. They can also be caught from shimmering shoals, which can yield other deep sea fish alongside giant krill.

Cooking giant krill requires level 69 in Cooking, resulting in a giant krill and 177.5 Cooking experience. If unsuccessful, it will result in a burnt giant krill instead.
32312:
Giant krill is a type of fish that restores 17 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking raw giant krill on a fire or cooking range. Cooking a giant krill requires level 69 Cooking, and grants 177.5 experience when successful.

When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt giant krill. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will only stop burning entirely if the player is wearing a Cooking cape, or at level 98 (95 if the elite Kourend & Kebos Diary has been completed) when cooking at the Hosidius Kitchen.
32317:
Raw haddock is a type of fish caught from haddock shoals whilst deep sea trawling, requiring level 73 Fishing and granting 128.5 experience per successful catch with a trawling net, or 25.7 if caught with a fishing rod. They can also be caught from shimmering shoals, which can yield other deep sea fish alongside haddock.

Cooking haddock requires level 73 in Cooking, resulting in a haddock and 180 Cooking experience. If unsuccessful, it will result in a burnt haddock instead.

Raw haddock can also be cut into fish offcuts by using a knife, with a chance (scaling with Cooking level) of receiving a haddock eye, a herblore secondary used to make super fishing potions.
32320:
Haddock is a type of fish that restores 18 Hitpoints when eaten. Haddock may also boost hitpoints above the base level, by 20% of the base level or by 10, whichever is lower. Similar to the anglerfish, eating a haddock will not overheal if the player is in combat in a PvP area, whether with another player or a monster.

It can be obtained by cooking raw haddock on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 73 Cooking and granting 180 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt haddock. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will only stop burning at level 99 (96 if the elite Kourend & Kebos Diary has been completed) when cooking at the Hosidius Kitchen.
32328:
Yellowfin is a type of fish that restores 19 Hitpoints and 20% run energy when eaten.

It can be obtained by cooking raw yellowfin on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 79 Cooking and granting 200 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt yellowfin. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will only stop burning at level 98 when cooking at the Hosidius Kitchen with the elite Kourend & Kebos Diary completed.

Yellowfin are useful where players lose significant hitpoints and run energy, for example during the Underground Pass quest.
32331:
Burnt yellowfin is the result of accidentally burning a raw yellowfin while attempting to cook yellowfin. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will only stop burning at level 98 when cooking at the Hosidius Kitchen with the elite Kourend & Kebos Diary completed.

The burnt yellowfin has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.
32333:
Raw halibut is a type of fish caught from halibut shoals whilst deep sea trawling, requiring level 83 Fishing and granting 195.5 experience per successful catch with a trawling net, or 39.1 if caught with a fishing rod. They can also be caught occasionally from shimmering and glistening shoals, which require level 69 and 76 Fishing to catch from respectively.

Cooking halibut requires level 83 in Cooking, resulting in a halibut and 212.5 Cooking experience. If unsuccessful, it will result in a burnt halibut instead.
32336:
Halibut is a type of fish that restores 20 Hitpoints when eaten.

It can be obtained by cooking raw halibut on a fire or cooking range. Cooking a halibut requires level 83 Cooking, and grants 212.5 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt halibut. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will only stop burning at level 99 when cooking at the Hosidius Kitchen with the elite Kourend & Kebos Diary completed.

Like cooked karambwan, halibut can be used as a fast food, a subtype of food that incurs non-standard attack or eating delays when consumed. Halibut may be consumed after other foods without delay; this does not work if the halibut is eaten first, and does not work when eating two halibut in a row. This technique (commonly referred to as combo eating) can be further enhanced by drinking a dose of Saradomin brew after your alternative food item, and before your halibut (food>brew>halibut).
32344:
Bluefin is a type of fish that restores 22 Hitpoints and 5 prayer points when eaten.

It can be obtained by cooking raw bluefin on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 87 Cooking and granting 215 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt bluefin. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will only stop burning at level 99 when cooking at the Hosidius Kitchen with the elite Kourend & Kebos Diary completed, or when wearing a Cooking cape.

The bluefin is the second highest instant-health single consumption food, behind the marlin, alongside the tuna potato, anglerfish, dark crab and manta ray.
32352:
Marlin is a type of fish that restores 24 Hitpoints when eaten, making it the highest immediate-healing single-bite food.

It can be obtained by cooking raw marlin on a fire or cooking range. Cooking a marlin requires level 91 Cooking, and grants 225 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt marlin. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, but will never stop burning even at level 99 unless a cooking cape is equipped.
32355:
Burnt marlin is the result of accidentally burning a raw marlin while attempting to cook marlin. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels; there is no level where marlins stop being burned, although wearing a cooking cape will prevent players from burning any food.

The burnt marlin has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.
32357:
A haddock eye is a Herblore secondary used to make super fishing potions. It can be obtained by using a knife on a raw haddock from deep sea trawling, yielding one eye per haddock upon success, whose chance scales with the player's Cooking level.

If cutting on a chum facility, players will receive haddock eyes equal to the number of haddocks cut on that tick, assuming a successful cut. For example, a chum spreader can cut 4 haddocks per tick, yielding a potential 4 haddock eyes scales per tick.
32362:
Marlin scales is a Herblore secondary used to make extended stamina potions, requiring one scale per dose. It can be obtained by using a knife on a raw marlin from deep sea trawling, yielding three scales per marlin upon success, whose chance scales with the player's Cooking level.

If cutting on a chum facility, players will receive scales equal to three times the number of marlin cut on that tick, assuming a successful cut. For example, a chum spreader can cut 4 marlins per tick, yielding a potential 12 marlin scales per tick.
32364:
Camphor crates are an item made with a camphor log and four adamantite nails, by using either a hammer or chisel on the logs (both must be present in the inventory, or Imcando hammer equipped). Doing so requires level 62 Crafting, granting 50 experience.

Once made, players can use an ice cooler (purchasable from any Slayer Master) on the crate to create an empty fish crate, which are used to store deep sea fish caught via deep sea trawling,
32366:
Empty fish crates are an item made by using a camphor crate with an ice cooler, which are purchased from Slayer Masters; up to 10 can be made per action. They are used to store raw fish obtained from shoals whilst deep sea trawling; deep sea fish can only be stored within the crate in sets of 10.

Empty fish crates are stackable when empty, allowing it to only take one space in the cargo hold of a boat. When emptying a trawling net into the cargo hold with empty fish crates stored inside, the crates will automatically be filled, with any remainders stored as normal. As each crate can store 10 fish, players can effectively store up to 10 times the cargo hold's capacity in fish by storing crates filled with fish, which can drastically lengthen a trawling trip.

Filled fish crates can only be emptied while standing inside a bank, returning the crate without the ice cooler. This must be done by right-clicking the "Empty" option whilst having a banking interface open; if emptying the fish crate otherwise, the crate will be lost.
32368:
Fish crate (giant krill) is a fish crate containing 10 raw giant krill. It can be obtained by emptying a trawling net filled with at least 10 raw giant krill whilst an empty fish crate is stored in the cargo hold, which effectively allows players to store 10 deep sea fish per cargo space. It may also be made by using them on the crate.

Filled fish crates can only be emptied while standing inside a bank, returning a camphor crate without the ice cooler. This must be done by right-clicking the "Empty" option whilst having a banking interface open; if emptying the fish crate otherwise, the crate will be lost.
