32386:
The Medallion of the Deep is a neck-slot item which allows the player to dive underwater without the need for a diving apparatus and fishbowl helmet. It can also be used during The Great Brain Robbery to safely explore Harmony Island. It is created by assembling eight medallion fragments found on various islands accessed via the Sailing skill, granting 750 Sailing experience along with 500 Crafting experience.

Assembling the medallion requires that the player read the waterlogged journal, which was written by the medallion's creator and contains hints on the location of the fragments. As the final fragment is found on Wintumber Island, the minimum Sailing level needed to obtain the medallion is 63.

If the medallion is lost, players can reclaim it by searching the crate where the waterlogged journal was found (near Henderson on the Pandemonium). Upon doing so, a chatbox message will appear, stating "Against all common sense, the Medallion of the Deep has somehow found its way into this crate. You quickly grab it before you lose it again."
32388:
Medallion fragments are items found on various islands accessed via the Sailing skill through a variety of activities. There are eight of these fragments, which are assembled into the Medallion of the Deep, an item that allows the wielder to breathe underwater. The medallion is also required for a master clue.

The locations of the fragments are hinted within the waterlogged journal, which was written by the medallion's creator and must be read before the medallion can be assembled. As the final fragment is found on Wintumber Island, the minimum Sailing level needed to obtain the medallion is 63.

If the Medallion is stored in the STASH or lost, the medallion fragments do not need to be reobtained, as the complete Medallion can be retrieved from the crate on The Pandemonium, near Henderson.
32389:
Medallion fragments are items found on various islands accessed via the Sailing skill through a variety of activities. There are eight of these fragments, which are assembled into the Medallion of the Deep, an item that allows the wielder to breathe underwater. The medallion is also required for a master clue.

The locations of the fragments are hinted within the waterlogged journal, which was written by the medallion's creator and must be read before the medallion can be assembled. As the final fragment is found on Wintumber Island, the minimum Sailing level needed to obtain the medallion is 63.

If the Medallion is stored in the STASH or lost, the medallion fragments do not need to be reobtained, as the complete Medallion can be retrieved from the crate on The Pandemonium, near Henderson.

32396:
The waterlogged journal is a book found in a crate near Henderson on the Pandemonium.

The journal is written by an unnamed wizard from the first Wizards' Tower (only referred to as "W.S."), who left the Order of Wizards to become a sailor. To aid their crew in finding underwater treasure, they created the Medallion of the Deep, though it was split into eight fragments after the wizard killed their crew in self-defence. The wizard was sent to Rock Island Prison, where they began having nightmares showing them the locations of each fragment. Reading the journal is a requirement for the player to assemble the Medallion of the Deep. If the Medallion of the Deep has been assembled, the journal can no longer be found in the crate.

At this time, the journal cannot be placed within a bookcase in the player-owned house.
32398:
The sailors' amulet is an item that can be obtained as loot when sorting through salvage obtained from shipwreck salvaging. The amulet allows the player to teleport to the Pandemonium, Port Roberts, Red Rock, and Deepfin Point. In order to make use of the amulet's destinations, the player must activate their corresponding Sailors' Marker there.

The amulet consumes 90% less law runes, as it uses one charge per teleport and ten charges can be added by using one law rune and 10 water runes on the amulet, up to a maximum of 10,000 charges. This makes the cost of ten charges 176 coins and the cost of fully charging it 176,000 coins. The amulet cannot be uncharged. No experience points are granted when charging the amulet, and rune-saving equipment such as a staff of water cannot be used to decrease the rune cost.

The amulet's capabilities are at its best when the player has access to Deepfin Point with level 67 Sailing, as the teleport places the player around eight tiles from the bank chest, making it incredibly useful for players who do not have a Crafting cape for a quick bank. The Deepfin Point teleport is also very close to a furnace, anvil, and charter ship.

Only one sailors' amulet can be owned at a time. If lost, players must sort through salvage for another one.

32402:
The gale catcher schematic is a lost schematic that must be read in order to unlock the ability to build a gale catcher for a boat.

The schematic is obtained by using a small key to open the lockbox on Anglers' Retreat.

The key can be obtained by digging at the location on the Onyx Crest. Without the key, the player will instead obtain a set of lockbox directions hinting at the key's location.

Because of its location, the schematic requires a Sailing level of 51 to obtain and cannot be boosted.
32403:
The eternal brazier schematic is a lost schematic that must be read in order to unlock the ability to build an eternal brazier for a boat, which is required to navigate the Northern Ocean.

The schematic is obtained by using a small key to open the lockbox on Buccaneers' Haven.

The key can be obtained by digging at the location on the north-western corner on the Tear of the Soul. Without the key, the player will instead obtain a set of lockbox directions hinting at the key's location.

Because of its location, the schematic requires a Sailing level of 76 to obtain and cannot be boosted.
32405:
The rosewood cargo hold schematic is a lost schematic that must be read in order to unlock the ability to build a rosewood cargo hold for a boat.

The schematic is obtained by using a small key to open the lockbox on the Crown Jewel.

The key can be obtained by digging at the location on Minotaurs' Rest, which requires completion of Children of the Sun to access. Without the key, the player will instead obtain a set of lockbox directions hinting at the key's location.

Accessing the island requires completion of Children of the Sun.

Because of its location, the schematic requires a Sailing level of 64 to obtain and cannot be boosted.

The small key is an item dug up on the Pandemonium by following the lockbox directions from the lockbox on Chinchompa Island: "On the Pandemonium, you'll dig on dry land, but make sure to move as far east as you can."

The small key can be obtained without ever obtaining the lockbox directions, and can be banked should the player not have the level 42 Sailing requirement to dock on Chinchompa Island.

The small key can be obtained without ever obtaining the lockbox directions, and can be banked should the player not have the level 64 Sailing requirement to dock on the Crown Jewel.

The small key can be obtained without ever obtaining the lockbox directions; upon opening the lockbox on Deepfin Point with this small key, players are given the dragon cannon schematic.

32419:

32431:
The book about lighthouses is an item obtained by bringing the captain's log to Gerardus once the Northern Ocean is fully charted, which requires a Sailing level of at least 78.

It is given to Larrissa in front of the lighthouse in order to unlock Armadylean paint for boat trims. Doing so requires completion of Horror from the Deep; otherwise, she will be too worried about her darling to give out Armadylean paint.
32432:
The charred key is an item obtained by bringing the captain's log to Gerardus once the Unquiet Ocean is fully charted, which requires a Sailing level of at least 47 and to have started Troubled Tortugans.

It is used to open the old chest in the Charred Dungeon beneath Charred Island, which unlocks Zamorakian paint for boat trims. As the chest is located on Charred Island, the paint requires a Sailing level of at least 60 to obtain. Players will need a rope the first time they enter the dungeon, which spawns on the southern tip of the island.
32433:
The void orb is an item obtained by bringing the captain's log to Gerardus once the Shrouded Ocean is fully charted, which requires a Sailing level of at least 72.

It is given to Elite Void Knight at the Void Knights' Outpost in order to unlock Guthixian paint for boat trims.
32434:
The holy sheet is an item obtained by bringing the captain's log to Gerardus once the Ardent Ocean is fully charted, which requires a Sailing level of at least 38.

It is given to High Priest on Entrana in order to unlock Saradominist paint for boat trims.
32435:
A crate of adamantite ore is an item that may be obtained from a ledger table after taking on a courier task, which must then be delivered to the corresponding destination's port by boarding their boat and sailing to said destination. Players without a crewmate to navigate their boat must store the crate in the cargo hold before they can man the helm.

Multiple of a crate may be required to be delivered for a courier task, in which case players must board their boat multiple times to store the crates (as they can only carry one at a time) or have a crewmate assist them, who will automatically take a crate when the player does so. While any crewmate can carry a crate, those with Deckhandiness levels of at least 3 can carry two at once.

Players cannot unequip the crate normally, nor can they teleport or leave the port area with the crate equipped. If the player leaves the area, a game message appears stating You're leaving port with some cargo. If you do not return it, it will be confiscated by the shipwright wizard's autonomous tracking unit. After 22 ticks (13.2s), the crate will be removed with an accompanying game message stating Your cargo has been confiscated by the S.W.A.T. team.

Multiple of a crate may be required to be delivered for a courier task, in which case players must board their boat multiple times to store the crates (as they can only carry one at a time) or have a crewmate assist them, who will automatically take a crate when the player does so. While any crewmate can carry a crate, those with Deckhandiness levels of at least 3 can carry two at once.

Players cannot unequip the crate normally, nor can they teleport or leave the port area with the crate equipped. If the player leaves the area, a game message appears stating You're leaving port with some cargo. If you do not return it, it will be confiscated by the shipwright wizard's autonomous tracking unit. After 22 ticks (13.2s), the crate will be removed with an accompanying game message stating Your cargo has been confiscated by the S.W.A.T. team.

Multiple of a crate may be required to be delivered for a courier task, in which case players must board their boat multiple times to store the crates (as they can only carry one at a time) or have a crewmate assist them, who will automatically take a crate when the player does so. While any crewmate can carry a crate, those with Deckhandiness levels of at least 3 can carry two at once.

Players cannot unequip the crate normally, nor can they teleport or leave the port area with the crate equipped. If the player leaves the area, a game message appears stating You're leaving port with some cargo. If you do not return it, it will be confiscated by the shipwright wizard's autonomous tracking unit. After 22 ticks (13.2s), the crate will be removed with an accompanying game message stating Your cargo has been confiscated by the S.W.A.T. team.

Multiple of a crate may be required to be delivered for a courier task, in which case players must board their boat multiple times to store the crates (as they can only carry one at a time) or have a crewmate assist them, who will automatically take a crate when the player does so. While any crewmate can carry a crate, those with Deckhandiness levels of at least 3 can carry two at once.

Players cannot unequip the crate normally, nor can they teleport or leave the port area with the crate equipped. If the player leaves the area, a game message appears stating You're leaving port with some cargo. If you do not return it, it will be confiscated by the shipwright wizard's autonomous tracking unit. After 22 ticks (13.2s), the crate will be removed with an accompanying game message stating Your cargo has been confiscated by the S.W.A.T. team.

Multiple of a crate may be required to be delivered for a courier task, in which case players must board their boat multiple times to store the crates (as they can only carry one at a time) or have a crewmate assist them, who will automatically take a crate when the player does so. While any crewmate can carry a crate, those with Deckhandiness levels of at least 3 can carry two at once.

Players cannot unequip the crate normally, nor can they teleport or leave the port area with the crate equipped. If the player leaves the area, a game message appears stating You're leaving port with some cargo. If you do not return it, it will be confiscated by the shipwright wizard's autonomous tracking unit. After 22 ticks (13.2s), the crate will be removed with an accompanying game message stating Your cargo has been confiscated by the S.W.A.T. team.

32876: An aquanite tendon is an item obtained from aquanites found within the Ynysdail Cavern. Players with level 60 Smithing can create the aquanite hopper by using the tendon on an anvil with a mithril bar and hammer in the inventory, granting 350 experience.
32879:
The aquanite hopper is a ranged offhand requiring level 60 Ranged to equip. It is created by using an aquanite tendon on an anvil whilst having a mithril bar and hammer in the player's inventory, requiring level 60 Smithing and granting 350 experience.

The hopper is a purely offensive shield slot item with no defensive bonuses, but possesses a passive effect in which crossbows are given an 11% chance to fire a second shot when the hopper is equipped. This second shot has 33.3% reduced accuracy, 66.7% reduced damage, and 66.7% reduced enchanted bolt proc chance; if the first shot procs an enchanted bolt effect, the second shot will never do so.
32882: Reef snake gland is the venom gland of a reef snake.
32886:
A chain is an item used to link two cannonballs together to create two chainshot cannonballs for boat combat. These require the same Smithing level, and gives the added bonus of halving a target's movement speed for 8 ticks (4.8s).

They are created at an anvil with one steel bar, requiring level 34 Smithing and granting 37.5 experience.

Aside from making chainshot cannonballs, they are used to create the Ivandis flail by linking the enchanted emerald sickle (b) and the rod of Ivandis together.

Chains can be freely obtained from a crate in the old Myreque Hideout under Old Man Ral's house during A Taste of Hope. After the quest, it can be obtained again from the same place, but the player can only collect one at a time without performing the drop trick.
32892:
A cupronickel bar is a metal bar used in shipbuilding, as well as certain island amenities. It can be smelted at level 74 Smithing by using 2 copper ore and 1 nickel ore on a furnace or by using the Superheat Item spell from the standard spell book.

When attempting to make cupronickel bars at the Blast Furnace, up to 14 nickel ore can be deposited at a time. As a result, players should deposit 18 copper ore and 9 nickel ore each run, withdrawing the bars once every three runs for a total of 27 bars per withdraw.
32895:
A coin pouch is an item obtained from pickpocketing certain NPCs, which contains several coins depending on the NPC it was obtained from. To obtain the coins from them, players can simply click their stack of coin pouches to open them all at once, or they can right-click them to open one at a time. They cannot be traded or banked.

Up to 28 coin pouches can stack in a player's inventory, after which the player must open them to collect the coins inside before being able to pickpocket more. This limit can be increased by completing the Ardougne Diary, where it increases to 56, 84, and 140 after completing the Medium, Hard, and Elite diaries, respectively.

Coin pouches have different variants depending on who the player pickpocketed it from; for example, a coin pouch from pickpocketing guards does not stack with pouches from pickpocketing Ardougne knights. NPCs who are pickpocketed via blackjacking yield coins directly while they are knocked out instead of coin pouches. If rogue equipment is used to receive double the loot from pickpocketing, only one coin pouch is obtained (containing the normal amount) while the other half is obtained directly as coins.
32904:
Camphor logs are logs, which can be cut from camphor trees, requiring 66 Woodcutting to chop and grants 143.5 Woodcutting experience per log. Their primary purpose is to be converted into camphor planks at a sawmill, costing 2,500 coins each, planks which are extensively used for boat upgrades and amenities in the Sailing skill. Alternatively, the Lunar spell Plank Make can allow players to convert them to planks at a lower cost, but at the expense of runes.

Players can also burn these logs with the Firemaking skill for 180 experience at level 66 or above.

Camphor trees are only located on the Great Conch, which requires partial completion of Troubled Tortugans. Players with level 66 Farming can also farm them by planting a camphor sapling at a hardwood tree patch.
32907:
Ironwood logs are logs which can be cut from ironwood trees, requiring 80 Woodcutting to chop and grants 175 Woodcutting experience per log. Players can burn these logs with the Firemaking skill for 220.5 experience at level 80 or above.

Players training Construction can bring ironwood logs to a sawmill to get a ironwood plank at a cost of 5,000 coins each. Alternatively, the Lunar spell Plank Make can allow players to convert them to planks at a lower cost, but at the expense of runes.

Ironwood trees are only located on Sunbleak Island, which requires 72 Sailing to dock at. Players with level 80 Farming can also farm them by planting an ironwood sapling at a hardwood tree patch.
32910:
Rosewood logs are logs which can be cut from rosewood trees, requiring 92 Woodcutting to chop and grants 212.5 Woodcutting experience per log. Players can burn these logs with the Firemaking skill for 268 experience at level 92 or above.

Players training Construction can bring rosewood logs to a sawmill to get a rosewood plank at a cost of 7,500 coins each. Alternatively, the Lunar spell Plank Make can allow players to convert them to planks at a lower cost, but at the expense of runes.

Rosewood trees are only located on Drumstick Isle, which requires level 79 Sailing to dock at. Players with level 92 Farming can also farm them by planting a rosewood sapling at a hardwood tree patch.

Because Drumstick Isle is far from a bank, having a greater teleport focus is recommended to chop large quantities, although this can be rather costly and/or even more time-consuming to obtain. Without the greater teleport focus, using the Prifddinas dock and sailing north to the teal portal is the fastest way to get to the isle. A log basket is recommended to extend trip lengths, and if intending to make planks out of the logs, a plank sack with runes and coins for Plank Make, as well as sawmill vouchers is a further optimisation.

Multiple of a crate may be required to be delivered for a courier task, in which case players must board their boat multiple times to store the crates (as they can only carry one at a time) or have a crewmate assist them, who will automatically take a crate when the player does so. While any crewmate can carry a crate, those with Deckhandiness levels of at least 3 can carry two at once.

Players cannot unequip the crate normally, nor can they teleport or leave the port area with the crate equipped. If the player leaves the area, a game message appears stating You're leaving port with some cargo. If you do not return it, it will be confiscated by the shipwright wizard's autonomous tracking unit. After 22 ticks (13.2s), the crate will be removed with an accompanying game message stating Your cargo has been confiscated by the S.W.A.T. team.

A crate of potions is an item that may be obtained from a ledger table after taking on a courier task, which must then be delivered to the corresponding destination's port by boarding their boat and sailing to said destination. Players without a crewmate to navigate their boat must store the crate in the cargo hold before they can man the helm.

Multiple of a crate may be required to be delivered for a courier task, in which case players must board their boat multiple times to store the crates (as they can only carry one at a time) or have a crewmate assist them, who will automatically take a crate when the player does so. While any crewmate can carry a crate, those with Deckhandiness levels of at least 3 can carry two at once.

Players cannot unequip the crate normally, nor can they teleport or leave the port area with the crate equipped. If the player leaves the area, a game message appears stating You're leaving port with some cargo. If you do not return it, it will be confiscated by the shipwright wizard's autonomous tracking unit. After 22 ticks (13.2s), the crate will be removed with an accompanying game message stating Your cargo has been confiscated by the S.W.A.T. team.
33002:
Holy moleys are a cosmetic variant of the holy sandals, made by combining a pair of holy sandals and mole slippers via Wyson the gardener. Like the holy sandals, they require 31 prayer to wear. To combine them, players must use either item on him, which will initiate a confirmation message to combine them.

As a variant of the holy sandals, holy moleys retain the same properties, such as combat stats and counting as a Saradominist item in relevant content (ex. God Wars Dungeon and Bandit Camp). However, holy moleys cannot be stored in the treasure chest of a costume room.

While the holy moleys are untradeable, they can be reverted anytime via the "Dismantle" option, returning both items after the player confirms they wish to do so. Additionally, upon a PvP death, the killer will receive the holy sandals and mole slippers as loot.

Holy moleys count as warm clothing when subduing the Wintertodt.

The Annihilation weapon scroll can be used to cosmetically change the toxic staff of the dead, Bow of Faerdhinen (c), or all three pieces of crystal armour. It can be purchased from the Deadman Reward Store for 12,000 Deadman Points, which are earned from participating in seasonal Deadman events.

The scroll can be used by bringing it to Nigel. When you give the scroll to Nigel, it will permanently unlock the 5 cosmetics for the player and remove the scroll permanently. You can then freely switch any of the items between their standard and deadman variant at Nigel, and it can be applied to however many of the item you wish.

Crystal equipment reverted from the Deadman variant will be reset to the default colours of the item; the Meilyr clan colours for the armour, and the Hefin clan colours for the bow.

Upon PvP death the PK'er will receive the normal variant of the item.

Annihilation blueprints can be used to change a player-owned house's appearance to the Wilderness theme house style. Having the Estate agent re-decorate your house into the Wilderness house style while having the blueprints in the inventory will consume them and permanently unlock the house style.

Upon unlocking the house style, a set of Annihilation exit portal blueprints will replace the consumed Annihilation blueprints in the player's inventory, which can then be used to recolour the exit portal. These exit portal blueprints can be infinitely reclaimed from Nigel in Lumbridge.
33018: The Annihilation teleport scroll is an item that can be purchased from the Deadman Reward Store for 10,000 Deadman Points, which are earned from participating in seasonal Deadman events. It can be used to unlock a Wilderness lever themed Home Teleport animation override. To enable it, players can right click "Animation" on the Home Teleport spell icon in their spellbook and select "Annihilation."
33021:
The bow of Faerdhinen (c) is a corrupted version of the Bow of Faerdhinen that does not degrade, with its appearance altered to resemble the corrupted crystal seen within the Corrupted Gauntlet. The bow's colours may be changed to other colours of the Elven Clans by buying crystals from Lliann's Wares in Prifddinas, which cost 500,000 coins each. It can also be reverted to its original colour by using the crystal of Hefin on any variant of the corrupted bow.

The bow can be upgraded by bringing it and 2,000 crystal shards to a singing bowl. Doing so requires level 82 Smithing and Crafting (the levels can be boosted), and grants no experience. If the player does not meet the Smithing and Crafting requirements, they can have Conwenna or Reese sing the crystal in their stead for an extra 1,000 crystal shards. Excess charges in the bow will be taken into account; for example, a newly created bow with 10,000 charges will require 1,900 crystal shards to corrupt and a fully charged bow will only cost 1,800 crystal shards to upgrade.

Alternatively, the Bow of Faerdhinen can be corrupted passively through use: every 100 shots fired from the bow contributes 1 shard worth of progress toward the 1,900-shard corruption requirement. Once this cumulative amount is reached, the bow can be corrupted at the singing bowl with the level requirements or have Conwenna corrupt it for you for the 1000 shard price. Any combination of progress towards corruption, charges in the bow, and crystal shards can be used to meet the crystal shard requirement to corrupt the bow.

Upon creating the corrupted bow, the chatbox message states "With the help of the crystal bowl, you sing a dark song which corrupts the crystals."

While untradeable, the bow can be uncharged, but the crystal shards used to upgrade it will not be returned.

Like its regular variant, the bow requires level 80 Ranged and 70 Agility to wield, and provides the highest Ranged Attack and Ranged Strength bonus out of any weapon for its attack speed. It also benefits from damage and accuracy boosts when crystal armour is equipped. Each crystal armour piece equipped grants additional bonus accuracy and damage, adding up to a total 15% damage and 30% accuracy bonus when the full set is equipped.

When using crystal armour, the bow provides similar damage per second to the twisted bow and toxic blowpipe; however, these weapons excel against targets with high Magic level and low Defence respectively. Unlike the twisted bow or toxic blowpipe, the corrupted bow of Faerdhinen suffers no significant drawback and provides consistent performance due to its high accuracy and damage per shot, along with its moderate attack speed, long range, and unlimited ammunition.

The mooleta is a melee off-hand dropped by the post-quest version of Brutus. It has no requirements to wield and offers similar bonuses to a steel defender.

The mooleta is the only shield slot item in free-to-play to give a melee strength bonus, as well as stab, slash, and crush attack bonuses.
33112: A burnt t-bone steak is the result of accidentally burning a raw t-bone steak while attempting to make a cooked t-bone steak. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels.
33115:
Bull bones are remains dropped by Brutus. Unlike most items, which only have a "Take" option on the ground, the item has a "Bury" option instead, which when selected prompts a confirmation message whether the player wishes to receive 40 Prayer experience. This confirmation message is shared with giant bones, and toggling it off for one of the bones toggles it off for both.

Telekinetic Grab cannot be cast on the bones, and the bonecrusher works to automatically bury them. As they cannot be picked up, they cannot be used for alternative Prayer training methods, such as the gilded altar or the deep Wilderness chaos altar.
33118:
Abyssal potatoes are obtained by harvesting the growth just north of the fire in the Scar. Harvesting the potato causes the message You harvest an odd looking object. It kind of looks like a potato. to appear. It provides a +1 Strength boost when eaten, with the message You eat the potato. You feel strangely powerful.

Feeding an abyssal potato to Brutus upgrades the fight to its hard version, Demonic Brutus. Obtaining the potato requires completion of Desert Treasure II; defeating the Leviathan alone is insufficient to obtain the potato. This item cannot be put in sacks.
33122:
Annihilation exit portal blueprints are received when first using the Annihilation blueprints to redecorate a player-owned house to the wilderness theme house style. They are used to construct an Annihilation exit portal, which can be used with any house style.

To use the blueprints, players must build an Annihilation exit portal in the centrepiece space of a garden or formal garden in their player-owned house, requiring 10 iron bars and the Annihilation exit portal blueprints. The player must have a hammer and saw in their inventory to build it. If players only have one exit portal in their house, they will not be able to remove it until a second one is built.

Players will not receive back the blueprints upon removing the portal. However, additional copies can be obtained by speaking to Nigel in Lumbridge.
33124:
Beef is a pet that can be obtained from defeating Brutus.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.

Beef has an Interact option, in which the player can choose the options "Moo" and "Emote". The "Moo" option will make Beef (as well as a random nearby cow) say "moo".
33133:
Pristine spider silk is an item dropped by Sarachnis, which can be combined with the herb sack to create a silklined herb sack, which gives an increased storage capacity.

There are no additional level requirements or items needed in order to upgrade the herb sack, and it does not need to be emptied prior to doing so.

Extra sheets of pristine spider silk can be given to Brother Aimeri in exchange for a grubby key. This requires starting the miniquest In Search of Knowledge, by healing him with five pieces of food (must be meat, fish, or vegetables).
33135:
A silklined herb sack is an upgraded variant of the herb sack, made by using a pristine spider silk on it. It will store up to 100 of each of the grimy normal herbs instead of 30, for a total of 1,500 stored. Because of the greatly expanded capacity, it is a useful item for farming herbs. A full herb sack is worth 3,590,500 coins.

It can be manually filled by using the left-click 'Fill' option, which will deposit any grimy herbs from your inventory, unless it is full. It can be opened or closed with the right-click options 'Open' or 'Close' respectively. An open sack will automatically deposit any grimy herbs that are picked up by the player, as well as those harvested from a herb patch and Herbiboars, provided there is space for it. A closed sack will not automatically deposit herbs.

The 'Empty' option deposits herbs into the inventory, starting from the lowest level herb, and with the bank open it will deposit all of the contents into the bank. Using the 'Check' option will list all currently stored herbs within it in the chat box. Using the 'Check' option while the sack is empty will result in the messages You look in your silklined herb sack and see: The silklined herb sack is empty.

The herb sack is useful for killing monsters that often drop valuable herbs, such as chaos druids, flesh crawlers, aberrant spectres, and deviant spectres, since it only takes up one inventory slot. It can also be used when lighting incense burners during open altar house parties, reducing the frequency of banking or unnoting Marrentill at Phials.

Herbs stored within it are not lost upon death, and will stay in the herb sack upon death, unless the player has untoggled this setting. Even if the herb sack is one of the items kept on PvP death, the herbs inside the herb sack are NOT kept on death when killed by a player.

33146:
The Scribbled notes can be obtained from the note on a table during the 2026 Easter event, or reclaimed from the Easter Bunny if lost.

Reading the notes shows different hints to help the player find Archibald depending on their progress through the event:

"I heard there is a potion that can make me stronger!" - Search shelves in Apothecary's pharmacy.

"I heard about a guy who sells bendy sticks." - Search stepladder on the 2nd floor of Lowe's Archery Emporium. You will also receive an egg box, for which the code to unlock it is "LOWE".

"I heard the view from up here is the best!" - Search the wall at the very top of the Varrock church. You will go through a cut-scene.

"I heard you can buy shiny, pointy sticks from this guy." - Search the table with weapons on it at Varrock Swordshop.

"I heard about an evil place of worship. Sounds cool!" - Go to the building in south-east Varrock, where the Mage of Zamorak resides and search the chair.

"Bil noun omen." - Anagram for Blue Moon Inn. Search the bed in the easternmost room on the top floor to find a decoy egg box. Click the egg box to receive the next note.

"I heard there is a real king, in a court!" - Go to Varrock Palace and search the eastern suit of armour in King Roald's room.

"I heard there is this massive vault of riches underground." - Go to Varrock west bank and catch Archibald underground, next to the gate.

Return the egg to the Easter Bunny to complete the event.

33166:
A crystal body is a piece of crystal armour requiring 70 Defence and 50 Agility to equip. When equipped, a 7.5% damage bonus and 15% accuracy bonus is applied to the crystal bow or Bow of Faerdhinen when either is equipped. This bonus stacks additively with the crystal legs and crystal helm's bonuses, for a total of 15% damage and 30% accuracy. The bonus also stacks with the slayer helmet (i) and is useful for bosses similar to the Abyssal Sire.

Players can create a crystal body via a singing bowl by combining 150 crystal shards and three crystal armour seeds. Doing so requires level 74 Smithing and Crafting to sing the crystal (the levels can be boosted), and grants 7,500 experience in both skills. Players can configure the charges while the crystal body is in their bank by right-clicking on Configure-Charges, as long as players have the required materials. If the player does not meet the Smithing and Crafting requirements, they can have Conwenna or Reese sing the crystal for them for an extra 60 crystal shards, for a total of 210.

The body's colours may also be changed to other colours of the Elven Clans by buying crystals from Lliann's Wares in Prifddinas, which cost 500,000 coins each. It can also be reverted to its original colour by using the crystal of Meilyr on any variant of the body.

If lost to another player in a dangerous PVP death, the crystal body will revert to 3 crystal armour seeds, which will then be dropped for the killer. All crystal shards will be lost should this happen. If the crystal body is protected on death, the body will be kept, and will not lose any charges- similar to a blowpipe or trident.

When combined with an imbued slayer helmet, the damage bonus from crystal armour pieces is multiplied by the 15% ranged damage boost from the helmet. Assuming players are wearing both the crystal body and legs, this results in a damage bonus of approximately 29.375%.
33168: Crystal legs from Last Man Standing is a minigame-exclusive variant of the normal Crystal legs. It can be obtained from opening the chests with a bloody key or bloodier key. It is dropped upon death to whoever killed you.
33178: The noxious halberd from Last Man Standing is a minigame-exclusive variant of the normal noxious halberd. It can be obtained from opening the chests with a bloody key, or looting the crates that spawn at random locations on the map. It is dropped on death to whoever killed you.
33182:
The ultor ring is one of four ancient rings which currently boasts the highest strength bonus of any ring, surpassing the imbued berserker ring by +4. The ring requires players to have killed Vardorvis at least once to wear, which is done during Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire; attempting to wear it otherwise will result in the message The ring slips off your finger. The power within it seems unfamiliar.

The ring requires level 90 Magic and 80 Crafting to create (both being boostable), as well as having learnt how to combine Fremennik ring icons with ancient vestiges via Peer the Seer.

Players who are able to craft the ring must first combine the berserker icon, 500 blood runes, and the ultor vestige, obtained as an untradeable drop from Vardorvis. Next, they must bring the resulting ultor icon to a furnace, alongside three chromium ingots and a ring mould, to craft the ring.

Unlike their predecessors, the Fremennik rings, the ancient rings cannot be imbued.
33184: Purging staff from Last Man Standing is a minigame-exclusive variant of the normal Purging staff. It can be obtained from opening the chests with a bloody key, or looting the crates that spawn at random locations on the map. It is dropped on death to whoever killed you.
33186:
A dragonfire shield is an upgraded anti-dragon shield, and one of the best shields in the game behind the elysian spirit shield and Dinh's bulwark. Equipping it requires 75 Defence and having started Dragon Slayer I. It retains the same dragonfire protection as the anti-dragon shield and it also provides partial protection against the icy breath of wyverns, like the dragonfire ward, elemental shield, and mind shield.

When uncharged, it is tradeable and offers slightly more defensive bonuses than a mithril sq shield, however, each charge it gains increases melee defensive bonuses and the range defensive bonus by 1 for a total of +50 at maximum for those four defensive stats. To charge the shield, dragonfire needs to be absorbed from dragonfire or icy breath attacks while it is equipped. Bottled dragonbreath can also be used to charge the shield.
33188:
The twisted buckler is a ranged-class shield that is obtained as a possible reward from the Chambers of Xeric, requiring level 75 Ranged and Defence to equip.

The buckler currently offers the best Ranged Attack and Ranged Strength bonus for the shield slot in the game. It also has some of the best Magic defence in its slot, beaten only by the dragonfire ward and spectral spirit shield. Its melee defence bonuses are comparable to an adamant sq shield.
33190:
The fortified Masori body is an upgraded variant of the Masori body. It is created by combining a Masori body with four Armadylean plates. This process requires level 90 Crafting, and is not reversible.

Part of the Masori armour set, the fortified body requires level 80 Ranged and Defence to equip, and boasts increased defence bonuses and a +1 prayer bonus in comparison to the standard variant.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Masori armour (fortified) set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
33194:
The Torva platelegs are part of the Torva armour set, requiring 80 Defence to wear. The platelegs boast the highest strength bonus of any legs slot equipment, being 2 higher than the Bandos tassets. As a Zarosian-aligned item, Torva armour will give Zarosian protection within the God Wars Dungeon.

The platelegs are created by combining damaged Torva platelegs, obtained as a drop from Nex, with two Bandosian components. This process requires level 90 Smithing, and is not reversible.
33202:
Aranea boots are a pair of boots dropped by araxytes. With no requirements to wear, they are currently the best-in-slot boots for one-defence pures and zerkers, due to the tribrid stats they have, with a ranged attack bonus between that of mixed hide boots and blessed dragonhide boots, a magic attack bonus equal to infinity boots, and a melee strength bonus equal to dragon boots.

The boots have a special web-negating mechanic that allows players to pass through webs in various locations without the need of a slash weapon. Additionally, the boots also negate certain special attacks once every 8 ticks (4.8 seconds) from arachnid bosses; when this occurs, a game message will state Your Aranea boots let you avoid the spider-based attack. The exception to this is Araxxor's venom cleave, which can be negated only once every 6 attacks, so every 12 seconds (20 ticks).

The following bosses can have their spider-based attacks negated:

Sarachnis' sticky web attack

Venenatis and Spindel's draining webs (The first tick is the only part of this ability negated)

Araxxor's venom cleave during his enrage phase

Araxxor's ranged auto attack; the magic auto attack is not negated.

Verzik Vitur's snapping webs during phase 3
33227:
The Evil eye is an item obtained during the Demonic Pacts League, given to players who picked the Evil Eye relic. The Eye allows players to teleport to the entrance of any boss or raid in the combat achievements list.

The eye can be retrieved from the Leagues Tutor in Yama's Lair if lost.
33229:
The transmutation ledger is an item obtained during the Demonic Pacts League, given to players who picked the Transmute relic.

The ledger, whether in the inventory or equipped, counts as an infinite source of nature runes. Additionally, players can use items compatible with transmutation spells on the ledger to show a list of what they can turn into.

The ledger is unnecessary to cast the transmutation spells, and the spells can be cast even if greyed-out in the spellbook.
33231:
Soul shards are an item obtained during the Demonic Pacts League by players who have picked the Soul Harvest relic, via harvesting any crops (including picking fruit at Tithe Farm or picking herbs in the Chambers of Xeric), as well as a replacement for bones and demonic ashes when killing any NPC that would otherwise drop them. Soul shards are automatically placed in the inventory providing space is available.

Soul shards can be used as a substitute for rune or pure essence while training Runecraft (including combination and sunfire runes), as well as blessed bone shards at the Teomat's libation bowl (requires 30 Prayer) to earn 550 Prayer XP per 100 shards (before Leagues multipliers); sacrificing soul shards does not require wine (jugs of blessed wine or blessed sunfire wine). Soul Shards may also be used on the Blood and Soul Altars in Kourend as a substitute for Dark essence fragments.
33235:
Clue contracts is an item obtained during the Demonic Pacts League, which may be rewarded from opening reward caskets with the Conniving Clues relic.

They can be used to teleport to the location of the current clue step, and are also used in place of the usual items Falo asks for. Each contract can be used for one teleport.
33237:
The butler's bell is an item obtained during the Demonic Pacts League, given to players who picked the Butler's Bell relic.

When rung it will summon a Demon butler to work for the player, who gathers and processes resources even while offline. Using the Check-option on the bell gives the status on what the butler is currently working on for the player.
33239:
The flask of fervour is an item obtained during the Demonic Pacts League, given to players who picked the Flask of Fervour relic.

When the Flask is consumed, Hitpoints, prayer points, and special attack energy are fully restored. The player may also use this when their hitpoints reach 0 but has not started the death animation. Over the next 4 ticks (2.4s), three explosions hit all enemies (with some exceptions, see below) within 3 tiles of the player's position at each intervals (follows the player) typeless damage equal to 60% of base Prayer level (30% in PvP). During the active effect, all damage taken is reduced to 0. Venom is cured upon use and sanity is restored to 100%.

The flask has a base cooldown of 3 minutes (300 ticks) which is reduced by 1 tick (0.6s) for each instance of 10 damage dealt in a single hit, meaning that a player who attacks for 40 damage, or deals 2x20 damage reduces the cooldown by 4 ticks (2.4s). Dealing 2x9 damage does not reduce the cooldown. Its own explosion damage also does not reduce the cooldown.

The flask can be retrieved from the Leagues Tutor in Yama's Lair if lost.

33243:
The infernal tecpatl is a two-handed echo weapon that can be obtained from Echo Amoxliatl during the Demonic Pacts League.

The weapon is essentially a mix of the lesser nagua weapons, sharing the same accuracy bonuses as the earthbound tecpatl, sulphur blades, and glacial temotli, and is able to use all three attack styles (stab, slash, and crush). The only differences between it and the three lesser nagua weapons is that it has a slightly better strength bonus (+70 vs +64), a demonbane effect, and a negative prayer bonus.

Each attack lands two independently rolled hits; the maximum damage of each hit is determined by calculating the combined max hit as normal and dividing it by two. If the combined max hit is odd, one max hit is rounded up while the other is rounded down (e.g., 45 → 22 + 23). Additionally, the infernal tecpatl has 10% demonbane, providing increased accuracy and damage against demons.
33247:
V's helm is a helmet that can be obtained from the Echo Dagannoth Kings during the Demonic Pacts League.

It acts as an imbued slayer helm and provides a passive effect which grants a 5% chance when the player is hit with 1 or more damage to reduce that damage to 0; when this occurs the player will receive the message V's helmet fills you with energy. and their next special attack within 60 seconds will not cost any special attack energy to perform. This secondary effect has no cooldown, but cannot be stacked (i.e. if a special attack has not yet been used since the first effect activated, the secondary effect is lost). The special attack orb's icon will change to a unique icon while this secondary effect is active ().
33249:
The Fang of the Hound is a one-handed echo weapon that can be obtained from Echo Cerberus during the Demonic Pacts League.

Every hit with the Fang of the Hound has a 5% chance to cast Flames of Cerberus at the target, which is a fire spell with a base max hit of 10, and can be increased with elemental weakness and magic strength. When the effect is triggered, the magic damage is dealt without needing to pass a second accuracy check. The effect also benefits from pacts.
33251:
King's barrage is a two-handed crossbow that can be obtained from Echo King Black Dragon during the Demonic Pacts League. It is able to fire bolts up to dragon, and additionally deals full damage to the Corporeal Beast.

The crossbow always shoots 2 bolts at once, dealing damage in two hitsplats, with both hitsplats having their max hit halved. The first bolt counts as a crossbow attack, while the other counts as an ice attack which will always freeze the current target in place for 24 ticks (14.4 seconds). The freeze effect can be toggled on and off with the weapon. The ice attack does not regenerate runes. The crossbow generates both ranged and mage experience.
33253:
The shadowflame quadrant is a one-handed staff that can be obtained from the Echo Thermonuclear smoke devil during the Demonic Pacts League. The staff acts as an infinite source of air, water, earth, and fire runes, and can autocast spells from all spellbooks.

When using elemental spells on the standard spellbook with the quadrant equipped, an additional spell will be fired, dealing 40% of the damage of the first attack. When attacking a monster with an elemental weakness, this weapon will cause the spell to be treated as if the target was weakest to that element. This does not change the originally cast spell, but instead modifies damage and accuracy according to the monster's highest weakness. For example, if a target has a 30% air weakness and the player is casting Water Surge, the quadrant will treat the target as if it had a 30% water weakness instead. This allows the player to benefit from Demonic Pacts that trigger when casting a certain elemental spell, even if their target is not weak to said spell.

It has a melee range of 8 tiles but does not allow for meleeing when equipped.
33255:
The lithic sceptre is a one-handed magic powered sceptre that can be obtained from the Echo Grotesque Guardians in the Demonic Pacts League. It is charged with 1 body rune and 3 earth runes per charge, holding up to 10,000 charges when fully charged.

Every time the player attacks with the sceptre, they will gain a "Shatter stack", which can be stacked up to 14. One Shatter stack will be lost every ~30s when out of combat, regardless of if it is equipped or not. Shatter stacks are also lost upon teleporting or entering an instance.

33423: Bosun's workbench schematic is a lost schematic and a quest reward from The Red Reef. Reading it permanently unlocks the ability to construct Bosun's workbench, a facility on players' boats that allows crewmates to automatically make repairs.
33424:

When in the inventory, the totem applies a red skull to the holder to highlight who is currently holding it. However, if the totem was stored in a looting bag, this red skull would not be applied. This was later fixed by making it so the totem cannot be stored in a looting bag.

33462: Oathplate helm from Last Man Standing is a minigame-exclusive variant of the normal oathplate helm. It can be obtained from opening the chests with a bloody key, or looting the crates that spawn at random locations on the map. It is dropped on death to whoever killed you.
33464:
A Void melee helm is a piece of Void Knight equipment that is obtained as a reward in the Pest Control minigame. It can be bought from a Void Knight for 200 commendation points, although a player must have at least level 42 Attack, Strength, Defence, Hitpoints, Ranged, and Magic, along with level 22 Prayer to buy and wear one.

The melee helm grants the player a 10% bonus towards melee damage and accuracy when worn with the void knight top, robe and gloves. The void knight mace and void seal are not required for the bonus. It has the same stats as the other two helmets. It is useful for training melee skills but maximum strength gear will be more effective. The void melee helm is the only Void Knight helmet that doesn't have any additional benefit with Elite Void.

If the player dies a PvP death at level 20 Wilderness or below and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 160,000 coins.

If the player dies a PvP death above level 20 Wilderness and the item is unprotected, it will be converted to coins. To prevent this, a Trouver parchment and a payment of 500,000 coins can be given to Perdu in order to permanently lock the item. The locked item will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a mangled, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 500,000 coins.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room.

The helm can also be given to the Dodgy Squire in exchange for 160 Void Knight commendation points.

The Void mage helm is a piece of Void Knight equipment. It can be bought from a Void Knight for 200 commendation points, if the player has at least 42 Attack, Strength, Defence, Hitpoints, Ranged, and Magic, and 22 Prayer to buy and wear one. It is worn in combination with the other pieces of Void Knight Armour (Void knight top, Void knight robe, and Void knight gloves) to achieve the designated set effect. The Void knight mace is not required for the bonus.

The Void mage set gives a +45% to magic accuracy. This typically provides less accuracy and defensive bonuses than Ahrim's robes, but can be easily switched with the other Void sets. If wearing Elite Void Knight robes, the set gives an additional 5% increase to magic damage.

The effective magic attack bonus can be calculated as 1.45x+28.8, where x is the total equipment magic attack bonus when wearing the Void mage set. For example, if you have a magic attack bonus of +16 while also wearing the Void mage set (which provides no bonus), the effective bonus becomes +52 taking into account the set effect. When wearing several best-in-slot pieces of magical gear, the accuracy of the Void mage set can surpass Ahrim's robes with the same gear.

If the player dies a PvP death at level 20 Wilderness or below and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 160,000 coins.

The Void mage set gives a +45% to magic accuracy. This typically provides less accuracy and defensive bonuses than Ahrim's robes, but can be easily switched with the other Void sets. If wearing Elite Void Knight robes, the set gives an additional 5% increase to magic damage.

The effective magic attack bonus can be calculated as 1.45x+28.8, where x is the total equipment magic attack bonus when wearing the Void mage set. For example, if you have a magic attack bonus of +16 while also wearing the Void mage set (which provides no bonus), the effective bonus becomes +52 taking into account the set effect. When wearing several best-in-slot pieces of magical gear, the accuracy of the Void mage set can surpass Ahrim's robes with the same gear.

33496:
The infernal max cape is the result of combining an infernal cape with a max cape, during which the max hood is required to be in the player's inventory and will automatically be converted to the infernal max hood.

Like the other max cape variants (a max cape combined with another cape slot item), the infernal max cape does not have the max cape's stats or perks; it only acts as a cosmetic upgrade to the infernal cape with the following exceptions when worn:

It acts as a Cooking cape to allow access to the Cooks' Guild without a chef's hat, golden chef's hat, Varrock armour 3 or 4

It acts as a Crafting cape to allow access to the Crafting Guild without a brown apron or golden apron

It acts as a Runecraft cape to prevent essence pouches from degrading (but does not allow access to runic altars)

It acts as a Firemaking cape to work as a piece of warm clothing

It can be used to perform the Skill Cape emote.

It is lighter, weighing 0.453kg instead of 1.814kg

The max cape and infernal cape can be separated by using a knife on the cape. Mac will also buy back a max cape, along with its variants, for 1,900,800 coins each. He will return the secondary item any max cape variant was combined with upon doing so.

If the player dies a PvP death at level 20 Wilderness or below and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 225,000 coins.

If the player dies a PvP death above level 20 Wilderness and the item is unprotected, it will be converted to coins. To prevent this, a Trouver parchment and a payment of 500,000 coins can be given to Perdu in order to permanently lock the item. The locked item will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a mangled, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 500,000 coins.

An infernal max cape cannot be gambled for a chance at Jal-Nib-Rek.

There were approximately 9,463 players who could have an infernal max cape as of 12th March 2022.

33500:
The infernal cape is the most powerful melee cape in terms of overall bonuses, awarded for defeating TzKal-Zuk in the Inferno. It surpasses its predecessor, the fire cape, boasting greater melee attack and strength bonuses, along with slightly higher defensive bonuses. In spite of this, it is still surpassed by the Ardougne cloaks 3 and 4 in stab attack and prayer bonuses, and by the mythical cape in crush attack.

An infernal cape can be exchanged for a chance of obtaining the Jal-Nib-Rek pet by speaking to TzHaar-Ket-Keh. Like killing TzKal-Zuk, there is a 1/100 chance of obtaining the pet this way. If the player already has the pet, capes cannot be exchanged.

An infernal cape can be combined with the max cape to change its appearance by turning it into the infernal max cape.

As of 1 August 2026, there are 170,755 accounts that have obtained an infernal cape.

If the player dies a PvP death at level 20 Wilderness or below and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 225,000 coins.

If the player dies a PvP death above level 20 Wilderness and the item is unprotected, it will be converted to coins. To prevent this, a Trouver parchment and a payment of 500,000 coins can be given to Perdu in order to permanently lock the item. The locked item will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a mangled, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 500,000 coins.

While equipping the fire cape will grant players the fiery attribute and will therefore make them susceptible to the extra damage from the special effect of pearl bolts (e), the infernal cape does not grant this attribute.

Note: It is possible to obtain at any level, but low level players may struggle specifically with the attacker role.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room.
33522:
The fighter torso (called the Penance torso in the Barbarian Assault Reward Shop) is armour that requires 40 Defence to equip and is a reward from the Barbarian Assault minigame. It can be purchased from Commander Connad for 375 honour points in all four roles, and one Penance Queen kill. It can be sold back to Connad for 300 honour points in all four roles by using it on him.

If the player dies a PvP death at level 20 Wilderness or below and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 150,000 coins.

If the player dies a PvP death above level 20 Wilderness and the item is unprotected, it will be converted to coins. To prevent this, a Trouver parchment and a payment of 500,000 coins can be given to Perdu in order to permanently lock the item. The locked item will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a mangled, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 500,000 coins.

Note: It is possible to obtain at any level, but low level players may struggle specifically with the attacker role.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room.
33528:
Blessed Dizana's quiver is an upgraded variant of Dizana's quiver, made by using it on a Shrine of Ralos while having a total of 150,000 sunfire splinters and a Dizana's quiver in the player's inventory. Charging the quiver with sunfire splinters contributes to the required amount of splinters to upgrade.

The blessed quiver permanently gains the effects of Dizana's Sunfire, where an additional +1 Ranged Strength and +10 Ranged accuracy is applied to stored arrows and bolts - essentially acting as a variant of the original with unlimited charges. The upgraded variant also retains its level 75 Ranged requirement to equip.

It can also be combined with the max cape to change its appearance by turning it into Dizana's max cape.
33530:

33532:

Like the other max cape variants (a max cape combined with another cape slot item), Dizana's max cape does not have the max cape's stats or perks; it only acts as a cosmetic upgrade to blessed Dizana's quiver with the following exceptions when worn:

It acts as a Crafting cape to allow access to the Crafting Guild without a brown apron or golden apron

It acts as a Runecraft cape to prevent essence pouches from degrading (but does not allow access to runic altars)

It acts as a Firemaking cape to work as a piece of warm clothing

It can be used to perform the Skill Cape emote.

The cape retains the perks of the blessed Dizana's quiver.

The max cape and quiver can be separated by using a knife on the cape. Mac will also buy back a max cape, along with its variants, for 1,900,800 coins each. He will return the secondary item any max cape variant was combined with upon doing so.

33534: The etched araxyte fang is an item created by using a chisel on an araxyte fang. With a Crafting level of 86, it can be combined with a amulet of torture to create the amulet of rancour. Unlike the normal araxyte fang, the etched version is tradeable but cannot be sacrificed to Death's Coffer.
33537:
Garlic cocktails are an item purchasable from a werewolf in the late Lord Myrmel's home, directly south of the Drakan's medallion Darkmeyer teleport.

As completion of The Blood Moon Rises causes vampyres to be tolerant towards the player, having the cocktail in the inventory causes vyrewatch and vyrewatch sentinels to once again be aggressive to the player; however, it has no effect on other vampyres, such as the Darkmeyer bankers or venators. As such, players can still use the Darkmeyer bank with the cocktail in their inventory, and can drop or store the cocktail in their bank if they wish to lose aggression.
33539:
A bucket of bloodwood sap is an item obtained in Vampyrium by cutting either bloodwood trees or the engorged bloodwood tree, and is used to make seeking arrows.

Buckets of bloodwood sap can be either used on any type of logs that can be fletched into arrow shafts, or directly on any unpoisoned arrows. Using one bucket of sap directly on arrows yields 15 seeking arrows, while using one on logs turns it into sap-treated logs.

Because higher tier logs yields higher quantities of arrow shafts per log, using bloodwood sap on logs and then fletching them into seeking arrow shafts will give a better return for the player's time. For arrows that are already made, players can add feathers to the shafts to create seeking headless arrows, then use it on an existing arrow to "upgrade" it to a seeking arrow.

When attempting to collect buckets of bloodwood sap with a full inventory, the bucket will not be collected and will instead be deleted immediately. Logging out will also cause any buckets and buckets of bloodwood sap sitting under the trees to disappear. Teleporting out, however, does not cause them to disappear.
33547:
A seeking headless arrow is used in fletching to make seeking arrows. A set of 15 feathers can be attached to sets of 15 seeking arrow shafts, yielding 15 experience and 15 seeking headless arrows.

Once made, a set of 15 arrowtips can then be attached to them to create seeking arrows; they can also be used on fully made arrows to convert them in sets of 150.
33553:
Seeking bronze arrows are an improved variant of bronze arrows, boasting a +20 ranged attack bonus over their regular variants, as well as increasing the player's minimum hit from 1 to 3 upon a successful hit.

Seeking bronze arrows can be made through several ways:

Attaching bronze arrowtips to seeking headless arrows, granting 19.5 Fletching experience per set of 15.

Using seeking headless arrows on bronze arrows to create them in sets of 150. No experience is given for this.

Using a bucket of bloodwood sap directly on bronze arrows to create them in sets of 15 per bucket. This is never recommended, as the sap can treat higher tier logs that yield higher quantities of seeking arrow shafts per log.
33559:

Using seeking headless arrows on iron arrows to create them in sets of 150. No experience is given for this.

33623:
Blood sacs are obtained from dissecting leechfin fished from leechfin fishing spots, or by killing Venators or the Maggot King within Vampyrium. 50 blood sacs can be squeezed to make a vial of blood with an empty vial in inventory, giving blood sacs an indirect value of 163.88. Making a vial of blood in this way does not complete the Vial of Blood Collection Log slot.

A warning will be given if attempting to squeeze a blood sac without a vial; continuing the attempt results in a game message stating You squeeze a sac. It empties onto the floor.
33625:
Letvek are bait for hunting stymphikes, obtained by catching letvek in box traps with 76 Hunter, or through monster drops on Vampyrium.

At high Hunter levels, upwards of 700 letvek can be caught per hour with 3-tick manipulation, yielding approximately 145,000 experience per hour. With 1-tick trap resetting, 160,000 experience per hour is possible.

Letvek will run away if dropped, but they can be placed on a table. Letvek cannot be stored in the huntsman's kit.
33627:
Dull ancient medals are an item commonly dropped by the Maggot King. When polished in Vampyrium, one of two messages will appear in the chatbox. If the message says The medal releases a trace of ancient magic as it falls apart., then 8 Prayer points will be restored every 6 ticks for 120 ticks (72s), for a total of 160 prayer points.

However, there is a 3/7 chance the message instead says The medal quivers with magic and breaks apart!, and in addition to the prayer restoration, the player's combat stats will be boosted, up to +20 in Attack, Strength, and Defence, +14 in Ranged, and +11 in Magic. This also inflicts 1 damage to the player. The boosted stats will remain for 4 minutes and 30 seconds, after which the boosted stats will begin to decay naturally.

When the prayer restoration effect ends, a chatbox message stating The prayer restoration blessing dissipates. will appear. For the combat boost, the effect ending is indicated by the message You feel the power start to diffuse.

As long as the player stays in Vampyrium, both effects will carry over upon death. However, they will end immediately upon leaving Vampyrium, either by teleporting or by using the portal at Castle Drakan.

This item is always lost upon death.
33628:
Stymphike tartare is a food dropped by the Maggot King. When eaten, it will heal 26 Hitpoints and poisons for 1 damage. It has a non-standard eat delay of 1 tick, meaning multiple can be consumed in quick succession. Additionally each piece consumed will delay the player's next attack by 4 additional ticks, which is also non-standard compared to the default 3 tick delay.

When leaving Vampyrium with the item present in the inventory, it will turn into rotten stymphike tartare, which can no longer be consumed. As such, if ending a trip at the boss with many stymphike tartare remaining, players may wish to make the trip back to Sangvesti to bank them so that they can be used in a subsequent trip. Attempting to eat one anywhere else however will result in the tartare rotting alongside a chatbox message stating "On closer inspection, it looks like that meat is rotten."
33629:
Rotten stymphike tartare is the result of a stymphike tartare being brought out of Vampyrium whilst it is present in the player's inventory, rendering it inedible.

Players who deposit a stymphike tartare into the bank, then attempt to eat one whilst not in Vampyrium, will result in the tartare rotting alongside a chatbox message stating "On closer inspection, it looks like that meat is rotten."
33631: The crimson kisten is a two-handed spiked weapon requiring level 60 Attack and 85 Strength to wield. Obtained as a rare drop from the Maggot King, the weapon is mainly used for its special attack, dealing high damage against opponents weak to crush attacks.
33634: The elder venator fang is an item dropped by the Maggot King. With a Crafting level of 84, it can be etched using a chisel to produce the tradable etched elder venator fang, which is used to upgrade the necklace of anguish into the necklace of rupture, giving 500 Crafting experience. The etched elder venator fang, despite being tradable, cannot be sacrificed in Death's Coffer.
33636: The etched elder venator fang is an item created by using a chisel on an elder venator fang. With a Crafting level of 84, it can be combined with a necklace of anguish to create the necklace of rupture.
33642:
Maggot marquess is a pet that can be obtained from defeating the Maggot King, being a much smaller version of it.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.
33644: Dummy stymphike feather is an unobtainable item. Notably, it is listed on the Grand Exchange and is not a members only item. Unlike the actual stymphike feather, it can be wielded.
33651:
Stymphike feathers are dropped by stymphikes caught using the Hunter skill, as well as from various monsters on Vampyrium.

They may be handed in to the aranei at the Apsul and Virer Hunting Grounds for limited off-task access to venators. Each venator kill requires 30 feathers, costing 2,790 per venator if purchasing from other players.

Stymphike feathers can also be used in place of standard feathers for fletching, when making bolts, darts, and arrows, however they are not able to be used for fly fishing.

Stymphike feathers may be used to pay the aranei scout near the portal to Castle Drakan to move the player's grave near to them, if they had died whilst fighting the Maggot King. Depending on the current prices of stymphike feathers, this may be the most cost-effective way to pay.
33653:
Stymphike carcasses are dropped when hunting stymphikes and have no known uses. It cannot be stored in a meat pouch.

When used on Soar Leader Pitri, they say "I don't know what that thing is, but I don't believe it counts as meat! Get some of the raw meats that the hunters bring back; the birds will eat those."

If attempting to use it on Renu, it will reject it and drop one feather beneath the player's feet, accompanied by a game message stating You generously offer the quetzal your carcass. At the horrific smell, it disgorges a feather.

Attempting to use it on a fire or range yields the message You can't cook that.
33655: Makeshift spears are a tool used to hunt stymphikes in Vampyrium. Players can obtain these in bundles of 10 from the pile of makeshift spears.
33657: Orikalkum gravel is unrefined orikalkum that can be obtained as a drop from venators and the Maggot King. It has no uses other than its high alchemy value.
33659:
Grapevines are an item dropped by venators. They can be picked for roughly 10-15 grapes; Bologa's blessings can be used to pick Zamorak's grapes instead, providing an alternative way to obtain them instead of using grape seeds.

By default, grapevines do not stack in the inventory or bank. However, using them on one another combines them with the message You tie the grapevines together, creating an even longer grapevine..

They can be picked from the inventory while the bank interface is open, which automatically deposits the grapes.
33661: Venator fangs are an item dropped by venators and the Maggot King. These can be traded in for dragon arrowtips at a 1:1 ratio by speaking to the aranei by the aranei shrines in the Apsul or Virer Hunting Grounds, or by choosing their right-click "Trade-teeth" option.
33663: Venator teeth are an item dropped by venators and the Maggot King. These can be traded in for dragon dart tips at a 1:1 ratio by speaking to the aranei by the aranei shrines in the Apsul or Virer Hunting Grounds, or by choosing their right-click "Trade-teeth" option.
33665:
Maggot eggs are obtained by killing the Maggot King and taking eggs from its corpse rather than looting the stomach. There are six variants of maggot eggs, each offering a different chance of hatching into the maggot marquess pet.

When taking into account the drop rate of all six eggs, alongside the pet rate from the eggs, the overall chance of receiving the pet from taking eggs is 1/1,502.4 to receive the pet on a given kill, which is roughly 2.33 times the drop rate from looting the stomach.

Polishing the sword will display the message You rub the tarnished longsword on your clothes and are surprised to find a shine underneath the grime.

33695:
A venator heart can be obtained by killing venators with the Sunspear special attack, which is then inserted into the player's inventory rather than a drop that requires picking up. If the player's inventory is full, the heart is not obtained.

Venator hearts can be offered on the aranei shrine to restore 50% special attack energy and up to 24 prayer points. Leaving Vampyrium with the heart will cause it to turn into a dried out venator heart. The player can drop the heart on the ground and retrieve it before the timer is up, if they need to teleport away, without having the heart dry up.
33699: Vials are typically filled up with water and are most commonly used in the Herblore skill to make potions or mixes. Upon finishing a potion, the empty vial is left in the player's inventory; however with completion of Alfred Grimhand's Barcrawl, players may speak to the barbarian guard outside of the Barbarian Outpost to learn how to automatically smash vials upon finishing a potion. This feature also works in free-to-play. The player may also toggle this feature from the settings menu.
33701:
The squire's journal is given to the player by Ivan Strom in the Paterdomus Mausoleum during the The Blood Moon Rises quest.

If lost, it can be reclaimed from a bookcase within a player-owned house.
33702: From Misthalin to Morytania is a book written by Iriandul Caistlyn. It can be found during The Blood Moon Rises by searching a bookcase on the 1st floor of the Paterdomus Temple.
33704: A scruffy notebook is a book written by Derygull Templeton. It can be found during The Blood Moon Rises by searching a bookcase on the 1st floor of the Paterdomus Temple.
33706: The Life of Friar is a book written by Friar Twiblick. It can be found during The Blood Moon Rises by searching a bookcase on the 1st floor of the Paterdomus Temple.
33707: Essiandar's notes is a book written by Essiandar Gar. It can be found during The Blood Moon Rises by searching a bookcase on the 1st floor of the Paterdomus Temple.
33708:
Ivandis' writings is a book written by Ivandis Seergaze himself, obtained during The Blood Moon Rises. It details the truth behind the blessing of the River Salve and the unintentional side effect it had on him, and reveals the existence of an underground tunnel that leads directly to Castle Drakan.

If lost, it can be reclaimed from a bookcase within a player-owned house.
33709:
The diamond sickle (b) is an item obtained by using a diamond on a silver sickle (b) during The Blood Moon Rises. It can be enchanted into an enchanted diamond sickle (b) by casting Lvl-4 Enchant on it, or with the enchant diamond tablet provided during the quest.

The sickle has a right-click "bloom" option which can be used next to rotten logs, branches, or bushes in Mort Myre swamp to obtain Mort myre fungi, stems, and pears. These items can be used to fill the Druid pouch which allows the player to fight Ghasts. Bloom can also be cast on dead vines in the Ancient Guthixian Temple to grow them into flowering vines which can be picked to obtain a vine flower.

It can also be used to harm Vampyres and Vampyre Juvinates, but this is not recommended due to its weak stats.
33711:

It is to be used on blisterwood logs to create a blisterwood sickle (e), which is then used to create the hallowed flail.

During The Blood Moon Rises, it is combined with some hallowed marks and the blisterwood flail to create the hallowed flail. After quest completion, it is sold by Efaritay Hallow in Castle Drakan.

The sickle has a right-click "bloom" option which can be used next to rotten logs, branches, or bushes in Mort Myre swamp to obtain Mort myre fungi, stems, and pears.
